context.description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.

latestRelease.title: v0.5.17
latestRelease.notes:
# Highlights

*582 PRs from 194 contributors.*

**Kimi K3 day-0 support**: A 2.8T-parameter multimodal LatentMoE (896 experts, top-16, routed in a 3584-dim latent space) with a 1M-token context, 69 KDA linear-attention layers interleaved with 24 MLA layers, and a MoonViT3d vision tower, shipping as a native MXFP4 checkpoint. SGLang serves it from day 0 with DCP, DSpark speculative decoding, chunked-prefill PP with TP decode, KDA-aware prefix caching, HiCache L2 over DCP, LoRA on the quantized weights, and reasoning, tool-call and OpenAI-compatible serving, verified on NVIDIA GB300 and AMD MI35x ([#32541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32541), [#32828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32828), [#32890](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32890), [#33025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33025), [#33112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33112), [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3), [roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607)).

**MiniMax-H3 day-0 support**: MiniMax's video generation model that produces a video and a synchronized stereo audio track in one request, served natively on SGLang-Diffusion across all three public task profiles: text-to-video-and-audio (`t2va`), first/last-frame conditioning (`fl2va`), and image/video/audio reference conditioning (`ref2va`, which also covers video-to-video). Verified on B200 (TP2 + Ulysses4), H100 (TP2 + Ulysses2), AMD MI300X and MI355X (Ulysses1/2/4/8), and 2x RTX 5090 with layerwise offload ([#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275), [cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3)).

**Other new models added**: [EmbeddingGemma](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Google/EmbeddingGemma) and [LFM2.5](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/LiquidAI/LFM2.5) embedding models, nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, plus cookbook recipes for Poolside's [Laguna-S-2.1](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) family and [Inkling-Small](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/ThinkingMachines/Inkling-Small).

**Initial support for the Rust frontend**: Migrates the front half of the server, everything from network ingress up to the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler, from Python to a multi-threaded Rust implementation ([#29799](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799)).

**DCP communication backends and q-replicate (Helix)**: The DeepSeek-MLA decode context-parallel path gains pluggable comm backends. `a2a` exchanges packed attention output plus fp32 LSE in a single NCCL collective per layer, with fp8 KV carried as uint8 byte transport; `fi_a2a` delegates the cross-rank exchange to the FlashInfer MNNVL kernel on GB200. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` projects full-head Q locally and skips the per-layer Q head-dim all-gather. Select with `--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}` ([#21637](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21637)).

**DWDP for MoE prefill**: A new prefill parallelism strategy that prefetches peer expert weights over NVLink P2P and computes all experts locally, removing EP all-to-all token dispatch. On 4x B200 with gpt-oss-120b, prefill-only, DWDP4 reaches **1.92x over DEP4** at MNT 32K / ISL 32K, and **506K vs 329K tok/s (1.54x)** at saturation (CONC=128, ISL=8K). Enable with `--dwdp-size`; the authors mark it early-development ([#29778](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29778)).

**Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache**: For agentic and RL-rollout workloads, requests can carry a stable `session_id` so eviction knows which prefixes an active session still references, instead of evicting purely by cache policy. Release the references with `/close_session`. Opt in with `--enable-session-radix-cache` ([#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173)).

**SM90 FP8 MegaMoE for DeepSeek-V4**: Adds the DeepGEMM MegaMoE A2A path on SM90 for DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro FP8, including the pre-dispatch JIT kernel and FP8 expert weight preparation. Guarded behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` ([#29016](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29016)).

**Faster large-MoE model loading**: Oversized or non-contiguous CPU weight views were driving pathological H2D transfers, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 spending 27 to 32 minutes in H2D on some ranks. Copying those views into contiguous storage before H2D cuts full model loading from about **35 minutes to 6m20s (5.6x)**, and GPT-OSS-20B BF16 from **545s to 70s (7.8x)**, with Qwen3.5-397B measured at 1.93x to 2.3x. Opt in with `SGLANG_MOE_COPY_WEIGHT_VIEWS_BEFORE_H2D`, off by default ([#32315](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32315)).

**Lower DeepSeek-V4 memory on AMD**: Removing unnecessary expert padding drops MI355X FP4 MoE model weights from **159.07 GB to 112.36 GB**, and bringing the HIP compress-state pool into the memory_saver KV_CACHE region lets colocated RL reclaim it, cutting the measured training-phase footprint from about **143 GiB to 87 GiB per GPU** ([#31450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31450), [#31747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31747)).

**Faster engine recovery**: Large-model restarts cost 3 to 6+ minutes today, about 6.5 minutes for Qwen3-235B FP8 on 4 GPUs, because weights reload from storage and CUDA graphs recapture. A weight-cache daemon holds weights per GPU so a restarting engine can recover from cache instead ([#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139)).

**Lower host overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode**: Under spec-v2 overlap scheduling each decode step runs draft, verify and extend CUDA graphs, and the eager seams between them become GPU idle time at low concurrency. This trims that host work so the host stays off the critical path ([#32219](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32219)).

**Dependencies**: flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 ([#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927)), sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1 ([#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345), [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)), helion 1.4 ([#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)), mooncake 0.3.12.post1 ([#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)), dynamo-tokenizers 1.7.0 ([#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)). PyTorch stays at 2.11.0 and the CUDA base image at 13.0.1.

*Full release notes by category below; breaking changes and known issues are at the end.*

* [Fix][AMD] Qwen3.5 MoE: disable global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends (MoRI + dp-attention init crash): [#31793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31793)

* [AMD] Fix JIT compile failure in sgl_kernel/warp.cuh: [#33195](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33195)

## NPU / Ascend

* [NPU] Optimize DeepSeek-V4 performance: [#31931](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31931)
* :sparkles: [llm][npu][quant] Add W8A8 MXFP8 quantization for Qwen3 MoE on Ascend NPU: [#30768](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30768)
* [NPU] adapt dflash v2 on npu: [#31739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31739)
* [NPU] Adapt MiMo-V2.5-W8A8: [#29131](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29131)

* [NPU] ascend fuseep use moe ep group: [#32040](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32040)

* [NPU] [FIX] Fix performance degradation of Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: [#32130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32130)

* [Intel GPU] Add XPU Platform support: [#31949](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31949)
* [XPU] Enable breakable prefill CUDA graph on XPU: [#30273](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30273)

* [Bugfix] Fix CUDA import on non-CUDA platforms: [#31919](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31919)

## Dependencies

* Bump FlashInfer to 0.6.15.post1: [#31927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31927) ⭐
* Bump sgl-deep-gemm to 0.1.5: [#32345](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32345)
* Replace Kimi K3 DeepGEMM patch with 0.1.5.post1: [#33143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33143)
* Bump helion version to 1.4: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* chore: bump mooncake version to 0.3.12.post1: [#32302](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32302)
* bump dynamo-tokenizers to 1.7.0: [#32981](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32981)
* [AMD] ROCm AITER pin reverted to 9127c94, then updated to d9e5ef7: [#32879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32879), [#32939](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32939)
* Fix PyPI release: drop the git-only sgl-eval dep from packaged metadata: [#32354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32354)

## Breaking Changes & Upgrade Notes

* **`helion` jumps 0.2.6 to 1.4**, a major-version move for anyone depending on helion-backed kernels: [#32562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32562)
* **`sglang.jit_kernel` is retired into `sglang.kernels`**, completing RFC [#29630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29630). Imports from the old module path must move: [#32072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32072), [#31666](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31666), [#32015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32015), [#32045](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32045)
* **Breakable prefill CUDA graph is now on by default for DP attention**: [#31682](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31682)
* **CuteDSL BF16 GEMM on SM100 is on by default** when the heuristic allows it: [#30567](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30567)
* **sgl-kernel AOT `bmm_fp8` is deleted in favor of `flashinfer.bmm_fp8`; the AOT router GEMM and fused A GEMM are also removed**: [#31202](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31202), [#30280](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30280)
* **The FP8 per-tensor GEMM backend on SM120 switches to cuBLAS**: [#31961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31961)
* **Unfetchable or unparseable multimodal inputs now return HTTP 400 instead of 500**, and text-only models reject media input outright: [#31417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31417), [#32914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32914)
* **Diffusion request-level quality is restricted to two validated tiers**, lossless (default) and high: [#33453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33453)
* **`ServerArgs` is being made read-only** behind namespace config bags. Code that mutated `ServerArgs` at runtime must route through the new accessors: [#31809](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31809), [#31811](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31811), [#33334](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33334), [#33338](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33338)

## Known Issues

* **The FlashInfer rmsnorm + quant fusion for SM90/SM100/SM120 was landed and reverted** this cycle ([#32994](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32994), [#33455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33455)). It is not in this release.
* **Breakable CUDA graph is disabled for NemotronH** pending a fix: [#33130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33130)
* **`test_update_weights_from_disk` is skipped on ROCm** pending a reload fix ([#31924](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31924)): [#31925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31925)
* **The SM120 DeepGEMM release-pipeline test is temporarily skipped**: [#32193](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32193)

**Full Changelog**: [`v0.5.16...v0.5.17`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/compare/v0.5.16...v0.5.17)

signals.text: ### Checklist - [X] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed. - [X] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed. ### Motivation As https://github.com/thu-ml/SageAttention mentioned, the quantized 8-bit attention will improvement the speed of inference about 2x and more with the same accuracy, so shall we give it a try or do some verification? ### Related resources github: https://github.com/thu-ml/SageAttention

signals.title: [Bug] txn545/Qwen3.5-27B-NVFP4 fails to load on latest main: missing input_scale param + shape assertion in qwen3_5.py
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Hi SGLang team, I am trying to run `txn545/Qwen3.5-27B-NVFP4` using native SGLang inside WSL2 on Windows 11, and the model fails during weight loading on the latest `main` branch. ## Failure The load fails with: ```text [2026-02-28 11:04:19] Parameter model.layers.0.linear_attn.in_proj_a.input_scale not found in params_dict [2026-02-28 11:04:19] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): ... File "/home/richard/llm/sglang-qwen35-nvfp4/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1117, in load_weights weight_loader(param, loaded_weight) File "/home/richard/llm/sglang-qwen35-nvfp4/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 416, in weight_loader assert param_data.shape == loaded_weight.shape ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ AssertionError [2026-02-28 11:04:19] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed. Loading safetensors checkpoint shards: 0% Completed | 0/1 [00:05<?, ?it/s] Killed ``` ## What I already verified * `nvidia-smi` works inside WSL * `torch.backends.cudnn.version()` returns `91600` * `import sglang; print(sglang.__file__)` points to my local GitHub checkout: `/home/richard/llm/sglang-qwen35-nvfp4/sglang/python/sglang/__init__.py` * `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py` in my checkout contains the expected Qwen3.5 NVFP4-related entries such as: * `.weight_scale` * `.input_scale` * `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj` remapping * `git pull origin main` reports the repo is already up to date ## Interpretation This looks like a checkpoint / loader compatibility issue rather than a CUDA or WSL setup issue. signals.title: [Feature] Unified JIT / Precompilation Cache Directory
signals.text: ### Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation ## Summary **Request:** Unify all JIT and precompilation cache paths under a single configurable root so that users and operators can manage cache location, size, and persistence in one place. The current situation is fragmented across multiple env vars and default paths (including `/tmp`), which makes it hard to reason about where compiled artifacts live and to reuse caches across runs or machines. ## Current State (Fragmented) ### 1. Triton JIT cache | What | Env var / source | Default / behavior | |------|------------------|--------------------| | Direct `@triton.jit` (e.g. allocator, MoE kernels) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (Triton runtime) | Triton default: `~/.triton/cache`; often overwritten by Inductor to a path under `/tmp/torchinductor_*` | | SGLang override | `SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.triton/cache` or `~/.cache/triton` | - Set only in some entry paths (engine, gRPC launcher, scheduler process); custom/PD launchers may not set it. - When PyTorch Inductor runs first, it can set `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` to its own subdir, so later Triton JIT (including allocator) writes under `/tmp`. ### 2. PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile) | What | Env var / source | Default / behavior | |------|------------------|--------------------| | Inductor cache | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (PyTorch) | `/tmp/torchinductor_<user>` (or similar) | | SGLang override | `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` (if implemented) | e.g. `~/.cache/sglang/inductor` | - Default lives in `/tmp`, so cache is often non-persistent and can conflict with other users on shared nodes. ### 3. DeepGEMM JIT cache | What | Env var / source | Default / behavior | |------|------------------|--------------------| | DeepGEMM cache | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` | `~/.cache/deep_gemm` | - Set in `layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/compile_utils.py`; separate from Triton/Inductor. - ## Problems 1. **No single root:** Triton, Inductor, SGLang torch_compile, and DeepGEMM each have their own env or default; some write to `/tmp`, others to `~/.cache/...`. ## Proposal ### 1. Introduce a single JIT cache root - **New env var:** `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT` (or `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` if we want to align with existing `SGLANG_CACHE_ROOT` in custom_all_reduce_utils). - **Default:** `~/.cache/sglang` (or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/sglang` when set). - **Semantics:** All JIT/precompilation caches that SGLang controls should live under this root in fixed subdirs. ### 2. Standard layout under the root Suggested subdirs (all under `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT`): | Subdir | Purpose | Maps from | |--------|---------|-----------| | `triton/` | Triton JIT (direct `@triton.jit` and, when possible, Triton used by Inductor) | `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` | | `inductor/` | PyTorch Inductor (torch.compile) | `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` | | `torch_compile/` | SGLang torch.compile cache (hash-based, when using SGLangBackend) | `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` + `torch_compile_cache` | | `deep_gemm/` | DeepGEMM JIT | `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR` / `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` | - If we keep backward compatibility, existing env vars (`SGLANG_TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, `SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR`) could override the default subdir path when set; otherwise they are derived as `{SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_ROOT}/{subdir}`. CC @Fridge003 @hnyls2002 ### Related resources _No response_

signals.title: [Bug] Mamba radix cache can turn fresh prefill prefix hits into 0-hit after split
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] This report is in English. ### Summary `MambaRadixCache` can degrade a structurally valid prefix match into an effective 0-hit on fresh prefills. The problematic combination is: 1. fresh prefill lookup intentionally matches at most `input_len - 1` tokens in `Req.init_next_round_input()` so that one token is left for the current extend/logprob step, 2. if that lookup ends in the middle of a compressed radix edge, `_split_node()` creates a new internal prefix node with `mamba_value = None`, 3. `_match_prefix_helper()` advances `best_value_len` only when the current node has a `mamba_value`, and 4. `_match_post_processor()` truncates the returned KV indices to `value[:best_value_len]`. Net effect: the tree can structurally match a prefix, but the returned `device_indices` can still become length 0. ### Why this seems surprising The `input_len - 1` behavior itself makes sense for generation: if the entire input were prefix-hit, the current extend batch would have 0 tokens and would not produce the next-token logits. However, in the Mamba radix cache, that legitimate `n - 1` lookup interacts badly with split semantics. A fresh request with an identical prompt can fail to reuse any device KV, even though the prompt prefix is already present in the radix tree. ### Minimal scenario Assume request 1 has prompt `[A, B, C]`. After request 1 prefill completes, `cache_unfinished_req()` inserts the current `req.fill_ids` into `MambaRadixCache`. In the common fresh-prefill case this is the prompt itself, e.g. `[A, B, C]`, with a valid `mamba_value` on that node. Then request 2 arrives with the same prompt `[A, B, C]`. During `Req.init_next_round_input()`: - `fill_ids = origin_input_ids + output_ids = [A, B, C]` - `max_prefix_len = input_len - 1 = 2` - the cache lookup key becomes `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, C]` If the tree currently contains a compressed child/key `[A, B, C]`, matching `[A, B]` causes a split: - original: `root -> [A,B,C] (has mamba)` - after split: `root -> [A,B] (mamba=None) -> [C] (original suffix)` The fresh request stops at `[A,B]` because that is the entire lookup key for this round. At that point: - the path was structurally matched, - but the matched node has `mamba_value = None`, - so `best_value_len` does not advance, - and `_match_post_processor()` truncates the returned KV hit to length 0. ### Code paths involved - `python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py` - `Req.init_next_round_input()` - comment: "the matched length is at most 1 less than the input length to enable logprob computation" - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/mamba_radix_cache.py` - `_split_node()` sets `new_node.mamba_value = None` - `_match_prefix_helper()` updates `best_value_len` only when `node.mamba_value is not None` - `_match_post_processor()` truncates `value` to `value[:best_value_len]` ### Impact This can make prompt reuse much worse than expected for sequential workloads and rollout-style workloads: - identical prompt reuse across fresh requests can collapse to 0-hit, - shared-prefix reuse is much more brittle than in the standard radix cache, - the behavior is especially easy to trigger because fresh prefill intentionally uses `n - 1` lookup. ### Expected behavior At minimum, it would be helpful to confirm whether this is intended. If not intended, possible fixes could include one of the following directions: - preserve usable prefix reuse across split boundaries for fresh prefill lookups, - avoid truncating full KV hits solely because the split/internal node has no `mamba_value`, and rely on `mamba_branching_seqlen` to re-track state as needed, - or introduce explicit intermediate checkpointing so the `n - 1` fresh-prefill lookup lands on a node with a valid Mamba state more often. ### Related issue This seems related to, but distinct from, #22326: - #22326 is a feature proposal to add more Mamba checkpoints during prefill, - this report is about current behavior where a valid fresh-prefill prefix match can degrade to 0-hit because of split semantics plus Mamba-gated KV truncation.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP16+PP2 crashes with CUDA illegal memory access during CUDA Graph replay under serving load
signals.text: ### Checklist - [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [ ] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When serving DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 4 nodes with TP16 + PP2, SGLang crashes under benchmark load with: ``` torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The failure happens inside CUDA Graph replay: ``` cuda_graph_runner.py self.graphs[graph_key].replay() ``` After one TP worker crashes, the remaining PP stages fail with: ``` RuntimeError: [/pytorch/third_party/gloo/gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:547] Connection closed by peer ``` The Gloo error appears to be a secondary failure caused by one scheduler process exiting after the CUDA illegal memory access. ### Reproduction **Launch Command** ``` SGLANG_DYNAMIC_CHUNKING_SMOOTH_FACTOR=0.75 \ CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 \ SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 \ GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0 \ NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_3,mlx5_5 \ NVSHMEM_HCA_LIST="mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_3,mlx5_5" \ PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \ sglang serve \ --model-path /data/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \ --tp-size 16 \ --pp-size 2 \ --dist-init-addr ${DIST_ADDR}:${DIST_PORT} \ --nnodes 4 \ --node-rank ${NODE_RANK} \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8000 \ --moe-runner-backend marlin \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --context-length 204800 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --enable-metrics \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --model-loader-extra-config \ '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' ``` **Benchmark** python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang-oai \ --host 10.72.41.74 \ --port 8000 \ --model /mnt/weka/llm-models/modelscope/hub/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 100 \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency 32 **Error** The first failure occurs on PP1: ``` File ".../cuda_graph_runner.py", line 1354, in replay self.graphs[graph_key].replay() torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Full stack: ``` model_runner.forward() -> _forward_raw() -> graph_runner.replay() -> torch.cuda.graphs.CUDAGraph.replay() CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` Immediately afterwards: ``` Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed. ``` Other PP workers then fail with: ``` RuntimeError: [/pytorch/third_party/gloo/gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:547] Connection closed by peer ``` _Observations_ The failure does not happen during: model loading CUDA graph capture warmup The server starts successfully and serves requests. Crash occurs only after benchmark traffic begins. Right before the crash: ``` Decode batch #running-req: 3 #full token: 15616 Prefill batch #new-token: 256 ``` The illegal memory access happens during generation replay rather than prefill. ### Environment 镜像：lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12

signals.title: moe_kernels.py, stage-2 reduce path: small SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK silently corrupts output (gsm8k=0) at low concurrency
signals.text: ## Summary On the MoRI expert-parallel backend, a small `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` **silently corrupts decode output** — the model still generates fluent-looking tokens (speculative acceptance length stays high), but the content is semantically wrong and gsm8k drops to **0.00**. The value is forwarded to MoRI's `max_num_inp_token_per_rank` with no minimum/validation, so configs that legitimately produce a small per-rank dispatch buffer (low concurrency × dp-attention × MTP) hit it with no error or warning. This is a silent correctness bug: nothing crashes, throughput even looks marginally *better*, so it is easy to ship a broken Pareto point. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x` (sglang v0.5.12.post1) - HW: AMD MI355X (CDNA, warpSize 64) - Model: DeepSeek-R1 (FP4), prefill/decode disaggregated - Decode parallelism: TP8 / EP8 / **dp-attention** / **MTP (num-draft-tokens=4)** - Backends: `--moe-a2a-backend mori --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori --deepep-mode normal` ## Symptom At decode concurrency 64 with TP8 + MTP3, the per-rank dispatch buffer works out to `64/8 * 4 = 32` tokens. The server starts, warms up, benchmarks at full speed, and produces grammatical output — but gsm8k = 0. Raising the buffer fixes it. ## Reproduction / evidence (shmoo of the env var, same config) | `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` | gsm8k (strict) | output tok/s | run | |---|---|---|---| | 32 | **0.0000** | 6312 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26913235190 | | 64 (= warpSize) | **0.0000** | 6324 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26919517564 | | 256 | **0.9424** | 6219 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26920499507 | (Run links are internal CI; the relevant log excerpts are inline below.) All three runs generate identical token volume — 640 requests, 589,927 generated tokens — so the numbers are directly comparable. Note the corrupt runs are ~1.5% *faster* (less real work), which is why this slips through perf-only validation. Eval log (256, correct): ``` [MoRI floor] DISPATCH_TOKENS=32 < floor 256; clamping to 256 Decode env: SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 PASS: gsm8k exact_match,strict-match = 0.9424 (>= 0.85) ``` ## This is not the LL vs non-LL kernel switch `get_ep_dispatch_configs()` selects `InterNodeV1LL` vs `InterNodeV1` by comparing the dispatch size to `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256). In the failing run that threshold was set to 16, and the decode log confirms: ``` [DP+EP override] Decode: ... DISPATCH_TOKENS=8, ... INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH=16 ``` Since `32 > 16`, the **non-LL `InterNodeV1`** kernel is selected — and it still corrupts. So the bug is the per-rank buffer size itself, not the kernel variant. ## Where it originates in sglang In `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py` (v0.5.12): - The value is read with a default of 4096 and **no lower bound**: ```python self.num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank = get_int_env_var( "SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK", 4096) ``` - It is passed straight through to MoRI as `max_num_inp_token_per_rank=num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank`. - There is already a `if num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank < 128:` branch that swaps the launch config (`warp_num_per_block`), so small dispatch sizes are clearly known to be special — but that branch does **not** prevent the corruption at 32/64. ## ~~Likely mechanism (hypothesis — root cause is in MoRI)~~ — **CORRECTED, see below** ~~The MoRI dispatch kernel writes received tokens into warpSize-aligned slots: `destTokId = flagSlotId * warpSize + laneId`, into a per-PE region whose stride is `max_num_inp_token_per_rank`. When that region is smaller than warpSize (64), or smaller than the routing fan-in a rank can receive from all peers, the writes go out of bounds. Empirically warpSize (64) is necessary but not sufficient; ≥256 is needed for this config. Filed in parallel against ROCm/mori: `src/ops/dispatch_combine/internode_v1.cpp` (`DispatchInterNodeSend` / `DispatchIntraNodeBlock`). https://github.com/ROCm/mori/issues/356~~ > ### UPDATE, corrected root cause (not MoRI issue) > > The MoRI hypothesis is wrong, and `ROCm/mori#356` was closed as not-a-MoRI-issue. No out-of-bounds write in the dispatch kernel is involved. > > The actual root cause is prob in AITER's FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce path (`aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`), confirmed by @billishyahao: > > - The reduce intermediate is allocated with `torch.empty` (**uninitialized**). > - In EP, gemm2 writes only valid local-expert slots; masked (non-local) slots are never written. > - `torch.sum` over `topk` then folds those uninitialized slots in → NaN/garbage → corrupt-but-fluent output. > - Only the **M≈1024 tuning bucket** selects this reduce kernel; other buckets use a zero-init atomic accumulate, which is why M=1032/2048 were fine and only specific low-concurrency points corrupt. > > **Fixed in [ROCm/aiter#3377](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3377)** (masked gather `valid = expert_mask[topk_ids] != 0` + EP tuned-key `topk -= is_ep`), pulled into SGLang via **#27555** (AITER commit bump `6740fb7` → `7a8ff7d`). > > **Not fully resolved:** with the fix applied, conc64 passes but **conc32 and conc16 still fail** ([run](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27225030090)) — the sub-1024 M-buckets likely need the same masked-reduce treatment. Keeping this open until those are covered. ## Requested fix 1. In `moriep.py`, **enforce or validate a minimum** for `num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank` (and/or emit a clear warning) instead of silently forwarding a too-small value. 2. Revisit the `< 128` launch-config branch — it does not make small buffers correct. 3. Coordinate the actual kernel-level fix with ROCm/mori (sizing from fan-in, or asserting a minimum). At minimum, a silent correctness failure should become a loud one.

signals.title: [Bug] --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass + FP8 weights crashes with AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner'
signals.text: ### Summary When launching sglang with an FP8 quantized MoE model and explicitly selecting `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, the server passes startup and CUDA graph capture cleanly, but **crashes on the first forward pass** with: ``` AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner' ``` The combination is silently accepted at config time and only fails when an actual request arrives, which is a poor user experience. The expected behavior is either: 1. A clear `NotImplementedError`/`ValueError` at server startup explaining that `flashinfer_cutlass` is not supported on the FP8 path (and pointing users at `--moe-runner-backend cutlass` instead), **or** 2. A real implementation of FP8 + flashinfer cutlass MoE. The lightweight first option would already remove a sharp edge for users. ### Environment - sglang: main HEAD (commit `10219bd9d` at time of repro) - flashinfer: 0.6.3 - torch: 2.9.1 / triton: 3.5.1 - transformers: 5.8.1 - Hardware: 1× NVIDIA H200 (SM 9.0) - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8` ### Reproducer ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --port 31103 ``` Then any request: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:31103/generate -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"text": "Hello", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 8}}' ``` ### Server log (truncated to the relevant frame) ``` File "sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 1447, in apply if self.runner.runner_backend.is_deep_gemm(): ^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner' ``` ### Root cause analysis In `sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner` only assigns `self.runner` for a limited set of backends: ```python # python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py (main HEAD, ~line 1779) if ( moe_runner_backend.is_deep_gemm() or moe_runner_backend.is_triton() or moe_runner_backend.is_aiter() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm_routed() ): self.runner = MoeRunner(moe_runner_backend, moe_runner_config) else: # TODO(cwan): refactor other backends pass ``` When the user passes `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, none of the `is_*()` checks match, so the `else: pass` branch silently runs and `self.runner` is never set. Later in the same module, `Fp8MoEMethod.apply()` (~line 1938 on main) dispatches by reading `self.runner.runner_backend`: ```python if self.runner.runner_backend.is_deep_gemm(): ... elif self.runner.runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() ...: ... ``` Hitting `self.runner` then raises `AttributeError`. Note: the FP8 path already has a separate `cutlass` branch a few lines earlier that uses sglang's native `cutlass_fused_experts_fp8`: ```python if get_moe_runner_backend().is_cutlass(): output = cutlass_fused_experts_fp8(...) return StandardCombineInput(hidden_states=output) ``` So the working path for FP8 + cutlass is `--moe-runner-backend cutlass`, not `flashinfer_cutlass`. Users hitting the bug are likely confused by the BF16 path, where `flashinfer_cutlass` is the right (and now well-tuned, since #26496) choice. ### Suggested fix (minimal) Add an explicit failure mode in `Fp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner` so the incompatibility surfaces at startup, not at first request: ```python if ( moe_runner_backend.is_deep_gemm() or moe_runner_backend.is_triton() or moe_runner_backend.is_aiter() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm_routed() ): self.runner = MoeRunner(moe_runner_backend, moe_runner_config) elif moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutlass(): raise NotImplementedError( "FP8 MoE does not currently support --moe-runner-backend " "flashinfer_cutlass. Use --moe-runner-backend cutlass for FP8 " "(sglang's native cutlass_fused_experts_fp8 implementation). " "flashinfer_cutlass is currently only supported on the BF16 " "path (unquant.py)." ) else: # TODO(cwan): refactor other backends pass ``` This is a strictly user-experience fix; the underlying implementation gap (no FP8 path through flashinfer's cutlass MoE kernel) is a separate discussion. ### Related - PR #26496 ("Changes for SM120 perf and usability for NVFP4", merged 2026-06-04) recently re-enabled `flashinfer_cutlass` in the FlashInfer autotune allowlist, restoring a 4.7-8.4× speedup on H200 BF16 models when users explicitly request `flashinfer_cutlass`. This is excellent — but it also makes it more likely users will reach for `flashinfer_cutlass` on FP8 models, which is exactly the path that hits this AttributeError. See our independent validation: PR #26496 with FP8 attempt also crashes the same way (would have validated this issue earlier if we'd tried FP8 first). ### Discovery context Found while benchmarking sglang BF16 vs FP8 throughput on H200 with a deterministic bench harness. The BF16 path with `flashinfer_cutlass` worked beautifully (5-8× over the triton default once #26496-style autotune is enabled); migrating the same flag to FP8 produced this crash. Happy to share the per-regime benchmark numbers and the bench-spec setup if that helps narrow down the failure mode. ### Willingness to contribute I'm happy to send a PR for the minimal user-experience fix (option 1 above) if maintainers agree that's the right framing. The real implementation (option 2) is out of scope for me — I don't know whether flashinfer's cutlass MoE has a working FP8 path on Hopper that sglang could plug into.

signals.title: [Feature] Per-request Observability: TTFT Breakdown + HiCache Metrics
signals.text: ## Problem Currently, SGLang lacks per-request observability in two key areas: 1. **TTFT cannot be decomposed** — there's no way to know how much of TTFT is queue wait, schedule delay, or GPU forward time. Operators can only see total TTFT, making prefill performance tuning guesswork. This problem exists regardless of whether HiCache is enabled. 2. **HiCache tier performance is invisible** — with three-tier KV cache (GPU→CPU→NVMe) enabled, L2 DMA time, L3 prefetch I/O time, and per-tier hit/miss counts are not available per-request. No Prometheus metrics exist for cache hit rates, prefetch latency distributions, or eviction pressure. ## Proposed Solution A lightweight per-request trace + Prometheus metrics system covering both TTFT decomposition and HiCache observability, implemented across 5 files. ### Part A: Per-request Trace (JSON log, debug level) One JSON line per request at `logger.debug` level. The TTFT fields work universally; HiCache fields are gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache`: ```json { "rid": "b3f3e0e1...", "prompt_tokens": 136921, "input_tokens_cache_hit": 119040, "input_tokens_no_cache_hit": 17881, "output_tokens": 4096, "L1_hit": 0, "L1_hit_pct": 0.0, "L2_hit": 119040, "L2_hit_pct": 86.9, "L3_hit": 0, "L3_hit_pct": 0.0, "L3_pf_alloc_ms": 0, "L3_pf_io_ms": 0, "L3_pf_tree_ms": 0, "queue_ms": 9.9, "schedule_ms": 2.4, "forward_ms": 1174.6, "TTFT_ms": 78907.9 } ``` #### TTFT Decomposition (universal — works with or without HiCache) `TTFT ≈ queue_ms + schedule_ms + forward_ms` | Field | Source | Meaning | | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | | `queue_ms` | `time_stats.scheduler_recv_time → wait_queue_entry_time` | Tokenizer → enqueue | | `schedule_ms` | `time_stats.wait_queue_entry_time → forward_entry_time` | Wait in queue + chunk waits | | `forward_ms` | `time_stats.forward_entry_time → prefill_finished_time` | GPU prefill compute | #### HiCache Fields (gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache`) Per-tier hit token counts with percentages, L3 prefetch phase breakdown. > **Why no L2 DMA time?** `cache_controller.load()` is asynchronous — it allocates GPU memory and queues the DMA operation, then returns immediately. The actual DMA runs on a CUDA stream in a background thread (`start_loading()`). CPU-side `time.perf_counter()` cannot capture the DMA completion time. Since DMA bandwidth is fixed (PCIe 5.0 × 16 ≈ 64 GB/s), the transfer time is a known constant: `L2_hit_tokens × 48 KB/token ÷ 64 GB/s`. L2 token count alone is sufficient to characterize L2 performance. **L3 prefetch phase breakdown** (key finding made possible by this instrumentation): | Phase | P50 | Meaning | | ---------------- | ----- | ---------------------- | | `L3_pf_alloc_ms` | 0.1ms | Host memory allocation | | `L3_pf_io_ms` | 91ms | Pure NVMe→CPU I/O | | `L3_pf_tree_ms` | 0.4ms | Radix tree insertion | Without this breakdown, the total L3 prefetch time is often conflated with scheduler queue delays (~2.4s vs actual I/O ~91ms). ### Part B: Prometheus Metrics 6 Histograms + 2 Counters exposed at `/metrics`: | Metric | Type | Description | | -------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------ | | `sglang:hicache_l1_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L1 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l2_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L2 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l3_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L3 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l3_prefetch_seconds` | Histogram | L3→L2 prefetch total duration | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_alloc_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: alloc phase | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_io_wait_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: I/O phase | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_tree_insert_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: tree insert phase | | `sglang:hicache_cached_input_tokens_total` | Counter | Cumulative cached tokens | | `sglang:hicache_uncached_input_tokens_total` | Counter | Cumulative uncached tokens | ### Part C: Eviction Metrics `RadixCacheMetricsCollector.increment_eviction_num_tokens()` called from cache eviction code paths (previously unused in `HiMambaRadixCache`): - L1→L2 eviction counter (tokens evicted from GPU to CPU) - L2→L3 eviction counter (tokens evicted from CPU to NVMe) > Write-back timing is excluded for the same reason as L2 DMA — `cache_controller.write()` is also asynchronous. ## Implementation Scope 5 files, ~100 lines of instrumentation total: | File | Change | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `scheduler.py` | `_hicache_trace_one_request()` method: trace JSON + metrics observe | | `metrics_collector.py` | 7 HiCache Histograms + 2 Counters | | `hi_mamba_radix_cache.py` | L2/L3 timing in `load_back`/`write_backup`/`evict`/`evict_host` | | `hiradix_cache.py` | Same for MHA models | | `cache_controller.py` | `_page_transfer` I/O timing via `try/finally` | ## Compatibility - TTFT decomposition fields work universally (no flag required). HiCache fields gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache` - Trace output at `logger.debug` level only (no overhead at default `info` level), `tp_rank == 0` only - HiCache metrics guarded by `enable_metrics` and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` - No breaking changes to existing APIs ## Related - [#10916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/10916) — Unified Observability Interface proposal (tracing + metrics + TimeStat). This proposal can serve as a concrete implementation of that unified interface for TTFT and HiCache. - [#13511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13511) — Request Tracing Roadmap. This proposal fills the "HiCache tracing" item under "Tracing for uncovered engine components." - PRs #13152, #17862 — trace-level/module unification (compatible approach)

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B text rerank returns identical scores on NGC 26.05
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] The report is in English. ### Describe the bug `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B` appears to be broken for text-only reranking on `nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang:26.05-py3` (internal SGLang version reported in the live run: `0.5.11+05fb6a52`). The NGC build has native VL-reranker support in `/v1/rerank`: the serving code auto-detects this model family and returns the expected guidance to relaunch without `--is-embedding`. However, in generation mode the text-only rerank results are not discriminative: all documents receive the same score. Verified live excerpts from the DGX Spark activation run: ```text /v1/rerank: all documents scored identically: 0.4494 ``` The server log shows the likely failure point in prompt assembly: ```text Warning: More image data items provided than corresponding tokens found in the prompt ``` The same run showed each document prefill entering as one token: ```text #new-token: 1 ``` `/v1/score` was also not a usable workaround on this build. It ignored `label_token_ids` and returned a uniform distribution: ```text /v1/score: uniform 1/2048 distribution despite label_token_ids ``` This looks like the text-only path for the multimodal reranker is constructing or tokenizing the multimodal prompt incorrectly, causing both `/v1/rerank` and `/v1/score` to lose the query/document content. ### Reproduction Hardware/context: - NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 - Architecture: aarch64 - GPU target: SM121 - Container image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang:26.05-py3` - Internal SGLang version observed: `0.5.11+05fb6a52` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B` Request shape was a normal text-only rerank call: one text query and multiple text documents, with one obviously relevant document and one junk/irrelevant document. The exact request/response pairs and pod logs are available if useful; I am keeping this issue to verified excerpts rather than fabricating a minimal traceback. Observed behavior: - `/v1/rerank` returns identical scores for relevant and irrelevant text documents (`0.4494` in the captured run). - Server logs include `More image data items provided than corresponding tokens found in the prompt`. - Per-document prefill is logged as `#new-token: 1`. - `/v1/score` ignores `label_token_ids` and returns uniform `1/2048` probabilities. Expected behavior: - Text-only rerank should produce different relevance scores for clearly relevant vs irrelevant documents. - Text-only inputs should not trigger image-token mismatch warnings. - `/v1/score` should respect `label_token_ids` or fail explicitly if that mode is unsupported for this family. ### Additional context The model card documents Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B as a multimodal reranker that supports text inputs as well as image/video/mixed inputs. The same cluster has `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` (text) working correctly on SGLang 0.5.12.x via formatted `/v1/score`, so this appears specific to the VL reranker path in the NGC 26.05 / 0.5.11 build rather than a general reranking deployment issue.

signals.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash on ROCm MI350X fails during weight loading: `ModuleNotFoundError: deep_gemm`; `sgl-deep-gemm` wheel requires `libcudart.so.13`
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug I am trying to serve `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on a **single AMD Instinct MI350X 288GB / gfx950** using SGLang ROCm images. The model reaches weight loading, but then crashes in the DeepSeek-V4 loader because `deep_gemm` is imported during weight post-processing: ```text from deep_gemm import transform_sf_into_required_layout ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'deep_gemm' ``` When I try to install `sgl-deep-gemm`, the package installs, but import fails because the wheel is CUDA-linked and requires `libcudart.so.13`: ```text RuntimeError: Failed to load dynamic shared library .../deep_gemm/_C.so libcudart.so.13: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory ``` This suggests that the ROCm / MI350X DeepSeek-V4 path is still entering a CUDA DeepGEMM dependency path during weight post-processing. I also tried the latest relevant `rocm/sgl-dev` images listed on Docker Hub: <https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/sgl-dev/tags> The same `deep_gemm` import problem appears across the tested images. ### Reproduction ### Model ```text deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash ``` The checkpoint is used as shipped from Hugging Face. No manual quantization is applied. ### Images tested I tried the latest relevant images from the Docker Hub page: <https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/sgl-dev/tags> Including MI35x / ROCm 7.2 / DeepSeek-V4-oriented tags such as: ```text rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0610-dsv4 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260609 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm700-mi35x-20260609 rocm/sgl-dev:rocm720-mi35x-da28108-20260609-DSv4 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260608 rocm/sgl-dev:rocm720-mi35x-da28108-20260608-DSv4 rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0605-fix-2 rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0605-fix ``` I also tried upstream ROCm SGLang images: ```text lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x-20260611 ``` ### Minimal launch command The current launch is single-GPU TP=1: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8002 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --context-length 262144 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --schedule-policy lpm \ --attention-backend triton \ --allow-auto-truncate \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-cache-report \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 ``` I also tested a larger config with: ```bash --context-length 1048576 --max-running-requests 2 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --enable-mixed-chunk --enable-hierarchical-cache ``` but the same error occurs before serving starts. ### Docker Compose fragment ```yaml services: deepseek-v4-flash-mi350x: image: lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x container_name: deepseek-v4-flash-mi350x ipc: host shm_size: "64g" ports: - "8002:8002" devices: - /dev/kfd - /dev/dri group_add: - video - render security_opt: - seccomp:unconfined cap_add: - SYS_PTRACE volumes: - ${HF_HOME:-~/.cache/huggingface}:/root/.cache/huggingface - ./logs:/app/logs - /etc/localtime:/etc/localtime:ro environment: - HF_TOKEN=${HF_TOKEN:-} - PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 - SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 - HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1 entrypoint: ["python3", "-m", "sglang.launch_server"] command: > --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 --trust-remote-code --tp 1 --context-length 262144 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 1 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --schedule-policy lpm --attention-backend triton --allow-auto-truncate --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report --watchdog-timeout 3600 ``` ### Environment [docker-compose.yml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28911924/docker-compose.yml) Driver installation config: https://github.com/bogdannadev/inference-ops/blob/master/rocm/7.2.4_installation_guide.md Host (Digital Ocean's droplet): ```text GPU: 1x AMD Instinct MI350X (VF) VRAM: 288GB Architecture: gfx950 / CDNA4 Host ROCm: 7.2.4 OS: Ubuntu Docker Compose: yes ``` Runtime/container configuration: ```text Devices mounted: /dev/kfd, /dev/dri Groups: video, render Security: seccomp=unconfined Capability: SYS_PTRACE IPC: host SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 ```

signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug When the OpenAI-compatible API receives a chat request with large multimodal data, the server stops responding to all other in-flight and new requests until the current one finishes. In `qwen_vl.py::process_mm_data_async`, three heavy calls run on the asyncio event-loop thread: 1. `self.load_mm_data(...)` — sync, internally blocks on concurrent.futures.Future.result(). 2. `preprocess_video(...)`— declared async but the body is fully sync (frame decode, resize, pin_memory); also processes videos sequentially. 3. `self.process_and_combine_mm_data(...)` — sync HF processor / tokenizer call. These caused API server hang when processing multimodal data. Might related https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23271 ### Reproduction Start a qwen3.5 server and send multiple video understanding requests. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Mar 19 2026, 20:20:58) [GCC 14.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.8, V12.8.61 CUDA Driver Version: 580.95.05 PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu128 sglang: 0.5.10 sglang-kernel: 0.4.1 flashinfer_python: 0.6.7.post3 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.7.post3 flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.5.1 transformers: 5.6.0 torchao: 0.9.0 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.13.5 fastapi: 0.136.0 huggingface_hub: 1.11.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.35.4 orjson: 3.11.8 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.0 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.2 python-multipart: 0.0.26 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.44.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.1.32 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.12.0 anthropic: 0.96.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.9.1 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 NIC0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X PIX 0-15 0 N/A NIC0 PIX X Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks NIC Legend: NIC0: mlx5_0 Hypervisor vendor:: KVM ulimit soft: 1048576 ```

signals.title: [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Add fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold
signals.text: # [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold ## Summary Two NPU-only fused kernels for the LLaDA2.1-mini dLLM JointThreshold decode path on Ascend, replacing per-layer small-op swarms in MoE expert tracking and coreset keep-mask selection with single kernels, behind a runtime flag with a pure-Torch fallback. On GSM8K (n=50) they deliver **+5.14% output throughput at identical accuracy (92.0%)**. This RFC proposes kernel placement and the kernel → release → integration upstream sequence. ## Motivation In the JointThreshold decode loop, two operations run per MoE layer per denoising forward: 1. the history-gate tracker max + EMA update, and 2. the per-call coreset keep-mask selection (softmax-sum score → group-balanced top-q). On NPU these are dispatch-bound: each is a handful of small kernels whose host launch cost dominates their compute, so the device idles between launches. Fusing each path into one kernel removes those launches from the decode critical path without changing the selection semantics. ## Proposed kernels 1. **`moe_gate_max_update`** — fuses the per-expert running-max update and the EMA update into one NPU kernel (replaces a `torch.maximum(...)` + `mul_`/`add_` pair per layer). 2. **`moe_shortlist_mask`** — computes the per-call coreset selection (bf16-rounded softmax-sum score; exact top-q-per-group with lowest-index tie-break, matching `torch.topk(q)`), writes the keep-set, and masks dropped experts, in one HBM round-trip (replaces ~6–10 small vector ops per layer). Both are NPU-only and shape-specialized to the current LLaDA2 MoE (E=256, 8 groups). The Python integration uses them only when enabled; otherwise the existing Torch path runs unchanged. ## Upstream sequence (kernel / release / integration) Kernel source and the SGLang Python caller land as separate PRs because the kernel package is released separately: 1. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Kernel source PR** — add the two ops + bindings + a correctness test. 2. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Release** — a maintainer ships a release containing the new ops. 3. **[sglang] Python integration PR** — env-gated NPU-only call sites with Torch fallback, depending on the sgl-kernel-npu release that contains the ops. Target repos: kernels → `github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu`; Python → `github.com/sgl-project/sglang`. ## Guarded-fallback design (integration PR) The integration is NPU-only and guarded; CUDA/default execution is structurally untouched because the kernels are NPU-only. The call site checks: `device.type == "npu"`, fp32 dtype + contiguity, op availability (`hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "moe_gate_max_update")` / `"moe_shortlist_mask"`), and the runtime flag — otherwise it runs the existing Torch path. The model still loads and serves when the kernels are not present; the Torch path simply runs. ## Evidence GSM8K (n=50), Ascend 910B3, LLaDA2.1-mini, SGLang dLLM JointThreshold. Control runs the identical recipe and runtime-flag stack with the two new kernels off (`TRACKER_MAX_UPD_KERNEL=0`, `PERCALL_KEEP_KERNEL=0`). | Run | Accuracy | Output TPS | Elapsed | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Control (kernels off) | 46/50 = 92.0% | 355.107 | 42.68 s | | + tracker-max-update + coreset-keep kernels | 46/50 = 92.0% | 373.346 | 40.60 s | Δ = **+18.24 tok/s (+5.14%)** at identical accuracy. Next: extend to n ≥ 100 and add a per-op fallback equivalence test. Excluded from this RFC: cbout, maxfold, tracker sum-update, and deferred-flush variants. They were tested locally but were not reproducible release candidates. ## Environment | Component | Version | | --- | --- | | NPU | Ascend 910B3 | | CANN | 9.0.0 (V100R001C10SPC001B250) | | torch / torch_npu | 2.10.0 / 2.10.0 | | dtype / attention / max-running-requests | bfloat16 / ascend / 1 | ## Open questions 1. Should these kernels live under the existing `sgl-kernel-npu` layout, or a dLLM-specific submodule? 2. What is the release/version mechanism for sgl-kernel-npu — how should the integration PR pin the release that contains these ops? ## Reviewers / references NPU backend: @ping1jing2 @iforgetmyname @whybeyoung · DLLM: @ClawSeven @btw616 Style references: #27127 (guarded NPU-only fallback), #21094 (before/after dLLM throughput evidence), #18485 (how-to-run + benchmark evidence), #27144 (concise NPU dLLM PR with GSM8K evidence).

signals.title: [Bug] HiCacheFile file backend: single flat directory causes ENOSPC at scale (millions of cached pages)
signals.text: ## Describe the bug The local file storage backend (`HiCacheFile`, `--hicache-storage-backend file`) writes every cached page as an individual `.bin` file **directly under a single flat directory** (`SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR`). On a long-running single-replica deployment this directory accumulated **~7.5M files**, at which point writes began failing with: ``` OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device: '.../<hash>.bin.tmp...' ``` …even though the filesystem had **~24 TB free and ~456M free inodes** (`df` and `df -i` both healthy). The cause is the **ext4 per-directory index (htree) limit**: a single directory can only index a bounded number of entries, and once that is hit the kernel returns `ENOSPC` regardless of free space/inodes. **Effect:** the L3 (restart-survival) cache tier silently stops persisting new pages (~8.3k failed writes/hour in our logs). Evicted/restarted sessions then miss the prefix cache and pay a full re-prefill. Secondary issue: `batch_exists` / `_collect_existing_component_keys` performs a full `os.scandir(self.file_path)` **per call**, i.e. O(total cached files) — a per-request scan over the entire cache directory at scale. ## Reproduce Run with `--hicache-storage-backend file` and drive enough distinct prefixes that the storage dir accumulates millions of `.bin` files. Writes fail with `ENOSPC` while `df`/`df -i` show ample free space and inodes. ## Environment Latest `main` is affected — `hicache_storage.py` still writes flat (`os.path.join(self.file_path, f"{key}.bin")`), `clear()` uses a one-level `os.listdir`, and `_collect_existing_component_keys` scandirs the whole directory. ## Proposed fix Shard files into 2-level hash-prefix subdirectories (`<ab>/<cd>/<name>.bin`, derived from the leading hex of the filename) so no single directory accumulates unbounded entries, and switch the batch-existence check from a full-dir scandir to per-key `os.path.exists` (O(keys)). PR coming.

signals.title: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (dense, hybrid GDN): intermittent silent decode degeneracy — tiny-output loop + decode-throughput collapse (extra_buffer, A100)
signals.text: ### Describe the bug Serving **`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` (dense, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet)** on a single **A100 80GB**, the server **intermittently** degenerates. It is **non-deterministic on byte-identical input**, **worsens over server uptime**, and **clears on a fresh restart/redeploy**. Two manifestations, both in the same bad windows: 1. **Tiny-output loop.** The model emits a burst of short, non-progressing completions — `completion_tokens` ~80–225 with `reasoning_tokens` collapsed to ~15–90 (vs ~260–690 in healthy completions), every one stopping on `finish_reason {matched: 248046}`, `num_retractions: 0`. An agentic ReAct loop on top of this cannot make progress and hits its recursion limit in ~20–48 s while producing nothing. 2. **Decode-throughput collapse.** A single request's decode drops to **~0.02 tok/s** while the GPU is pinned at **100% util and power-capped** (`clocks_event_reasons.active = 0x4` SW Power Cap, ~304 W vs 72 W idle), with `#running-req: 1`, `full token usage: 0.06`, `mamba usage: 0.03`, `cuda graph: True`. The GPU is busy but our decode does not advance. Crucially, **nothing is logged as an error** — no OOM, no KV-cache retraction, no NaN, no watchdog fire, no traceback, no restart. The model *successfully* returns degenerate output that looks like a normal `stop`. The same prompt that loops in a bad window produces a correct multi-hundred-token answer minutes earlier/later. ### What we ruled out (on the pod) - **GPU hardware:** ECC all-zero (volatile + aggregate SRAM/DRAM), no thermal slowdown, 29–39 °C. - **Server crash / OOM / KV retraction / NaN:** server log clean across hours of uptime; no restart. - **KV / mamba pool pressure:** `full token usage` 0.02–0.13, `mamba usage` ~0.03 (KV pool ~362 K tokens, single request). `num_retractions: 0` throughout. - **#23687 (FP8 weight_scale_inv dropped at load):** does not apply — the checkpoint loads with no `gate_gate_up_proj.weight_scale_inv not found` warnings and produces coherent output in good windows. The combination (GPU pinned 100% + power-capped + ~0.02 tok/s decode + short stop-token-248046 completions, no error) points at the **GDN / mamba decode path** entering a degenerate runtime state, not memory/cache or hardware. ### Reproduction Intermittent, so not reliable on demand. It surfaces under a sustained **agentic / multi-turn workload with long reasoning traces** (thinking enabled), typically within ~30 min of a fresh start; fixed-prompt and short-conversation probes run clean in a *healthy* window (so a one-shot repro proves nothing). We can attach server-side `--log-requests` captures of the degenerate `Finish:` lines + the `Decode batch` throughput-collapse lines + `nvidia-smi` from the moment. ### Environment - SGLang **0.5.13.post1** (official `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image), CUDA 13.x, FlashInfer attn/sampling, xgrammar. - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` (dense hybrid GDN), `max_model_len` 262144, KV bf16. - GPU: 1× **A100 80GB PCIe** (SM80). Shared host (load avg ~16–28 from neighbours). - Launch flags: `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 262144` (radix cache on; no speculative decoding; `disable_piecewise_cuda_graph=True`). ### Questions for maintainers 1. Is this a known GDN/Gated-DeltaNet (or `extra_buffer` mamba-scheduler) decode-path degeneracy on Ampere, and is there a fix on `main` / a dev tag not yet in a released version? 2. Would `--mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer` avoid it? (We use `extra_buffer` specifically to avoid the `no_buffer`+flashinfer SSM-state aliasing / accuracy regression — #20791 — so this is a trade-off, not a clean toggle; `--disable-radix-cache` is rejected with `extra_buffer`.) 3. Any recommended `mamba_ssm_dtype` / `mamba_backend` / `max_mamba_cache_size` setting for stability on A100?

signals.title: [Bug] GLM-5.2-FP8 (DeepSeek-V3.2 / DSA block-fp8) produces wrong output on gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X): aiter gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle is numerically incorrect
signals.text: ## Summary On **gfx950** (MI350X / MI355X), block-fp8 DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture models (validated with **GLM-5.2-FP8**, `glm_moe_dsa`) produce **numerically wrong output**: in-context reasoning is broken (GSM8K accuracy **0.000**, 72% unparseable) even though the server runs without error and simple factual prompts often look fine. Root cause: sglang's block-fp8 linear (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) routes all weight shapes outside a small hard-coded triton allowlist to the aiter **`gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`** CK kernel (with weights preshuffled at load). On this gfx950 + ROCm 7.2 build that kernel is numerically inaccurate — it introduces a small error in **every** linear layer that compounds across all 78 layers. Switching to the plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` kernel (what vLLM uses) fully fixes it. The code already carries a warning about this kernel: ```python # layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:65 # ROCm 7.0 hipcc miscompiles gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle on gfx95 (#23319). _use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = _use_aiter_gfx95 and get_hip_version() >= (7, 2, 0) ``` It is gated to ROCm ≥ 7.2 on the assumption the miscompile is fixed, but it is **still wrong** on ROCm 7.2 / gfx950. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13.post1-rocm720-mi35x` (ROCm 7.2, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` baked in) - HW: AMD MI350X (gfx950), TP=4 - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (block-fp8, 128×128 weight scales) - Flags: `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang` (DSA), `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` (cliff is deterministic in bf16; fp8 KV adds non-determinism but is also wrong) ## Reproduction / evidence Greedy in-context induction prompt — `"The capital of France is Paris. The capital of Germany is"`: - **stock**: `" Paris. The capital of France is Paris..."` (WRONG, deterministic) - vLLM (`rocm/vllm-dev:nightly`, same HW/model/quant, `--linear-backend aiter`): `" Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome..."` (correct) GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot, `few_shot_gsm8k.py`): | | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---| | stock (bpreshuffle) | **0.000** | 0.72 | | plain CK (fix below) | **0.925** | 0.00 | Cross-engine per-layer residual-stream cosine vs vLLM (pos 1) confirms a **gradual, compounding** divergence, not a single bad layer: | layer | 0 | 16 | 32 | 48 | 77 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | stock | 0.96 | 0.96 | 0.89 | 0.53 | **0.10** | | fix | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | **1.00** | Ruled out as causes (all verified correct on stock): DSA indexer top-k selection, RoPE (fused / optimized / native), the absorbed-MLA attention core (`cos = 1.0` vs a torch reference on identical inputs), the `w_kc` absorption GEMM, fp8 activation-quant granularity (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN`). The only thing that fixes it is changing the block-fp8 GEMM kernel. ## Root cause detail `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` (`layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:764`): - gfx950 + ROCm≥7.2 ⇒ `_use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = True` - For shapes **not** in `use_aiter_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned_gfx950` (a 14-entry allowlist) ⇒ kernel = `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, and weights are preshuffled at load (`fp8.py:567`, `shuffle_weight`). - vLLM (`model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/aiter.py: AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`) instead uses `triton_gemm_a8w8_blockscale` (its own tuned allowlist) **or plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`** — never the bpreshuffle variant. So most of GLM-5.2's layers run on a different (and, on gfx950, broken) kernel than vLLM. Scope: **gfx950 only** (`is_gfx95_supported()`); gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) takes `use_triton=True` and is unaffected. ## Fix / workaround One-line correctness fix — disable the bpreshuffle path so block-fp8 falls back to the plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` (and the load-time preshuffle is skipped, since `fp8.py` imports the same flag): ```python # layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:66 _use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = False # was: _use_aiter_gfx95 and get_hip_version() >= (7, 2, 0) ``` With this, GLM-5.2-FP8 on gfx950 matches vLLM: GSM8K 0.925, per-layer cosine ≈ 1.0, and **EAGLE/MTP acceptance recovers to 2.65–3.77** (was ~1.3) — i.e. the bpreshuffle bug was also the cause of the previously-reported poor MTP acceptance on gfx950. Possible upstream resolutions (maintainer call): 1. Disable `bpreshuffle` on gfx950 for correctness until the aiter CK kernel is fixed (perf regression for the shapes where it currently works), or 2. Fix `aiter`'s `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` on gfx950/ROCm 7.2 (the real fix; cf. #23319), or 3. Expand `use_aiter_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned_gfx950` to cover these shapes (route them to the working triton kernel), or 4. Add an env flag to disable bpreshuffle (none currently exists). A correctness gate (option 1/3) is preferable until the kernel is verified, given the severity (silently wrong output, GSM8K 0.0). ## Note There is currently **no runtime flag** to avoid this — it requires a source change — so all current `*-mi35x` images serving block-fp8 DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5.2 on gfx950 are affected.

signals.title: [Feature] Reduce Mamba/GDN verify cache memory overhead in DFLASH speculative decoding
signals.text: Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation DFLASH speculative decoding can introduce a large target-verify cache overhead for hybrid Mamba/GDN models. Today, for a DFLASH verify block of size `D`, the target side keeps intermediate recurrent state snapshots for each draft position. For Mamba/GDN, this is much heavier than ordinary per-token KV cache because each draft position stores a full recurrent SSM state. The intermediate SSM cache is roughly: ```text [num_mamba_layers, num_request_slots, D, recurrent_state_shape...] For a Qwen3Next/Qwen3.5-style GDN model, using: ~36 linear/GDN layers DFLASH block size D = 16 SSM dtype = fp32 conv dtype = bf16 max_running_requests = 48 the extra DFLASH verify cache is approximately: normal Mamba/GDN state per request slot: ~73.7 MiB DFLASH intermediate SSM cache per request slot: ~1152 MiB DFLASH intermediate conv cache per request slot: ~10 MiB total extra per request slot: ~1162 MiB So the full DFLASH intermediate cache is about 15.8x the normal Mamba/GDN state per request slot. Estimated extra cache per GPU: ┌─────────┬───────────────────────────┐ │ TP size │ extra DFLASH verify cache │ ├─────────┼───────────────────────────┤ │ TP=1 │ ~55.6 GiB │ │ TP=2 │ ~27.8 GiB │ │ TP=4 │ ~13.9 GiB │ │ TP=8 │ ~7.0 GiB │ └─────────┴───────────────────────────┘ Most of this comes from intermediate SSM snapshots. If we cache only the first K verify steps and replay/ recompute the accepted tail before commit, the overhead can be reduced substantially: ┌────────────────┬────────────────────────┐ │ cached steps K │ TP=1, 48 request slots │ ├────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 16 │ ~55.6 GiB │ │ 8 │ ~28.1 GiB │ │ 4 │ ~14.3 GiB │ │ 1 │ ~3.9 GiB │ │ 0 │ ~0.5 GiB │ └────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ Related work: - #27658 Feat: add compact linear spec cache replay to reduce intermediate cache memory](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27658) - #26520: GDN MTP cache mode for final-state recompute (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26520) - #28695: GDN ReplaySSM ring spec-verify (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28695) - #28451: ReplaySSM buffered output-only decode for Linear Attention (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28451) Related PR: - #28010: Add DFLASH Mamba/GDN reduced-cache replay (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28010)

signals.title: [Bug] HiCache NIXL L3 cleaner group-key parsing misses hybrid pool suffixes, so eviction is not atomic per logical entry
signals.text: ## Describe the bug The L3 cleaner's design guarantee is that eviction is atomic per logical cache entry: all physical shards of one entry (per-rank files, K/V splits, hybrid pool components) are grouped and deleted together, preserving the cluster-wide all-or-nothing `batch_exists` invariant (`_GroupInfo` docstring, `nixl_cleaner.py:28-37`). `_parse_group_key` (`nixl_cleaner.py:40-55`) only handles two name shapes: - a trailing bare `_k` or `_v` (`_KV_SUFFIXES`, line 23) - a trailing `_{tp_rank}_{tp_size}` (`_RANK_SUFFIX_RE`, line 22) But `_get_hybrid_component_keys` (`hicache_nixl.py:200-219`) generates physical names of the form `{hash}{config_suffix}{component}` where `{component}` is: - `_{pool}_temporal` and `_{pool}_conv_{i}` for Mamba pools - `_{pool}_k` / `_{pool}_v` for two-component pools - `_{pool}_{i}` for other multi-component pools - `_{pool}` for named single-component pools (`_get_component_key`, `hicache_nixl.py:188-193`) None of these strip, and because the component sits after the rank suffix, the rank suffix (anchored with `$`) never strips either. Concrete outcomes for one logical page of a hybrid model with `config_suffix = "_model_0_8"`: ```python _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8") # "page-a_model" (intended group) _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_swa_k") # "page-a_model_0_8_swa" _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_mamba_temporal") # "page-a_model_0_8_mamba_temporal" _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_mamba_conv_0") # "page-a_model_0_8_mamba_conv_0" ``` One logical entry fragments into many "groups": per rank, per pool and (for Mamba) per physical file. ## Impact Under watermark pressure the cleaner deletes fragments independently in mtime order, so a hybrid entry can lose its temporal file while its conv/K/V files survive (or lose rank 3's shard while ranks 0-2 survive). `batch_exists` then reports the entry missing while most of its bytes still occupy disk, which is the worst of both: the space is not reclaimed proportionally and the entry is gone. The grouped-delete design exists precisely to prevent this, and the class docstring's compatibility claim ("MHA, MLA, and DSA naming", `nixl_cleaner.py:75-76`) does not hold for hybrid naming. The existing unit test only covers the bare shapes (`test_hicache_nixl_cleaner.py:43-48`), which is how this slipped through. ## Reproduce CPU-only: the four `_parse_group_key` calls above, or extend `TestHiCacheL3Cleaner` with hybrid names and observe one logical entry spread across multiple `_GroupInfo` groups and deleted partially by `_tick`. ## Proposed fix (happy to send a PR) Options, in my order of preference: 1. **Pass the naming down instead of guessing it back.** `HiCacheNixl` knows its `config_suffix` and the exact component-suffix set it generates; hand both to `HiCacheL3Cleaner` at construction so grouping strips exact known suffixes by construction. New pool types then cannot drift out of sync with the parser. 2. **Extend the parser's stripping rules**: strip a known component tail (`_(k|v|temporal|conv_\d+|\d+)$` then an optional `_{pool}` for pool in the `PoolName` values) before the rank suffix. Smaller diff, but the parser has to chase key-generation changes forever. 3. **Group by hash prefix alone** (`name.split("_", 1)[0]`; hashes are hex and cannot contain `_`). Simplest and future-proof, but it couples eviction across models sharing a mount: same-hash entries of other instances would be evicted together, which has the same shared-mount courtesy problem as #32693. Related: #32693 (unscoped `clear()` on shared mounts) and the tenant-aware L3 directory layout discussed on #26693; a namespaced layout would make both this grouping and scoped clears trivial. ## Environment Found by code inspection on main @ 5f33000; affects any hybrid model (Mamba, SWA, DSA multi-component naming) using `--hicache-storage-backend nixl` with the L3 cleaner enabled.
