signals.title: [Bug][kimi-k3] Long-context [PAD] (id 163839) storms + DSPARK inf/nan asserts — NaN-contaminated logits; released kimi-k3 image predates #32477; pad not stopped/filtered; allowed_special="all" makes [PAD] injectable
signals.text: ## Summary Serving **Kimi-K3** on the `kimi-k3` branch with DSPARK speculative decoding, we observe two recurring production failure modes that we believe share one root cause (transient **NaN contamination of logits**, consistent with the write-side bug fixed by #32477 — which is **not in any released `kimi-k3` image**): - **A. Mid-generation `[PAD]` token storms** — the model suddenly starts emitting the pad token (**id 163839**) as literal `[PAD]` text mid-response (in either the think channel or the content channel) and never stops until `max_tokens` or client disconnect. Worst single stream we captured: **17,256 `[PAD]` occurrences, ~2 MB of SSE, 664 s of decode**. - **B. DSPARK CUDA assert crashes** — sporadic full-engine aborts with `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` (TensorCompare.cu assert) raised from the DSPARK prefill/draft path, killing all TP ranks (auto-recovers after reload). Both are bursty, correlate with **long contexts (≈90k–237k tokens)**, and are invisible in short-context testing. ## Environment - Branch: `kimi-k3` @ `f37baeb52f` source (image lineage `lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729`), SGLang 0.5.16, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0 - Single node, 8× Blackwell-class GPUs (SM10x), TP=8 - Launch (per the Kimi-K3 cookbook, unified recipe): `--tp-size 8 --context-length 1000000 --disable-custom-all-reduce --enable-symm-mem --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-draft-model-path <RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark> --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 --enable-linear-replayssm-spec --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.1 --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 6 --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-write-policy write_back --trust-remote-code` - Weights: official MXFP4 checkpoint (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`), draft `RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark` ## Symptom A in detail — `[PAD]` storms Observed at gateway level over a 48 h window under real agentic traffic (large system prompts, 10–80 tools, 25k–240k-token contexts): **140 storm events in 11 bursts**, hours of complete quiet in between. Channel split: ~70% inside the think channel (`reasoning_content` / thinking deltas), ~30% in visible content. Typical stream shape (chat completions, abridged): ``` data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" evaluating the"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":" user's"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD]"}}]} data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"reasoning_content":"[PAD][PAD][PAD][PAD]..."}}]} # unbounded until max_tokens / disconnect ``` During a storm the engine's own decode logs show **`accept len: 1.00, accept rate: 0.00` for hundreds of consecutive DSPARK batches** — the draft model cannot predict the degenerate distribution, so throughput collapses to non-speculative while burning until `max_tokens` (with `max_tokens=128000` agent requests this is expensive). Impact on agent harnesses is severe: the turn produces thinking + garbage and no tool call / no content, the harness re-prompts, the poisoned long context storms again → retry loop, each cycle re-prefilling ~100k+ tokens. ## Symptom B in detail — DSPARK assert ``` /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel: Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. ... terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' ``` Raised under the DSPARK worker prefill path under long-context load; whole TP group dies (SIGQUIT cascade). ~1 event/day/8-GPU node at our traffic. `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_draft.py` already anticipates exactly this ("an all-NaN row would otherwise make multinomial raise"), so NaN reaching sampling is a known-possible state. ## Why we believe these are the same bug — mechanism chain 1. **#32477 describes the write-side defect**: CUDA-graph padding rows carry undefined K/V yet target the reserved padding slot 0; page-table padding points at that page; a partially valid tile loads the page before masking → `0 × NaN` contaminates attention output. That lands NaN in logits *transiently, depending on batch composition* — matching our "mid-response, one bad step, then normal again" signature. 2. **NaN logits in sampling are UB** — `sanitize_nan_logits()`'s own docstring: NaN logits "can come back as **out-of-vocab token ids**". The guard is **default-off** (`SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=False`). 3. **`[PAD]` = id 163839 = `vocab_size − 1`** — precisely the boundary index a corrupted argmax/top-k walk lands on. (Related precedent: #32396 fixed NaN mis-selection in the EAGLE fused top-k=1 kernel; the AITER greedy path has a comparable guard for all-NaN rows returning `vocab_size`.) 4. The same NaN reaching DSPARK's `torch.multinomial` produces Symptom B. Two exits, one defect. **Cross-validation from production:** we cherry-picked `ee678910f7` (#32477) onto `f37baeb52f` and rolled it out worker-by-worker today. During the partial-rollout window, **every further storm landed on not-yet-patched workers; patched workers have recorded zero storms so far** (early data, hours; we will update this issue with 48 h A/B numbers against the 140-events/48 h baseline). ## Two aggravating factors independent of the root cause **(a) `[PAD]` is not a stop token and is not filtered.** K3's `generation_config.json` only sets `eos_token_id: 163586`; pad 163839 is not in stop ids, and the serving layer must run `skip_special_tokens=False` (the XTML think markers need to survive detokenization). Net effect: one degenerate sample doesn't self-terminate — it streams literal `[PAD]` text to clients unboundedly. A single mis-sampled token becomes a 128k-token incident. **(b) `allowed_special="all"` makes special tokens injectable from user text.** The checkpoint tokenizer (`tokenization_kimi.py`) encodes with `allowed_special="all"`, so a user message *containing the literal string* `[PAD]` tokenizes to the real pad id 163839 (verified). Untrusted input can therefore seed real special tokens into the context — and because storm output that reaches conversation history is replayed on the next turn, there is also a self-contamination loop (later turns imitate the degenerate pattern). ## Suggested actions 1. **Publish a new `kimi-k3` image containing #32477** (current latest `kimi-k3-c6ad1f26-20260729` predates it; the branch HEAD already has it via the main merges). For long-context K3 + DSPARK this appears to be correctness-critical, not just hygiene. 2. **Treat pad as a hard stop / filter for K3 serving**: add 163839 to default stop ids for `kimi_k3` (or drop pad tokens in the detokenizer even when `skip_special_tokens=False`). Either bounds the blast radius of any future sampling corruption to one token. 3. **Consider defaulting `SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS=1`** (or at least recommending it in the K3 cookbook) — with the caveat that for a *fully*-NaN row it converts the failure into a uniform-random sample; a cheap boundary-id guard in the sampling kernels (like #32396 did for EAGLE) may be the better structural fix. 4. **Reconsider `allowed_special="all"` for untrusted chat text** (encode user content with special-token strings escaped), keeping structural tokens injectable only by the chat encoder itself. Happy to provide additional stream captures, decode-log excerpts, or run instrumented builds — and we'll report the post-#32477 A/B numbers here either way.

signals.title: [Bug] sglang 0.5.17 + hierarchical cache + chunked prefill 16K: scheduler hang in DSV4 sparse prefill (watchdog abort) on DeepSeek-V4 FP8 / H20 — plus sampling device-side assert on 0.5.16+PR
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Key launch arguments ``` --tp-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --max-running-requests 64 --page-size 256 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 3.0 --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ (speculative_num_steps=1, speculative_eagle_topk=1, speculative_num_draft_tokens=6) ``` Scheduler init line: ``` max_total_num_tokens=9027840, chunked_prefill_size=16384, max_prefill_tokens=32768, max_running_requests=64, context_len=1048576, available_gpu_mem=17.10 GB DSV4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=9259.90, available_bytes=79.15 GB, full_token=9027840 ``` ## Crash A (0.5.17, primary): scheduler hang -> watchdog abort in DSV4 sparse prefill Timeline on 2026-08-08 (hicache ON, chunked_prefill_size=16384): - 12:28:02 server starts on 0.5.17 - 15:02:37 last batch log (decode batches, ~89.9K full tokens, SWA window active) - 15:08:34 all 8 TP ranks: `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` - 15:08:53 CUDA coredump attempt (`CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP` was not set), 60s wait - 15:09:53 `kill_process_tree` py-spy dump (`--native`) of the scheduler MainThread — identical shape on all ranks: ``` cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda.so.580.95.05) cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart.so.13) at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda (libtorch_cuda.so) at::native::item / at::_ops::item::call torch::autograd::THPVariable_item (libtorch_python.so) build_swa_token_ids (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:241) build (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:333) _forward_prefill_sparse (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1794) forward (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1710) forward (deepseek_v4.py:1287 / 1698 / 2423 / 2615) _execute_extend (runner/eager_runner.py:331) _forward_prefill (dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:412) run_batch (scheduler.py:3594) -> event_loop_overlap -> run_scheduler_process ``` The main thread is blocked in `.item()` inside `build_swa_token_ids`, i.e. `cudaStreamSynchronize` never returns: a kernel enqueued during sparse prefill apparently never completes (device-side hang). The watchdog then aborts all 8 scheduler processes. There is no Python-level exception; the server simply freezes and stops serving. ## Crash B (0.5.16 + PR patches): device-side assert in sampling (NaN/Inf in probs) Observed twice with the same chunked-prefill-16K config: - 2026-08-05 14:15:50, hicache **ON** — preceded by a large prefix-cache hit (`#cached-token: 178176`), matching the signature of issue #33656 (hicache restores target-side KV/SWA but not the DSpark draft-side SWA state -> SWA KV written at wrong positions -> NaN logits). dmesg shows all 8 GPUs raised Xid 43 in cascade. - 2026-08-06 18:02:24, hicache **OFF** — same assert, so the plain radix-cache large-prefix path seems able to trigger it too (or a related SWA/prefix-reuse bug remains). All 8 TP ranks die with: ``` Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. (_assert_async_cuda_kernel, /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109) ... File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 448, in _forward_prefill ctx_lens = torch.tensor(batch.extend_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` (reported asynchronously at the H2D copy; the asserting kernel is multinomial sampling, i.e. the model produced NaN/Inf logits/probs.) Note: the Aug 5 occurrence looks like issue #33656, whose fix (PR #30393) only landed in 0.5.17. The Aug 6 occurrence had hicache disabled, which #33656 does not explain. ## Previously observed, resolved (for completeness, logs omitted) On 0.5.16 + PR patches we also hit a plain CUDA OOM inside deep_gemm `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (~7 GiB transient workspace). It disappeared after lowering `--mem-fraction-static` and has not recurred; we believe it is unrelated to the two failures above. ## Reproduction notes - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ## Questions 1. Any known issue in the DSV4 sparse prefill path (`sparse_prefill_utils.build` / `build_swa_token_ids`) that can deadlock/hang the CUDA stream with chunked prefill 16K + hierarchical cache on 0.5.17 (i.e. *with* PR #30393 included)? The `.item()` sync in the hot path also looks fragile — should this be pre-computed on CPU? 2. Crash B on Aug 6 reproduced with hicache OFF, which issue #33656 / PR #30393 does not cover. Is there another known NaN source in the DSV4 / DSPARK prefix-reuse path (0.5.16 era), and is a fix included in 0.5.17? 3. We are also aware of issue #31023 (compact-verify TP8 + overlap IMA instability); we run the default static ragged-verify mode, so it should not apply — but mentioning it in case it is related to Crash A. Full (sanitized) log excerpts attached: `sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt` [sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30889446/sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt) ### Reproduction - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ### Environment - sglang: **0.5.17** (released 2026-08-08; installed 12:16 and crashed the same day). 0.5.17 includes PR #30393 (HiCache packed/sidecar draft caches, the fix for issue #33656), yet the hang below still occurred with hicache ON. - The two earlier crashes (Aug 5-6) below were on **0.5.16 + local PR patches** (local patches only touch the decode-stage grammar vocab mask; they predate the upstream fix PR #30393). - torch 2.11.0, triton 3.6.0, flashinfer-python 0.6.15.post1, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, sglang-kernel 0.4.5, transformers 5.12.1 - GPU: 8x NVIDIA H20-3e (139.80 GiB each), driver 580.95.05 - Model: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, FP8 weights, KV cache fp8_e4m3, context_len = 1048576 - OS: Linux, Python 3.12

signals.title: [Bug] Two SM10x-gated cluster/tcgen05 kernels fail on B300 (sm_103): cutedsl TGV BF16 GEMM raises Xid 13 CGA "CTA Not Present", trtllm-gen MoE finalize hangs silently
signals.text: Both are reached because `is_sm100_supported()` is a *family* check (`major == 10`), so sm_103 takes SM100-specific paths. Each was identified by name from a CUDA coredump, not inferred. They are separable — happy to split into two issues if preferred — but they share one gate and one diagnostic, so filing together. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8× NVIDIA B30Z, compute capability **(10, 3)** / sm_103 | | Model | Kimi-K3, TP=8, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, decode CUDA graphs on | | sglang | `0.0.0.dev1+g6c7498113` (commit `6c7498113`, 2026-08-07, Kimi-K3 branch) | | torch / driver | 2.13.0+cu130 / 580.159.04 | | flashinfer | 0.6.15.post1, cubin cache verified complete (17372 files, 0 missing) | | workload | offline eval harness, ≤10 concurrent, mixed text and 512×512 images | Everything else is stock: attention backend left unset (auto-selects `trtllm_mla`), `mamba_backend=triton`, CUDA graphs on. I am on a Kimi-K3 branch, so please confirm whether `main` carries the same gating — the code quoted below is from this tree. ## How both were found `kill -9` on a wedged server destroys the evidence, and neither failure prints anything useful on its own. What worked, every time, was reading the CUDA coredump that `--crash-dump-folder` produces: ```bash cuda-gdb -batch -ex "target cudacore core.cuda.<pid>" -ex "info cuda kernels" ``` **The signature: seven ranks hold only a collective kernel and one holds something else. That one is the culprit.** It held for both bugs below. I attributed each from symptoms first and was wrong both times. (Note for anyone reproducing: `cuda-gdb` is often absent, and the conda `cuda-gdb` package ships only the wrapper script — the real `cuda-gdb-minimal` / `cuda-gdb-python3.X-tui` binaries are not in it. The NVIDIA apt `.deb` extracts fine with `dpkg-deb -x`, no system install needed.) --- ## Bug 1 — `TgvGemmCuteExtKernel` (cutedsl BF16 GEMM) faults with Xid 13 ### Symptom All ranks hang forever in `process_batch_result_decode` → `result.copy_done.synchronize()` → `cudaEventSynchronize`, with **zero CUDA errors raised in-process**. SGLang's 300 s watchdog eventually aborts. Twice, on different days and **different GPUs**: | | 2026-08-10 09:55 | 2026-08-10 11:44 | |---|---|---| | 7 ranks holding | `all_reduce_pull_res_kernel` | `all_reduce_pull_res_kernel` | | outlier rank | **device 3**, sm 145 | **device 5**, sm 109 | | outlier kernel | `TgvGemmCuteExtKernel_cta64x16x128_2cta1_pdl1_bias0_tensorptrbf16…` | same | | launch geometry | GridDim (112,1,1), BlockDim (256,1,1), **cluster dim (2,1,1)** | identical | Different GPUs with an identical kernel and geometry rules out one bad board. ### The Xid For the 11:44 crash, the host kernel log has: ``` NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:a7:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 0, TPC 8, SM 1): CTA Not Present ``` `cuda-gdb` reports device 5 as PCI `a7:00.0` — the same device it found holding the kernel. **CGA is the thread-block cluster**, and this kernel launches 2-CTA clusters, so "CTA Not Present" names the launch shape exactly. Worth flagging for others hunting this: dmesg on our host is a ~73 minute ring buffer, so the Xid for the earlier crash was already gone by the time we looked. The coredump is the durable artifact. ### Why it runs on sm_103 ```python # srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:91 if backend_str == "auto" and is_sm100_supported(): backend_str = "cutedsl" ``` ```python # srt/utils/common.py:286 is_sm100_supported = lru_cache(maxsize=1)( partial(_check_cuda_device_version, device_capability_majors=[10], cuda_version=(12, 8)) ) ``` `device_capability_majors=[10]` accepts **any** 10.x, so sm_103 (and sm_110) pass. Measured on this box: ``` torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) -> (10, 3) is_sm100_supported() -> True ``` And the selected kernel is explicitly SM100 two-SM: ```python # kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:149-152 if use_2cta: self.cluster_shape = (2, 1, 1) self.mma_tiler_mn = (cta_m * 2, cta_n) self.cta_group = tcgen05.CtaGroup.TWO self.tma_op = cute_ext.OperationTypeEnum.SM100_TMA_LOAD_2SM ``` 2-CTA clusters and `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` depend on SM-pairing topology, which is not identical between SM100 and SM103. ### Workaround `--bf16-gemm-backend torch`. **No measurable throughput cost** here — aggregate went from 297–610 tok/s (noisy) to 595–666 tok/s, which makes sense since Kimi-K3's compute is dominated by MXFP4 MoE, not unquantized BF16 GEMM. --- ## Bug 2 — `moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernelVecLoad` (trtllm-gen MoE) hangs With Bug 1 worked around, the Xid stopped and a **different** signature appeared after 73 min of serving (2026-08-10 20:35): | rank | resident kernel | |---|---| | device 1–7 | `all_reduce_pull_norm_kernel` — waiting in the collective | | **device 0** | **`moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernelVecLoad`**, GridDim (24,1,1) — never returns | All eight Python stacks in `process_batch_result_**prefill**` → `synchronize` → `cudaEventSynchronize`; SGLang's 300 s watchdog fired and dumped every rank. **No Xid, no CUDA error, nothing in dmesg.** The kernel does not fault, it simply never completes — so without the coredump this is indistinguishable from a scheduler deadlock, and it looks a lot like #26454 while having a different cause. Contrast the two: | | Bug 1 | Bug 2 | |---|---|---| | Xid | 13, CGA / CTA Not Present | **none** | | nature | kernel faults | kernel hangs | | Python frame | `process_batch_result_decode` | `process_batch_result_prefill` | | time to failure | 20 min – 2 h | 73 min and 3 h 07 min | ### Arch coverage `moe_runner_backend=auto` selects `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM10x when the trtllm-gen SiTU cubin pool is present. That pool ships prebuilt binaries, and its sm_103 coverage is thin: | kernel set | sm100f | sm103a | sm103a share | |---|---:|---:|---:| | trtllm-gen **MoE** cubin pool (`20260617_v0613rc1`) | 1636 | 60 | **3%** | | trtllm-gen FMHA cubins | 11248 | 1892 | 14% | flashinfer exposes `gen_cutlass_fused_moe_sm103_module` but only `gen_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_**sm100**_module` — no sm_103 generator for this path. ### Workaround `--moe-runner-backend marlin`, which SGLang's own Kimi-K3 override already suggests (`srt/arg_groups/overrides.py:574`). Marlin is compiled from source in `sgl_kernel` for the local arch and launches no clusters. Measured cost: | | trtllm-gen | marlin | |---|---|---| | single stream (`#running-req: 1`) | ~103 tok/s | ~84 tok/s (−18%) | | aggregate at 9–10 concurrent | ~705 tok/s | ~385 tok/s (−45%) | --- ## Result With `--bf16-gemm-backend torch --moe-runner-backend marlin` and everything else stock: - **11 h+ of continuous serving, zero restarts, zero new Xids**, versus a 20 min – 3 h failure cadence before. - A full 63-configuration benchmark sweep (9 tiers × 7 tasks × 10 trials) completed on it, including image-heavy multi-turn workloads. ## Suggested fix Both kernels look like they want the treatment `cutlass_mla_decode` already gets in this tree — hard-gated to `sm_version == 100` with a comment that half the accuracy tests fail on SM103a (#27384). Concretely: 1. Gate the cutedsl `use_2cta` path (or the whole cutedsl BF16 GEMM) to `sm_version == 100`, falling back to `torch` on sm_103 rather than trapping. 2. Do the same for trtllm-gen MoE selection when no sm_103a cubin exists for the required kernel, falling back to marlin — which the code already knows how to suggest, just not automatically. 3. More generally: `is_sm100_supported()` reads as a capability check but is a family check. Anywhere it guards SM100-specific cluster/tcgen05 features, an exact-arch predicate seems more appropriate. Happy to send a PR for (1) and (2) if the approach sounds right. ## Related - #27384 — sibling tcgen05 kernel already hard-gated to `sm_version == 100` ("On SM103a, half of the accuracy tests are failing"); the ungated sibling traps. - #21904 — any model hangs at high concurrency on (G)B300 (SM103) with TRTLLM attention. - #25564 — flash-attn-4 cute kernel arch check rejects sm_103 (the *opposite* direction: a gate too narrow, where these two are too wide). - #25574 — `topk_transform_512_v2` fused-cluster kernel crashes on B300. - #26454 — frame-identical `copy_done.synchronize()` hang, but GB200/sm_100 and no Xid; likely a different cause from either of these. - #30010 — closest in shape to Bug 2: a MoE kernel (`moeA2ACombineKernel`) deadlocking with all ranks spinning, under CUDA graphs. Different kernel and different configuration, but the same "one MoE kernel never returns and the collective piles up behind it" pattern. - vllm-project/vllm#50880 — independent corroboration outside SGLang: B300 hard hangs under concurrency, and changing the attention backend does not help because it leaves the MoE expert path untouched. I have the coredumps, per-rank py-spy dumps and full server logs for all three crashes and can share whatever is useful.

signals.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 tool call parser fails ~8x/hour in production: TypeError 'string indices must be integers' and json 'unexpected character'
signals.text: ## Describe the bug Running Kimi-K3 with `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3` in production (agentic coding workload, Claude-Code-style tool loop), the tool call parser raises on a significant fraction of model outputs. Over a 24h window with moderate traffic we counted **~190 parser failures**: - 106x `Tool call parsing error: string indices must be integers` (TypeError — a parsed call is indexed like a dict but is a str) - 84x `Tool call parsing error: unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (json.loads on a non-JSON argument payload) - 1x `Tool call parsing error: Input is a zero-length, empty document` Logged from `serving_chat.py` ("Tool call parsing error") — the request then falls back to returning the raw text instead of a structured `tool_calls` entry, so the client sees a turn without tool calls and the agent loop degrades or retries. ## Environment - SGLang 0.5.17-tree, ROCm (8x MI350X, gfx950), `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-strict-thinking`, grammar backend xgrammar - Failures occur both with streaming and non-streaming chat completions ## Analysis `function_call/kimik3_detector.py` extracts calls via `_CALL_RE`/`_ARG_RE` and then: - `json.loads(raw_value)` on each argument value — raises `unexpected character` when the model emits an unquoted/partial value (this is exactly the second error class), and - downstream consumers index `call["name"]`/`call["arguments"]` — the `string indices` TypeError suggests a code path where the parsed call is still a plain string (e.g. malformed/partial `<|open|>call ...` block that the regex only partially matches). ## Expected behavior Malformed tool-call blocks from the model should be handled defensively (skip the malformed call and/or return it as text with a warning), never raise inside the parser. Given Kimi-K3 is explicitly advertised for agentic workloads, hardening this parser has outsized impact — at our traffic every ~7-8 minutes an agent turn silently loses its tool call. ## Reproduction We do not yet have a captured raw failing sample (the error log does not include the payload). We are happy to add debug logging in production and attach concrete failing model outputs if that helps — please tell us the preferred capture point. ## Checklist - [x] Searched existing issues — found tool_call_id-related PRs for kimi-k3 but nothing covering these parser exceptions.

signals.title: [Bug] TypeError in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs during NEXTN TARGET_VERIFY — mamba_next_track_idx is None (hybrid-mamba + speculative decoding + lazy buffer mode)
signals.text: **Env:** SGLang 0.5.14 (pip wheel) · model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 · GPU: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB each) · NEXTN speculative decoding enabled **Crash:** \`TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer\` at \`schedule_batch.py:1594\` in \`set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()\` during TARGET_VERIFY. **Mechanism (from reading v0.5.14 source):** \`Req.mamba_next_track_idx\` initializes to \`None\` (schedule_batch.py:790) and is only assigned in the extend path — an assignment that lazy buffer mode skips (line ~2325, deferring to \`mamba_lazy_prealloc_at_boundary\` in \`prepare_for_decode\`). NEXTN's TARGET_VERIFY builds the track-index tensor (line 1589+) before any decode step has run for a fresh request, so the tensor build receives \`None\`. **Workaround (running stably on my machine):** for req in batch.reqs: if req.mamba_next_track_idx is None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = 0 placed immediately before the torch.tensor build. Zero is the semantically correct initial ping-pong slot per the field's own comment ("0 or 1"). A maintainer may prefer initializing at the source instead. **Context:** the same architectural class (hybrid-recurrent state index reaching a spec-decode kernel unset/unbounded) has three known instances in vLLM (vllm#43559, vllm#50021) — SGLang fails loudly with this TypeError where vLLM's analogues fault in-kernel. Downstream discussion: noonghunna/club-3090#803.

signals.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signals.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [ ] Speculative decoding - [x] MTP https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35161 - [ ] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35058 - [ ] Unified memory
signals.author: ispobock

signals.title: [Bug] EAGLE/NEXTN TP=2 hangs at warmup on Intel XPU after #34238 moved the verify-decision TP broadcast out of the sampling branch
signals.text: ## Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. - [x] Please use English. ## Describe the bug On the **Intel XPU backend**, EAGLE/NEXTN speculative decoding with `--tp 2` intermittently hangs on the first decode step after warmup. The scheduler watchdog fires at 300 s and the server never becomes ready, so the test fails at setup after the 600 s launch timeout. We started seeing this after #34238 ("[AMD] Broadcast the EAGLE greedy verify decision across TP ranks on ROCm", merged 2026-08-15). It is intermittent: on the same commit, one run hung at warmup and a later run of the same command passed (GSM8K 0.920, accept len 3.18). ### Why XPU is newly exposed by #34238 #34238 did not add a new code path — it de-indented the existing TP broadcast in `eagle_sample()` out of the `else:` (sampling / rejection-sampling) branch so it now runs after **both** verify branches: ```python # python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: ... # greedy verify -- XPU ALWAYS lands here else: ... # tree_speculative_sampling_target_only / chain_speculative_sampling_triton # after #34238 this runs for BOTH branches (it used to live inside `else:`) tp_group = get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() if tp_group.world_size > 1: tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` `_is_xpu` is a term in that branch condition, so **XPU can never reach the `else` branch**. These three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238 and now execute on every verify step. NVIDIA is effectively unchanged: the non-greedy path already had them, and the newly-covered all-greedy case is a semantic no-op because NCCL's all-reduce yields bitwise-identical logits on every rank. The newly-live set is ROCm (the intended fix), XPU, NPU, CPU, and CUDA-all-greedy — all at TP > 1. ### Stacks at the hang (`--tp 2`, watchdog dump) **TP1 — active, stuck on a Level Zero device event inside the draft extend that follows verify:** ``` Thread 1012034 (active): "MainThread" sched_yield (libc.so.6) 0x7214ac5fa8ed (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) 0x7214ac5fb768 (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) ur::level_zero::urEventWait (libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0.12.0) compute_spec_mrope_positions (forward_batch_info.py:1131) init_new (forward_batch_info.py:949) prepare_for_draft_extend (eagle_worker_common.py:178) _draft_extend_for_decode (eagle_worker_v2.py:887) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1198) run_batch (scheduler.py:3696) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1803) ``` **TP0 — idle, already past `run_batch`, waiting on the CPU-group request broadcast of the next iteration:** ``` Thread 1012033 (idle): "MainThread" pthread_cond_wait (libc.so.6) c10d::Work::wait (libtorch_cpu.so) broadcast (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3080) broadcast_pyobj (utils/common.py:2406) _broadcast_reqs_across_ranks (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:210) recv_requests (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:93) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1772) ``` Timeline from the log: weights loaded, `max_total_num_tokens=76412`, one warmup `Prefill batch` at 17:33:49, then no further progress; `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` on both ranks at 17:41:12-13. So the stall is on the **first decode/draft-extend step after the first verify** — i.e. immediately after the first `eagle_sample()` call. ### Hypothesis (not yet proven — maintainer input welcome) TP0 has drained and is waiting on the **CPU/gloo** group for requests, while TP1's **XPU device queue** never completes an event. That is the signature of an unmatched or stalled collective on the xccl *device* group leaving TP1's queue blocked, with the visible `urEventWait` being downstream work that can never retire. Relevant: `GroupCoordinator.broadcast()` issues a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` on `self.device_group`. That is exactly the call shape XPU deliberately avoids for all-reduce — `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` routes XPU through the `inplace_all_reduce` custom op, with this comment in `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: > Route through inplace_all_reduce custom op so Dynamo treats this as an opaque call and does not > decompose it into `_c10d_functional` primitives (which invoke `sycl_event.wait()` and break XPU > graph capture). `broadcast()` has no such wrapper, so #34238 introduces three raw eager device-group collectives per verify step on a backend that has an explicit carve-out against them. ### What we have and have not verified - Verified: the hang and the two stacks above, on a commit that contains #34238. - Verified by code reading: the three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238. - **Not** verified: a hang-rate comparison against the parent of #34238. The failure is intermittent (1 hang, 1 pass observed on the same code), so we are still collecting runs and will post the numbers here. Attribution to #34238 is currently based on when we started seeing it plus the code reading above. ### Side issues found while filing this (happy to send PRs) 1. **`python3 -m sglang.check_env` crashes on Intel XPU**, which blocks the required Environment field of this template. `python/sglang/check_env.py` dispatches on `is_cuda_v2/is_hip/is_npu/is_musa/is_mps` with no XPU branch and no `else`, so `env` is never bound: ``` File ".../python/sglang/check_env.py", line 594, in <module> env.check_env() NameError: name 'env' is not defined ``` The Environment section below was therefore collected manually. 2. **`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is silently ignored on XPU.** The `_is_xpu` term forces greedy verify, so the rejection-sampling kernel is never reached even when the flag is set — the test below is named for a path it does not exercise on XPU. ### Candidate fix Smallest XPU-scoped change; restores exactly the pre-#34238 XPU behavior and leaves the ROCm fix intact: ```diff - tp_group = ( - get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() - ) - if tp_group.world_size > 1: - tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) + # XPU opts out: a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` decomposes to `_c10d_functional`, + # whose `sycl_event.wait()` breaks XPU graph capture (why all_reduce takes the + # `inplace_all_reduce` detour). The greedy path never ran this sync on XPU before, + # so skipping it keeps the prior behavior. + if not _is_xpu: + tp_group = ( + get_parallel().attn_tp_group + if is_dp_attention_enabled() + else get_tp_group() + ) + if tp_group.world_size > 1: + tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` If XPU does need the rank-0 sync for the same reason ROCm does, the alternative is to route the broadcast through a custom op the way XPU all-reduce already is, rather than skipping it. Happy to send whichever the maintainers prefer. ## Reproduction Model `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, 2x Intel Arc Pro B60, `--device xpu --tp 2`: ```bash pytest -sv test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_reject_sampling.py::TestQwen35EagleRS::test_a_gsm8k ``` Equivalent standalone server command (taken verbatim from the failing run): ```bash sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code --tp 2 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-rejection-sampling \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache \ --device xpu --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 ``` Effective server args from the hanging run: `attention_backend='triton'`, `cuda_graph_config` decode=`disabled` prefill=`disabled` (no graph capture involved), `page_size=1`, `disable_radix_cache=True`, `speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True`, `enable_dp_attention=False`, `watchdog_timeout=300`, `disable_overlap_schedule=False`. The hang reproduces before the GSM8K workload starts, during server warmup, so no eval data is needed to trigger it. ## Environment Collected manually because `python3 -m sglang.check_env` raises `NameError` on XPU (see side issue 1 above). ``` sglang: 0.5.18.dev687 (source checkout containing #34238) python: 3.12.13 os: Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 torch: 2.12.0+xpu xccl: available (torch.distributed.is_xccl_available() == True) ipex: not installed oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch: not installed xpu devices: 8x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, 24 GB each, driver 1.14.36300+8 (this repro uses 2 of them via --tp 2) ``` cc @JessicaJiang-123 @XinyuJiangCMU (authors of #34238), @Ying1123 @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @Qiaolin-Yu (CODEOWNERS for `python/sglang/srt/speculative`)

signals.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8 DSpark forced-reject is not lossless: accumulated GDN state drift vs Base decode
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Summary With RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark, I can reproduce a deterministic correctness divergence between ordinary Base decode and DSpark TARGET_VERIFY even when every speculative draft token is deliberately rejected and only the target model's own argmax token is committed. The failure is cumulative rather than context-local: Base decode is deterministic across independent processes with a fixed seed. Under gamma=1 forced rejection, DSpark initially matches Base but later diverges. Rebuilding the same prefix through normal prefill restores the correct Base result at the divergence context. Using FP32 Mamba/SSM persistent state delays the divergence substantially, but does not eliminate it. This suggests accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift somewhere in the TARGET_VERIFY / intermediate-state / commit path. Possibly related to the state-correctness work tracked in #34899 and #34297. Environment SGLang: SGLANG_BUILD_COMMIT=c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5 SGLANG_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260814-c4271c3f CUDA 13.0 TP=1 attention backend=triton linear attention backend=triton Target model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 revision: 52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854 Draft model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark revision: 923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda Diagnostic configuration: max_running_requests=1 gamma=1 verify_num_draft_tokens=2 SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static CUDA graph disabled prefill CUDA graph disabled seed=123456789 Triton GDN backend Model weights are not modified. Forced-rejection diagnostic SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 by itself is not a semantically valid forced-rejection test because it changes correct_len without recomputing the naturally selected target bonus token. For gamma=1 I therefore used this local diagnostic patch in dspark_verify.py: if self._simulate_acc_len > 0: - correct_len = self._simulated_correct_len( - bs=bs, dtype=correct_len.dtype, device=correct_len.device + target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( + bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens ) + correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) + bonus = target_predict[:, 0] + cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) The resulting request reports: spec_accept_rate=0.0 spec_num_correct_drafts=0 spec_num_proposed_drafts=95 spec_verify_ct=95 spec_accept_histogram=[95] Thus every first draft is rejected and the committed output token is the target model's own argmax. Exact request The same exact 24 input_ids are used for every run: INPUT_IDS = [ 248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11, 10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271, ] Input verification: count: 24 SHA256: f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0 The SHA256 is computed as: hashlib.sha256( ",".join(map(str, INPUT_IDS)).encode() ).hexdigest() Sampling: temperature: 0 top_p: 1 top_k: -1 max_new_tokens: 96 ignore_eos: true Example request: payload = { "input_ids": INPUT_IDS, "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "top_k": -1, "max_new_tokens": 96, "ignore_eos": True, }, "stream": False, } Server configuration Relevant arguments: sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 16384 \ --max-total-tokens 16384 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --random-seed 123456789 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 Environment: SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 For the FP32-state diagnostic I additionally use: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 Results 1. Base oracle is deterministic Base-only greedy decode is deterministic across independent server processes with seed 123456789. Original BF16 Base oracle SHA256: a935dafc6111c5acf3280bb9fa1d545f39abf5c9ba92285ba29d39949e971848 2. Original TARGET_VERIFY + forced rejection With gamma=1, static verify, CUDA graph disabled, and the forced-rejection diagnostic: first divergence: output index 13 Base token: 1070 DSpark token: 836 Indices 0..12 match Base. 3. Concrete beta precision mismatch One concrete numerical difference exists between Base packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY. Base rounds beta through the beta tensor's source dtype, while TARGET_VERIFY originally keeps the sigmoid computation in FP32. Diagnostic patch: - b_beta = 1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-b_b)) + b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) With only this change: first divergence: 13 -> 23 Indices 0..22 now match Base. This appears to be a real numerical contributor, but not the complete cause. 4. Fresh-prefix localization Using the beta-aligned path, I rebuilt a fresh request consisting of: original input IDs + exact Base output IDs [0:22] No text was retokenized. The request reported: cached_tokens=0 Expected next Base tokens: [2438, 5306] Generated: [2438, 5306] Exact match. Therefore the long-request divergence at index 23 is not a direct TARGET_VERIFY failure at that context when recurrent state is freshly rebuilt through ordinary prefill. It requires accumulated speculative-state evolution. 5. FP32 persistent SSM state Using the same beta alignment but changing both Base and DSpark to: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 results are: FP32 Base SHA256: 5557ae475bafcb00ff5ea564e14954f5590cf8e77535edec878a7203225561fc FP32 DSpark SHA256: a982aa8b26b5e7f51d11669da7b42a730d839d721d0d386944c3a964321a2fcb first divergence: index 38 Base token: 6338 DSpark token: 2279 So increasing persistent SSM precision changes: BF16 SSM + beta alignment: index 23 FP32 SSM + beta alignment: index 38 but does not eliminate the divergence. This suggests BF16 persistent-state storage is an error amplifier rather than the sole root cause. 6. KV precision control With FP32 SSM and beta alignment, changing target KV cache from FP8 E4M3 to BF16 moved first divergence only: 38 -> 39 This suggests full-attention KV precision is not the primary cause of the remaining drift. Other isolation work Delta reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's delta projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation did not improve correctness: beta + Base-layout delta projection: first divergence = 6 Output reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's output projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation also regressed: beta + Base-layout output projection: first divergence = 6 Softplus expression TARGET_VERIFY originally evaluates: beta_x = softplus_beta * x softplus_x = tl.where( beta_x <= softplus_threshold, (1.0 / softplus_beta) * tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(beta_x)), x, ) Runtime parameters were confirmed as: softplus_beta=1.0 softplus_threshold=20.0 Changing only this expression to Base's literal form: softplus_x = tl.where( x <= 20, tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(x)), x, ) regressed the FP32 test: first divergence: 38 -> 6 Because the two forms are algebraically equivalent for the actual runtime parameters, this appears to demonstrate sensitivity to Triton floating-point/codegen behavior rather than identify the root cause. Convolution state A source audit found persistent conv state and TARGET_VERIFY intermediate conv windows use the same default BF16 dtype and the expected post-anchor snapshot/scatter semantics for gamma=1. Attempting the independent diagnostic: SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float32 cannot currently be used as a clean control because the current implementation hits: RuntimeError: Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match, got Float for the destination and BFloat16 for the source. ReplaySSM The current build exposes: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec but DSPARK/DFLASH explicitly rejects this path for Qwen3.8 GDN: ValueError: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires a KDA (kimi_linear) model; got a non-KDA model. So I could not use ReplaySSM as a GDN DSPARK correctness control. Current hypothesis The strongest evidence is: forced reject + repeated TARGET_VERIFY rounds -> divergence fresh prefill of the exact same prefix -> correct again higher persistent SSM precision -> divergence substantially delayed KV precision change -> almost no effect My current hypothesis is that a small difference enters a committed/intermediate GDN recurrent state during repeated TARGET_VERIFY reject/commit rounds and accumulates until it changes the target argmax. For gamma=1, I also audited the reject/commit indexing: candidate row 0 = anchor/current token commit_lens = 1 last_correct_step_indices = 0 and the committed conv window appears to correspond to the post-anchor state as expected. The remaining high-value localization would therefore seem to be the SSM state boundary rather than further source-expression A/B tests. Expected behavior Under this diagnostic every speculative draft token is rejected and only the target model's own greedy token is committed. I would expect DSpark to preserve the same greedy token sequence as ordinary Base decode. If exact Base equivalence is intentionally not guaranteed for GDN TARGET_VERIFY because the recurrent numerical paths differ, clarification on the intended correctness invariant/tolerance would also be useful. Questions Is this accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift a known limitation or bug in the current DSpark TARGET_VERIFY path? Is there an existing GDN state-commit / TARGET_VERIFY correctness patch that should be tested on this Qwen3.8 path? Would the most useful next instrumentation be a per-layer/per-round comparison of: Base persistent SSM state before decode TARGET_VERIFY input persistent SSM state TARGET_VERIFY intermediate step-0 SSM state post-commit/scatter persistent SSM state Is the beta source-dtype rounding difference described above expected, or should TARGET_VERIFY match Base packed decode here? If exact Base equivalence is not expected between packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY, what correctness invariant should speculative decoding enforce for recurrent GDN models? I can provide the exact request script, complete Base/DSpark output token arrays, hashes, and the small diagnostic source patches if useful. ### Reproduction Models: Target: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` revision `52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854` Draft: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` revision `923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda` Server configuration: ```bash export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 16384 \ --max-total-tokens 16384 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --mm-feature-transport cpu \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --random-seed 123456789 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 For the forced-rejection diagnostic, I locally changed the SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN branch in dspark_verify.py so that gamma=1 always rejects the draft but commits the target model's own argmax: target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens ) correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) bonus = target_predict[:, 0] cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) I also tested the following beta precision alignment in fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py: b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) Exact request: INPUT_IDS = [ 248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11, 10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271, ] payload = { "input_ids": INPUT_IDS, "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "top_k": -1, "max_new_tokens": 96, "ignore_eos": True, }, "stream": False, } Input SHA256: f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0 With FP32 SSM + beta alignment + forced rejection, Base and DSpark match through output index 37 and first diverge at index 38: Base token: 6338 DSpark token: 2279 Rebuilding the exact same prefix through ordinary prefill restores the correct Base continuation, indicating accumulated recurrent-state drift. ### Environment /sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/environ.py:1402: UserWarning: Environment variable SGLANG_FLASHINFER_PR4266_SOURCE has been deprecated. warnings.warn(f"Environment variable {old_name} has been deprecated.") Calling register_constant() on Enum subclasses is deprecated and will be an error in a future release. Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 610.88 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1 flashinfer_python: 0.6.18 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.18.dev20260807 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.18.dev20260807+cu130 triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu130 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.39.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.3 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.52.3 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.122.0 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.15.0+cu130 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks Hypervisor vendor:: Microsoft ulimit soft: 1024

signals.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signals.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices

signals.title: [Bug] Radix cache `evictable_size()` double-counts shared pages, killing the scheduler at idle
signals.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Surfaced while investigating a KV accounting report from @ApsarasX on #32992; the check there fails for the same reason but is unrelated to that PR's fix. With radix cache enabled, the idle pool-invariant check in `on_idle()` fails and raises, killing the scheduler. All requests complete successfully first — the server dies the next time it goes idle. ``` ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=469952, available=96, evictable=470016, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0 ``` `96 + 470016 = 470112`, i.e. **+160 tokens (5 pages) more than the pool holds**. This is not a debug-only path: `SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_IDLE` defaults to `True`, and `_check_all_pools()` in `on_idle()` is not env-gated, so the default configuration raises. No `SGLANG_*` variables were set in the runs below. ## It is a counting bug, not a leak I instrumented `on_idle()` to walk the radix tree, collect every page referenced by a tree node, and intersect that set with the allocator's free list: ``` [PROBE] tree_nodes=14687 tree_pages=14683 free_pages=3 OVERLAP(tree AND free)=0 ``` - Physical pages balance exactly: `14683 + 3 = 14686 = 469952 / 32`. - `OVERLAP=0` — no page is simultaneously free and referenced by the tree, so there is no use-after-free and no risk of serving stale KV. - But `evictable` reports `470016` tokens = 14688 pages' worth, while the tree references only **14683 distinct pages**. Five pages are counted more than once, which is exactly the `+160`. So `evictable_size()` appears to count per node reference rather than per distinct page, while `total` is a per-page quantity. Nothing leaks and nothing is corrupted; the invariant compares two different units. `--disable-radix-cache` makes the check pass and the run complete cleanly. ## Scope of what I verified - Reproduced on **Ascend NPU with a dLLM model** (LLaDA2.1-mini, `JointThreshold`), TP=1 and, per @ApsarasX, TP=8 with LLaDA2.1-flash. - **It appears specific to the dLLM path, not to paged radix in general.** Qwen3-8B (autoregressive) on the same hardware with the same workload and an explicit `--page-size 32` and radix on completes cleanly — `Successful requests: 256`, no idle assertion. One model and one workload, so not conclusive, but it is a real negative control. - **`page_size > 1` is not NPU-specific here.** `_dllm_page_size` in `arg_groups/overrides.py` forces `page_size = dllm block_size` (32) whenever a dLLM algorithm is selected and radix cache is on, with no device predicate — so a CUDA dLLM run should land on the same code path. I have no GPU available to confirm this, so it is a code-reading claim, not a measurement. - I have **not** tested SWA / mamba caches. - I have not found *why* those pages end up with multiple tree references — only that the duplication is on the counting side, not on page ownership. ### Reproduction Reproduced on `4f51dad1da` (2026-07-30) and `d6c837489a` (2026-08-18) with the **identical** `+160` — 926 commits apart, so it is deterministic and long-standing. In that window `invariant_checker.py` changed only by a refactor (`server_args` → `get_parallel()`) and `radix_cache.py` has no `evictable_size` changes. ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <LLaDA2.1-mini> --trust-remote-code \ --device npu --attention-backend ascend --dllm-algorithm JointThreshold \ --tp-size 1 --max-running-requests 64 --enable-tokenizer-batch-encode \ --disable-overlap-schedule --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode full \ --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 12 16 24 32 48 64 --port 31099 python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --port 31099 \ --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix --gsp-num-groups 1 --gsp-prompts-per-group 256 \ --gsp-system-prompt-len 0 --gsp-question-len 4096 --gsp-output-len 1536 \ --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 64 --flush-cache ``` All 256 requests succeed (`0` request errors), then the scheduler raises at idle. `--gsp-question-len 4096` is page-aligned; the correlation with page-aligned prompt lengths was first noticed by @ApsarasX in #32992, where a TP=8 LLaDA2.1-flash run showed `+224` = 7 pages against exactly 7 page-aligned prompts in the dataset. ### Environment - Ascend 910B3, `aarch64`, Ubuntu 22.04 - page_size resolves to 32: not passed on the command line — the NPU default is 128 (hardware_backend/npu/utils.py), and _dllm_page_size knocks it down to the dLLM block size. On CUDA the default is 1 and the same override raises it to 32, which is why this should not be NPU-specific. - Model: LLaDA2.1-mini

signals.title: [Feature] Batched Candidate-Trajectory Ensembling for Stochastic Action Generation
signals.text:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Add a first-class, opt-in execution contract for generating multiple independent action trajectories from one conditioning context, executing the candidates as one physical batch, and reducing them to one served action result. SGLang Diffusion already has most of the lower-level pieces: - `Req.num_outputs_per_prompt` represents multiple outputs; - latent preparation preserves per-request RNG streams and batches the deterministic packing/scaling work; - pipeline stages can expand shared conditioning to the sample batch; and - Cosmos3 is implemented as a composed pipeline with explicit latent, timestep, denoising, action, and decode stages. What is missing is a model/runtime contract that says these outputs are *candidates for one logical prediction*, not independent public media outputs. Without that distinction, a world-action model has to implement sequential sampling or ad hoc aggregation inside model code, and the runtime cannot preserve candidate identity, enforce RNG independence, or measure the benefit of batching. This proposal is intentionally narrow. It does not propose averaging images or videos, and it does not change default `num_outputs_per_prompt` behavior. It adds an opt-in path for models whose public action output has a validated candidate reducer. #### Proposed execution contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateTrajectorySpec: count: int = 1 reducer: str = "none" # "none", "mean", or a registered model reducer return_candidates: bool = False seed_policy: str = "per_candidate" @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateGroup: request_id: str candidate_ids: tuple[int, ...] public_output: str = "action" ``` The model/pipeline adapter would declare: 1. which tensor is the candidate action trajectory; 2. whether reduction occurs before or after denormalization; 3. the supported reducer and output dtype/shape; 4. which conditioning tensors are candidate-invariant; and 5. whether video or another auxiliary branch must execute for action correctness. The runtime owns grouping, candidate identity, batching, failure handling, observability, and final response construction. The model owns the mathematical reduction rule. #### Request and execution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Req["One logical request
conditioning + candidate count N"] Validate["Validate model capability
and candidate contract"] Seeds["Create N independent
request-owned RNG streams"] Shared["Compute candidate-invariant
conditioning once"] Expand["Expand/fan out conditioning
and build candidate batch"] Denoise["One batched denoising path
candidate axis = N"] Action["Model-specific action
postprocessing"] Reduce["Validated reducer
mean or registered reducer"] Resp["One public action result
optional raw candidates"] Req --> Validate --> Seeds --> Shared --> Expand --> Denoise --> Action --> Reduce --> Resp ``` #### RNG and equivalence rules Candidate batching must not collapse stochastic independence or silently change seed semantics. - Candidate `i` receives a stable stream derived from `(base_seed, i)` or an explicitly supplied generator. - `count=1` must preserve the current output exactly. - For a fixed candidate seed list, batched execution must produce the same candidate set as the sequential reference under the model's declared equivalence rule. - Candidate ordering is stable across dynamic batching and output slicing. - Retry/fallback may rerun the whole group, but must not reuse a partially advanced generator as though it were fresh. The existing grouped latent-preparation logic is a useful precedent: it already draws request-owned random latents separately and only batches deterministic work afterward. The candidate path should retain the same property. #### Scheduler and batching behavior Phase 1 should admit a candidate group atomically when it fits the configured execution batch. If it does not fit, the runtime should fail clearly or use a documented sequential fallback; it should not silently truncate the group. A later phase may split candidates into microbatches and aggregate when all slices finish, but the request state must then track: - candidate IDs completed/pending; - seed/generator state per candidate; - partial reducer state; and - cancellation semantics for the entire logical request. Candidate-invariant conditioning should be encoded once where the stage contract permits it. An adapter may use an expanded view or an explicit attention fan-out; physical tensor replication is not required by this RFC. #### Integration points Suggested initial ownership: - request fields and validation: diffusion sampling/request data; - group identity and completion: request/scheduler state; - independent raw noise: `LatentPreparationStage`; - conditioning expansion: pipeline configuration's existing sample-batch expansion hook; - candidate reducer: a small action-output capability implemented by opt-in world-model pipelines; - metrics: candidate count, physical forwards, fallback reason, reducer time, and action-only branch time. The first model integration could be Cosmos3 action generation because SGLang already has an explicit Cosmos3 composed pipeline. The framework abstraction should not contain Cosmos-specific tensor names. #### Correctness and quality gates Required tests: 1. `count=1` is identical to the existing path. 2. Fixed per-candidate seeds produce the same ordered candidate tensors in sequential and batched modes. 3. The reduced action matches a standalone reducer applied to captured candidate tensors. 4. Candidate IDs remain stable when unrelated requests are co-batched. 5. CFG serial and CFG-parallel paths preserve candidate membership. 6. TP/SP output reconstruction happens before reduction when the action tensor is sharded. 7. Cancellation and one-candidate failure do not return a partial aggregate as a valid result. 8. Auxiliary video decode can be skipped only when the model declares it irrelevant to the action output. Quality validation must be model-specific. The framework should report candidate-level and reduced-output artifacts but should not hard-code a universal action metric or assume that a larger candidate count always improves quality. #### Benchmark plan Report, for `N in {1, 2, 4, 8, 10}`: - sequential reference latency; - batched latency and peak memory; - number of physical transformer forwards; - conditioning encode time; - candidate-reduction time; - candidate tensor parity under fixed seeds; and - model-declared action-quality metrics. Benchmark at more than one parallel topology. Wider TP may help the larger candidate batch while regressing `N=1`; the RFC should not encode one topology as universally optimal. #### Alternatives considered - **Keep aggregation in application code.** This forces repeated RPCs or model-specific server loops and prevents the runtime from preserving one logical request/candidate group. - **Treat candidates as ordinary independent outputs.** This loses the reduction contract and makes failure/cancellation semantics ambiguous. - **Always expose raw candidates.** This moves a model-system accuracy feature into every client and expands the public payload unnecessarily. - **Average videos/latents generically.** Out of scope and not semantically valid for this proposal. #### Rollout 1. Land internal types and validation with no model enabled. 2. Add a Cosmos3 action adapter and sequential-equivalence tests. 3. Add atomic candidate-group scheduling and metrics. 4. Benchmark before enabling any default. 5. Consider microbatching and additional reducers only after the initial contract is stable. ### Related resources - Cosmos3 composed pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - Latent preparation and per-request RNG handling: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/latent_preparation.py - Diffusion denoising stage and sample-batch expansion: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - vLLM-Omni request-selected output routing RFC (complementary output-branch contract): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6302
