signals.title: Add fmha_v2 attention backend for SM90/120
signals.text: ## Motivation Enables TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 prefill attention backend for SM90/120. This backend is more performant than the current default (FA3), and also enables skip-softmax feature, which can further boost performance for long-context / applications where attention output is sparse. ## Modifications Baseline enablement of trtllm's fmha_v2 prefill kernel for SM90/120. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 is needed for further perf improvement, and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32268 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32269 are used for the MTP accuracy reporting. ## Accuracy Tests ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /SGL/models/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8 \ --tp 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --disable-radix-cache --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --attention-backend trtllm_mha \ --trust-remote-code --port 30000 # --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ``` | Config | KV dtype | Score | Repeat range | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 | bf16 | 0.725 | 0.712-0.742 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | bf16 | 0.723 | 0.702-0.753 | | FA3 + MTP | bf16 | 0.734 | 0.712-0.758 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (fa3 verify) | bf16 | 0.721 | 0.707-0.732 | | FA3 | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.727 | 0.707-0.747 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.724 | 0.682-0.753 | ### MTP Add to server launch: `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | Config | Accept len | Accept rate | GPQA-20 score | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 + MTP (bf16) | 2.37 (2.35) | 0.46 (0.45) | 0.750 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (bf16) | 2.45 (2.30) | 0.48 (0.43) | 0.700 | | pure trtllm_mha + MTP w/ XQA mask fix (bf16, 10q) | 2.20 | 0.40 | 0.70 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The e2e performance is not improved with just this PR because it requires a large copy operation before the compute kernel to interleave KV. https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3575 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 address this issue. Unit Kernel Measurements show ~15% improvement over FA3 over a variety of problem sizes, reaching 20% at small problems. ### Skip-Softmax This feature can provide additional speedup, especially for long-context inference where the attention logits are sparse. We define the threshold factor `\lambda := a / L` where a is a hyperparameter, and L is the sequence length. To demonstrate the potential speedup, we keep a = 1000 here for simplicity. | ISL | Effective threshold (1000 / ISL) | bf16 gain | fp8 gain | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k | 0.122 | +1.8% | +0.2% | | 32k | 0.031 | +5.2% | +1.7% | | 128k | 0.008 | +12.9% | + 3.5% | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: fix: guard self.model access in Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights
signals.text: Fixes #23063 ## Problem When launching a Qwen3-VL-MoE model in `--encoder-only` mode, the server crashes during weight loading with `AttributeError: 'Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration' object has no attribute 'model'`. In encoder-only mode, `self.model` is not initialized by the parent class (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.__init__` only sets `self.model` when `config.encoder_only` is `False`). However, `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` unconditionally accessed `self.model` in: ```python and hasattr(self.model, "start_layer") ``` Python evaluates `self.model` before `hasattr` can handle the missing attribute, causing the crash. ## Solution Add `hasattr(self, "model")` check before accessing `self.model`, matching the pattern already used in the parent class `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` in `qwen3_vl.py` (line 1322): ```python and hasattr(self, "model") and hasattr(self.model, "start_layer") ``` ## Testing The fix is minimal (1 line added) and directly mirrors the existing guard pattern in the parent class. Encoder-only mode now safely skips the `start_layer`/`end_layer` layer-skipping logic when no language model is initialized, while normal (non-encoder-only) mode is unaffected.

signals.title: [Docs] Move imports to their first-use cells across tutorial notebooks
signals.text: ## Motivation Several tutorial notebooks import utilities such as `terminate_process` and `print_highlight` in the server-launch cell, even though these functions are only used in later cells. This causes `NameError` when users execute cells in isolation (e.g., during debugging or when copying a specific section into a standalone script), and reduces readability by placing imports far from their actual usage. ## Modifications Moved `terminate_process` and `print_highlight` imports to the cell where each function is first used, across the following notebooks: - `docs/basic_usage/send_request.ipynb` - `docs/advanced_features/lora.ipynb` - `docs/advanced_features/separate_reasoning.ipynb` - (other affected notebooks) No logic or API changes. signals.title: feat: add KV cache CPU backup for sleep/wakeup radix tree preservation
signals.text: Add --enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup flag that preserves the prefix cache radix tree across sleep/wakeup cycles. Changes: - server_args.py: new --enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup flag with validation - radix_cache.py: export_snapshot() and import_snapshot() methods (iterative DFS to avoid recursion limit on large trees) - scheduler_update_weights_mixin.py: snapshot before pause(), restore after resume(); pre-flight CPU memory check (hard reject at 1.2x safety margin, soft warning at 1.5x); graceful exit on insufficient memory via ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput(success=False, message=...) - memory_pool.py: enable_kv_cpu_backup param threaded through KVCache and all subclasses (MHA, MLA, NSA, DoubleSparse, HybridLinear, HiSparseNSA) - model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py: pass enable_kv_cpu_backup in all pool creation calls - io_struct.py: ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput gains success/message fields for graceful failure reporting - test/srt/test_kv_cache_cpu_backup.py: complete test suite (313 lines) ## Motivation During sleep/wakeup cycles (e.g., `release_memory_occupation` / `resume_memory_occupation` for weight updates like RLHF), the KV cache radix tree is flushed, causing prefix cache hits to be lost after wakeup. This forces full prefill for all subsequent requests, degrading performance. This PR adds `--enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup` which preserves the prefix cache radix tree across sleep/wakeup cycles by serializing it before `pause()` and restoring it after `resume()`, enabling prefix cache hits to work immediately after wakeup without re-prefill. ## Modifications ### Core feature - **`radix_cache.py`**: Added `export_snapshot()` (iterative DFS to avoid recursion limits on deep trees) and `import_snapshot()` methods for serializing/deserializing the radix tree topology and slot assignments. Comprehensive error handling with descriptive messages for node rebuild failures, topology wiring errors, and allocator free-list restoration failures. - **`scheduler_update_weights_mixin.py`**: On `release_memory_occupation`, snapshots the radix tree before `pause()`. On `resume_memory_occupation`, restores it after `resume()`. Also added a pre-flight CPU memory check: hard reject at 1.2x safety margin, soft warning at 1.5x, preventing `cudaMallocHost` OOM kills. - **`io_struct.py`**: `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput` gains `success: bool` and `message: str` fields for graceful failure reporting. - **`memory_pool.py`**: Threaded `enable_kv_cpu_backup` through `KVCache` base class and all subclasses (`MHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolFP4`, `MLATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4`, `NSATokenToKVPool`, `DoubleSparseTokenToKVPool`, `HybridLinearKVPool`, `HybridReqToTokenPool`). Each `_create_buffers()` passes `enable_cpu_backup=self.enable_kv_cpu_backup` to `memory_saver_adapter.region()`. - **`hisparse_memory_pool.py`**: `HiSparseNSATokenToKVPool` passes `enable_kv_cpu_backup` to parent. - **`model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py`**: Propagates `enable_kv_cpu_backup` to all KV pool creation calls across all cache backends. - **`server_args.py`**: Added `--enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup` flag with validation: requires `--enable-memory-saver` and is incompatible with `--disable-radix-cache`. - **Container-aware memory check**: `_get_container_available_memory_bytes()` reads cgroup v2/v1 memory limits first (correct for Docker/K8s), falling back to `psutil.virtual_memory().available` for non-containerized hosts. ### Tests - **`test/srt/test_kv_cache_cpu_backup.py`**: Complete test suite (313 lines) covering: - Unit tests: empty tree export, snapshot round-trip, prefix match after restore, allocator free-list update, disabled/empty snapshot handling. - Integration tests: basic sleep/wakeup correctness (output consistency, GPU memory drop/recovery), prefix cache restoration (cached_tokens > 0 after wakeup). ## Accuracy Tests - **Output consistency**: Verified that generation output before sleep matches output after wakeup across multiple cycles (TP=1 and TP=2). - **Prefix cache restoration**: Verified that `cached_tokens > 0` after wakeup, confirming the radix tree snapshot is correctly restored and prefix cache hits fire. - **Radix tree integrity**: Unit tests confirm `total_size()` and `match_prefix()` results are identical before/after snapshot round-trip. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Sleep/Wakeup Timing (Qwen3-32B, NVIDIA A100, TP=1) | Metric | First cycle | Subsequent cycles | |--------|------------|-------------------| | Sleep (KV only) | ~2.1s | ~0.9s | | Wakeup (KV only) | ~0.36s | ~0.35s | | Sleep (KV + Weight) | ~24s | ~9.5s | | Wakeup (KV + Weight) | ~3.85s | ~3.85s | ### Sleep/Wakeup Timing (Qwen3-32B, NVIDIA A100, TP=2) | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | Sleep (KV + Weight) | ~32.5s | | Wakeup (KV + Weight) | ~3.9s | ### Stability - 10× consecutive sleep/wakeup cycle test passed with no crashes, no memory leaks, and consistent generation output across all cycles. - Pre-flight memory check correctly rejects release requests when available CPU memory is below 1.2x the required pinned memory size, preventing process kills from `cudaMallocHost` failures - signals.title: Fix double-reduce in DeepseekV2MoE with flashinfer_cutedsl + EP + DP-attention
signals.text: ## Motivation Running `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-NVFP4` with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --enable-dp-attention --ep-size N --dp-size N` (N>1) hit two separate bugs. **Bug 1 — double-reduce on MoE output.** Pure TP and EP without DP-attention both worked; only `cutedsl × EP × DP-attention` produced gibberish. Root cause: the MoE output was reduced **twice**. 1. `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` / `forward_normal_dual_stream` unconditionally ran `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` on the MoE output. 2. When `should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` was True (cutedsl + DP-attention + `EP == DP`), `LayerCommunicator._scatter_hidden_states` additionally performed `reduce_scatterv`, which also summed across TP ranks. The result was scaled by the TP world size, corrupting every token. The cutlass fp4-allgather path already had a symmetric guard (`not should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`); the cutedsl reduce-scatterv path was simply missing the same guard. **Bug 2 — `max_num_tokens` under-sized in CuteDSL wrapper under DP-attention.** With CUDA graph enabled, `ensure_cutedsl_wrapper` sized the wrapper with `max(cuda_graph_max_bs, chunked_prefill_size)`. But when `--enable-dp-attention` is set, `chunked_prefill_size` has already been divided by `dp_size` in `server_args`, while the MoE layer receives hidden states gathered across all DP ranks (i.e. per-rank tokens × `dp_size`). The mismatch crashed the worker with `ValueError: num_tokens (N) exceeds max_num_tokens (N/dp_size)` during prefill/warmup. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`: in both `forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream`, add `and not should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` to the all-reduce guard so the reduction is only performed by `reduce_scatterv` in the communicator. The two guards are mutually exclusive by construction (`should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` already requires `not should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`), so no other config is affected. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py`: when `enable_dp_attention` is on, scale `max_num_tokens` back up by `dp_size` so the wrapper covers the gathered MoE input. Verified on 4×B200 with `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-NVFP4` + `trtllm_mla` (`tp=ep=dp=4 + DP-attention + cutedsl`, CUDA graph enabled): gsm8k = **0.957** (512 examples).

signals.title: [CI] Install protoc + Rust toolchain in rerun-test-cpu
signals.text: ## Summary - `rerun-test.yml`'s `rerun-test-cpu` job was running `uv pip install -e \"python[dev]\"` without first installing `protoc` or the Rust toolchain, so builds of the bundled `rust/sglang-grpc` extension (added in #22736) failed with `Could not find \`protoc\``. - Mirror `pr-test.yml:646-652` by invoking the shared `scripts/ci/utils/install_protoc.sh` and `scripts/ci/utils/install_rustup.sh` utilities before the pip install step. ## Context Example failure: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24679201427/job/72171535463 — the CPU rerun job dies at the `Install dependencies` step with: ``` Error: Could not find \`protoc\`. ``` The CUDA rerun job already goes through `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`, which installs both tools, so only the CPU path was broken. ## Test plan - [ ] Trigger a `rerun-test-cpu` run and confirm the `Install protoc` + `Install Rust toolchain` steps succeed and the subsequent pip install now builds `rust/sglang-grpc`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: [Bug] Fix overlap scheduler for embedding/classification/reward models
signals.text: ## Motivation Two fixes that make overlap scheduling usable for prefill-only (non-generation) models: embeddings, classifiers, and reward models. Both bugs are hit immediately once overlap scheduling is enabled for such models and a batch goes big enough to trigger `batch_is_full`. ### Bug 1 — FutureMap allocated but unused `FutureMap` tracks future tokens emitted during the decode step. Embedding, classification, and reward models produce their output in a single forward pass and never consume the map, but `init_overlap` allocates one as long as `enable_overlap=True`. For a non-generation deployment, this is pure wasted memory. ### Bug 2 — `batch_is_full` never resets for prefill-only batches `get_new_batch_prefill` flips `self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True` when admission control kicks in on a large batch. For generation models this is fine — the flag is reset when the prefill batch is merged into `running_batch` on the next iteration. Prefill-only batches (embedding / classification / reward) are **never merged** into `running_batch`, so the flag stays `True` forever and the scheduler stops admitting new batches for the rest of the server's lifetime. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: - `init_overlap`: skip `FutureMap` allocation and return early when `self.is_generation` is False. - Main scheduling loop: add an `elif self.last_batch.is_prefill_only:` branch that resets `self.running_batch.batch_is_full = False` in the same place we'd normally merge the last batch. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical changes — the fixes only affect admission control and memory allocation. Verified existing embedding/classification tests pass with `--disable-overlap-schedule` **and** without it (i.e. overlap now actually works end-to-end for non-generation models). ## Benchmarking and Profiling Measured on `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, bs=256, input=512 tokens, H100: | Config | RPS | HFU | GPU util | |---|---|---|---| | Overlap disabled (`--disable-overlap-schedule`) | 18.1 | 27.4% | 87% | | Overlap enabled (with this fix) | **20.9** | **31.4%** | **98%** | **+15.5% throughput, +13.4% lower latency.** Before this fix, enabling overlap on an embedding server would freeze admission after the first large batch, so this benchmark wasn't even reachable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. - [x] Provide test results, including accuracy and performance analysis. - [x] For reviewers: follow the [Code Review Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/code_review_guide.html).

signals.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for Encode Prefill Disaggregation
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR adds CI test coverage for encoder disaggregation features on Ascend NPU. Specifically, it validates the `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder` parameter, which allows a language-only VLM server to intelligently route single‑image requests locally while dispatching multi‑image requests to remote encoder servers. The tests ensure that the Ascend backend correctly supports: - `--encoder-only` and `--language-only` disaggregated deployments. - The `zmq_to_scheduler` and `zmq_to_tokenizer` transfer backends. - Adaptive dispatch logic that prevents single‑image requests from attempting to contact an encoder server (allowing safe use of dummy encoder URLs for validation). Without these tests, encoder disaggregation behavior on NPU could regress silently. ## Modifications Added the following test scripts under `test/registered/ascend/basic_function/EPD/`: 1. **`test_npu_adaptive_dispatch_to_encoder.py`** - Contains `TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoder` and `TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoderMultiImage`. - Validates single‑image local processing and multi‑image remote forwarding with `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder`. 2. **`test_npu_disaggregated_vlm.py`** - Contains `TestDisaggregatedVLM` (base) and `TestDisaggregatedVLM_ZMQ_Tokenizer`. - Provides foundational tests for `--encoder-only` + `--language-only` disaggregated VLM deployments on NPU. Both scripts set `SGLANG_MM_SKIP_COMPUTE_HASH=True` to work around Ascend’s lack of `_local_scalar_dense` support for `UInt64` in multimodal hash computation. This test suite implements the validation plan for the following encoder disaggregation parameters: - `--encoder-only` / `--language-only` - `--encoder-transfer-backend` - `--encoder-urls` - `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder` Additionally, the PR includes the existing `TestDisaggregatedVLM` base class and its `zmq_to_tokenizer` variant, which were previously added and serve as foundational tests for disaggregated VLM deployments on NPU. ## Accuracy Tests All tests are implemented in the scripts listed above and use deterministic settings (`temperature=0`) with a fixed inline image to guarantee reproducible results. - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_language_only_text_generation`** Validates that the language‑only server correctly answers a text‑only prompt (`"The capital of France is"` → `"Paris"`). - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_encoder_processes_image_via_language_server`** End‑to‑end image description through the encoder → language pipeline. - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_encoder_processes_multi_images_via_language_server`** Similar validation with two images. - **`TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoder.test_single_image_processed_locally`** Ensures a single‑image request succeeds without a real encoder server, confirming local processing. - **`TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoderMultiImage.test_multi_image_forwarded_to_encoder`** Ensures a multi‑image request succeeds when a real encoder server is available, confirming remote dispatch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable – this PR adds functional correctness tests only; no kernel or runtime changes that affect performance. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre‑commit. - [x] Add unit tests (via CI registration for NPU nightly suites). - [ ] Update documentation – encoder disaggregation flags are already documented; adaptive dispatch documentation will be tracked separately. - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks – not required for test‑only changes. - [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

signals.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for --skip-server-warmup and --nccl-port arguments
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces specific integration tests for NPU (Ascend) environments to verify critical server argument behaviors. The motivation is to ensure: 1. **NCCL Port Configuration**: The `--nccl-port` argument correctly configures the distributed communication port, which is essential for multi-card NPU setups. 2. **Server Warmup Control**: The `--skip-server-warmup` argument effectively bypasses the warmup phase, preventing unnecessary initialization overhead or errors on specific hardware backends. ## Modifications 1. **Added `test_npu_nccl_port.py`**: * Launches the server with `--nccl-port 9111` and `--tp-size 2`. * Verifies that the inference service is healthy (`/health_generate`). * Programmatically checks via `netstat` that the process is listening on the specified NCCL port (9111). 2. **Added `test_npu_skip_warmup.py`**: * Launches the server with the `--skip-server-warmup` flag. * Captures server startup logs to a temporary file. * Verifies that the inference result is correct (e.g., "Paris" for the capital of France). * Asserts that the startup logs **do not** contain the warmup request signature (`GET /model_info`), confirming the warmup phase was skipped. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> These are infrastructure tests. The accuracy logic is verified by checking standard inference outputs (e.g., ensuring the model generates "Paris" correctly) within the test scripts. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> N/A. These tests verify startup configurations and argument parsing logic. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for Dynamic Batch Tokenizer
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces comprehensive NPU-side test coverage for the --enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer feature and its associated parameters (--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size, --dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout). The dynamic batch tokenizer significantly reduces tokenization overhead under high concurrency by asynchronously batching incoming requests, which is especially beneficial for deployments with many short-prompt requests. The added test suite verifies correctness and stability under various configurations (batch size 1 and 64, different timeouts), concurrency patterns, mixed prompt lengths, streaming, varied sampling parameters, and compatibility with disabled radix cache. It also includes an accuracy regression test using the GSM8K benchmark to ensure no degradation in generation quality. In addition, a utility helper send_concurrent_requests is added to test_ascend_utils.py to enable true concurrent HTTP load generation using threading (avoiding asyncio limitations with blocking I/O). The new test is registered for the NPU nightly CI suite. ## Modifications 1. **Dynamic Batch Tokenizer Logic:** - Implemented an `AsyncDynamicBatchTokenizer` that maintains an internal async queue. - A background task `_dynamic_batch_loop` continuously collects incoming requests. - Supports dynamic batching based on `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size` and `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout`. - Utilizes a single-threaded `ThreadPoolExecutor` to handle blocking tokenizer calls safely. 2. **Server Arguments:** - Added `--enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer` to activate the feature. - Added `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size` (default: 32) to control the maximum batch window. - Added `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout` (default: 0.002s) to balance latency and throughput. 3. **Utility Enhancement:** - Added `send_concurrent_requests` in `test_ascend_utils.py` to facilitate reliable concurrency testing for NPU environments. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K accuracy is measured for both configurations using run_eval with 200 examples and max_new_tokens=512. The threshold is set to 0.86. Observed scores in NPU CI runs: Configuration GSM8K Score Latency (s) Throughput (tok/s) batch_size=64, timeout=0.001 ~0.87–0.88 ~12.5 ~620 batch_size=1, timeout=0.005 ~0.87–0.88 ~11.8 ~650 The accuracy remains well above the 0.86 baseline, confirming that the dynamic batch tokenizer does not degrade model output quality. ## Speed Tests and Profiling While this PR focuses on correctness testing, the GSM8K runs also provide indicative performance metrics. The throughput and latency numbers above are collected from actual NPU hardware (Atlas A3 4-card TP=4). The dynamic batch tokenizer reduces tokenization overhead under concurrency; the tests with batch_size=64 and very short timeout (0.001s) demonstrate that the server remains stable and accurate even with aggressive batching windows. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for multi-item scoring
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces a multi-item scoring feature for the `/v1/score` endpoint via the new server argument `--multi-item-scoring-delimiter`. The feature allows batching a single query with multiple items into one forward pass by concatenating them with a user-specified delimiter token. This avoids multiple independent inference calls, substantially improving throughput when evaluating many query–item pairs. The change is especially beneficial for scoring tasks (e.g., reward modeling, classification, or multiple-choice evaluation) where a single query is paired with a list of candidates. ## Modifications - Added `--multi-item-scoring-delimiter` (type `int`) to the server arguments. - The specified token ID is used to separate the query from items and items from each other in the constructed input sequence. - Enforces that `--disable-radix-cache` and `--chunked-prefill-size -1` are set when the delimiter is used (otherwise the server raises an error). - Extended `/v1/score` handling to accept either text strings or pre-tokenized integer lists for `query` and `items`. - Modified the tokenizer manager and scheduler output processor to: - Build a single sequence: `query + <delimiter> + item1 + <delimiter> + item2 + <delimiter> ... + itemN + <delimiter>`. - Extract logprobs only at the delimiter positions that correspond to the end of each item. - Return scores for each label token ID specified in `label_token_ids`. - Added comprehensive unit tests for Ascend NPU CI (`test_npu_multi_item_scoring_softmax.py`): - `test_softmax_true_text_input`: validates `apply_softmax=True` produces proper normalized probabilities and correct semantic ordering. - `test_softmax_false_tokenized_input`: validates `apply_softmax=False` returns raw scores in `[0, 1]` and confirms difference from softmax output. - `test_item_first_flag`: verifies that the `item_first` parameter is ignored (as expected) in multi-item scoring mode. ## Accuracy Tests All tests pass on NPU (Ascend) hardware using the Qwen3-32B model. The correctness of softmax normalization and semantic ordering is verified with a simple arithmetic reasoning task ("1 plus 2 equals 3"). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable for this PR (the feature is an API enhancement that reduces the number of forward passes from N to 1, which inherently improves throughput; exact speedups depend on batch size and model size). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(Documentation update will follow in a separate PR)* - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for Speculative Decoding
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR adds a comprehensive suite of NPU-specific CI tests for speculative decoding and expert parallelism features on Ascend hardware. The goal is to validate the correctness, accuracy, and robustness of the following SGLang parameters and configurations in NPU environments (A2/A3 servers): **Speculative Decoding:** - `--speculative-algorithm` (EAGLE3, NEXTN) - `--speculative-draft-model-path` - `--speculative-draft-model-revision` - `--speculative-draft-load-format` (auto, dummy) - `--speculative-num-steps` - `--speculative-eagle-topk` - `--speculative-num-draft-tokens` - `--speculative-token-map` - `--speculative-attention-mode` (prefill, decode) - `--speculative-moe-runner-backend` - `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend` (ascend_fuseep) - `--speculative-draft-attention-backend` (ascend) - `--speculative-draft-model-quantization` **Expert Parallelism:** - `--moe-a2a-backend` (deepep, ascend_fuseep) - `--deepep-mode` (auto) - `--tp-size` / `--ep-size` (multi-NPU scenarios) - **Environment Variable:** `SGLANG_NPU_FUSED_MOE_MODE` These tests ensure that speculative decoding models (e.g., Qwen3-32B + EAGLE3, DeepSeek-R1 + NEXTN) produce acceptable accuracy on GSM8K, and that parameter combinations (including dummy weights, token maps, and attention mode swaps) are handled gracefully without degrading performance or correctness. ## Modifications The following new test files are added to `sglang/test/ascend/`: 1. **`test_npu_speculative_attention_mode.py`** - Verifies PD disaggregation + MTP scenario with `--speculative-attention-mode` set to `decode` on Prefill and `prefill` on Decode. - Uses Qwen3-32B-W8A8 + EAGLE3 draft model (TP=4). - Evaluates GSM8K accuracy (threshold ≥ 0.86). 2. **`test_npu_speculative_draft_attention_backend.py`** - Tests `--speculative-draft-attention-backend ascend` and `--speculative-moe-runner-backend auto` with NEXTN on DeepSeek-R1-W4A8 (TP=16). - Validates GSM8K score ≥ 0.90. 3. **`test_npu_speculative_moe_a2a_backend.py`** - Tests `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep` with NEXTN on DeepSeek-R1-W8A8 (TP=16). - Also sets `--moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep` and `--deepep-mode auto`. - **Crucially sets `os.environ["SGLANG_NPU_FUSED_MOE_MODE"] = "1"`**, which is mandatory for the `ascend_fuseep` backend on NPU. - GSM8K threshold ≥ 0.95. 4. **`test_npu_speculative_multi_npu.py`** - Tests `--speculative-draft-load-format dummy` and `--speculative-draft-model-revision main` with EAGLE3 on Qwen3-32B (TP=4). - Verifies server info endpoint reflects the parameters. - Performs a simple generation test to confirm functionality. 5. **`test_npu_speculative_token_map.py`** - Covers two scenarios: - EAGLE3 with an invalid token map (ignored; accuracy threshold ≥ 0.86). - EAGLE (legacy) with a valid token map (`FR_SPEC_TOKEN_MAP_PATH`) on Llama-3-8B (accuracy threshold ≥ 0.79). - Uses TP=8 for EAGLE3 and TP=4 for EAGLE. 6. **`test_npu_eagle3.py`** (existing baseline, updated GSM8K test method) - Single-NPU test for Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3, GSM8K threshold ≥ 0.81. All tests are registered with `@register_npu_ci` and target the appropriate nightly test suites (e.g., `nightly-1-npu-a3`, `nightly-4-npu-a3`, `nightly-8-npu-a3`, `nightly-16-npu-a3`). ## Accuracy Tests | Test Case | Model | Draft Model | TP | GSM8K Threshold | Observed (CI) | |-----------|-------|-------------|----|-----------------|---------------| | `TestAscendSpeculativeAttentionMode` | Qwen3-32B-W8A8 | Qwen3-32B-EAGLE3 | 4 | ≥ 0.86 | ✅ | | `TestAscendSpeculativeDraftAttentionAndMoeRunner` | DeepSeek-R1-W4A8 | NEXTN | 16 | ≥ 0.90 | ✅ | | `TestAscendDistTimeout` (moe-a2a) | DeepSeek-R1-W8A8 | NEXTN | 16 | ≥ 0.95 | ✅ | | `TestNpuSpeculativeTokenMap.eagle3` | Qwen3-32B-W8A8 | Qwen3-32B-EAGLE3 | 8 | ≥ 0.86 | ✅ | | `TestNpuSpeculativeTokenMap.eagle` | Llama-3-8B-Instruct | Llama-3-8B-Eagle | 4 | ≥ 0.79 | ✅ | | `TestNpuEagle3` | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-8B-EAGLE3 | 1 | ≥ 0.81 | ✅ | | `TestNpuSpeculativeDraftParams` | Qwen3-32B-W8A8 | Qwen3-32B-EAGLE3 (dummy) | 4 | N/A (functional) | ✅ | *Note: GSM8K evaluations use 1319 examples with 5-shot, temperature=0.0.* ## Speed Tests and Profiling These tests are primarily functional and accuracy-focused; they do not include dedicated performance benchmarks. signals.title: ci: prefetch HF snapshots and skip redundant metadata calls to survive 429s
signals.text: ## Summary CI 429s against the HF API (example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24707205487/job/72263640803) happen when a runner has an incomplete cache for a test's model — the offline-mode guard falls through to online, the server launch issues `HfFileSystem.ls()` → `repo_info` (`python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py:502-503`), and one saturated 5-min window 429s every concurrent job. This PR closes the leak: - **`_try_enable_offline_mode_if_cache_complete`** (`python/sglang/test/test_utils.py`) used to bail to online mode whenever the cache was missing or incomplete. Now calls the new `_ci_prefetch_snapshot` which does a full `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download` with `max_workers=1` (NFS `.incomplete` safety), 3-retry 429 handling that honors `Retry-After`, and recovers a 429 signal from `str(e)` when the error has no `response` object. With the snapshot populated, offline mode is enabled for the server subprocess so the failing `fs.ls()` — which is gated on `not HF_HUB_OFFLINE` — is skipped entirely. Matches the vllm pattern of per-launch snapshot fetches; no manifest to maintain, new test models just work. - **`scripts/ci/utils/prevalidate_cached_models.py`**: parallelize the per-snapshot validation with `ThreadPoolExecutor(16)`. Each worker assembles its full log block as a single string to avoid interleave; the main loop wraps `future.result()` in try/except so one worker raising doesn't abort the whole pass (matches prior serial `FAIL (error)` behavior). Expected runtime on a 221-snapshot cache: ~47s → a few seconds. Failure path on a persistent 429 window is preserved (best-effort: prefetch gives up after 3 retries and falls through to online, same as today). ## Test plan - [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` — clean on touched files. - [ ] Re-trigger the failing job (`stage-b-test-2-gpu-large (0)` on PR #23281) and confirm the `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` server launch now enables `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` instead of 429'ing. - [ ] Verify prepare_runner.sh `Prepare runner` step drops from ~60s to ~15-20s on a warm cache (221 snapshots). - [ ] Spot-check log output: per-snapshot blocks remain intact (each `[idx/total] model` header is immediately followed by its PASS/FAIL/SKIP line, even with 16 concurrent workers). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: WIP: [Speculative] Add draft-DP mode to eliminate allreduce/all-to-all during draft multi-step decode
signals.text: ## Motivation In speculative decoding with MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1 with MTP), the draft model's multi-step decode phase incurs significant collective communication overhead (allreduce, all-to-all) across TP/EP ranks. Since the draft model is much smaller than the target model, running it with full TP/EP parallelism is wasteful — the communication cost dominates the compute savings. This PR introduces `--speculative-draft-dp`, which runs the draft model with data parallelism (tp_size=1, ep_size=1 per rank), so each rank loads all draft experts locally and skips all collective communication during draft decode steps. ## Modifications - **`server_args.py`**: Add `--speculative-draft-dp` flag with validation logic (auto-sets `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend=none`, warns if tp/ep=1). - **`parallel_state.py`**: - Extend `patch_tensor_parallel_group` with `also_patch_attn_tp` parameter for full TP+ATTN_TP patching. - Add `patch_moe_parallel_group` context manager to temporarily override `_MOE_EP` / `_MOE_TP`. - **`spec_utils.py`**: Add `draft_dp_full_context` (patches TP+ATTN_TP+MOE_EP+MOE_TP) and `create_draft_dp_group` (creates a single-rank GroupCoordinator per rank). - **`eagle_worker.py`**: - Draft init: patch parallel groups so draft model weights are loaded with tp=1, ep=1; allgather target's embed/lm_head for the draft model. - Draft forward: wrap multi-step decode, draft extend, and draft extend-after-decode with `_draft_forward_context` to patch MoE A2A backend. - Support both draft-DP + DPA (recommended) and draft-DP standalone paths. ## Benchmark Results **Setup:** 8×B200, DeepSeek-R1 MTP, FP8, same prompt and parameters. ### Throughput & Latency | Metric | DPA Baseline | Draft DP | Change | |--------|-------------|----------|--------| | Avg throughput | 97.1 tok/s | 101.7 tok/s | **+4.7%** | | Avg latency | 2.65s | 2.53s | **-4.5%** | | Avg accept_len | 2.64 | 2.65 | ≈0 (correctness verified) | ### Profile (same workload) | Metric | Baseline | Draft DP | Change | |--------|----------|----------|--------| | Total communication | 5838ms (38.1%) | 4672ms (31.2%) | **-20%** | | Total GPU time | 15343ms | 14980ms | **-2.4%** | | NCCL AllGather | 2827ms | 2137ms | **-24%** | | custom allreduce 2stage | 1708 calls | 1152 calls | **-32.5%** | | FP8 GEMM (bmm) | 1877ms | 2139ms | +14% (draft computes more experts) | | fused_moe | 154ms | 253ms | +64% (8 vs 1 expert/rank) | **Key takeaway:** Draft-DP trades a small increase in per-rank compute (each rank runs all draft experts) for a large reduction in communication overhead, resulting in a net **4.7% throughput improvement** and **4.5% latency reduction**. Accept length remains unchanged, confirming correctness. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.title: [Docs]: clarify chunked_prefill_size and max_prefill_tokens semantics
signals.text: ## Motivation `--chunked-prefill-size` and `--max-prefill-tokens` are both per-batch token budgets that are decremented together as requests are admitted, but the existing docs describe them as independent limits with no mention of their interaction. Additionally, `--chunked-prefill-size` silently gets divided by `dp_size` when `--enable-dp-attention` is set, and neither this behavior nor the truncation semantics are documented. Raised in #20018. ## Modifications - `docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.md`: extended the descriptions of `--chunked-prefill-size` and `--max-prefill-tokens` to clarify (1) both are shared per-batch budgets, not per-request caps; (2) `--chunked-prefill-size` additionally triggers truncation of individual requests; (3) whichever budget is tighter bounds the batch; (4) the effective value of `--chunked-prefill-size` is `chunked_prefill_size // dp_size` when DP attention is enabled. - `docs/advanced_features/hyperparameter_tuning.md`: added a note in the OOM tuning bullet pointing readers to the server arguments reference for the interaction between the two parameters. Docs-only change. No code or behavior change. ## Accuracy Tests N/A ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Loading `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4` with MTP (speculative EAGLE) fails during weight loading: ``` File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py", line 314, in load_weights super().load_weights(weights, is_nextn=True) File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2339, in load_weights self.do_load_weights(weights, is_nextn) File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 361, in do_load_weights future.result() ... File "sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 271, in weight_loader assert param.size() == loaded_weight.size() ``` **Root cause:** `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN.hf_to_sglang_mapper` maps **all** `model.layers.61.*` weight names to `model.decoder.*`. This is correct for decoder sub-modules (self_attn, mlp), but incorrect for NextN-specific weights (`eh_proj`, `embed_tokens`, `enorm`, `hnorm`, `shared_head`) which live directly under `model`, not `model.decoder`. This causes the quark quantization exclude list to be incorrectly transformed: | Checkpoint name | Mapped name (before fix) | Actual param prefix | Correct? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `model.layers.61.eh_proj` | `model.decoder.eh_proj` | `model.eh_proj` | No | | `model.layers.61.embed_tokens` | `model.decoder.embed_tokens` | `model.embed_tokens` | No | | `model.layers.61.enorm` | `model.decoder.enorm` | `model.enorm` | No | | `model.layers.61.hnorm` | `model.decoder.hnorm` | `model.hnorm` | No | | `model.layers.61.shared_head` | `model.decoder.shared_head` | `model.shared_head` | No | | `model.layers.61.self_attn.*` | `model.decoder.self_attn.*` | `model.decoder.self_attn.*` | Yes | | `model.layers.61.mlp.*` | `model.decoder.mlp.*` | `model.decoder.mlp.*` | Yes | Because `should_ignore_layer("model.eh_proj", ["model.decoder.eh_proj", ...])` fails to match, `QuarkLinearMethod` creates FP4-packed parameter ## Modifications - Update `hf_to_sglang_mapper` in `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN` to add explicit longer-prefix mappings for NextN-specific weights (`eh_proj`, `embed_tokens`, `enorm`, `hnorm`, `shared_head`). Since `WeightsMapper` sorts by substring length (longest first), these specific entries take priority over the generic `model.layers.61 -> model.decoder` fallback. - After this fix, the quark exclude list is correctly mapped, `should_ignore_layer` properly identifies `eh_proj` as excluded, and `UnquantizedL ## Accuracy Tests **DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4 launch cmd** ```bash sglang serve --model-path /dockerx/data2/models/amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4/ \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size=8 \ --chunked-prefill-size=32768 \ --mem-fraction-static=0.8 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --num-continuous-decode-steps=4 \ --max-prefill-tokens=32768 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs=256 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` **GSM8K evaluation cmd** ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --port 30000 ``` | Model | GSM8K acc | Output throughput | | --- | --- | --- | | dpsk-r1-0528-mxfp4-mtp-moefp4 (mtp, before fix) | CRASH | N/A | | dpsk-r1-0528-mxfp4-mtp-moefp4 (mtp, after fix) | **0.960** | 582.3 tok/s | ## Related Model Tests | Model | Config | GSM8K Accuracy | Throughput | Status | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | DeepSeek-R1-0528 | no MTP | 0.955 | 676.8 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528 | EAGLE + external NextN draft | 0.975 | 999.5 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 | EAGLE (built-in MTP) | 0.935 | 1621.3 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 | EAGLE + external NextN draft | 0.935 | 1369.5 tok/s | PASS | | GLM-5.1-MXFP4 | EAGLE (built-in MTP) | 0.965 | 687.9 tok/s | PASS | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: [bugfix]  Fix unnecessary recompilation in fla l2norm_fwd_kernel by removing constexpr from runtime T
signals.text: ## Motivation This kernel is invoked by GDN / KDA / RWKV-style linear-attention layers on every forward pass, so the recompilation penalty hits every request in production serving. In `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/l2norm.py`, the `l2norm_fwd_kernel` declares `T: tl.constexpr`. However, `T` represents the total number of input rows (`num_tokens` × `num_heads`), which is a **runtime-dynamic** value that changes on every batch during inference. In Triton, a `tl.constexpr` parameter is treated as a compile-time constant. Every distinct value of `T` triggers a full JIT recompilation of the kernel (~90 ms each on L20Y). During online serving, `T` varies continuously across batches, causing: - **Repeated unnecessary recompilations**: each new `T` value compiles a new kernel variant - **Unbounded compilation cache growth**: hundreds of kernel copies accumulate - **Latency spikes**: compilation overhead (~90 ms) dwarfs the kernel execution time (~0.03 ms) The upstream FLA library has already addressed this by using `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])` with `T` as a plain parameter: https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/fla/modules/l2norm.py `T` is only consumed by `tl.make_block_ptr(shape=(T, D), ...)` for shape description and boundary masking; it never participates in control flow, loop bounds, or constant folding. Therefore removing `constexpr` cannot change generated PTX semantics — only the specialization key. ## Modifications Two-line change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/l2norm.py`: 1. `@triton.jit` → `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])` 2. `T: tl.constexpr` → `T` (plain parameter) ```diff -@triton.jit +@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"]) def l2norm_fwd_kernel( x, y, eps, NB: tl.constexpr, - T: tl.constexpr, + T, D: tl.constexpr, BT: tl.constexpr, BD: tl.constexpr, ): ``` Added test file: `test/manual/layers/test_fla_l2norm.py`---- — this is a verification script for reviewers to reproduce the fix, and is not intended to be merged into the main codebase. Feel free to remove it before merging. ## Accuracy Tests Both kernel variants (constexpr `T` vs runtime `T`) tested against a pure-PyTorch L2 norm reference implementation (float32 accumulation) with `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2` on bfloat16 inputs. 10 different `T` values with fixed `D=128`: | T | constexpr T | runtime T | |-----|-------------|-----------| | 16 | PASS | PASS | | 37 | PASS | PASS | | 64 | PASS | PASS | | 100 | PASS | PASS | | 128 | PASS | PASS | | 200 | PASS | PASS | | 256 | PASS | PASS | | 333 | PASS | PASS | | 500 | PASS | PASS | | 777 | PASS | PASS | Both variants produce numerically identical results. The change does not affect computation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Environment**: NVIDIA L20Y (80 GB, SM90), CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.9.1, Triton 3.5.1 **Test methodology**: Two independent kernel copies defined in the test file (one with `T: tl.constexpr`, one with plain `T`). Same inputs, same launch parameters. The only difference is the `T` declaration. **Experiment parameters**: - `D=128` (fixed, typical `head_k_dim` for GDN/KDA models) - `dtype=bfloat16` - `BT=16, BD=128, NB=1, num_warps=8` (all fixed `constexpr`) - `T` is the **only** varying parameter across calls ### Compilation count (10 different T values, NB=1 for all) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | New compilations | 10 | 0 | | Cache growth | 1 → 11 | 1 → 1 | ### End-to-end latency (20 batches, T=16,32,...,320) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |---------------|-------------------|-------------------| | Total time | 1335.14 ms | 0.60 ms | | Per-batch avg | 66.76 ms | 0.03 ms | | **Speedup** | — | **2224x** | > Note: the 2224x figure reflects steady-state inference where the old version recompiles on nearly every batch. The cold-start table below (10.7x) reflects the worst case where the new version still pays one compilation. ### Cold-start latency (fresh kernels, 10 batches, T=16,66,...,466) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |---------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | Total time | 903.9 ms | 84.5 ms | | Compilations | 10 | 1 | | Per-batch avg | 90.4 ms | 8.4 ms | | **Speedup** | — | **10.7x** | | Wasted compile time | ~819 ms | — | ## Reproduce ```bash python test/manual/layers/test_fla_l2norm.py ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(N/A — internal kernel optimization, no user-facing API change)* - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. ## Acknowledgements Thanks to [@HuayiJin](https://github.com/HuayiJin) and [@whitelok](https://github.com/whitelok) for collaboration on this fix. *From Engine Architecture Group 5, Engine Infrastructure Department, Xiaohongshu (RedNote).* > **Note to maintainers**: please include the following trailers when squashing: > > ``` > Co-authored-by: HuayiJin <27394199+HuayiJin@users.noreply.github.com> > Co-authored-by: whitelok <whitelok@163.com> > ```

signals.title: XPU: Enable GLM5.1 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) DSA Attention
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> GLM5.1 uses Dynamic Sparse Attention (DSA/NSA) with an FP8 indexer that scores KV pages before sparse attention. This PR enables the path on XPU. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> **1. server_args.py** When GLM5.1 (or any DSA model) runs on XPU, automatically set: - `decode_attention_backend = "dsa"` — puts `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` as the decode backend inside `HybridAttnBackend`, so it can manage the DSA index K-cache and FP8 logit scoring. - `prefill_attention_backend = "dsa"` — We use the dense version of prefill MLA for now since no XPU sparse prefill kernel exists yet in sgl-kernel-xpu. - Disable `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` — the v2 topk uses TileLang/TVM JIT compilation which requires CUDA. **2. hybrid_attn_backend.py** In `HybridAttnBackend`, when the selected backend is not the decode backend (i.e. during prefill when Triton is selected), also call `decode_backend.init_forward_metadata()` and `get_indexer_metadata()` from the decode backend. This ensures the DSA decode backend (`DeepseekSparseAttnBackend`) remains responsible for the DSA indexer even during prefill passes. **3. dsa_backend.py** Guard `flashmla_metadata` computation with `not _is_xpu`. The `get_mla_metadata` function is from `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` which is CUDA-only. **4. dsa/dsa_indexer.py** Replace `torch.cuda.get_device_properties` and `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` with XPU-aware equivalents in `_get_mqa_logits_budget_bytes`. **5. rotary_embedding/base.py** In `forward_xpu`, handle 2D input tensors `(N, head_size)` for the fallback `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding` kernel which expects 3D `(N, num_heads, head_size)`. The DSA indexer passes a single-head `k_rope` as 2D. **6. jit_kernel/dsa/__init__.py** Guard the CuteDSL import (NVIDIA CUDA DSL) on XPU, matching the existing ROCm guard. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> N/A since the original model is too big for BMG. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> N/A since the original model is too big for BMG. ## Checklist - [X] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [X] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: ci: bundle in_process_group tests into one python3 -m unittest invocation
signals.text: ## Motivation `run_unittest_files` invokes one fresh `python3 file.py -f` per test file in a partition. Each invocation pays ~10 s of `import sglang.*` + CUDA init before doing any test work. For a partition with N pure module-level tests, that's ~10×N seconds of pure overhead. Measured locally on the attention-backend unittest suite (27 files): | Invocation | Wall time | |---|---| | `python3 file.py -f` × 27 (current CI loop) | **~5 min** | | `python3 -m unittest -f <27 mods>` (one process) | **~50 s** | The savings exist for any test set where the import cost dominates the actual test work. For a typical 8-12-file partition of pure module-level tests, this can cut wall time by 3-5×. ## Architecture context GitHub Actions stages run `partitions[suite]` jobs in a matrix; each partition is a separate GHA runner with its own checkout + install + warmup. Inside one partition, `run_unittest_files` loops the partition's files sequentially. That's the natural scope for amortizing imports — one warm Python per partition. But `auto_partition` LPT-bin-packs files by `est_time`, so the 27 attention files would normally end up scattered across 8 partitions (~3-4 per). Without grouping at the partitioner, savings shrink proportionally. ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_register.py` * New kwarg-only `in_process_group: Optional[str]` on every `register_{cuda,cpu,amd,npu,xpu}_ci`. Persisted as `CIRegistry.in_process_group` (defaults to None → existing behavior unchanged). * New `CIBundle` dataclass: `group_key`, `members: List[CIRegistry]`, `est_time`. Acts as a single atomic bin-pack unit. * `_bundle_in_process_groups()` rolls members with the same group key into a `CIBundle` **before** `auto_partition` runs LPT. The whole group always lands in one partition. Bundle `est_time`: - prefers grouped `live_est["group:<key>"]` from a prior measurement; - falls back to `sum(member.est_time) - (N-1) * _BUNDLE_IMPORT_COST_SEC` (each extra member avoids one cold `import sglang`). * `auto_partition()` return type widens to `List[Union[CIRegistry, CIBundle]]`. ### `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_utils.py` * `_filename_to_module()` — converts `registered/foo/test_x.py` → `registered.foo.test_x` for the unittest CLI argv (cwd is `test/` per `_pr-test-stage.yml:157`). * `_run_one_bundle()` — handles one bundle: builds `python3 -m unittest -f <mod1> <mod2> ...`, runs under `run_with_timeout`, credits/discredits members en bloc, supports the existing retry-on-flake loop. Per-bundle timing recorded under `file_elapsed["group:<key>"]` so `live_est` picks up grouped wall time for future bin-packing. * `run_unittest_files()` per-iteration loop dispatches `CIBundle` units to `_run_one_bundle` and continues; `CIRegistry`/`TestFile` units take the existing per-file `Popen(["python3", file, "-f"])` path unchanged. * `units_passed_count` so the "Test Summary" line reports unit counts (not member counts). * `_repo_relative_path()` returns `group:<key>` verbatim so TIMINGS JSON keys are stable across runner layouts. ### No test files change `in_process_group` is opt-in. The first consumer (attention-backend unittest suite, PR #26517) will add the field in a follow-up commit on that branch. ## How a suite opts in ```python register_cuda_ci( est_time=25, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200", in_process_group="attention_unittest", # ← single new kwarg ) ``` All files with the same group value run together as one `python3 -m unittest -f <mods>` invocation in whichever partition `auto_partition` picks for the bundle. ## Risks + mitigations | Risk | Mitigation | |---|---| | Members of a group share a Python interpreter — one file's monkey-patch could affect another | Opt-in. Authors mark their group only when they've confirmed shared-interpreter safety. Out of the box, no test files are marked. | | One file crashing kills the whole bundle | v1 fails the whole bundle and credits the bundle's error to every member. Per-member fallback re-run on failure is a follow-up. | | Group too large for any partition's timeout | `bundle_timeout = max(timeout_per_file, est_time * 2 + 60)` — generous slack, but extremely large groups still need to be split manually for now. | | `live_est` from before rollout is per-file → bundle bin-packing overestimates | Acceptable for first run; once grouped runs land, `live_est["group:<key>"]` takes over and packing tightens. | ## Accuracy Tests * Parsed all 779 registered test files (1051 registries) with the new field — unchanged behavior, `in_process_group=None` everywhere, no regressions in `collect_tests` / `auto_partition` for existing tests. * End-to-end synthetic bundle: 2 stub test files registered with `in_process_group="bundle_validation"`, `auto_partition` produces a `CIBundle`, `run_unittest_files` runs `python3 -m unittest`, bundle key recorded in TIMINGS with `passed: true`, summary line `1/1 unit(s) passed`. ## Speed Tests | Path | Today | With this PR (attention suite, 27 files marked) | |---|---|---| | One partition handling 3-4 attention files mixed with others | ~5×10 s import overhead | n/a — group always lands in one partition | | One partition handling the whole attention bundle | n/a | one `python3 -m unittest -f <27 mods>` → ~50 s total | ## Checklist - signals.title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
signals.text: ## Motivation When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash. The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607. ## Modifications This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue. I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1. 1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads. pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch. PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues. This prevents divergence. 2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads. Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN). This behavior is consistent with TP. This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works. Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted. However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread. This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead. ## Accuracy Tests Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`. I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model. I ran two groups: - Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled. Resolved 356/500. - Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled. Resolved 353/500. I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B. The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test. Hints to make L3 are in-use: - Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests. - Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2. ```sh # Group A sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp-size 8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # Group B sglang serve \ --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --pp-size 4 \ --tp-size 2 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --max-total-tokens=500000 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \ --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}' # SWE bench agent python -m minisweagent.run.benchmarks.swebench \ --subset verified \ --split test \ -c swebench.yaml -c environment.container_timeout=24h \ -o /root/swe_test/result \ -m "openai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" \ -w 128 # SWE evaluation python -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation \ --predictions_path /root/swe_test/result/preds.json \ --dataset_name princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified \ --split test \ --max_workers 32 \ --run_id test-mini-swe-agent \ --timeout 1200 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling I tested with L1 only, L1+L2 and L1+L2+L3. The size of L1 and L2 are configured not to hold all tokens. L3 is large enough to hold all tokens. `request-rate` is set to `1` so that L3 prefetch are performed and not limited by budget. ```sh # L1 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ --page-size=64 \ --enable-metrics # L2 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ --page-size=64 \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-hierarchical-cache \ --hicache-mem-layout=page_first # L3 sglang serve \ --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \ --tp-size=2 \ --pp-size=4 \ --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen25 \ signals.title: feat(diffusion): add OmniDreams autoregressive video world model
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Adds NVIDIA **OmniDreams** — a 2B distilled autoregressive driving-video world model (Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B based, production runtime = FlashDreams) — to `multimodal_gen`. Given a first frame + a per-frame HD-map (lane lines + actor boxes) control signal, it rolls out a temporally-coherent driving video via 2-step Self-Forcing flow-match denoising over a rolling block KV cache. Served both one-shot (HTTP `/v1/videos`) and realtime (WebSocket `/v1/realtime_video/generate`). Relates to #27214. Cookbook: [/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams/OmniDreams). ## Modifications - **DiT model:** OmniDreams 2B — 3D NeoX RoPE (44:42:42) with `shift_t` chunk positioning, AdaLN-LoRA modulation, flat-checkpoint loading (570-key `.pt`). - **AR pipeline (3 stages):** text/i2v/HD-map pre-encode → block-causal rollout (`BlockKVCache`: sink + rolling window) → seam-free Wan-2.1 VAE decode (clean per-chunk latents concatenated and decoded in one pass so the causal 3D cache flows across chunk boundaries). - **Conditioning:** 2-step flow-match scheduler (sigmas `{1.0, 0.8036, 0.0}`, shift=5.0) with first-frame i2v pinning; Cosmos-Reason1-7B `full_concat` text embedding; per-frame HD-map raster sequence VAE-encoded as one causal clip and sliced into per-chunk latent groups. - **Pure-Python runtime (no custom CUDA):** the vendored native CUDA FP8 DiT extension tree was removed; the runtime is now eager bf16 DiT + weight-only FP8 (pre-quantized E4M3 weights dequantized to bf16, cached for reuse), with an optional FP8-compute path (`torch._scaled_mm`). Self-attention uses SDPA; a SageAttention-3 FP4 backend and a CUDA-graph capture of the steady-state AR step are split out into separate follow-up PRs. The DiT file tree follows the single-file convention every sibling DiT uses (9 helper files → 4). - **Realtime online serving:** WebSocket `/v1/realtime_video/generate` streaming adapter (per-chunk HD-map control events + incremental frame output); `OmniDreamsRealtimeAdapter` reuses the `RealtimeModelAdapter` base class. Open-loop today (repeats last HD-map frame when the client lags); closed-loop per-chunk conditioning is planned. - **Serving:** TP via `Column/RowParallelLinear` head sharding (cross-view attention scaffolded, fail-loud gated off for single-view); HTTP API `hdmap_path` / `num_views`, with a guard rejecting local FS paths over HTTP (only `http(s)://` / `data:`) to close an arbitrary-file-read vector. - **Docs:** OmniDreams cookbook (`docs_new/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams/OmniDreams.mdx`) + card in the diffusion cookbook overview. ## Accuracy Tests Two fixes were needed to match the reference distribution and produce sharp output: - **Text encoder runs without an `attention_mask`** — the checkpoint is trained (FlashDreams' `CosmosReason1TextEncoder`) on the full padded sequence unmasked, and the DiT cross-attends over all 512 token embeddings (valid + padding). Adding a mask pushes padding-token conditioning OOD → washed-out rollouts (measured: normalized latent std collapses to ≈0.52 vs ≈0.84 unmasked). - **Clean first-frame re-injected during context-noise KV writes** so the pinned frame-0 doesn't accumulate noise in the rolling cache. **Distribution match:** after the text-conditioning fix the generated rollout's normalized latent std recovers `0.52 → 0.84`, matching real GT `≈0.84` — sharp, temporally coherent (no washed-out collapse). **Generalization, not memorization:** stays sharp across unseen seeds, mismatched first-frame/HD-map pairings, and a held-out scene; gen-vs-GT PSNR declines monotonically with rollout depth (`40.8 dB` @f1 → `23.6 dB` @f29). **CPU unit tests** — 101 cases in one file `test_omnidreams.py` (117 passed, 4 skipped with the lighttae/lightvae checkpoints available): ``` python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_omnidreams.py -q ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling **rtx6kd (RTX 6000D 85GB, sm_120) — 13 frames, 2 denoise steps, default WanVAE:** | Path | Config | Denoise | Total | Peak VRAM | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | offline eager | `native_dit_acceleration=disabled` | 2.93s | 7.08s | 44.8GB | bf16 baseline | | offline **fp8_compute** | `native_dit_acceleration=fp8_compute` | 3.03s | 6.99s | 45.8GB | real FP8: 196 linears on `torch._scaled_mm`, weights stay FP8, SDPA attention. Faster than eager. | | offline `weight_only_fp8` (cold-start) | `native_dit_acceleration=weight_only_fp8` | 40.4s | 44.6s | 48.1GB | **dequant fallback**: loads the offline FP8 `.pt` then dequantizes to bf16 (~36s one-time, cached) and runs eager. For GPUs without FP8-compute; not the headline FP8 path. | | online `sglang serve` + `/v1/videos` | eager + WanVAE | 2.93s | 7.26s | 44.8GB | HTTP one-shot | Output is sharp across all paths (per-frame std ~48–52, frame-to-frame meandiff ~1.9, no gray-mush), numerically identical between eager and fp8_compute. **Two FP8 modes (both consume the offline-quantized `omnidreams_fp8_dit.pt` artifact):** - `fp8_compute` — the proper offline-quantization path: weights quantized to FP8 E4M3 (per-output-channel) and kept FP8 in VRAM; GEMMs via `torch._scaled_mm` (rowwise) + SDPA attention. Faster than eager on Blackwell. This is the recommended FP8 path. - `weight_only_fp8` — a fallback that dequantizes the offline FP8 weights back to bf16 and runs the eager DiT. It trades a one-time ~36s dequant (cached for the process lifetime) for a smaller checkpoint on disk, with no VRAM or steady-state speed benefit. Use it only on GPUs without FP8-compute support. **Benchmarks still missing:** - [ ] Warm-serve fp8_compute latency + realtime per-chunk latency (the SageAttention-3 backend + CUDA-graph capture were split out into follow-up PRs; will re-bench the warm/realtime paths once those land). - [ ] Multi-GPU / TP scaling (rtx6kd is single-GPU; needs a multi-GPU host). Sample inputs: `nvidia/omni-dreams-samples` (gated). HD-map is mandatory — without it the rollout goes OOD and collapses to gray after ~2 frames (expected). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) (OmniDreams cookbook + cookbook-overview card). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) — partial (see Speed section: eager / fp8_compute / weight_only_fp8 done; warm-serve + realtime + TP scaling pending). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32173051147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173051147)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32173050971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173050971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [sglang-miles] RDT/NIXL weight sync support for Ray scheduler actors
signals.text: ## What sglang-side support for **RDT (Ray Direct Transport / NIXL) weight sync** — lets the [miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) trainer push RL weights to rollout engines via a zero-copy RDMA pull instead of NCCL broadcast. Paired with the miles-side PR (radixark/miles#1313), which has the perf write-up. ## Changes - **`ray/scheduler_actor.py`** — add `pull_weights()`, which uses `ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref` to RDMA pre-sharded weight buckets directly into the model's `param.data` buffers (no intermediate receive buffers / copies). - **`ray/engine.py` + `ray/data_parallel_controller.py`** — register `SchedulerActor`s as **detached** named actors with the http **port** baked into the name, so the trainer (a different Ray job) can discover them via `list_named_actors` even when several engines share a node; raise `max_concurrency` so a concurrent `pull_weights` is not starved while `run_event_loop` blocks; set `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` so the absolute GPU id from `get_accelerator_ids()` stays valid. - **`server_args.py`** — add `enable_engine_info_bootstrap` to start the engine-info bootstrap server and register per-rank parallelism config **without** the mooncake/verbs P2P transfer-engine seeding. - **`entrypoints/engine.py` + `model_executor/model_runner.py`** — honor `enable_engine_info_bootstrap`; make the P2P transfer-engine memory registration non-fatal so EFA/verbs clusters where it fails don't crash the scheduler (RDT only needs the parallelism config). - **`model_loader/loader.py`** — make `post_load_weights` public so the RDT path can invoke it. - **`pyproject.toml`** — require `ray>=2.55.1` (`ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref`). ## Notes Targeting the `sglang-miles` integration branch; rebased onto current `sglang-miles` (#28001, #29339). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32193574872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32193574872)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32193574518](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32193574518)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
