signals.title: [GLM-5.2] Keep GlmMoeDsa MoE e_score_correction_bias in fp32
signals.text: ## Problem GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`) MoE `e_score_correction_bias` values are ~34. `MoEGate.__init__` downcasts the bias to bf16 when a `quant_config` is present (GLM-5.2-MXFP4 uses quark), and bf16's ULP of **0.25 at that magnitude collapses 174 distinct bias values to ~3**, which corrupts the noaux_tc top-k expert routing (~99.6% wrong top-8). Output is garbage at *all* reasoning efforts, not just Max. The CUDA grouped-topk paths already run the bias in fp32; only the aiter path re-downcasts it. ## Fix (minimal — one real change, two sites) 1. `models/deepseek_v2.py`: add a module-level `_is_glm_moe_dsa(config)` helper (the `"GlmMoeDsa"` substring matches both the main `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` and the NextN draft `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN`), and arch-gate the correction-bias dtype block so **both** bf16 downcast sites are skipped for GlmMoeDsa (dtype stays fp32). 2. `layers/moe/topk.py`: in the aiter `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` path, pass the bias/logits as fp32 **when the bias is already fp32** — a dtype-gate, so non-GLM aiter models (quantized DeepSeek-V3, …) keep their exact bf16 dtype (byte-identical), without threading arch info through the hot routing function. Both hunks are required together: without the topk change the fp32 param is re-downcast to bf16 at the aiter boundary. Applies to the main model **and** the NextN/MTP draft. ## Testing (all pass) **`test/registered/unit/models/test_glmmoedsa_correction_bias_fp32.py`** — **9/9 PASSED**: | class::method | asserts | |---|---| | `TestMoEGateCorrectionBiasDtype::test_glm_main_keeps_fp32` | real `MoEGate` keeps `e_score_correction_bias` fp32 for `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (fails on pre-fix code) | | `TestMoEGateCorrectionBiasDtype::test_glm_nextn_keeps_fp32` | …and for the NextN draft `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLMNextN` | | `TestMoEGateCorrectionBiasDtype::test_non_glm_still_downcasts_bf16` | a non-GLM aiter-fp8 config still downcasts to bf16 (no blast radius) | | `TestIsGlmMoeDsaHelper::test_matches_main_and_nextn` | helper matches both GLM arches | | `TestIsGlmMoeDsaHelper::test_matches_when_present_among_others` | matches when GLM arch is among several | | `TestIsGlmMoeDsaHelper::test_rejects_non_glm` | rejects a non-GLM arch | | `TestIsGlmMoeDsaHelper::test_returns_false_for_none_or_empty_architectures` | `None`/`[]` architectures → False, never mis-gates | | `TestCorrectionBiasBf16Collapse::test_bf16_collapses_distinct_biases` | 174 distinct fp32 biases collapse to ≤4 in bf16 | | `TestCorrectionBiasBf16Collapse::test_bf16_bias_scrambles_topk_routing` | bf16 bias diverges the top-8 expert routing | **E2E** (with the ROCm EAGLE-sampling fix): GPQA-Diamond **89.9% (178/198)**, NVFP4 SGLang parity. ## Test steps (reproduce) **Environment.** 8× MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`. `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is the image default, which is what puts the aiter paths below in play. <details> <summary>1. Unit tests</summary> GPU devices must be passed through even for CPU-only cases — importing `sglang` pulls in `aiter`, which shells out to `rocminfo` at import time. ```bash docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g \ -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_glmmoedsa_correction_bias_fp32.py -q -p no:randomly' ``` Red-before/green-after: re-run after `git checkout origin/main -- python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` and the new case fails. </details> <details> <summary>2. Serve GLM-5.2 (shared by the e2e steps)</summary> Use **GLM-5.2-FP8**, not MXFP4, on this image: MXFP4 is `quant_method: quark`, and the image's `quark.py` imports `declare_load_time_override` from `arg_groups/overrides.py`, which does not exist there, so the scheduler dies at weight load (`main` has since moved past that code). FP8 is also in the `("fp8","compressed_tensors","quark")` tuple, so it exercises the same routing path. ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 ``` </details> <details> <summary>3. GPQA-Diamond via lm-evaluation-harness</summary> GSM8K is **not** a useful gate here — GLM-5.2 sits at ~94% on it, so it is saturated and hides routing/sampling regressions. Always split the samples jsonl by response length (a terminated answer is 1 character) before trusting a GPQA number. - `--limit 198` selects one permutation per question (`process_docs` uses `n_repeats=2`, so the full task is 396); 198 matches the 178/198 figures quoted here. </details> <details> <summary>4. Confirm the aiter routing path is actually taken (this PR)</summary> The fix only matters if `biased_grouped_topk_gpu`'s aiter branch runs. Insert a one-shot probe before the `aiter_biased_grouped_topk(...)` call and serve as above; on GLM-5.2-FP8 it prints: ``` biased_grouped_topk_gpu AITER branch HIT bias.dtype=torch.float32 gating.dtype=torch.bfloat16 distinct=174 ``` i.e. the bias reaches the kernel as fp32 with **174 distinct values** while `gating_output` is bf16 — so the pre-fix `correction_bias.to(dtype=gating_output.dtype)` is a live 174-level → bf16 collapse on the hot path. Reading the raw checkpoint tensors directly shows the same thing (`e_score_correction_bias` is stored fp32; 238 distinct values → **8** after a bf16 cast). </details> ### Results **Routing divergence on a live server (the decisive measurement).** Instrumented `biased_grouped_topk_gpu` to compute the top-k expert set twice on the *same real* `gating_output` — once with the true fp32 bias, once with the bf16-rounded bias — over 400 MoE calls / 203,200 tokens on GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8: | build | bias distinct (fp32 / bf16) | tokens whose top-8 expert set changes | per-slot mismatch | |---|---|---|---| | stock | **8 / 8** | 0.00% | 0.00% | | + this PR | **224 / 8** | **98.50%** | **93.75%** | The `fp32=8` on the stock row *is the bug*: `MoEGate.__init__` allocates `e_score_correction_bias` as bf16, so the 224 distinct values are destroyed **at weight-load time** — by the time the kernel sees it there is nothing left to collapse, which is why stock shows 0% divergence. With the bias kept fp32, comparing 224 levels against the 8 that stock feeds the kernel shows **98.5% of tokens select a different top-8 expert set**. So on stock essentially every token is routed on a corrupted bias. **Accuracy benchmarks cannot see this, and that is expected.** MoE experts are redundant, so changing which experts a token visits does not necessarily change answer quality: | eval | stock | + this PR | |---|---|---| | GSM8K (1319) | 0.941 | 0.947 | | GPQA-Diamond (396, no spec decode) | 0.8333 ± 0.0188 | 0.8182 ± 0.0194 | Both deltas are inside their difference-stderr. GSM8K is additionally saturated (~94%) for this model. **This PR should be judged as a routing-correctness fix, not on a benchmark delta** — HF stores the tensor as fp32, and the bf16 allocation silently discards 224 levels down to 8. *(Caveat on the GPQA numbers: they were measured at `max_tokens=32768`, where ~32% of GLM-5.2's answers truncate mid-reasoning and get graded by a stray letter from the thinking trace, which inflates variance. On the non-truncated subset the model scores 0.951. That noise is another reason the benchmark route is the wrong instrument here.)* ### Performance Keeping the bias in fp32 means `gating_output` is upcast to fp32 for the aiter call, so the cost was measured rather than assumed. **Isolated microbenchmark** of `biased_grouped_topk` (GLM-5.2 shape: 256 experts, topk=8), MI355X: | tokens | stock (bf16) | this PR (fp32) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 16.6 us | 21.8 us | +30.8% | | 1024 | 16.5 us | 21.0 us | +27.4% | | 16384 | 16.5 us | 21.2 us | +28.5% | The delta is a flat **+4.5 us and does not grow with token count**, i.e. it is the launch overhead of the extra cast kernel, not bandwidth — so it does not scale up with batch size. **Extrapolated to a full forward**: GLM-5.2 has 75 MoE layers (78 - 3 dense), so 75 x 4.5 us = 338 us per forward, which at a 29 ms decode step (2200 tok/s @ concurrency 64) is **~1.2%**. That is an upper bound: the microbenchmark is eager, while decode runs under CUDA graphs, which amortise exactly this launch overhead. **Measured end to end**: no regression is detectable. Two GSM8K runs put the patched build slightly *ahead* (n=200: 643.9 -> 699.3 tok/s; n=1319: 947.1 -> 970.0 tok/s) — noise, but it bounds any real regression well below the run-to-run floor. An alternative that costs nothing was considered and rejected: since the bias only selects experts (`topk_weights` is gathered from `scores`, not `scores_for_choice`), top-k is invariant to a uniform shift, so subtracting the mean before the bf16 cast recovers 8 -> 122 levels and cuts routing divergence from 91.9% to 1.31% at zero cost. It was not taken because it is still only approximate; ~1.2% (in practice unmeasurable) is a fair price for exactly correct routing on a correctness bug.

signals.title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
signals.text: ## Problem On ROCm/HIP, EAGLE speculative-decode **verify silently commits `argmax` (greedy)**, ignoring `temperature`/`top_p`. The gate in `srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py::eagle_sample` is: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: target_predict = torch.argmax(...) # greedy ``` `_is_hip` is in the predicate because the sampling-verify ops (`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob`, `top_p_renorm_prob`) are imported only under `is_cuda()/is_musa()` in `srt/layers/sampler.py`. Result: **every EAGLE spec-decode run at `temperature>0` on ROCm decodes greedy**, which on long-reasoning generations degenerates into verbatim repetition loops. Not model-specific. ## Fix Route HIP through the pure-Triton `chain_speculative_sampling_triton` (`srt/speculative/reject_sampling.py`, no CUDA deps), with a **Triton pivot binary-search top-p renorm** replacing the CUDA-only sgl_kernel renorm, and make it the **default on HIP** so users don't have to know a flag: 1. `eagle_utils.py`: factor the gate into a pure `_verify_uses_greedy(...)` helper (testable, and **byte-identical to the original predicate for every non-HIP platform**); add `_top_p_renorm_kernel` (Triton pivot search, ~5× faster than a full sort and exact, `top_p=1.0` is a true no-op) + a HIP renorm wrapper; guard the CUDA-only imports; keep both CUDA NaN probes. 2. `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`: in `_handle_eagle_family` (resolution pipeline), **default `speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True` on HIP** for EAGLE/EAGLE3 + topk==1 + default accept-thresholds + non-deterministic. The predicate is a strict superset of the existing rejection-sampling validation's raises, so the flip can never turn a working config into an error. CUDA still uses the sgl_kernel renorm + `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`. - NEXTN is aliased to EAGLE before this hook, so GLM-5.2 (NEXTN→EAGLE, topk==1) gets the default-on. ## Testing (all pass) **`test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py`** — pure-CPU gate truth table, **4/4 PASSED**: | method | asserts | |---|---| | `test_non_hip_is_byte_identical_to_pre_patch` | gate == the original predicate for every non-HIP row of the full {CUDA,CPU,NPU,XPU}×{greedy,sampling}×{rej on/off} matrix | | `test_hip_samples_only_with_rejection_and_non_greedy` | HIP samples **iff** rejection-sampling on and batch not all-greedy | | `test_cuda_keyed_on_all_greedy_only` | CUDA behavior unchanged (keyed on `is_all_greedy`) | | `test_cpu_npu_xpu_always_greedy` | CPU/NPU/XPU still forced greedy | **`test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py`** — Triton HIP renorm vs a torch nucleus reference, **run on gfx950 (MI350X), 5/5 PASSED**: | method | asserts | |---|---| | `test_top_p_matches_nucleus` | max\|Δ\| < 1e-6 vs nucleus for top_p ∈ {0.5, 0.9, 0.95} | | `test_top_p_one_is_exact_noop` | top_p=1.0 is bit-exact (max\|Δ\| == 0) | | `test_top_k_restriction` | top-k mask honored | | `test_edge_top_p_to_zero_keeps_top1` | degenerate top_p→0 keeps the argmax token | | `test_edge_single_nonmasked_token` | single-token row | **E2E** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI350X, Max effort, temp 1.0/top_p 0.95, fp8 KV): GPQA-Diamond **89.9% (178/198)** vs ~77% stock (forced-greedy); the two hard repetition-loopers terminate cleanly with correct answers at ~2.1× the spec-off throughput (full MTP speedup kept). ## Known residual gaps (pre-existing, not regressions) On HIP, EAGLE topk==1 with `--enable-deterministic-inference` or non-default accept-thresholds is intentionally *not* flipped (rejection sampling is genuinely incompatible there), and HIP **tree-draft** (topk>1) sampling remains greedy (the Triton chain sampler is chain-only). Both are out of scope here. ## Test steps (reproduce) **Environment.** 8× MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`. `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is the image default, which is what puts the aiter paths below in play. <details> <summary>1. Unit tests</summary> GPU devices must be passed through even for CPU-only cases — importing `sglang` pulls in `aiter`, which shells out to `rocminfo` at import time. ```bash docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g \ -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py -q -p no:randomly' ``` Red-before/green-after: re-run after `git checkout origin/main -- python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` and the new case fails. </details> <details> <summary>2. GPQA-Diamond via lm-evaluation-harness</summary> GSM8K is **not** a useful gate here — GLM-5.2 sits at ~94% on it, so it is saturated and hides routing/sampling regressions. GPQA-Diamond is the discriminating eval (model card: 91.2). Task yaml: `utils/evals/gpqa_diamond.yaml` (task `gpqa_diamond_cot_n_shot`, dataset `Idavidrein/gpqa`/`gpqa_diamond`). lm-eval pinned at `b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476`. ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --tasks gpqa_diamond.yaml --output_path "$RESULTS" --log_samples \ --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:30000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,\ eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=163840" \ --limit 198 --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=98304,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95" ``` Serve with a matching `--context-length 163840`. Two things are required for a reasoning model, or the score collapses for harness reasons rather than model reasons: - lm-eval's `LocalChatCompletion.parse_generations` must fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, otherwise every graded answer is the empty string. - `Idavidrein/gpqa` is a **gated** dataset — export `HF_TOKEN` first or the load fails with `DatasetNotFoundError`. - **The token budget must be large or the score is meaningless.** GLM-5.2 routinely reasons past 32k tokens on GPQA. A response that hits `max_tokens` mid-thought never emits a final answer, so `content` is empty, the `reasoning_content` fallback hands the grader ~110k characters of raw reasoning, and the task's `(?i)\b\(?([A-D])\)?\b` filter with `group_select: -1` returns the **last** A–D match in it — usually the English article "a", scored as option A. Confirm verify stops committing argmax (this PR)</summary> Serve as above **with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2`**, probe which branch `eagle_sample` takes, and send a `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95` request: | build | branch taken on a non-greedy batch | |---|---| | stock | `GREEDY(argmax) branch TAKEN` ← the bug | | + this PR | `SAMPLING branch TAKEN` | Two traps when reproducing: - Probe the **first non-greedy** call, not the first call: server warmup issues a greedy request, so a naive one-shot probe reports `is_all_greedy=True` and tells you nothing. signals.title: [DSA] Page-aware move_kv_cache for the DSA indexer cache (fix page_size>1 corruption)
signals.text: ## Problem `IndexKeyCache.move` (`srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py`, reached from `DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache`) moved the DSA indexer cache with a per-token whole-row copy: ```python for index_k in self.buffer: # PAGE-indexed: (num_pages, page_size*(...)) index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] # tgt/src are per-TOKEN locations ``` The index buffer is **page-indexed** — dim-0 is the page, and within a page row the `page_size` fp8 keys form one block (`page_size × index_head_dim` bytes) followed by a block of `page_size` fp32 scales. But `tgt_loc/src_loc` are **token** locations. Indexing dim-0 with token locations is correct only for `page_size == 1`; at `page_size == 64` the token locations run up to `size` — far beyond `num_pages ≈ size/64` — so the copy lands on the **wrong page row or out of bounds**. This is not "quietly-slightly-wrong logits": an OOB row index is a direct crash / device assert, and a wrong-page write scrambles the indexer cache — either way it breaks DSA topk selection. ## Why CUDA has never hit this This move is reached **only** via `move_accept_tokens_to_target_kvcache` on the **`topk>1`** path. CUDA DSA conventionally runs EAGLE/MTP with **`topk == 1`** (the linear chain), so the path is simply **never exercised** on CUDA — `page_size == 64` is the CUDA DSA norm, but the buggy move never runs there, which is why nothing has blown up despite this being a general (not ROCm-specific) bug. It also explains why the unit test below is **GPU-free**: there is no CUDA end-to-end repro to ship until `topk>1` drafting is enabled on DSA. ## Fix Map each token location to its `(page, offset)` and move both of its sub-slices — the fp8 key and the fp32 scale — using `as_strided` views over the two per-page blocks: ```python fp8 = index_k.as_strided((num_pages, ps, hd), (row_stride, hd, 1), base) scale = index_k.as_strided((num_pages, ps, 4), (row_stride, 4, 1), base + ps*hd) fp8[tgt_page, tgt_off] = fp8[src_page, src_off] # RHS gathers before the LHS write -> scale[tgt_page, tgt_off] = scale[src_page, src_off] # overlapping src/tgt is safe ``` This is correct for **any** page size (it subsumes the old `page_size == 1` path), so the previous per-token row copy — and the stop-gap `NotImplementedError` guard — are removed. The base MLA `super().move_kv_cache` (token-indexed `kv_buffer`, already correct) is unchanged, as is the 0-row placeholder skip for skip-topk layers. > Rebased onto current `main`: the DSA index buffer moved behind the `IndexKeyCache` facade > (`index_key_cache.py`), so the fix now lands in `IndexKeyCache.move` rather than > `memory_pool.py`. The bug was carried over verbatim by that refactor. ## Testing `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache.py` — **2/2 PASSED** (GPU-free): hand-builds the page-packed buffer with a per-token signature in both the fp8 key and the scale, moves a cross-page + varied-intra-page-offset set, and asserts each moved token's key **and** scale match its source and that untouched tokens are unclobbered. - `test_page_size_64_moves_correct_subslices` — the real case; fails on the pre-fix whole-row copy. - `test_page_size_1_still_correct` — the legacy path stays correct. Verified red-before/green-after on the rebase: reverting `IndexKeyCache.move` to `main`'s body makes `test_page_size_64_moves_correct_subslices` fail with `IndexError: index 249 is out of bounds for dimension 0 with size 4`, exactly the wrong-page/OOB mechanism above. ## Test steps (reproduce) **Environment.** 8× MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`. `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is the image default, which is what puts the aiter paths below in play. <details> <summary>1. Unit tests</summary> GPU devices must be passed through even for CPU-only cases — importing `sglang` pulls in `aiter`, which shells out to `rocminfo` at import time. ```bash docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g \ -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_move_kv_cache.py -q -p no:randomly' ``` Red-before/green-after: re-run after `git checkout origin/main -- python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py` and the new case fails. </details> <details> <summary>2. Serve GLM-5.2 (shared by the e2e steps)</summary> Use **GLM-5.2-FP8**, not MXFP4, on this image: MXFP4 is `quant_method: quark`, and the image's `quark.py` imports `declare_load_time_override` from `arg_groups/overrides.py`, which does not exist there, so the scheduler dies at weight load (`main` has since moved past that code). FP8 is also in the `("fp8","compressed_tensors","quark")` tuple, so it exercises the same routing path. ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 ``` </details> <details> <summary>3. GPQA-Diamond via lm-evaluation-harness</summary> GSM8K is **not** a useful gate here — GLM-5.2 sits at ~94% on it, so it is saturated and hides routing/sampling regressions. GPQA-Diamond is the discriminating eval (model card: 91.2). Task yaml: `utils/evals/gpqa_diamond.yaml` (task `gpqa_diamond_cot_n_shot`, dataset `Idavidrein/gpqa`/`gpqa_diamond`). lm-eval pinned at `b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476`. ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --tasks gpqa_diamond.yaml --output_path "$RESULTS" --log_samples \ --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:30000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,\ eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=163840" \ --limit 198 --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=98304,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95" ``` Serve with a matching `--context-length 163840`. Two things are required for a reasoning model, or the score collapses for harness reasons rather than model reasons: - lm-eval's `LocalChatCompletion.parse_generations` must fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, otherwise every graded answer is the empty string. - `Idavidrein/gpqa` is a **gated** dataset — export `HF_TOKEN` first or the load fails with `DatasetNotFoundError`. - **The token budget must be large or the score is meaningless.** GLM-5.2 routinely reasons past 32k tokens on GPQA. A response that hits `max_tokens` mid-thought never emits a final answer, so `content` is empty, the `reasoning_content` fallback hands the grader ~110k characters of raw reasoning, and the task's `(?i)\b\(?([A-D])\)?\b` filter with `group_select: -1` returns the **last** A–D match in it — usually the English article "a", scored as option A. Measured at `max_tokens=32768`: 19/60 samples truncated, and the split was **0.951 on terminated answers vs 0.526 on truncated ones**, blending to a bogus 0.817. Always split the samples jsonl by response length (a terminated answer is 1 character) before trusting a GPQA number. - `--limit 198` selects one permutation per question (`process_docs` uses `n_repeats=2`, so the full task is 396); 198 matches the 178/198 figures quoted here. </details> ### Reachability (please read before prioritising) The buggy code is real and the regression test fails on `main`, but **no runnable configuration reaches it today**. Both callers of `DSATokenToKVPool.move_kv_cache` require `speculative_eagle_topk > 1`: - `_finalize_accept_tree_path` is guarded by `topk > 1` (`eagle_worker_common.py`) - the prefix-branch replication in `eagle_worker_common.py` indexes `topk - 1` - `ngram_worker.py` calls it unguarded, but ngram drafting is itself a tree (`topk > 1`) and `speculative_hook.py` rejects `topk > 1` together with `page_size > 1` at startup unless the attention backend is in `("flashinfer","fa3","triton")` (EAGLE) or `"flashinfer"` (NGRAM). DSA forces `attention_backend="dsa"` with `page_size=64`, which is in neither allowlist. Confirmed empirically — NGRAM on GLM-5.2 refuses to start: ``` ValueError: speculative_eagle_topk(10) > 1 with page_size(64) > 1 is unstable and produces incorrect results for paged attention backends. This combination is only supported for the 'flashinfer' backend. ``` So this is **hardening / a prerequisite** for enabling topk>1 tree drafting on DSA, not a fix for something users are currently hitting. That is also why it ships a GPU-free unit test rather than an end-to-end repro.

signals.title: [ray] Support Ray metric backend for engine metrics
signals.text: ## Motivation We need SGLang metrics to show up on Grafana dashboards when running Ray serve LLM with SGLang as the backend. SGLang already exposes the `ServerArgs.stat_loggers` DI hook and Ray-backed collectors in `observability/ray_wrappers.py`, but that backend isn't usable as-is: it's not auto-wired, non-ASCII descriptions are rejected, and two collector paths crash on `prometheus_client` internals. #### § Why modifying `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py` is required? With `RayEngine`, schedulers run as separate Ray actor processes: the Ray-backed collectors record via `ray.util.metrics`, which forwards to the node's Ray metrics agent, which aggregates and exposes one Prometheus endpoint Ray scrapes. Aggregation happens out-of-process in the agent, so code touching in-process `prometheus_client` bucket internals must be guarded. ## Modification - **`ray_wrappers.py`**: ASCII-coerce metric descriptions (Ray rejects non-ASCII); add `build_ray_stat_loggers()` (role → Ray-backed collector map). - **`ray/engine.py`**: `RayEngine` auto-wires those collectors when `enable_metrics` is set and no `stat_loggers` are passed. - **`metrics_collector.py`**: guard the two `TokenizerMetricsCollector` paths to use the public `observe()` API instead of `_buckets`/`_sum`/ `_upper_bounds`, which don't exist on an injected backend. ## Validation SGLang metrics now show up in the dashboard! Ray side PR: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64797. ## Accuracy Tests N/A ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. signals.title: [Feat][GLM5.2] Shared KV Cache for Prefill CP
signals.text:
## Motivation DSA Prefill context parallelism requires every CP rank to consume the complete Main KV and Indexer history. Upstream main supports a layer-sharded path through [#29421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29421), using NCCL and remaining applicable across NVLink domains. This PR adds another option for same-host deployments within one peer-accessible NVLink domain: CP ranks share one CUDA VMM view and directly read peer-owned HBM pages. The two paths cover different topology and communication trade-offs. Like layer sharding, the shared layout stores one aggregate Main-K/Indexer cache instead of eight replicated copies, providing up to 8x logical cache capacity over Base CP8 for the same KV memory budget. The difference is the access model: instead of materializing each owner layer on every rank through a collective, attention kernels directly read peer-owned pages through the shared VMM view. On full GLM-5.2-FP8 / H20-3e, Shared KV stays within 1.86% of Base CP8 warmed mean Prefill latency through 256K. Base CP8 fits about 380K tokens in the tested configuration; Shared KV is intentionally capped at 1.2M tokens for the benchmark and successfully serves a 1M input. The tested 100K L2 host-cache restore reduces latency by 92.67%. ## Modifications - Add `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache` for same-host DSA L1/L2 sharing. - Store Main KV and Indexer once per CP group with owner-sharded CUDA VMM pages; kernels read the group-wide cache directly without per-layer KV broadcast. - Preserve the same ownership in page-first HiCache and Mooncake Prefill transfer, with mandatory CP synchronization before peer data is consumed. ## Design Logical page `p` is owned by CP rank `p % cp_size`, and each rank allocates only its owner pages. CUDA VMM exposes the physical allocations as one group-wide tensor view. Main KV uses the canonical view; Indexer adds a rank-local alias over the same physical allocation for the paged DeepGEMM path, without duplicating HBM. A mandatory CP write fence runs before any rank reads peer-owned pages. Page-first L2 keeps the same logical IDs and ownership. Each rank allocates pinned DRAM only for its owner pages and transfers only between local DRAM and local HBM. CPU failure agreement and a device fence complete each group-wide backup or restore. Mooncake Prefill transfer uses bounded registered staging buffers rather than a second HBM cache. The current scope is one host, one peer-accessible NVLink domain, GLM-5.2 DSA, FP8 KV, `tp=attn_cp`, interleaved Prefill CP, `pp=1`, page-first L1/L2, and Mooncake Prefill transfer. HiSparse, speculative decoding, and L3 storage are not enabled with this path. ## Trade-offs Both shared KV and layer sharding remove CP cache replication. They differ in how each rank accesses the complete cache: **Layer sharding** ```mermaid flowchart LR L1["Layers are sharded across CP ranks"] L2["Owner rank provides the current layer KV"] L3["Per-layer NCCL collective"] L4["Materialize full-layer receive scratch
on every CP rank"] L5["Attention reads local HBM"] LC["General NCCL-connected topology
Cost: transfer, collective sync, full-layer scratch"] L1 --> L2 --> L3 --> L4 --> L5 --> LC ``` **Shared KV (this PR)** ```mermaid flowchart LR S1["Logical page p → owner rank p mod CP size"] S2["Owner-sharded HBM mapped into
one group-wide CUDA VMM view"] S3["Owner-only page write"] S4["Mandatory CP publication fence"] S5["Attention directly reads
local or peer-owned pages"] SC["One peer-accessible NVLink domain
No per-layer KV collective or full-layer scratch"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> SC ``` | | Layer sharding | Shared KV | | --- | --- | --- | | Data access | Materialize the owner layer, then read local HBM | Read peer-owned pages through one VMM address space | | Communication | Per-layer collective transfer | No per-layer KV collective; mandatory write fence | | Temporary HBM | Full-layer receive scratch | No full-layer scratch | | Topology | Works across general NCCL-connected topologies | Requires one peer-accessible NVLink domain | | Main cost | Data movement and collective synchronization | Peer-HBM latency and write synchronization | In the current upstream implementation, the layer-sharded path has not yet optimized its communication to fetch only active/sparse KV. Under the matched setup used here, Shared KV reduces warmed mean Prefill latency by 49.01% at 4K (798.09 vs. 406.91 ms), 16.26% at 128K (14,877.29 vs. 12,457.69 ms), and 7.87% at 1M (179,701.77 vs. 165,565.18 ms). These results describe the current implementations rather than an inherent limit of layer sharding; the comparison should be repeated after its sparse-fetch communication path is optimized. ## Performance ### L1 Prefill Hardware/model: one H20-3e node, full 78-layer GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/CP8, FP8 KV, `page_size=64`, `mem_fraction_static=0.88`, FlashMLA Sparse Prefill, FlashMLA KV Decode, and 8192-token chunks. Base CP8 disables cache sharding and supports about 380K tokens in this configuration. Shared KV uses `--max-total-tokens 1200000` as a test limit; this configured limit is not the architectural capacity ratio. Base CP8 uses `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 24` to fit its maximum capacity. All other workload and backend arguments match. **Metric:** mean end-to-end latency over three measured requests after one warmup request and a cache flush. This is a mean, not P90. With output length 1, E2E latency is used as Prefill latency. Actual concurrency is 0.995-1.000 and cache hit rate is 0% for every row. | Input | Base CP8 | Shared KV | Shared vs Base CP8 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4K | 399.87 ms | 406.91 ms | +1.76% | | 32K | 2,891.98 ms | 2,913.81 ms | +0.75% | | 64K | 5,869.68 ms | 5,925.54 ms | +0.95% | | 128K | 12,331.04 ms | 12,457.69 ms | +1.03% | | 256K | 27,087.90 ms | 27,591.12 ms | +1.86% | | 512K | N/A (capacity) | 66,010.15 ms | N/A | | 1M | N/A (capacity) | 165,565.18 ms | N/A | The 4K-to-256K rows are matched performance comparisons. The 512K and 1M rows demonstrate the additional capacity and are not Base CP8 latency comparisons.
Server and benchmark commands ```bash SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python:$PWD/sgl-kernel/python \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30080 \ --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsa \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \ --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \ --max-total-tokens 1200000 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --skip-server-warmup \ --enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30080 \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --model /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --num-prompts 3 --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len ${INPUT_LEN} --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf \ --tokenize-prompt --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache \ --cache-report --output-details --disable-tqdm \ --seed ${SEED} --output-file ${OUTPUT_FILE} ```
### L2 HiCache With a 150K-token L1, `hicache_ratio=10`, page-first layout, `write_through`, kernel IO, and no L3, each rank allocates 11.57 GB for its owner pages. CP8 provides one aggregate 92.56 GB / 23,528-page L2 cache instead of eight replicated logical copies. An A/B1/B2/A test uses three distinct 100K prompts so B1 and B2 evict A from L1. Restoring A reports `device=0, host=99968`, reproduces `Paris` / token `[12089]`, and reduces E2E latency from 10,509.29 ms to 770.31 ms (-92.67%). No L3 backend is configured or observed. ## Correctness - Fixed short, 100K, and 128K output-1 prompts match Base CP8; a short semantic decode also matches. - GSM8K500 24-shot completion scores `0.956` against the registered `0.94` threshold. MMLU64 sanity scores `0.796875`, equal to ordinary Base. - Targeted CPU tests pass `90` cases, CP8 multi-GPU tests pass `3` cases, and the L2 host-only restore reproduces the cold answer. All changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass. Co-authored with [@foraxe](https://github.com/foraxe) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #30150164674](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30150164674) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30150164598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30150164598)

signals.title: [NVIDIA] Support flashinfer Mega Moe
signals.text: Fork from https://github.com/djns99/sglang/tree/djns99/mega_moe_flashinfer @djns99 is the main author of this PR. ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. # MoE backend benchmark: `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` (baseline) vs `flashinfer_megamoe` Benchmark of the DeepSeek-V4-Flash NVFP4 model comparing two MoE backend configurations on the serving path. `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` (trtllm routed MoE runner + flashinfer A2A) is used as the **baseline**; `flashinfer_megamoe` is the compared configuration. All deltas are reported relative to the trtllm_routed baseline. ## Environment - Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` - Parallelism: TP=4, DP=4, DP-attention enabled (`attn_dp_size=4`, so per-rank decode batch = `max_running_requests / 4`) - 1x node, same hardware for both runs ## Server commands **Baseline — `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer \ --max-running-requests 1024 ``` **Compared — `flashinfer_megamoe`:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --max-running-requests 1024 ``` ## Client command ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $((5 * C)) \ --max-concurrency C # C in {32, 128, 1024}, num-prompts = 5 x C ``` ## Results ### Output token throughput (tok/s, higher is better) | max_conc | trtllm_routed (baseline) | megamoe | Δ (megamoe vs baseline) | |---------:|-------------------------:|--------:|------------------------:| | 32 | 876.88 | 674.21 | −23.1% | | 128 | 1215.93 | 1092.54 | −10.1% | | 1024 | 3223.92 | 3245.20 | +0.7% | ### Mean TPOT (ms, lower is better) | max_conc | trtllm_routed (baseline) | megamoe | Δ (megamoe vs baseline) | |---------:|-------------------------:|--------:|------------------------:| | 32 | 34.49 | 38.77 | +12.4% | | 128 | 109.93 | 106.83 | −2.8% | | 1024 | 422.61 | 394.92 | −6.6% | ### Full metrics | config | max_conc | out_tput (tok/s) | mean TPOT (ms) | median TPOT (ms) | p99 TPOT (ms) | achieved conc | mean TTFT (ms) | |--------|---------:|-----------------:|---------------:|-----------------:|--------------:|--------------:|---------------:| | trtllm_routed | 32 | 876.88 | 34.49 | 33.32 | 102.42 | 28.76 | 421 | | megamoe | 32 | 674.21 | 38.77 | 40.27 | 78.13 | 26.53 | 321 | | trtllm_routed | 128 | 1215.93 | 109.93 | 104.71 | 395.33 | 116.12 | 797 | | megamoe | 128 | 1092.54 | 106.83 | 101.22 | 345.54 | 103.68 | 776 | | trtllm_routed | 1024 | 3223.92 | 422.61 | 343.54 | 2429.78 | 994.81 | 3142 | | megamoe | 1024 | 3245.20 | 394.92 | 322.13 | 2356.07 | 951.20 | 3261 | ## Takeaways - **Low/mid concurrency (c32, c128): `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` wins on throughput** — +23% at c32 and +11% at c128 output token throughput, with comparable or better median TPOT. It also sustains higher achieved concurrency (28.8/116.1 vs 26.5/103.7), i.e. it drains the request queue faster. - **High concurrency (c1024): the two are effectively tied on throughput** (3224 vs 3245 tok/s, +0.7% for megamoe — within run-to-run noise). At this point both are decode-bound / saturated (achieved conc < target, p99 TPOT ~7x median), so the MoE backend is no longer the bottleneck. - **TPOT crossover:** megamoe has slightly lower mean TPOT at c1024 (−6.6%) but a worse p99 tail at low load (c32: 102 ms vs 78 ms). trtllm_routed gives more consistent per-token latency at low concurrency. - **Net:** `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` is the better default for latency-sensitive / low-to-mid concurrency serving; at saturation the choice is throughput-neutral. ## FlashInfer MegaMOE env knobs This PR exposes `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE` for the FlashInfer NVFP4 MegaMOE path. It selects the cross-rank combine wire format passed to `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig.combine_dtype`. Supported values: - `bf16`: default, exact combine path. - `mxfp8`: quantized combine traffic with a small accuracy tradeoff. - `nvfp4`: lower combine traffic with a small accuracy tradeoff. Example: ```bash SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE=nvfp4 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe ``` `mxfp8` and `nvfp4` are incompatible with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=1`; server args validation now rejects that combination early. > Note: the `flashinfer_megamoe` in-kernel FC2-reduce variant (`SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=1`) was excluded from this comparison due to a known issue and is not reflected here. Update 7/27/2026: ## MoE backend comparison — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4, TP4/DP4/EP4 Baseline: `trtllm`. Positive throughput and negative latency are both wins. Tokens/rank = per-DP-rank prefill chunk (DP attention routes each request wholly to one rank; `--chunked-prefill-size` is divided by `dp_size` internally). ## Prefill ### 2048 tokens/rank (input len 2048, concurrency 128) | Backend | Input tput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 38,884 | 3,084 | 3,233 | 4,104 | | **deepgemm megamoe** | **46,117** | **2,572** | **2,719** | **3,372** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 42,324 | 2,952 | 3,018 | 3,849 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 41,291 | 3,036 | 3,122 | 3,955 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4 | 42,408 | 2,953 | 3,044 | 3,838 | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Input tput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---|---| | **deepgemm megamoe** | **+18.60%** | **-16.59%** | **-15.88%** | **-17.84%** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +8.85% | -4.28% | -6.65% | -6.21% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +6.19% | -1.57% | -3.43% | -3.63% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4 | +9.06% | -4.23% | -5.84% | -6.48% | > Note: trtllm/deepgemm rows are 640 requests (676,871 input tokens); the flashinfer rows are > 1,280 requests (1,327,019 input tokens). Same input len and concurrency, so the rates are > comparable, but the request counts differ. ### 8192 tokens/rank (input len 8192, 640 requests, 2,665,479 input tokens, concurrency 128) | Backend | Input tput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 151,213 | 3,137 | 3,339 | 4,361 | | deepgemm megamoe | 154,359 | 3,047 | 3,286 | 4,163 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 162,342 | 2,945 | 3,159 | 4,146 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 165,658 | 2,831 | 3,018 | 3,835 | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **169,175** | **2,745** | **2,905** | **3,753** | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Input tput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | +2.08% | -2.84% | -1.58% | -4.52% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +7.36% | -6.10% | -5.39% | -4.93% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +9.55% | -9.73% | -9.60% | -12.06% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+11.88%** | **-12.50%** | **-13.00%** | **-13.93%** | ## Decode Input len 32, output len 1024, 10,240 requests, concurrency 8192, 5,256,337 generated tokens. | Backend | Output tput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 8,783 | 795.2 | 727.4 | 2,244.7 | | deepgemm megamoe | 8,620 | **762.8** | 721.3 | **1,944.3** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 8,832 | 783.1 | 722.0 | 2,167.6 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 8,849 | 780.0 | 717.7 | 2,182.1 | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **8,886** | 776.6 | **715.8** | 2,151.7 | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Output tput | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT | P99 TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | -1.86% | **-4.08%** | -0.84% | **-13.38%** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +0.55% | -1.53% | -0.75% | -3.44% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +0.75% | -1.91% | -1.33% | -2.79% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+1.17%** | -2.34% | -1.60% | -4.14% | ## Takeaways - **Prefill: the best backend depends on tokens/rank.** deepgemm wins at 2048 tok/rank (+18.6% throughput, -16.6% mean TTFT) but only edges trtllm at 8192 tok/rank (+2.1%). flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe is the reverse: +9% at 2048, +11.9% at 8192. - **Prefill: the flashinfer variant ranking does not hold across sizes.** At 8192 tok/rank it is `plain < ikr < combine_nvfp4`. At 2048 tok/rank, `plain` and `combine_nvfp4` are tied (+8.85% vs +9.06%, mean TTFT within 2 ms) and `ikr` is weakest (+6.19%). - **Decode is nearly a wash on throughput.** All backends land within ±2% of trtllm (8,620-8,886 tok/s), far tighter than the prefill spread. At concurrency 8192 this workload is memory-bound, so the MoE kernel is not the bottleneck. - **Decode tail latency is where backends separate.** deepgemm cuts P99 TPOT by 13.4% and mean TPOT by 4.1%, at the cost of 1.9% throughput — the only backend that trades throughput for tail latency. flashinfer improves both modestly. - **combine_nvfp4 is the best flashinfer variant in decode**, leading on every metric (+1.17% throughput, -2.34% mean TPOT), reproducing the 8192 tok/rank prefill ordering. - **Overall recommendation:** `flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4` for large-prefill and decode-heavy serving; `deepgemm megamoe` if small-prefill throughput or decode P99 dominates. ## Reproduce `<VARIANT-SELECTOR>` below is whatever selects plain / ikr / combine_nvfp4 — it is not a server arg (all three record `moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_megamoe`). ### Decode — flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe ```bash # server python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --max-running-requests 8192 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 # <VARIANT-SELECTOR> # client python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 10240 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 8192 ``` The trtllm baseline is the same command with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer`. | Backend | Input tput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | +2.08% | -2.84% | -1.58% | -4.52% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +7.36% | -6.10% | -5.39% | -4.93% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +9.55% | -9.73% | -9.60% | -12.06% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+11.88%** | **-12.50%** | **-13.00%** | **-13.93%** | ## Decode Input len 32, output len 1024, 10,240 requests, concurrency 8192, 5,256,337 generated tokens. | Backend | Output tput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 8,783 | 795.2 | 727.4 | 2,244.7 | | deepgemm megamoe | 8,620 | **762.8** | 721.3 | **1,944.3** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 8,832 | 783.1 | 722.0 | 2,167.6 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 8,849 | 780.0 | 717.7 | 2,182.1 | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **8,886** | 776.6 | **715.8** | 2,151.7 | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Output tput | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT | P99 TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | -1.86% | **-4.08%** | -0.84% | **-13.38%** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +0.55% | -1.53% | -0.75% | -3.44% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +0.75% | -1.91% | -1.33% | -2.79% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+1.17%** | -2.34% | -1.60% | -4.14% | ## Takeaways - **Prefill: the best backend depends on tokens/rank.** deepgemm wins at 2048 tok/rank (+18.6% throughput, -16.6% mean TTFT) but only edges trtllm at 8192 tok/rank (+2.1%). flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe is the reverse: +9% at 2048, +11.9% at 8192. - **Prefill: the flashinfer variant ranking does not hold across sizes.** At 8192 tok/rank it is `plain < ikr < combine_nvfp4`. At 2048 tok/rank, `plain` and `combine_nvfp4` are tied (+8.85% vs +9.06%, mean TTFT within 2 ms) and `ikr` is weakest (+6.19%). - **Decode is nearly a wash on throughput.** All backends land within ±2% of trtllm (8,620-8,886 tok/s), far tighter than the prefill spread. At concurrency 8192 this workload is memory-bound, so the MoE kernel is not the bottleneck. - **Decode tail latency is where backends separate.** deepgemm cuts P99 TPOT by 13.4% and mean TPOT by 4.1%, at the cost of 1.9% throughput — the only backend that trades throughput for tail latency. flashinfer improves both modestly. - **combine_nvfp4 is the best flashinfer variant in decode**, leading on every metric (+1.17% throughput, -2.34% mean TPOT), reproducing the 8192 tok/rank prefill ordering. - **Overall recommendation:** `flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4` for large-prefill and decode-heavy serving; `deepgemm megamoe` if small-prefill throughput or decode P99 dominates. ## Reproduce `<VARIANT-SELECTOR>` below is whatever selects plain / ikr / combine_nvfp4 — it is not a server arg (all three record `moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_megamoe`). ### Decode — flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe ```bash # server python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --max-running-requests 8192 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 # <VARIANT-SELECTOR> # client python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 1024 \ --num-prompts 10240 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 8192 ``` The trtllm baseline is the same command with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer`. ### Prefill 8192 tokens/rank — flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe ```bash # server python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --max-running-requests 1024 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 # <VARIANT-SELECTOR> # client python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang --model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 \ --num-prompts 640 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 128 ``` For the 2048 tokens/rank point, use `--chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192` on the server and `--random-input-len 2048 --num-prompts 1280` on the client. <details> <summary>Setup & caveats</summary> - `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, `page_size=256`, EP4, dp-attention enabled - Best run per metric across repeats (max throughput, min latency) - Repeat counts vary: prefill flashinfer variants 2-6 runs each, trtllm/deepgemm 1-2 runs; decode is a single run per backend - Prefill 2048 tok/rank: the plain/combine_nvfp4 throughput gap (~200 tok/s) is inside the run-to-run spread (~1,100 tok/s), so treat those two as tied rather than ranked - Decode: single run per backend. The flashinfer variants span only 0.6% in throughput and 0.8% in mean TPOT, so their relative ordering is suggestive, not established. The deepgemm P99 TPOT win (-13.4%) is large enough to be credible from one run. - Server commands above are reconstructed from the recorded `server_args`; `mem_fraction_static` was auto-derived (0.8 decode, 0.681 / 0.876 prefill) and is not passed explicitly - FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE point to the autotuned configs. </details> Remaining soft spot: every decode number is a single run, and the three FlashInfer variants differ by well under 1% in throughput. If you want the decode ranking to hold up in review, 2–3 repeats per variant would settle it; the deepgemm P99 result is the only decode finding that stands on its own. ## Accuracy — GSM8K (8-shot, 1316 questions) ```bash python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-shots 8 --num-questions 1316 --parallel 1316 ``` | Backend | Accuracy | vs baseline | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tput (tok/s) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 0.948 | - | 0.000 | 18.155 | 6,912 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 0.956 | +0.8 pt | 0.000 | 17.773 | 7,041 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 0.951 | +0.3 pt | 0.000 | 18.563 | 6,805 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4 | 0.956 | +0.8 pt | 0.000 | 18.482 | 6,749 | **No accuracy regression.** All three flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe variants match or slightly exceed the trtllm baseline, with zero invalid outputs. At n=1316 the binomial standard error is ~0.6 pt, so the +0.3 to +0.8 pt differences are within noise — the variants should be read as accuracy- equivalent to the baseline, not better than it. > The latency/throughput columns here are not a perf signal: an ~18 s run at `--parallel 1316` is > dominated by warm-up and scheduling, and the ordering contradicts the 10-minute decode benchmark > above. Use the decode section for throughput and TPOT. ## Update 7/29/2026 — latest 2048 tokens/rank prefill rerun Workload: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4, 2048 tokens/rank prefill, output len 1, 640 requests, max concurrency 128. | Backend / config | Input tput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P95 TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4, without autotune | 46,686.44 | 10,017.09 | 10,971.72 | 13,067.52 | 13,739.66 | | deepgemm megamoe | 51,865.66 | 8,959.21 | 9,848.21 | **11,661.31** | **12,296.46** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4, with autotuned config | **53,150.67** | **8,592.50** | **9,150.89** | 12,980.44 | 13,935.91 | Takeaway: in this latest setup, the autotuned `combine_nvfp4` config improves throughput and average TTFT over the non-autotuned `combine_nvfp4` path (+13.8% input throughput, -14.2% mean TTFT). Against `deepgemm megamoe`, autotuned `combine_nvfp4` has slightly higher input throughput (+2.5%) and lower mean TTFT (-4.1%), while `deepgemm megamoe` has better tail latency (-10.2% P95 TTFT, -11.8% P99 TTFT). ### CI States <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32111934708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32111934708)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32197714922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32197714922)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [dLLM] Decouple prefill chunk size from decode block size
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR addresses the long-prefill optimization proposed in #24644 and #24645. Previously, dLLM prefill and decode shared the same `block_size` (typically 32). As a result, a long prompt could advance by only one decode block per scheduler round, causing excessive scheduling overhead and underutilizing the GPU. This PR decouples the maximum prefill chunk size from the fixed decode block size: - decode still processes exactly one `block_size` block per request; - pure prefill can process multiple aligned blocks in one scheduler round; - the non-aligned prompt tail is handled together with masks by the following decode block. ### Execution-mode separation Pure-prefill requests intentionally use the regular `ForwardMode.EXTEND`, while decode requests continue to use `ForwardMode.DLLM_EXTEND`. Pure prefill has a dynamic extend length and commits only real prompt KV; decode must preserve the fixed `block_size` dLLM semantics and its dedicated CUDA Graph path. **This separation is a key correctness point for review.** The scheduler must determine the final request phase before it constructs the phase-aware `PrefillAdder` and selects the forward mode. A stale or prematurely selected prefill phase could incorrectly send a decode request through regular `EXTEND` instead of `DLLM_EXTEND`. ### Phase-selection correctness problems addressed This PR also fixes two ordering issues exposed by multi-block prefill: 1. `determine_dllm_phase()` previously ran with stale `prefix_indices`. Prefix-cache matching could update the matched prefix without reclassifying the request, so a prompt-tail-plus-mask block could remain incorrectly classified as pure prefill. Phase determination now runs after cache matching has finalized `prefix_indices`. 2. `get_new_batch_dllm()` previously selected `is_prefill`, created the adder, and selected the forward mode before incoming requests were fully prepared. Even if `process_dllm_incoming_reqs()` later changed a request to decode, the current round had already been configured as prefill. All managed dLLM requests are now collected and prepared before phase selection, so the adder and forward mode are constructed from the final cache-matched phases. Related to #24644, #24645. ## Modifications ### Configurable multi-block prefill - Add an optional `prefill_block_size` field to `--dllm-algorithm-config`. - Add `--dllm-prefill-block-size` as a command-line override for the YAML `prefill_block_size` value. - Default `prefill_block_size` to `block_size` to preserve the existing behavior. - Require `prefill_block_size >= block_size` and divisibility by `block_size`. - Require users to explicitly pass `--attention-backend flashinfer` when `prefill_block_size > block_size`, because multi-block dLLM prefill currently depends on FlashInfer's custom attention-mask support. - Reject unsupported attention backend combinations at startup instead of silently using incorrect attention semantics. The existing single-block behavior (`prefill_block_size == block_size`) is unaffected by this requirement. Example: ```yaml block_size: 32 prefill_block_size: 1024 threshold: 0.95 ``` The YAML value can be overridden without editing the configuration file: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server ... \ --dllm-prefill-block-size 1024 \ --attention-backend flashinfer ``` ### Phase-aware dLLM scheduling - Separate pure-prefill scheduling from fixed-size decode scheduling. - Fetch incoming requests and prepare all managed dLLM requests before selecting the round phase. - Re-run phase determination after prefix-cache matching updates `prefix_indices`, preventing stale-prefix phase classification. - Use phase-aware scheduler budgets: - prefill: `max_running_requests * prefill_block_size`; - decode: `max_running_requests * block_size`. - Perform prefix-cache matching before determining the dLLM phase. - Construct the phase-aware adder and select `EXTEND` versus `DLLM_EXTEND` only after the final request phases are known. - Preserve the incoming request lifecycle until admission by `PrefillAdder`. - Prefer staging requests over incoming requests within the same phase. - Prevent unadmitted requests from advancing `dllm_block_offset`. - Align pure-prefill frontiers to `block_size`. For example, with `block_size=32` and a 300-token prompt, pure prefill advances to token 288. The remaining 12 prompt tokens and 20 masks are processed by the next 32-token decode block. ### Block-wise prefill attention Multi-block dLLM prefill uses the following visibility rule, where `B` is the dLLM block size: ```text visible(q, k) = floor(k / B) <= floor(q / B) ``` The custom-mask implementation in this PR is an interim solution until FlashInfer's native [Block Extend Attention support](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2722) is merged, released, and available in SGLang's supported FlashInfer version. Once that native operator is available, this path can use its block-expanding mask semantics directly and avoid constructing and passing an additional attention mask. Migrating to the native operator is therefore the intended follow-up rather than keeping the explicit custom-mask path permanently. This provides: - bidirectional attention within the same dLLM block; - visibility into all preceding blocks; - isolation from future blocks. Masked and unmasked ragged prefill use separate persistent FlashInfer wrappers. The custom-mask wrapper is pinned to FA2, preventing an unmasked FA3 plan from being incorrectly reused for a later masked request on SM90. Unsupported combinations such as multi-block custom masks with sliding-window dispatch or multi-item scoring fail explicitly. ### Breakable prefill CUDA Graph - Run pure dLLM prefill through `ForwardMode.EXTEND`. - Allow reuse of Breakable prefill CUDA Graphs when: - CUDA and FlashInfer are used; - the prefill graph backend is Breakable; - the token count exactly matches a captured bucket; - no unsupported input mode is active. - Fall back to eager execution when these conditions are not satisfied. - Propagate dLLM prefill metadata through graph replay so the same block-wise mask is reconstructed. Exact bucket matching is required because upward padding would change dLLM bidirectional attention and KV-write semantics. ### Tests and documentation - Add scheduler/configuration tests for: - phase-aware budgets; - aligned and non-aligned prompt boundaries; - incoming request lifecycle and prefix-cache phase detection; - fixed decode blocks; - request admission and offset updates; - FlashInfer backend validation; - Breakable CUDA Graph capability checks. - Add FlashInfer attention tests for: - block-mask construction; - heterogeneous batches; - single-block fast path; - non-aligned prefixes; - masked/unmasked wrapper isolation; - ragged output against a dense reference; - prefix cascade output and LSE parity; - future-block isolation; - paged fallback parity. - Document the new server argument and scheduling/attention design. ## Accuracy Tests Validation environment: | Item | Value | | ------------------------ | --------------------------- | | GPU | 2x NVIDIA H200 143 GB | | Model | `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini` | | PyTorch | `2.11.0+cu128` | | FlashInfer | `0.6.12` | | dLLM block size | 32 | | Multi-block prefill size | 1024 | ### GSM8K quality GSM8K was evaluated with 200 examples, `temperature=0`, TP=1, and radix cache disabled. | Configuration | Score | | -------------------------- | ----- | | Main baseline | 0.895 | | Current single-block eager | 0.895 | | Multi-block eager | 0.915 | | Multi-block Breakable | 0.910 | Acceptance results: ```text multi_eager - main = +0.020 multi_eager - single_block = +0.020 multi_breakable - multi_eager = -0.005 ``` Both the multi-block eager and Breakable configurations pass the configured absolute and relative quality thresholds. Single-block and multi-block execution are not expected to be token-identical for longer prompts because changing the prefill chunk boundaries also changes kernel shapes, KV submission boundaries, and floating-point accumulation. This difference was also observed after forcing both paths to FA2. The end-to-end GSM8K quality evaluation shows no accuracy regression. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### GSM8K latency (H200, TP=1, 200 examples) | Configuration | Latency (s) | Output throughput (tok/s) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Main baseline | 65.8 | 381.0 | | Current single-block eager | 121.6 | 205.2 | | Multi-block eager | 58.6 | 435.0 | | Multi-block Breakable | 47.1 | 540.7 | Compared with the existing single-block eager configuration: - multi-block eager improves output throughput from `205.2` to `435.0 tok/s` (`2.12x`); - multi-block Breakable improves output throughput to `540.7 tok/s` (`2.63x`); - multi-block Breakable reduces evaluation latency from `121.6s` to `47.1s`. Compared with multi-block eager, Breakable prefill graph replay improves output throughput by approximately `1.24x`. ### Prefill serving matrix (H200, TP=1, exact Breakable buckets) Full matrix under `benchmark_results/pr_prefill_perf_matrix_20260720/`: - configs: `main` (`block_size=32`) + current-branch `prefill_block_size ∈ {32,128,512,1024,2048,4096}` - input lengths: `128, 256, 512, 1024, 4096, 8192, 16384` - `num_prompts=16`, `output_len=64`, `max_concurrency=1`, fixed seeds (`seed = 2000 + input_len`) Input token throughput (tok/s): | input | main | pbs32 | pbs128 | pbs512 | pbs1024 | pbs2048 | pbs4096 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 128 | 528 | 416 | 451 | 438 | 441 | 441 | 442 | | 256 | 917 | 774 | 897 | 846 | 850 | 847 | 849 | | 512 | 1832 | 1545 | 1967 | 1968 | 1982 | 1989 | 1977 | | 1024 | 2563 | 2251 | 2975 | 3245 | 3250 | 3268 | 3299 | | 4096 | 4784 | 4251 | 8561 | 10759 | 12420 | 12810 | 12320 | | 8192 | 5517 | 4543 | 11845 | 18841 | 23248 | 25174 | 25671 | | 16384 | 5193 | 3757 | 13103 | 22751 | 27713 | 30709 | 29577 | vs `main` input-throughput delta at long context: | input | pbs1024 | pbs2048 | pbs4096 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4k | +160% | +168% | +158% | | 8k | +321% | +356% | +365% | | 16k | +434% | +491% | +470% | Mean TTFT (ms) at 16k: `main 2996` → `pbs1024 410` / `pbs2048 351` / `pbs4096 365`. signals.title: [Model] Add LLaDA2.2 Block Routing MoE support
signals.text: ## Motivation LLaDA2.2 uses block routing in its MoE router: each diffusion block first chooses a capacity-limited set of candidate experts, and each token then selects its top-k experts from that block-local expert set. This PR adds the SGLang serving-side implementation for that routing mode so LLaDA2 checkpoints that expose `expert_capacity` / `block_size` in their config can run through the native LLaDA2 model path. The default LLaDA2 routing path is unchanged. Block routing is enabled only when the model config has `expert_capacity`. ## Modifications - Add a two-phase Triton block top-k router in `python/sglang/srt/models/llada2.py`: - Phase 1 (`_block_aggregation_kernel`): computes block-level expert scores via max aggregation over tokens in the block, then selects `expert_capacity` allowed experts using a threshold + cumsum approach with index-based tie-breaking. - Phase 2 (`_token_topk_kernel`): each token selects its top-k experts from only the block-allowed set; weights are normalized via row-max rescaling with a uniform fallback for near-zero scores. - Wire block routing through the existing `Llada2MoeBlock` by conditionally calling `block_topk_triton` when `expert_capacity` and `block_size` are present in model config, constructing `StandardTopKOutput` for downstream compatibility. - Add a manual unit test (`test/manual/layers/moe/test_block_topk_triton.py`) comparing the Triton kernel against a pure PyTorch reference for: - Small and large expert counts (16 to 256 experts); - Various capacity constraints (tight capacity, full capacity, production-like); - Edge cases: `top_k=1` (no normalization path), `block_size=1` (per-token degenerate case); - Stress test with 256 tokens. ## Checklist - [x] Triton kernel implementation with two-phase block routing - [x] Unit tests (7 cases, all passing on GPU) - [x] End-to-end serving verification with block routing active Co-authored with @R00Kie-Liu, @AsaHIXx, @utdawn, @SolarisAdams. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31769406527](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31769406527)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31769406331](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31769406331)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [dLLM] Add JointThresholdInDel algorithm for insertion & deletion decoding
signals.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces the `JointThresholdInDel` algorithm, which extends `JointThreshold` with structural edit token support for diffusion LLMs. It enables the model to not only fill masks and refine tokens, but also **delete** positions (block shrinks) and **insert** new positions via SPLIT (block expands). This is essential for models trained with insertion and deletion capabilities (e.g., LLaDA2.2-flash with InDel training). ## Modifications ### New Algorithm: `JointThresholdInDel` - **DELETE token**: When the model predicts a DELETE token at a position, that position is removed from the block, remaining positions shift left, and the block is padded with mask tokens. - **SPLIT (insert) token**: When the model predicts a SPLIT token, the position expands into `[mask, current_token]`, allowing the model to insert new content. - **Original mask tracking (`is_orig_mask`)**: Distinguishes masks from the initial block vs. masks introduced by DELETE padding or SPLIT expansion, ensuring correct M2T scheduling. - **Anti-loop mechanism**: Detects repeated block states and deterministically injects diversity at the lowest-confidence position via `argmin`, preventing infinite loops caused by DELETE/SPLIT cycles. - **Bounded final cleanup**: When the post-edit budget is reached or the regular-update limit is exceeded, selects every remaining non-prompt mask and suppresses MASK, DELETE, and SPLIT. If token IDs change, one additional forward is performed before emitting the request so the KV cache matches the final block. - **FDFO compatible**: All iteration state is carried in the `states` dict, fully compatible with First-Done-First-Out scheduling. ### Config Changes Added `delete_token_id` and `split_token_id` to `DllmConfig`. `JointThresholdInDel` reads them from explicit checkpoint configuration, with a compatibility entry for the official `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.2-flash` checkpoint, and rejects unsupported checkpoints at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signals.title: [Do Not Merge][BCG]Use piecewise cuda graphs
signals.text: ## Motivation Inspired by SGLang's work on breaking graphs into piecewise CUDA graphs, we've built a small, standalone pure-Python package -- piecewise-cuda-graphs (https://github.com/meta-pytorch/piecewise-cuda-graphs). Our goal is to make it easily reusable across the PyTorch community, so that projects don't each have to maintain their own version. This PR swaps SGLang's in-tree piecewise CUDA graph code for the new PyTorch annex package. The behavior is identical in the context of SGLang. We'd love it if you could run your CI on this to see how it holds up in your setup. Whether or not it's a fit to merge is entirely your call -- we completely understand if you'd rather keep it in-tree, and no worries either way. Happy to iterate on anything, and thanks for taking a look! ## Modifications **Code (commit 1).** The `breakable` prefill backend's hand-maintained segmented-capture engine is replaced with the library, called directly at every site: | in-tree (removed) | `piecewise_cuda_graphs` | | --------------------------- | ----------------------- | | `BreakableCUDAGraph` | `CUDAGraphSequence` | | `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` | `piecewise_graph` | | `eager_on_graph` | `no_graph` | | `break_graph` | `force_no_graph` | `piecewise-cuda-graphs==0.1.0` is added as a dependency. Backend name, config, and CLI flags are unchanged (still `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`). **Docs (commit 2).** Updates the Breakable CUDA Graph page for the new package. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3-8B scores **0.840** on mgsm_en with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=breakable` (the integration test threshold is 0.80) -- unchanged from the in-tree engine. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No regression from the swap. Benchmarked with `bench_one_batch` on H100, this branch vs. its parent (the in-tree engine), on identical shapes (input 512, output 8, batch 1/4/16) across five models: gpt-oss-120b, Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8 (tp8), Llama-3-70B-Instruct (tp4), Llama-3-8B-Instruct, and MiniMax-M2.7 (tp4). Every prefill delta -- the only path this swap touches -- is within **+/-1.6%** and mixed in sign. Decode runs on the unchanged `full` backend. Repeating a fixed config on one build puts the harness's run-to-run variance at **~3% std**, which exceeds every prefill delta, so nothing here is distinguishable from noise. ## Limitation after rebase Rebasing onto main picked up four breakable features that `piecewise-cuda-graphs==0.1.0` cannot yet express: `barrier_fn` and `capture_stub` (both #31987), CUDA graph segment dedup (`SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_DEDUP`, default off), and XPU (#30273) all dropped here and intended as follow-ups on the package side. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32177332303](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32177332303)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32177331705](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32177331705)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
