signals.title: [AMD][Fix] Route MoRI through the Qwen MoE all-to-all path
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving **Qwen3.5 MoE** (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` on MI355X/ROCm (DP=1 / TP=2, EP=2) produced near-zero accuracy — gsm8k **0.006**. The Qwen2/Qwen3 MoE gates key on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`, which recognises **only** pure DeepEP. MoRI is a DeepEP-class backend and needs the same per-rank EP expert layout, so under MoRI the block silently fell through to the plain-TP path: - the shared expert stayed sharded by TP=2, so each token computed only one shared-expert shard and lost the other half of the contribution; - `can_fuse_shared_expert` still allowed the fusion, placing the shared expert in a **global** slot that the per-rank EP layers never allocate; - the block never entered `_forward_deepep()`, so the routed experts never went through the MoRI dispatch/combine at all. The corrupted first token then poisons everything generated after it. This PR is the correctness follow-up to #31793 (which only disabled the global-slot shared-expert fusion to get MoRI past the init crash). ## Modifications Add `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()` alongside the existing `is_deepep()` at the four gates in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: `can_fuse_shared_expert` (`:153`), the shared-expert TP override (`:328`), the EP layout branch (`:347`), and the forward dispatch (`:563`). MoRI now uses the correct per-rank EP expert layout, replicates the shared expert per rank (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`), enters `_forward_deepep()`, and each token receives the full shared-expert output. The remaining DeepEP-class backends (Mooncake, PPLX) are deliberately **not** included — they have no Qwen MoE coverage to validate against, so `is_mori()` keeps the change byte-identical to `main` for the CUDA-side backends this PR does not exercise. A CPU unit test in `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` pins that `can_fuse_shared_expert` refuses for both `deepep` and `mori`, and still fuses on plain TP. ## Two earlier changes have been removed from this PR On-hardware re-validation no longer shows either of the two bugs they targeted. ### Decode CUDA graph disable (`server_args.py`) — removed MoRI normal mode **is** CUDA-graph safe, as @Duyi-Wang said. `mori_cpp.build_args` returns an args struct whose values (input/indices pointers, `curRankNumToken`, and the preallocated shmem buffer pointers) are snapshotted per graph node by `hipModuleLaunchKernel`, and every comm buffer has fixed capacity and a stable address. The earlier "serial gsm8k 1.000 eager → 0.000 graph" reading was a misattribution of the routing bug above. With the routing gates reverted, gsm8k is **0.000 in both eager and graph** — no code state produces the eager/graph split that motivated the guard: | routing gates | decode CUDA graph | gsm8k (40q serial) | |---|---|---| | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | on | 0.000 (invalid 0.625) | | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | **off (eager)** | **0.000** (invalid 0.600) | | fixed (this PR) | on | 0.967 (60q) | The clincher: the eager number this PR originally reported (**0.935** @ parallel 200) matches the graph number measured now (**0.932** @ parallel 200) — at 2.2x the throughput. If graph replay were misrouting experts, accuracy would collapse, not match to three decimals. Disabling the decode graph also costs spec-decode acceptance, which is what regressed `test/registered/amd/test_moriep_small.py::TestMTP::test_gsm8k` (2.51 against a 2.8 bar; passes on `main` at 3.0077). Reproduced independently on Qwen3.5 with EAGLE MTP — same server, only the graph flag differs: | decode CUDA graph | accept length | |---|---| | on | **3.47 – 3.59** | | off | 2.59 – 2.91 | ### AITER eager-metadata buffer capacity (`aiter_backend.py`) — removed The `Target sizes: [111] / Tensor sizes: [112]` crash no longer reproduces, and the sizing change did not fix the remaining high-concurrency fault: with it applied, Qwen3.5 + MTP at 64 running requests still dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N`, and it does so exactly when the log shows `mamba usage: 1.00` — linear-attention state pool exhaustion, not `kv_indptr` overflow. That is a separate bug and is tracked outside this PR. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, 2x MI355X, TP2 / EP2, `--moe-a2a-backend mori` (deepep_mode normal), aiter attention, fp8 KV cache, decode CUDA graph **on**: | Questions | Parallel | Accuracy | |---|---|---| | — | — | 0.006 (before fix) | | 60 | 30 | 0.967 | | 400 | 64 | 0.925 | | 1000 | 200 | **0.932** | With EAGLE MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), 200 questions / parallel 30: accuracy **0.935**, accept length **~3.5**. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GSM8K 1000 questions / parallel 200, same config: **1552.6 tok/s** output throughput (vs 691 tok/s with the decode graph disabled). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] MiniMax-M3 : Fuse QKV+index proj for block-fp8
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation The sparse-attention QKV+index projection fusion (one GEMM instead of two) was skipped whenever MXFP8 weights are converted to block-fp8 (gfx942 always; gfx950 under SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT), because the fused holder bypasses process_weights_after_loading. Run the same block-fp8 pipeline on the concatenated weight inside _FusedQKVIndexProj. q/kv and index output sizes are 128-aligned, so converting the concatenation is equivalent to converting each proj separately. Non-block paths are unchanged (still derive the MXFP8 scale layout). signals.title: [AMD] MiniMax-M3: fuse sparse QK norm, RoPE and cache writes with AITER
signals.text: ## Motivation After the packed QKV+index projection from #32099, every MiniMax-M3 sparse attention layer still launches separate kernels for Q/K and index Q/K norm + RoPE, followed by main K/V and index-K cache writes. This PR connects AITER `fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm` to the SGLang MiniMax-M3 sparse path. It keeps the current SGLang cache contract and is opt-in: ```bash SGLANG_M3_USE_AITER_FUSED_QKNORM=1 ``` Default behavior is unchanged when the env is unset. ## Changes - Fuse main/index per-head Gemma RMSNorm, partial NeoX RoPE, main K/V cache write and index-K cache write. - Use SGLang's existing page-1 NHD, unit-scale FP8 main KV and BF16 index-K contract. - Skip the old duplicate cache-store path in both prefill and decode when the fused producer has already written the cache. - Fall back to the existing path if the AITER op, packed projection, dtype, layout or model shape is not compatible. - Keep the integration opt-in for compatibility with older AITER wheels. This only changes the sparse attention preparation/cache stage. Dense attention layers, index score/top-k, sparse GQA, output projection, MoE and all-reduce are unchanged. ## Results MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, MI355X, TP4, BF16, FP8 E4M3 KV, fixed ISL 8192 / OSL 1024. The baseline and candidate use the same four-PR stack (#32036, #32099, #32190, #32230); the fused env is the only functional difference. | concurrency | total tok/s/GPU | median TTFT (s) | median TPOT (s) | uplift vs. four-PR baseline | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 188.27 | 0.33 | 0.01 | **+5.50%** | | 2 | 343.66 | 0.53 | 0.01 | **+6.77%** | | 4 | 614.34 | 0.88 | 0.01 | **+5.95%** | | 8 | 991.32 | 1.48 | 0.02 | **+4.78%** | | 16 | 1640.26 | 2.69 | 0.02 | **+5.74%** | | 32 | 2330.60 | 5.11 | 0.03 | **+5.99%** | | 64 | 3236.21 | 9.96 | 0.03 | **+3.89%** | | 128 | 4041.67 | 19.77 | 0.05 | **+3.26%** | | 256 | 4758.47 | 39.16 | 0.08 | **+3.05%** | The fused path is faster at every tested concurrency from 1 to 256. ## Accuracy MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, MI355X TP4, 5-shot GSM8K, 1319 questions, `temperature=0`: | path | accuracy | correct | invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Existing path | 0.846 | 1116/1319 | 0.001 | | Fused path | 0.864 | 1140/1319 | 0.001 | Both runs completed successfully with no runtime traceback during evaluation. The fused path did not regress aggregate GSM8K accuracy. ## Test configuration ```bash HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7 \ SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_M3_USE_AITER_FUSED_QKNORM=1 \ SGLANG_OPT_USE_BF16_ROUTER_GEMM=0 \ SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT=1 \ SGLANG_MXFP8_MOE_KEEP_NATIVE=1 \ SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=1 \ SGLANG_M3_ALLOW_CUSTOM_AR=1 \ ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 \ ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --quantization mxfp8 --dtype bfloat16 --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --context-length 32768 --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Benchmark workload: random dataset, request rate `inf`, ignore EOS, 10x concurrency prompts and 2x concurrency warmups. ## Dependencies and scope - Requires the unit-scale AITER contract from `ROCm/aiter#4362`. - Directly builds on the packed projection from #32099. - Tested on top of #32036, #32099, #32190 and #32230. - The tested SGLang version resolves `moe_runner_backend` to Triton in both baseline and candidate, so the numbers above only claim the fused attention producer change. ## Checklist - signals.title: [PP&Sepc] enable dspark under pipeline parallelism (deepseek-v4 & kimi-k3)
signals.text: ## Motivation roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11857, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30344, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607 Our previous PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31139) enabled PP + EAGLE support. Testing showed DSpark speculation performs far better than EAGLE, so this PR builds on it to add DSpark + PP compatibility. This PR depends on the previous one and should be merged afterwards. DSpark's verify path is structurally different from EAGLE's (per-layer aux hidden capture, linear block verify, confidence-driven budget), so it could not reuse the EAGLE PP machinery verbatim. This PR lifts that ban and makes DSpark run under PP, targeting DeepSeek-V4-Flash + the bundled DSpark draft checkpoint. ## Modifications The core idea mirrors the EAGLE PP design — the draft model lives only on the last PP rank, every rank runs its own target verify forward, and the draft proposal is relayed across stages so each rank rebuilds an identical verify context. The DSpark-specific work is making the per-layer aux-hidden capture and the linear block verify cross the PP boundary correctly. 1. **Per-rank draft proposal carrier (`DSparkPPVerifyInputRaw`).** A new spec input type carries the last rank's draft / confidence / accounting fields (bonus tokens, draft tokens, new seq lens, confidence, accept/cap-trim/verify lens) across the PP ring. Every rank rebuilds an identical verify layout from the same source each iteration, so all PP ranks produce byte-identical verify windows. It mixes in the shared `DFlashDecodePrepareMixin` so the non-last rank's verify forward (which reads `verify_cache_loc` from `req_to_token`) pre-allocates KV headroom exactly like the last rank. Linear verify reuses the formal `req_to_token` slots, so `accept_index` is always `None` and the token-move step in `batch_result_processor` is skipped automatically. 2. **Per-layer aux hidden capture across PP stages (`deepseek_v4.py`).** DSpark's draft needs per-layer aux hidden states (`dspark_aux_hidden_states`), but each PP rank only executes layers in its own `[start_layer, end_layer)` range. The aux list is now stacked as `[L, num_tokens, hidden]`, relayed downstream under the `"dspark_aux"` key in `PPProxyTensors`, and rebuilt in global layer order on the last rank (upstream layers first, then local captures). `set_dspark_layers_to_capture` no longer early-returns on non-last ranks, so every rank registers its own capture range. 3. **PP-aware verify forward.** `pp_proxy_tensors` is threaded through `TargetVerifyExecutor.run` / `run_non_compact` so the target verify forward relay hidden states along the PP ring on every rank. `TargetVerifyResult` carries `pp_hidden_states_proxy_tensors` back to the scheduler. Logits adjustments (penalizer / vocab mask / logit bias) are now gated on `result.logits_output is not None`, since non-last ranks never sample and their logits output is `None`. 4. **Embed / weight loading split (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`).** The DSpark draft used to borrow `embed_tokens` from the target. Under PP the last rank builds its own `VocabParallelEmbedding` and only `lm_head` is shared from the target; `attach_shared_modules` now takes `embed_tokens: Optional` so the PP path passes `None` and the draft keeps its locally-built embedding. Weight-name remapping keeps `embed_tokens.weight` on the last PP rank. 5. **PP proxy buffer sizing (`base_runner.py`).** The static `pp_proxy_tensors` buffers are allocated by max token count, not batch size, so the dummy / capture buffer fits the verify-token-expanded shape `[num_tokens, *hidden]` produced under speculative decoding. 6. **Planner / draft fixes for the relayed layout.** `alloc_verify_window` and `DraftBlockProposer` derive `prefix_lens` from the verify window's anchor position instead of `batch.seq_lens`, because the last rank's re-propose pass builds the next window from post-iter seq lens while `batch.seq_lens` is still the pre-iter value. The planner forces `RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=STATIC` and non-compact (eager) verify under PP, since the confidence-driven ragged scheduler and the cuda-graph compact path only run on the last rank and cannot keep cross-rank layout identity. Supporting changes: `draft_worker_common.build_draft_tp_worker` accepts a `pp_global_random_seed` so the draft sampler on the last rank is seeded consistently with the target; `speculative_hook` replaces the blanket `pp_size != 1` ban with a narrower "PP + DP-attention unsupported" check (DP-attention partitions the batch, which conflicts with the PP requirement that every rank see an identical batch). ### Limitations asserted now - **PP + DP-attention** is rejected. Only `--dp-size 1` is permitted under PP. - **PP forces static verify and eager (non-cuda-graph) verify** ## Accuracy Tests Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 GSM8K accuracy (200 examples, 5-shot, temperature=0): | Configuration | GSM8K Accuracy (%) | |---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 98.00 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 98.50 | ## Speed Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; three PP2+TP4 configs: - **PP2-TP4** — PP2+TP4, no spec (baseline) - **PP2-TP4-MTP314** — PP2+TP4 + EAGLE (`speculative-num-steps=3`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens=4`) - **PP2-TP4-DSpark** — PP2+TP4 + DSpark (this PR) bench_serving: `--dataset-name random` with local ShareGPT path (`--dataset-path /datasets/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json`), `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts 5`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--random-output-len 1024`, `--seed 42`; 3 rounds per point, reporting the min. **TPOT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 11.11 | 11.14 | 11.13 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 5.39 | 5.43 | 5.65 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 2.30 | 2.34 | 2.38 | **Average accepted length (tokens / iter)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 2.75 | 2.90 | 2.83 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 4.91 | 4.85 | 4.87 | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: Amd/dsv4 shared experts fusion top6
signals.text: # [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: fix shared-experts fusion for top-6 ## Summary Enabling shared-experts fusion (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) for DeepSeek-V4 on MI355X (gfx950) crashed at startup. Two independent issues in the fused topk / append path assume DeepSeek-V3 conventions (fp32 correction bias, power-of-two topk) that DeepSeek-V4 (bf16 correction bias, **top-6** routing) violates. This PR fixes both so the fused path runs, and shows it is a **~+8–11% output-throughput win at low concurrency with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`** — in `biased_topk_jit_kernel_impl`, cast `correction_bias` to `float32` before calling `moe_fused_gate`. DeepSeek-V4 stores `e_score_correction_bias` in bf16 (for the aiter sqrtsoftplus topk path), but `moe_fused_gate` asserts a float32 bias (`AssertionError: bias must be float32`). Only the fused-gate branch (taken when `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`) is touched. - **`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`** — `_fused_append_shared_experts_kernel` indexed the routed/shared lanes with `tl.arange(0, K)` / `tl.arange(0, S)`, which Triton only accepts for power-of-two ranges. DeepSeek-V4 routes top-6 (`K=6`), so it failed with `ValueError: arange's range must be a power of 2`. The kernel now iterates over `next_power_of_2(K)` / `next_power_of_2(S)` blocks with masking, mirroring the existing `_fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights_kernel` sibling. Behavior is unchanged for power-of-two `K`. - **`test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py`** — new unit test covering non-power-of-two `K`/`S` (incl. the DSV4 `K=6` case) against a pure-torch golden reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, Fusion = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py -q 3 passed, 7 subtests passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 2000 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | fusion | |----:|:--------:|:------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.943 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.937 | | 3 | 0.936 | 0.940 | | **avg** | **0.939** | **0.940** | Invalid ≈ 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy is preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | fusion (tok/s) | Δ | |------------:|:----------------:|:--------------:|:-----:| | 1 | 69.59 | 77.06 | **+10.7%** | | 2 | 122.31 | 135.33 | **+10.6%** | | 4 | 216.26 | 238.91 | **+10.5%** | | 8 | 366.29 | 403.37 | **+10.1%** | | 16 | 569.47 | 613.60 | **+7.7%** | ### Commands used Server (per config; `$FLAG` = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` or `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`): ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend dsv4 --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 --max-running-requests 16 \ --context-length 10240 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 $FLAG ``` Accuracy: ```bash python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 ``` Performance (per concurrency `C` in 1 2 4 8 16): ```bash python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` no longer crashes for DeepSeek-V4 (top-6) on gfx950. - [x] New unit test `test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py` passes (non-pow2 K/S incl. K=6). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.940 vs 0.939). - [x] Output throughput improves ~+8–11% at concurrency 1–16 (TP4, 8k/1k). - [x] Power-of-two `K` behavior unchanged (regression guard in the unit test). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32142107014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32142107014)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32142106609](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32142106609)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [SM120] Add optional b12x PCIe all-reduce (one-shot + fused RMSNorm + FP8 DMA ring)
signals.text: ## Motivation On Blackwell workstation / server parts (SM120 & SM121 — RTX PRO 6000, RTX 6000D, RTX 50-series, GB10) the GPUs are connected over PCIe with no NVLink. The per-layer tensor-parallel all-reduce therefore dominates both decode latency and long-prompt prefill: on 8x RTX 6000D running GLM-5.2-NVFP4, NCCL needs 45 us for a 4 KB all-reduce and 344 us for 64 KB, which is most of the per-token budget at low batch sizes. [`b12x`](https://pypi.org/project/b12x/) (Apache-2.0) is an SM120/SM121-only CuTe DSL kernel library that ships IPC-backed PCIe all-reduce runtimes for exactly this topology. This PR wires two of them into SGLang behind an opt-in flag. ## What this adds A new `B12xPCIeCommunicator` and a three-tier dispatch inside `GroupCoordinator._all_reduce`: | message size | path | |---|---| | `<= 8 MB` | b12x PCIe **one-shot** all-reduce (decode-sized hidden states) | | `8 MB .. 256 MB` | b12x PCIe **DMA ring**, optional FP8 wire format (prefill chunks) | | otherwise | existing NCCL path, unchanged | The one-shot runtime also exposes a fused `all-reduce + residual add + RMSNorm`, plugged into the existing `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm` coordinator hook that AITER already uses (`layers/communicator.py` + `layers/layernorm.py`). That kernel is specialized for `<= 36` rows, so the dispatch helpers cap on token count and fall back when it does not apply — including an explicit all-reduce fallback in `_forward_with_allreduce_fusion`, since the caller has already skipped its own all-reduce when it takes the fusion path. ## Safety / blast radius - Off by default: `SGLANG_B12X_PCIE_AR` and `SGLANG_B12X_PCIE_DMA` are `EnvBool(False)`. - The communicator is only constructed for the **tensor-parallel** group (other groups would just pin IPC buffers). - `b12x` is an optional dependency; when it is not installed the setup logs a warning and everything stays on NCCL. No changes to any default code path. - Every tier re-checks dtype / contiguity / size and returns to NCCL when the kernel declines. ## Results GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 8x RTX 6000D (SM120, PCIe), driver 595.71.05, KV cache FP8, greedy, prefix caching off. **Kernel microbenchmark** (8 ranks, NCCL vs b12x one-shot): 4 KB 45.0 -> 7.3 us (6.1x), 12 KB 58.5 -> 15.3 us (3.8x), 64 KB 344.5 -> 38.5 us (8.9x). **TP8 decode** (ISL 1 / OSL 256), median TPOT / output tok/s: | bs | baseline (NCCL) | + b12x | |---|---|---| | 1 | 23.9 ms / 41 | **14.7 ms / 66** | | 8 | 70.6 ms / 112 | **29.8 ms / 264** | | 32 | 105.8 ms / 300 | **69.2 ms / 457** | **TP8 e2e 8K** (ISL 8192 / OSL 64), median TTFT: `6103 ms -> 1384 ms` (DMA ring tier). **TP4xPP2 + MTP, 64K** (ISL 65536 / OSL 1024), bs1: TTFT `11.5 s -> 9.3 s`, TPOT `10.3 ms -> 9.5 ms`, accept length 3.00. **Accuracy**: GSM8K (20 questions) stays at 0.900 for both TP8 and TP4xPP2+MTP — identical to the NCCL baseline — with `Invalid 0.000`, and greedy output matches token-for-token on a fixed prompt. ## Test plan - [x] TP8 and TP4xPP2(+MTP) launch with both tiers active (8/8 ranks report one-shot + DMA enabled, no init failures) - [x] Communicator is built for the TP group only (`world=4` under TP4xPP2, PP group untouched) - [x] GSM8K 0.900 / Invalid 0.000, greedy output matches baseline - [x] decode (bs 1/8/32), e2e 8K, 64K sweeps as above - [x] Gate off (default): unchanged NCCL behaviour ## Notes for reviewers - Requires `pip install b12x` (plus `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, pulled in as a wheel dependency; kernels are JIT-compiled on first use). - The DMA ring allocates a scratch slab sized by `SGLANG_B12X_DMA_MAX_BYTES` (default 256 MB); on memory-tight setups this competes with the KV pool, so raise `--mem-fraction-static` accordingly when enabling it together with speculative decoding. - `_FUSED_MAX_ROWS = 36` mirrors the current kernel limit and is duplicated in `communicator.py` as `_B12X_FUSED_MAX_ROWS`; happy to expose it from the package instead if maintainers prefer. - This is orthogonal to #30775 (PP x speculative decoding). Stacking both is what produces the 64K number above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32143670090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32143670090)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32143669597](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32143669597)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NPU] Enable non-greedy MTP sampling
signals.text: ## Motivation NPU MTP verification currently uses greedy argmax for non-greedy requests. Consequently, `temperature`, `top_k`, and `top_p` do not take effect during speculative verification. With GLM-4.7-Flash on GPQA, enabling non-greedy MTP reduced the observed accuracy from approximately ~70% to ~50%. This PR enables probability-based non-greedy MTP sampling on NPU. ## Modifications - Add an explicit NPU non-greedy branch in `eagle_sample`. - Keep NPU-specific sampling logic in `srt/hardware_backend/npu/speculative/mtp_sampling.py`. - Apply temperature scaling and sequential top-k/top-p probability renormalization. - Support target-only sampling for general EAGLE trees and classic rejection sampling for `tree_topk=1` chains. - Validate input topology and probability tensors before dispatching kernels. - Preserve the existing greedy path and fail explicitly for unsupported non-greedy configurations. Sampling algorithm and kernel unit tests are covered in `sgl-kernel-npu`; no duplicate SGLang-local test is added. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `GLM-4.7-Flash` Dataset: `GPQA` | Configuration | Sampling | Before | After | |---|---|---:|---:| | NPU TP/TP+EP without MTP | `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95` | ~70% | ~70% | | NPU TP+MTP/TP+EP+MTP | `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95` | ~50% | ~70% | | NPU MTP greedy | `temperature=0`, `top_p=1` | ~50% | ~50% | The non-greedy MTP accuracy recovered to the expected range, while existing non-MTP and greedy behavior remained unchanged. before: after: ## Speed Tests and Profiling | Check | Result | |---|---| | End-to-end throughput | No measurable performance impact | | End-to-end latency | No measurable performance impact | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31466214974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31466214974) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31466214842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31466214842)

signals.title: feat(kv-events): Add component_types field to BlockStored for per-component placement tracking
signals.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routers consume `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` to track which blocks live on which tier. On hybrid models the unified radix tree keeps several independent KV components on one node — full attention, sliding window, mamba state — and evicts and restores them independently. A `BlockStored` today only says "this block is on GPU". That is ambiguous once SWA has been tombstoned off an internal node while its full KV stays resident: the router still believes the block is fully reusable and routes a request that then has to recompute the window. This adds an opt-in per-component placement dimension so a consumer can tell what is actually resident at a given medium, following the same shape as #18205 which added the `medium` field. ## Modifications Gated behind `--enable-kv-events-component-types`, off by default. 1. **Schema.** A trailing `Optional[list[str]]` on `BlockStored` plus the `KV_COMPONENT_FULL/SWA/MAMBA` wire names. `BlockRemoved` stays whole-block — a removal always means the base (full) component left the tier, so there is nothing partial to express. 2. **Plumbing.** The flag flows from `ServerArgs` through `CacheInitParams` into the cache builder, and is documented in the server arguments reference. The UMBP subscriber logs the component dimension but does not forward it; its external-KV API is keyed by `(hashes, tier)` only. 3. **Emission.** `KVCacheEventMixin` gains a `_component_types_for_page` hook defaulting to `None`; `UnifiedTreeCore` overrides it and reports residency off live tree state, anchoring the single per-leaf mamba state to the leaf's last page. 4. **Tests.** 20 unit tests in `TestUnifiedRadixCacheComponentPlacementEvents`, plus wire-layout tests in `test_kv_events.py`. Three ordering constraints shaped the implementation and are worth flagging for review: - *Gains defer, losses do not.* SWA and Mamba attach device values through barrier-applied actions (`SWARebuild`, `MambaEvictExcessPathStates`), so a node's component set is not final until those apply. Inserts collect nodes in `_InsertWalkState` and emit one snapshot per node in the TAIL step; evictions are final when the component is dropped and emit immediately. - *Emission is root-first.* SWA splits the fresh leaf at commit time, so nodes are noted in neither tree nor creation order. `_record_store_event` seeds a node's lazily computed hash chain off its parent's hash, so announcing a child first would publish it as a root block under a hash no other code path reproduces. - *Partial eviction restates, never removes.* When SWA or Mamba is tombstoned while full survives the block has not left the tier, so we restate the smaller component set. Whole-block teardowns (`_demote`, host-leaf eviction) keep emitting `BlockRemoved` and never restate. `commit_load_back` also moves its emit after every component restores, unioning each component's `nodes_to_load`; emitting on full's list alone reported a promoted block as full-only. ## Subscriber compatibility `BlockStored` is a msgspec `array_like` struct, so every field is always encoded positionally — an unset `component_types` is a trailing `nil`, not an omitted slot (pinned by `test_component_types_is_the_trailing_slot`). With the flag **off** that `nil` is exactly what a positional decoder reads for an absent optional, so subscribers are unaffected; verified against both in-tree decoders, sgl-router (which drains unknown trailing fields, `experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/kv_events/wire.rs:420`) and dynamo's kv-router. With the flag **on**, the slot holds a list. sgl-router still ignores it. dynamo's kv-router, however, shares one positional layout with vLLM in which that slot is `lora_name` (a string), so it rejects the whole event batch. This is exactly why the feature is opt-in, and enabling it against a dynamo subscriber is not supported today. Aligning the two representations — dynamo already models this as one event per KV-cache group tagged with `kv_cache_spec_kind` — is a larger cross-project change and deliberately out of scope here. Only component-aware caches honour the flag; the mixin hook returns `None` elsewhere, so `radix_cache`, `hiradix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `mamba_radix_cache` and `hi_mamba_radix_cache` are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — observability only. This touches no kernel, no model forward path, and no cache eviction or placement decision; it changes what is reported about placement, never the placement itself. Unit tests run locally across page_size 1/4/16/64/128 and the FULL, FULL+SWA, FULL+MAMBA and FULL+SWA+MAMBA configurations (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_kv_events.py`, and the radix/hiradix/swa/mamba mem_cache units): 1113 passed, 1030 skipped (config-conditional), 140 subtests passed. `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` is one of the 12 files currently deferred at module level by #31812 during the ServerArgs config-namespace migration, so those cases will not run in CI until that skip is lifted upstream; the run above was done locally with the module skip removed. The wire-layout tests live in `test_kv_events.py`, which is not deferred and does run in CI. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. With the flag off the added cost is one boolean check per store event. With it on, a per-page component scan bounded by the component count (at most 3) plus one ancestor walk per insert flush. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32145461383](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145461383)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32145460870](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145460870)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec][DSV4] perf: Skip inactive target-verify metadata tails
signals.text: ## Motivation DSV4 MTP target verification captures metadata buffers for a 1M-token maximum context. On every CUDA-graph replay, `_page_table_positions_kernel` and `_init_compressed_attn_metadata_kernel` traversed the full capture capacity even when the current sequence was short. This made two memory-bound metadata kernels a measurable part of target-verify GPU time. ## Modifications - Add CUDA-graph-safe live-prefix execution to both Triton metadata kernels. Launch grids stay static, while blocks beyond device-side live lengths exit without rewriting inactive tails. - Preserve scalar metadata updates and the required C128 sentinel for empty sequences. - Enable the optimization only for the validated default SM100 path. Alternative indexer, top-k, HiSparse, and non-CUDA paths retain full-tail initialization. - Add focused B200 replay and poisoned-tail consumer tests, plus a local non-CI CUDA-graph benchmark. ## Accuracy Tests ```bash sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 \ --num-threads 32 Run directory: /root/.sgl_eval/sgl_eval_gsm8k_20260727-052647 gsm8k: 100%|█████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 1319/1319 [03:58<00:00, 5.53it/s, acc=96.44%] == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 238.6s | 738 tok/s | 176K tokens * score = 96.44% stop_rate = 100.00% truncated_rate = 0.00% error_rate = **0.00%** ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Local B200 benchmark, verify width 4 and fixed capture capacity 1,048,577. Each request contributes four causal metadata rows, so `metadata rows = BS × 4`. Values are CUDA-graph replay p50 after 1,000 warmups and 2,000 measured replays. | BS | Metadata rows | Current max sequence length | Full tail | Live prefix | Reduction | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 4 | 1,024 | 15.872 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.6% | 2.07x | | 1 | 4 | 4,096 | 15.840 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.5% | 2.06x | | 1 | 4 | 32,768 | 15.840 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.5% | 2.06x | | 1 | 4 | 1,048,576 | 43.488 µs | 7.648 µs | 82.4% | 5.69x | | 4 | 16 | 1,024 | 15.840 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.5% | 2.06x | | 4 | 16 | 4,096 | 15.840 µs | 7.648 µs | 51.7% | 2.07x | | 4 | 16 | 32,768 | 17.856 µs | 9.664 µs | 45.9% | 1.85x | | 4 | 16 | 1,048,576 | 46.560 µs | 9.696 µs | 79.2% | 4.80x | | 8 | 32 | 1,024 | 15.840 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.5% | 2.06x | | 8 | 32 | 4,096 | 15.840 µs | 7.680 µs | 51.5% | 2.06x | | 8 | 32 | 32,768 | 17.888 µs | 9.696 µs | 45.8% | 1.84x | | 8 | 32 | 1,048,576 | 46.560 µs | 9.696 µs | 79.2% | 4.80x | | 16 | 64 | 1,024 | 15.840 µs | 9.728 µs | 38.6% | 1.63x | | 16 | 64 | 4,096 | 15.840 µs | 9.728 µs | 38.6% | 1.63x | | 16 | 64 | 32,768 | 15.872 µs | 7.712 µs | 51.4% | 2.06x | | 16 | 64 | 1,048,576 | 46.400 µs | 9.696 µs | 79.1% | 4.79x | | 32 | 128 | 1,024 | 15.840 µs | 9.696 µs | 38.8% | 1.63x | | 32 | 128 | 4,096 | 15.840 µs | 9.696 µs | 38.8% | 1.63x | | 32 | 128 | 32,768 | 17.888 µs | 9.696 µs | 45.8% | 1.84x | | 32 | 128 | 1,048,576 | 46.560 µs | 13.760 µs | 70.4% | 3.38x | main bs=1: PR bs=1: ## Validation - Focused live-prefix metadata tests: 6/6 passed. - Existing DSV4 attention suite: 18/18 passed. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32127175035](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32127175035) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32127174785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32127174785)

signals.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
signals.text: ## Summary Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`** - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once. - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native). - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`, falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`. - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact) and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch (only 2 model files differ). Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q 8 passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.947 | | 2 | 0.943 | 0.943 | | 3 | 0.937 | 0.944 | | **avg** | **0.941** | **0.945** | Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | patched (tok/s) | Δ | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | |------------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:-----:|:---:|:---:| | 4 | 216.38 | 219.66 | **+1.5%** | 17.507 | 17.242 | | 8 | 367.65 | 372.98 | **+1.4%** | 20.715 | 20.423 | | 16 | 568.64 | 579.04 | **+1.8%** | 26.460 | 25.960 | | 32 | 792.79 | 800.70 | **+1.0%** | 38.165 | 37.808 | | 64 | 1033.97 | 1042.04 | **+0.8%** | 58.854 | 58.412 | ### Commands used ```bash # Accuracy python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 # Performance (per concurrency C in 4 8 16 32 64) python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] New unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py` passes (8 passed; gfx95 numerical). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.945 vs 0.941, invalid 0.000). - [x] Output throughput improves +0.8%–1.8% at concurrency 4–64 (TP4, 8k/1k), TPOT reduced. - [x] Falls back to unfused hc_post + hc_pre when no fused kernel fires (non-gfx95 / import failure). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32085370546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085370546)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32085370376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085370376)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Bound each MI355X disagg benchmark phase
signals.text: ## Motivation `nightly-amd-mi355x-disagg` run [30237209346](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30237209346) (`dsv4flash-fp4-1k1k-1p1d-dp8ep8-mtp`) froze at 1023/1024 requests in the `conc=256` point and produced nothing for the next 2h15m, until SLURM killed the step at the wall clock and every role exited rc=143. From the run artifacts, both servers were idle and healthy the whole time — the last prefill batch was at 13:21:28, the last decode batch at 13:21:42, decode's final log line shows `#prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0`, and both answered their `/health` probe every 60s until the kill. The `smg` router started and head-finished all 1280 requests of that phase (256 warmup + 1024). Only the client was still waiting. That is possible because nothing bounds a single request: `bench_serving` waits on each response stream with no per-request deadline, and the sweep's only guard was `|| true`, which covers a phase that crashes but not one that hangs. One unterminated stream therefore costs the entire allocation, including the concurrency points that had not run yet. This PR does not diagnose why that one stream never completed; it stops that class of failure from consuming a 2.5h reservation and taking the rest of the sweep with it. ## Modifications - Run the GSM8K gate and each concurrency point under `timeout -k 30 $BENCH_PHASE_TIMEOUT` (new env knob, default 600s). Measured phase durations on the last green run of this config are 52-76s for the sweep points and ~60s for the gate, so the default is ~8x headroom. - On a timeout, record the concurrency, keep sweeping so the remaining points still produce numbers, and fail the leg at the end. - A phase that fails for any other reason keeps its previous behaviour (logged, sweep continues). The deferred failure is deliberate. The result normalizer already skips a missing `raw_conc<C>.json` with `WARN: missing ...`, and the leg only fails when the bench rc is non-zero or zero results were produced — so simply dropping a timed-out phase would have reported this failure as **green**. Exiting non-zero at the end of the sweep propagates through `bench_exit` -> `drive.sh` -> `salloc` -> `SALLOC_RC` while the partial results are still normalized and uploaded. ## Tests Shell-only change to a generated script, so it was first verified by expansion, then exercised end to end on the runner (below): - `bash -n` on the launcher. - Expanded the `bench.sh` heredoc with realistic variables and `bash -n` on the generated file, then extracted the inner single-quoted `bash -lc` block and `bash -n` on that too (the escaping inside that block is the actual risk). The substitution lands as intended: `timeout -k 30 600` baked in, `$C` / `$RC` / `$OUT` preserved for runtime. - Simulated the control flow against stub commands: healthy phases exit 0; hung phases are killed per phase, the sweep continues, and the leg exits 1; a crashing phase preserves the pre-existing continue-and-pass behaviour. - `pre-commit run --files scripts/ci/slurm/launch_mi355x.sh` clean. ## Validated on the MI355X runner Dispatched this branch at the affected leg (`dsv4flash-fp4-1k1k-1p1d-dp8ep8-mtp`, pinning the image via the `workflow_dispatch` inputs) to confirm the new budget does not perturb a healthy sweep. It did not fire in either run, and both completed all seven concurrency points: - [Run 30310490611](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30310490611) on `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260726`, the image the original hang appeared on: **success**, GSM8K 0.925, `conc=256` 1024/1024 in 64.85s. - [Run 30310514312](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30310514312) on `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`, the last image this config was green on: GSM8K 0.918, `conc=256` 1024/1024 in 64.67s. This one reads *cancelled* at the workflow level only because I cancelled it as redundant once the first run passed - the benchmark job had already finished every step and uploaded its results. The last scheduled green run of this config did `conc=256` in 64.96s, so the guard costs nothing on a healthy phase. Incidentally this also answers the triage question those runs were dispatched for: the hang does not reproduce on the image it first appeared on, so R292 looks like a rare race rather than a regression - which is the case this PR is meant to contain rather than fix. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31543110660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31543110660)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31543110390](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31543110390)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix transcription & audio-understanding for ASR/audio/speech models
signals.text: ## Motivation Fix transcription for decoder-only speech/audio models that were already present Adds /v1/audio/transcriptions support for three decoder-only speech/audio LMs, so they serve real ASR instead of falling back to the Whisper adapter: - Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct - zai-org/GLM-ASR-Nano-2512 - ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-8b ## Modifications **New transcription adapters.** Added glmasr.py, qwen2_audio.py, granite_speech.py (registered as GlmAsr / Qwen2Audio / GraniteSpeech). Each disables language detection and implements build_sampling_params (emitting temperature + a duration-scaled max_new_tokens: max(floor, int(duration_s * 15)), so long clips aren't silently truncated while short clips use a per-model floor) and build_verbose_response (no timestamp segments; "auto" default language). Without these, resolve_adapter() falls back to the Whisper adapter and injects Whisper-only params (_detect_language, forced language/task prefix) these models don't support. **Transcription-endpoint prompt handling.** The /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint sends text="", which carries no audio placeholder for the encoder features to fill. Added a per-processor _build_transcription_prompt() to qwen_audio.py / glmasr.py, and an audio branch + _build_audio_prompt() to transformers_auto.py (Granite), that render the model's audio placeholder via apply_chat_template when the request text is empty — fixing the empty-prompt failure while leaving the chat path unchanged. Also added audio_token_index to the generic processor's audio-token lookup. **Model-side audio-feature handling.** Rewrote GlmAsrForConditionalGeneration.get_audio_feature to reshape encoder output per 30s window and keep only the valid embeddings per window (derived from input_features_mask via the conv-subsampling + merge_factor downsampling), mirroring HF's get_audio_features. This keeps the emitted embedding count aligned with the inserted audio-placeholder tokens for variable-length / multi-window clips. Forced truncation=True for the Qwen2-Audio processor so clips longer than 30s are capped to the audio tower's fixed 3000-mel window instead of raising. **base_processor.py.** Added GraniteSpeechProcessor to the audio=-kwarg allowlist (its HF processor expects audio=, not the deprecated audios=). **Tests.** Added test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_transcription_adapters.py (CPU CI): adapter resolution per architecture + Whisper fallback, the max_new_tokens floor/duration-scaling boundary, and the verbose-response contract. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32207211055](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207211055)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207211005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207211005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Windowed draft-decode attention for built-in EAGLE / MTP drafts
signals.text: # [Spec] Windowed draft-decode attention for built-in EAGLE / MTP drafts ## Motivation In [arXiv:2607.21535](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535) we show that a built-in MTP draft head's full-attention KV read grows with the prefix until it dominates the decode step, and that restricting the *draft's* attention to a sink plus recent window cuts the per-decode-step cost by +28% to +44% at 1M context across three architecture families at near-unchanged acceptance, with the target still verifying every token at full attention. The same idea motivated `--speculative-draft-window-size` in #24664, but that flag reaches the drafter through the model file (`llama_eagle3.py` sets `sliding_window_size` per layer) and the backend's per-layer SWA path, so it applies to `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` checkpoints. This PR applies the window one level down, in the shared draft-decode index builder, so the built-in EAGLE / MTP (NEXTN) draft-decode path gets it on the Triton and FlashInfer draft backends with no model-file change and no second attention wrapper — the draft simply gets a shorter KV list. Only the windowing mechanism is upstreamed here; the paper's ring-buffer reclaim of the unread draft KV is possible follow-up work. ## Modifications 1. `generate_draft_decode_kv_indices` gains `window_size` and `sink_size` `tl.constexpr` params, both defaulting to `0`. With `window_size > 0` a draft-decode step gathers `[first sink_size tokens] + [most recent window_size tokens]` instead of the whole prefix, then appends the draft tree tokens unwindowed as before. `window_size == 0` collapses every added op to the identity, so the default path and the kernel's other callers (AITER, MLA) are unchanged. 2. `--speculative-draft-window-size` is now also honored by the built-in EAGLE / MTP draft-decode path on the Triton and FlashInfer draft backends. `spec_utils.resolve_draft_decode_window()` is the single mapping from server args to `(window_size, sink_size)`; both `*MultiStepDraftBackend`s call it once in `__init__`. 3. New `--speculative-draft-sink-size` for the attention sink, since a pure recent window drops the initial tokens attention reliably parks on. The window keeps DFLASH's unit and anchor — KV entries, counted back from the end of the prefix — so a step reads `min(seq_len, window + sink)` prefix entries, which at the default `sink=0` is `min(seq_len, window)`, the same expression as `_compute_compact_draft_seq_lens`, with no `-1`. Tree tokens are never capped, so the existing `window_size >= num_draft_tokens` check still holds. 4. A draft model with a sliding window of its own keeps it, and this windowing stays off. That covers an MTP head with SWA in its config and a `LlamaForCausalLMEagle3` drafter, whose window comes from this same flag. One KV list is shared by every draft layer, so the index builder cannot express a per-layer window, and a checkpoint's own window should win over a server flag either way. We warn only when the resulting window differs from the requested one, so the EAGLE-3 case stays quiet. CUDA graphs are safe: the per-request kept length rides in `kv_indptr`, exactly like the variable-seqlen path the graph already replays. Same launch grid, no host sync, no dynamic shapes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Qwen3.6-35B-A3B bf16, one B200, `trtllm_mha` target, EAGLE `steps=6 topk=1 draft_tokens=7`, `W=4032 S=64` (4096 prefix entries per draft step), batch 1, RULER `niah_multiquery_enum`, 512 output tokens. `window` vs `native` on the same draft backend; the target is identical in every arm. `T_iter` is per-iteration wall time — the mechanism, without acceptance mixed in — and TPOT is `T_iter / AL`. | context | draft backend | TPOT native → window | speedup | T_iter native → window | AL native → window | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 32K | triton | 3.895 → 3.068 ms | 1.27× | 12.67 → 10.05 ms (−21%) | 3.25 → 3.28 | | 64K | triton | 4.414 → 3.264 ms | 1.35× | 19.06 → 13.48 ms (−29%) | 4.32 → 4.13 | | 128K | triton | 7.047 → 4.568 ms | 1.54× | 31.65 → 20.02 ms (−37%) | 4.49 → 4.38 | | 256K | triton | 10.448 → 6.093 ms | 1.71× | 57.35 → 33.45 ms (−42%) | 5.49 → 5.49 | | 32K | flashinfer | 2.199 → 2.142 ms | 1.03× | 7.20 → 7.01 ms (−3%) | 3.28 → 3.28 | | 64K | flashinfer | 1.728 → 1.738 ms | 0.99× | 7.46 → 7.18 ms (−4%) | 4.32 → 4.13 | | 128K | flashinfer | 1.799 → 1.696 ms | 1.06× | 8.08 → 7.44 ms (−8%) | 4.49 → 4.38 | | 256K | flashinfer | 1.735 → 1.499 ms | 1.16× | 9.36 → 8.05 ms (−14%) | 5.39 → 5.37 | Dense (no speculation) TPOT at those four contexts, for reference: 2.997 / 3.158 / 3.320 / 3.698 ms. - `T_iter` drops at every point on both backends and the drop grows with context, which is the mechanism doing what it should: the draft's read is capped while native's grows. - TPOT also depends on acceptance, so the 64K FlashInfer point is a wash — a 4% per-iteration saving against a 4% acceptance dip. The window is a clear win on FlashInfer from ~128K up and at every point on Triton, whose full-prefix draft read is far more expensive to begin with. - Acceptance never beats native in this sweep. It does past 512K in the paper, but that needs RoPE extension beyond this checkpoint's 256K native context, so we leave it out of the PR's numbers. ## Testing `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_decode_window.py` — 13 tests / 28 subtests, 16 s on one GPU. Every expectation comes from a closed-form oracle over `seq_lens`, never from the kernel's own packing, so a bug can't be mirrored on both sides. - `window_size == 0` reproduces the full-KV read plan, offsets and gathered slots, for single- and multi-request batches at `topk` 1 and 2. This is the off-by-default regression guard. - Windowed `kv_indptr` lengths are `min(seq_len, sink + window) + tree`, and the gather really is `[sink] + [recent] + [tree]`, parametrized past 256K/512K/1M. - Tree drafts (`topk > 1`): each `(request, branch)` slot gets its own windowed base list plus its own branch at the oracle offset. Covered at `page_size == 1` and on the `page_size > 1 and topk > 1` paged branch, where tree tokens are read from the uncapped prefix end but written at the capped offset. - `resolve_draft_decode_window`, including the own-window opt-out and exactly when it warns, plus a CPU-only guard that both draft backends resolve through it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/development_guide_using_docker.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31621192148](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31621192148)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31621191599](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31621191599)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: bounded long audio with encoder-window caching
signals.text: ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in realtime ASR path for long audio items. It bounds the acoustic work submitted by each update, reuses completed audio encoder windows through SGLang's existing multimodal cache, and publishes decoder progress through the existing append-only transcription delta event. The current realtime path re-submits all audio accumulated for an item every 2 seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but both prefill and memory grow with the session. On long items, per-update latency eventually dominates realtime playback. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, the opt-in path works as follows: 1. Keep the existing cumulative path through the first 60 seconds. 2. On the first update after 60 seconds, establish a one-way handoff from the cumulative transcript to encoder-window continuation. 3. Keep at most eight complete model-native 8-second audio windows plus the current incomplete tail in each later request. 4. Reuse complete-window embeddings through the existing MM cache; always recompute the mutable tail. 5. Carry older semantic context in a bounded, confirmed transcript prefix and generate only the new suffix. 6. Stream decoder progress through the existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` event. No client schema or new event type is added. The default remains `cumulative`. Encoder windowing is currently enabled only for an explicitly declared English session on a local single-GPU runtime. Unsupported models, languages, and topologies keep the cumulative path and its 60-second safety boundary. ## Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client appends PCM] --> B[2-second inference boundary] B --> C{Received audio over 60 seconds?} C -- No --> D[Submit audio from 0 to current end] D --> E[Cumulative transcript reconciliation] C -- Yes, first handoff --> F[Submit full audio once] F --> G[Create bounded confirmed-text prefix] C -- Yes, steady state --> H[Choose 8-second-aligned rolling range] G --> H H --> I[Up to 8 complete windows plus mutable tail] I --> J[Complete windows: existing MM embedding cache] I --> K[Mutable tail: encode, do not retain] J --> L[Decoder prefix plus new suffix generation] K --> L E --> M[Reconcile decoder updates] L --> M M --> N[Emit only append-safe delta text] N --> O[Existing transcription.delta event] O --> P[Advance absolute PCM cursors and compact old audio] ``` The first windowed request intentionally includes the full handoff audio. Once the handoff succeeds, steady-state requests retain no more than 64 seconds of complete encoder windows plus an incomplete tail shorter than 8 seconds. For example, a steady-state request near 130 seconds looks like this: ```text Older audio represented by confirmed text | v text: [bounded decoder prefix] audio: [w0][w1] ... [w7][tail] encoder: [cache hits / misses][encode] decoder: [prefix] + [rolling acoustic context] -> new suffix only wire: -> append-only stable deltas ``` ## Encoder-window reuse Qwen3-ASR declares its independent encoder geometry in the multimodal processor. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one complete window is 8 seconds and produces 104 encoder tokens. The generic audio-window builder: - extracts complete windows independently from the mutable tail; - expands one audio placeholder into per-window token ranges; - hashes the exact feature, attention mask, modality, and token geometry; - marks complete windows as cacheable; - marks the mutable tail `use_embedding_cache=False`; and - provides an explicit encoder batch key for variable-width audio features. A cache miss or eviction simply re-encodes the window. Cache reuse is therefore a performance optimization, not persistent session state and not a correctness dependency. The cache is model-owned only through declarative capability data: ```text Transcription adapter -> activation threshold, language gate, text-prefix limits Multimodal processor -> independently encodable window geometry Generic audio-window builder -> feature extraction, MM items, identity, cacheability Existing MM scheduler/cache -> lookup, miss batching, embedding assembly ``` There is no ASR-specific scheduler session, cache service, GPU lease, or model forward API. ## Append-only decoder streaming Each backend ASR request now uses `stream=True` when the realtime endpoint provides a callback. Partial decoder text is stripped of model-specific output markers, reconciled against cumulative or windowed transcript state, and sent only when it extends the text already published for that request. This is decoder-token-driven stable delta streaming, not a guarantee of one WebSocket event per tokenizer token. Local Agreement and suffix holdback may release several tokens together. If a completed decode revises a prefix that was already emitted, the request fails closed rather than sending a conflicting append-only transcript. No client changes are required. The wire protocol remains: ```text conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed ``` ## Enablement ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 ``` The client uses the existing realtime transcription session format and must declare a supported language before sending audio: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is the total accepted duration of one client item. Resident PCM is independently compacted after the encoder-window handoff. ## Alternatives evaluated Before selecting this implementation, four approaches were run under the same controlled setup: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one RTX 4090, Triton attention, identical native audio, 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, and 2-second flood-mode appends. Processing time is measured from the first send to the completed event; it measures server work rather than realtime playback. "Word error" is the normalized edit distance from the published reference; lower is better. | Approach | Long-audio behavior | Result | Decision | |---|---|---|---| | Cumulative | Re-submit all received audio every 2 seconds | 178.5 seconds of audio took 153.240 seconds; 291.1 seconds did not finish within 300 seconds | Keep as the unchanged default for normal items | | PCM tail slicing | Submit a bounded PCM tail plus 2-second overlap | 178.5 seconds took 109.735 seconds with 39.81% word error; longer cases did not finish | Rejected: bounded audio alone did not bound decoder-prefix work or preserve quality | | Encoder-aligned rolling context | Reuse complete windows and continue from confirmed text | Completed 291/593/908/1687-second inputs in 16.947/31.721/51.097/90.195 seconds | Selected: fastest completed long-stream approach and no client protocol change | | Independent segment finals | Finalize disjoint segments without a cross-segment prefix | Completed the same inputs in 18.804/35.343/55.127/98.233 seconds | Not selected: slower and requires replaceable snapshot semantics | The long-input comparison was: | Input | Cumulative | PCM slicing | Encoder windows | Independent segments | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | LongLibriHeavy 178.5 s | 153.240 s, 12.04% error | 109.735 s, 39.81% | 9.911 s, 11.30% | 11.586 s, 11.30% | | TED Al Gore 291.1 s | >300 s, incomplete | >300 s, incomplete | 16.947 s, 3.87% | 18.804 s, 4.66% | | LongLibriHeavy 592.6 s | >405 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 31.721 s, 7.95% | 35.343 s, 7.74% | | TED Craig Venter 907.8 s | >405 s, incomplete | >405 s, incomplete | 51.097 s, 4.50% | 55.127 s, 4.75% | | Earnings22 EXCOF 1686.7 s | >397 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 90.195 s, 12.80% | 98.233 s, 10.55% | ## Current-head GPU validation Environment: - Commit: `135eb6cf66` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24,564 MiB - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, snapshot `5eb144179a02acc5e5ba31e748d22b0cf3e303b0` - Attention backend: Triton - Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.8.1 - 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, 2-second appends - `--mem-fraction-static 0.75`, 100 MiB MM cache, 1800-second item cap All reported accuracy and performance cases below are complete, unmodified published source rows or source files. No reported audio was concatenated, cropped, padded, or silence-extended. For every successful WebSocket case: ```text concatenate(all transcription.delta text) == completed transcript snapshot events == 0 ``` Selected native-audio results on the current head: | Input | Duration | Server processing time | Reference word error | Result vs pre-streaming encoder-window path | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Qwen English demo | 15.1 s | 0.814 s | no published reference | Byte-identical | | LongLibriHeavy | 75.0 s | 4.245 s | 11.02% | Same normalized output and error rate | | LongLibriHeavy | 93.4 s | 4.899 s; fresh rerun 5.222 s | 7.98%; rerun 7.45% | One-word first-run variation; rerun matched baseline | | TED Al Gore | 291.1 s | 16.837 s | 3.87% | Normalized-exact | | TED Barry Schwartz | 1104.6 s | 58.373 s; rerun 58.485 s | 2.39% both runs | Normalized-exact, full opening and ending | | Earnings22 EXCOF | 1686.7 s | 88.901 s; rerun 88.367 s | 12.80% both runs | Full opening and ending; 0.20-0.22% run-to-run text variation | The 28-minute Earnings22 run issued 844 backend requests. Of 888,608 prompt tokens, 511,624 were cache hits (57.6%); uncached prompt work was 376,984 tokens. The server remained healthy after every request. ### Paced streaming receipt The 15.05-second Qwen demo was also sent at realtime pace instead of flood mode: - 8 backend ASR requests; - 37 existing `transcription.delta` events; - 0 snapshot events; - the joined deltas were byte-identical to the completed transcript; and - the first six deltas arrived between 2.171 and 2.208 seconds after the run began, while 4 seconds of audio had been sent. This confirms that output is emitted while one backend decode is still running, while preserving the endpoint's append-only transcript contract. ## Public audio sources - Qwen English demo: <https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_en.wav> - LongLibriHeavy: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/inesc-id/longlibriheavy> - TED-LIUM long form: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form> - Earnings22: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/earnings22> The benchmark manifest records dataset revisions, row ids, decoded-audio SHA256, wire-PCM SHA256, duration, sample rate, and reference text. Every result reported above uses one native source row or source file without local audio construction. ## Implementation | Area | Responsibility | |---|---| | `realtime/asr_processor.py` | Selects cumulative/windowed requests, reconciles decoder updates, advances absolute cursors, and compacts PCM | | `realtime/audio_buffer.py` | Maintains the per-item absolute PCM timeline | | `realtime/decoder_suffix.py` | Reconciles bounded decoder-prefix continuations without fuzzy deletion | | `realtime/session.py` | Owns WebSocket lifecycle and emits existing append-only events | | `streaming_asr.py` | Runs backend streaming generation and model-specific partial-output processing | | Transcription adapter | Declares activation, supported languages, decoder-prefix limits, and streaming postprocessing | | `audio_encoder_windowing.py` | Builds complete-window and mutable-tail multimodal items | | Base/Qwen multimodal processors | Provide generic construction plus model-config-derived window geometry | | `MultimodalDataItem` / `mm_schedule.py` | Support opt-in cacheability and producer-declared compatible miss batching | | `server_args.py` | Adds the off-by-default `encoder_window` strategy | ## Validation ```text 37 focused CPU tests passed 20 parameterized subtests passed py_compile passed git diff --check passed Ruff format check passed PR-file pre-commit hooks passed (black-jupyter skipped; no notebooks changed) GPU: 15-1687-second unmodified native-audio regression complete TED-LIUM and Earnings22 long-form recordings 1105- and 1687-second long-form reruns realtime-paced decoder-streaming trace ``` ## Limits - Encoder windowing is experimental, off by default, English-only for Qwen3-ASR, and currently limited to a local single-GPU runtime. - Operators must raise `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` above 60 seconds for the strategy to activate. - Stable deltas are driven by backend token streaming, but Local Agreement may group tokens. This is not raw one-event-per-token passthrough. - `finish_reason=length`, irreconcilable streamed-prefix revisions, and unsafe no-word-boundary continuation fail closed. - No timestamps, forced aligner, model-native streaming state, distributed encoder cache, or scheduler-owned ASR session is introduced. - Validation is bounded to Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 4090 and does not establish universal multilingual quality or production capacity. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194510888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194510888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194510769](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194510769)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
