signals.title: [Perf] wave_backend: drop dead per-layer D2H sync in forward_extend
signals.text: ## Problem `WaveAttnBackend.forward_extend()` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/wave_backend.py`) ran this block once per attention layer: ```python max_extend_len = self.forward_metadata.max_extend_len computed_max_ext_seq_len = torch.max(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens) if computed_max_ext_seq_len != max_extend_len: assert len(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens) == 1 forward_batch.extend_seq_lens[0] = max_extend_len forward_batch.seq_lens = max_extend_len ``` For an extend batch `forward_batch.extend_seq_lens` is a CUDA int32 tensor (`ForwardBatch.init_new` H2D-converts the host list via `.to(device)`), so evaluating `tensor != int` as a bool forces a device-to-host sync on the forward stream — once per attention layer per `forward_extend` pass. Measured on B200: 26.7 µs p50 for the bare sync (×90 attention layers ≈ 2.4 ms per pass), 30-70 µs per layer including the queued-work drain (up to ~6.3 ms per pass at the top of the range). These are microbench projections, not e2e numbers. The block's body was unreachable on both modes that reach `forward_extend`: - **EXTEND** (the only mode with a live comparison): `init_forward_metadata` computes `max_extend_len = torch.max(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens).item()` from the *same* tensor of the *same* batch, and nothing mutates `extend_seq_lens` between metadata init and the per-layer calls. The comparison is therefore always false; the `assert` and the two writes below it never execute. - **TARGET_VERIFY**: `ForwardBatch.init_new` only tensor-izes `extend_seq_lens` outside decode-or-idle *and* outside target-verify, so under target-verify it is still a host list (or `None`) and `torch.max(...)` raises `TypeError` — the block aborts `forward_extend` before the attention call, so target-verify + wave has never executed. ## Fix Delete the dead block, and replace its accidental target-verify abort with an explicit guard at the top of `forward_extend` (before any KV-cache write): target-verify batches now raise `NotImplementedError`. Why the explicit guard is required rather than letting the path run: `extend_attention_wave` (the Wave MLIR kernel wrapper, `wave_ops/extend_attention.py`) accepts `custom_mask`/`mask_indptr` parameters but never feeds them to the generated kernel — the kernel is causal-only. If the deleted block's `TypeError` were simply removed, target-verify + wave would stop crashing and instead silently compute verification attention without the draft-tree mask (sibling drafts attending each other). Keeping the combination explicitly unsupported preserves the pre-existing behavior (crash) with a clear error message, until the kernel grows mask support. ## Tests None added: the reachable change is the deletion of a redundant per-layer sync whose comparison is provably always false, plus a guard raise; there is no behavior surface to unit-test without a GPU and a wave-lang toolchain. Net diff vs `main`: +10/-7 in one file. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32125031199](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125031199)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32125030858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125030858)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signals.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in while making the path safer to extend, adding an opt-in automatic fallback mode, and validating the overlap path on hybrid/VLM and MoE/EP models. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured, deterministic admission plan and rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: supported configurations use overlap, while rejected configurations retain serial startup. - Verify resolved checkpoint sources before capture-safe model mutation. If `auto` discovers PT or secondary weights, it reuses the already allocated model and resolved sources for serial loading rather than allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across real-weight commit. - Fail closed when real loading leaves capture-safe sentinel values behind. - Report complete startup-overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Harden best-effort checkpoint prefetch failure/cancellation behavior. - Add narrowly validated Qwen3.5 dense-hybrid, Qwen3.5 MoE-hybrid, and Qwen3 MoE EP profiles. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` still fails during preflight with deterministic reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs those reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Validated configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | Quantization, speculative decoding, DP/PP/CP, LoRA, offload, DeepEP/other MoE A2A backends, EPLB, redundant or elastic experts, and unvalidated model implementations remain outside the overlap matrix. Qwen hybrid FullCG prefill is also excluded after an H100 probe reproduced an existing hybrid linear-attention replay failure during capture. `auto` sends these configurations through serial startup. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from model-class resolution. The preflight only resolves/imports the native implementation after all cheap rules pass, so `auto` can select serial without remote-code imports, exception-driven control flow, or model mutation. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are only known after source resolution. That second fallback boundary remains before sentinel initialization. The default loader can therefore serial-load the real weights into the initialized model from the already resolved sources, preserving normal iterator prefetch/multithread behavior without a second model allocation. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization verifies that real loading refreshed the existing storage rather than rebinding anything captured by CUDA graphs. Models can explicitly enumerate graph-visible derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not attempt an in-process serial retry after the model has been mutated or CUDA graphs have captured its storage. Page-cache prefetch remains best-effort: a failed worker falls back to the normal checkpoint reader, and late failures are reported without invalidating a successful real load. Both Scheduler startup and `bench_one_batch` route lifecycle hooks from the manager actually selected by admission, rather than from the requested mode string. ## H100 validation ### Qwen3.6 dense hybrid VLM `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. Three cold-cache trials per mode after one JIT warmup: | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 34.48 s | 28.05 s | -18.7% / 1.23x | | Process ready | 43.93 s | 37.48 s | -14.7% / 1.17x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 14.62 s | 7.59 s | -48.1% | Correctness covered BS1, BS2, long-prefix branching, and an image request. Text, token IDs, and output logprobs matched exactly; maximum absolute output-logprob difference was `0.0`. ### Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE and linear attention, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. Both modes started from zero resident checkpoint pages across 14 safetensors shards (71.9 GB): | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 149.70 s | 48.14 s | -67.8% / 3.11x | | Process ready | 158.52 s | 56.96 s | -64.1% / 2.78x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 126.61 s | 24.46 s | -80.7% | This is an end-to-end mode comparison, not a claim that CUDA-graph overlap alone exceeds the `t1 + t2 -> max(t1, t2)` bound. The overlap mode also coordinates checkpoint page-cache prefetch across TP ranks, so the result includes cold-storage I/O deduplication and a hot-cache real-weight commit. A serial+coordinated-prefetch arm is still needed to isolate the incremental graph-overlap contribution. Serial, overlap, and auto produced identical token IDs and output logprobs across three text prompts, a BS2 request, and an image request (six responses total). `auto` selected the `qwen3_5_moe_hybrid_vlm` profile. ### Qwen3 MoE with expert parallelism `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE, standard EP, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. The checkpoint has 16 safetensors shards totaling 61.1 GB. Five alternating cold-cache trials (three overlap, two serial) kept JIT caches warm and evicted only checkpoint pages before each run: | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 51.11 s | 28.66 s | -43.9% / 1.78x | | Process ready | 60.33 s | 38.07 s | -36.9% / 1.58x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 31.59 s | 8.23 s | -73.9% | Both ranks passed storage-manifest and sentinel validation while each rank loaded 64 local experts. Correctness covered a BS4 prompt set with different routes plus a long-prefix seed and two branches (seven responses total). Text and token IDs matched exactly; maximum absolute output-logprob difference was `0.0`. ## Tests - Focused startup-weight-load unit suite passed on the development superset (`52 passed`); the submitted diff removes three GLM-only tests/hooks after deferring that unvalidated runtime profile. - `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/test_server_args_migration.py::TestServerArgsAnnotatedCli::test_startup_weight_load_mode` (`1 passed`) - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, and `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037` on all changed files - `python3 -m py_compile` on all auto-fallback implementation and test files - Registered-test, bare-pytest, and package-registration lint checks - `git diff --check` ## Follow-up This PR intentionally keeps `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated profiles for GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and Kimi linear/K3; define capture-stable contracts for quantized/repacked weights; add a serial+coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm for clean overlap attribution; and, after broader operational evidence, make automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32182075332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182075332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32182074978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182074978)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(model-gateway): accept token ID prompts in /v1/completions
signals.text: ## Motivation The Python OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API accepts pre-tokenized prompts as `List[int]` and batched token prompts as `List[List[int]]`. The Rust model gateway currently models `prompt` as a string or an array of strings only. As a result, valid token-ID completion requests are rejected by Axum during request deserialization with HTTP 422 before they can be forwarded to the backend. This creates an API compatibility gap between the Python server and the Rust model gateway. ## Modifications * Extend the Rust completion prompt representation to accept: * text prompt * batch of text prompts * single token-ID sequence * batch of token-ID sequences * Preserve token-ID prompts when forwarding requests to workers. * Update completion batch-size detection for token-ID batches. * Add regression coverage for unified and PD routing paths. This PR only adds request parsing/forwarding compatibility. Token-ID prompts bypass the current text-based cache-aware routing; token-ID-aware radix/cache routing is intentionally left to a separate follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not modify model computation or model outputs. Route-level regression tests cover: * existing text completion * single `List[int]` token prompt * batched `List[List[int]]` token prompts * PD batch request semantics Before this change, a real Axum `/v1/completions` request with a token-ID prompt returns HTTP 422. With this change, the same request is accepted and forwarded successfully. Validation: * focused Rust tests: passed * `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`: passed * `cargo fmt --check`: passed * patch/apply check against upstream main: passed No GPU is required for this protocol-level fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This is a request-schema and routing compatibility fix and does not change the inference execution path. ## Checklist * [ ] Format your code according to the [[Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). * [x] Add unit tests according to the [[Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). * [x] Update documentation according to [[Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing behavior beyond restoring existing Python API compatibility.) * [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [[Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [[Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (No performance benchmark needed for this protocol-only change.) * [x] Follow the SGLang code style [[guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32171702497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32171702497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32171702123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32171702123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Avoid full-logits all-gather for TP greedy sampling
signals.text: ## Motivation Tensor-parallel generation currently materializes and all-gathers full-vocabulary logits on every rank before a strict greedy `argmax`. For greedy-only requests, each rank only needs to contribute its local maximum value and global token ID. This PR adds an experimental opt-in path that changes the logits communication from `O(batch * vocab)` to `O(batch * TP)` candidates. It is related to, but does not duplicate, #31079: that PR gathers full logits to rank 0, while this path reduces each vocab shard locally and never communicates full logits. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_SHARDED_GREEDY=1` (off by default). - Compute local FP32 LM-head logits and the local `(max value, global token ID)` on each TP rank. - Pack each candidate into two 32-bit lanes, all-gather the candidates, and select the global winner with the same lowest-token-ID tie behavior as full-vocabulary `torch.argmax`. - Pass the selected token IDs through `LogitsProcessorOutput` without constructing full-vocabulary logits. - Strictly fall back to the existing path for logprobs, top-logprobs, token-ID logprobs, grammars, custom logit processors, logit bias, penalties, sampling masks, speculative modes, prefill-only requests, added embeddings, unsupported LM-head layouts, and CUDA-graph logits buffers. - Add unit tests and a TP communication microbenchmark. ## Accuracy Tests ```text pytest -q test/registered/unit/sampling/test_tp_sharded_greedy.py 18 passed ``` The tests cover per-row winners, exact ties, NaNs, explicit opt-in, and all full-logits fallback gates. A fixed greedy E2E probe produced identical results with the feature disabled and enabled: ```text prompt: "Hello" output_ids: [13, 358] text: ". I" ``` The communication benchmark also checks candidate-path token IDs against full all-gather + argmax with `rtol=0, atol=0` before timing each shape. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/software: - 2x NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB (SM80), TP=2 - PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, NCCL 2.28.9 - BF16 model weights, FP32 logits - CUDA graphs disabled (the experimental path currently falls back when graph logits buffers are present) - `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` for both paths because P2P/IPC communicator initialization hangs on this PHB-connected hosted instance; both paths use the same NCCL transport Microbenchmark (`vocab_size=128256`, 100 iterations): | Batch | Full all-gather + argmax (us) | Candidate all-gather (us) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 213.91 | 403.08 | 0.531x | | 4 | 420.88 | 400.34 | 1.051x | | 16 | 1185.63 | 378.73 | 3.131x | | 64 | 5100.59 | 384.84 | 13.254x | E2E serving benchmark: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` - 128 requests, random input length 256, output length 128 - concurrency 64, temperature 0, TP=2 - CUDA graphs/custom all-reduce/overlap scheduling disabled for both paths - cache flushed before every run - A/B/A ordering after kernel caches were warm | Metric | Baseline runs | Feature runs | Mean change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput (tok/s) | 1603.47, 1583.17 | 1698.81, 1717.17 | **+7.20%** | | Median E2E latency (ms) | 4892.71, 4913.26 | 4628.27, 4534.11 | **-6.56%** | | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 4962.94, 5030.94 | 4737.79, 4737.67 | **-5.19%** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 33.55, 33.93 | 31.71, 31.80 | **-5.88%** | The microbenchmark shows why the path remains experimental and opt-in: it targets medium/high-batch greedy decode, not batch 1. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with the repository's pinned Ruff, isort, and Black versions. - [x] Added unit tests for correctness and fallback behavior. - [x] Documented the experimental environment variable inline; no public default behavior changes. - [x] Included accuracy, microbenchmark, and E2E benchmark results. - [x] Followed the existing SGLang code style. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32107422729](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32107422729)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32107422138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32107422138)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach
signals.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32144619670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144619670)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32144619414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144619414)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
signals.text: ## Motivation Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled: 1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549) 2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay. 3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`. ## Modifications 1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.) 2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why. 3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe. Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease. ## Accuracy Tests Server launched following the cookbook: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-adaptive \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook: | | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k | | -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- | | cookbook | 88.1 | 95 | 96.13 | | before | 88.13 | 98.33 | 96.89 | | after | 88.04 | 97.29 | 96.97 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signals.title: [PD] Align defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori
signals.text: - RFC: [PD disaggregation: single protocol layer, per-backend transport #33861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861) - Staged implementation plan and PR tracking: [PD shared-protocol implementation plan #34510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510) - Preceding PR: [NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout #34692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34692) ## Background #34692 added the missing NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout. This PR continues Step 1 of #34510 by aligning clear, low-risk defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori without changing the Common state machine, wire format, completion channel, or Transport architecture. These changes preserve the current backend structure. They only add missing behavior or fix local race/layout issues. Extracting the common protocol and Transport remains work for later stages. ## Outline This PR groups the changes into five areas: 1. Complete Mori peer/request failure detection and ABORT delivery; 2. Prevent NIXL/Mori workers from executing stale work after teardown; 3. Keep Mooncake/NIXL control loops serving after malformed messages; 4. Align Mori MHA/MLA KV layout planning; 5. Fix the initialization race before the Mooncake control thread starts. ## 1. Mori peer and request failure handling Related commits: - `b285ea79ce` — `align Mori Decode heartbeat` - `62c13f66ba` — `align Mori abort handling with common protocol` Mori Decode did not start the existing Common heartbeat checker, so a dead Prefill would not trigger route/cache eviction or active-room failure. This PR only wires in the existing `_start_heartbeat_checker_thread()`, matching Mooncake and NIXL. Common Receiver sends an `ABORT` frame without a Mori guard, while Mori Prefill previously validated `MORI_GUARD` first and discarded ABORT as malformed. This PR recognizes the existing Common ABORT frame before guard validation: - Mark an active room as `Failed`; - Continue to ignore Success/unknown rooms; - Drop only the current message when ABORT is malformed. This only fixes ABORT delivery. It does not define ACK, cancel, or quiescence semantics. Terminal-state and safe-release behavior remains deferred to the later RFC stages. ## 2. Skip stale work after room teardown Related commit: - `46056556a5` — `skip cleared rooms in NIXL and Mori workers` Chunks already queued do not disappear when the Sender clears a room. - NIXL previously allowed a missing room to bypass its Failed check and then enter the exception path at the `transfer_infos` assertion; - Mori could continue into `add_transfer_request()` and subsequent terminalization. Mooncake already checks at `transfer_worker()` entry whether the room still exists or is `Failed`. On a match, it finishes the current chunk trace, removes residual `_staging_outstanding` state, and continues without reading that room's transfer metadata. This PR makes the other two backends discard queued tasks for missing rooms at worker entry: - NIXL aligns with Mooncake's missing-room/Failed guard, removes the room's residual `_staging_outstanding` count, and continues; - Mori uses an equivalent early return because chunk execution lives in Sender `_run_chunk()`. The stale task therefore cannot read deleted `transfer_infos`, submit to the Transport, advance state, or trigger terminalization. Existing `clear()` paths remain responsible for normal room cleanup; these guards only consume queue items that arrive after teardown. When the common protocol is extracted, this should be replaced by unified idempotent room teardown/tombstone semantics. For now, the backend-local guards avoid expanding the scope into Common state-machine changes. ## 3. Isolate malformed control messages Related commit: - `a716ceaac7` — `harden Mooncake and NIXL control message parsing` Mooncake/NIXL control loops serve multiple rooms, but previously indexed, decoded, or unpacked frames directly. An empty message, truncated ABORT, invalid guard, or unexpected frame count could terminate the long-lived thread. Mori already treats one message as the exception boundary: its Prefill bootstrap loop and Decode status loop validate guard/frame input inside `while True`, log an error for the current message, and continue receiving the next one. A bad frame therefore does not remove control-plane service from later rooms. This PR aligns Mooncake and NIXL with that behavior by adding minimum frame/tag/guard validation at the Mooncake Prefill/Decode and NIXL Prefill/Decode-staging message entries. Empty messages, truncated fields, and invalid encodings are logged and skipped without terminating the long-lived control thread. ## 4. Align Mori KV layout planning Related commits: - `48c5e1569d` — `align Mori speculative MHA layout with common planner` - `081186c4c8` — `align Mori same-PP and hybrid MLA layout planning` Together, these commits fix Mori descriptor slicing that differed from the existing Common planner. The first part handles Decode-only speculative KV layout: ```text [K_main..., V_main..., draft_K..., draft_V...] ``` Mori previously split descriptors in half and could select a draft region as main V. This PR uses the same V-offset rule as `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp()`. The second part adds: - Same-PP peer descriptor lists are already aligned local layouts and must not have the global layer offset applied again; - Hybrid MLA uses MLA descriptor slicing instead of falling through to the regular MHA path. These fixes remain inside Mori for now because they operate on Mori `MemoryDesc` lists, and planner/materialization are still coupled in Mori Manager. A later stage can extract target/draft, same-PP, and MHA/MLA logical layer selection into a Common helper, leaving Mori responsible only for mapping the common plan to `MemoryDesc` and `batch_write()`. ## 5. Initialize Mooncake state before starting the control thread Related commit: - `12a88dbcfe` — `initialize Mooncake session state before control thread` Mooncake Prefill previously started its receive thread before creating state that the thread accesses: ```text session_failures failed_sessions session_lock ``` If Decode registration arrived immediately after thread startup, it could hit an initialization race. This PR only moves these three fields before `start_prefill_thread()` while preserving all other queue, worker, probe, and receive ordering. This is intentionally a minimal ordering fix rather than a Step 1 reorganization of backend thread lifecycle. When the common Manager/Transport is extracted, control-thread initialization, startup, shared state, and shutdown should be managed together. ## Testing CPU red/green regression tests are kept on a dedicated test branch: ```text branch: https://github.com/jambow0320/sglang/tree/rfc-pd-test path: test/registered/unit/disaggregation/rfc-test/ ``` Coverage includes: - Mori ABORT delivery before guard validation; - Cleared-room stale work in NIXL/Mori; - Malformed control-message isolation in Mooncake/NIXL; - Mori speculative MHA descriptor selection; - Mooncake session-state initialization order. The tests pass with the fixes and reproduce the original failures against the corresponding unfixed source. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32110778332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32110778332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32110778109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32110778109)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: test: switch the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic suite to DSPARK
signals.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Two knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), and the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture. This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse, which trips the `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` this class already asserts. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. On 4x GB300 the class runs 650.79 s and the whole file 1093 s; spec roughly doubles this class against the no-spec arm it replaces (360 s → 685 s on the bf16 checkpoint at the same tp). `est_time` 2000 is an estimate for B200 pending a real CI number, which `scripts/ci/update_est_time.py` will correct. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32206930212](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206930212)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32206930000](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206930000)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] DCP: advertise the logical KV-event block size
signals.text: ## Motivation Under DCP, SGLang runs two page sizes: the configured **physical** `page_size`, and a **logical** page `page_size * dcp_size` that the allocator is built with (`mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`) and that the radix tree inherits (`mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py`). KV events are chunked by the tree's page size, so they go out at the logical width. `/server_info`'s `kv_events` descriptor advertised the **physical** `page_size`. A KV-aware router honoring the documented contract — *"subscribers MUST hash prompts at this size"* — then hashes requests at a width no emitted block can ever match. Stores apply cleanly, every lookup misses, and the router's KV hit rate is silently **exactly 0** while all local metrics look healthy. ## Modifications - Add `ServerArgs.kv_event_block_size` (property): `page_size * dcp_size`, the width events are actually emitted at. - `describe_kv_events_publisher` advertises it instead of the physical `page_size`. The `page_size` field itself is unchanged — only the advertised value is corrected. - Document that the descriptor's `dp_size` is deliberately *not* DCP-scaled: DCP shards within a rank rather than adding publishers. No working configuration changes behavior — under DCP the advertised value was unusable (hit rate 0), and without DCP the value is identical. ## Verification Measured on 4x H200 with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (`tp=4 dcp=4 page_size=64`): - **Engine only, no router:** plain `sglang.launch_server` — before, `/server_info` reported `kv_events.block_size=64` while the ZMQ wire carried `BlockStored.block_size=256`; after, it reports 256, matching the wire. - **End to end through a KV-aware router:** the equivalent consumer-side mistake gave a hit rate of **exactly 0** over six identical 1,686-token prompts, against **4.814814814814815 / 6** (the 96.3% arithmetic maximum, `5 * 26/27`) on otherwise identical no-DCP arms — including a same-attention-backend control arm, which rules out the backend. Correcting the width restored it to `5 * 6/7 = 4.285714285714286 / 6`, the arithmetic maximum for the 256-token logical page, and again to `3 * 6/7` on fresh content. - The same consumer-side bug in Dynamo's SGLang integration (reading `server_args.page_size` directly, bypassing this descriptor) was fixed independently in ai-dynamo/dynamo#12765. This PR fixes the engine's own advertised contract, so any subscriber that honors it — e.g. sgl-router, whose `BlockSizeOracle` takes its width from this field and whose hashes must reach bit-parity with SGLang's `hash_page` at that width — is correct without needing DCP awareness of its own. - **Unit tests** (`TestDcpKvEventContract`): red on `main`, green with the fix; covers `page_size=1 + dcp` (paged at `dcp_size`) and the non-DCP default. `pre-commit` passes. ## Note on scope An earlier revision of this PR also added an args-time `tp_size % dcp_size` guard. That was **dropped**: `parallel_state.py` already raises `RuntimeError("tensor_model_parallel_size (N) must be divisible by decode_context_parallel_size (M)")` during dist init, before weights load. Confirmed by launching `--tp-size 1 --dcp-size 2` on `main`. Thanks @alexnails for questioning whether that check was needed — it wasn't. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation as needed. - [x] Provide verification results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32195664272](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195664272)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195663998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195663998)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Guard harmony parsing against malformed gpt-oss output in Responses API
signals.text: ## Motivation gpt-oss occasionally samples a malformed harmony message header, for example a duplicated `to=` in a tool-call header. `openai_harmony`'s `StreamableParser.process` raises `HarmonyError` on such headers, and `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/context.py` calls it with no exception handling at four sites: `HarmonyContext.append_output`, both loops in `StreamingHarmonyContext.append_output`, and `StreamingHarmonyContext.render_for_completion`. Repro against the pinned `openai-harmony==0.0.4`: ```python from openai_harmony import HarmonyEncodingName, Role, StreamableParser, load_harmony_encoding enc = load_harmony_encoding(HarmonyEncodingName.HARMONY_GPT_OSS) parser = StreamableParser(enc, role=Role.ASSISTANT) text = '<|channel|>commentary to=functions.get_weather to=functions.get_weather<|message|>{}<|call|>' for t in enc.encode(text, allowed_special="all"): parser.process(t) # openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"] ``` Because this is model output rather than client input, the failure is intermittent, and the user-visible impact differs by path: - Non-streaming `/v1/responses`: the exception propagates out of `responses_full_generator` into the catch-all in `create_responses`, which returns it as a 400 `invalid_request_error`. A model-side failure gets reported as the client's fault. - Streaming `/v1/responses`: `responses_stream_generator` consumes the generator with no try/except around the `async for`. The 200 status and SSE headers have already been sent, so the exception kills the stream mid-flight with no error event. The client sees a truncated stream and no explanation. Two aggravating details: - After such an error, the parser keeps raising `HarmonyError` for every following token until the next `<|start|>` token, then recovers on its own. So one malformed header poisons the whole remainder of the turn if the exception is allowed to escape, even when the rest of the output is well formed. - #33717 makes the same observation about harmony parse failures surfacing as 400s, but fixes a different crash (`parse_output_message` on preamble messages in `harmony_utils.py`). It does not guard `parser.process`, so the two changes are complementary. ## Modifications Guard the parser at the source instead of in each consumer, so the streaming and non-streaming paths are fixed at once: - New `HarmonyContext._process_token()` wraps `parser.process()`, catches `HarmonyError`, logs the first failure of a malformed stretch (one log line per desync, not one per token), and skips the token so the parser re-synchronizes at the next message start. This mirrors how the tool-call detectors already treat malformed model output: `base_format_detector.parse_streaming_increment` logs and degrades instead of raising. - All four `parser.process` call sites in `context.py` go through the guard. Resulting behavior on malformed output: the malformed message is dropped and logged, following well-formed messages in the same turn still parse, the non-streaming path returns the surviving output instead of a 400, and the streaming path finishes the SSE stream cleanly instead of dying mid-flight. The same failure class exists in vLLM's harmony plumbing; I have a parallel fix open there (vllm-project/vllm#52055). New unit test `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/test_harmony_context.py` (registered in `base-a-test-cpu`): - non-streaming `append_output` survives the malformed tool-call header above, logs exactly once, drops the malformed message, and still parses the following well-formed message - the same for streaming `append_output` fed one token per chunk - well-formed output parses unchanged, with no error logs Without the guard, the first two tests fail with `openai_harmony.HarmonyError: unexpected tokens remaining in message header: ["to=functions.get_weather"]` at the previously unguarded call sites. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable, no kernel or model forward changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The guard adds a try/except and a flag assignment per token on the harmony parsing path, which is negligible next to the parse itself. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signals.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32207835753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207835753)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207835632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207835632)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kimi-K3] Fix "wrong grids" crash in DP-sharded vision preprocessing
signals.text: ## Motivation Regression introduced by #34404 On Kimi-K3 with cpu transport and DP-sharded vision, one batch with ≥2 images of different resolutions crashes the server with `ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids`. Root cause: the deferred path reads `grid_thws_host` with shard-local positions instead of global image positions. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`: index `grid_thws_host` by global image position at both deferred reads, mapping shard-local positions back via `image_indices`. - `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py`: `test_kimi_k3_preprocesses_only_dp_owner_images` now uses distinct per-image grids (identical ones mask the bug); signals.title: [AMD][DSV4][SWA-BITEXACT 2/5] Host pools and L3 namespacing for strict SWA offload on unified_kv + HiCache
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Part **2/5** of the strict bit-exact SWA prefix reuse for DeepSeek-V4 on the `unified_kv` attention backend with prefix cache enabled, described in [RFC #34562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34562) and split out of [#32214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32214). Builds on [1/5](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35303). This part builds the storage substrate the later parts write into: a host pool that can hold SWA pages, a state pool for the coupled c4 / c4-indexer overlap state, an L3 key namespace that isolates the new blob layout, and the startup guards that keep an unusable configuration from booting. **This part still cannot serve a reuse hit, and refuses to pretend otherwise.** Nothing captures or restores yet, so rather than leave a flag that quietly allocates host memory and returns nothing, `SGLANG_UNIFIED_KV_BIT_EXACT_HICACHE=1` makes the server **refuse to start** ("the SWA capture/restore path is not fully wired"). That temporary guard is removed in 5/5, when the last half lands. With the flag off — the default — no behavior changes. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `memory_pool_host.py`: SWA host-pool support. Per-page capture-completion events (`record_capture_done` / `wait_capture_done` / `sync_capture_done`) so that cross-stream consumers of a captured page — the restore H2D, the L3 write-through, the device-landing check — are ordered against the capture that produced it; `promote_captured_page` and `load_to_device_all_layer` for the transfer paths. - `hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: the feature gate, the pool sizing, and the startup guards. Also registers the coupled state pool. - **sizing.** One SWA window every `--hicache-swa-offload-page-stride` full host pages, plus one tail window per in-flight request (bounded by the device ring), floored at the device ring. The default stride of 1 is therefore the largest this pool ever gets, and raising the stride is the one knob that shrinks it — roughly linearly. - **DRAM budget.** The pool is pinned host memory, so it is checked at startup and never clamped: above 16 GB/rank it warns, because page-locking that much is slow enough to be mistaken for a hung launch; above 90% of available DRAM per rank (real available DRAM / ranks-per-node) it fails with the breakdown and the stride hint, since that pool summed across the node's ranks would exhaust host DRAM outright rather than merely delay the boot. - **write-through is required.** `write_back` cannot guarantee the SWA ring is offloaded before its slot is recycled, so the window a later request would reuse may never have reached the host. Fail at startup rather than serve a silently non-exact hit. - **the temporary "not usable yet" guard** described above, removed in 5/5. - `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`: `swa_region_buffers()` and `get_swa_state_coupling_infos()` expose the ring regions and which state rides with which window, so the capture side in 3/5 does not need to know the pool's internals. - `hicache_storage.py`, `storage/nixl/hicache_nixl.py`: L3 key namespace version (`_swaind1`). The strict path persists the window and its state as independent pools coupled by key, with no A-gather tail packing, so its byte layout differs from the older packed `_swapk1` blobs. Namespacing by layout version makes it impossible to read a stale packed blob under the new layout, in either direction. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> Not reachable in this part. With the flag off nothing in the changed paths executes differently; with the flag on the server refuses to start. Accuracy for the completed feature is reported in #32214 and the RFC. `test/registered/mem_cache/test_swa_bitexact_hicache.py` adds 21 unit tests: the sizing arithmetic across strides and page counts (including that a coarse stride shrinks the pool and that the tail allowance stays bounded by the device ring), both DRAM tiers — the warning that does not clamp and the ceiling that fails with the stride hint — plus its per-rank derivation, both startup guards, and the ring-region geometry and its delegation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> No runtime path changes while the flag is off. The host memory this reserves once enabled is the sizing above; at the default stride of 1 that is one host page per full-KV host page plus the device-ring tail, which is why the stride knob exists. ## Stack | part | contents | |---|---| | [1/5](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35303) | extension points, flag, server arg | | **2/5 (this PR)** | HiCache substrate: SWA host pool, L3 key namespace, startup guards | | 3/5 | capture of SWA windows and c4/indexer overlap state | | 4/5 | window riding on radix nodes and the strict reuse gate | | 5/5 | c4/indexer state riding; completes the feature | [#32214](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32214) stays open as the full-context reference until the stack is in. A fork PR can only target `main`, so this PR's "Files changed" also contains [1/5](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35303) (15 files) until that lands. Reviewing the last commit gives just this part's change (6 files). ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [AMD] Fuse Kimi-K3 MLA Q and cache preparation
signals.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. The larger measured gain is with BF16-Q + FP8-KV. ## AITER dependency This SGLang integration requires AITER #4342 / commit `770790cd` or newer `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` semantics, including the `compute_all_q_rope` behavior used for correct batch-64 execution. The AITER revision currently pinned by main (`d9e5ef7`) is insufficient: its old schema rejects the new argument, and a 14-argument compatibility call produces incorrect token-64 output. This PR intentionally documents rather than changes the AITER pin. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused operator tests: `9 passed` - GSM8K 1319: `0.955` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Historical matched results for the same integration: - BF16 KV: C32 `+0.63%`, C64 `+0.53%` - FP8 KV: C32 `+3.26%`, C64 `+3.57%` - FP8-KV median TPOT: approximately `-4%` ## Test plan - [x] BF16/BF16, FP8/FP8, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV operator tests at token counts 1 and 64 - [x] Negative slot handling - [x] CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs - [x] Narrow support/fallback predicates - [x] Full GSM8K 1319 with Triton prefill/decode and FP8 KV - [ ] Re-run after the target branch updates its AITER pin AITER prefill was not used in the full-model test because 12-head AITER attention-backend enablement is maintained separately; this fusion acts on the decode path. signals.title: [Feat][GLM-5.2] Shared KV Cache for Prefill and Decode
signals.text: ## Summary > **Supersedes [#31435](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31435).** This PR continues its GLM-5.2 Prefill CP Shared KV work and replaces it with a unified mixed Prefill/Decode implementation, adding Demand Cache, optional Shared Indexer, and EAGLE support. Add an opt-in DSA Shared KV cache for GLM-5.2 TP8/Attention-CP8 serving(CP8TP8), with CP Prefill and TP Decode on the same workers. In the tested **H20-3e** configuration, token capacity is about **3.1x–4.8x** Base and **TPOT overhead is < 2 ms**. Persistent Main KV and, by default, Indexer pages keep one owner-sharded copy per CP group. Main KV uses a local Demand Cache for FlashMLA-KV, while Shared Indexer reuses the existing full-batch Indexer compute path. The Base path is unchanged when the feature is disabled, and **EAGLE** is supported. ## Motivation Regular CP8 keeps eight physical Main KV and Indexer replicas for one logical cache. Shared KV stores one owner-sharded copy across the CP group and maps it into a common CUDA VMM address space. - LayerSplit: layer owner → **per-layer NCCL broadcast** → local full-layer scratch → attention - Shared KV: page owner → common VMM view → **local HBM read or demand peer-memory load** → attention Demand loading is intentionally simple: - **owner-local** rows are read directly - a ready local cache row is consumed as a **hit** - on a **miss**, FlashMLA-KV consumes the authoritative peer VMM row and opportunistically fills the local Demand Cache - a **collision or in-progress fill** does not wait; it falls back to the authoritative row Decode keeps current rows in a small local shadow. Shared Indexer materializes only the active shared pages into a reusable local buffer before running the existing full-batch Indexer compute. EAGLE Decode/verify uses the same Shared + Demand path; only draft-model KV remains local and replicated. ## Usage Add `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache --max-running-requests N` to the existing GLM-5.2 Attention-CP FlashMLA-KV command. `N` is configurable in `[1, 32]` and determines the preallocated Decode Demand workspace. Add `--disable-dsa-shared-indexer-cache` to share Main KV while retaining the replicated Indexer. <details><summary>Benchmark launch script</summary> The two simulation variables below are benchmark-only. Production serving must leave both unset. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail MODE=${1:?base|main-only|full} MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH} case "${MODE}" in base) SHARED_ARGS=() ;; main-only) SHARED_ARGS=(--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache --disable-dsa-shared-indexer-cache) ;; full) SHARED_ARGS=(--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3 export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model "${MODEL_PATH}" --tokenizer-path "${MODEL_PATH}" \ --trust-remote-code --quantization w4afp8 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30080 \ --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 --dp-size 1 \ --attention-backend dsa \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_kv --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \ --enable-dsa-prefill-context-parallel \ --dsa-prefill-cp-mode round-robin-split \ --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp "${SHARED_ARGS[@]}" \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --max-running-requests 32 --max-queued-requests 32 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 8 32 \ --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 --random-seed 20260820 \ --skip-server-warmup --enable-cache-report --enable-metrics \ --decode-log-interval 20 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 3 ``` </details> <details><summary>Benchmark script</summary> ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail SCENARIO=${1:?4k-cold-b32|100k-prefix90-b8|256k-prefix90-b16} OUT=${OUT:-benchmark-${SCENARIO}} case "${SCENARIO}" in 4k-cold-b32) INPUT_LEN=4096; BATCH=32; EXPECTED_CACHED=0; POPULATE_LEN=0 ;; 100k-prefix90-b8) INPUT_LEN=102400; BATCH=8; EXPECTED_CACHED=92160; POPULATE_LEN=92224 ;; 256k-prefix90-b16) INPUT_LEN=262144; BATCH=16; EXPECTED_CACHED=235904; POPULATE_LEN=235968 ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac mkdir -p "${OUT}" bench() { local name=$1 input_len=${2:-${INPUT_LEN}} output_len=${3:-1024} local num_prompts=${4:-${BATCH}} python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30080 \ --dataset-name random-ids --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \ --random-input-len "${input_len}" --random-output-len "${output_len}" \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --max-concurrency "${num_prompts}" \ --warmup-requests 0 --seed 20260820 --tokenize-prompt \ --disable-tqdm --output-details --cache-report \ --extra-request-body '{"ignore_eos":true,"temperature":0}' \ --output-file "${OUT}/${name}.jsonl" >"${OUT}/${name}.log" 2>&1 } validate() { python3 - "$1" "${INPUT_LEN}" "${BATCH}" "${EXPECTED_CACHED}" <<'PY' import json, sys p, input_len, batch, cached = sys.argv[1], *map(int, sys.argv[2:]) d = json.loads(open(p).readline()) assert d["completed"] == batch and d["max_concurrency"] == batch assert d["total_input_tokens"] == input_len * batch assert d["total_output_tokens"] == 1024 * batch assert all(x == cached for x in d["cached_tokens"]) assert not any(d["errors"]) assert abs(d["accept_length"] - 3.0) < 0.02 assert all(1020 <= len(x) <= 1023 for x in d["itls"]) PY } # Disjoint JIT warmup; its KV is flushed before measurement. bench warmup 4096 1 1 curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30080/flush_cache >"${OUT}/flush-after-warmup.json" for round in round1 round2; do curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30080/flush_cache >"${OUT}/${round}-flush.json" if (( POPULATE_LEN > 0 )); then bench "${round}-populate" "${POPULATE_LEN}" 1; fi bench "${round}" validate "${OUT}/${round}.jsonl" done ``` The Prefix populate lengths include one extra 64-token page because the radix cache withholds its final page. Formal requests therefore report exactly 92,160 cached tokens for 100K and 235,904 for 256K. </details> ## Capacity Representative H20-3e startup capacity with `mem-fraction-static=0.85` and no explicit token cap: | Storage mode | Token capacity | vs Base | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Base | 960,704 | 1.0x | | Shared Main + replicated Indexer | 2,993,472 | 3.1x | | Shared Main + Shared Indexer | 4,615,808 | 4.8x | ## Prefill/Decode performance EAGLE accept length is fixed at 3. Values are R1/R2; all runs reached the target concurrency with Decode queue 0 and no errors. | Workload | Mode | Cache hit | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Output TPS | TPOT delta | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4K→1K, B32 Cold | Base | 0% | 8.51/8.45 s | 31.38/31.29 ms | 806.47/809.53 | baseline | | 4K→1K, B32 Cold | Shared Main + replicated Indexer | 0% | 8.70/8.44 s | 32.03/31.87 ms | 789.88/798.14 | +0.62 ms | | 4K→1K, B32 Cold | Shared Main + Shared Indexer | 0% | 8.41/8.36 s | 33.13/32.88 ms | 774.26/779.89 | +1.67 ms | | 100K→1K, B8 Prefix-hit | Base | 90% | 7.05/6.84 s | 15.79/16.16 ms | 352.51/350.06 | baseline | | 100K→1K, B8 Prefix-hit | Shared Main + replicated Indexer | 90% | 7.00/6.52 s | 16.74/17.59 ms | 339.09/333.70 | +1.19 ms | | 100K→1K, B8 Prefix-hit | Shared Main + Shared Indexer | 90% | 6.54/7.00 s | 17.74/17.58 ms | 331.34/327.48 | +1.68 ms | | 256K→1K, B16 Prefix-hit | Shared Main + Shared Indexer | 89.99% | 28.95/28.97 s | 56.01/55.95 ms | 189.58/189.64 | Base/Main-only unsupported | <details><summary>Representative raw benchmark output</summary> ```text # Base, 4K→1K/B32 Cold, R1 Successful requests: 32 Benchmark duration (s): 40.63 Input token throughput (tok/s): 3225.89 Output token throughput (tok/s): 806.47 Peak concurrent requests: 32 Accept length: 3.00 Mean TTFT (ms): 8506.64 Median TTFT (ms): 9233.34 Mean TPOT (ms): 31.38 Median TPOT (ms): 30.67 Mean ITL (ms): 31.40 Cache hit rate: 0.0% # Full Shared, 100K→1K/B8 Prefix-hit, R1 Successful requests: 8 Benchmark duration (s): 24.72 Input token throughput (tok/s): 33133.80 Output token throughput (tok/s): 331.34 Peak concurrent requests: 8 Accept length: 3.00 Mean TTFT (ms): 6544.17 Median TTFT (ms): 7141.72 Mean TPOT (ms): 17.74 Median TPOT (ms): 17.16 Mean ITL (ms): 17.75 Total cached tokens: 737280 Cache hit rate: 90.0% # Full Shared, 256K→1K/B16 Prefix-hit, R1 Successful requests: 16 Benchmark duration (s): 86.42 Input token throughput (tok/s): 48532.75 Output token throughput (tok/s): 189.58 Peak concurrent requests: 16 Accept length: 3.00 Mean TTFT (ms): 28946.13 Median TTFT (ms): 28632.25 Mean TPOT (ms): 56.01 Median TPOT (ms): 56.24 Mean ITL (ms): 56.01 Total cached tokens: 3774464 Cache hit rate: 90.0% ``` </details> ## Correctness and release validation - Periodic 32K and 100K EAGLE output IDs match exactly across Base, Main-only, and Full Shared; all correctness and benchmark requests completed without errors or retractions. - The same 500-example, 24-shot GSM8K gate scored Base `0.948`, Main-only `0.950`, and Full Shared `0.944`; all pass the `0.94` threshold. - Focused and multi-GPU tests cover remote VMM, Demand hit/fill/collision, current-row shadow, EAGLE relocation, and CUDA Graph replay. Python compilation and `git diff --check` pass. - Fixed-accept performance runs are performance evidence only and are not reused as correctness evidence. ## Current limitations - Shared CP ranks currently need to be in one peer-accessible NVLink domain; a future extension can use Multi-Node NVLink (MNNVL) fabric memory for multi-node NVLink supernodes such as GB200/GB300 NVL72. - The current release guardrails require `--max-running-requests` in `[1, 32]` and EAGLE verify width up to four; both limits can be extended after larger workspace, CUDA Graph, and concurrency validation. - The supported Shared Demand attention path currently uses FlashMLA-KV for Prefill and Decode; other DSA backends are not yet in the release scope. Co-authored with [@foraxe](https://github.com/foraxe) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32128324083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32128324083)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32128323998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32128323998)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
