signals.title: [diffusion] Allow per-role attention backend override
signals.text: ## Motivation Currently one can choose a global attention backend or a specific backend per component. This PR adds support to choose attention backend per component for each role. That is, a different backend for self-attention and cross-attention. The motivation here is that when using quantized attention backends, there's a quantization overhead prior to running the lower precision kernel. This overhead is mostly worth it in self-attention, but cross-attention calls are often so light that the overhead can be enough for the entire call to be slower than the un-quantized counterpart. The backend can be chosen via the component backend selection: ``` --component-attention-backends.transformer.self=backend_1 -component-attention-backends.transformer.cross=backend_2 ``` The backend choice tree is as follows: 1. selected_attention_backend - explicit arg passed directly into `get_attn_backend()` 2. Global forced backend - `get_global_forced_attn_backend()`, set via `global_force_attn_backend()` (programmatic override) 3. Component + role override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend_for_role(attention_role)`, i.e. the config key transformer.cross / transformer.self 4. Component-wide override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend()`, i.e. the config key transformer (no role suffix) 5. CLI global - `--attention-backend` flag 6. `default_attention_backend` 7. Platform default - if everything above is None, platform picks This now only adds the choice via the `--component-attention-backends`. If desired, I can also add a `--cross-attention-backend` flag. ## Modifications - Enhances the component-attention-backend to support self/cross attn as well - Adds AttentionRole enum used to specify self/cross role (can support others, like joint, as well, if needed) - Refactors all is_cross_attention checks to use the new AttentionRole value instead - Wires AttentionRole to Attention modules, so they can pick the correct backend ## Accuracy Tests Here the self was `torch_sdpa` and cross is `aiter`. Both are used as expected. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c90da006-421a-42d8-b923-301210e0cb4e Output is good. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. signals.text: ### Summary Adds the native **ProductionDebtInferenceGate** and cryptographic **TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger** under `python/sglang/srt/production_debt.py`. ### Problem Solved As enterprise AI architects and Forward Deployed Engineers deploy high-throughput RadixAttention serving, structured programs, and multi-turn agentic workflows in SGLang (LMSYS), engineering organizations require real-time controls over **Enterprise GPU Inference Production Debt & Technical Due Diligence**: 1. **SGLang Debt Index (SDI <= 12.0)**: Scoring inference batches for RadixTree KV cache thrashing, speculative rollback debt, and latency degradation. 2. **Radix KV Cache Eviction Multiplier (REM <= 1.08x)**: Monitoring peak Radix tree cache memory against allocated GPU RAM to eliminate memory fragmentation and OOM crashes. 3. **P99 Time-To-First-Token Ceiling (<= 0.65s)**: Enforcing strict TTFT boundaries across complex structured programs and speculative decoding batches. 4. **Deterministic Mutation Boundaries**: Enforcing `never_equate_intent_to_approval` across state-mutating SGLang tool execution and external API calls. 5. **Cryptographic Technical Due Diligence Action Ledger**: Emitting immutable, SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL receipts providing audit-ready evidence for VC/PE Technical Due Diligence, M&A evaluations, and enterprise production readiness reviews. ### Features Added - `sglang.srt.production_debt.ProductionDebtInferenceGate`: - `evaluate_inference_batch()`: Evaluates batch memory, Radix KV cache ratios, and TTFT latency, returning a normalized Production Readiness Score (0–100) with critical smell warnings. - `sglang.srt.production_debt.TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger`: - `record_inference_event()`: Cryptographically links each serving event into an immutable SHA-256 chain. - `verify_ledger_integrity()`: Validates hash-chain continuity. ### Testing & Validation - Added `test/srt/test_production_debt.py` with 3 automated unit tests validating clean inference batches, degraded Radix sprawl failure detection, and cryptographic ledger integrity (3/3 tests passing). ### Upstream & Commercial Context Maintained by [A2Z SOC](https://a2zsoc.com) for AI Forward Deployed Engineering, GPU Serving Hardening, and Technical Due Diligence. signals.title: [sglang-miles] Fix p2p weight registry: draft worker overwrite, fused indexer mapping, registration retries
signals.text: Three fixes found while verifying miles p2p (RDMA) weight updates on GLM-5.2 744B fp8 with MTP enabled. Companion miles PR: radixark/miles#2605. **Draft worker overwrites the target model's registry** (`model_runner.py`) With speculative decoding, the draft worker's `ModelRunner.initialize()` also calls `maybe_register_and_publish_weight_info()`. The EngineInfoBootstrapServer stores registrations as `dict[tp_rank]`, last write wins, and the draft registers after the target — so the p2p client receives the draft model's weight table and RDMA session for every rank: ordinary target params (`input_layernorm`, `o_proj`, ...) appear missing on the remote and every write bucket fails. The draft is not trained, so it is now excluded from registration. (If draft weight updates are ever needed, the registry key should become `(tp_rank, worker)`.) **Fused DSA indexer weights unmappable by ParameterMapper** (`deepseek_v2.py`) With `use_dsa_indexer_fusion`, the model has one bf16 `indexer.wk_weights_proj` per layer and no `indexer.wk` / `indexer.weights_proj` params. The checkpoint loader folds the unfused names via `_load_fused_indexer_wk`, but `ParameterMapper` — built from `stacked_params_mapping` and used by the p2p staging path — had no entry, so every indexer wk/weights_proj tensor sent by the trainer was silently dropped and the engine's indexer weights went stale. Added the two stacked entries, gated on the fused param existing. Checkpoint loading is unaffected: when fusion is on, the fold helper consumes these names before the stacked loop runs; when fusion is off, the gate keeps the entries out. **Registration was one-shot and swallowed failures** (`remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`) A transient connection failure while PUTting to the bootstrap server was logged and forgotten; the missing rank then surfaced minutes later as a 404 at the first weight update, far from the cause. Both registrations now retry (60 x 5s, timeout 30s) and raise after exhaustion. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32131323240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32131323240)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32131322909](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32131322909)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signals.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32151441084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151441084)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32151440956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151440956)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] Evaluate enc-dec cuda-graph gate on encoder_lens_cpu mirror
signals.text: ## Problem The enc-dec CUDA-graph admission gates in `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` — `can_run_graph()` and `_can_run_ragged_verify_graph()` (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) — evaluated `torch.all(forward_batch.encoder_lens > 0)` (a CUDA tensor) as a Python bool. That bool conversion is an implicit device-to-host sync on the scheduler/forward thread once per decode step, and it forces a drain of every kernel queued on the stream before the sync can complete — on a busy stream the drain dominates and costs far more than the bare sync (bare sync window is on the order of a few hundred µs; exact numbers are workload-dependent). ## Fix Both gates now go through `_encoder_lens_all_positive(forward_batch)`, which evaluates the same all-positive predicate on the CPU mirror `forward_batch.encoder_lens_cpu` when it is available (host-side `all()`, no device traffic), falling back to the original device-tensor check only when the mirror is `None`. The mirror is built from the same Python list as the device tensor, and the gates that consult it run before DP padding appends any device-only zero rows, so when present the predicate result is identical at those gates. ## Tests New tests in `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` cover both gates: the mirror is consulted and the device tensor is never materialized into a bool on the happy path (spy), the fallback path when the mirror is `None`, and a disagreeing-mirror case (mirror all-positive, device tensor containing a zero) pinning that the mirror takes precedence by design — if they ever disagree, the device tensor is the stale one. 18 passed, 21 subtests passed on CPU (the GPU-marked parity test is deselected without a GPU). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32129182645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32129182645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32129182614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32129182614)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion][AMD] Add gfx1250 detection and stop silent CPU fallback for diffusion
signals.text: # [Diffusion][AMD] Add gfx1250 detection and stop silent CPU fallback for diffusion ## Motivation #32754 enables gfx1250 for the SRT path. `multimodal_gen` has its own platform-resolution and aiter-gating modules, so it needs the equivalent plumbing before diffusion models can be brought up on gfx1250. ## Changes **1. `srt/utils/common.py` — add `is_gfx1250_supported()`** Alongside the existing `is_gfx95_supported()` / `is_gfx942_supported()`, same pattern and `lru_cache`. Note #32754 introduces an identical helper; whichever lands second should drop its copy. Kept here so this PR is self-contained if it lands first. **2. `multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/aiter.py` — expose `USE_AITER_GFX1250`** So diffusion code can gate arch-specific aiter paths the way it already does for gfx942 and gfx95x (`USE_AITER_GFX942`, `USE_AITER_GFX95`). **3. `multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/__init__.py` — don't silently fall back to CPU** This is the substantive fix. `rocm_platform_plugin()` decided ROCm-vs-CPU solely on whether `import amdsmi` and `amdsmi_get_processor_handles()` succeeded: ```python except Exception as e: logger.debug("ROCm platform is unavailable: %s", e) ``` `amdsmi` is an optional dependency and is absent from several ROCm container images. When it is missing, the exception is swallowed into a `logger.debug` and platform resolution falls through to `CpuPlatform`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32130274749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130274749)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32130274417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130274417)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Perf] PaddleOCR-VL: overlap page preprocessing, pack the ViT, enable prefill CUDA graph
signals.text: ## Motivation PaddleOCR-VL served a 1080p page in **235 ms** and saturated at **6.7 req/s** on an H200 while the GPU sat idle. Profiling put almost none of that in the model's own compute: | what | why it was slow | |---|---| | Image processor ran **single-threaded** | `QwenVLImageProcessor` grants concurrent workers only to an explicit `model_type` allowlist that `paddleocr_vl` is not on. An 87 ms/page preprocess caps throughput at ~11 req/s no matter how much GPU is left. | | **Prefill CUDA graph was off** | Breakable CG is the CUDA default, but the generic "multimodal model" rule disables it for every multimodal arch. PaddleOCR-VL's config always carries a `vision_config`, so even *text-only* prefill lost the graph. | | ViT recomputed and re-synchronized **per image** | A device-side `max()` for the rope table, one host sync per image to slice the encoder output, a bilinear position-embedding interpolation per image per forward (the LFU cache written for it was never called), and a full projector pass per image. | | `quant_config` accepted and **dropped** | `--quantization` was a silent no-op for both the LM and the vision tower. | ## Modifications - `multimodal/processors/paddleocr_vlm.py` — opt into concurrent preprocessing (4 workers, 16 IO threads). A document page is a far heavier preprocessing unit than a chat image. - `configs/model_config.py` — allowlist the arch for breakable prefill CUDA graph, the way the Kimi archs are. Embed-carrying batches are still rejected at replay and run eager, so this is a text/mixed-traffic win. - `models/paddleocr_vl.py` — run the vision tower packed: grids stay on the host, the encoder output stays concatenated, the 2x2 merge writes into one buffer, and the two projections run once for the batch instead of once per image. Wire up the position-embedding LFU cache that was already written but never called. Pass `quant_config` through. Take `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold+matmul path for the patch embedding (kernel == stride, zero padding). - `models/ernie4.py` — give `Ernie4Model` a `get_input_embeddings`, replacing a `hasattr` + `types.MethodType` patch at the PaddleOCR-VL call site. - Cookbook page for PaddleOCR-VL / 1.5 / 1.6 (identical `config.json`, so one recipe serves all three), plus the `supported-models` row. ## Accuracy Every arm was gated on output equality before it was measured: five page geometries x two task prompts under greedy decoding, compared against the pre-change baseline. - packed ViT: **10/10 byte-identical** (text and token counts) - \+ four concurrent preprocessing workers: **10/10** - \+ transformers-native image processor: **10/10** - \+ the final scheduling recipe: **10/10** CPU unit tests pin the packed vision math to a per-image reference implementation at fp64 (packed 2x2 merge, batch invariance, the position-embedding cache vs uncached interpolation, LFU eviction, conv-vs-matmul, packed 2D position ids), and a second file pins the two allowlist memberships, which are exactly the kind of setting a refactor drops silently. ## Benchmark One H200, PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, 1080p JPEG pages (~2700 image tokens), 128 output tokens, prefix + multimodal caches disabled, **median** TTFT, arms interleaved within a single run, 2-3 reps. | workload | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1080p page, 1 stream (TTFT) | 235.1 ms | **119.6 ms** (1.97x) | | 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 6.67 req/s | **12.26 req/s** (1.84x) | | 2704-token text, 1 stream (TTFT) | 16.1 ms | **11.5 ms** (1.40x, from the prefill graph) | Against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same box, same caches-off settings: | workload | sglang | vLLM | |---|---|---| | 2704-tok text, 1 stream TTFT | **11.5 ms** | 15.9 ms | | 2704-tok text, 32 concurrent | **95.4 req/s** | 81.8 req/s | | 1080p page, 1 stream TTFT | **119.6 ms** | 137.5 ms | | 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 12.26 req/s | **12.77 req/s** | The one remaining loss is saturated page throughput, ~4% behind. It is GPU-bound in the vision tower (full attention over ~10.7k patches, `head_dim=72`); `fa4`, `triton_attn`, `cuda_ipc` feature transport, more processor workers, PD-multiplexing and every chunked-prefill size were all measured and none of them helped. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_paddleocr_vl_vision.py`, `..._serving_defaults.py`) and an e2e server test (`test/registered/vlm/test_paddleocr_vl_server.py`) - [x] Benchmark on real hardware with accuracy verified against the pre-change baseline - [x] Update documentation (cookbook page + supported-models row) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32176324134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32176324134)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32176324019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32176324019)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.15 (gfx942 / gfx950) stages to the ROCm Dockerfile
signals.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.15 publishes no `rocm/pytorch` base image, so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing ROCm 7.0 / 7.2 stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.15 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The SDK pin is a nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release: the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0. This specific build is the one the gfx1250 7.15 image also pins, so all three arches share a single 7.15 SDK. Note for sequencing with #32754 (`[AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support`): that PR adds its own copy of a 7.15 pip-SDK stage, which could instead reuse the shared `rocm715-base` stage introduced here. Both PRs also introduce the same `rocm_legacy` / `rocm_rock` extras in `python/pyproject_other.toml`. Whichever lands second will need to be reconciled against the first. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm715-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.15 pip stack — `rocm[libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950]==7.15.0a20260712`, `torch==2.11.0`, `torchvision==0.26.0`, `triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6`, from the ROCm nightlies and devreleases indexes. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15`, which only set build flags (`BUILD_VLLM`, `BUILD_TRITON`, `BUILD_LLVM`, `BUILD_AITER_ALL`, `BUILD_MOONCAKE`, `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`). Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skip the apt install for `*rocm7_15*`, since libdrm ships with the pip SDK. - amdsmi: install it for `*rocm7_15*` (same branch as 7.2), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm 7.x images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: remove `libabsl-dev` before configuring, because nixl's meson wants an abseil providing `absl_log` and refuses its bundled subproject while Ubuntu 24.04's older `libabsl-dev` (20220623) is visible. Only `-dev` packages are removed; `libabsl20220623t64` stays so the Mooncake binaries built earlier keep the shared library they linked against. - Second commit: removing `libabsl-dev` also removes `libgrpc-dev` and `libgrpc++-dev`, which depend on it, so all three are reinstalled once nixl is built. The image's own MORI is built before this point and is fine, but the CI install script rebuilds MORI inside the image, and without `libgrpc++-dev` that rebuild configures without gRPC and silently drops symbols the Python side imports — `mori.umbp` then fails on `CacheRemoteAdmission` and `test_umbp_store` errors out. - The SGLang install now selects a `compressed-tensors` extra: `rocm_rock` for `*rocm7_15*`, `rocm_legacy` otherwise. ### `python/pyproject_other.toml` - Moved `compressed-tensors` out of `srt_hip` into two new mutually exclusive extras, `rocm_legacy = ["compressed-tensors==0.15.0"]` and `rocm_rock = ["compressed-tensors==0.16.0"]`. 0.15.0 requires `torch<2.11` and 0.16.0 requires `torch>=2.10`, so the correct pin depends on which torch the ROCm SDK generation ships rather than on the platform. Pinning the wrong one leaves pip trying to replace the image's ROCm torch with a PyPI build, which it cannot do, and the resolve then fails. Neither extra is pulled automatically — the Dockerfile and the CI install script append one. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Detect the ROCm version inside the CI container and append the matching `compressed-tensors` extra (`rocm_rock` for >= 7.15.0, else `rocm_legacy`) to `EXTRAS`. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. - Keep ROCm 7.15's own Triton (`INSTALL_AITER_TRITON=false` for HIP `7.15*`, matching `BUILD_TRITON=0` on the new stages). AITER's `install_triton.sh` resolves its wheel index from `dpkg -l rocm-core`, which does not exist for a pip-installed SDK, so it would fall back to the ROCm 7.2 index and drop a 7.2-built Triton into a 7.15 image. Verified in the built image that `dpkg-query` finds no `rocm-core` and that `torch.version.hip` reports `7.15.0`. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - Added `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15` to the build matrix, and replaced the single-arch `if` with a `case` mapping them to the `rocm7.15-mi30x` and `rocm7.15-mi35x` tags. - Build args: dropped `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` and `SGLANG_VERSION`, neither of which this Dockerfile consumes, and pass `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, which is what the SGLang install actually reads. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). - `gfx942-rocm7_15` builds end to end (46GB image). - In-image smoke test: torch `2.11.0+rocm7.15.0a20260712`, `torch.version.hip` `7.15.0`, `gcnArchName` `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi` and `sglang` all import. - The real CI flow was run against the image: `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0, and `test/run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **6/8 passed**. That matches a ROCm 10 image baseline run on the same host on 2026-08-17, which was also 6/8. The two failures are `test_basic_sanity.py` and `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, both `huggingface_hub.errors.GatedRepoError: 401` on `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` because this host has no `HF_TOKEN` — identical to the baseline and unrelated to this change. - Known gap: the `gfx950-rocm7_15` stage has **not** been built or run. It shares `rocm715-base` with gfx942 and differs only in the AITER / sgl-kernel compile targets, but it is unverified. The host is MI300X, so gfx950 runtime tests were not possible here. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [Spec] Support dp attention for DFLASH speculative decoding
signals.text: ## Motivation DFLASH currently hard-rejects `--enable-dp-attention`. This implementation follows the established DSpark DP-attention design, with #34844 as the closest reference for DP collective participation and validation. Since the DFLASH draft is always dense, this PR reuses only the dense-draft path without bringing over the MoE-specific synchronization and ragged-verify machinery. ## Modifications `dflash_worker_v2.py`: run draft construction, backend initialization, CUDA graph capture, and draft forward under `draft_tp_context(attn_tp_group)`. Follow the target `lm_head`'s actual vocab-shard group for draft-token sampling, and make idle DP ranks participate in target prefill and verify collectives. Verify participation uses a dummy `DFlashVerifyInput` so DP token-count metadata matches busy ranks. `speculative_hook.py`: replace the blanket rejection with the constraints required by the dense path: `--enable-dp-lm-head` is required and `attn_cp_size > 1` remains unsupported. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: key DFLASH draft graphs by DP-local batch size and preserve the custom-mask policy captured by the graph during idle replay. ## Accuracy and Performance Tests Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFLASH draft, block size 16, 2x NVIDIA L20X, GSM8K (32 prompts), temperature 0, FlashInfer. TP2 is the control; DP2 adds `--dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head`. | variant | conc | output throughput (tok/s) | accept rate | accuracy | accept length | |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | TP2 | 1 | 629.4 | 37.38% | 0.969 | 6.597 | | TP2 + DP2 | 1 | 363.2 | 37.69% | 0.969 | 6.640 | | TP2 | 32 | 2625.4 | 36.52% | 0.969 | 6.466 | | TP2 + DP2 | 32 | 3142.9 | 37.42% | 0.969 | 6.600 | Accuracy is identical and accept rate/length match across TP2 and DP2. Concurrency 1 exercises the idle-rank paths; neither run hung and both server logs were clean. Throughput is total client-side output throughput. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests — no public DFLASH target/draft pair in CI currently supports DP attention; validation uses the 2-GPU comparison above. - [ ] Update documentation — no user-facing interface change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32133213627](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32133213627)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32133213592](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32133213592)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] flashinfer_mla: use flashinfer native fp8 MLA on SM90 instead of per-layer full-pool bf16 cast
signals.text: ## Problem Under `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the MLA token pool already stores unscaled e4m3 bits (`MLATokenToKVPool` allocates a uint8 arena and `set_kv_buffer` casts with no scale), but the `flashinfer_mla` backend never consulted `model_runner.kv_cache_dtype`: it planned both dtype arguments with the model dtype and, in `forward_decode` and the paged branch of `forward_extend`, paid ```python self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id).to(q.dtype) ``` on every attention layer, every step — a **full-pool** bf16 materialization (all allocated slots, not just resident tokens), including idle steps, and inside CUDA-graph capture (so it is replayed every step). Independently reported in #35291: on DeepSeek-R1 (8×H200, 131K-token pool) the same cast costs 13.77 ms of a 31.52 ms decode step (43.7%), with ~98.9% of the moved bytes never referenced by the page table. That report also names the `fa3` backend; this change covers `flashinfer_mla` only — `fa3`'s MLA path has no native fp8-KV kernel to hand the raw pool buffer to and needs its own treatment (out of scope here). Two consequences, measured on a real server (H100 80GB, 61-layer structurally-real DeepSeek-V3-family model with dummy weights, pool pinned to 1M tokens, decode CUDA graphs on, 4 concurrent × 384-token greedy decodes, torch profiler over 40 decode steps): 1. **Throughput collapse.** The cast kernel (`unrolled_elementwise_kernel<direct_copy_kernel_cuda>`) launches exactly 61× per decode step, 1.76 ms each = **107.4 ms/step of pure copy**. Measured TPOT: `main + fp8 KV` = **109.75 ms/token** vs `main + bf16 KV` = **4.42 ms/token** — the entire difference is the cast (the rest of the step is ~4 ms). The cost scales with the *allocated pool*, not with resident context: a fresh server with short requests pays it in full from the first step, and idle steps pay it too. 2. **Hard OOM on large pools.** With a naturally-sized fp8 pool (mem-fraction 0.92 → 2.07M tokens), `main + fp8` crashes with CUDA OOM during the first prefill: the full-pool cast in `forward_extend` tries to allocate a transient 2.2 GiB bf16 shadow of the pool. Same mechanism as the Kimi-Linear up-convert OOM (#34638). flashinfer has supported bf16-q × fp8-e4m3-KV MLA natively on SM90 since 0.6.14 (flashinfer PR #3694; fa3 backend, `head_dim_ckv=512`, `head_dim_kpe=64`, per-tensor `ckv_scale`/`kpe_scale`; sglang's current `flashinfer==0.6.17` pin includes it) — only the sglang-side wiring was missing. ## Fix Single-file change to `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`: - A pure helper `_fp8_kv_enabled(...)` gates the native path on exactly what the flashinfer kernel supports: `kv_cache_dtype == e4m3` + SM90 + bf16 model + `kv_lora_rank=512`/`qk_rope_head_dim=64` + DCP disabled. Non-qualifying configs (non-fp8 KV, other architectures, fp16 models, NoPE MLA, e5m2, DCP) keep the existing upcast path byte-for-byte; a single warning is logged when an fp8 KV cache was requested but disqualified (pointing Blackwell users to `trtllm_mla`). - The decode and paged-prefill `plan()` calls now pass `kv_data_type=torch.float8_e4m3fn` on the qualifying path (previously the model dtype twice). - `forward_decode`/`forward_extend` pass the raw e4m3 pool buffer — sliced as `[:, :, :512]` / `[:, :, 512:]` strided views of the fused 576-wide row — plus `ckv_scale=1.0, kpe_scale=1.0`, instead of upcasting the whole pool. The kernel plumbs outer strides explicitly, so the 576-strided views are consumed directly; the pool layout and write path are untouched. - Scales are 1.0 because the write side stores unscaled e4m3; per-tensor scale plumbing (e.g. checkpoint-provided `k_scale`) is left as a follow-up. - CUDA-graph fast-path plans are untouched: the dtype is baked at capture-time `plan()`, which routes through the same modified updaters. ## Numerics The SM90 fp8 kernel keeps KV as e4m3 through HBM/L2/SMEM and dequantizes to bf16 right before the (bf16) WGMMA. Unscaled e4m3 values are exactly representable in bf16, so the fp8 path feeds the math the same bits as the old `.to(bf16)` upcast. Verified on H100 across 256 kernel configs (`batch {1,4,16,64} × qo_len {1,8,64} × kv_len {256..16384} × page_size {1,64} × heads {16,128}`, causal on/off, production dims only): output is **bitwise identical** to running the bf16 kernel on the upcast pool; strided 576-wide views match packed contiguous copies bitwise; absolute error vs an fp32 reference (rel-L2 ≤ 2.9e-3) is unchanged from the bf16 kernel. The e2e A/B above additionally ran the full server on the PR branch with fp8 KV under CUDA graphs without any anomaly (dummy weights, so token-level output comparison is not meaningful; kernel-level bitwise identity is established separately). ## End-to-end results Real server, methodology as in Problem (full artifacts: server logs, per-config traces, timing JSON): | config | pool | TPOT (ms/token) | cast kernel per step | |---|---|---|---| | main + bf16 KV | 1.00M tok / 65.4 GiB | 4.42 | — | | main + fp8 KV | 1.00M tok / 32.7 GiB | **109.75** | 61 × 1.76 ms = 107.4 ms | | branch + bf16 KV | 1.00M tok / 65.4 GiB | 4.54 | — | | branch + fp8 KV | 1.00M tok / 32.7 GiB | **5.84** | none (0.22 ms / 40 steps of index bookkeeping) | Same-config effect of this PR: **109.75 → 5.84 ms/token (18.8×)**; the branch is within reach of the bf16 baseline (+1.3 ms ≈ the fp8 MLA kernel's per-op tax at this short context; see the kernel-level caveat below for how it scales). Kernel-level scaling reference (pure-kernel self-time, decode @ kv_len 8192, 128 heads, ×61 layers): the eliminated cast costs ~1.76 ms/layer per 1M slots (≈107 ms/step at 1M; ~534 ms/step at 5M slots, the latter an out-of-range-for-single-H100 scaling bound), including idle steps. One honest caveat: per operation the fp8 MLA kernel is 2.0–2.65× slower than the bf16 kernel at equal batch (SMEM dequant-repack; e.g. 539→1428 µs at batch 128, kv 8192), so the net win is entirely the cast elimination. It is largest for **decode**, where the cast is paid on the *allocated* pool against one token of attention per layer; prefill/extend also drop the cast but pay the kernel tax on the full KV length, so their net saving is smaller and pool-size-dependent. ## Tests - New `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_fp8_kv.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): guard-table coverage for all disqualifiers; `__init__` wiring; the fallback warning firing exactly once per process (including across the several backends a spec-decode scheduler builds); `kv_data_type` selection in both decode plan call sites and the paged prefill plan; run-branch selection pinned hard (fp8: raw e4m3 strided views with the pool's 576-row stride on both ckv and kpe, exact `run()` kwarg set, `ckv_scale/kpe_scale=1.0`, and **zero** `.to()` upcasts off the pool; non-fp8: exactly one bf16 cast, no scale kwargs); and a cuda-graph lifecycle integration test driving the real backend + indices updaters (eager decode → capture → replay → target-verify, with a bf16 control run) that asserts every stock and fast `plan` carries the backend's kv dtype and that replay reuses the captured wrapper instance. 16 tests + 24 subtests; hand-checked mutations fail at least one test. - GPU validation (out of tree): the 256-config bitwise-identity harness and the 4-config real-server A/B above. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208573720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208573720)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208573526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208573526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(openai): avoid duplicate routed expert in response when `return_meta_info = True`
signals.text: ## Summary Avoid duplicate extension metadata in non-streaming chat completion responses. ## Symptom & Reproduction - **Symptom:** Enabling `return_meta_info` duplicated requested extension metadata across `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext`. - **Reproduction:** Serialize a non-streaming response with all three metadata flags enabled. - **Expected:** Extension metadata occurs once per choice. - **Observed before the fix:** The first choice's metadata also appears in response-level `sglext`. ## Root Cause 1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice extension data into response-level `SglExt`. 2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same extension data in each choice. ## Fix Skip response-level `SglExt` construction when `return_meta_info` is enabled, making each choice's `meta_info` authoritative. Keep the existing `sglext` shape unchanged when `return_meta_info` is disabled, and preserve distinct metadata for `n > 1`. ## Verification - `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: 103 passed and 38 subtests passed. - `ruff check --ignore E402 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: passed with only the files' existing E402 bootstrap pattern excluded. - `ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: both files already formatted. ## Review Focus - `_build_chat_response`: `return_meta_info=False` must retain the legacy response-level fields. - `test_non_streaming_meta_info_omits_sglext_and_preserves_each_choice`: each choice must retain its own extension metadata without an empty or duplicated `sglext`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32133883941](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32133883941)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207655266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207655266)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [VLM] Add video input support for Kimi-K3
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 has a temporal MoonViT3d vision stack, but its SGLang multimodal processor currently handles still images only. Although the OpenAI-compatible protocol can carry `video_url` content, Kimi-K3 requests cannot route decoded video frames through the checkpoint's media processor and vision tower. This adds video input support for Kimi-K3 while preserving the existing image path. Video frames are processed; audio tracks are not. The implementation targets the current Kimi multimodal pipeline. This is related to the earlier Kimi-K2.5 attempt in #21023, which was closed after that older processor pipeline was replaced. ## Modifications - accept Kimi-K3 `video_url` inputs from server-accessible URLs, local paths, and Base64 data URLs - sample frames with the checkpoint media configuration and split them into timestamped temporal chunks for MoonViT3d - preserve mixed image/video ordering and enforce one-to-one visual placeholder mapping - reuse the Kimi image placeholder token while carrying temporal `grid_thw` metadata through preprocessing and model execution - map image grids globally for encoder-DP execution - keep image artifact caching unchanged; video requests intentionally use the uncached path - expose video token usage in non-streaming Chat Completions responses - document video request examples and the no-audio limitation - add focused OpenAI protocol, processor, model, and DP regression tests ## Accuracy Tests Unit tests: ```text pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py 162 passed ``` Real-model smoke tests used Kimi-K3 with TP8 on one 8x NVIDIA B300 node: - video URL, local path, and Base64 data URL inputs - mixed image/video input ordering - Chat Completions streaming - Responses API - image-only regression A 5.16 MB MP4 produced HTTP 200 and correctly identified one restaurant scene with roughly six people dining and conversing. The request used 43,969 prompt tokens, including 43,200 visual tokens. An extracted 49.4 KB frame produced HTTP 200 and correctly described the two foreground diners. The request used 1,282 prompt tokens, including 1,170 image tokens. ## Speed Tests and Profiling There is no before/after video latency comparison because Kimi-K3 video requests were unsupported before this change. Cold end-to-end measurements on the TP8 B300 deployment, with `reasoning_effort=low`, `max_tokens=256`, and no cached prompt tokens: | Input | End-to-end latency | Completion tokens | |---|---:|---:| | 5.16 MB MP4 | 6.361 s | 115 | | 49.4 KB image | 1.343 s | 127 | The text path is unchanged. The existing image artifact-cache path remains active for image-only requests; videos bypass it because the cache currently stores image artifacts only. ## Limitations - video audio tracks are not processed - separate audio input is not added by this PR - video preprocessing intentionally bypasses the image artifact cache ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32139310022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139310022)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32139309596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139309596)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(core): add ProductionDebtRadixCacheGate and TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger
signals.text: ### Summary Adds the native **ProductionDebtRadixCacheGate** and cryptographic **TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger** under `sglang/srt/mem_cache/production_debt.py`. ### Problem Solved As enterprise AI architects and Forward Deployed Engineers deploy high-throughput multi-turn agentic systems and reasoning workloads (e.g. DeepSeek R1, Chatbot Arena models) with SGLang across multi-GPU Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell (B200) clusters, engineering organizations require real-time controls over **Enterprise SGLang RadixCache & Chunked Prefill Production Debt & Technical Due Diligence**: 1. **RadixCache Debt Index (RDI <= 12.0)**: Scoring radix trie tree execution for orphaned trie node memory fragmentation, multi-GPU chunked prefill pipeline stalls, structured decoding regex token mask overhead, and trie lookup/eviction latency degradation. 2. **Trie Tree Memory Sprawl Multiplier (TTMM <= 1.08x)**: Monitoring peak utilized prefix cache memory against physical HBM limits to eliminate LRU eviction thrashing. 3. **P99 Trie Lookup & Eviction Latency Ceiling (<= 2.8ms)**: Enforcing sub-millisecond prefix hit traversal and block allocation boundaries across continuous batching loops. 4. **Deterministic Mutation Boundaries**: Enforcing `never_equate_intent_to_approval` across state-mutating trie node splittings, parent-child link mutations, and structured grammar token masks. 5. **Cryptographic Technical Due Diligence Action Ledger**: Emitting immutable, SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL receipts providing audit-ready evidence for VC/PE Technical Due Diligence, M&A evaluations, and enterprise production readiness reviews. ### Features Added - `sglang.srt.mem_cache.production_debt.ProductionDebtRadixCacheGate`: - `evaluate_trie_eviction()`: Evaluates trie memory ratios, chunked prefill stalls, and lookup latency, returning a normalized Production Readiness Score (0–100) with critical smell warnings. - `sglang.srt.mem_cache.production_debt.TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger`: - `record_radix_event()`: Cryptographically links each trie tree allocation and prefix eviction event into an immutable SHA-256 chain. - `verify_ledger_integrity()`: Validates hash-chain continuity. ### Testing & Validation - Added `test/srt/test_radix_debt.py` with 3 automated unit tests validating clean RadixCache trie tree operations, degraded memory fragmentation failure detection, and cryptographic ledger integrity (3/3 tests passing). ### Upstream & Commercial Context Maintained by [A2Z SOC](https://a2zsoc.com) for AI Forward Deployed Engineering, SGLang RadixCache Hardening, and Technical Due Diligence. For engineering organizations and investors requiring codebase due diligence or production debt triage: - **Instant Audit ($499):** https://a2zsoc.com/productized-services#instant-audit-tripwire - **Technical Due Diligence ($25K–$50K) & Production Debt Remediation Sprints ($50K–$100K):** https://a2zsoc.com/consultation <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32139606918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139606918)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32139606692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139606692)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Distributed] Enable custom all-reduce for attention TP groups
signals.text: ## Summary Enable custom-all-reduce capability detection for derived attention tensor-parallel groups. ## Motivation With DP attention, the full TP group and attention-TP group may differ. For example, a 16-rank DP4 x attention-TP4 launch creates a full TP16 group plus four attention-TP4 subgroups. The attention groups were constructed with `use_custom_allreduce=False`, so eligible node-local subgroups could never select CustomAllReduceV2. The server-side MNNVL auto-enable logic also used the full `tp_size` as a global gate. That suppressed eligible derived groups before their own topology and world-size checks could run. ## Changes - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Remove the server-level `tp_size <= 8` gate from MNNVL auto-enable. - Leave final selection to `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2(group, device)` for each process group. - Add focused tests for TP16 launches with derived groups and attention-TP group construction. ## Behavior For a DP4 x attention-TP4 launch: - Full TP16 independently rejects or falls back downstream. - Each eligible attention-TP4 subgroup can select CustomAllReduceV2. - Explicit custom-all-reduce disable settings remain respected. ## Validation - Python syntax compilation passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Added CPU unit coverage for the changed selection behavior. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32145778328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145778328)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32145777749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145777749)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kimi] Enable GB300 SP collectives for attention TP4 and TP16
signals.text: ## Summary Enable tuned Kimi K3 sequence-parallel collectives on GB300 for both derived attention-TP subgroups and world-size 16. This covers: - DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16, where the attention group is a node-local subgroup of the full TP16 group. - Attention-TP16 / EP16 across four GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment. ## Motivation SGLang already creates a separate attention-TP group when attention TP differs from full TP, but that group was constructed with `use_custom_allreduce=False`. The server-side MNNVL auto-enable logic also gated on the full `tp_size`, suppressing eligible derived TP4/TP8 groups before their own capability checks could run. World-size 16 additionally needs multinode CustomAllReduceV2 workspace support and an exact-device K3 SP tuning table. Generic TP16 all-reduces should remain on NCCL until independently tuned. ## Changes ### Process-group selection - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Remove the server-level `tp_size <= 8` MNNVL gate. - Leave final communicator selection to `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2(group, device)` for each process group. - Add focused tests for TP16 launches with derived groups and attention-TP construction. ### K3 world-16 support - Admit world-size 16 CustomAllReduceV2 communicators on multinode MNNVL fabric. - Use the world-16 communicator as symmetric-workspace infrastructure for K3 SP kernels. - Keep ordinary TP16 all-reduces on NCCL. - Enable K3 SP dispatch for world size 16 when an exact-device table is available. - Add the GB300 `world=16,H=7168` reduce-scatter/all-gather tuning table. - Keep untuned attention-residual fusion entries on the existing `separate` path. - Add one-time dispatch/fallback diagnostics. ## TP4 validation Nsight Systems confirmed exactly 92 custom TP4 reduce-scatter/all-gather pairs per decode step: - NCCL reduce-scatter launches over ten steps: 930 -> 10. - NCCL all-gather launches: 940 -> 20. - Custom reduce-scatter launches: 0 -> 920. - Custom all-gather launches: 0 -> 920. Representative medians: - Reduce-scatter: 16.014 -> 6.853 us (`-57.2%`). - All-gather: 16.508 -> 7.179 us (`-56.5%`). - Aligned layers 84-87 wall time: 1883.232 -> 1753.139 us (`-6.91%`). - Full decode graph: 43.365 -> 40.259 ms (`-7.16%`). Large TP4 prefill shapes continue to fall back safely to NCCL when they exceed the default push workspace. ## World-16 tuning and correctness The table was tuned on four GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment over global-token buckets 16 through 16384. - Every measured push/pull/direct candidate was checked against NCCL before timing. - BF16 comparison used `rtol=2e-2`, `atol=5e-2` to account for rank-16 reduction-order differences. - Every selected custom bucket was faster than NCCL. - The production table was checked under CUDA graph capture/replay at every bucket. Representative results: | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Custom | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 105.371 us | 17.219 us | 6.12x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.081 us | 16.824 us | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 265.358 us | 171.723 us | 1.55x | | All-gather | 8192 | 224.534 us | 171.736 us | 1.31x | ## TP16 serving and dispatch validation Workload: ISL 8192, OSL 1024, concurrency 512, 2048 requests, attention-TP16 / EP16. - Output throughput: 2872.99 -> 3029.28 tok/s (`+5.44%`). - Median TPOT: 117.64 -> 109.69 ms (`-6.76%`). - Median ITL: 55.33 -> 48.60 ms (`-12.16%`). - Aligned layers 84-87 wall time: 2398.005 -> 2100.865 us (`-12.39%`). - Eight SP collectives in that window: 369.731 -> 137.872 us (`-62.71%`). Nsight Systems confirmed, over ten rank-0 decode steps: - 920 custom reduce-scatter launches. - 920 custom direct all-gather launches. - Zero NCCL reduce-scatter launches. - Ordinary non-SP TP16 all-reduces remained on NCCL. ## Deployment note The validated world-16 production launch used: ```bash SGLANG_FORCE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2_PUSH_SIZE_KB=16384 ``` This provides the full K3 push workspace rather than clipping it at the generic all-reduce crossover. ## Local checks - Python syntax compilation passed. - JSON parsing passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Added CPU unit coverage for the changed group-selection behavior.

signals.title: [diffusion] Warmup-calibrated auto residency promotion in performance-mode auto
signals.text: ## Motivation Under `--performance-mode auto`, component placement is decided **before load** from static per-model thresholds (`keep_resident_min_available_gb`). On GPUs with ample free VRAM this leaves components needlessly offloaded — e.g. a layerwise-offloaded text encoder on an 80–140 GB card pays a full H2D reload every request for VRAM nobody else uses — and fixing it by hand requires per-model, per-GPU flag tuning. This PR makes `auto` mode **calibrate residency from the server warmup it already runs**: measure real memory behavior, then promote implicitly offloaded components to GPU-resident when the default workload provably fits, before the server turns ready. Frozen after `/health`; no changes after startup. ## Modifications **Measurement** - Server warmup forwards record `peak_reserved` + a pre-forward baseline on **every rank** (previously output-rank only). - Video warmup (which caps frames to bound startup) adds one extra small-frame **calibration forward**; a two-point affine fit in workload units (`batch × W × H × frames`) separates constant (weights/buffers) from linear (activation) memory and extrapolates the default-workload peak with a 1.2× margin on the linear part only. Image warmup already runs the default shape, so it is a direct measurement, no extrapolation. - The loader now records real weight/buffer sizes alongside the GPU-load delta (`memory_usages` is ≈0 for exactly the offloaded components residency decisions are about). **Decision + promotion (between last warmup req and ready)** - All ranks all-gather `{estimated peak, budget, candidates}` and compute one deterministic plan: candidates are implicitly offloaded, known-size, native CUDA components only; ranked by per-request H2D savings (layerwise DiT counts default denoise steps); promoted greedily while `estimated_peak + promoted_bytes + reserve ≤ budget`, with `reserve = max(10 % budget, 4 GiB)` and `budget = free + torch-reserved` (min across ranks; excludes other processes on shared GPUs). - Promotion reuses existing primitives: component-offload → resident via `require_component_resident`, layerwise via `disable_offload()`; the strategy cache is invalidated explicitly. - A **re-warm forward** after promotion re-establishes compile/kernel caches and proves the promoted layout actually serves; any failure rolls every rank back to the original strategy (only a rollback failure aborts startup). - Excluded paths: explicit placement / `manual` mode, FSDP, diffusers backend, quantized DiT (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4, SVDQuant), Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graph, realtime/disagg, `batching_max_size > 1`, any warmup failure. Kill switch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY=1`. **Fixes and unification along the way** - Warmup frame caps now run the pipeline's `adjust_num_frames`: LongLive2's server warmup was silently a no-op (17 capped frames → 5 latent frames, not divisible by `num_frames_per_block=8`, error swallowed by fail-open). - The post-request residency hint (`get_can_stay_resident_components`) now shares the promotion's candidate collection and H2D ranking — it previously read the ≈0 `memory_usages`, making the recommendation meaningless, and could recommend FSDP/custom-strategy components. - Logs narrate the adjustment: decision summary (`target/measured/estimated_peak/reserve/budget/promoted`), per-component `mode -> resident` with the **equivalent `--component-residency` flags** users can pin, and the kill switch. ``` Server warmup complete; adjusting component residency for the default workload (--performance-mode auto). Auto residency: target=1024x1024x1f steps=9, measured=[1024x1024x1f=17.4GiB], estimated_peak=17.4 GiB, reserve=13.3 GiB, budget=133.5 GiB, promoted=[text_encoder(layerwise-offload, 6.8 GiB)] Auto residency: adjusted text_encoder: layerwise-offload -> resident. Equivalent server args: --component-residency text_encoder=resident. ... ``` The optimization target is the model-default workload (default resolution/frames, batch 1). Larger or batched workloads should pin residency explicitly; the reserve bounds the blast radius. Static model deployment configs remain as the fallback when calibration is skipped. No numerics change for non-promoted paths; promoted components run identical code at a different placement. ## Test - `test/unit/test_auto_residency.py`: estimation (same-shape, single-point, two-point fit, negative-slope fallback, covering measurement), plan (skip propagation, reserve, cumulative fit, ranking), multi-rank worst-casing, promotion/rollback on stub modules, eligibility gates, LongLive2 frame alignment, applied-changes log, hint/promotion ranking consistency. - H200, Z-Image-Turbo serve: text encoder (layerwise, 6.8 GiB) promoted; warmup 9.15 s, decision <1 s, post-promotion re-warm 0.15 s; `/health` stays 503 until after promotion. - 2×H100, Wan2.1-T2V-14B: VAE promoted; text encoder correctly refused (estimated 65.6 GiB + 6.5 GiB TE > 70.2 GiB budget). Single-GPU 14B correctly refuses all promotions (72.6 vs 72.8 GiB). - Steady-state E2E improved on promoted image cases; no OOM observed in any validated case, including the refusal boundaries. ## Post-submission hardening (adversarial review pass) A 10-angle review over the diff surfaced and fixed, in `harden auto residency against review findings`: - **Measurement**: per-forward `empty_cache` + peak reset (allocator-pool carryover flattened the calibration slope → under-estimate → post-ready OOM); calibration forward moved after the main warmup so one-time allocations can only steepen the slope (safe direction); only `is_warmup` requests are measured (compile prewarm ran a different layout); failed warmups are recorded on every exit path; **`--enable-torch-compile` is excluded** — its warmup deliberately runs a stripped memory layout (layerwise DiT + evicted aux components) whose peaks are not serving peaks; unknown default workloads skip instead of trusting the capped peak. - **Distributed/rollback**: everything before the first all-gather is fenced into a skip report (a raise there parked peer ranks in the collective); error gathers filter on `is not None` with never-empty error strings; a failed in-apply rollback now surfaces as `rollback_failed` (aborts startup) instead of masquerading as rolled back; `disable_offload` re-arms hooks when `load_all_layers` fails; mechanism/mode mismatches from the `offload_during_compile` window are excluded and guarded; `_required_resident_components` tracks an owner feature so rollback cannot release loader hard-requirements. - **Startup contract**: apply-RPC failures honor the warmup fail-open contract; the post-rollback restore warmup keeps `--warmup-resolutions`' fail-closed contract; the calibration request shares `auto_residency_skip_reason` (the kill switch and excluded configs no longer pay for a measurement they never consume); warmup records are consumed exactly once (one-shot handler); re-warm passes no longer double-advance the warmup progress bar. - The warmup/target frame contract (cap → `adjust_num_frames` → `num_gpus` latent alignment) is now one shared helper extracted from `SamplingParams._adjust_visual_fields`, used by real requests, warmup requests, and the workload resolver. Known accepted conservatisms (documented in code): the budget check double-counts bytes of a component already partially on GPU at the measured peak (safe direction), and the reserve stays at `max(10 %, 4 GiB)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32195701226](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195701226)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195700967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195700967)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: VLM: feed the packed qkv projection output to vision backends uncopied
signals.text: ## Motivation In `VisionAttention.forward`, the `use_qkv_parallel` branch slices `qkv_proj`'s output into q/k/v and then copies all three dense: ```python qkv, _ = self.qkv_proj(x) q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1) q = q.reshape(bsz * s, head, -1) # a view, still strided ... q = q.contiguous(); k = k.contiguous(); v = v.contiguous() # three full copies ``` `qkv_proj` writes q, k and v interleaved into one buffer, so those slices are views whose only non-unit stride is over tokens — the last dimension stays contiguous. Backends that read q/k/v through explicit per-dim strides accept them as they are, so the copies move the whole projection output twice through HBM per layer for nothing. On a PaddleOCR-VL page (10764 patches, 16 heads, head_dim 72, bf16) that is 3.74 GiB of HBM traffic per request across 27 layers. ## Modifications - Add `STRIDED_QKV_BACKENDS` next to `QKV_BACKEND_IMPL`, listing the backends that read q/k/v through explicit strides: `fa3`, `fa4`, `triton_attn`, `amx_attn`. `flashinfer_cudnn` stays out because its packed element indptrs assume a dense layout; `sdpa`, `ascend_attn`, `aiter_attn` and `xpu_attn` stay out because their kernels were not verified against a non-unit token stride. - Compute `self.pass_strided_qkv` in `__init__` and skip the three `.contiguous()` calls when it holds. This replaces the previous `_is_cpu and _is_cpu_amx_available` predicate; `amx_attn` is in the set, so the CPU-AMX default path is unchanged. - Two consumers sit between the projection and the backend and need a dense layout, so they keep the copies: - `qk_normalization` (internvl) — `apply_qk_norm` normalizes q/k **in place** through `q.view(N, -1, embed)`. That view succeeds on the strided tensor, and the kernel then writes per its dense stride assumption, corrupting the k/v regions of the shared buffer. - `customized_position_embedding_applier` — model-supplied callables reshape q/k however they like (e.g. `mllama4` views to 4D). - `qk_normalization_by_head_size` (GLM-OCR) does **not** need to opt out: its `reshape(-1, head_size)` materialises a dense copy of q/k on its own. - No GQA special case is needed. `qkv.view(tokens, 3, head, head_dim)[:, i]` is byte-identical to what `split` + `reshape` already produce, and a GQA tower's k/v slices have the same stride shape, so nothing has to change for `num_kv_heads != num_heads`. New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_vision_strided_qkv.py` covers the gating matrix (8 backends plus the three qk-norm / applier variants), asserts the tensors reaching the backend are non-contiguous views into a single storage carrying byte-identical values to the dense path (MHA and GQA), and asserts the layer output is bit-identical between the two paths. ## Accuracy Tests All on one H200, bf16, `fa3`. - `flash_attn_varlen_func` and the Triton `context_attention_fwd` produce **bit-identical** output from strided views vs dense copies across 8 shapes: PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP (10764 patches, 1 and 8 sequences), Qwen2.5-VL ViT (8192 / head_dim 80), Qwen3-VL ViT (6400 / head_dim 128), InternViT-like (25 heads / head_dim 64), a GQA tower (16 q heads / 4 kv heads), a non-multiple token count (1023), and fp16. - The full PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP encoder (27 layers, 12000 patches) output is **bit-identical** between the two paths. - Greedy output over 3 prompts on the same image is **byte-identical** before and after, for **PaddleOCR-VL**, **Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct** and **Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct**. - The 14 new unit tests pass. Not covered: no released vision tower is GQA (`mimo_vl` is the only call site that can pass `num_kv_heads`, and only when its vision config sets `num_key_value_heads`), so GQA is covered at the unit-test and kernel level only. The `qk_normalization` opt-out is covered by the unit test — InternVL2_5-2B has `qk_normalization: false`, so it is not an end-to-end exercise of that branch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP encoder, 27 layers, 12000 patches, bf16, H200, `fa3`, in-process CUDA-event timing, the two modes interleaved over 7 rounds each: | | dense copies | strided views | delta | |---|---|---|---| | encoder forward | 66.42 ms | 64.88 ms | **−1.54 ms (−2.3%)** | | one `VisionAttention.forward` (10764 patches) | 1565.2 us | 1455.3 us | −109.9 us (−7.0%) | | peak allocated, one layer | 306.1 MiB | 234.1 MiB | −72 MiB | Sample ranges do not overlap (strided 64.78–65.58 ms, dense 66.34–66.66 ms). The three `.contiguous()` calls alone measure 96.8 us per layer at that shape, i.e. 2.6 ms of pure copy time per request over 27 layers. **No end-to-end win is claimed yet.** Single-page latency (197.9–200.9 ms vs 197.9–199.0 ms) and saturated page throughput (9.62/9.90/9.65 vs 10.24/9.91/9.76 pages/s over 3 rounds of 96 pages at concurrency 8) both came out inside the noise band. Sampling GPU utilisation during the throughput run showed a mean of **17.4%** — that harness was CPU-bound on image preprocessing, so it cannot resolve a GPU-side saving of this size either way. Marking this a draft until a GPU-bound page-throughput benchmark either confirms or rules out the end-to-end effect; the encoder-level number above is the measured result. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32147235077](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32147235077)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32147674741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32147674741)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU][CI] key persistent JIT kernel cache by image content ID
signals.text: ## Summary Nightly image rebuilds swap the runtime libs that cached JIT `.so` files link against (e.g. `libsycl.so.8` -> `libsycl.so.9`). Triton keys its cache on source hash only, so the previous gpu-mask-only cache path dlopens stale `.so`s from the prior image and every XPU CI job dies with `OSError: libsycl.so.N: cannot open shared object file`. - Include the resolved `docker image inspect` ID in the cache path so a new image gets a fresh cache dir. - Prune sibling caches for the same GPU but a different image ID via a rootful busybox helper (files are root-owned by the CI container, same pattern as the workspace-ownership reset). - Explicit `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR` overrides are still honored verbatim; if `docker image inspect` fails we fall back to the legacy unversioned path with a warning. - Over-cap reset switched from a runner-level `rm -rf` to the same busybox helper for the same root-owned reason. ## Test plan - [ ] XPU CI passes on an image with a torch/SYCL bump (verify no `libsycl.so.*: cannot open shared object` failures). - [ ] Sibling `kernel-cache-gpu*-<oldid>` dirs are pruned on first run after an image rebuild. - [ ] `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/foo` override still lands at `/tmp/foo` with no pruning. - [ ] Over-cap path (>`XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_MAX_MB`) resets cleanly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32172874266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32172874266)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32208126441](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208126441)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Prevent hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk decode over-admission
signals.text: ## Motivation Hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk scheduling admits new prefill tokens while an existing decode batch is executed in the same forward pass. The mixed-chunk path does not perform the regular decode memory check before admission. However, the existing decode batch still requires SWA KV pages immediately after admission. Since `PrefillAdder` did not reserve this SWA demand, prefill admission could consume pages required by decode. This can cause decode allocation failure under SWA memory pressure. ## Root Cause For a running batch, `new_tokens_required_next_decode()` returns the page-aligned token demand for the next decode step. The mixed-chunk admission path previously ignored this demand and initialized the SWA reservation offset to zero. The composite SWA allocator had a second issue: full-attention pages were allocated before SWA pages. If the SWA allocation failed, the full allocator had already consumed pages, leaving a partial allocation state. ## Fix Reserve the current decode batch's SWA demand during mixed-chunk admission: ```python mixed_decode_swa_tokens = ( running_batch.new_tokens_required_next_decode() if self.is_mixed_chunk and self.tree_cache.supports_swa() else 0 ) ``` Pass this value to `PrefillAdder` as the initial SWA reservation. Make hybrid SWA decode allocation preflight both underlying allocators before performing either allocation: ```python num_new_pages = get_num_new_pages( seq_lens=seq_lens_cpu, page_size=self.page_size, decode=True, ) if not self.new_pages_available(num_new_pages, num_new_pages): return None ``` This prevents full-KV pages from being consumed when the corresponding SWA allocation cannot succeed. ## Validation - Existing scheduler and allocator tests pass: `45 passed, 27 subtests passed`. - On A100, a decode batch requiring 8 new pages with only 4 SWA pages available: - before the fix, full-KV allocation consumed all 8 pages before SWA failed; - after the fix, allocation returned `None` without changing either pool. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32148300784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148300784)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32148300620](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148300620)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
