signals.title: [diffusion] Per-request lossy accelerations: Cache-DiT, CFG gating, attention backend override
signals.text: ## Motivation Lossy accelerations should be **per-request** switches, not process-wide env vars / server args: one deployment should be able to mix accelerated and lossless requests. SGLang-Diffusion already follows this for TeaCache (`enable_teacache`), Spectrum, progressive resolution, and `quality="high"` — but Cache-DiT was ~20 process-wide `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_*` env vars, CFG gating was a process-wide `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CFG_GATE_STEP` float, and approximate attention (SageAttention) was only selectable server-wide. Design rule going forward: anything whose state is request-scoped, or process-level but safely switchable at a batch boundary, belongs in `SamplingParams` (participating in the dynamic-batch signature). Env vars remain as server-wide defaults for unset requests, and are planned to be deprecated/removed later. ## Modifications **1. Cache-DiT (`enable_cache_dit` / `cache_dit_params`)** - `SamplingParams.enable_cache_dit: bool | None` — `None` follows the `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED` server default; `True`/`False` opt this request in/out (explicit `False` is a kill switch, winning even over MiniMax-H3 `quality="high"`). CLI `--enable-cache-dit true|false`; OpenAI image/video APIs accept both fields via `extra_body`. - `SamplingParams.cache_dit_params: dict | None` — per-request DBCache/SCM knob overrides on top of the env defaults, with a nested `secondary` dict for dual-DiT models (unset secondary keys inherit the request primary, then `SECONDARY_*` env). Unknown keys fail the request (`resolve_cache_dit_request_overrides`). - `DenoisingStage` generalizes MiniMax-H3's quality-transition logic: at each batch boundary it unmounts/remounts hooks when a request opts out or changes knobs, and keeps the cheap `refresh_context` path when settings are unchanged. - MiniMax-H3 generic mode honors the request switch; LTX-2's TI2V suppression now reports "not requested" so hooks mounted by a prior text-only request actually unmount (previously they silently stayed active during image-conditioned requests — the stale-activation hazard its comment warns about). Progressive-resolution SCM preset honors the per-request override. **2. CFG gating (`cfg_gate_step`)** - `SamplingParams.cfg_gate_step: float | None` — fraction of steps after which the cached cond−uncond residual is reused instead of running the unconditional branch. `None` follows the `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CFG_GATE_STEP` server default; `1.0` disables for this request. Its state was already rebuilt per denoising loop, so no transition logic is needed. CLI `--cfg-gate-step`; APIs via `extra_body`. **3. Attention backend override (`attention_backend_override`)** - One server can serve exact and approximate attention side by side: requests switch the DiT denoise attention backend among the exact/drop-in dense kernels (`fa`, `torch_sdpa`, `sage_attn`, `sage_attn_3`). CLI `--attention-backend-override`; APIs via `extra_body`. - The attention layers (`UlyssesAttention` / `LocalAttention` / `USPAttention`) keep their impl ctor kwargs and a per-backend impl cache; switching is two-phase (prepare every layer's impl first — may raise, mutates nothing — then flip all), so a rejected request leaves the transformers untouched. Non-default impls are built lazily: dual residency costs a few plain Python objects per layer, no GPU memory (sage/fa step metadata is empty/None). - **Fail-fast**: incompatible server settings reject the request with a server log instead of silently falling back — breakable CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` bake the kernel into a captured/traced graph; sparse server backends can't be mixed with per-request dense switching; ring parallelism requires a ring-capable target; unknown/unsupported/unavailable targets are refused (including silent selector fallbacks). All three fields participate in the dynamic-batch signature, so requests with different settings never share a batch and every transition happens at a batch boundary. No new env vars or server args are added. ## Test - New `test/unit/test_cache_dit_per_request.py`: request-param validation, overrides-key change detection, mount→refresh→unmount→remount transitions, explicit-disable-wins-over-env, secondary inheritance, warmup gating. - New `test/unit/test_attention_backend_override.py`: switch/restore/fast-path orchestration, all fail-fast rejections (BCG, compile, sparse, ring, unknown/non-switchable names, no layers), two-phase atomicity, layer prepare/apply including silent-fallback refusal. - Extended `test_cfg_gating.py`: request fraction overrides env default, request `1.0` disables an env-enabled gate, invalid request fraction rejected. - Updated fakes in `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py` / `test_minimax_h3_admission.py` for the new SamplingParams fields. - Docs: `cache_dit.mdx` rewritten around per-request usage; `attention_backends.mdx` gains a per-request override section; perf-tuning skill table updated. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32160110319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32160110319)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32160109959](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32160109959)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][bugfix] Add moe_ep_size/moe_tp_size to the allreduce-fusion gate test stub
signals.text: ## Motivation `TestAiterAllreduceFusionGate` in `test/registered/ops/test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py` has been erroring on every AMD run since 2026-08-12. The hybrid EP+TP guard added in #30700 (commit `c7c03ec53`, 2026-08-11) reads two new fields at the very top of `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`: ```python parallel = get_parallel() if parallel.moe_ep_size > 1 and parallel.moe_tp_size > 1: return False ``` The AMD gate test stubs `get_parallel()` with a `SimpleNamespace` that only carries `tp_size`, so every one of the 7 gate cases now raises: ``` AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'moe_ep_size' ``` Because the guard sits before every other branch, all 7 cases fail; CI's failfast only surfaces the first one (`test_dense_tp_fuses`). This is a test-stub gap only. The aiter fused all-reduce + RMSNorm kernel itself is fine: the three GPU subtests (`test_fused_ar_rms_benchmark`, `test_fused_ar_rms_multi_hidden_dim`, `test_fused_ar_rms_residual_accuracy`) pass. Scheduled ROCm 7.2 runs on `main`, shard 3 — the guard landed at 2026-08-11T23:46Z: | run date | shard 3 | | --- | --- | | 08-09, 08-10, 08-11 17:46 | success | | 08-12 12:21 onward (every run) | failure | ## Modifications Add `moe_ep_size=1` and `moe_tp_size=1` to the `get_parallel()` stub. Both being 1 means no MoE EP and no MoE TP, so the hybrid EP+TP guard stays inactive and the aiter branch is what decides — which is what all 7 existing cases are written to exercise. No existing assertion changes meaning. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — test-only change, no kernel or model forward code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149134311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149134025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134025)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signals.text: ## Problem `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` partition 0 (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has been failing deterministically on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. The empty DP-attention batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` right after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`: ```python if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: ``` But when the fused AR+quant path is active (`--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` + `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on a block-FP8 Qwen3.5), `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn()` returns `hidden_states` as a **tuple** produced by `forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_group()` — `(fp8, scale)` for the attention layer (`keep_bf16=False`) and `(bf16, fp8, scale)` for the GatedDeltaNet layer (`keep_bf16=True`). A tuple has no `.shape`, so the guard raises and the server dies during decode CUDA-graph capture: ``` File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' [2026-08-18 00:27:54] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed. ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which surfaces to the test as the unhelpful `Server process exited with code -9`. This only affects the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant (GPUs 0-3). The `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant (GPUs 4-7) stays on the tensor path and is unaffected. Only `qwen3_5.py` carries this guard, which is why no other suite regressed. Failing job: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420 ## Fix Take the row count in a tuple-aware way, preserving the guard's original intent. This is behavior-preserving for the fused path: `prepare_attn()` short-circuits on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only ever appear when the row count is already `> 0`. The new guard is therefore always `True` on the tuple path (exactly the pre-#34474 behavior), while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch protection. ## Verification Reproduced and verified end-to-end on an 8x MI350X (gfx950) node, following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py --suite stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x --auto-partition-id 0 --auto-partition-size 3`. **Before** (at `91144797c`, the failing scheduled-run SHA): `AttributeError` at `qwen3_5.py:806`, byte-for-byte the same signature as the CI log. **After:** | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | ``` Ran 1 test in 176.302s OK Test Summary: 1/1 passed ``` cc @Lzy17 Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149183042](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149183042)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149298089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149298089)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [VLM] Route every multimodal processor through the worker pool's call site
signals.text: ## Motivation `process_and_combine_mm_data` is the function the multimodal processor worker pool actually runs (`MultimodalProcessorExecutor.run(self.process_and_combine_mm_data, ...)`). **33 of the 37 call sites called it directly**, so those models can never use the pool: with `--mm-processor-worker-num > 1` they build the thread pool and its `deepcopy`'d processor clones at startup and then route every request straight past them. The failure is silent — the model just serves at one-worker speed. That is why PaddleOCR-VL preprocessed pages single-threaded from the day it was added: opting it in (#35318) moved 32-way concurrent throughput from 6.7 to 10.9 req/s on an H200, purely by letting an 87 ms/page preprocess overlap. Only `qwen_vl`, `kimi_k25`, `kimi_k3` and `muse_glimmer` were on the right call site. ## Modifications Mechanically rewrite the 33 sync call sites to `await self.process_and_combine_mm_data_async(...)`, and add a test that pins the invariant. **This is an identity transform, not a behavior change:** - `process_and_combine_mm_data_async` delegates straight to the sync function when `self.mm_processor_executor is None`, which is the case for every model that has not opted into concurrency. - Awaiting a coroutine that never itself suspends does not yield to the event loop, so request interleaving is bit-for-bit unchanged. Only `await loop.run_in_executor(...)` — reached solely when an executor exists — introduces a suspension point. So nothing about scheduling moves until a model sets `supports_mm_processor_concurrency`. What this PR buys is that opting a model in becomes a three-line change instead of a call-site migration plus an audit. ## Verification The migration was generated and checked by AST, not by hand: - 33 sync call sites before, **0** after; 37 async call sites after. - Every call site sits inside an `async def`, before and after — so each edit is exactly `await` + `_async`. - Each of the 33 changed lines differs from its original **only** by that rename (0 deviations, checked mechanically against the diff). - Every touched file compiles; `isort` / `black` / `ruff` clean. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py` re-runs the same scan as a CPU test, so a processor added later cannot quietly opt out of the pool again. It reports 37 call sites on this branch and would have reported 33 offenders before it. ## Notes for reviewers Turning concurrency *on* for a given model is deliberately **not** part of this PR. That decision is per-model and needs measurement, for two reasons: - The executor is a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, so a model only benefits if its preprocessing releases the GIL (PIL / numpy / torch C code does; pure-Python preprocessing would not). - More workers spread request arrivals, which fragments GPU prefill batches — the tradeoff `qwen_vl` documents when it picks 2 workers, and which showed up in measurement as `--mm-processor-worker-num 8` being slower than 4 on PaddleOCR-VL. `muse_glimmer` is already on the async call site but has no capability flag, so it is the one existing model that could opt in for free once measured. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test (`test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py`) - [x] Verify the change is an identity transform rather than benchmarking it (there is nothing to benchmark: behavior is unchanged until a model opts in) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32150110753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32150110753)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32150110283](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32150110283)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Sync FlashInfer autotune tactic choice across TP ranks
signals.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer's autotuner times every candidate tactic on the rank's own GPU and keeps whichever came out fastest. That works fine on one GPU. With TP > 1 each rank runs that search on its own, and the ranks don't come out the same. Measured on `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300 (sm103), flashinfer 0.6.17. The per-rank tactic caches sglang already writes (`rank_tp{0..3}_pp0_dp0.json`) show it directly: | | Tuned shape buckets | Diverging across ranks | |---|---|---| | Before | 20 | **20 / 20** | | After | 20 | **0 / 20** | Every tuned `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` shape landed on a different tactic somewhere, and not just as a tie-break — at m=16 rank 0 took a tile-8 tactic while ranks 1–3 took tile-16. Same shape, different tile size. Dumping the autotuner's per-tactic timings per rank explains it. Each rank recorded 12,188 measurements, the same count on all four, so the tuning loop is already walking in step; what differs is the numbers it walks away with: | m | candidates | same-tactic spread across ranks | gap best → runner-up | tactics within noise of best | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 920 | 3.5% | 2.14% | 5 | | 8 | 920 | 2.9% | 0.43% | 25 | | 16 | 920 | 1.2% | 0.08% | 28 | | 256 | 920 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 10 | | 4096 | 50 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 6 | The last two columns are the whole story. In all 20 buckets the gap between the winner and the runner-up is smaller than the noise on a single tactic's own measurement, and anywhere from 2 to 28 candidates sit inside that noise. `argmin` over a field like that is a coin flip, which is why divergence is 20/20 rather than occasional, and why it's worst at small `m` where the kernel runs ~20 µs and jitter dominates. It costs something, too. Scored against the consensus best — the tactic that wins on the mean of all four ranks' timings — the worst rank was +2.45% off at m=1, and +0.63% off averaged across buckets. Once the timings are shared, every rank lands on the consensus best and that gap closes to zero. ## Modifications - `_autotune_tactic_sync_group` hands FlashInfer the TP group's `cpu_group` through `set_autotune_process_group`. FlashInfer then all-reduces each tactic's measured time, so every rank minimizes over the same numbers instead of its own. TP is the right scope, since those ranks run the same dummy forward; a lone rank has nobody to agree with and tunes without a group. - `_autotune_process_group` wraps the `autotune()` block and puts the previous group back on the way out, so a nested tuning pass can't leave a stale one behind. - Sharing the timings only helps if the ranks start from the same cache, because a cache hit skips a profile and knocks them out of step. `_drop_diverged_autotune_cache` all-gathers a digest of what each rank would actually load — the cache file plus the environment stamp `load_configs` checks it against, since a stamp mismatch makes FlashInfer discard the file wholesale — and deletes the caches when those digests disagree. - The extend pass used to swallow a rank-local OOM and carry on. Tuning is collective now, so carrying on would strand the other ranks inside the reduce; the OOM is re-raised whenever a sync group is active. - `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py` (CPU suite) covers the digest's load-decision semantics, plus the cache gate itself over a real 2-rank gloo group and real files: matching caches survive, diverged ones are dropped on every rank, and so are caches that differ only in their metadata stamp. ## Accuracy Tests GPQA diamond on gpt-oss-120b TP=4, reasoning effort low, temperature 1.0. Each run grades 1,584 samples — 198 questions, eight shuffles each — and the whole run is repeated: | | Runs | Mean | |---|---|---| | Before | 60.86 / 63.64 / 61.93 / 61.87 | **62.1** | | After | 63.26 / 62.25 / 63.19 | **62.9** | The sides overlap: 2.8 points of spread before, 1.0 after, 0.8 points between the means. Tactic selection picks among kernels FlashInfer treats as interchangeable for a given shape, and the scores agree. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300, clean autotune cache for each configuration. "Before" is the same build without the cross-rank reduction. Single stream, `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 --warmup-requests 8 --flush-cache`, three repetitions: | | Output tok/s | Mean E2E (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | Before | 508.74 / 509.99 / 509.95 → **509.56 ± 0.72** | 2008.1 | 1.94–1.95 | | After | 510.60 / 510.61 / 510.83 → **510.68 ± 0.13** | 2003.7 | 1.94 | At concurrency 32 (1k in / 512 out, 128 prompts) total throughput went 22,956 → 23,130 tok/s. Both deltas — +0.22% and +0.8% — are small enough that the honest claim is no regression rather than a speedup, though they point the same way the tactic-cost numbers above predict. The clearer effect is stability: run-to-run spread tightened about 5x (±0.13 vs ±0.72 tok/s), which is what you'd expect once all four ranks are running the same kernel. Tuning wall-clock goes 79 s → 106 s from the extra per-tactic reduction. That's paid once — the result is cached, and a warm restart reuses it with no retune and no cache drop. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — nothing user-facing to document. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32151944979](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151944979)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32151944469](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151944469)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Step-reuse execution contract for iterative denoising models
signals.text: ## Summary Implements the step-reuse execution contract proposed in #35332 as a real, opt-in skip-forward strategy usable today -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/cache/step_reuse.py`): - `StepReusePolicy` -- declares `observation_point`, `history_size`, `max_skip_steps`, forced real-forward points (`first_one`, `first_two`, `terminal`), and the `state_scope` axes a policy is keyed by. - `StepReuseState` -- per-scope lifecycle: last real prediction, bounded similarity history, remaining skip budget, and metrics. - `StepSideEffectContract` -- lets a model declare that the terminal step must always run a real forward (e.g. to commit a persistent KV/session write). - `StepReuseController` -- multiplexes independent `StepReuseState` lifecycles across arbitrary `scope_key` tuples (request / modality / CFG branch / ...), enforces the skip budget and forced points, and never feeds a *reused* prediction back into the similarity history. **Real integration** (this is now wired into the actual serving path, not just tested in isolation): - `SamplingParams.enable_step_reuse` (+ `StepReuseParams`), mutually exclusive with `enable_teacache`/`enable_spectrum`. - Threaded through the OpenAI-compatible API surface: `protocol.py`'s Image/Video request schemas, `image_api.py`, `video_api.py` (both JSON and multipart form paths) -- mirrors every existing `enable_teacache` call site. - `StepReuseMixin` mixed into `CachableDiT` alongside `SpectrumMixin`/`TeaCacheMixin`, so any DiT model can opt in. - **`WanTransformer3DModel.forward()`** (`wanvideo.py`) actually calls it: a real, working alternative to the existing TeaCache call sites (should-skip check, block loop, cache/retrieve), gated by `enable_step_reuse`. A model-tuned threshold (like TeaCache's per-model `teacache_thresh` coefficients) would need real benchmarking against actual model output that isn't possible without GPU hardware and model weights, so `step_reuse_params` stays a single generic default on the base `SamplingParams` rather than a fabricated per-model number -- matching `teacache_params`' own convention (`None` at the base class, populated per model in `configs/sample/wan.py`). Per-model calibration is legitimate, separable follow-up work; it doesn't block the mechanism itself from being real and correct. ## Test plan - `test_step_reuse.py` -- 19 tests on the pure `StepReuseController`/`StepReusePolicy` contract (skip windows, forced points including the new `first_one`, side-effect contract, scope isolation, reset, metrics, validation). - `test_step_reuse_mixin.py` -- **5 new integration tests** wiring `StepReuseMixin` exactly the way `WanTransformer3DModel` does: real torch tensors, the real `set_forward_context` context manager, a toy DiT-like module. Covers reset-on-new-request, forced first/terminal steps, and CFG positive/negative branch isolation. - This test caught a real bug during development: copying `TeaCacheMixin`'s reset guard verbatim (`current_timestep == 0 and not self.is_cfg_negative`) is only correct if the negative CFG branch is always dispatched first at each timestep. Calling positive before negative silently double-reset and dropped state. Fixed with an order-independent "reset armed" flag instead of relying on that branch-order assumption. All 24 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved device. Full production imports (the real `sglang.multimodal_gen.*` module tree) require this project's CUDA-only extras (`flashinfer`, `cuda-python`, etc.) that cannot install on this machine, so `test_step_reuse_mixin.py` was additionally verified against an isolated sandbox containing only the real source files it imports before being placed in the real test tree, where CI's full dependency stack runs it directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35332. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166805209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166805209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166804905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166804905)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: initialize reasoning parser from prefilled think token
signals.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35148. Qwen3.8's chat template injects the opening `<think>` token into the generation prefill when thinking is enabled. The generated output therefore starts directly with reasoning text and contains only the closing `</think>` token. The gateway's Rust `qwen3` parser starts outside reasoning mode and previously waited for an opening `<think>` token in the generated output. Because that token was already consumed as part of the prompt, the gateway returned the reasoning text in `content` and left `reasoning_content` empty. ## Modifications - Detect whether the rendered generation prompt ends with a prefilled `<think>` token. Inspecting the rendered prompt also respects request-level chat template kwargs, including explicitly disabling thinking. - Propagate the prefill reasoning state through regular and PD-disaggregated chat response processing. - Initialize fresh reasoning parser instances from that state in both streaming and non-streaming paths. - Use an isolated parser for each non-streaming choice instead of sharing a stateful pooled parser. - Add parser-level and response-processing regression tests for Qwen3 output that begins with reasoning text and contains `</think>` without a generated `<think>` token. ## Upstream Compatibility / Maintainer Input The latest upstream SMG implementation already supports this case explicitly: newer `reasoning-parser` versions expose parser state methods such as `mark_reasoning_started()` and `mark_think_start_stripped()`, while newer `llm-tokenizer` versions expose whether a chat template injects thinking into the prefill. This repository currently pins `reasoning-parser = 1.0.0` and `llm-tokenizer = 1.3.2`, which do not provide those APIs. This PR intentionally does not upgrade either dependency because doing so would introduce a much larger dependency and integration change for a narrowly scoped bug fix. Instead, it detects the state from the rendered prompt and initializes the existing parser through its incremental parsing interface, which is equivalent for the `<think>` format used here. Maintainers: would you prefer to keep this targeted compatibility fix, or update the gateway to newer upstream parser/tokenizer versions and use their explicit prefill-thinking APIs instead? I am happy to adjust the implementation based on the preferred dependency-upgrade strategy. ## Accuracy Tests Added four CPU-only Rust regression tests covering: - rendered-prefill detection, including prompts that end with `<think>`, prompts where the reasoning block is already closed, and historical reasoning that must not affect the new response; - complete non-streaming Qwen3 parsing when generated output contains reasoning text and `</think>` but no generated `<think>`; - incremental streaming Qwen3 parsing for the same output format; and - the non-streaming response-processing path using an in-memory tokenizer and a synthetic gRPC `GenerateComplete`, asserting that reasoning is returned in `reasoning_content` and the final answer is returned in `content`. Executed: ```bash cd sgl-model-gateway cargo test --lib --quiet cargo test --lib prefill cargo fmt --all -- --check ``` The full library test suite reported 396 passed and 0 failed. The filtered `prefill` run reported 13 passed and 0 failed, including all four new regression tests. These tests do not load a real tokenizer or model and do not download model weights. The parser-level tests use fixed strings, while the response-processing test uses an in-memory tokenizer and a synthetic gRPC response. Cargo may download Rust crate dependencies on a clean development environment. A Qwen3.8-27B model end-to-end test was not run because the change is confined to gateway response parsing and is directly covered by deterministic unit tests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The change adds one suffix check to the rendered prompt and initializes per-response parser state; it does not modify model execution or the token generation path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation update is not required because there is no user-facing API change. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable to this response-parsing fix. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32153080147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32153080147)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32153079822](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32153079822)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: Fix fused DeepSeek top-k capability fallback
signals.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently selects FlashInfer's `fused_topk_deepseek` based on shape constraints without checking whether the active GPU architecture is supported by that kernel. On A10G (SM86), FlashInfer raises `BackendSupportedError` during DeepSeek grouped top-k routing instead of allowing SGLang to use its existing fallback. This was observed in the Dynamo nightly SGLang data-parallel test: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/32114902544/job/95672470424 ## Modifications - Read FlashInfer's `is_compute_capability_supported` metadata before selecting `fused_topk_deepseek`. - Preserve compatibility with FlashInfer versions that do not expose capability metadata. - Add focused coverage for unsupported SM86 and supported SM89/SM90 devices. ## Accuracy Tests The numerical implementation is unchanged. Unsupported devices now use the existing SGLang fallback instead of entering a kernel that raises before producing output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. Supported devices retain the fused path; the added check is one device-capability lookup during top-k dispatch. ## Validation - `python3 -m compileall -q python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_topk_deepseek.py` - `uvx ruff check test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_fused_topk_deepseek.py` - GPU pytest not run locally because the available environment does not include PyTorch/CUDA. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project guidance for the changed test. - [x] Add unit tests for the capability-selection behavior. - [x] No documentation update is needed for this internal dispatch fix. - [x] Accuracy and performance impact are described above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32154747529](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32154747529)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32154747252](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32154747252)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [VLM] Default to two multimodal preprocessing workers
signals.text: Stacked on #35342 (which routes every processor through the worker pool's call site). Review that one first; this PR is the one line that actually turns the pool on. ## Motivation Preprocessing an image costs real CPU time on the tokenizer's event loop, so with a single worker a model's request throughput is capped at `1 / preprocess_time` no matter how much GPU is idle. That cap is why PaddleOCR-VL saturated at 6.7 req/s on an H200 with GPU headroom to spare — and only four processors in tree had opted out of it. ## The benefit generalizes, because the mechanism does Image preprocessing is numpy / torch / PIL underneath, so it releases the GIL. Wall-clock speedup of 4 threads over 1 on the same work, 1080p input, `torch.set_num_threads(1)` so intraop parallelism cannot be mistaken for thread scaling: | image processor | 1 thread | 4 threads | speedup | `deepcopy` | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2VL (fast / slow) | 24.3 / 24.1 ms | 7.1 / 7.0 ms | 3.41x / 3.45x | ok | | Idefics3 | 46.1 ms | 12.7 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Pixtral | 19.0 ms | 5.2 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Llama4 | 27.0 ms | 7.7 ms | 3.52x | ok | | GLM4V | 31.8 ms | 9.0 ms | 3.51x | ok | | PaddleOCR-VL | 28.4 ms | 8.7 ms | 3.27x | ok | | CLIP | 9.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.28x | ok | | Gemma3 | 5.7 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.94x | ok | | SigLIP | 5.5 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.69x | ok | | *pure-Python control* | *81.0 ms* | *80.5 ms* | *1.01x* | — | The control validates the probe. `copy.deepcopy` succeeded on all nine, and the executor already falls back to synchronous processing with a warning if cloning ever fails. ## Two workers, and not more Past two, spreading request arrivals fragments the GPU prefill batches faster than the extra overlap pays for itself — the tradeoff `qwen_vl`'s processor already documents. Swept at 32-way concurrency on an H200: | workload | 1 worker | 2 workers | 4 workers | |---|---|---|---| | PaddleOCR-VL 1080p pages, 128-token outputs | 6.72 | **9.55** | 8.92 req/s | | PaddleOCR-VL 360p pages, 512-token outputs | 22.38 | **25.20** | 25.06 req/s | | Qwen2.5-VL 360p images, 512-token outputs | 12.54 | **12.60** | 12.25 req/s | The middle row is the shape that was supposed to break this: light preprocessing, where overlap has little to win, and long outputs, where batch fragmentation has the most to cost. Two workers gained 13% there instead of regressing. Four workers is where the documented regression actually appears (bottom row, −2.3%). Greedy output is unaffected: two workers against one is byte-identical across five page geometries × two task prompts on PaddleOCR-VL. ## Limitation reviewers should weigh All of this is **Hopper**. The regression `qwen_vl` documents was observed on Blackwell, and no B200 was available to me (GB300 is arm64). A Blackwell check on the light-preprocessing / long-output shape would be worth having before this rides a release — that is the one measurement that could still overturn the default. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test pinning the default (`test_default_worker_count_stays_at_the_measured_optimum`), so raising it requires a fresh sweep - [x] Benchmark on real hardware, including the shape most likely to regress - [x] Verify greedy output is unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32207382432](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207382432)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207382289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207382289)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Diffusion] Candidate-trajectory execution contract (phase 1: types + validation)
signals.text: ## Summary Implements the candidate-trajectory execution contract proposed in #35331 as a real, opt-in path -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/pipelines_core/candidates.py`): - `CandidateTrajectorySpec` -- `count` / `reducer` / `return_candidates` / `seed_policy`, with eager validation: `count=1` must use `reducer="none"` (provably identical to the existing non-candidate path), `count>1` requires a real registered reducer. - `CandidateGroup` -- stable, sorted, unique `candidate_ids` per `request_id`. - A reducer registry (`"none"`, `"mean"`, plus `register_candidate_reducer()` for model-owned rules). - `derive_candidate_generators()` -- one `torch.Generator` per candidate, derived from `(base_seed, candidate_id)` via a splitmix64-style bit mixer. - `validate_candidate_admission()` / `reduce_candidates()` -- atomic group admission and partial-failure-safe reduction. **Real integration**: - `SamplingParams.candidate_spec`, validated against `num_outputs_per_prompt` -- the RFC's premise is that `num_outputs_per_prompt`'s existing outputs *become* the candidate axis, not a separate count, so `candidate_spec.count` must equal it. - **`InputValidationStage._generate_seeds`** (the real per-request seed/generator construction used by every model) now uses `derive_candidate_generators` instead of the existing naive `base_seed + i` scheme whenever `candidate_spec` is set. This is the RFC's core RNG-independence safety requirement, not a nicety -- plain addition can produce visibly correlated draws for nearby seeds. When `candidate_spec` is `None` (the default), behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The actual candidate-reduction *application* point (averaging N action outputs down to one served result) needs real per-model tensor-shape knowledge -- e.g. Cosmos3's `action_latents` layout -- that can't be added correctly without a real model and weights to validate against. That's left for the model-adapter phase the RFC's own rollout plan describes (step 2: "Add a Cosmos3 action adapter"); the RNG-derivation wiring above is what's provably safe to land now. ## Test plan - **30 tests** in `test_candidate_trajectory.py` (27 original + 3 new), covering: - RFC required-tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (count=1 identity, sequential/batched seed equivalence, reducer parity, stable candidate IDs across co-batched requests, no partial-aggregate on failure). - The exact multi-prompt aggregation pattern `_generate_seeds` now uses: prompt-major/candidate-minor flattening order, cross-prompt independence, single-prompt equivalence to bare `derive_candidate_generators`. - Requirements 5, 6, 8 (CFG-parallel candidate membership, TP/SP reconstruction before reduction, conditional video-branch skip) still need a real model/pipeline adapter and are out of scope until that phase. All 30 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend. `input_validation.py` itself has a heavy import surface (`torchvision`, which isn't installed on this machine, plus a deep `pipeline_configs`/`platforms`/`server_args` chain) that makes it impractical to instantiate `InputValidationStage` directly in a local sandbox, so the new branch's logic is validated at the level of the RNG derivation it calls into (already exhaustively tested) rather than via a live call through the stage class; CI's full dependency stack can exercise that path directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35331. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166068209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166067961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166067961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [mxfp8-kv] Skip writes to the reserved CUDA-graph padding slot
signals.text: ## Motivation Slot 0 of the KV pool is the reserved CUDA-graph padding sink: padded lanes write their dummy K/V there, and padded page-table entries read its page back. Padding lanes carry undefined activations (upstream model kernels legitimately leave rows past the real token count uninitialized), which the MXFP8 path quantizes into NaN fp8 payload and `0xFF` (e8m0 NaN) scale bytes. The bf16 write path already guards this: the `store_cache` jit kernel skips writes targeting `reserved_skip_index` (slot 0), so the reserved page keeps its zeros. The MXFP8 pool had no equivalent guard on any of its write paths — the direct fancy-index stores, `store_sf_interleaved` (scales), and the fused `quant_store_kv_mxfp8` kernel all wrote to slot 0. A poisoned slot 0 is then read back by attention for padded/masked lanes, where a NaN V defeats probability masking (`0 * NaN = NaN` in the PV accumulator) and poisons real outputs. We root-caused a production NaN crash in MXFP8-KV serving (galileo-class hybrid model, prefill CUDA graphs) to exactly this write-side poison; the bf16 configuration was immune only because it has the `store_cache` guard. ## Modifications Same skip-at-source design as the bf16 path, with the skip inside kernels that were already running (measured cost: run noise vs the unguarded baseline): - The direct path (precomputed scales) now routes the fp8 payload through the `store_cache` jit kernel — a byte-width-agnostic row copier (fp8 row = `head_num * head_dim` bytes) that already skips `reserved_skip_index = 0` — and fuses the K+V scatters into one launch. Asserts replace the previous fancy-index writes and capture-mode alt-stream branch: this pool is CUDA-only (`float8_e8m0fnu` + triton + FA4) and `head_dim % 32 == 0` makes rows always `store_cache`-compatible, so those paths were unreachable. - `_store_sf_interleaved_kernel` masks out `slots == 0` (one predicate). - `_mxfp8_quant_store_qkv_kernel` (fused quant-store path) returns early when `myloc == 0`. ## Test `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_mxfp8_kv_reserved_slot.py` (next to `test_store_cache.py`, which covers the bf16 guard; SM100+): every `set_kv_buffer` sub-path (direct, fused, capture-mode flag) leaves slot 0 at exactly zero payload/scale bytes under NaN padding-lane writes; page-0 neighbor slots (payload and interleaved per-slot scales) stay byte-identical across writes targeting the reserved slot; and `set_kv_buffer` captures and replays inside a `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`. Negative control (verified on the equivalent internal tree): with the fix reverted, all tests fail with "reserved slot K payload written"; with the fix, all pass. The asserts require slot 0 to equal its init value rather than merely be NaN-free, so finite-garbage writes fail too. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32156928171](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32156928171)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32156928085](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32156928085)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] ComfyUI: add a MiniMax-H3 node and a generic extra-fields passthrough
signals.text: ## Summary The ComfyUI plugin's executors cover flux / qwen_image / zimage — all image models — so there was no route to MiniMax-H3 from ComfyUI. H3 does not fit the executor route. It denoises a packed video+audio sequence in one pass and routes conditioning by task (`t2va` / `fl2va` / `ref2va`), while ComfyUI's KSampler drives a single latent tensor and has no audio branch. Rebuilding that inside ComfyUI would duplicate the visual/audio/reference conditioning stages the server already runs, so this wires H3 through the server route instead. Two changes: - **`generate_video` gains `extra_fields`.** The video request schema already accepts unknown fields, so the client only needed a way to reach a model's own request surface. `extra_fields` is merged last, so a model-specific field wins over a generic default of the same name. No further change to this client is needed for the next model that adds request fields. - **`SGLDiffusionGenerateH3`** builds H3's `task` / `conditions` / `target` shape from ComfyUI-native inputs. Keyframes carry a `frame_index`; references keep request order because the prompt addresses them positionally per modality; local paths become `file://` URIs while remote URLs pass through unchanged. Output dimensions are read from the response, because H3 aligns the canvas server-side and `short_edge` alone cannot reconstruct it. ## Test plan - [x] 9 new tests drive the real node through the real client and mock only HTTP, so a change on either side of the payload contract fails. They cover the three task shapes, keyframe frame-index mapping, modality ordering for prompt tags, remote-URL passthrough, the server-resolved canvas, the task/conditioning validation errors, and `extra_fields` precedence. - [x] Run on a plain checkout and on an H200 box: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/test/test_h3_request.py --import-mode=importlib` **Not covered:** an end-to-end run against a live H3 server. The tests pin the request shape against the documented contract and the shape used by the existing H3 CI case, but nothing here has generated a video through ComfyUI yet. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32158669747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32158669747)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32158669388](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32158669388)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [diffusion] make --vae-tiling honest, fix the decode OOM advice, gate NVFP4 on Blackwell
signals.text: ## Summary Three failures that all present as something other than what they are. Found while auditing consumer-GPU support. **`--vae-tiling` was a silent no-op on any VAE without `enable_tiling`.** The call sat under a bare `except Exception: pass`. MiniMax-H3's VAE is one of those, and it happens to tile anyway because `decoder_tiling` is set from its VAE config at construction — so the flag looked accepted while doing nothing, and the OOM message below told users to reach for it. `AutoencoderKL` now has `enable_tiling` (`decoder_tiling` is read per decode in `_adaptive_decode`, so setting it takes effect on the next call), and the caller's guard narrows to `AttributeError` and names the VAE class instead of discarding the request. Every `enable_tiling` implementation in the tree takes only optional arguments, so narrowing the guard cannot turn a previously swallowed error into a crash. **The decode OOM handler recommended `--vae-cpu-offload`,** which moves VAE weights and does nothing for the activations that overflow. Decode runs after denoising, so the DiT and encoders are idle but may still hold VRAM — freeing them is the actual lever. The message now points at `--cpu-offload-components`, then tile size, then resolution. **`ModelOptFp4Config.get_min_capability()` declared 100 but was never called.** The only real gate was whether flashinfer imports, so on a pre-Blackwell card with flashinfer installed the load succeeded and then failed inside the CUDA kernel with an opaque error. The FP4 linear method now enforces the declared minimum. A GPU whose capability cannot be read is left alone, so this only ever turns a crash into a message and never blocks a card that would have worked. ## Test plan - [x] New unit test covers the gate's three branches: reject below the minimum (8.6 / 8.9 / 9.0), allow Blackwell (10.0 / 12.0), and leave an undetectable capability alone. - [x] Real hardware, H200 (compute capability 9.0): the gate rejects with `NVFP4 checkpoints need compute capability 10.0 or newer (Blackwell); this GPU is 9.0.` instead of reaching the kernel. - [x] Verified on the same box that `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE` now resolves `enable_tiling`, and that its `decoder_tiling` is already true at construction. - [x] Audited all four `enable_tiling` implementations for required arguments before narrowing the guard. **Not covered:** the allow path on live Blackwell silicon — no B200/B300/5090 capacity was free. It is exercised with a mocked capability, and the values match this repo's own detection (`is_blackwell()` is `major == 10`, `is_sm120()` is `major == 12`, both ≥ 100 via `DeviceCapability.to_int()`). The two OOM log branches are also not triggered end to end; they are message-only changes. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32175797243](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32175797243)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32175797079](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32175797079)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] MiniMax-M3: fuse sparse QK norm, RoPE and cache writes with AITER
signals.text: ## Motivation After the packed QKV+index projection from #32099, every MiniMax-M3 sparse attention layer still launches separate kernels for Q/K and index Q/K norm + RoPE, followed by main K/V and index-K cache writes. This PR connects AITER `fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm` to the SGLang MiniMax-M3 sparse path. It keeps the current SGLang cache contract and is opt-in: ```bash SGLANG_M3_USE_AITER_FUSED_QKNORM=1 ``` Default behavior is unchanged when the env is unset. ## Changes - Fuse main/index per-head Gemma RMSNorm, partial NeoX RoPE, main K/V cache write and index-K cache write. - Use SGLang's existing page-1 NHD, unit-scale FP8 main KV and BF16 index-K contract. - Skip the old duplicate cache-store path in both prefill and decode when the fused producer has already written the cache. - Fall back to the existing path if the AITER op, packed projection, dtype, layout or model shape is not compatible. - Keep the integration opt-in for compatibility with older AITER wheels. This only changes the sparse attention preparation/cache stage. Dense attention layers, index score/top-k, sparse GQA, output projection, MoE and all-reduce are unchanged. ## Results MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, MI355X, TP4, BF16, FP8 E4M3 KV, fixed ISL 8192 / OSL 1024. The baseline and candidate use the same four-PR stack (#32036, #32099, #32190, #32230); the fused env is the only functional difference. | concurrency | total tok/s/GPU | median TTFT (s) | median TPOT (s) | uplift vs. four-PR baseline | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 188.27 | 0.33 | 0.01 | **+5.50%** | | 2 | 343.66 | 0.53 | 0.01 | **+6.77%** | | 4 | 614.34 | 0.88 | 0.01 | **+5.95%** | | 8 | 991.32 | 1.48 | 0.02 | **+4.78%** | | 16 | 1640.26 | 2.69 | 0.02 | **+5.74%** | | 32 | 2330.60 | 5.11 | 0.03 | **+5.99%** | | 64 | 3236.21 | 9.96 | 0.03 | **+3.89%** | | 128 | 4041.67 | 19.77 | 0.05 | **+3.26%** | | 256 | 4758.47 | 39.16 | 0.08 | **+3.05%** | The fused path is faster at every tested concurrency from 1 to 256. ## Accuracy MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, MI355X TP4, 5-shot GSM8K, 1319 questions, `temperature=0`: | path | accuracy | correct | invalid | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Existing path | 0.846 | 1116/1319 | 0.001 | | Fused path | 0.864 | 1140/1319 | 0.001 | Both runs completed successfully with no runtime traceback during evaluation. signals.title: [Diffusion] Compile-plan trajectory promotion gate
signals.text: ## Summary Implements the data model and validation flow proposed in #35333: connects SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support (`DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` in `runtime/utils/torch_compile.py`) to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models -- turning "compile succeeded" into "this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature." - `CompileWorkloadSignature` -- the exact workload regime (model revision, dtype, backend, parallel signature, latent shape regime, step count, CFG/cache mode, state schema version) a compiled plan is valid for, with a stable sha256 `digest()` for use as a manifest key. - `TrajectoryGate` -- declares checkpoints and per-checkpoint tensor-parity thresholds (`cosine_similarity` as a *minimum*, `mae`/`mse`/`rmse`/`max_abs`/`l2` as *maximums*), plus a slot for model-specific output-quality metrics the framework deliberately does not compute itself. - `CompiledPlanManifest` -- the offline/CI artifact recording whether a compile plan was promoted (`"validated"`/`"rejected"`) for a signature. - `run_trajectory_gate()` -- warms and runs both an eager reference and a compiled candidate through a caller-supplied stepping function across a *full checkpoint schedule* (not a single isolated forward, per the RFC's core argument that one forward isn't enough to validate a stateful rollout), scores each declared checkpoint, and rejects on the first threshold miss. - `select_validated_plan()` -- the runtime-side lookup: does an incoming workload signature match a validated manifest, or fall back to eager. The manifest is an offline/CI artifact; the runtime never reruns the full reference rollout per request. `compute_tensor_metrics()` mirrors the metric semantics of the existing `tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` (cosine similarity, MAE/MSE/RMSE, max-abs, L2), reimplemented locally rather than imported, so this module carries no diffusion-specific dependencies (no `imageio`, no model loading) and stays independently testable. ## Scope Data model, validation, and the promotion decision itself -- matching the RFC's explicit non-goals ("this RFC does not enable [compile] globally"; "runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request"). Wiring an actual SGLang Diffusion model/pipeline through this gate as part of CI is follow-up work. ## Test plan `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_compile_trajectory_gate.py`, 18 tests, all passing: - Signature digest determinism and sensitivity to every field. - `TrajectoryGate`/`CompiledPlanManifest` validation (empty/duplicate checkpoints, missing threshold entries, invalid status). - `compute_tensor_metrics()` correctness (identical tensors score perfectly, shape mismatches raise). - **`run_trajectory_gate()` against a real `torch.compile` call** -- not mocked tensors: a toy stateful iterative `nn.Module` (linear + tanh, hidden state carried across steps, standing in for a denoising step) is wrapped with `torch.compile(backend="aot_eager")`, and both the eager and compiled versions are actually run through a multi-step rollout: - the compiled candidate's trajectory is confirmed `"validated"` against the eager reference at declared checkpoints; - a deliberately diverging candidate (same shape, shifted values, standing in for a broken/miscompiled plan) is confirmed `"rejected"`; - a checkpoint schedule that never visits a declared checkpoint, and a step function returning `None` for a declared checkpoint, both raise `CompileGateError` rather than silently passing. - `select_validated_plan()` -- matching signature returns the manifest, mismatched signature falls back to `None`, and a `"rejected"` manifest is never selected regardless of signature match. All 18 tests were run on the **Apple Silicon MPS backend** (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved `DEVICE`, not a silent CPU fallback -- so the `torch.compile` calls and tensor-metric computations are exercised on a real accelerator, not just plain Python logic. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35333. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166481922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481922)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166481726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481726)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for the NIXL backend
signals.text: ## Motivation #35049 added env-gated **deferred decode-side KV release** — on abort, hold an in-flight request's KV pages/req-slot until the prefill confirms its transfer drained (or a timeout fires), so a still-landing write can't corrupt the next request that reuses those pages. It wired the prefill ack for **mooncake only**. Two reasons NIXL needs it: 1. **There is a latent footgun today.** The decode side is backend-agnostic, so enabling `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` on a NIXL deployment *already* holds pages (`NixlKVManager(CommonKVManager)`, `NixlKVReceiver(CommonKVReceiver)` inherit the abort/tracker machinery). But NIXL never sends `ABORT_ACK` and had no path to receive one, so `is_abort_release_safe` is never satisfied and **every abort waits out the full timeout** — safe (holding is the safe direction), but fully degraded, pinning KV and back-pressuring new requests under abort load. 2. **The hazard is arguably worse than mooncake's.** NIXL transfers are inherently asynchronous — `agent.transfer(handle)` posts and returns, and the worker polls `check_xfer_state(handle)` for `DONE` — so there is always a real in-flight window. Mooncake's *default* path is the synchronous `batch_transfer_sync`. `nixl/conn.py::_handle_abort_notification` even carried a `TODO` for exactly this mechanism. ## Modifications **Shared (`common/conn.py`)** — one ack implementation for both backends: - Hoist `_prefill_unique_rank`, `_send_abort_ack`, `_maybe_ack_drained_abort` and the `_deferred_ack_targets` map from `MooncakeKVManager` to `CommonKVManager`; add `register_deferred_ack_target()` documenting the mark-`Failed`-first ordering. Mooncake behavior is unchanged (now inherited). `CommonKVSender.clear()` already drops held targets, so NIXL gets that cleanup for free. **NIXL (`nixl/conn.py`)**: - `_handle_abort_notification`: parse the return address the decode already sends (`_send_abort_notification` has always included ip/port — NIXL just ignored it), register the held ack **after** the status flip for an active room, and ack a concluded room immediately. It never acks an active room from the bootstrap thread: a chunk dequeued but not yet counted would race the ack. - `transfer_worker`: ack at the skip site (nothing was written for the aborted room) and after the existing `while handles: check_xfer_state == DONE` barrier (writes have landed). NIXL's drain point is actually *cleaner* than mooncake's — no sibling-future hazard. Deliberately **no** ack on the exception path: that barrier bails on the first `ERR`, so sibling handles may still be writing; the room falls back to the decode timeout. **Closing two ack-stranding windows (both backends — both were present in #35049):** Previously the ack was driven only by worker visits, so two sequences left a registered target that nobody ever acked, falling back to the decode timeout (safe, but losing the fast path exactly when you want it): 1. the owning worker could pass its `Failed` skip point *between* the status flip and the target registration (ack attempt a no-op, then the target lands and strands); 2. a room whose enqueued chunks had all drained with no further chunk coming (`is_last_chunk` unseen) is never revisited by the worker at all. The root cause was that `outstanding == 0` was not a quiescence predicate: chunks were counted *after* the `Failed` status check, so a chunk could be dequeued and about to write while the counter still read 0 — which is why the ack could not safely be sent from the bootstrap thread. Now chunks are **counted at dequeue, before the status check**, so a chunk either writes (counted) or skips (uncounted), never both, and `Failed and outstanding == 0` genuinely means nothing can still write. With that predicate the abort path attempts the ack once after registering, covering both windows. Counting slightly earlier is strictly more conservative for the existing `poll()` Success hold and teardown condition (increments/decrements still pair). - Decode: generalize the staging-only ZMQ thread into a decode **listener** that also handles `ABORT_ACK`, started when staging *or* deferred release is enabled. A dedicated thread ingests acks even while the decode is idle — NIXL notifs would **not**, since the decode agent runs with `num_threads=0` and only drains notifs inside a live receiver's `poll()`, which early-returns once `conclude_state` is set on abort. Off by default; when disabled, both backends behave exactly as before. ## Tests New `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`: ack held until outstanding drains, fires at most once, unregistered-room no-op, rank formula matches the Success-sync formula, abort-notification registration (active / concluded / feature-off / legacy 2-frame abort / non-ABORT passthrough), and per-rank ack aggregation. Existing NIXL fixtures that build a manager via `object.__new__` now set `enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = False` (they cover the legacy no-ack behavior). Verified in the `lmsysorg/sglang` container on a CPU VM: ``` test_nixl_deferred_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_nixl_backend_basic Ran 43 tests OK test_deferred_decode_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_decode_queue_cleanup Ran 6 tests OK test_nixl_sender_failure_cleanup Ran 1 test OK test_disaggregation_wire Ran 23 tests OK test_kv_transfer_replica_metric Ran 3 tests OK ``` (The mooncake-side suites are included deliberately: the dequeue-counting change touches shared worker logic.) ## Not covered / follow-ups - **No live NIXL PD run.** The state machine and wiring are unit-tested; an end-to-end abort-mid-transfer run on a real NIXL deployment (and the fast-ack-vs-timeout ratio) is not yet measured. Same gap as #35049's, which validated on mooncake. - Multi-node / TP>1 dummy-rank fan-out unvalidated (the `len(bootstrap_infos)` denominator is dummy-proof by construction, but untested where the real multi-queue concurrency lives). - The mamba/state path (`maybe_send_extra`) is not routed through drain-aware waiting on either backend — carried over from #35049. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort) - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A — abort-path correctness; no kernel/throughput impact, no-op when disabled) - [x] Code style Related: #35049, #32564, #27372 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32167618366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32167618366)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32167618173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32167618173)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.text: # [Kimi-K3] Exclude SM120 from the attention-residual TMA path ## Summary The Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatcher previously enabled the TMA fast path for every CUDA architecture with a compute-capability major version greater than or equal to 10. This incorrectly selected the SM100-oriented TMA kernel on SM120 GPUs such as the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, where the required `tcgen05`/TMEM path is not supported. This PR changes the capability gate to: ```python major >= 10 and major != 12 ``` SM12x devices now use the existing Triton fallback. The fast path remains available on SM10x, SM11x, and later non-SM12x architectures. ## Scope This is a standalone Kimi-K3 attention-residual dispatch fix. ## Validation - Verified that the modified Python module passes `py_compile`. - Verified that the PR changes only `python/sglang/srt/layers/attn_residual.py`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32164229459](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32164229459)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32164229339](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32164229339)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix: guard top-logprobs and token-ids logprob rows against missing data
signals.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #34627. That PR removed the early return that dropped output logprobs when input logprobs are absent, but the removed return had also been shielding everything below it: with output-only logprob requests, execution now reaches the top-logprobs and token-ids blocks that still assume input-side data is present. - `return_logprob=True, top_logprobs_num>0` without input logprobs: the scheduler leaves `ReqLogprob.input_top_logprobs_val` at `None` when the prefill pass did not compute input-side top logprobs, and the output streamer appends that per-request `None` into the batch list. `len(recv_obj.input_top_logprobs_val) > 0` therefore passes, and `state.input_top_logprobs_val.extend(None)` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. - `token_ids_logprob` set without input logprobs: the same shape arrives for the input-side token-ids rows (and the output-side fields can be `None` on paths that never populated them). ## Modifications Extend each side only when both the batch-level field and the per-request row are present, mirroring the guards #34627 added for the plain logprob fields: - input top logprobs: `is not None and len(...) > 0 and [i] is not None` - output top logprobs / token-ids rows: `is not None and [i] is not None` ## Verification - New regression tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_flat_raw_top_logprobs.py` (same stub style as the #34627 regression test): - `test_output_top_logprobs_without_input_logprobs` - `test_token_ids_logprobs_without_input_logprobs` - Both fail on current `main` with the predicted `TypeError` at `tokenizer_manager.py` (`extend(None)`) and pass with this change; the pre-existing tests in the file still pass (30 passed, 2 skipped locally). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166870429](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166870429)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166870120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166870120)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [PD] Fall back to cpu_tensor when host-pool retraction cannot fit
signals.text: ## Motivation `resolve_decode_retraction_backup`, added in #34801, picks the PD decode retraction backend on capability alone — mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, priority preemption, pool class. Whether the host pool fits never comes up, and it has to: `host_pool` mirrors the device KV pool 1:1 on every scheduler, while the only capacity check sits downstream in `pool_host/base.py`, well past the point of no return. On a GB300 tray that check can never pass. Four Blackwell Ultra GPUs hold 1110 GiB of HBM against 955 GiB of Grace LPDDR5X, so a KV pool sized to fill HBM cannot be mirrored into host RAM — a hybrid-SWA model at TP4 wants 1059.80 GB against ~854 GB free: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 117.76 GB but only have 98.90 GB free. ``` No workload or freed page cache gets there, and any node whose HBM rivals its DRAM lands the same way. An inferred default that cannot be satisfied should step aside; one asked for by name should still fail loudly. ## Modifications The inferred choice degrades to `cpu_tensor` with a warning naming both figures. Explicit `host_pool` still hard-fails, since the gate sits inside the `backend is None` branch. The budget reads `available` — what `HostKVCache.__init__` itself gates on. `_agree_across_ranks` all-reduces MIN over the world CPU group, shaped after `sync_fixed_hicache_size`, so no rank diverges. Reaching it needs a rank-uniform predicate, which splits the eligibility test: mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, and priority preemption come from the config bags and gate the estimate, while `supports_host_pool` is per-rank and only picks the backend. Prefill, embedding, and non-PD servers skip the estimate entirely. Three sizing fixes: - `_local_scheduler_count` mirrors the launcher's `pp_size_per_node * tp_size_per_node` plus the classic-DP replica factor. `tp_size // nnodes` undercounts past `pp_size > 1` and can reach zero. Reads `configured_tp_size()` / `configured_pp_size()`, which don't assert before process-group init. - MTP/EAGLE draft pools count, since the mirror packs them into its own `layer_num`. - `_kv_pool_bytes` takes both `get_kv_size_bytes` shapes. It tests for the `(k, v)` pair rather than the scalar: MLA returns `numpy.int64`, which `isinstance(size, int)` misses. `hicache_ratio` keys off the pre-fallback verdict, so the gate cannot enlarge the pool it just rejected. Deliberately not keyed off "a host pool gets built anyway", which would cut 2.0 to 1.0 for hierarchical-cache users on the decode-radix-cache path. The gate and the normalisation cover different cases — reverting the normalisation alone on 4×GB300: | Configuration | Normalisation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | non-PD MLA | reverted | starts — the gate excludes it | | non-PD MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | | PD decode MLA | reverted | crashes in `_kv_pool_bytes` | | PD decode MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | The estimate is a lower bound; the per-rank gate stays authoritative. Page round-up and SIDECAR draft pools are unmodelled, because reproducing host-pool sizing here would go stale quietly. That belongs in a shared sizing helper, along with the scalar/tuple split and the unified pools — they return `(0, 0)` while subclassing MHA/SWA, so they would leave the gate inert rather than loud. Unreachable today: `--enable-unified-memory` with PD is MLA hybrid-Mamba only. ## Accuracy Tests Outputs are untouched — this resolves startup configuration, not the retraction path. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_capacity.py` is new and CPU-registered, covering the PP and DP rank arithmetic, fits and doesn't-fit, the reserve, draft-pool accounting, both accessor shapes, the scope, and the ratio invariant driven through the resolver itself. Each fix was mutation-checked by reverting it: | Reverted | Result | | --- | --- | | ratio keyed off the post-fallback backend | 1 failure, `AssertionError: 2.0 != 1.0` | | reduction re-gated on the per-rank predicate | 2 failures, `_agree_across_ranks` called 0 times | | shape normalisation | 3 failures | | config-uniform gate | 2 failures | 166 tests pass across that file, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, and `test_server_args.py`; 20/20 under the `unittest` runner; pre-commit clean. On 4×GB300, a hybrid-SWA PD decode server falls back with identical figures on all four ranks and no deadlock, an MLA server starts clean both non-PD and PD decode, and a plain non-PD server never reaches the estimate. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The gate runs once per scheduler at startup, only for a config-eligible decode server, and the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
