signals.title: [diffusion] fix: unblock the ComfyUI passthrough denoise path
signals.text: ## Motivation The ComfyUI passthrough pipeline feeds pre-encoded embeddings straight to the transformer, so it runs neither `TextEncodingStage` nor timestep preparation. Three downstream consumers assume those stages have run, so the passthrough denoise path cannot complete: - `require_text_seq_lens()` reads `batch.prompt_seq_lens`, which only `TextEncodingStage` populates. - `DenoisingStage` reads `batch.scheduler`, which is left unset without timestep prep. - `ComfyUIPassThroughScheduler.step()` increments `self._step_index`, but `DenoisingStage` clears it to `None` before the loop, so the increment fails on the first step. Running the Flux passthrough test off CUDA surfaced two more issues: the test hard-codes `device="cuda"`, and it passes `negative_prompt_embeds` with an empty `neg_pooled_embeds`. ## Modifications - `comfyui_latent_preparation.py`: back-fill `batch.prompt_seq_lens` / `batch.negative_prompt_seq_lens` from the incoming embeddings, since there is no `TextEncodingStage` to do it. - `denoising.py`: resolve the scheduler through `get_or_create_request_scheduler()` instead of reading `batch.scheduler` directly. - `scheduling_comfyui_passthrough.py`: re-seed `_step_index` from `_begin_index` when `DenoisingStage` has cleared it. - `configs/pipeline_configs/base.py`: add `PipelineConfig.seq_lens_from_prompt_embeds()` — the "seq lens from maskless embeddings" rule (2-D means `batch=1`), previously inline in `TextEncodingStage`. - `text_encoding.py`: use the shared helper, so the new back-fill and the text-encoding path share one definition. - `test_flux_pipeline.py`: use `current_platform.device_type` instead of hard-coded `"cuda"`, and pass a zeroed `neg_pooled_embeds` when `negative_prompt_embeds` is set — Flux `time_text_embed` needs a pooled projection on every CFG branch. - `component_residency_strategies.py`: offload synchronously on XPU. An async copy into pageable host memory can reach the backend memcpy with a null argument there, and cannot overlap anything anyway. ## Accuracy Tests Nothing here changes model math on the existing CUDA paths. The forward-affecting changes are scoped to the ComfyUI passthrough pipeline, which previously could not run to completion, and to the CFG negative branch of the Flux passthrough test, which previously supplied no pooled projection at all. The `text_encoding.py` change is intended to be a pure no-op refactor: `seq_lens_from_prompt_embeds()` reproduces the removed `ndim == 2` / else branches exactly. Local test logs are not attached yet — please run the diffusion suite in CI, and I will add XPU `test_flux_pipeline.py` output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected impact. The XPU offload change trades an async copy for a synchronous one on XPU only, where the async path could not overlap work regardless; CUDA offload behavior is unchanged. The remaining changes are one-time per-request setup, not per-step work. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — `black`, `isort`, `ruff` (repo rule set) and `codespell` all clean. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — existing `test_flux_pipeline.py` updated; no new test file added. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a, no user-facing API or flag change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — rationale above; numbers to follow if reviewers want them. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32168791851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168791851)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32168791670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168791670)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [XPU] fix: drop CUDA assumptions from the mamba/GDN and weight-load paths
signals.text: ## Motivation Several mamba/GDN state paths and the remote-instance weight loader hard-code CUDA even though nothing about them is CUDA-specific — the kernels are plain Triton, and the allocations already have a configured device to hand. On a non-CUDA device they fail rather than run. One of these is a latent bug on any device: the XPU `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` wrapper does not pass `stride_h0_source`, which the shared kernel in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py` takes as a required argument (the CUDA caller passes it). ## Modifications - `srt/hardware_backend/xpu/kernels/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py`: pass `stride_h0_source=initial_state_source.stride(0)` (0 when the source is `None`). Envelope-strided state pools have a per-slot pitch `!= HV*K*V`, so the stride has to come from the caller. - `kernels/ops/mamba/mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`: `fused_mamba_state_scatter_with_mask` and `fused_conv_window_scatter_with_mask` rejected any tensor that was not `.is_cuda`. They now share a `_require_triton_device()` helper that requires a common, non-CPU device — the same guarantee the Triton kernels actually need. Error messages now name the calling function. - `srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py`: three `MambaPool` buffers were allocated with `device="cuda"` while every sibling allocation in the same methods uses the configured device. They now use it too. - `srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`: `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` / `torch.cuda.synchronize()` after rebinding the embedding and LM head become `current_platform` calls. - `test/registered/model_loading/test_load_weights_from_remote_instance.py`: `torch.cuda.set_device/synchronize/empty_cache` become `current_platform` equivalents, the 2-GPU precondition uses `get_device_count()`, and `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` / `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE` are only set on cuda-alike platforms. The `init_process_dst` `set_device` moved below `base_gpu_id` so it can use it — previously it called `set_device(rank * tp_size)` and then recomputed the same value. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical change on CUDA: - `current_platform.empty_cache()` / `synchronize()` / `set_device()` dispatch to the `torch.cuda` equivalents on CUDA. - The `device="cuda"` → configured-device changes are no-ops when the configured device is CUDA, which it was in every path that previously worked. - `_require_triton_device()` only relaxes a precondition; the accepted CUDA inputs and the kernels themselves are untouched. The `stride_h0_source` fix is the one behavioral change. It makes the XPU wrapper match the CUDA caller, which already passes the same expression; the wrapper could not previously reach the kernel at all. `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` is registered CUDA/AMD CI, so its existing coverage exercises this refactor directly — please trigger it. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected impact: no kernel body, launch configuration, grid, or allocation shape changes. The `stride_h0_source` value is computed once per call from an existing tensor. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — `black`, `isort`, `ruff` (repo rule set) and `codespell` all clean. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — covered by the existing registered `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance`; no new test file added. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a, no user-facing API or flag change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — rationale above; numbers to follow if reviewers want them. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32168852958](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168852958)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32168852494](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168852494)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: feat(cake_gemm): add Cake batch DeepGEMM FP8 backend
signals.text: ## Real-weight inference validation Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324) using all 163 real safetensors shards with native FP8 weights. Both runs used 4x NVIDIA GB300, TP4/EP4, the same server configuration, and the same deterministic inputs. ### Accuracy parity Here, accuracy means backend numerical/decoding parity, not a downstream model-quality benchmark such as MMLU. Token exact match is `matching generated token IDs / 48`; sequence exact match requires every generated token in a prompt to match. | Check | FlashInfer/DeepGEMM reference | Cake | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Greedy prompts | 3 | 3 | same inputs | | Generated tokens per prompt | 16 | 16 | 48 tokens compared | | Token exact-match accuracy | 48 | 48 | **48/48 = 100%** | | Sequence exact-match accuracy | 3 | 3 | **3/3 = 100%** | | Finish reasons | 3 | 3 | **3/3 exact** | | Non-finite output logprobs | 0 | 0 | **pass** | | Maximum output-token logprob absolute difference | — | — | **0.0** | ### Steady-state SGLang E2E SGLang's serving benchmark used 64 requests per round, exact 16-token inputs and 128-token outputs, concurrency 8, request rate `inf`, seed 42, and three rounds per backend. A separate 16-request x 32-output-token warmup ran first. Model loading, server startup, JIT compilation, and warmup are excluded; the reported metric is steady-state end-to-end request wall clock. The harness invoked `sglang.benchmark.serving.run_benchmark` directly. This is the CLI-equivalent command sequence used once against the reference server and once against the Cake server; the measured loop runs three rounds: ```bash python - <<'PY' import json from pathlib import Path rows = [ { "conversations": [ {"value": f"Deterministic serving benchmark prompt number {i} for real weight inference."}, {"value": "Deterministic benchmark response."}, ] } for i in range(128) ] Path("random-corpus.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n") PY BENCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:31000 # reference; use :32000 for Cake CORPUS_PATH=./random-corpus.json # fixed 128-row deterministic corpus COMMON_ARGS=( --backend sglang --base-url "$BENCH_URL" --dataset-name random --dataset-path "$CORPUS_PATH" --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 --random-input-len 16 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 8 --seed 42 --disable-tqdm ) # Excluded warmup. curl -fsS -X POST "$BENCH_URL/flush_cache" python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --num-prompts 16 --random-output-len 32 # Three measured rounds. run_benchmark performs its own one-request warmup # before its benchmark_start_time; the explicit cache flush is also outside it. for BENCH_ROUND in 0 1 2; do curl -fsS -X POST "$BENCH_URL/flush_cache" python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --num-prompts 64 --random-output-len 128 done ``` | Round | Reference duration (s) | Cake duration (s) | Reference output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 378.054856 | 204.302219 | 21.668813 | 40.097460 | **1.850469x** | | 1 | 377.507678 | 202.967479 | 21.700221 | 40.361146 | **1.859942x** | | 2 | 372.968888 | 205.485857 | 21.964299 | 39.866491 | **1.815059x** | | Three-round median metric | Reference | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Duration | 377.507678 s | 204.302219 s | **1.847790x** | | Output throughput | 21.700221 tok/s | 40.097460 tok/s | **1.847790x** | | Total throughput | 24.412748 tok/s | 45.109642 tok/s | **1.847790x** | | Mean E2E latency | 47,185.254 ms | 25,534.840 ms | **1.847877x** | | Median E2E latency | 47,198.526 ms | 25,529.890 ms | **1.848756x** | | Mean TTFT | 1,112.430 ms | 592.937 ms | **1.876137x** | | Median TTFT | 1,028.638 ms | 546.565 ms | **1.882004x** | | Mean TPOT | 362.778 ms | 196.393 ms | **1.847206x** | | Median TPOT | 363.052 ms | 196.489 ms | **1.847700x** | Reference output-throughput CV: `0.745%`. Cake output-throughput CV: `0.617%`.

signals.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signals.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets that run on a consumer card, so the barrier for those users is not VRAM — it is the download and the host memory that offload pins. This adds GGUF as a diffusion quantization family so the transformer can come from a single community-quantized file: **17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB** for the same model. That shrinks the download, the pinned host memory, and the bytes streamed per layer, all by ~3.5x. It is complementary to `kitchen_int8` (#34581) rather than an alternative: that path is faster, but quantizes online and therefore still needs the full BF16 checkpoint on disk and in host RAM. **GGUF does not reduce peak VRAM** — peak is set by the offload buffers and VAE decode, not the weight dtype. There is also a large existing ecosystem of community GGUF checkpoints for other DiTs (Qwen-Image, Wan, FLUX), which this makes reachable. ## Modifications `--model-path` stays the base model; `--transformer-weights-path` takes the `.gguf`. A local path, `owner/repo/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` all resolve. `--quantization gguf` is deliberately *not* the selector — the quantization is read from the file header. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF:Q4_K_M \ --num-gpus 1 \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` **New:** - `runtime/loader/gguf_weights.py` — header reader, tensor-layout metadata, weights iterator, Hub reference resolution. - `runtime/layers/quantization/gguf.py` — `GGUFConfig` + `GGUFLinearMethod`. Weights stay packed on device and are dequantized per use via the in-tree `ggml_dequantize`; `F.linear` broadcasts the DiT's N-D activations. **Changed:** - `loader/fsdp_load.py` (+10) — optional `weights_iterator` so a caller whose checkpoint is not safetensors can supply its own source. - `loader/transformer_load_utils.py` — GGUF resolution and the constraint checks. - `loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py` — routes the GGUF branch. - `models/dits/minimax_h3.py` (+6) — skip the qkv reorder, which translates the safetensors layout; GGUF already stores `[q_all, k_all, v_all]`. - `pipelines_core/lora_pipeline.py` — reject LoRA on packed weights before offload is disabled. The packed byte shape of every tensor is read from the header *before* the model is constructed, so `create_weights` registers each parameter with its exact packed shape. The generic weight loader's cast to the meta parameter's dtype is then a no-op on an already-`uint8` parameter, which is why **`linear.py` is untouched** and no lazily-materialized parameter is needed. **Rejected at startup**, rather than misbehaving later: non-CUDA, `--tp-size > 1`, FSDP for the loading component, LoRA (including a dynamic `set_lora`), `--quantization`, `--enable-svdquant`, the H3 AdaLN cache/online flags, a non-native byte order, and a tensor whose element count is not a whole number of 256-element super blocks (the K-quant/IQ dequantize kernels have no bounds check; IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS round the block count up and would write out of bounds). ## Accuracy Tests Dequantized weights compared tensor-by-tensor against the BF16 reference checkpoint (shard 1, all 54 shared tensors): | GGML type | tensors | min cosine | max rel. err | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | F32 | 9 | 1.00000 | 0.00000 | | BF16 | 24 | 1.00000 | 0.00000 | | Q4_0 | 3 | 0.99738 | 0.072 | | Q4_K | 18 | 0.99686 | 0.079 | End to end on 1× RTX 5090, `t2va` at 1344×768 × 107 frames: valid MP4 (H.264 + AAC 32 kHz stereo, clean full decode), output bit-identical across runs at a fixed seed. 36 CPU unit tests in `test/unit/test_gguf_diffusion.py`, passing with and without a visible GPU. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GGUF is not a speed optimization — it pays one dequantization per linear per denoise step. Measured on 1× RTX 5090, same checkpoint and request, showing the VAE offload trade-off (output bit-identical either way): | `--layerwise-offload-components` | Peak VRAM | Denoise | VAE decode | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `dit,text_encoder` | 26.3 GiB | 39.0 s | 9.5 s | | `dit,text_encoder,vae` | 19.6 GiB | 39.0 s | 57.2 s | Adding `vae` saves 6.7 GiB of peak at ~6x the decode time, because the decoder is re-streamed per tile. The docs give both rows so the choice is explicit. **Not validated:** other quantization types, the `ref2va` partition, multi-GPU (sequence parallelism is not rejected, since it shards activations rather than weights, but it is untested), Cache-DiT and `torch.compile` combinations. Pruned community checkpoints that fold the AdaLN branches into a low-rank table change the module structure and are not loadable by this path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32173149796](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173149796)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32173149595](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173149595)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector
signals.text: ## Motivation Two additions to the DFlash draft, both switched on by the checkpoint. A DFlash checkpoint declares neither and takes the path it always took. **Grouped dynamic depthwise convolution** inside each block, so a proposal position can see the ones before it without another backbone pass. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`, taps zero across the block boundary. Wraps each sublayer in and out from one projection of its input. On when `conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` are set. **Candidate selector.** Instead of an independent argmax per slot, keep the target head's top-K per slot, score adjacent transitions `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`, and walk the best path from the verified anchor. At T>0 it walks by inverse CDF and returns q over the K candidates for the lossless verify. On when `selector_rank` and `selector_top_k` are set. ## Modifications ``` srt/models/dflash.py the convolution, the selector, the walk kernel srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py four config fields srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py the proposal and the T>0 verify ``` The selector's decode is folded into the draft CUDA graph, greedy and sampled alike. The walk is one Triton program per request: a slot's K scores stay in registers, greedy rows take the argmax and emit a one-hot q, and the slot-to-slot dependency is a loop inside the program rather than a kernel per slot. No new server args, no new env vars, nothing outside DFlash touched. ## Accuracy Tests ``` python -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py ``` `4 passed` and `5 passed`. `test_dflash_logits.py` covers the selector's sampled path end to end, the mixed greedy/sampling batch — each row identical to running it alone, with greedy rows asserted to carry a one-hot q — and the rejection of a quantized target LM head. Lossless decoding is the property that matters here and it is structural: greedy walks emit the point mass at the token they take, and sampled walks return the realized q over the K candidates, so the verify sees the proposal distribution it actually drew from. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Published evaluation for [`z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2) on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`: SGLang on one H200 with FlashAttention 3, block size 8 (seven draft tokens per verification step), Qwen3.8's recommended sampling (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) at `xhigh` reasoning effort, 4096 max new tokens, prompts formatted by [`z-lab/dflash`](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash). Compared against the target's built-in MTP and a community DSpark drafter, [`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark), both also proposing seven tokens per step. ### Acceptance length Per-request mean of completion tokens over verification steps. | Dataset | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 | |---------|----:|-------:|---------:| | GSM8K | 5.02 | 4.36 | **5.46** | | MATH-500 | 4.72 | 3.92 | **5.28** | | HumanEval | 3.91 | 3.30 | **4.39** | | MBPP | 3.99 | 3.51 | **4.79** | | MT-Bench | 3.74 | 3.01 | **4.10** | ### Throughput, GSM8K Output tokens over end-to-end wall time, with speedup over autoregressive decoding. | conc | autoregressive | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 | |------|---------------:|----:|-------:|---------:| | 1 | 68.9 | 178.5 (2.59×) | 185.3 (2.69×) | **236.1 (3.43×)** | | 8 | 467.2 | 1,022.1 (2.19×) | 1,040.8 (2.23×) | **1,328.7 (2.84×)** | | 32 | 1,329.8 | 1,381.1 (1.04×) | 1,506.5 (1.13×) | **1,922.5 (1.45×)** | Full tables for the other four datasets, and for [`z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2) against Meta's published DFlash assistant, are on the model cards. ### What it costs The convolution and the selector are the whole difference between a DFlash draft and a DFlash 2 draft, so their cost is what a step loses by having them. Measured against Meta's published DFlash assistant on the same target, [`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B), block 16, GSM8K, four H200 shards. `cost` is `(1 + accept gain) / (1 + throughput gain) - 1` — the throughput gain the extra acceptance would have produced had the step stayed the same length, against the gain it actually produced. | conc | acceptance | throughput | cost | | acceptance | throughput | cost | |------|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|---|-----------:|-----------:|-----:| | | **T=0** | | | | **T=1** | | | | 1 | +13.6% | +11.7% | 1.7% | | +24.4% | +21.1% | 2.7% | | 8 | +14.0% | +11.4% | 2.3% | | +24.5% | +21.5% | 2.5% | | 32 | +14.1% | +11.9% | 2.0% | | +24.0% | +21.2% | 2.3% | | 64 | +14.0% | +12.3% | 1.5% | | +24.3% | +22.2% | 1.7% | So 1.5–2.7%, and it falls as the batch grows: the target verify grows with the batch while the selector's work does not keep pace. It falls as the target grows for the same reason. Acceptance enters this table only as a ratio between the two drafts, both measured the same way — as total accepted tokens over total verification steps, where the model card reports a mean over per-request ratios. The two statistics differ on absolute values but nearly cancel in the gain: +24.3% here at concurrency 64 against the card's +21.0% for the same pair of checkpoints. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32199057265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199057265)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32199057143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199057143)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Support wider rows in mega_moe_pre_dispatch
signals.text: ## Motivation `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` assigns one thread to each 8-element input chunk, so a single CUDA block can only cover hidden dimensions up to 8192. Wider shapes are rejected before launch. ## Modifications - Cap the block size at the CUDA 1024-thread limit and process wider rows in strided chunks. - Recompute quantization-group indices for each chunk while preserving the UE8M0 scale layout. - Keep a separate single-chunk kernel specialization so existing shapes retain the same instruction path. - Reject wide shapes whose tail would split a warp-level reduction. ## Accuracy Tests - Verified bitwise FP8 output and UE8M0 scale bytes against a reference implementation for hidden dimensions 3584, 5632, 8192, 12288, and 16384. - Verified exact top-k copies and idle-slot padding. - Verified that hidden dimension 8320 fails with the expected full-warp alignment error. - JIT-compiled the ported CUDA header successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - The single-chunk specialization produces the same SASS instruction stream as the previous kernel. - CUDA-event microbenchmarks showed no measurable regression for shapes that already fit in one chunk. ## Original commits - `d7c54c96f5` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). The relevant clang-format, codespell, whitespace, and EOF checks passed; full pre-commit initialization was blocked by local network policy. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing documentation changes are required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32180304913](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32180304913)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32180304818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32180304818)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Nemotron-3.5
signals.text: ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856` - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The tuned configs reduce kernel latency by 32.2% to 39.6% across the measured token counts. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191091618](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191091618)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191091591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191091591)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Add H200 FP8 MoE configs for recent Qwen models
signals.text: ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for recent Qwen FP8 models: - Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP1, with separate up/gate and down-projection tables - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, dynamic FP8, TP1 - Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8: `E=512,N=256`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP8 per rank in the verified H200 TP8 x PP4 recipe The tuned up/gate configs reduce kernel latency by 3.5% to 19.6% across the original measured token counts. The Qwen3.5 down-projection table adds a 4.9% to 17.9% incremental reduction over reusing the up config and includes decode sizes 1-128 required for stable serving. Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 BF16 share `E=256,N=512`; an H200 BF16 table already exists in `triton_3_7_1`, and Triton 3.6 falls back to it, so no duplicate non-quant config is added. Qwen3.8 BF16 has no H200 deployment recipe because the approximately 4.8 TB checkpoint does not fit the supported H200 topology. No official Qwen3.7 release was found. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `7f51e6bba096348a7eb27f31ef0e3f5946786d2c` - Up/gate token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Qwen3.5 down token counts: 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape - Real-model validation: SGLang v0.5.17, ten 200-question GSM8K runs per side ## Results | Model | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 256 | 255.43 | 220.90 | 1.156x | 13.52% | | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 512 | 265.41 | 242.75 | 1.093x | 8.54% | | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 1024 | 284.93 | 274.94 | 1.036x | 3.50% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 256 | 245.56 | 218.58 | 1.123x | 10.98% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 512 | 282.61 | 231.81 | 1.219x | 17.98% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 1024 | 303.11 | 260.82 | 1.162x | 13.95% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 256 | 1058.83 | 851.62 | 1.243x | 19.57% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 512 | 1077.81 | 876.50 | 1.230x | 18.68% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 1024 | 1138.28 | 999.70 | 1.139x | 12.17% | Each tuned config was also run on both H200s. Both GPUs selected the same configs and produced closely matching latency. ### Qwen3.5 down-projection kernel The dedicated down table was tuned with expert routes captured from the real Qwen3.5 checkpoint on a standard GSM8K prompt. The incremental column compares the dedicated down config with the runtime's previous behavior of reusing the up/gate config. | Tokens | Generic default (us) | Up-config fallback (us) | Tuned down (us) | Reduction vs generic | Incremental reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 8.41 | 7.75 | 7.34 | 12.73% | 5.24% | | 4 | 15.65 | 11.83 | 11.26 | 28.08% | 4.88% | | 16 | 30.08 | 21.48 | 20.30 | 32.52% | 5.48% | | 32 | 41.05 | 28.33 | 26.83 | 34.64% | 5.27% | | 64 | 49.27 | 35.54 | 33.43 | 32.14% | 5.93% | | 128 | 66.23 | 49.63 | 46.91 | 29.16% | 5.47% | | 256 | 78.51 | 62.99 | 57.25 | 27.07% | 9.11% | | 512 | 96.06 | 85.86 | 74.59 | 22.35% | 13.13% | | 1024 | 113.29 | 107.87 | 88.59 | 21.80% | 17.87% | ### Real-model SGLang v0.5.17 GSM8K Checkpoint: `/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49` Both sides used SGLang v0.5.17 commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`, seed 0, one H200, the same server settings, a 20-question warmup, and ten repetitions of SGLang's standard `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` with 200 questions. | Metric | Baseline | Tuned up + down | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Median latency | 11.8005 s | 11.5760 s | -1.90% | | Mean latency | 11.8812 s | 11.6347 s | -2.07% | | Median output throughput | 3045.77 tok/s | 3183.42 tok/s | +4.52% | | Mean output throughput | 3032.40 tok/s | 3184.10 tok/s | +5.00% | | Mean GSM8K accuracy | 0.8295 | 0.8150 | -1.45 pp | | Invalid outputs | 0 | 0 | unchanged | The accuracy ranges overlapped across runs (baseline 0.810-0.845, tuned 0.805-0.830), but the lower tuned mean is reported rather than hidden. This is a performance result, not an accuracy-improvement claim. The first down-only table covered only 256/512/1024 and completed three runs, but eventually exposed a serving stall when a decode batch reused the 256-token TMA config. That table was rejected. Adding independently tuned 1/4/16/32/64/128 decode entries removed the stall and completed all ten final runs. Up-projection TMA was also audited and rejected because the exact v0.5.17 runtime does not support `USE_TMA` in the up config; compatible no-TMA alternatives were within noise of the existing up table. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODELS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-model-configs RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full searches: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen35-fp8-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen35-fp8-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen35-fp8" \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen35-fp8-tp1/tune.log" & CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen36-fp8-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen36-fp8-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen36-fp8" \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen36-fp8-tp1/tune.log" & wait CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen38-fp8-tp8/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen38-fp8-tp8/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen38-fp8" \ --tp-size 8 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen38-fp8-tp8/tune.log" ``` Baseline and tuned validation was run three times for each model. The command below was used first with the generated config absent, then repeated after copying that model's generated JSON into `triton_3_6_0`: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$GPU" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL_CONFIG" \ --tp-size "$TP_SIZE" \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$OUTPUT_DIR/$PHASE-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` The concrete validation invocations were: ```bash /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen35-fp8" 1 fp8_w8a8 qwen35-fp8-tp1 \ 'E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json' /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen36-fp8" 1 fp8_w8a8 qwen36-fp8-tp1 \ 'E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json' /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen38-fp8" 8 fp8_w8a8 qwen38-fp8-tp8 \ 'E=512,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json' ``` Concurrent dual-H200 validation for each model: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL_CONFIG" \ --tp-size "$TP_SIZE" \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$DUAL_GPU_OUTPUT/gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Real-route capture and Qwen3.5 down-projection search: ```bash RUN=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-tuned VENV="$RUN/venv-tuned" MODEL=/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49 DATA="$RUN/data/gsm8k_test.jsonl" ROUTES="$RUN/qwen35-real-topk" UP_CONFIG="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0/E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json" # The route-capture server must be launched with # --enable-return-routed-experts. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation/capture_qwen35_routes.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --dataset "$DATA" \ --model-config "$MODEL/config.json" \ --output-dir "$ROUTES" \ --min-tokens 1024 run_down_tuning() { local gpu=$1 output=$2 shift 2 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" \ PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" \ "$VENV/bin/python" "$RUN/tune_qwen35_down_real_routes.py" \ --kernel down \ --tuner "$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py" \ --model "$MODEL" \ --topk-ids-dir "$ROUTES" \ --up-config "$UP_CONFIG" \ --output-dir "$RUN/qwen35-down-tuning/$output" \ --batch-sizes "$@" \ --tune-iters 30 \ --validation-iters 100 \ --validation-repeats 3 } run_down_tuning 0 small-a 1 16 64 & run_down_tuning 1 small-b 4 32 128 & wait run_down_tuning 0 m256 256 & run_down_tuning 1 m512 512 & wait run_down_tuning 0 m1024 1024 ``` Matched SGLang v0.5.17 server and standard GSM8K commands: ```bash RUN=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation MODEL=/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49 DATA="$RUN/data/gsm8k_test.jsonl" # Run once with the baseline worktree/venv and once with the tuned worktree/venv. signals.title: [Memory] Borrow CUDA graph pool storage for EAGLE sampling
signals.text: ## Summary - expose wholly-free runs in the shared CUDA graph pool through a persistent `torch.cuda.MemPool` - allow stable, externally managed graph storage to register fixed borrow extents - guard graph capture/replay and borrowed eager allocations with exclusive pool ownership - reuse those runs for EAGLE's step-local full-vocabulary verification probabilities - generalize the existing KV VMM bump allocator to support multiple caller-owned extents - keep the feature opt-in with `SGLANG_ENABLE_GRAPH_POOL_BORROW=1` ## Safety - only inactive runs from wholly-free graph-pool segments are exposed - allocations fail normally if no single run can satisfy them; there is no silent fallback - capture retires stale borrow extents before re-carving the graph pool - capture, replay, and borrowing are mutually exclusive and report the conflicting users - cross-stream deferred frees are drained before the persistent borrow pool is retired - CUDA-only and default-off; the disabled path remains a no-op <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196238756](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196238756)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196238644](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196238644)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Avoid multi-layer EAGLE SWA scheduler synchronization
signals.text: ## Motivation Paged sliding-window KV eviction performs a data-dependent uniqueness pass for request segments that are already complete and page-aligned. Multi-layer EAGLE also leaves the scheduler without the final draft graph's shared-read completion event, forcing a broader stream synchronization before the shared buffers can be reused. ## Modifications - Add a fixed-shape SWA segment-free path for page-aligned request prefixes, with the existing token path retained for page size 1 and unified allocation. - Route sliding-window eviction through that path when the allocator supports it. - Publish `shared_read_done_event` after the final multi-layer draft graph step, including the single-graph replay path. - Point the worker's last shared-read runner at the final draft runner. - Add allocator and CPU event-publication regression tests. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output behavior changes. The relevant unit suites pass: ```text 14 SWA allocator tests passed (plus 15 subtests) 14 SWA eviction-boundary tests passed 2 shared-read event tests passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked independently. The allocator change removes a device-side uniqueness operation from complete page-aligned SWA segments, and the event publication lets the scheduler use its event-scoped shared-read barrier for multi-layer EAGLE. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal implementation change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32182552708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182552708)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32182552201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182552201)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Test] Tighten the DCP HiCache KL threshold to 0.005
signals.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` (Kimi Linear + DCP4 + HiCache L2 + UnifiedRadixCache) has gated at `kl_threshold = 0.01` since it landed in #33112. Every other fp8 hybrid cache-hit KL case in the same directory gates at 0.005: | case | threshold | | --- | --- | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` | **0.01** | A looser threshold tolerates float noise and small state bugs alike, and the thing this case exists to catch — a missing DCP logical→physical translation handing back another rank's KV on a cache hit — is exactly what slack hides. This PR tries the house value so the DCP translation path is held to the same bar as the non-DCP ones. This is an experiment: the point is to find out whether the DCP path actually holds at 0.005 in CI. If it flakes, the measured headroom tells us either to keep 0.01 with a comment recording why (the way the mamba case documents its own 0.003 → 0.005 bump) or that there is real divergence worth chasing. ## Modifications One line: `kl_threshold` 0.01 → 0.005 in `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`. No source changes. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output changes. The case is registered as `stage="extra-b"`, `runner_config="4-gpu-b200"`, so it needs the extra CI stage to actually exercise the new threshold. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test threshold only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32183451677](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183451677)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32183451328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183451328)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly, and stop running two Qwen jobs that are not paying for themselves
signals.text: ## Motivation Two related changes to AMD nightly Qwen coverage: add the missing Qwen3.8 job, and stop spending runner time on two Qwen jobs that are redundant or dead. **Add Qwen3.8.** [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD Instinct recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. The model reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (the checkpoint reports `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs today with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing currently guards it. A change to the shared Qwen3.5 hybrid path or to the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade Qwen3.8 output quality or throughput on ROCm with no signal. The new job follows the single-node MI355X cell the cookbook publishes ([`hw=mi355x`, `quant=mxfp4`, `strategy=balanced`, `nodes=single`](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8#hw=mi355x&variant=default&quant=mxfp4&strategy=balanced&nodes=single)). **Stop running the Qwen3-235B jobs.** They duplicate `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` coverage that survives elsewhere, including per-commit. ### Why MXFP4 and not the FP8 checkpoint directly At 2.4T parameters FP8 is ~2.4 TB, against 8 x 288 GB = 2.30 TB on an MI355X node, so the FP8 checkpoint has no single-node AMD recipe at all — the cookbook serves it as MI300X TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, and the AMD nightly runners are single-node. Single-node on AMD therefore means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization **of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`** (~1.2 TB, ~150 GB per GPU). Only the routed experts are quantized — attention, the shared expert, the MoE gate and `lm_head` stay at source precision — so AMD measures the same **97.49** GSM8K as the FP8 baseline (100% recovery). The FP8 checkpoint's quality is what this job is gating; MXFP4 is just the packaging that fits one node. ## Modifications ### New: Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x job **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in one file, registered to the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite (`est_time=14400`, `nightly=True`): - `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` — GSM8K few-shot at TP8, gated at 0.93. - `test_b_serving_perf` — serving benchmark over batch sizes 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out, reported through the shared `generate_simple_markdown_report`. Both phases launch from a single `SERVER_ARGS`, which reproduces the recipe published on the AMD model card: ``` --tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --trust-remote-code --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' ``` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and the eval runs `run_eval` gsm8k over the test split at 512 threads, `max_tokens=2048`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`. **Why accuracy and perf share a suite** rather than splitting into `nightly-amd-accuracy-*` and `nightly-perf-*`: sharing one `SERVER_ARGS` means the throughput numbers describe the exact configuration the accuracy gate covers, and a flag change cannot drift one out from under the other. Perf is also skipped unless accuracy passed (`accuracy_passed` class flag, with ordering from unittest's alphabetical method sort): a server that decodes garbage still benchmarks fine, so publishing its throughput would be worse than publishing nothing. Two flags in `SERVER_ARGS` are load-bearing rather than restatements of a default, and are commented as such in the file: - `--page-size 1` — `_page_size_default` bumps the default to 64 on HIP when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, so the measured geometry only holds if the page size is pinned. - `--attention-backend aiter` — no arg override picks a backend for `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` on ROCm, so the AITER path has to be named. The server deliberately runs with **no `--reasoning-parser`**: the scorer extracts the last number in the reply, so a `<think>` block still scores when reasoning stays in `message.content`. With a reasoning parser on, it would be split into `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty and scoring 0. The model path is overridable via `QWEN38_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH` for hosts with a local copy. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x, and the model card pins ROCm 7.2.0 for MI350/MI355. There is no MI30x counterpart — gfx942 has no hardware MX matmul, and the FP8 checkpoint it would otherwise serve needs two nodes. It is a single step rather than the usual accuracy/perf pair, because both phases live in the same suite. `timeout-minutes: 420` / `--timeout-per-file 21600` budget two loads of the 1.2 TB checkpoint, one per phase, which dominate wall time well before either the eval or the benchmark starts; `ENABLE_CACHE_HOST: "1"` keeps the weights on the runner cache so steady-state nights are far cheaper than the first. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite under `NIGHTLY_SUITES[HWBackend.AMD]`. ### Removed: the Qwen3-235B nightly jobs Only the workflow jobs go. No file under `test/` is touched — the tests, their launch recipes and their thresholds stay exactly as they are, so re-enabling is re-adding the job, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` still works by hand in the meantime. (Marking the tests `disabled=` was considered and rejected: on top of removing the job it changes no behavior, and it would make that manual re-run silently skip.) **All three Qwen3-235B jobs** — `test_qwen3_instruct.py` (BF16), `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py` (FP8) on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, and `test_qwen3_instruct_mxfp4.py` (`amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`, TP4 + EP2) on MI35x, across *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is well covered without them: - **Per-commit, on both ROCm lanes**, `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` runs on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` in the `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite, quantizes `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` with `--quantization mxfp4` and asserts `gsm8k >= 0.89`. That suite is dispatched by `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0 container) *and* `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (`--rocm-version rocm720`), so the MXFP4 MoE kernels for this architecture's shapes are checked on every PR against both ROCm versions, not once a night against one. This is why the removal applies to the ROCm 7.0 nightly as well as 7.2: neither lane is left without a substitute. - **Nightly**, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py` and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. - Serialized Quark MXFP4 *checkpoint loading* is covered by the Qwen3.8 job added here plus the DeepSeek-R1, GLM-5 and Kimi-K3 nightlies. What loses its substitute is the combination rather than any single ingredient: a pre-quantized Quark checkpoint on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale over TP4 + EP2. The per-commit test quantizes online at TP1, and expert parallelism survives nightly only through the MiniMax jobs — no Qwen job exercises EP after this. That is the deliberate trade for four 8-GPU jobs per night — two per nightly, each capped at `timeout-minutes: 120`, two on the `linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang` pool and two on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. The jobs removed are `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b[-rocm720]` and `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, along with their `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` dependencies in each workflow. Their three test files then join the other registered-but-undispatched AMD nightly tests noted below. ### Out of scope After this change, a scan turns up **36 AMD nightly test files** registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — the three Qwen3-235B tests above plus 33 pre-existing ones, mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left untouched here. One is worth calling out for whoever picks that up: `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` is not merely dormant but unrunnable — `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has no `setup_profile_directory()` and `run_benchmark_for_model` takes no `enable_profile=`, so `test_b_perf` would `AttributeError` on its first line, and its model paths are runner-local `/data/amd/` directories rather than HuggingFace ids. It is deliberately left unmodified by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests **Validation run:** [Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2) #32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) — dispatched on this branch's head with `job_select: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720`, so it covers both the accuracy and perf phases. Job selection resolves as intended: `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` is the only active job, the other 45 are skipped, and no `qwen3-235b` job exists at this SHA, confirming the removal took effect. An earlier dispatch (#32185767315) predated the perf phase and was cancelled in its favour. Expect a long run: the 1.2 TB checkpoint has to be fetched onto the runner cache, and both nightlies fire at `30 17 * * *` and drain the same `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` pool, so a manual dispatch queues behind their MI35x backlog. The gate is `ACCURACY_THRESHOLD = 0.93`, ~5% below AMD's published 0.9749 — the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.yaml` uses `rtol: 0.05` against 0.9704, i.e. a 0.922 floor). The threshold is inherited from AMD's measurement rather than from a run on the CI fleet, so if the dispatch lands materially off 0.9749 on the CI image, the number should be recalibrated to the observed run the way the Kimi-K3 job was. No model or kernel code is touched by this PR, so there is no output-affecting change to validate beyond the job itself. Static checks, run locally without GPUs: both workflows parse and every `check-all-jobs` dependency resolves to a defined job, with no `job_select` option pointing at a removed one; the AST registry parser resolves the new file to `backend=AMD, suite='nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4', nightly=True, est_time=14400` and no file under `test/` other than the new one differs from `main`; the suite string matches across all three files with no stale references to the pre-rename name; and every symbol the new test imports exists in its source module. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, isort, black, ruff and codespell all pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The perf phase is the speed coverage this PR adds; it publishes a latency / input-throughput / output-throughput / ITL table to the job summary rather than asserting a threshold, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Batch sizes and sequence lengths are overridable through the usual `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS` environment variables. Net runner impact: one new MI35x job added, four 8-GPU jobs removed (two per nightly, split across the mi300 and mi35x pools). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe; no doc change needed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signals.title: [Fix] DCP: reject fa3 for MLA and stop defaulting to it on Hopper
signals.text: > Stacked on #35298 (base: `fix-dcp-args-validation`). This PR's own diff is the last commit; GitHub will retarget it to `main` once #35298 merges. ## Motivation `fa3` has no DCP decode path for MLA models: it returns no LSE for the cross-dcp-rank reduction, so `forward_mla`'s `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` unpacks two values from a single return and a `--dcp-size > 1` run dies at decode cuda-graph capture with `ValueError: too many values to unpack` — far from the actual misconfiguration. `fa3` is also the **Hopper MLA auto-default**, so every Hopper DCP launch without an explicit `--attention-backend` hits this. Blackwell is unaffected because its MLA default is already `flashinfer`, which carries the DCP metadata. ## Modifications - `_handle_dcp_validation`: reject an explicit `fa3` (`--attention-backend` or `--decode-attention-backend`) with `dcp_size > 1` on MLA models, naming DCP-aware alternatives. Prefill-only disaggregation workers are exempt — they never run the DCP decode path. - `_get_default_attn_backend`: Hopper MLA under DCP defaults to `flashinfer` instead of `fa3`, matching the Blackwell branch. No working configuration changes behavior: the rejected combination previously crashed at capture, and the default change replaces a guaranteed crash with a backend that works. ## Verification - Reproduced on 4x H200 with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (`tp=4 dcp=4`): the capture crash on the fa3 auto-default, and a clean start on `flashinfer`. - **Unit tests** (`TestDcpAttentionBackend`): verified red on pre-fix code, green post-fix. Negative branches pin that prefill-only workers and MHA models still accept fa3, and that the non-DCP Hopper MLA default stays `fa3`. - `pre-commit run` passes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation as needed. - [x] Provide verification results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194002702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194002702)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194002504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194002504)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(moe): handle bf16 DeepEP low_latency dispatch (a_scales=None) in cutlass W4A8
signals.text: ### Problem `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_ll()` unconditionally calls `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton(x_scale=a_scales, ...)`. Under DeepEP **low_latency**, the cutlass W4A8 backend dispatches in **bf16** (its default; also forced by `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype bf16`), so the dispatch returns bf16 tokens with **no per-token fp8 scales** — `a_scales is None`. The unconditional call then dereferences `None`: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size' ``` at decode cuda-graph capture → scheduler dies (exit -3). Hit on Kimi-K3-W4AFP8 with `--deepep-mode auto` (normal prefill + low_latency decode), cuda-graph ON. ### Fix When `a_scales is None`, quantize the bf16 masked tokens to per-tensor fp8 in-place with the static input scale via `per_tensor_quant_fp8(...)` — byte-for-byte the same quantization `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal()` already applies to its bf16 input. Forcing fp8 dispatch instead is not a general fix: the per-token triton kernel asserts `hidden % 1024 == 0`, which fails for models whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible (e.g. Kimi-K3 = 3584). ### Validation mini-K3 (2 nodes, EP16, `--deepep-mode auto`, cuda-graph ON) passes decode capture and serves completions without the crash. Draft pending upstream CI + a full multi-node run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190125293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125293)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190125037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125037)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Kernel] Tune Kimi-K3 Marlin MoE block sizes on H200
signals.text: ## Summary Tune the Marlin MoE `BLOCK_SIZE_M` selector for the documented Kimi-K3 H200 deployment topologies: - TP16 / EP16: 896 global experts, 56 local experts per rank, top-k 16 - TP32 / EP32: 896 global experts, 28 local experts per rank, top-k 16 Kimi-K3's H200 recipes explicitly use `--moe-runner-backend marlin`, so Triton fused-MoE JSON configs are not consulted. This change adds H200-only Marlin block-size tables while preserving the existing heuristic for every other device and shape. Base commit: `955704544c` ## Environment - 2x NVIDIA H200 - PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime `13.0` - CUDA compiler `13.1` - Triton `3.6.0` - Python `3.12` ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH=python export CPATH=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12 cd "$ROOT" ``` ## Tuning commands The benchmark uses random packed MXFP4 weights with Kimi-K3's exact rank-local dimensions: - hidden size: 3584 (`routed_expert_hidden_size`) - intermediate size: 3072 - global experts: 896 - top-k: 16 - remote expert ids mapped to the standard dispatcher's `-1` sentinel - three repetitions per candidate; each repetition is the median of 30 timed calls after 10 warmups Both H200s were used concurrently: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 1 4 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --blocks 8 16 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 30 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-extended-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 1 4 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --blocks 8 16 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 30 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-extended-tp32.json ``` Large-token fallback validation: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 8192 16384 \ --blocks 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 5 \ --iterations 20 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-tail-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 8192 16384 \ --blocks 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 5 \ --iterations 20 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-tail-tp32.json ``` ## Final baseline versus tuned validation The baseline forces the previous heuristic's block. The tuned path calls the selector normally, including the new H200 table. Each result is the median of three repetitions, with 50 timed calls per repetition after 10 warmups. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_kimi_k3_marlin_tuning.py \ --tuner /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 50 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-final-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_kimi_k3_marlin_tuning.py \ --tuner /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 50 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-final-tp32.json ``` ### TP16 / EP16 | Tokens | Baseline block | Tuned block | Baseline (ms) | Tuned (ms) | Reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32 | 16 | 8 | 0.285248 | 0.270016 | 5.34% | | 64 | 32 | 8 | 0.593280 | 0.446304 | 24.77% | | 128 | 48 | 8 | 0.742240 | 0.479968 | 35.34% | | 256 | 64 | 16 | 0.910304 | 0.551712 | 39.39% | | 512 | 64 | 16 | 0.987008 | 0.653952 | 33.74% | | 1024 | 64 | 32 | 1.136192 | 0.903392 | 20.49% | | 2048 | 64 | 48 | 1.431456 | 1.308736 | 8.57% | | 4096 | 64 | 48 | 2.846432 | 2.584288 | 9.21% | ### TP32 / EP32 | Tokens | Baseline block | Tuned block | Baseline (ms) | Tuned (ms) | Reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 32 | 32 | 8 | 0.317440 | 0.242080 | 23.74% | | 64 | 48 | 8 | 0.394720 | 0.260736 | 33.94% | | 128 | 64 | 16 | 0.478624 | 0.290528 | 39.30% | | 256 | 64 | 16 | 0.519264 | 0.345600 | 33.44% | | 512 | 64 | 32 | 0.594496 | 0.475520 | 20.01% | | 1024 | 64 | 48 | 0.745024 | 0.681664 | 8.50% | | 2048 | 64 | 48 | 1.452384 | 1.311200 | 9.72% | | 4096 | 64 | 64 | 2.422336 | 2.421856 | 0.02% | The maximum relative L2 difference observed between the previous and tuned block schedules was `9.20e-05`. ## Kimi-K2.7-Code audit Kimi-K2.7-Code uses compressed-tensors INT4 W4A16 with Marlin at the documented H200 TP8 topology (`E=384`, rank-local intermediate size `256`, top-k 8). ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-k27-gpu1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k27_marlin_block_size.py \ --tokens 1 4 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 30 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k27-sweep.json ``` No K2.7 config is added: - The existing selector was already optimal at the H200 default 8192-token prefill chunk. - It was also optimal at the broadly useful 32-2048 token points. - Block 48 improved the isolated 4096-token point by about 14%, but regressed 3072 tokens by about 42% on both H200s, so a narrow override would not be robust. Kimi-K2.6 was released on April 14, 2026 and was excluded by the post-April model cutoff. ## Non-quantized audit - Kimi-K2.7-Code has no official non-quantized checkpoint; the official checkpoint is compressed-tensors INT4. - Kimi-K3 has no official non-quantized checkpoint; routed experts are MXFP4. - Kimi-K3's unquantized shared experts are separate dense MLPs and do not use this Marlin MoE block-size selector. ## Tests Block-selection tests: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" \ test/registered/quant/test_marlin_moe.py \ TestMarlinMoeBlockSizeSelection ``` Full Marlin MoE GPU tests: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-tests \ "$VENV/bin/python" \ test/registered/quant/test_marlin_moe.py \ TestFusedMarlinMoe ``` Result: 2 tests passed in 649.064 seconds. Focused lint: ```bash uvx pre-commit run --files \ python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/fused_marlin_moe.py \ test/registered/quant/test_marlin_moe.py ``` All focused pre-commit hooks passed. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191093029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191093029)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191092794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191092794)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
