signals.title: [AMD] Qualify ROCm 7.2.4 for the profiler: HIP-graph capture probe + libdrm-amdgpu prerequisite
signals.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo report that on every `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 image (v0.5.12 through v0.5.17, `*-rocm720-*`), `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph, and they have been patching `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` / `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200` out of a ROCm 7.2.4 install to work around it. This PR is the ROCm 7.2.4 evaluation that request asked for: it adds the check that decides whether a candidate image traces graph-launched kernels, and fixes the one image-level prerequisite that a 7.2.4 base introduces. The report now reproduces on MI355X. Profiling ten decode steps of gpt-oss-20b-bf16 through `/start_profile`, the shipped `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x` image records 513 device kernels where a 7.2.4 image built from this branch records 3933 on an identical workload — 87% of decode kernels never reach the trace. Numbers and method are in the test plan. The report is confirmed upstream, and the fix is already released: - ROCTracer can fail to report kernel operations: [ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), closed with "Resolved in ROCm 7.2.2". - ROCm 7.2.0's HIP runtime also has a wrong doorbell index in `dispatchGenericAqlPacketBatch` (the graph batch-dispatch path) plus an InterceptQueue ring-buffer heap corruption, both fixed in 7.2.1 ([pytorch/pytorch#177873](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177873)). That matches the `CUDAGraph::replay` deadlock inside `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` seen in our own CI (#34452), which is the same bug class surfacing as a hang instead of a gap. - The candidate base carries the fixed libraries: `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_*` ships `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204` and `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204` (`hip-runtime-amd` 7.2.26015.70200 -> 7.2.53211.70204, `roctracer` 4.1.70200 -> 4.1.70204). So the ROCm patch bump is what fixes this, and it does not require the torch/Python upgrade: AMD publishes `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1`, which matches our current rocm720 stack (Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10, torch 2.9.1) with only the ROCm patch level changed. #30984 remains the vehicle for the rocm724 flavors; nothing here competes with it. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` — libdrm-amdgpu is a prerequisite for any 7.2.4 base The step that fixes empty `hipDeviceGetName` results skipped every `*rocm720*` flavor on the grounds that "ROCm 7.2 base images already ship these packages". That is a property of how the base installed ROCm, not of its version, and it does not hold for 7.2.4: | base image | ROCm install | AMD libdrm + `amdgpu.ids` | | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | `amdgpu-install --usecase=rocm` | yes (`/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids`, `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/20-amdgpu.conf`) | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | `apt-get install rocm` | no | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0` (used by #30984) | `apt-get install rocm` | no | Verified from the registry manifests and layer listings, and measured on an MI355X. The only `amdgpu.ids` left in a 7.2.4 image is the distro's, from `libdrm-common`, and what that costs depends on the release: | base | AMD libdrm | distro `amdgpu.ids` | `get_device_name(0)` on MI355X | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_*` (today's rocm720) | yes | 10962 B, no `74A*`/`75A*` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_*` | no | 10962 B, no `74A*`/`75A*` | `''` | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_*` (used by #30984) | no | 23250 B, `74A0`/`74A1`/`74A2`, no `75A*` | `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` | Ubuntu 24.04's table does carry the MI300 series, so a noble 7.2.4 base resolves MI300X and degrades only on MI355X — and it degrades to a generic vendor string rather than an empty one, which is worse to detect because anything testing for a missing name sees a non-empty result. Either way every device-name-keyed tuned config (fused MoE Triton configs, K3 SP collective tables, `moe_front` configs) silently misses. `graphics/7.2.4` publishes the packages, and its `libdrm-amdgpu-common` lists `74A1 AMD Instinct MI300X` and `75A3 AMD Instinct MI355X`. The step now tests for `/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` and derives the graphics repo (`x.y.z`, falling back to `x.y`) plus the codename from the image itself, with an `AMDGPU_GRAPHICS_VERSION` build-arg override. Behaviour for the flavors on main is unchanged: 7.2.0 still skips, and 7.0 still installs from `graphics/7.0 jammy`. Note for #30984: it extends the skip to `*rocm724*` on a noble 7.2.4 base, which ships a `gfx950-rocm724` image reporting `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` — measured on its exact base image, details in [that PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5336201854). This commit makes that arm unnecessary. ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` — the acceptance check `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts that the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it. The probe closes that gap: it captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and compares the device kernels in the exported trace against the number launched. An eager control run separates "cannot trace graph replay" from "cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because 7.2.0 can wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch` rather than merely lose events. It also prints the ROCm version, the mapped HIP/tracing sonames, and warns when the device name does not identify the part (the libdrm gap above) — on an Instinct arch that means anything without an Instinct model in it, so the generic `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` a noble 7.2.4 base reports on MI355X trips it as surely as an empty string does. Two measured properties of the failure decide how the check is built, and getting either wrong makes the probe pass a broken image: - **The loss is partial, not total.** A 7.2.0 image that drops 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels still writes a trace full of kernels, so the verdict compares traced against launched rather than asking whether any arrived. The eager control is held to the same completeness bar, which keeps a runtime that drops events generally distinct from one that only loses graph events. - **It only appears past a graph size.** A four-node capture traces completely on 7.2.0. The default capture is 64 kernels (`--graph-nodes`), where 7.2.0 reports 448 of 512 and 7.2.4 reports 512 of 512, ten runs out of ten on each. ``` torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4 (hip 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a), rocm 7.2.0 device: 'AMD Instinct MI355X' (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) hip/tracing libs: libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200, libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.70200, librocprofiler-register.so.0.6.0, libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200 eager launch: 512/512 kernels traced, 11246 us device time, 6213 trace events graph replay: 448/512 kernels traced, 3983 us device time, 1005 trace events VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches trace completely but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reach it. This is the roctracer reporting failure fixed in ROCm 7.2.2 (https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102). Profile with --disable-cuda-graph on this image, or move to a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. ``` Deliberately not registered in CI yet: on today's rocm720 images it is expected to fail, and (per #34452) it can take the process down with it. It should be registered in the AMD suites once the images move to a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime, at which point it guards the behaviour permanently. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Document the known gap for users on the current images, how to check an image, and the `--disable-cuda-graph` workaround, with the caveat that decode numbers collected that way exclude the replay path. ## Accuracy Tests No model-facing code changes. The Dockerfile change affects image contents only; it makes `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` resolve on 7.2.4 bases, which restores tuned-config selection rather than altering kernels. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the change itself. On the current 7.2.0 images the reported symptom is that decode kernels are absent from traces; the probe is the measurement that qualifies a fixed image. ## Test plan Local, without GPU access: - Every branch of the new Dockerfile shell logic exercised in a sandbox with stubbed apt: base with `amdgpu.ids` skips; ROCm 7.2.4 resolves `graphics/7.2.4`; ROCm 7.0.0 falls back to `graphics/7.0` (matching today's hardcoded values); missing version info fails with an actionable error; `AMDGPU_GRAPHICS_VERSION` overrides. Repo URLs and package availability checked against repo.radeon.com. - Dockerfile parses as a single `RUN` instruction (`dockerfile-parse`). - Probe: trace parsing validated against a real `export_chrome_trace` output plus synthetic device events, all verdict paths (pass, eager-blind, eager-incomplete, graph hang, graph crash, graph incomplete) exercised with canned phase results, and the timeout path's process-group kill verified. On a host with no GPU it reports `environment: unusable` and exits 1. On hardware — 8x MI355X (gfx950), KMD 6.16.13, this branch merged with #35398 (clean merge), plus a `gfx950-rocm724` image built from that tree: | image | ROCm | probe | graph replay | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | 7.2.0 | FAIL | 448/512 | | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818` | 7.2.0 | FAIL | 448/512 | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | 7.2.4 | PASS | 512/512 | | built from this branch, `gfx950-rocm724` | 7.2.4 | PASS | 512/512 | Five repeats on each SGLang image gave identical counts, so the check does not flake. The eager control traces 512/512 on both runtimes at every graph size tried (4 through 1024 nodes), which is what places the loss on graph replay rather than on profiling generally. The user-facing symptom, on a real decode rather than the microbenchmark — gpt-oss-20b-bf16, triton attention backend, `/start_profile` with `num_steps=10`. The two graph-enabled runs agree exactly on 3520 `cpu_op`, 1993 `cuda_runtime` and 63 graph replays, so only the runtime differs: | run | device kernel events in trace | | --- | --- | | ROCm 7.2.0 shipped image, CUDA graphs on | 513 | | ROCm 7.2.0 shipped image, `--disable-cuda-graph` | 3924 | | ROCm 7.2.4 built from this branch, CUDA graphs on | 3933 | That is the reported bug, the documented workaround recovering from it, and the 7.2.4 image recovering from it with graphs left on. libdrm, on the same host, and the warning that reports it: | image | device name | probe warns | | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_*` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | no | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_*` | `''` | yes | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_*` | `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` | yes | | built from this branch, `gfx950-rocm724` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | no | The built image takes `/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` from `graphics/7.2.4` and copies it to `/usr/share/libdrm/`, where it lists both `74A1` and `75A3`. Not covered: gfx942 / MI300X, for want of the hardware. The nightly in #35398 probes both generations. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- The new probe is the test; it cannot be registered until the images ship a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. --> - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. signals.title: [AMD][CI] Prune dead Qwen coverage from the AMD nightly
signals.text: ## Motivation Two pieces of AMD nightly Qwen coverage that are not paying for themselves. **1. `test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` has never run and could not run.** It registers the suite `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`, and that name appears nowhere else in the repo — no workflow dispatches it by `--suite`, no job invokes the file by path, and it is absent from `NIGHTLY_SUITES`. Consistent with never having executed, it is also broken as written: the perf phase calls `runner.setup_profile_directory()` and passes `enable_profile=` to `run_benchmark_for_model`, and `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has neither, so it would `AttributeError` on the first line of `test_b_perf`. It additionally points at local `/data/amd/` checkpoints rather than HuggingFace ids, so it would not resolve weights on a fresh runner either. **2. The MI30x Qwen3-235B job duplicates architecture coverage that survives elsewhere.** `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` runs `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507` in BF16 and FP8 on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, in *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies, for ~1h each. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` keeps a nightly heartbeat without it — `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py`, and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. ## Modifications **Deleted** `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`, plus `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_instruct.py` and `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py`, which fed the removed suite. Removing the job without removing its test files would just move them into the registered-but-undispatched pile rather than out of it. **Removed** the `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` / `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b-rocm720` job from `nightly-test-amd.yml` and `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, along with its `job_select` option and `check-all-jobs` dependency in each. **Kept** the MI35x MXFP4 job (`nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, serving `amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`). It is the only coverage of MXFP4 on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` anywhere in the AMD nightly — the other MXFP4 jobs pair that quantization with DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Qwen3.5-family architectures — and the only Qwen MoE job exercising `--ep 2`. The section comments were retitled from `8-GPU Qwen3-235B (MI30x + MI35x MXFP4)` to `8-GPU Qwen3-235B-MXFP4 (MI35x only)` with a note recording why the MI30x half went away. ### What this trades away The removal gives up `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale and its FP8 path, in exchange for roughly 2h of 8-GPU mi300 time per night across the two nightlies. That is the deliberate call here rather than an oversight; if the FP8 path at scale turns out to matter, the cheaper restoration is a single mi300 job in the ROCm 7.2 nightly only, not both. ### Out of scope While verifying that these removals did not orphan anything, a broader scan turned up **32 other AMD nightly test files** that are registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left alone here. Unlike the file deleted in this PR they are not known to be broken, and several look deliberately parked for occasional manual dispatch. Worth a follow-up pass to either wire them up or retire them, but not mixed into this change. ## Accuracy Tests No product code is touched; this only removes CI jobs and test files. Verified locally: both workflows still parse as YAML; no `check-all-jobs` dependency references a job that no longer exists; no `job_select` option references a missing job; no reference to the removed suite, jobs, or deleted filenames remains anywhere in the tree; and the three deleted files were confirmed against `origin/main` to have never been invoked by path from any workflow. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py` and codespell pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The net effect is ~2h/night less 8-GPU mi300 occupancy. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — removal-only PR; no new tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing docs cover these CI jobs. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190432995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190432995)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190432913](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190432913)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [CI] Skip fast-fail for scheduled stages
signals.text: ## Summary - Skip the cross-job PR health fast-fail when a reusable test stage is invoked with `scheduled: true`. - Keep the existing skip behavior for explicit health-check bypasses, parallel dispatches, and run-all requests. ## Root cause Release Branch Cut invokes the nightly workflow through `workflow_dispatch`. The reusable stage therefore cannot rely on `github.event_name == 'schedule'`. Although the nightly workflow passes `scheduled: true`, `SKIP_PR_TEST_HEALTH_CHECK` previously ignored that input, so later nightly jobs could cascade fast-fail after an earlier failure. ## Impact Nightly and weekly stages using `inputs.scheduled` will continue running to collect all failures. Regular PR stages retain fast-fail behavior. ## Validation - Evaluated the workflow expression for regular PR, scheduled, explicit skip, parallel dispatch, and run-all inputs. - Ran `actionlint -ignore SC2086 .github/workflows/_pr-test-stage.yml`. - Ran repository pre-commit checks. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190496623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190496623)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190496419](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190496419)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Stop unparsed Kimi K3 template syntax from leaking into responses
signals.text: ## Motivation Kimi K3 emits its channels (`<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, `<|open|>call ...`, `<|close|>message<|sep|>`, ...) as literal text, so any path that does not run the tool-call parser hands that syntax straight to the client. Two such paths exist today: - **Parsing disabled.** With `tool_choice="none"` or no tools, `serving_chat` / `serving_responses` skip the parser and `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream` returns `full_text` verbatim. Measured on a K3 deployment: ~10% of `tool_choice="none"` completions came back containing a raw tools section. - **Truncation.** `KimiK3Detector.has_tool_call` is `self.bot_token in text`, so output cut mid-marker (`...<|open|>too`) misses detection and `parse_non_stream` again returns the raw text. With small `max_output_tokens` this reproduced in 97-100% of samples. Separately, `ResponsesRequest._normalize_input_item_for_validation` defaults the SDK-required `input_image.detail` only under `item["content"]`. Tool-output items carry their parts under `item["output"]`, so an image tool result without `detail` (what Codex sends) fails validation with a 400. ## Modifications - `base_format_detector.py`: two identity-by-default hooks, `strip_template_artifacts(text, reasoning_separated)` and `strip_template_markers(text)`. Formats whose tool channel is literal text override them; every other detector is unaffected. - `kimik3_detector.py`: implements both. Artifact stripping cuts from an unparsed `TOOLS_OPEN` / `CALL_OPEN` onward, drops the think channel when a reasoning parser already routed the trace to its own field, unwraps the response channel, and removes whole and cut-off markers. Marker stripping only removes syntax, keeping the text it wrapped — used for reasoning content. - `kimik3_format.py`: `ALL_MARKERS`, `ARGUMENT_OPEN`, and a `min_len` on `partial_suffix_len` so a reply legitimately ending in `<` is not truncated. - `function_call_parser.py`: the two paths that returned `full_text` unchanged (no tools, detection missed) now route it through `strip_template_artifacts`. - `serving_chat.py` / `serving_responses.py`: apply the hooks to non-streaming assistant text and reasoning content, regardless of whether parsing ran. A Responses turn whose text was nothing but syntax still emits an `output_text` item (empty) rather than an output array with no message. - `utils.py`: `align_token_logprobs_to_text`. The cleanup is pure span deletion, so the cleaned text is a subsequence of the concatenated tokens; entries whose token was removed are dropped, and the array becomes `None` if the two cannot be reconciled rather than being returned misaligned. Applied only when cleanup actually changed the text, so logprobs on paths this PR does not touch are unchanged. - `protocol.py`: normalize `input_image.detail` under `output` as well as `content`. Streaming is out of scope: the chunk handlers can still emit markers verbatim, and fixing that needs cross-chunk marker buffering. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward or kernels — this only affects post-generation text handling in the OpenAI entrypoints. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A; the added work is a few regex passes over the response text. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191148180](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191148180)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191147947](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191147947)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: model_loader: only open the MTP-head shards for a NextN/MTP draft load
signals.text: ## Motivation An EAGLE/MTP **NextN draft** is loaded from the **same combined checkpoint** as the target, so `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` hands it **every shard in the safetensors index** — the whole checkpoint — even though the draft consumes only the appended NextN layer: - `embed_tokens` / `shared_head.head` are **shared from the already-resident target** (`deepseek_weight_loader` skips them: `if "shared_head.head" in name or "embed_tokens" in name: continue`), not read from disk; - every other tensor is skipped by the NextN weight loader (`if not name.startswith(layer_prefix): continue`) **after** the iterator has already opened the file. Net: a small draft head **re-opens the full multi-hundred-GB checkpoint** — wasted I/O, and a misleading full-checkpoint-size weight-load progress bar on the draft. On a real MTP model (`GlmMoeDsa*`-family, 78 layers + 1 NextN layer, FP4, EAGLE), the NextN head lives in **3 of 47 shards** but the draft opened all 47. ## Modifications Add `maybe_filter_nextn_shards` (weight_utils.py), called right next to `maybe_add_mtp_safetensors` in `DefaultModelLoader._get_weights_iterator`. For a **draft** config it restricts the shard list to just the shard(s) holding the MTP head. Deliberately conservative: - **Draft-only** — acts only when the architecture ends in `NextN` / `MTP`; **target loads are untouched**. - **Checkpoint-discovered MTP layer** — finds the MTP layer by the NextN-only modules it carries (`eh_proj` / `enorm` / `hnorm` / `shared_head`), **not** config arithmetic, since some archs rewrite `num_hidden_layers` (e.g. Longcat resets it to the nextn count). A wrong guess can **never drop needed weights**: no markers / no index / no reduction ⇒ the list is returned unchanged. - **Keeps index-undescribed files** — e.g. a separately-added `mtp.safetensors` (the `maybe_add_mtp_safetensors` path) is never dropped. Runs before the weights iterator is chosen, so it benefits every safetensors load path for NextN drafts. ## Accuracy Tests No output impact: the NextN draft loads the **identical** head weights — the same tensors the loader already kept. This change only avoids *opening* shards whose tensors the NextN loader already skips (target body / main-model layers), so the resulting model state is unchanged. Verified in production: the draft reaches ready and serves normally. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on a production MTP deployment (`GlmMoeDsa*` FP4, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE`, 8×B200, cold node), before vs after this change — **same target, same node class**: | Phase | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Target (`role=main`) load | 47.83 s | 47.79 s (unchanged) | | **Draft (`role=draft`) load** | **41.51 s** | **4.29 s** (**9.7× faster**) | | Draft shards opened | 47 / 47 | **3 / 47** | | Draft weight-load bar total | 433 GB | **23.4 GB** | The log confirms the narrowing: > `NextN draft load: restricting 47 checkpoint shard(s) to the 3 holding MTP layer(s) ['78'] (target body skipped).` The target load is unchanged (confirming the filter is draft-only); the draft speedup comes entirely from not re-reading the target body. The win scales with checkpoint size and node coldness. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit (pre-commit run passes: black / isort / ruff / codespell). - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_utils.py::TestMaybeFilterNextnShards`): draft → MTP-only shards, target untouched, `num_hidden_layers`-rewrite safety, separately-added `mtp.safetensors` kept, no-marker / no-index no-ops. - [ ] Update documentation — n/a (internal loader optimization, no user-facing flags). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. --- *Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); validated in production as shown above.* <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191339576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191339576)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191339452](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191339452)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [AMD] Gate the ROCm 7.2.4 nightly on the MI300X/MI355X profiling probe
signals.text: > **Scope reduced.** This PR originally added the `rocm724` Dockerfile stages, a `relax_torch_triton_pin.py` metadata patch, a separate rocm724 nightly, and the tagged-release matrix entry. #30984 provides all four, has green `gfx942-rocm724` and `gfx950-rocm724` release builds, and is going in first. What it does not have is any check that a published 7.2.4 image actually traces graph-launched kernels, which is the only reason the flavor exists. That gate is all this PR is now. ## Motivation ROCm 7.2.0 drops kernel-dispatch events for work submitted through `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in 7.2.2), and SGLang decodes from replayed graphs, so a `torch.profiler` trace shows the host-side launch with no GPU kernels under it. That is what AMD/Silo report against every `*-rocm720-*` image, and recovering it is what the 7.2.4 flavors are for. Measured on an MI355X, profiling ten decode steps of gpt-oss-20b-bf16 through `/start_profile` on an identical workload: | image | device kernel events in trace | | --- | --- | | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`, CUDA graphs on | 513 | | same image, `--disable-cuda-graph` | 3924 | | a `gfx950-rocm724` image, CUDA graphs on | 3933 | Nothing in CI would notice if a published 7.2.4 image lost that again. `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it. ## Modifications ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml` #30984 extends this nightly to build all four ROCm 7.2 flavors, and its `publish` job pushes to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` directly. This splits that push into a `promote` job and puts the probe between them: | job | runner | what it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `publish` | `amd-docker-scale` | unchanged, minus the lmsys push: builds and pushes `rocm/sgl-dev:v<version>-rocm7??-mi3?x-<date>` | | `probe` | `linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang`, `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` | runs `check_hip_graph_profiling.py` inside each 7.2.4 image, on the GPU it targets | | `promote` | `amd-docker-scale` | republishes to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`, requiring a passing probe for the 7.2.4 flavors | Points worth a reviewer's attention: - **Only the 7.2.4 flavors are gated.** The rocm720 images run the runtime that has the bug and would never pass; they promote exactly as before. The gate is a step inside `promote` conditioned on the flavor, not a job-level dependency, so a 7.2.4 regression cannot hold back a 7.2.0 image. - **gfx942 is probed on MI300X and gfx950 on MI355X**, because the behaviour lives in the HIP runtime rather than in SGLang and is worth confirming per device generation. - **Promotion stays per-leg.** `promote` runs under `always()`, so a leg whose build failed has no tag artifact and fails at its own download rather than blocking the legs that did publish. That preserves today's behaviour, where the lmsys push lived inside each `publish` leg. - **The probe job installs no dependencies.** It exercises the image's own torch and HIP runtime, which is the thing under test. - **`workflow_dispatch` takes a `probe_image`**, which qualifies an already-published image without a rebuild, on the GPU its `gpu_arch` selects. That is the cheap way to answer "does this candidate trace graph replay", and pointing it at a `*-rocm720-mi35x` tag is the negative control. ## Accuracy Tests No model, kernel, or image-content changes. This PR is a CI workflow only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Recovering profiling is the point, and the gate is the measurement: the nightly refuses to promote a 7.2.4 image whose graph-replay kernels do not reach the trace. ## Test plan Local: - Workflow parses; job graph is `publish -> probe -> promote`; job names pass `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`. - The probe matrix expression evaluated against every dispatch case. Scheduled runs and `gpu_arch=all` probe both 7.2.4 flavors; `gpu_arch=gfx950-rocm724` probes that one; `gpu_arch=gfx942-rocm720` and `gfx950-rocm720` yield an empty matrix, so the probe is skipped and the rocm720 legs promote ungated. On hardware — 8x MI355X (gfx950), KMD 6.16.13 — running the gate's command against a `gfx950-rocm724` image built from #30984's stages plus #35390: ``` eager launch: 512/512 kernels traced, 11283 us device time, 6213 trace events graph replay: 512/512 kernels traced, 4533 us device time, 1133 trace events VERDICT: PASS -- all 512 graph-replay kernels reach the trace. ``` and against the shipped rocm720 image, which is the negative control the `probe_image` dispatch is for: ``` graph replay: 448/512 kernels traced, 3983 us device time, 1005 trace events VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches trace completely but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reach it. ``` Five repeats on each gave identical counts, so the gate does not flake. Not covered: gfx942 / MI300X, for want of the hardware — the `probe` job's MI300X leg is unexercised until this runs in CI. ## Notes for reviewers - **Stacked on #30984.** It supplies the `rocm724` stages this gate probes and the four-flavor nightly this edits. Until it lands, the diff here shows its commits too. - **Also needs #35390**, which adds `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` — the gate's command — and the libdrm fix that makes `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` resolve on a 7.2.4 base. On #30984's noble base a `gfx950-rocm724` image reports `'AMD Radeon Graphics'`; see [that thread](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5336201854). - **Dropped from this PR as redundant with #30984:** the `gfx942-rocm724` / `gfx950-rocm724` stages, `scripts/ci/amd/relax_torch_triton_pin.py` (its `patch_torch_triton_requirement.py` handles `triton-rocm` and re-pins to the installed version, which is what the torch 2.11 stack needs), the standalone `release-docker-amd-rocm724-nightly.yml`, and the `rocm724` entry in `release-docker-amd.yml`. - Follow-up, not here: teach `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh` to resolve `--rocm-version rocm724` images, and register `check_hip_graph_profiling.py` in the AMD suites once the images run a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime, at which point it guards the behaviour on every PR rather than only at publish time. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- CI workflow only; the probe it runs is added in #35390. --> - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). <!-- Documented in #35390. --> - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32194584123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194584123)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194583932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194583932)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [GDN] Route Qwen TP4 decode and verify rows through Cake
signals.text: ## Summary - lazily load the optional public FlashInfer Cake GDN decode package on SM100/SM103 - fail closed on unsupported dtype, layout, shape, stride, state-pool, or graph-capture combinations - preserve caller-stream and CUDA graph semantics with preallocated workspace/state and cached FP32 dt bias - route the actual Qwen3-Next TP4 BF16 decode and verify rows through the promoted tile16 full-warp kernels ## Qualification - rebased onto current SGLang main b814a7e812fb9367d994af307085bd30de329f96 - B200/SM100, job 3752127 on umbriel-b200-037: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including actual TP4 eager and CUDA Graph paths - GB300/SM103, job 510532 on nvl72d093-T03: 9 tests passed and 26 subtests passed, including the same paths - exact route IDs: cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_t1.tile16_fullwarp and cake.gdn_decode.indexed_bf16_verify_t4.tile16_fullwarp - exact TP4 shapes: B=4,T=1,H=4,HV=8 and B=8,T=4,H=4,HV=8 - same-environment cold-L2 CUPTI kernel A/B versus live FlashInfer 8044d94bf9: - B200 T1 0.003296 vs 0.003472 ms (1.053x), T4 0.006400 vs 0.006944 ms (1.085x), geometric mean 1.069x - GB300 T1 0.003040 vs 0.003296 ms (1.084x), T4 0.006304 vs 0.006736 ms (1.069x), geometric mean 1.076x - correctness uses fixed BF16 atol=rtol=1e-2; dual-arch public ABI/stream/graph and sanitizer gates pass - exact Qwen3-Next 80B FP8 TP4/MTP model replay, four GB300s, job 3137824: 4/4 tests pass; cache-hit KL 0.0007701/0.0017106 versus the fixed 0.0035 ceiling; all four TP ranks record the Cake T4 route during CUDA Graph capture - attributed serving ABBA, four GB300s, job 3137849: all eight measured 128-request rounds complete; four-round median output/total throughput 1.000280x, mean/median TPOT 1.003214x/1.005037x, and mean TTFT 0.987693x versus FlashInfer (the ~1.25% TTFT regression is retained explicitly) The PR remains Draft while the public FlashInfer dependency and broader delivery review remain open. ## Dependencies - FlashInfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4581 Supersedes #35328 because repository rules prohibit force-pushing its protected head branch after rebase. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194845350](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194845350)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194845119](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194845119)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Bugfix] Kimi-K3: fix vision-DP rank-local indexing into global grid_thws_host
signals.text: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3 with vision-DP sharding (observed on `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8` with DSPARK speculative decoding, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`), the first `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries **two or more images with different geometries** kills the scheduler: ``` ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids ``` The request returns 500 and the server never recovers — every subsequent request fails until the container is restarted. Single-image requests, and multi-image requests whose images share one NaViT grid, are unaffected — which is how this survives typical smoke tests. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`, `materialize_item_features(image_indices)` receives the **global** image indices assigned to this vision-DP rank, but the deferred-preprocessing block indexes `grid_thws_host` — a global tensor with one row per image in the batch — with the rank-**local** enumerate positions: ```python expected_grids = grid_thws_host[indices] # local idx into global tensor ... patch_counts = [int(grid_thws_host[index].prod().item()) for index in indices] # same bug ``` On any rank whose assigned images are not the global prefix `[0..k)`, the expected grids and patch split counts are read from the wrong rows. If the wrongly-read row happens to hold a different grid, the `torch.equal` sanity check fires and raises, taking the scheduler down. (The non-DP path passes `list(range(len(items)))`, where local == global, so it never triggers.) ## Fix Translate the local enumerate positions through the closure's `image_indices` before indexing `grid_thws_host`, in both the expected-grid comparison and the `patch_counts` split. No numeric effect on correct batches — the check now compares each produced grid against the row it was actually produced from. ## Accuracy Tests Deterministic repro: one chat completion with two images, 504×504 and 1344×756 (different NaViT grids), against a TP8/DCP8 B300 deployment. - **Before:** request returns 500, scheduler dead (`/health` times out until restart) — reproduced 2/2. - **After:** request returns 200 (14.8s cold) with a correct description of both images; `/health` stays 200; subsequent multimodal and text traffic unaffected. Model outputs for previously-working requests are unchanged: the patch only affects index bookkeeping inside a validation check, not any computed feature. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — two list-indexing expressions inside the deferred-preprocessing validation branch; no hot-path change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black/codespell clean; ruff `F401,F821,UP037` and isort report zero *new* findings vs the base revision of this file) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (A unit test for this path needs multi-GPU vision-DP; validated with the deterministic E2E repro above. Happy to add a mocked test if maintainers prefer.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194807740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194807740)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194807547](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194807547)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Spec] Route weight updates through the _draft_model_runners() guard
signals.text: ## Motivation `BaseSpecWorker.update_weights_from_disk` and `update_weights_from_ipc` iterate `self.draft_worker.draft_runners` directly. This dereference is unguarded: - **NGRAM** has no draft worker → `AttributeError` on any weight-update request while ngram speculation is enabled. - **DFlash family** exposes `model_runner` rather than `draft_runners`, so the current loop targets the wrong attribute there too. `BaseSpecWorker` already owns the correct abstraction for exactly this case: `_draft_model_runners()` returns `()` for ngram / frozen-kv-mtp / absent draft worker and maps the dflash family to its `model_runner`. ## Modifications Both update paths now iterate `self._draft_model_runners()` instead of `self.draft_worker.draft_runners` (2-line change, no new code paths): - ngram / frozen-kv-mtp: weight updates no longer crash; they correctly no-op over zero draft runners and return success. - dflash: the update reaches the actual draft `model_runner`. ## Accuracy Tests No model-forward changes; behavior is identical for the EAGLE family (where `_draft_model_runners()` returns exactly `draft_worker.draft_runners`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable (control-path only, executed once per weight-update request). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with `pre-commit run --all-files` - [x] Two-line change reusing an existing guard; no new dependencies 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_015bz4X1Dc9F6SQoV26ribYP <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32195486495](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195486495)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195486153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195486153)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [NVIDIA] Fix SM107 MXFP8 activation prep
signals.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107. GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path. The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path. The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available. - Preserve Kimi K3's existing fused route/quant handoff. - Preserve the existing Triton activation-quantization path on other SM10x architectures. - Preserve FlashInfer quantization for padded hidden dimensions. - Correct the FlashInfer custom-op fake scale-buffer size for both linear and swizzled layouts so `torch.compile` metadata matches the real quantizer. - Add CPU regression tests covering dispatch behavior, padded inputs, route handoff, and fake output shapes. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> * Validated GPT-OSS with real weights on SM107 with 4 focused regression tests passed on SM107. * Verified the fake quantizer reports the expected scale shape. * Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signals.title: [AMD] Kimi-K3 MoE front optimization
signals.text: ## Motivation 1. The weight of routed expert down proj and routed expert up proj is now bf16. Enabling MXFP4 online quantization for routed expert down proj and routed expert up proj can reduce memory overhead in high-concurrency/large-batch scenarios. Now enable MXFP4 quant when M > 2048 (basically enabled at the prefill stage). 2. MoE front is now using a torch.mm fallback to calculate the MoE front GEMM (shared expert gate up + routed expert down proj + gate); dispatch this to the aiter tuned GEMM instead. This part depends on aiter PR https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4834. ## Modifications 1. quantize latent MoE projections to MXFP4 on large batches (b801b07046) - New sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/latent_mxfp4_aiter_hip.py: pack bf16 weights to MXFP4 (pack), run the quantized GEMM (run), and gate availability on gfx950 (supported). - KimiK3MoE._prepare_moe_latent_mxfp4(): builds MXFP4 copies of the latent down_proj/up_proj weights at weight-load time (bf16 originals stay live for small batches). Handles all three front-merge layouts (three-way fused, EP [gate | latent down] pair, unmerged). - New env var SGLANG_K3_MOE_LATENT_MXFP4 (opt-in) and _MOE_MXFP4_MIN_TOKENS = 2048 threshold; above that token count, _forward_unfused and _forward_fused route the down/up projections through the MXFP4 GEMM instead of the bf16 ReplicatedLinear. 2. use tuned kernel for moe front bf16 kernel (56ce1f2198) - _k3_bf16_gemm now dispatches to aiter.tuned_gemm.tgemm on HIP (when SGLANG_USE_AITER is set and no output buffer is requested), in addition to the existing cutedsl path. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k 1319: 0.947, reduced ~0.008 due to mxfp4 quantization ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signals.title: [CI] Trim the base-c 4-gpu-h100 stage from 5 shards to 4
signals.text: `base-c-test-4-gpu-h100` runs its shards serially (`max_parallel = 5 // 3 = 1`), so cutting `est_time` is a linear wall-clock win. **5470s / 16 files -> 3572s / 13 files, 5 shards -> 3.** Nothing is dropped from CI. Most of it is placement: several tests sat on the 4-GPU runner without needing four GPUs. - `test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` -> `base-b`/`1-gpu-small`, dropping its `4-gpu-b200` and `4-gpu-gb300` registrations. Collectives are faked and every arch branch is `patch.object`-mocked, so the three runners ran identical mocks. - `test_hicache_storage_3fs_backend.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Max `--tp-size` is 2 and both configs are H100. - `test_disaggregation_unified_memory.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Its two classes are prefill tp1 on GPU 0 plus decode at `decode_base_gpu_id=1`, i.e. two GPUs; the two classes left in `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` need three (prefill tp2/pp2 plus `decode_base_gpu_id=2`). The shared parity base class stays in the latter and is imported. Four PD tests already run on `2-gpu-large` with the same `PDDisaggregationServerBase` fixture. - `test_pp_gemma4.py` (new) -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`, taking `TestGemma4PPAccuracy` and `TestGemma4PLEPPAccuracy` out of `test_pp_single_node.py`. Both are tp1/pp2; the four classes left behind are tp2/pp2. Both already carry `@unittest.skipIf(is_in_amd_ci())`, so no AMD registration moves. - The two `*AllocFail` classes and three DeepEP crossings move to new `*_extra.py` files on `extra-b`. Dead code removed (594 lines, no CI time since none of it ran): - `test_deepep_small.py::TestNoGatherdBuffer`, skipped as "covered in test_deepep_large.py" -- verified: `test_deepep_large.py::TestDeepseek` runs the same dp-attention + DeepEP + `--moe-dense-tp-size 1` + `--enable-dp-lm-head` combination. - `test_deepep_small.py::TestMTP`, skipped as "covered in TestMTPWithTBO". That claim was inaccurate -- it is tp4/dp2 while `TestMTPWithTBO` is tp4/dp4 -- so removing it does drop the dp2 + MTP combination rather than a duplicate. - `test/registered/rl/test_release_memory_occupation.py`, carrying `disabled="Temporarily disabled - needs investigation"` since 2026-05-26. Nothing imports it, and the sibling `test_multi_instance_release_memory_occupation.py` is self-contained. All moved classes keep their bodies byte-for-byte; the only edit is renaming the PD parity base class so it can be imported. `base-b-test-2-gpu-large` absorbs the three moves at 6701s -> 8121s, which raises it from 5 shards to 7 and its `max_parallel` from 1 to 2, cutting its serial waves from 5 to 4. `base-b-test-1-gpu-small` stays at 8 shards. Reviewer note: the DeepEP split takes **attention-TP + TBO off the per-commit path**; every other dimension there keeps a representative. The two new `2-gpu-large` `est_time` values (900s, 220s) are estimates split from the parent files -- the live partition model will correct them. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208152940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152940)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208152857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208152857)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(multimodal): let load_video accept an already-constructed decoder
signals.text: ## Motivation `load_video` returns a `VideoDecoderWrapper` for a URL/path/bytes source, but rejects one on the way in. `_normalize_video_input` has no case for that type and returns `None`, so the call raises `ValueError: Unsupported video input type`. The function is therefore not idempotent with respect to its own return value. This blocks any caller that constructs the decoder itself — a custom decode backend, or a caller that fetched the bytes under its own network policy and wants SGLang to keep owning frame selection via `smart_nframes`. Today such a caller has to pre-sample frames and hand over a bare `ndarray`, which takes the `not is_video_obj` early return in `preprocess_video` and bypasses the `video_config` policy (`fps` / `nframes` / `min_frames` / `max_frames`) entirely. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: pass a `VideoDecoderWrapper` through, next to the existing `list`/`tuple`/`Tensor`/`ndarray` passthrough, and widen the type hint. Unsupported types still raise. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_load_video_passthrough.py` (CPU, no decoder backend needed — `VideoDecoderWrapper` is patched with a stub). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. This only widens accepted input types on the decode path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one `isinstance` check on a non-hot path. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1: ``` BEFORE RAISED ValueError: Unsupported video input type: <class 'Stub'> AFTER passthrough returned Stub, is-same: True ``` New unit test: 2 failed / 2 passed before the fix (the two failures being the passthrough cases, the passes being the regression guards for the existing types), 4 passed after. Also reproduced on `v0.5.16-cu130-runtime` and `v0.5.17-cu130-runtime`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196807882](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196807882)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196807536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196807536)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(multimodal): resolve image token counts for decoded image tensors
signals.text: ## Motivation `BaseMultimodalProcessor.resolve_image_token_counts` reads `image.height` / `image.width`, which only exist on PIL images. But `gpu_image_decode` is `True` by default (`base_processor.py`), and `load_image` routes JPEG payloads through `torchvision.io.decode_jpeg(..., device="cuda")`, which returns a CHW `uint8` tensor. So the **default** configuration feeds this method a value it cannot read: ``` AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'height' ``` The failure is easy to miss because the call site wraps the block in `except Exception` and logs: > `Due to {e}, falling back to decode+retokenize, which may change prompt length (token drift).` The practical effect is that `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` — whose entire purpose is to avoid that drift — silently does nothing for JPEG images whenever GPU decode is on. It degrades to a warning rather than an error, so the feature looks enabled while never taking effect on the most common image format. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`: add a small `_image_height_width` helper that reads the trailing two axes for a `torch.Tensor` (decoded image tensors are channels-first, so the spatial dims are always last) and keeps the PIL attribute path otherwise. `resolve_image_token_counts` uses it. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_resolve_image_token_counts_tensor.py` (CPU, no model or GPU required). Mixed lists of PIL images and tensors are handled, and a degenerate tensor (`ndim < 2`) raises `ValueError` rather than silently producing a wrong size. ## Accuracy Tests This change *restores* accuracy rather than affecting it: with the fix, `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` can keep the user's exact tokens for JPEG images instead of falling back to decode+retokenize, which is the path that can change prompt length. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — an `isinstance` check per image, off the hot path. It does avoid an unnecessary retokenize when the flag is enabled. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1: ``` BEFORE RAISED AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'height' AFTER [7] ``` New unit test: fails to even import before the fix, 6 passed after. Also reproduced on `v0.5.16-cu130-runtime` and `v0.5.17-cu130-runtime`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196829036](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196829036)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196828914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196828914)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: fix(encode-server): do not forward None video metadata to the processor
signals.text: ## Motivation `MMEncoder._flatten_and_load_videos` guards the `video_metadata` kwarg with `if video_metadata:`, which tests the list for **emptiness** rather than for content: ```python videos, video_metadata = map(list, zip(*video_processed)) video_processor_kwargs["do_sample_frames"] = False if video_metadata: video_processor_kwargs["video_metadata"] = video_metadata ``` `preprocess_video` returns `(video, None)` whenever its input is not a `VideoDecoderWrapper` — i.e. for video that was already decoded upstream and handed over as frames. The guard then sees `[None]` (or `[None, None, ...]`), finds it truthy, and forwards it. transformers' `make_batched_metadata` converts the value only when it is `None` (synthesizing defaults), or when it is a list whose first element is a `list` or a `dict`. A list holding `None` matches neither branch and is returned unchanged, so the consumer dereferences `None`. Measured against transformers 5.12.1: ``` video_metadata=None -> [VideoMetadata(total_num_frames=4, width=8, height=8, frames_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3], ...)] video_metadata=[None] -> [None] -> .fps raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fps' video_metadata=[{...}] -> [VideoMetadata(..., fps=24.0)] ``` So omitting the kwarg is strictly *better* than forwarding `None`s: transformers then derives `total_num_frames`, `width`, `height` and `frames_indices` from the video itself. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py`: forward `video_metadata` only when every entry is present. The list is positionally parallel to `videos`, so individual entries cannot be dropped without misaligning the rest — hence `all(...)` rather than `any(...)`; a partially-populated list is omitted entirely. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_encode_server_video_metadata.py` covering all-`None`, all-real, mixed, and ordering (CPU, no model or GPU required). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. When metadata is present the behavior is unchanged; when it is absent the processor now receives no kwarg instead of `None` entries. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one pass over a list whose length is the number of videos in the request. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1. New unit test against the shipped `encode_server.py`: **2 failed, 2 passed** — the failures are exactly `test_all_none_metadata_is_not_forwarded` and `test_mixed_metadata_is_not_forwarded`, while the real-metadata and ordering controls pass. After the fix: **4 passed**. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196854673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196854541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854541)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signals.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signals.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`. The **decode** path picks its depth from `--mamba-track-interval` instead, and that arg: - has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page; - is never resolved anywhere — `grep mamba_track_interval` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty. Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | `test_kimi_k3_b300.py::TestKimiK3B300` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) is on the broken row today: Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read at the sites that pick a checkpoint depth: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Every one of them already holds a `ScheduleBatch`, so the page comes off `batch.tree_cache` exactly the way `_mamba_radix_cache_v2_req_prepare_for_extend` already takes it. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask, where a finer grid remains a superset of the snapshot steps it has to cover, and Inkling's `sconv`, which holds only a `ForwardBatch` and has no DCP coverage. ## Accuracy Tests Behaviour changes for exactly one shipped config: Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 + HiCache, grid 256 -> 512. That halves KDA checkpoint frequency there and is the correct frequency — the 256-boundary checkpoints were being attached to the wrong node. Verified unchanged for page 64 x dcp 4, page 32 x dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end. **Draft because I have not run the tests** — no sglang install on the machine I wrote this on. `py_compile`, isort, ruff, black and codespell pass. Undrafting once CI runs the unit case. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32198960136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32198960136)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32198960077](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32198960077)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
