signal.title: [Fix] flashinfer_mla: use flashinfer native fp8 MLA on SM90 instead of per-layer full-pool bf16 cast
signal.text: ## Problem Under `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` the MLA token pool already stores unscaled e4m3 bits (`MLATokenToKVPool` allocates a uint8 arena and `set_kv_buffer` casts with no scale), but the `flashinfer_mla` backend never consulted `model_runner.kv_cache_dtype`: it planned both dtype arguments with the model dtype and, in `forward_decode` and the paged branch of `forward_extend`, paid ```python self.token_to_kv_pool.get_key_buffer(layer.layer_id).to(q.dtype) ``` on every attention layer, every step — a **full-pool** bf16 materialization (all allocated slots, not just resident tokens), including idle steps, and inside CUDA-graph capture (so it is replayed every step). Independently reported in #35291: on DeepSeek-R1 (8×H200, 131K-token pool) the same cast costs 13.77 ms of a 31.52 ms decode step (43.7%), with ~98.9% of the moved bytes never referenced by the page table. That report also names the `fa3` backend; this change covers `flashinfer_mla` only — `fa3`'s MLA path has no native fp8-KV kernel to hand the raw pool buffer to and needs its own treatment (out of scope here). Two consequences, measured on a real server (H100 80GB, 61-layer structurally-real DeepSeek-V3-family model with dummy weights, pool pinned to 1M tokens, decode CUDA graphs on, 4 concurrent × 384-token greedy decodes, torch profiler over 40 decode steps): 1. **Throughput collapse.** The cast kernel (`unrolled_elementwise_kernel<direct_copy_kernel_cuda>`) launches exactly 61× per decode step, 1.76 ms each = **107.4 ms/step of pure copy**. Measured TPOT: `main + fp8 KV` = **109.75 ms/token** vs `main + bf16 KV` = **4.42 ms/token** — the entire difference is the cast (the rest of the step is ~4 ms). The cost scales with the *allocated pool*, not with resident context: a fresh server with short requests pays it in full from the first step, and idle steps pay it too. 2. **Hard OOM on large pools.** With a naturally-sized fp8 pool (mem-fraction 0.92 → 2.07M tokens), `main + fp8` crashes with CUDA OOM during the first prefill: the full-pool cast in `forward_extend` tries to allocate a transient 2.2 GiB bf16 shadow of the pool. Same mechanism as the Kimi-Linear up-convert OOM (#34638). flashinfer has supported bf16-q × fp8-e4m3-KV MLA natively on SM90 since 0.6.14 (flashinfer PR #3694; fa3 backend, `head_dim_ckv=512`, `head_dim_kpe=64`, per-tensor `ckv_scale`/`kpe_scale`; sglang's current `flashinfer==0.6.17` pin includes it) — only the sglang-side wiring was missing. ## Fix Single-file change to `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`: - A pure helper `_fp8_kv_enabled(...)` gates the native path on exactly what the flashinfer kernel supports: `kv_cache_dtype == e4m3` + SM90 + bf16 model + `kv_lora_rank=512`/`qk_rope_head_dim=64` + DCP disabled. Non-qualifying configs (non-fp8 KV, other architectures, fp16 models, NoPE MLA, e5m2, DCP) keep the existing upcast path byte-for-byte; a single warning is logged when an fp8 KV cache was requested but disqualified (pointing Blackwell users to `trtllm_mla`). - The decode and paged-prefill `plan()` calls now pass `kv_data_type=torch.float8_e4m3fn` on the qualifying path (previously the model dtype twice). - `forward_decode`/`forward_extend` pass the raw e4m3 pool buffer — sliced as `[:, :, :512]` / `[:, :, 512:]` strided views of the fused 576-wide row — plus `ckv_scale=1.0, kpe_scale=1.0`, instead of upcasting the whole pool. The kernel plumbs outer strides explicitly, so the 576-strided views are consumed directly; the pool layout and write path are untouched. - Scales are 1.0 because the write side stores unscaled e4m3; per-tensor scale plumbing (e.g. checkpoint-provided `k_scale`) is left as a follow-up. - CUDA-graph fast-path plans are untouched: the dtype is baked at capture-time `plan()`, which routes through the same modified updaters. ## Numerics The SM90 fp8 kernel keeps KV as e4m3 through HBM/L2/SMEM and dequantizes to bf16 right before the (bf16) WGMMA. Unscaled e4m3 values are exactly representable in bf16, so the fp8 path feeds the math the same bits as the old `.to(bf16)` upcast. Verified on H100 across 256 kernel configs (`batch {1,4,16,64} × qo_len {1,8,64} × kv_len {256..16384} × page_size {1,64} × heads {16,128}`, causal on/off, production dims only): output is **bitwise identical** to running the bf16 kernel on the upcast pool; strided 576-wide views match packed contiguous copies bitwise; absolute error vs an fp32 reference (rel-L2 ≤ 2.9e-3) is unchanged from the bf16 kernel. The e2e A/B above additionally ran the full server on the PR branch with fp8 KV under CUDA graphs without any anomaly (dummy weights, so token-level output comparison is not meaningful; kernel-level bitwise identity is established separately). ## End-to-end results Real server, methodology as in Problem (full artifacts: server logs, per-config traces, timing JSON): | config | pool | TPOT (ms/token) | cast kernel per step | |---|---|---|---| | main + bf16 KV | 1.00M tok / 65.4 GiB | 4.42 | — | | main + fp8 KV | 1.00M tok / 32.7 GiB | **109.75** | 61 × 1.76 ms = 107.4 ms | | branch + bf16 KV | 1.00M tok / 65.4 GiB | 4.54 | — | | branch + fp8 KV | 1.00M tok / 32.7 GiB | **5.84** | none (0.22 ms / 40 steps of index bookkeeping) | Same-config effect of this PR: **109.75 → 5.84 ms/token (18.8×)**; the branch is within reach of the bf16 baseline (+1.3 ms ≈ the fp8 MLA kernel's per-op tax at this short context; see the kernel-level caveat below for how it scales). Kernel-level scaling reference (pure-kernel self-time, decode @ kv_len 8192, 128 heads, ×61 layers): the eliminated cast costs ~1.76 ms/layer per 1M slots (≈107 ms/step at 1M; ~534 ms/step at 5M slots, the latter an out-of-range-for-single-H100 scaling bound), including idle steps. One honest caveat: per operation the fp8 MLA kernel is 2.0–2.65× slower than the bf16 kernel at equal batch (SMEM dequant-repack; e.g. 539→1428 µs at batch 128, kv 8192), so the net win is entirely the cast elimination. It is largest for **decode**, where the cast is paid on the *allocated* pool against one token of attention per layer; prefill/extend also drop the cast but pay the kernel tax on the full KV length, so their net saving is smaller and pool-size-dependent. ## Tests - New `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_fp8_kv.py` (CPU-only, no GPU needed): guard-table coverage for all disqualifiers; `__init__` wiring; the fallback warning firing exactly once per process (including across the several backends a spec-decode scheduler builds); `kv_data_type` selection in both decode plan call sites and the paged prefill plan; run-branch selection pinned hard (fp8: raw e4m3 strided views with the pool's 576-row stride on both ckv and kpe, exact `run()` kwarg set, `ckv_scale/kpe_scale=1.0`, and **zero** `.to()` upcasts off the pool; non-fp8: exactly one bf16 cast, no scale kwargs); and a cuda-graph lifecycle integration test driving the real backend + indices updaters (eager decode → capture → replay → target-verify, with a bf16 control run) that asserts every stock and fast `plan` carries the backend's kv dtype and that replay reuses the captured wrapper instance. 16 tests + 24 subtests; hand-checked mutations fail at least one test. - GPU validation (out of tree): the 256-config bitwise-identity harness and the 4-config real-server A/B above. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208573720](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208573720)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208573526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208573526)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix gfx950 Triton compiler crash on fp8 KV-cache attention
signal.text: ## Motivation `test/registered/attention/test_verify_shared_kv.py::test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache` has never passed on `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` since it was added (#34517); it fails inside the Triton AMD backend, not in sglang code ([latest instance](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166850277/job/95808413702)): ``` python3: llvm/ADT/SmallVector.h:292: Assertion `idx < size()' failed. extend_attention.py:305:0: error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline extend_attention.py:305:0: note: Pipeline failed while executing [`ConvertTritonAMDGPUToLLVM` ...] RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed ``` Only the fp8 variant fails; the bf16 variants of the same test pass. The crash is not test-specific — it is in the shared prefill kernel, so **any** model served with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on MI35x hits it, in decode as well as prefill. ### Root cause Every Triton attention kernel that reads a KV pool casts the wide operand *down* to the pool dtype before the dot (`tl.dot(q.to(k.dtype), k)`, `tl.dot(p.to(v.dtype), v)`), so an fp8 pool also feeds the fp8 matrix core. On gfx950 `AccelerateAMDMatmul` promotes an fp8 x fp8 `tl.dot` to the scaled `V_MFMA_*_F8F6F4` family, which is **16x16x128** under the `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16` launch hint all of these kernels pass. A dot whose reduction is narrower than 128 does not tile that instruction: `AMDMfmaEncodingAttr::getRepForOperand` clamps the resulting zero K-repetitions up to one, and `ScaledDotOpMFMAConversionHelper` then reads `kBase = 32` elements per lane from a register range that only holds `K / 4`. That is the out-of-bounds `SmallVector` access. `P @ V` reduces `BLOCK_N`, which is 64 (extend, verify) or 32 (decode, split-KV verify) — never 128 — so the fp8 path never compiles on gfx950. `Q @ Kpe` reduces `BLOCK_DPE` (32/64) and `Q @ K` reduces `BLOCK_DMODEL`, which is also below 128 at head_dim <= 64. Triton rejects the intrinsic instead of miscompiling it as of [triton-lang/triton#8278](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/8278), which dropped the `enforcedNonKDim == 0 &&` escape hatch that had let an explicit `matrix_instr_nonkdim` skip Triton's own "K is not a multiple of the intrinsic's kDim" check. The Triton 3.4.0 wheels in the ROCm CI images predate that fix, so the guard is skipped and the backend aborts. ## Modifications - New `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fp8_dot_support.py` with `dot_in_kv_dtype(kv_dtype, reduction_width)`: `True` for every non-fp8 pool and every arch other than gfx950, and on gfx950 only for reduction widths that tile the scaled MFMA instruction. - Each pool-reading dot in `_fwd_kernel` / `_fwd_kernel_unified` (extend), `_fwd_grouped_kernel_stage1` (decode), `_verify_mla_prefix_stage1`, and `_verify_prefix_stage1` gets its own constexpr verdict (`QK_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `QK_PE_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`, `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE`). When it is `False` the KV tile is upcast to the query dtype instead of the query tile being cast down. - CPU unit test pinning the predicate, the widths the crashing gfx950 tile config actually uses, and the presence of the per-dot flags. Every flag is `True` on non-gfx950 hardware and for bf16/fp16 pools, so those paths generate the same code as before. `matrix_instr_nonkdim`, tile sizes, warp counts, and the `#mma` layout are all untouched. Alternatives considered and rejected: dropping or raising `matrix_instr_nonkdim` for the fp8 path (Triton's own guard then rejects the intrinsic, but the 16x16 tile becomes 32x32, which changes `warpsPerTile` for the chain-dot tail from `[8, 1]` to `[4, 2]` and inserts a layout conversion between the two dots), and forcing `BLOCK_N = 128` (fixes only head_dim 256 and re-tunes the bf16 path with it). ## Accuracy Tests The change only affects gfx950 with an fp8 KV pool, where nothing compiles today, so there is no prior behaviour to regress. Within that path `P` reaches the dot as bf16 rather than quantized to e4m3, which is strictly more accurate; `extend_attention_fwd` and `verify_shared_kv_fwd` widen the same dots, so `test_qwen3_5_fp8_kv_cache`'s parity check compares like with like (this is the test the PR unblocks — please run `stage-b-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No measurement on MI35x yet. The reasoning for expecting no loss: the wide `Q @ K` dot keeps `tt.dot_scaled` (verified in the emitted TTGIR below), and for the narrow dots CDNA4's non-scaled `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_FP8_FP8` — what a Triton carrying #8278 would fall back to — reduces the same 32 elements per instruction as `V_MFMA_F32_16X16X32_BF16`, so bf16 operands run at the same rate. The extra cost is the fp8 -> bf16 converts on the V tile and a larger LDS footprint for it (80 KB total at head_dim 256 versus 128 KB for a bf16 pool, so still well inside the 160 KB budget). ## Verification Triton 3.4.0's AMD backend compiles for `hip:gfx950` without a GPU, so the fix was checked by driving the ttir/ttgir/llir stages directly on the same tile shape and launch hints as `extend_attention` at head_dim 256 (`BLOCK_M=128`, `num_warps=8`, `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`): | KV dtype | `PV_DOT_IN_KV_DTYPE` | `BLOCK_N` | Result | |---|---|---|---| | fp8_e4m3 | True (today) | 64 | **`RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False (this PR) | 64 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 32 | **`Assertion 'idx < size()' failed`** | | fp8_e4m3 | False | 32 | compiles | | fp8_e4m3 | True | 128 | compiles (128 tiles the instruction) | | bf16 | True | 64 | compiles (unchanged path) | The fixed variant's TTGIR keeps the fp8 fast path where it is legal and drops to bf16 only for `P @ V`, both under the same `#mma` layout as before: ``` %50 = tt.dot_scaled %28, %49, %cst_2 lhs = e4m3 rhs = e4m3 : tensor<128x256xf8E4M3FN, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 16}>> * tensor<256x64xf8E4M3FN, ...> %77 = tt.dot %76, %75, %73 : tensor<128x64xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> * tensor<64x256xbf16, dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 4}>> ``` The K3 MLA tile (`BLOCK_DMODEL=512`, `BLOCK_DPE=64`, `BLOCK_N=64`), where two of the three dots widen, behaves the same way: crashes today, compiles with the per-dot verdicts. Narrowing `BLOCK_DMODEL` to 64 crashes the `Q @ K` dot too, which is why the verdict is computed per dot rather than assuming `Q @ K` is always wide enough. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208402356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208402356)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208402191](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208402191)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: test: switch the Inkling-Small NVFP4 deterministic suite to DSPARK
signal.text: ## Motivation Roadmap item under #34899 — bit-exact correctness coverage for the unified radix cache, speculative-decoding row (DSpark / DFlash). `TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact` in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py` was added to cover the spec side of the sconv/mamba checkpoint save. It cannot reach it: `_is_mamba_track_enabled()` is a method of `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`, and EAGLE targets disable the prefill CUDA graph outright (`cuda_graph_setup.py`, #28386), so the runner is never constructed. Measured — reverting #34043 leaves that class green: ``` TestUnifiedHybridMTPBitExact, #34043 reverted → 2 passed, avg_kl_div=0.0 log: "Disable prefill CUDA graph for EAGLE target on tc_piecewise (#28386)" ``` DSPARK and DFlash are not `is_eagle()`, keep the prefill graph, and are the algorithms #34043 actually fixed (that PR measured a DFlash SWEBench subset going 55% → 35% from zeroed sconv state). ## Modifications `TestInklingSmallNvfp4Deterministic` now runs with DSPARK driving decode, and is renamed `TestInklingSmallNvfp4DsparkDeterministic`. The helpers, the 1e-9 floor, the `extra_buffer` / SWA / mamba-ratio / `KL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS` setup and the dedicated server are all unchanged. Two knobs move: `--mem-fraction-static` 0.85 → 0.80 for this class only (see below), and the file's `est_time` 1700 → 2000 for the draft load and graph capture. This replaces rather than adds: the DSPARK config exercises the same NVFP4 weights and the same `flashinfer_trtllm` fp4 GEMM/MoE path, so the FP4-regression coverage the class was written for is retained, and the non-spec cache-restore logic is covered on the shrunken checkpoint in `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_hybrid_bitexact.py`. A second no-spec arm here would cost another server launch on a `4-gpu-b200` slot for coverage that is not unique. The trade that buys: a reading here is no longer self-attributing. Inkling-Small is a 256-expert MoE where dropping `--enable-deterministic-inference` alone reads 5.0e-02 — the same order as the bug signal below — so a red case needs a manual re-run without the speculative flags to separate a state-reuse bug from batch variance. That is written into the class docstring. ## Accuracy Tests Revert-then-red against #34043. First measured on the **bf16** `Inkling-Small` checkpoint at tp=4 on GB300 (same server args plus `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK`, minus the fp4 flags): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **8.05e-02** | | `..._decode_cache_hit` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | no-spec arm (all three) | 0.0 | 0.0 | Eight orders of magnitude above the floor, and the failure lands where the mechanism predicts — the corruption reaches a request that *restores* a prefix, so the flush-both comparison and the decode-side reuse stay clean. The no-spec arm staying green under the same revert is what identified the reading as speculative-state-specific. Sanity of that run: `speculative_algorithm='DSPARK'`, accept len 1.7–3.5, `cuda graph: True`, and `cuda_graph_config.prefill.backend` resolves to `full`, so the class reaches the line #34043 changed. Probe sensitivity with `--enable-deterministic-inference` dropped: 5.0e-02 / 4.3e-02 / 5.9e-03. Since re-measured on this file's own config — NVFP4 `Inkling-Small` at tp=4 on 4x GB300 (SM100, same `modelopt_fp4` / `flashinfer_trtllm` path the class already used; there is precedent for that pairing in `test/registered/gb300/test_glm52_nvfp4.py`): | | fix in place | #34043 reverted | |---|---|---| | `..._logprobs_match` | 0.0 | 0.0 | | **`..._prefill_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **1.10e-01** | | **`..._decode_cache_hit`** | 0.0 | **`Too few decode cache hits: 31/32`** | ``` fix in place : 3 passed (650.79s) #34043 revert: 2 failed, 1 passed ``` So both open questions are closed: the bf16 DSPARK draft does pair with the `modelopt_fp4` target, and the exact-0 baseline holds on NVFP4. The signal is stronger here than on bf16 — the revert also drops one prompt out of the decode-cache reuse, which trips the `min_cache_hit_ratio=0.99` this class already asserts. Whole file on 4x GB300: 5 passed in 1093 s. **`--mem-fraction-static` is 0.80 for this class, not the 0.85 the others use.** The first CI run OOMed mid-test on B200: the draft weights and the speculative CUDA graphs (`974.89 MiB allocated in private pools`) left `avail mem=0.40 GB` at 0.85 on a 178 GB card. The GB300 verification could not have caught this — 284 GB per GPU is 60% more headroom. At 0.80 the KV pool still reports ~6.2M tokens against the ~130k this file uses, so the slack costs nothing. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Test-only. signal.title: [diffusion] CI: cut two setup cycles from the AMD multimodal-gen lanes
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD multimodal-gen jobs spend most of their runner time not testing. Measured on mi300 in [run 31443692177](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31443692177), every job pays a container pull of 27–97 min plus a dependency install of 23–98 min, so 100–155 min of fixed cost before a single test executes. Across the eight multimodal jobs in that run that is ~15.8 runner-hours of setup against ~5.6 hours of tests — roughly 74% overhead, and because both matrices are `max-parallel: 1` it is serialized into wall-clock. CUDA for comparison: `Install dependencies` takes 27 seconds and total fixed overhead is under a minute. The two clearest wins are removing whole setup cycles. ## Modifications **Fold the `unit` suite into a warm shard.** `multimodal-gen-unit-test-amd` paid ~110 min of setup to run ~5 min of portable CPU-style tests. It now runs as a step of `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd` part 0 (and the ROCm 7.2 counterpart), on the container that job already warmed. The step runs after the diffusion tests and on failure as well, so a diffusion regression cannot mask a unit regression, and it carries its own `timeout-minutes` so it cannot eat the diffusion step's budget. Trigger conditions are unchanged — on both lanes the 1-GPU job already gates on exactly the inputs the unit job did (`multimodal_gen` on `pr-test-amd`, `main_package || sgl_kernel` on ROCm 7.2). The standalone job, its `target_stage_select` entry, and its `needs` entry are removed; the `ci_coverage_report.py` comment naming it is updated (the `"unit": ("CUDA", "AMD")` mapping itself still holds). **2-GPU: 3 shards → 2.** Per-case timings from the same run were 14, 26 and 21 min of healthy work across the three shards; the third shard's other 96 min was `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus` (77.7 min) and `flux2_modelopt_fp8_tp2_t2i` (18.1 min) retrying, which is the known ROCm flux bug (#34351 / #34352), not real work. Two shards therefore land near 30 min of case time each — and even if one shard inherited both flux cases while they stay broken, ~126 min is still inside the 180 min step timeout. Net effect: 8 AMD multimodal jobs → 5 per lane, i.e. ~4 fewer setup cycles across the two AMD workflows, on the order of 8 runner-hours per full PR run. ## What this deliberately does not do **1-GPU stays at 4 shards.** It has no headroom today: shard 0 already ends with `The action 'Run diffusion server tests (1-GPU)' has timed out after 90 minutes`, spent retrying the broken `flux_image_t2i`. Merging 1-GPU shards should wait until that case is fixed or skipped, and would likely want the step timeout raised to 150 min to match the 2-GPU lane. **The retry amplification and the image pull are untouched.** Retrying a deterministically broken case seven times is what turns a 20-minute shard into a 127-minute one, and the ROCm image pull is the single largest line item in the whole lane — caching or pre-pulling it on the mi300 runners would beat any amount of matrix tuning. Both are worth separate work. ## Validation Dispatched on this branch against the ROCm 7.2 lane (the PR gate since #34204): [run 31638833841](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31638833841). **The unit fold works, including the case it had to get right.** On 1-GPU part 0 the diffusion step failed (7 passed, 1 setup error) and the folded `Run diffusion unit tests` step still ran and passed — 1360 passed, 10 skipped in 102 s. `if: matrix.part == 0 && (success() || failure())` fires after a failed predecessor, and the step is correctly skipped on parts 1-3. **The 2 two-GPU shards cover the suite and fit the timeout, but with less margin than I estimated.** They split into 13 cases + 3 standalone and 13 cases + 4 standalone. Shard 1 spent 45 min on cases plus 9 min on standalone. Shard 0 reached **149 min** against the 180 min step cap — not because two shards is too coarse, but because `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus` fails and the harness retries it: 64 min for the case block, then repeated ~13 min retry passes. Both shards' remaining failures are the pre-existing ROCm set (flux #34351 / #34352, and `test_ar_models` failing warmup with `Inference tensors do not track version counter`). So the split is safe today and drops to ~45-65 min per shard once the flux retries stop, but if a reviewer wants insurance while flux is broken, the options are to hold this until flux lands or to raise the 2-GPU step timeout. I have deliberately not raised it here: a larger cap means a wedged job holds a scarce mi300 runner longer. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — CI orchestration only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Covered above: the change is motivated entirely by measured CI wall-clock, and the numbers come from the per-step and per-case timings of run 31443692177. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: VLM: feed the packed qkv projection output to vision backends uncopied
signal.text: ## Motivation In `VisionAttention.forward`, the `use_qkv_parallel` branch slices `qkv_proj`'s output into q/k/v and then copies all three dense: ```python qkv, _ = self.qkv_proj(x) q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1) q = q.reshape(bsz * s, head, -1) # a view, still strided ... q = q.contiguous(); k = k.contiguous(); v = v.contiguous() # three full copies ``` `qkv_proj` writes q, k and v interleaved into one buffer, so those slices are views whose only non-unit stride is over tokens — the last dimension stays contiguous. Backends that read q/k/v through explicit per-dim strides accept them as they are, so the copies move the whole projection output twice through HBM per layer for nothing. On a PaddleOCR-VL page (10764 patches, 16 heads, head_dim 72, bf16) that is 3.74 GiB of HBM traffic per request across 27 layers. ## Modifications - Add `STRIDED_QKV_BACKENDS` next to `QKV_BACKEND_IMPL`, listing the backends that read q/k/v through explicit strides: `fa3`, `fa4`, `triton_attn`, `amx_attn`. `flashinfer_cudnn` stays out because its packed element indptrs assume a dense layout; `sdpa`, `ascend_attn`, `aiter_attn` and `xpu_attn` stay out because their kernels were not verified against a non-unit token stride. - Compute `self.pass_strided_qkv` in `__init__` and skip the three `.contiguous()` calls when it holds. This replaces the previous `_is_cpu and _is_cpu_amx_available` predicate; `amx_attn` is in the set, so the CPU-AMX default path is unchanged. - Two consumers sit between the projection and the backend and need a dense layout, so they keep the copies: - `qk_normalization` (internvl) — `apply_qk_norm` normalizes q/k **in place** through `q.view(N, -1, embed)`. That view succeeds on the strided tensor, and the kernel then writes per its dense stride assumption, corrupting the k/v regions of the shared buffer. - `customized_position_embedding_applier` — model-supplied callables reshape q/k however they like (e.g. `mllama4` views to 4D). - `qk_normalization_by_head_size` (GLM-OCR) does **not** need to opt out: its `reshape(-1, head_size)` materialises a dense copy of q/k on its own. - No GQA special case is needed. `qkv.view(tokens, 3, head, head_dim)[:, i]` is byte-identical to what `split` + `reshape` already produce, and a GQA tower's k/v slices have the same stride shape, so nothing has to change for `num_kv_heads != num_heads`. New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_vision_strided_qkv.py` covers the gating matrix (8 backends plus the three qk-norm / applier variants), asserts the tensors reaching the backend are non-contiguous views into a single storage carrying byte-identical values to the dense path (MHA and GQA), and asserts the layer output is bit-identical between the two paths. ## Accuracy Tests All on one H200, bf16, `fa3`. - `flash_attn_varlen_func` and the Triton `context_attention_fwd` produce **bit-identical** output from strided views vs dense copies across 8 shapes: PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP (10764 patches, 1 and 8 sequences), Qwen2.5-VL ViT (8192 / head_dim 80), Qwen3-VL ViT (6400 / head_dim 128), InternViT-like (25 heads / head_dim 64), a GQA tower (16 q heads / 4 kv heads), a non-multiple token count (1023), and fp16. - The full PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP encoder (27 layers, 12000 patches) output is **bit-identical** between the two paths. - Greedy output over 3 prompts on the same image is **byte-identical** before and after, for **PaddleOCR-VL**, **Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct** and **Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct**. - The 14 new unit tests pass. Not covered: no released vision tower is GQA (`mimo_vl` is the only call site that can pass `num_kv_heads`, and only when its vision config sets `num_key_value_heads`), so GQA is covered at the unit-test and kernel level only. The `qk_normalization` opt-out is covered by the unit test — InternVL2_5-2B has `qk_normalization: false`, so it is not an end-to-end exercise of that branch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling PaddleOCR-VL SigLIP encoder, 27 layers, 12000 patches, bf16, H200, `fa3`, in-process CUDA-event timing, the two modes interleaved over 7 rounds each: | | dense copies | strided views | delta | |---|---|---|---| | encoder forward | 66.42 ms | 64.88 ms | **−1.54 ms (−2.3%)** | | one `VisionAttention.forward` (10764 patches) | 1565.2 us | 1455.3 us | −109.9 us (−7.0%) | | peak allocated, one layer | 306.1 MiB | 234.1 MiB | −72 MiB | Sample ranges do not overlap (strided 64.78–65.58 ms, dense 66.34–66.66 ms). The three `.contiguous()` calls alone measure 96.8 us per layer at that shape, i.e. 2.6 ms of pure copy time per request over 27 layers. **No end-to-end win is claimed yet.** Single-page latency (197.9–200.9 ms vs 197.9–199.0 ms) and saturated page throughput (9.62/9.90/9.65 vs 10.24/9.91/9.76 pages/s over 3 rounds of 96 pages at concurrency 8) both came out inside the noise band. Sampling GPU utilisation during the throughput run showed a mean of **17.4%** — that harness was CPU-bound on image preprocessing, so it cannot resolve a GPU-side saving of this size either way. Marking this a draft until a GPU-bound page-throughput benchmark either confirms or rules out the end-to-end effect; the encoder-level number above is the measured result. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32147235077](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32147235077)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32147674741](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32147674741)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation There has been extensive discussion around making HiCache work better for small host-memory setups: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28614, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16909, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14056. signal.title: [AMD] Create the hipBLAS handle before CUDA graph capture
signal.text: `stage-b-test-2-gpu-large-amd-rocm720` shard 1 has been failing on and off since Aug-15 (5 of the last 7 scheduled runs) with `AssertionError: -1 not greater than 200` in `test_bench_one_batch_2gpu.py`. The `-1` means no throughput was measured because the server died. The real sequence, from [this log](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31916881653/job/95090118554), is: ``` [aiter] shape is M:1, N:14336, K:4096 ... not found tuned config in /tmp/aiter_configs/bf16_tuned_gemm.csv, will use default config! aiter/tuned_gemm.py:514: bgemm_internal_cublaslt error: HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR when calling hipblasLtMatmul out = F.linear(inp, weights, bias) RuntimeError: Triton Error [HIP]: Code: 900, operation not permitted when stream is capturing torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture [AITER] custom_all_reduce.cuh:3412 fail to call hipIpcOpenMemHandle(...) Fatal Python error: Aborted ``` The job benchmarks Llama-3.1-8B and Mixtral-8x7B, and the aiter config merge for this image pulls in `llama70B`, `dsv3`, `dsv4`, `glm47`, `glm5`, `gptoss`, `kimi*`, `minimax_m3_eagle` and `qwen3_5_397b` — no config covering these two models. So the M:1 decode shapes have no tuned entry, and aiter takes the `F.linear` fallback. hipBLAS creates its handle lazily on first use. When that first use is the fallback inside an active HIP graph capture, `hipblasCreate` is illegal, returns `HIPBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR`, and invalidates the capture. Everything after it — the Triton "operation not permitted when stream is capturing" from `CompiledKernel.__del__`, and the abort in the aiter custom all-reduce — is downstream of that. This does one small matmul during `warmup()`, next to the existing `_pre_initialize_*` helpers that already exist to keep uncapturable initialization out of the capture context. The handle then exists before capture starts and the fallback reuses it. Guarded on ROCm, and wrapped so a failure here can never break startup. This does not add the missing tuned configs — the fallback still runs, it just no longer corrupts the capture. Generating configs for these models would remove the fallback as well and is worth doing separately. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). `test_bench_one_batch_2gpu.py` is the existing test this repairs. No user-facing behaviour changes; the added work is one 1x1 matmul at startup. I have not reproduced this on hardware — the analysis is from the CI logs and the code path. The AMD CI job is the real check, and I would like a ROCm reviewer to sanity-check that a `torch.matmul` is enough to force the handle on this aiter/hipBLASLt version. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32208185546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208185546)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32208185409](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208185409)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Auto-detect aiter decode attention backend for MLA models on ROCm
signal.text: > **Draft status:** this April branch conflicts with current `main`; backend resolution has since been refactored. The old patch is not ready for review or GPU CI as-is. ## Motivation On MI355X, the AITER MLA decode backend materially reduced GLM-5.1 FP8 decode latency compared with the then-default backend. Automatically selecting it when the user has not chosen either attention backend could remove a manual tuning step for supported ROCm MLA models. ## Current blockers - The original insertion point in `ServerArgs` no longer matches current `main`'s backend-resolution pipeline. - `importlib.util.find_spec("aiter")` proves only that the package exists, not that the installed build, GPU, model shape, and decode mode are supported. - The branch has no regression tests for default selection, explicit user overrides, or unavailable/unsupported AITER. - The 42.6% result was measured on one MI355X GLM configuration and must not be generalized to every listed model or ROCm GPU without evidence. ## Required refresh before marking ready - [ ] Re-implement the default in current `arg_groups` / override resolution rather than patching the old block. - [ ] Add focused tests for default selection, both user override flags, missing AITER, and unsupported capability. - [ ] Rerun the GLM-5.1 MI355X benchmark against current `main` and record exact commands. - [ ] Smoke-test at least one additional supported MLA architecture or narrow the documented model scope. - [ ] Run current lint and AMD CI. The PR remains draft pending redesign and independent MI355X validation.

signal.title: [CI] Trim the base-c 4-gpu-h100 stage from 5 shards to 4
signal.text: `base-c-test-4-gpu-h100` runs its shards serially (`max_parallel = 5 // 3 = 1`), so cutting `est_time` is a linear wall-clock win. **5470s / 16 files -> 3572s / 13 files, 5 shards -> 3.** Nothing is dropped from CI. Most of it is placement: several tests sat on the 4-GPU runner without needing four GPUs. - `test_flashinfer_comm_fusion.py` -> `base-b`/`1-gpu-small`, dropping its `4-gpu-b200` and `4-gpu-gb300` registrations. Collectives are faked and every arch branch is `patch.object`-mocked, so the three runners ran identical mocks. - `test_hicache_storage_3fs_backend.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Max `--tp-size` is 2 and both configs are H100. - `test_disaggregation_unified_memory.py` -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`. Its two classes are prefill tp1 on GPU 0 plus decode at `decode_base_gpu_id=1`, i.e. two GPUs; the two classes left in `test_disaggregation_kimi_linear.py` need three (prefill tp2/pp2 plus `decode_base_gpu_id=2`). The shared parity base class stays in the latter and is imported. Four PD tests already run on `2-gpu-large` with the same `PDDisaggregationServerBase` fixture. - `test_pp_gemma4.py` (new) -> `base-b`/`2-gpu-large`, taking `TestGemma4PPAccuracy` and `TestGemma4PLEPPAccuracy` out of `test_pp_single_node.py`. Both already carry `@unittest.skipIf(is_in_amd_ci())`, so no AMD registration moves. - The two `*AllocFail` classes and three DeepEP crossings move to new `*_extra.py` files on `extra-b`. signal.title: [XPU][CI] key persistent JIT kernel cache by image content ID
signal.text: ## Summary Nightly image rebuilds swap the runtime libs that cached JIT `.so` files link against (e.g. `libsycl.so.8` -> `libsycl.so.9`). Triton keys its cache on source hash only, so the previous gpu-mask-only cache path dlopens stale `.so`s from the prior image and every XPU CI job dies with `OSError: libsycl.so.N: cannot open shared object file`. - Include the resolved `docker image inspect` ID in the cache path so a new image gets a fresh cache dir. - Prune sibling caches for the same GPU but a different image ID via a rootful busybox helper (files are root-owned by the CI container, same pattern as the workspace-ownership reset). - Explicit `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR` overrides are still honored verbatim; if `docker image inspect` fails we fall back to the legacy unversioned path with a warning. - Over-cap reset switched from a runner-level `rm -rf` to the same busybox helper for the same root-owned reason. ## Test plan - [ ] XPU CI passes on an image with a torch/SYCL bump (verify no `libsycl.so.*: cannot open shared object` failures). - [ ] Sibling `kernel-cache-gpu*-<oldid>` dirs are pruned on first run after an image rebuild. - [ ] `XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/foo` override still lands at `/tmp/foo` with no pruning. - [ ] Over-cap path (>`XPU_KERNEL_CACHE_MAX_MB`) resets cleanly. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32172874266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32172874266)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32208126441](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32208126441)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [VLM] Default to two multimodal preprocessing workers
signal.text: Stacked on #35342 (which routes every processor through the worker pool's call site). Review that one first; this PR is the one line that actually turns the pool on. ## Motivation Preprocessing an image costs real CPU time on the tokenizer's event loop, so with a single worker a model's request throughput is capped at `1 / preprocess_time` no matter how much GPU is idle. That cap is why PaddleOCR-VL saturated at 6.7 req/s on an H200 with GPU headroom to spare — and only four processors in tree had opted out of it. ## The benefit generalizes, because the mechanism does Image preprocessing is numpy / torch / PIL underneath, so it releases the GIL. Wall-clock speedup of 4 threads over 1 on the same work, 1080p input, `torch.set_num_threads(1)` so intraop parallelism cannot be mistaken for thread scaling: | image processor | 1 thread | 4 threads | speedup | `deepcopy` | |---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen2VL (fast / slow) | 24.3 / 24.1 ms | 7.1 / 7.0 ms | 3.41x / 3.45x | ok | | Idefics3 | 46.1 ms | 12.7 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Pixtral | 19.0 ms | 5.2 ms | 3.64x | ok | | Llama4 | 27.0 ms | 7.7 ms | 3.52x | ok | | GLM4V | 31.8 ms | 9.0 ms | 3.51x | ok | | PaddleOCR-VL | 28.4 ms | 8.7 ms | 3.27x | ok | | CLIP | 9.1 ms | 2.8 ms | 3.28x | ok | | Gemma3 | 5.7 ms | 1.9 ms | 2.94x | ok | | SigLIP | 5.5 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.69x | ok | | *pure-Python control* | *81.0 ms* | *80.5 ms* | *1.01x* | — | The control validates the probe. `copy.deepcopy` succeeded on all nine, and the executor already falls back to synchronous processing with a warning if cloning ever fails. ## Two workers, and not more Past two, spreading request arrivals fragments the GPU prefill batches faster than the extra overlap pays for itself — the tradeoff `qwen_vl`'s processor already documents. Swept at 32-way concurrency on an H200: | workload | 1 worker | 2 workers | 4 workers | |---|---|---|---| | PaddleOCR-VL 1080p pages, 128-token outputs | 6.72 | **9.55** | 8.92 req/s | | PaddleOCR-VL 360p pages, 512-token outputs | 22.38 | **25.20** | 25.06 req/s | | Qwen2.5-VL 360p images, 512-token outputs | 12.54 | **12.60** | 12.25 req/s | The middle row is the shape that was supposed to break this: light preprocessing, where overlap has little to win, and long outputs, where batch fragmentation has the most to cost. Two workers gained 13% there instead of regressing. Four workers is where the documented regression actually appears (bottom row, −2.3%). Greedy output is unaffected: two workers against one is byte-identical across five page geometries × two task prompts on PaddleOCR-VL. ## Limitation reviewers should weigh All of this is **Hopper**. The regression `qwen_vl` documents was observed on Blackwell, and no B200 was available to me (GB300 is arm64). A Blackwell check on the light-preprocessing / long-output shape would be worth having before this rides a release — that is the one measurement that could still overturn the default. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test pinning the default (`test_default_worker_count_stays_at_the_measured_optimum`), so raising it requires a fresh sweep - [x] Benchmark on real hardware, including the shape most likely to regress - [x] Verify greedy output is unchanged 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32207382432](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207382432)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207382289](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207382289)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [XPU][model]: Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (bge/NomicBERT/ModernBERT) + InternVL3_5
signal.text: Intel XPU support for four embedding / vision models, combined for review: `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`, `ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2`, and `OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B`. ## Motivation - **bge-base-en-v1.5** (`BertModel`) loads on XPU but returns wrong embeddings — SciFact 0, cosine vs HF 0.26-0.47. Two XPU-specific bugs in shared code affect every BERT/RoBERTa encoder on `intel_xpu`. - **nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`. - **granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache. - **InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** crashed at load (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and, once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1 (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST batching ViT tiles). ## Modifications Encoder embeddings: - `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`: honor `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY` / `DECODER_BIDIRECTIONAL` (was `causal = not is_cross_attention`). - `managers/{scheduler,tokenizer_manager,utils}.py`: preserve the trailing separator token when truncating over-length embedding inputs (gated on `not is_generation`). - `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA. - `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attn, GeGLU; SDPA. InternVL: - `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host-side `max_seqlen` into `prepare_vision_attention_metadata`; chunk the ViT forward to `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU. - `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` uses the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens` per block. - `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12). All XPU paths are guarded by `is_xpu()`; the encoder truncation change is embedding-only; decoder generation is unchanged. ## Accuracy Test Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference. Encoder — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1: | Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref | |---|---|---|---| | bge-base-en-v1.5 | 0.99997 | 0.6981 | 0.7387 | | nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) | | granite-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.000000 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 | InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16, ~14.43 GB/rank): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval: **mathvision_testmini 38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**. All four load with 0 skipped params. ## Speed Test and Profiling No change to existing code paths. Encoder fixes flip a boolean / run once per over-length request; the two new encoders are small SDPA models (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32207835753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207835753)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207835632](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207835632)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Reuse SRT Qwen vision and text modules
signal.text: ## Motivation The multimodal generation Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3, and Qwen3-VL encoders duplicated pure modules already implemented in SRT. Maintaining both copies also left the MMGen paths without reusable SRT tensor-parallel projections, embeddings, activation kernels, and checkpoint loaders. ## Modifications - Reuse SRT Qwen vision patch embeddings, MLPs, patch mergers, RMSNorm, and tensor-parallel linear layers from MMGen. - Reuse SRT Qwen2.5 text projections, split `Qwen2_5_VLMLP`, HF-semantics `RMSNorm`, and `VocabParallelEmbedding`. - Reuse SRT `SiluAndMul` and `RMSNorm` in the native Qwen3 and Qwen3-VL text paths. - Extend SRT RMSNorm kernels to flatten and restore higher-rank activations when a residual is present. This is required by diffusion text encoders with `[batch, sequence, hidden]` states. - Keep the Qwen2.5 split gate/up execution order as `act(gate) * up`; this avoids a concatenation and preserves HF numerical behavior. - Use replicated SRT linears at TP=1 and explicit TP rank/size at TP>1, while retaining the existing replicated fallback when a dimension is not TP-divisible. - Share one MMGen packed-sequence attention adapter between Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL. It remains MMGen-owned because diffusion backend selection and segmented SDPA fallback differ from SRT serving's attention contract. - Reuse SRT MRoPE in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL text attention. Keep MMGen LocalAttention and Qwen3-VL quantized linears because their diffusion runtime and quantization contracts differ from SRT serving. - Map MiniMax-H3 checkpoint `.attn.qkv.` names to the native SRT `.attn.qkv_proj.` parameters. - Keep `model.visual.blocks` and language-model layer ownership unchanged so layerwise offload and FSDP selection continue to work. - Bind each native encoder root to the TP group used to construct and shard it. One nested context now switches MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP together for construction, loading, and forward, then restores their previous values independently. ## Accuracy and Integration Tests Latest validation on H100 at exact head `0844a9a3088f3`: - Focused Qwen, encoder-folding, and group-lifecycle unit tests: `55 passed`. - The new two-GPU no-download guard uses a real SRT `RowParallelLinear` with DiT TP=1 and folded encoder TP=2. Its output matches the complete unsharded linear reference, and MMGen TP, SRT TP, and SRT attention TP all restore to size 1 after forward (`1 passed`, 24.63s). - Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL SRT MRoPE versus Transformers: FP32 maximum absolute error `2.38e-7`; BF16 maximum absolute error `0.015625` (1-2 ULP), with mean absolute error between `1.8e-4` and `4.0e-4`. - Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL batched GQA layout, three-axis positions, Transformers v5 RoPE config, and attention wiring are covered by focused tests. The full native server/pipeline encoder `fold` versus `replicate` e2e guard is in #35004. On its pre-fix runtime negative control it fails with SSIM `0.924886` and MAD `5.275228`; after the shared group fix it passes with SSIM `0.994886` and MAD `0.771159`. No consistency GT or threshold was changed. Broader component and E2E validation at parent head `6e57d71d6efe2`: - Focused GPU unit/component suite: `26 passed`, plus 2 parameterized subtests. - Qwen2.5 TP=2 MLP matches the previous MMGen implementation exactly; TP=2 embedding output is exact. - Qwen2.5 full-GEMM comparison differs only by expected BF16 TP reduction order (`max_abs=3.81e-6`). - Real Z-Image Qwen3 text component: cosine similarity `0.999898`. - Real Qwen-Image server/API case: CLIP/SSIM `1.0`, infinite PSNR, zero pixel difference; `/v1/models` success and not-found paths passed. - Real MiniMax-H3 2-GPU video E2E: minimum CLIP `0.9953`, minimum SSIM `0.9687`, minimum PSNR `43.06`. - Existing Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL vision TP=1/TP=2, layerwise-offload, component-accuracy, and Qwen-Image-Edit E2E checks remain covered. ## Performance - Qwen2.5 split text MLP, real model size, H100: paired median ratio `0.9961` versus the previous MMGen implementation. - Qwen-Image E2E: `12697.67 ms` versus `12799.17 ms` baseline. - MiniMax-H3 2-GPU E2E: `47120.89 ms` versus `47538.57 ms` baseline. - Existing full vision-tower measurements remain 1.08x faster for Qwen2.5-VL and 1.19x faster for Qwen3-VL. These measurements show no observed regression; the E2E results are within or better than their checked-in baselines. ## Checklist - [x] Full pre-commit range passed. - [x] Focused unit and weight-transfer tests passed. - [x] Validate folded SRT collectives and TP-group restoration on two GPUs. - [x] Validate TP=1, TP=2, higher-rank residual RMSNorm, layerwise offload, component accuracy, and real server E2E. - [x] Validate Qwen-Image public image/model APIs. - [x] Public CLI and model compatibility are unchanged; no documentation update is required. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32149737497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149737497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32149737388](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149737388)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: ## Summary Avoid duplicate extension metadata in non-streaming chat completion responses. ## Symptom & Reproduction - **Symptom:** Enabling `return_meta_info` duplicated requested extension metadata across `choices[*].meta_info` and response-level `sglext`. - **Reproduction:** Serialize a non-streaming response with all three metadata flags enabled. - **Expected:** Extension metadata occurs once per choice. - **Observed before the fix:** The first choice's metadata also appears in response-level `sglext`. ## Root Cause 1. `_build_chat_response` projected first-choice extension data into response-level `SglExt`. 2. `choice_meta_info` serialized the same extension data in each choice. ## Fix Skip response-level `SglExt` construction when `return_meta_info` is enabled, making each choice's `meta_info` authoritative. Keep the existing `sglext` shape unchanged when `return_meta_info` is disabled, and preserve distinct metadata for `n > 1`. ## Verification - `env PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sglang-dedupe-chat-meta-sglext/python pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: 103 passed and 38 subtests passed. - `ruff check --ignore E402 python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: passed with only the files' existing E402 bootstrap pattern excluded. - `ruff format --check python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py`: both files already formatted. ## Review Focus - `_build_chat_response`: `return_meta_info=False` must retain the legacy response-level fields. - `test_non_streaming_meta_info_omits_sglext_and_preserves_each_choice`: each choice must retain its own extension metadata without an empty or duplicated `sglext`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32133883941](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32133883941)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207655266](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207655266)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Refactor: Deprecate Prefill CP V1
signal.text: ## Motivation Prefill context parallelism still carried both the legacy and strategy-based implementations behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2`. This duplicated server-argument compatibility handling, coupled model implementations to CP internals, and left legacy paths in attention backends and DSA. This PR makes the strategy-based implementation the only prefill CP implementation and removes the version distinction. The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`. Supersedes #34983, whose base branch was deleted and therefore could not be reopened. ## Modifications - Remove `SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2` and the legacy CP server-argument aliases and compatibility rewrites. - Delete the legacy `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py` implementation. - Remove prefill CP branches from model files, including DeepSeek and Qwen MoE implementations, so modeling code no longer owns CP-specific data movement. - Remove CP v1 branches from CUDA, NPU, and MUSA attention backends and delete stale DSA v1 helpers. - Rename versioned APIs and fields, for example `is_cp_v2_active` to `is_cp_active`. - Delete v1-only and old parity tests while retaining canonical CP coverage. - Remove the v1-only Ascend/NPU prefill CP path, tests, launch recipes, and support documentation; canonical prefill CP now rejects NPU explicitly until a strategy backend exists. - Preserve DeepSeek V4 rank-local model IDs and physical-order global MoE IDs behind a model-facing execution-layout adapter. - Handle DSA CP warmup batches without speculative metadata and add regression coverage. ## Accuracy Tests Post-rebase validation on the exact final commit: - Selected CP strategy, DeepSeek V4 layout/rope, TBO, and server-argument tests on B200: 49 passed, 20 subtests passed. - Full changed-file pre-commit suite. - Python `compileall` for `python/sglang/srt` and `test/registered/cp`. - Registered-test registry validation. - Diff whitespace validation and scans confirming removal of the legacy flag, aliases, versioned CP API names, model-level CP dependencies, and stale Ascend CP documentation. - B200 DeepSeek V4 CP functional suite is being rerun on the exact post-rebase commit. Earlier functional devbox runs: - `test/registered/cp/test_dsa_prefill_cp.py`: 1/1 on H200; GSM8K score 0.946. - `test/registered/cp/test_gpt_oss_4gpu_mxfp4_cp.py`: 1/1 on B200; GPQA score 0.6566 (threshold 0.58). - Two compatible configurations in `test_gqa_prefill_cp.py`: GSM8K score 0.98 each. Environment-blocked configurations: - GQA CP4: FA3 architecture restriction on B200; the H100 retry was blocked during backend initialization. - DeepSeek V3: JIT CUDA `silu_and_mul_masked_post_quant` / NVSHMEM initialization failure before CP evaluation. - The H200 CP runner was unavailable for the final post-rebase rerun. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a legacy-path removal and API cleanup; no performance claim is made. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add/update unit tests. - [x] Update documentation. - [x] Provide available accuracy results and document environment-blocked runs. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers. 3. Trigger the relevant CP CI suites. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32207554937](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207554937)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207554689](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207554689)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NVIDIA] Fix SM107 MXFP8 activation prep
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Fix MXFP8 activation preparation for the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE backend on SM107. GPT-OSS on SM107 can reach the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE kernel without a pre-quantized route handoff. Previously, SGLang used the Triton per-token-group quantizer in this case. This does not reliably produce the activation representation expected by the FlashInfer SM107 path. The quantizer producing the activations must follow the same MXFP8 and UE8M0 layout contract as the FlashInfer MoE kernel consuming them. Using FlashInfer for both operations on SM107 avoids the incompatible producer/consumer path. The fake custom-op implementation also needs the real scale-buffer shape. Returning a placeholder one-element tensor can produce incorrect metadata during `torch.compile`. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - Use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantizer on SM107 when no route/quant handoff is available. - Preserve Kimi K3's existing fused route/quant handoff. - Preserve the existing Triton activation-quantization path on other SM10x architectures. - Preserve FlashInfer quantization for padded hidden dimensions. - Correct the FlashInfer custom-op fake scale-buffer size for both linear and swizzled layouts so `torch.compile` metadata matches the real quantizer. - Add CPU regression tests covering dispatch behavior, padded inputs, route handoff, and fake output shapes. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> * Validated GPT-OSS with real weights on SM107 with 4 focused regression tests passed on SM107. * Verified the fake quantizer reports the expected scale shape. * Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - signal.title: Fix transcription & audio-understanding for ASR/audio/speech models
signal.text: ## Motivation Fix transcription for decoder-only speech/audio models that were already present Adds /v1/audio/transcriptions support for three decoder-only speech/audio LMs, so they serve real ASR instead of falling back to the Whisper adapter: - Qwen/Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct - zai-org/GLM-ASR-Nano-2512 - ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-8b ## Modifications **New transcription adapters.** Added glmasr.py, qwen2_audio.py, granite_speech.py (registered as GlmAsr / Qwen2Audio / GraniteSpeech). Each disables language detection and implements build_sampling_params (emitting temperature + a duration-scaled max_new_tokens: max(floor, int(duration_s * 15)), so long clips aren't silently truncated while short clips use a per-model floor) and build_verbose_response (no timestamp segments; "auto" default language). Without these, resolve_adapter() falls back to the Whisper adapter and injects Whisper-only params (_detect_language, forced language/task prefix) these models don't support. **Transcription-endpoint prompt handling.** The /v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint sends text="", which carries no audio placeholder for the encoder features to fill. Added a per-processor _build_transcription_prompt() to qwen_audio.py / glmasr.py, and an audio branch + _build_audio_prompt() to transformers_auto.py (Granite), that render the model's audio placeholder via apply_chat_template when the request text is empty — fixing the empty-prompt failure while leaving the chat path unchanged. Also added audio_token_index to the generic processor's audio-token lookup. **Model-side audio-feature handling.** Rewrote GlmAsrForConditionalGeneration.get_audio_feature to reshape encoder output per 30s window and keep only the valid embeddings per window (derived from input_features_mask via the conv-subsampling + merge_factor downsampling), mirroring HF's get_audio_features. This keeps the emitted embedding count aligned with the inserted audio-placeholder tokens for variable-length / multi-window clips. Forced truncation=True for the Qwen2-Audio processor so clips longer than 30s are capped to the audio tower's fixed 3000-mel window instead of raising. **base_processor.py.** Added GraniteSpeechProcessor to the audio=-kwarg allowlist (its HF processor expects audio=, not the deprecated audios=). **Tests.** Added test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_transcription_adapters.py (CPU CI): adapter resolution per architecture + Whisper fallback, the max_new_tokens floor/duration-scaling boundary, and the verbose-response contract. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32207211055](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207211055)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32207211005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32207211005)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: moe_kernels.py, stage-2 reduce path: small SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK silently corrupts output (gsm8k=0) at low concurrency
signal.text: ## Summary On the MoRI expert-parallel backend, a small `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` **silently corrupts decode output** — the model still generates fluent-looking tokens (speculative acceptance length stays high), but the content is semantically wrong and gsm8k drops to **0.00**. The value is forwarded to MoRI's `max_num_inp_token_per_rank` with no minimum/validation, so configs that legitimately produce a small per-rank dispatch buffer (low concurrency × dp-attention × MTP) hit it with no error or warning. This is a silent correctness bug: nothing crashes, throughput even looks marginally *better*, so it is easy to ship a broken Pareto point. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x` (sglang v0.5.12.post1) - HW: AMD MI355X (CDNA, warpSize 64) - Model: DeepSeek-R1 (FP4), prefill/decode disaggregated - Decode parallelism: TP8 / EP8 / **dp-attention** / **MTP (num-draft-tokens=4)** - Backends: `--moe-a2a-backend mori --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori --deepep-mode normal` ## Symptom At decode concurrency 64 with TP8 + MTP3, the per-rank dispatch buffer works out to `64/8 * 4 = 32` tokens. The server starts, warms up, benchmarks at full speed, and produces grammatical output — but gsm8k = 0. Raising the buffer fixes it. ## Reproduction / evidence (shmoo of the env var, same config) | `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` | gsm8k (strict) | output tok/s | run | |---|---|---|---| | 32 | **0.0000** | 6312 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26913235190 | | 64 (= warpSize) | **0.0000** | 6324 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26919517564 | | 256 | **0.9424** | 6219 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26920499507 | (Run links are internal CI; the relevant log excerpts are inline below.) All three runs generate identical token volume — 640 requests, 589,927 generated tokens — so the numbers are directly comparable. Note the corrupt runs are ~1.5% *faster* (less real work), which is why this slips through perf-only validation. Eval log (256, correct): ``` [MoRI floor] DISPATCH_TOKENS=32 < floor 256; clamping to 256 Decode env: SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256 PASS: gsm8k exact_match,strict-match = 0.9424 (>= 0.85) ``` ## This is not the LL vs non-LL kernel switch `get_ep_dispatch_configs()` selects `InterNodeV1LL` vs `InterNodeV1` by comparing the dispatch size to `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256). In the failing run that threshold was set to 16, and the decode log confirms: ``` [DP+EP override] Decode: ... DISPATCH_TOKENS=8, ... INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH=16 ``` Since `32 > 16`, the **non-LL `InterNodeV1`** kernel is selected — and it still corrupts. So the bug is the per-rank buffer size itself, not the kernel variant. ## Where it originates in sglang In `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py` (v0.5.12): - The value is read with a default of 4096 and **no lower bound**: ```python self.num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank = get_int_env_var( "SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK", 4096) ``` - It is passed straight through to MoRI as `max_num_inp_token_per_rank=num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank`. - There is already a `if num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank < 128:` branch that swaps the launch config (`warp_num_per_block`), so small dispatch sizes are clearly known to be special — but that branch does **not** prevent the corruption at 32/64. ## ~~Likely mechanism (hypothesis — root cause is in MoRI)~~ — **CORRECTED, see below** ~~The MoRI dispatch kernel writes received tokens into warpSize-aligned slots: `destTokId = flagSlotId * warpSize + laneId`, into a per-PE region whose stride is `max_num_inp_token_per_rank`. When that region is smaller than warpSize (64), or smaller than the routing fan-in a rank can receive from all peers, the writes go out of bounds. Empirically warpSize (64) is necessary but not sufficient; ≥256 is needed for this config. Filed in parallel against ROCm/mori: `src/ops/dispatch_combine/internode_v1.cpp` (`DispatchInterNodeSend` / `DispatchIntraNodeBlock`). https://github.com/ROCm/mori/issues/356~~ > ### UPDATE, corrected root cause (not MoRI issue) > > The MoRI hypothesis is wrong, and `ROCm/mori#356` was closed as not-a-MoRI-issue. No out-of-bounds write in the dispatch kernel is involved. > > The actual root cause is prob in AITER's FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce path (`aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`), confirmed by @billishyahao: > > - The reduce intermediate is allocated with `torch.empty` (**uninitialized**). > - In EP, gemm2 writes only valid local-expert slots; masked (non-local) slots are never written. > - `torch.sum` over `topk` then folds those uninitialized slots in → NaN/garbage → corrupt-but-fluent output. > - Only the **M≈1024 tuning bucket** selects this reduce kernel; other buckets use a zero-init atomic accumulate, which is why M=1032/2048 were fine and only specific low-concurrency points corrupt. > > **Fixed in [ROCm/aiter#3377](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3377)** (masked gather `valid = expert_mask[topk_ids] != 0` + EP tuned-key `topk -= is_ep`), pulled into SGLang via **#27555** (AITER commit bump `6740fb7` → `7a8ff7d`). > > **Not fully resolved:** with the fix applied, conc64 passes but **conc32 and conc16 still fail** ([run](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27225030090)) — the sub-1024 M-buckets likely need the same masked-reduce treatment. Keeping this open until those are covered. ## Requested fix 1. In `moriep.py`, **enforce or validate a minimum** for `num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank` (and/or emit a clear warning) instead of silently forwarding a too-small value. 2. Revisit the `< 128` launch-config branch — it does not make small buffers correct. 3. Coordinate the actual kernel-level fix with ROCm/mori (sizing from fan-in, or asserting a minimum). At minimum, a silent correctness failure should become a loud one.
signal.author: Oseltamivir

signal.title: [Fix] DCP: advertise the logical KV-event block size
signal.text: ## Motivation Under DCP, SGLang runs two page sizes: the configured **physical** `page_size`, and a **logical** page `page_size * dcp_size` that the allocator is built with (`mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py`) and that the radix tree inherits (`mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py`). KV events are chunked by the tree's page size, so they go out at the logical width. `/server_info`'s `kv_events` descriptor advertised the **physical** `page_size`. A KV-aware router honoring the documented contract — *"subscribers MUST hash prompts at this size"* — then hashes requests at a width no emitted block can ever match. Stores apply cleanly, every lookup misses, and the router's KV hit rate is silently **exactly 0** while all local metrics look healthy. ## Modifications - Add `ServerArgs.kv_event_block_size` (property): `page_size * dcp_size`, the width events are actually emitted at. - `describe_kv_events_publisher` advertises it instead of the physical `page_size`. The `page_size` field itself is unchanged — only the advertised value is corrected. - Document that the descriptor's `dp_size` is deliberately *not* DCP-scaled: DCP shards within a rank rather than adding publishers. No working configuration changes behavior — under DCP the advertised value was unusable (hit rate 0), and without DCP the value is identical. ## Verification Measured on 4x H200 with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (`tp=4 dcp=4 page_size=64`): - **Engine only, no router:** plain `sglang.launch_server` — before, `/server_info` reported `kv_events.block_size=64` while the ZMQ wire carried `BlockStored.block_size=256`; after, it reports 256, matching the wire. - **End to end through a KV-aware router:** the equivalent consumer-side mistake gave a hit rate of **exactly 0** over six identical 1,686-token prompts, against **4.814814814814815 / 6** (the 96.3% arithmetic maximum, `5 * 26/27`) on otherwise identical no-DCP arms — including a same-attention-backend control arm, which rules out the backend. Correcting the width restored it to `5 * 6/7 = 4.285714285714286 / 6`, the arithmetic maximum for the 256-token logical page, and again to `3 * 6/7` on fresh content. - The same consumer-side bug in Dynamo's SGLang integration (reading `server_args.page_size` directly, bypassing this descriptor) was fixed independently in ai-dynamo/dynamo#12765. This PR fixes the engine's own advertised contract, so any subscriber that honors it — e.g. sgl-router, whose `BlockSizeOracle` takes its width from this field and whose hashes must reach bit-parity with SGLang's `hash_page` at that width — is correct without needing DCP awareness of its own. - **Unit tests** (`TestDcpKvEventContract`): red on `main`, green with the fix; covers `page_size=1 + dcp` (paged at `dcp_size`) and the non-DCP default. `pre-commit` passes. ## Note on scope An earlier revision of this PR also added an args-time `tp_size % dcp_size` guard. That was **dropped**: `parallel_state.py` already raises `RuntimeError("tensor_model_parallel_size (N) must be divisible by decode_context_parallel_size (M)")` during dist init, before weights load. Confirmed by launching `--tp-size 1 --dcp-size 2` on `main`. Thanks @alexnails for questioning whether that check was needed — it wasn't. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation as needed. - [x] Provide verification results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32195664272](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195664272)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195663998](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195663998)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
