signal.title: [Speculative] Fix DSpark base logits for quantized target lm_head
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving a **quantized** target model with a DSpark draft fails at startup (both eager and CUDA-graph capture) with: ``` RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (7x5120 and 2560x248320) ``` Reproduced on `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` drafting `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (RTX 5090, sglang 0.5.17 and current main). **Root cause**: DSpark dense drafts share the target's `lm_head` (`attach_shared_modules`). When the target is quantized, `lm_head.weight` is stored in a packed layout — e.g. NVFP4 stores `[vocab, 2560]` for a 5120-hidden target (5120 × 4 bit = 2560 bytes/row, with separate per-block `weight_scale`). `compute_base_logits` performs a raw `torch.matmul(hidden, weight.T)` against the packed layout, which is invalid for any quantized packing. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/models/dspark.py` — `DSparkDraftMixin.compute_base_logits`: - When `weight.shape[1] != hidden.shape[-1]` (packed layout), route through `lm_head.quant_method.apply(lm_head, hidden, bias)` — mirroring `LogitsProcessor._compute_lm_head` so the quant method's dequantize path applies. - Raise a clear `ValueError` when the lm_head is packed but carries no applicable quant method. - Unquantized targets keep the existing dense matmul path unchanged. ## Tests New CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/models/test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py` (3 cases, all passing locally): 1. packed weight routes through `quant_method.apply` (call verified via mock, returns expected logits) 2. unquantized weight still uses the dense matmul path 3. packed weight without a quant method raises `ValueError` ``` test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_routes_to_quant_method PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_packed_weight_without_quant_method_raises PASSED test_dspark_quantized_lm_head.py::TestDsparkQuantizedLmHead::test_unquantized_weight_uses_matmul PASSED ``` ## End-to-end validation With this patch, `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark` + `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` boots to `ready to roll` on an RTX 5090 (previously crashed at CUDA graph capture). Single-stream bench (random ISL 1024 / OSL 512, 20 prompts): 131.41 output tok/s, accept len 2.89/8. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32206503048](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206503048)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32206502903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206502903)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Support prefill context parallel two batch overlap for DeepSeek V4
signal.text: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 prefill context parallelism (CP) distributes long-context prefill across attention CP ranks, but introduces several per-layer CP collectives around attention and MoE. Previously, the DeepSeek V4 two-batch-overlap (TBO) path only supported non-CP DP/EP workflows: - `--enable-prefill-cp` with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` was rejected when DP attention was disabled. - CP batches were explicitly excluded by the runtime TBO gate. - Existing TBO operations only handled DP/EP communication and could not schedule CP all-gather/reduce-scatter operations. This PR enables TBO for the AMD/ROCm DeepSeek V4 DSA prefill CP path. Each eligible prefill batch is split into two sub-batches so that one sub-batch's CP MoE communication can overlap with the other sub-batch's attention and expert computation. Attention-side KV and `kv_score` all-gathers are also launched early and hidden behind projection, indexer, and compressor computation. The goal is to reduce TTFT and improve long-context prefill throughput while preserving CP-only accuracy and leaving existing CUDA and non-CP behavior unchanged. ## Modifications - Add a HIP-only CP-aware TBO forward path for DeepSeek V4: - Split each prefill batch into two independently managed sub-batches. - Rebuild CP metadata and round-robin split `hidden_states`, `positions`, and `input_ids` for each sub-batch. - Restore each sub-batch from CP layout and merge the outputs after overlapped execution. - Add a CP-specific TBO operation schedule: - Overlap one sub-batch's MoE all-gather with the other sub-batch's attention computation. - Overlap one sub-batch's reduce-scatter with the other sub-batch's MoE computation. - Use persistent buffers and stream events to safely manage asynchronous communication. - Add a duplicate `attn_cp_overlap` communicator over the same CP ranks. This allows collectives on the communication stream to execute concurrently with attention collectives on the compute stream without driving the same RCCL communicator from multiple streams, which can deadlock. - Add split-phase CP all-gather helpers: - Launch KV and `kv_score` all-gathers as soon as their inputs become available. - Delay synchronization until immediately before the gathered tensors are consumed. - Keep communication inputs alive until completion to prevent allocator reuse. - Update validation and fallback logic: - Enable CP+TBO only for HIP, DSA prefill CP with round-robin split, CP-v1, non-EP TP-MoE, single-stage PP, and valid sub-batches. - Fall back to the original eager path for unsupported or undersized batches. - Align TBO padding with both TP and CP requirements. - Preserve the existing behavior on NVIDIA/CUDA and non-CP paths. - Add an AMD 8-GPU DeepSeek V4 Pro FP4 nightly test covering CP+TBO startup, high-concurrency GSM8K accuracy, per-sub-batch CP metadata, and concurrent-communicator stability. CP+TBO overlap results ## Server command ``` #!/bin/bash set -uo pipefail ARM=${1:-cptbo} export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=${SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND:-unified_kv_triton} export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 export SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 export GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MODEL=${MODEL:-/mnt/raid0/pretrained_model/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro} CHUNK=${CHUNK:-51200} PREFILL_TOKENS=${PREFILL_TOKENS:-${CHUNK}} COMMON=( --model-path "${MODEL}" --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dp 1 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static "${MEM_FRAC:-0.9}" --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size "${CHUNK}" --max-prefill-tokens "${PREFILL_TOKENS}" --max-running-requests 256 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 ) case "${ARM}" in base | baseline) ARGS=() ;; cp) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave) ;; cptbo | cp_tbo) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-two-batch-overlap) ;; *) echo "unknown arm: ${ARM} (可选: base | cp | cptbo)" >&2 exit 2 ;; esac echo "[server] arm=${ARM} chunk=${CHUNK} max_prefill_tokens=${PREFILL_TOKENS} args=${ARGS[*]:-}" exec sglang serve "${COMMON[@]}" "${ARGS[@]}" ``` ## Accuracy Tests config | GSM8K 1319 accuracy | -- | -- cp | 0.944 cp+tbo | 0.936 ## Speed Tests and Profiling I/O = 8k/1k~256k/1k, conc=8, np=4*conc TBO's benefit scales with input length, moving from −3.6% throughput at 8k/1k to +7.2% at 256k/1k, with TTFT stabilizing at around −11% once the input reaches 64k. I/O | cp TPUT | cptbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | cptbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | cptbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 8k/1k | 3452 | 3327 | −3.6% | 1354 | 1477 | +9.1% | 19.51 | 20.18 | +3.4% 16k/1k | 6059 | 5961 | −1.6% | 2063 | 2055 | −0.4% | 20.39 | 20.77 | +1.9% 32k/1k | 10450 | 10513 | +0.6% | 3557 | 3296 | −7.3% | 21.71 | 21.83 | +0.6% 64k/1k | 16701 | 17198 | +3.0% | 6687 | 5962 | −10.9% | 24.46 | 24.28 | −0.7% 128k/1k | 23684 | 24899 | +5.1% | 13168 | 11624 | −11.7% | 30.42 | 29.83 | −1.9% 256k/1k | 29004 | 31102 | +7.2% | 27542 | 24383 | −11.5% | 43.37 | 41.74 | −3.8% I/O = 128k/1k, conc=2/4/8/16, np=4*conc At a fixed 128k input, TBO gains grow with concurrency (−1.2% → +4.6% throughput from conc 2 to 16), while TTFT improves consistently by 8–11% across all levels. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | tbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 9536 | 9424 | −1.2% | 4813 | 4417 | −8.2% | 22.25 | 22.97 | +3.2% 4 | 15534 | 15713 | +1.2% | 7663 | 7047 | −8.0% | 25.57 | 25.86 | +1.1% 8 | 22449 | 23349 | +4.0% | 13479 | 12258 | −9.1% | 32.51 | 31.96 | −1.7% 16 | 28333 | 29651 | +4.6% | 25237 | 22501 | −10.8% | 47.65 | 47.11 | −1.1% I/O = 50k/1, prefill only With decode removed, TBO reaches its full prefill-side benefit: 10–14% higher throughput and 8–12% lower TTFT at every concurrency level. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 44133 | 49299 | +11.7% | 2141 | 1941 | −9.3% 4 | 45040 | 49594 | +10.1% | 4042 | 3711 | −8.2% 8 | 45410 | 50311 | +10.8% | 8003 | 7266 | −9.2% 16 | 45536 | 51859 | +13.9% | 15683 | 13823 | −11.9% ## Checklist - signal.title: feat(kernels): generalize persistent CuTe JIT cache
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang already has a persistent CuTe JIT cache for FlashAttention, but it lives under the FlashAttention package and only supports TVM-FFI exports. Kimi-K3 KDA also uses explicit `cute.compile` calls, but its cache is process-local. ## Modifications - Move the existing cache to `sglang.kernels.jit.cute_aot_cache`. - Generalize it over consumer source roots and CuTe ABI while keeping per-key file locking. - Include the explicit `CUTE_DSL_ARCH` target, or the detected local CUDA architecture, in the source fingerprint. GPU probing remains lazy when persistence is disabled. - Publish compiled objects through a temporary path and `os.replace`, so readers never observe a partially written final object and failed exports leave no temporary artifact. - If an object fails to load, discard it while the per-key shared lock still excludes writers, then fall back to compilation. - Keep routine cache activity at debug level so enabling persistence does not add normal INFO-level server noise. - Keep FlashAttention as the TVM-FFI consumer. A small cache adapter preserves `FLASH_ATTENTION_CUTE_DSL_CACHE_*` behavior and gives `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` precedence when both configurations are present. - Add `SGLANG_CUTE_AOT_CACHE_DIR` as the shared opt-in cache root and document that it must be trusted. - Make Kimi-K3 KDA MTP the second consumer using the native CuTe ABI. - Normalize CUDA device ordinals only for disk keys so same-architecture ranks can share objects; KDA includes compute capability and indexing width in its compile key. The default remains process-local. This does not introduce rank authority, compiler monkeypatching, or kernel math changes. ## Reviewability Git detects the existing cache module as a 51%-similarity rename. The aggregate patch is 394 additions and 86 deletions across six files; 184 added lines are focused tests. The large add/delete presentation from the previous revision was caused by rename detection falling below GitHub's threshold and has been removed. ## Validation ### Focused unit and static validation - Eleven focused cache cases cover new/legacy FlashAttention environment precedence, quiet routine logging, disabled behavior, lazy architecture detection, factory/source/architecture namespacing, CUDA device ordinal normalization, both native and TVM-FFI export/load paths, atomic publication, failed-export cleanup, and invalid-object eviction. - SGLang's registered-test collector resolves the pytest file to `base-a-test-cpu`. - Black, Ruff, isort (for applicable paths), codespell, Python syntax compilation, `scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py`, and `git diff --check` pass. ### Real GPU cache validation Validated commit `e48384b39c` on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103) with Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NVIDIA CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and TVM-FFI 0.1.11. This was cache/kernel validation only; no model was loaded. - **KDA native ABI:** `TestKimiK3ComputeKernels.test_mtp_replayssm_ring` cold-compiled and exported two objects. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded both objects, passed the same output and recurrent-state checks, and left object hashes unchanged. - **FlashAttention TVM-FFI ABI:** a BF16 `[1, 64, 4, 64]` causal forward cold-compiled and exported one object. A fresh process with `cute.compile` replaced by an exception loaded it and produced the identical output SHA-256 (`780881b74eb262e7831f1f2a710c53a5ec209f52f371ec4fe51c6b43b2ff9678`). Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 was `0.001861` and max absolute error was `0.007716`. - **Corruption recovery:** the FlashAttention object was replaced with invalid bytes. The next process detected and removed it, recompiled with the same output SHA-256, and published a repaired object. A final fresh process with `cute.compile` blocked loaded the repaired object successfully. [Validation run](https://modal.com/apps/modal-flash/main/ap-3PyR14z34YcGgsm8zGdHgO) - No object hashes changed and no `.tmp.o` artifacts remained after validation. ## Speed tests and profiling No end-to-end speed benchmark is included. A warm process can load an existing FlashAttention or KDA object instead of compiling it again. ## Checklist - [x] Format code according to the project configuration. - [x] Add focused unit tests. - [x] Document the new environment variable and trust boundary. - [x] Validate native and TVM-FFI cold-to-warm round trips on a real GPU. - [x] Validate invalid-object eviction, recompilation, and repaired warm loading. - [x] Keep the cache move visible as a rename for review. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [ ] Provide an end-to-end speed benchmark (out of scope for cache validation). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32091161530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161530)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32091161307](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091161307)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Before this PR, `ModelRunner.init_threads_binding` picked the NUMA node / core group for a worker using `tp_rank`. signal.title: [Feature] Bit-exact correctness coverage for Unified Radix Cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Cache correctness is difficult to verify from model output alone. A corrupted KV block or recurrent-state checkpoint can still produce fluent text, and the resulting numerical drift can remain far below the tolerance used by accuracy and KL tests. These failures have shipped because the existing signals are approximate. Bit-exact logprob consistency turns one of these approximate signals into a correctness oracle. `kl_test_utils` evaluates the same token through prefill and decode. If both paths are batch-invariant and compute the same function, they must produce identical logprobs. Once that baseline is established, the contract for every cache-reuse path becomes: > **Any nonzero KL is a KV/state reuse bug.** This is stronger than threshold-based testing. It does not ask whether the error is large enough to matter to a benchmark. It asks whether restoring cached state is exactly equivalent to recomputing it. Bugs that previously sat below a model-specific noise floor become unambiguous regressions. Examples: - Incorrect reused state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34043, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34184, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29792 ## Foundation Bit-exactness depends on the model and execution path. Deterministic inference can remove batch-dependent kernel and communication behavior, but it cannot make two mathematically different algorithms identical. For example, Qwen3-Next uses different GDN kernels for prefill and decode, and retains a nonzero numerical floor. Inkling provides the combination needed for continuous gating. Its prefill and decode paths compute the same function, so under deterministic inference its prefill-versus-decode KL is exactly `0`. A shrunken checkpoint runs on one GPU. The model also contains `FULL`, `SWA`, and `MAMBA` cache components, so one test process exercises full KV, sliding-window, and recurrent-state reuse together. The resulting foundation has four layers: 1. deterministic execution makes repeated computation batch-invariant; 2. logprob consistency establishes an exact prefill/decode baseline; 3. cache tests apply that baseline to each state restoration path; 4. revert-then-red validation proves that each regression guard can detect the defect it claims to cover. Supporting work: - Inkling deterministic execution: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33417, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34159 - Workflow tools: [KL consistency test skill](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/.claude/skills/kl-consistency-test), https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34169 - Real-weight consistency coverage: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34168, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34356 - Per-commit guards: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34607 - Calibration and follow-up validation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34405, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653 ## Roadmap The remaining work is coverage, not a new testing method. Every feature that can save, move, or restore model state introduces a distinct correctness boundary and needs its own exact-KL test class. - [x] Base cache path - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer` - [x] Mamba `extra_buffer_lazy` - [x] HiCache multi-turn - [ ] Speculative decoding - [x] MTP https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35161 - [ ] DSpark / DFlash @alphabetc1 - Support return_logprob https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35058 - [ ] Unified memory

signal.title: [NPU] Reduce graph replay host overhead
signal.text: ## Summary - reuse a persistent, device-bound worker for NPU graph input updates instead of creating an OS thread on every replay - reuse the existing CPU mirror of speculative-decoding sequence lengths to avoid a blocking device-to-host copy per replay - preserve the device-copy fallback for callers without a host mirror ## Root cause A same-code container comparison showed that the 813 CANN/PTA/TA/Python stack exposed a host-side decode bottleneck: throughput dropped from 186.07 tok/s on 723 to 173.09 tok/s on 813. The replay path created three short-lived threads per speculative round and redundantly copied sequence lengths from device to host. The upgraded runtime amplified this latent main-code overhead. ## Performance impact On the 813 stack after this change: - exact registered test throughput: 184.52 tok/s (baseline 177.49, required >173.94) - TPOT: 5.29 ms (required <10 ms) - three manual runs averaged 182.25 tok/s ## Validation - `test/registered/npu/performance/qwen3_30b_a3b/test_npu_qwen3_30b_w8a8_1p_in3k5_out1k5_10ms.py` on CANN 9.1, torch_npu 2.10.0.post4, Python 3.12: passed - `git diff --check`: passed - Python bytecode compilation for both changed modules: passed with the workspace runtime <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32206847096](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206847096)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32206846900](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206846900)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU]Ensure tensors allocated by empty_like are contiguous
signal.text: ## Motivation `torch.empty_like(q)` inherits the memory format of `q` by default. signal.title: XPU: Enable GLM5.1 (GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM) DSA Attention
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> GLM5.1 uses Dynamic Sparse Attention (DSA/NSA) with an FP8 indexer that scores KV pages before sparse attention. This PR enables the path on XPU. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> **1. server_args.py** When GLM5.1 (or any DSA model) runs on XPU, automatically set: - `decode_attention_backend = "dsa"` — puts `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` as the decode backend inside `HybridAttnBackend`, so it can manage the DSA index K-cache and FP8 logit scoring. - `prefill_attention_backend = "dsa"` — We use the dense version of prefill MLA for now since no XPU sparse prefill kernel exists yet in sgl-kernel-xpu. - Disable `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` — the v2 topk uses TileLang/TVM JIT compilation which requires CUDA. **2. hybrid_attn_backend.py** In `HybridAttnBackend`, when the selected backend is not the decode backend (i.e. during prefill when Triton is selected), also call `decode_backend.init_forward_metadata()` and `get_indexer_metadata()` from the decode backend. This ensures the DSA decode backend (`DeepseekSparseAttnBackend`) remains responsible for the DSA indexer even during prefill passes. **3. dsa_backend.py** Guard `flashmla_metadata` computation with `not _is_xpu`. The `get_mla_metadata` function is from `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` which is CUDA-only. **4. dsa/dsa_indexer.py** Replace `torch.cuda.get_device_properties` and `torch.cuda.mem_get_info` with XPU-aware equivalents in `_get_mqa_logits_budget_bytes`. **5. rotary_embedding/base.py** In `forward_xpu`, handle 2D input tensors `(N, head_size)` for the fallback `sgl_kernel.rotary_embedding` kernel which expects 3D `(N, num_heads, head_size)`. The DSA indexer passes a single-head `k_rope` as 2D. **6. jit_kernel/dsa/__init__.py** Guard the CuteDSL import (NVIDIA CUDA DSL) on XPU, matching the existing ROCm guard. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> N/A since the original model is too big for BMG. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> N/A since the original model is too big for BMG. ## Checklist - [X] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [X] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Refactor] New EPD
signal.text: ## Motivation The EPD encoder had grown into a single 4464-line `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py` that owned the FastAPI application, the DP launcher, the request scheduler, CPU preprocessing, the GPU forward, and both transfer backends at the same time. That coupling caused three concrete problems: **1. Duplicated orchestration.** HTTP non-DP and DP workers each maintained their own copy of encode scheduling, batch/direct branching, backend detection, metadata publication, embedding staging, send scheduling, error handling, resource release and metrics updates. On top of that: - single-request and batch encode had two separate implementations; - Mooncake, ZMQ-to-scheduler and ZMQ-to-tokenizer each carried near-identical send logic; - `send` and `release` were tightly coupled, and embedding cleanup was scattered across the normal, error and timeout branches. **2. Unsafe resource lifetimes.** Because `send` implicitly released embeddings and cleanup lived in several places, concurrent encode / send / release had no ordering guarantee: a release racing an in-flight forward could tear down state that a pending send still needed, and a failed encode could leave a `send` waiting forever. **3. No layer to build on.** There was no protocol-neutral home for scheduling, so gRPC could not reuse the HTTP backend topology, and neither the CPU preprocessing nor the HTTP layer could be replaced by a Rust implementation. This PR restructures the encoder into a package with explicit layers and unifies everything after `receive` into a single pipeline, while keeping the external HTTP/gRPC surface unchanged. ## Modifications ## 2. One inference lifecycle for every path Everything after `receive` now follows a single chain, identically for HTTP non-DP and for DP workers: ``` receive (protocol-specific entry point) → execute_encode_pipeline → MMEncoder.encode / batch_encode → acquire encode ref → preprocess → publish metadata → model forward → stage embedding → release encode ref → delivery.send → release_request ``` - `encode()` becomes a batch-of-one call into `batch_encode()`, so there is no second encode implementation. `EncoderScheduler` only decides *whether* requests coalesce into a batch. - `execute_encode_pipeline()` owns metrics and tracing, direct-vs-batched dispatch, metadata publication, the `MMEncoder` call, final metadata sync, the ZMQ synchronous send or the Mooncake metadata response, and resource release on the normal, error and timeout paths. - `ReqState` holds the whole per-request lifecycle: `embedding_data`, `embedding_ready`, `active_encodes`, `active_sends`, `release_requested`, `preserve_metadata_on_release`, `lifecycle_condition`, driven by `_acquire_encode_ref()` / `_release_encode_ref()`. The resulting guarantees: - a release issued during encode cannot delete request state early; - a release waits until `active_sends == 0`; - once a release is requested, new sends are rejected; - a shared embedding is freed only after all destinations have finished; - a failed encode still stages the error, so a waiting `send` can never block forever. - `EncoderDelivery` isolates the backend differences. The previous `ZmqSchedulerDelivery` and `ZmqTokenizerDelivery` collapse into one `ZmqDelivery` parameterized by `cleanup_receive_state`; `self.transfer_backend` / `self.use_mooncake` are cached on `MMEncoder` instead of re-reading `server_args.encoder_transfer_backend` all over the code. - `embedding_to_send.pop()`, `discard_embedding()`, handler-`finally` cleanup, the Mooncake callback cleanup and the ZMQ rendezvous cleanup all collapse into `release_request()`. - Mooncake marks an embedding ready **only after the CUDA stream is synchronized**, so an RDMA read can no longer observe a GPU buffer whose write has not landed. Global-cache embeddings keep their existing per-send registration semantics. ### 3. Metadata is published right after preprocess Every backend publishes embedding shape, dtype and size as soon as preprocessing completes — before the forward runs. At that point `ReqState.embedding_data` holds a metadata placeholder; the real embedding is staged and validated afterwards, which is what sets `embedding_ready`. For Mooncake non-DP this lets the receiver call `/scheduler_receive_meta_data`, then allocate and register its landing buffer **in parallel with the encoder forward**; the RDMA transfer itself still waits for `embedding_ready`. ZMQ publishes the same metadata today, but has no early consumer yet. ### 4. Preprocessing metadata consolidated `EncoderPreprocessResult` returns `mm_inputs`, `grid_thw` and `token_counts` together. Grid normalization and patch/token counting move out of `MMEncoder` into `EncoderPreprocessor`, so `process_mm_items` parses the grid exactly once and the direct, cache, Mooncake and batch paths reuse the same result. `slice_embedding` and `_encode_missing` no longer recompute token counts from the grid. ### 5. Receiver: one embedding pool for both backends - `EmbeddingPool` absorbs `MooncakeEmbeddingPool` and gains `try_stage` / `release_on_gc`. When `SGLANG_EMBEDDING_POOL_SIZE_MB` is set explicitly, `zmq_to_scheduler` also keeps received embeddings resident in the GPU pool: zero-copy per-modality views, slot lifetime bound to `mm_inputs` garbage collection, and a `PENDING` retry when the pool is full. **Default behaviour is unchanged** — the 4096 MB default still applies to Mooncake only. - RDMA buffer release becomes an ownership transfer to the receiving thread, which removes an up-to-1800 s `join` block on the scheduler main thread. - `WaitingMMRequestBase` (ABC) unifies `recv_embedding`; the backend differences shrink to three abstract methods — `send_encode_request`, `_extract_embedding_from_buffer`, `_prepare_embedding_buffer`. Seven separate failure paths merge into `_fail_and_release`, and the classes are renamed off "Image" into the `Zmq` / `Grpc` / `RDMA` families. - Dead code on the `zmq_to_tokenizer` path is removed. ## EPD performance results ### Common workload - 4 random 1080p JPEG images per request - Random input length 1024, output length 64 - Temperature 0, request rate `inf` - Radix cache and MM global cache disabled - Paired values below are `main/new_epd` ## Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct ### Test setup - One 8×H20 node - Encoder TP1 on GPU 0–1; Language TP1 on GPU 2 - Encoder/Language memory fraction: 0.60 - `single`: client concurrency 1, scheduler max batch 1, 8 requests per round - `batch`: client concurrency 4, scheduler max batch 4, 16 requests per round - signal.title: Sync FlashInfer autotune tactic choice across TP ranks
signal.text: ## Motivation FlashInfer's autotuner times every candidate tactic on the rank's own GPU and keeps whichever came out fastest. That works fine on one GPU. With TP > 1 each rank runs that search on its own, and the ranks don't come out the same. Measured on `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300 (sm103), flashinfer 0.6.17. The per-rank tactic caches sglang already writes (`rank_tp{0..3}_pp0_dp0.json`) show it directly: | | Tuned shape buckets | Diverging across ranks | |---|---|---| | Before | 20 | **20 / 20** | | After | 20 | **0 / 20** | Every tuned `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` shape landed on a different tactic somewhere, and not just as a tie-break — at m=16 rank 0 took a tile-8 tactic while ranks 1–3 took tile-16. Same shape, different tile size. Dumping the autotuner's per-tactic timings per rank explains it. Each rank recorded 12,188 measurements, the same count on all four, so the tuning loop is already walking in step; what differs is the numbers it walks away with: | m | candidates | same-tactic spread across ranks | gap best → runner-up | tactics within noise of best | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 920 | 3.5% | 2.14% | 5 | | 8 | 920 | 2.9% | 0.43% | 25 | | 16 | 920 | 1.2% | 0.08% | 28 | | 256 | 920 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 10 | | 4096 | 50 | 0.7% | 0.14% | 6 | The last two columns are the whole story. In all 20 buckets the gap between the winner and the runner-up is smaller than the noise on a single tactic's own measurement, and anywhere from 2 to 28 candidates sit inside that noise. `argmin` over a field like that is a coin flip, which is why divergence is 20/20 rather than occasional, and why it's worst at small `m` where the kernel runs ~20 µs and jitter dominates. It costs something, too. Scored against the consensus best — the tactic that wins on the mean of all four ranks' timings — the worst rank was +2.45% off at m=1, and +0.63% off averaged across buckets. Once the timings are shared, every rank lands on the consensus best and that gap closes to zero. ## Modifications - `_autotune_tactic_sync_group` hands FlashInfer the TP group's `cpu_group` through `set_autotune_process_group`. FlashInfer then all-reduces each tactic's measured time, so every rank minimizes over the same numbers instead of its own. TP is the right scope, since those ranks run the same dummy forward; a lone rank has nobody to agree with and tunes without a group. - `_autotune_process_group` wraps the `autotune()` block and puts the previous group back on the way out, so a nested tuning pass can't leave a stale one behind. - Sharing the timings only helps if the ranks start from the same cache, because a cache hit skips a profile and knocks them out of step. `_drop_diverged_autotune_cache` all-gathers a digest of what each rank would actually load — the cache file plus the environment stamp `load_configs` checks it against, since a stamp mismatch makes FlashInfer discard the file wholesale — and deletes the caches when those digests disagree. - The extend pass used to swallow a rank-local OOM and carry on. Tuning is collective now, so carrying on would strand the other ranks inside the reduce; the OOM is re-raised whenever a sync group is active. - `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py` (CPU suite) covers the digest's load-decision semantics, plus the cache gate itself over a real 2-rank gloo group and real files: matching caches survive, diverged ones are dropped on every rank, and so are caches that differ only in their metadata stamp. ## Accuracy Tests GPQA diamond on gpt-oss-120b TP=4, reasoning effort low, temperature 1.0. Each run grades 1,584 samples — 198 questions, eight shuffles each — and the whole run is repeated: | | Runs | Mean | |---|---|---| | Before | 60.86 / 63.64 / 61.93 / 61.87 | **62.1** | | After | 63.26 / 62.25 / 63.19 | **62.9** | The sides overlap: 2.8 points of spread before, 1.0 after, 0.8 points between the means. Tactic selection picks among kernels FlashInfer treats as interchangeable for a given shape, and the scores agree. ## Speed Tests and Profiling `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, TP=4, 4x GB300, clean autotune cache for each configuration. "Before" is the same build without the cross-rank reduction. Single stream, `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 --warmup-requests 8 --flush-cache`, three repetitions: | | Output tok/s | Mean E2E (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---| | Before | 508.74 / 509.99 / 509.95 → **509.56 ± 0.72** | 2008.1 | 1.94–1.95 | | After | 510.60 / 510.61 / 510.83 → **510.68 ± 0.13** | 2003.7 | 1.94 | At concurrency 32 (1k in / 512 out, 128 prompts) total throughput went 22,956 → 23,130 tok/s. Both deltas — +0.22% and +0.8% — are small enough that the honest claim is no regression rather than a speedup, though they point the same way the tactic-cost numbers above predict. The clearer effect is stability: run-to-run spread tightened about 5x (±0.13 vs ±0.72 tok/s), which is what you'd expect once all four ranks are running the same kernel. Tuning wall-clock goes 79 s → 106 s from the extra per-tactic reduction. That's paid once — the result is cached, and a warm restart reuses it with no retune and no cache drop. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — nothing user-facing to document. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32151944979](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151944979)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32151944469](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151944469)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Weight Cache] Support static DP/EP layouts
signal.text: ## Motivation Weight-cache daemons and engines must construct identical model-parallel layouts before CUDA IPC can safely map a cached MoE shard. The existing daemon launcher rejected `dp_size > 1`, preventing static DP/EP deployments from using the daemon-backed weight cache. This change adds static DP/EP layout support to the CUDA IPC weight-cache path. It is the implementation foundation for the DP/EP roadmap in #33522. ## Modifications - Propagate static DP/EP, MoE DP, attention DP, MoE A2A, and DeepEP-mode configuration from the engine into weight-cache daemons. - Initialize daemon-side model-parallel and MoE state with the same static layout as the engine. - Extend `CacheConfig` with MoE DP/EP shard identity and layout fields, so daemon/client compatibility validation rejects incompatible shards. - Fix static Mooncake EP dispatch to use an all-active rank mask when Elastic EP state is absent. - Route Qwen3 MoE through the existing DeepEP-class backend predicate so Mooncake uses the EP execution path. - Add CPU coverage for MoE shard-rank calculation, extended cache fingerprints, and daemon DeepEP-mode forwarding. The implementation supports static layouts. Dynamic expert placement, EPLB, redundant experts, and recovery lifecycle ownership remain roadmap work. ## Accuracy Tests - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_cache_protocol.py` - `29 passed` - Eight-GPU Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 daemon IPC serving with `TP=DP=EP=8`, Mooncake low-latency A2A, DP attention, and DP LM head. - 8 daemons exported IPC handles. - 8 schedulers logged `Loaded model via IPC`. - A deterministic completion generated `Paris` for `The capital of France is`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This change establishes static DP/EP correctness and does not claim a new performance result. ## Checklist - [x] Format modified Python files with Black; CI will run the repository pre-commit hooks. - [x] Add unit tests according to [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32106334235](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32106334235)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32206259427](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32206259427)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(lora): build the MoE LoRA align JIT kernel on ROCm
signal.text: ## Problem The MoE LoRA align kernel is compiled through the JIT path, which invokes `hipcc` directly on ROCm instead of running the AOT hipify step. The source therefore fails first on `cub/cub.cuh`, then on CUDA-only runtime names and the kernel-pointer type expected by `hipFuncSetAttribute`. This kernel is used by the MoE LoRA prefill path, so the failure prevents ROCm MoE LoRA serving from starting. ## Solution - Select `hipcub` under `USE_ROCM` and keep the existing `cub::BlockScan` call through a local namespace alias. - Map the three CUDA device/function attribute names to their HIP equivalents in the shared JIT compatibility header. - Convert the kernel function pointer with the same C++20 `std::bit_cast<const void *>` pattern already used by another ROCm JIT kernel. - Register the existing align-kernel test for the AMD JIT suite. CUDA keeps the original include and runtime API path. ## Validation On `rocm/sgl-dev:miles-rocm720-mi35x`, starting from a cold JIT cache: - `_jit_moe_align_module(torch.int32)` compiled successfully on final head `b0075436d`; - `test/registered/jit/test_moe_lora_align_block_size.py`: 32 passed; - final 4x MI350X combined run with SGLang #34701 and Bridge #28 passed the Bridge ROCm contract test, trained per-expert gpt-oss MoE LoRA, saved mixed-stub optimizer shards, restored them on all four ranks, and completed a second training job. The PR intentionally targets `sglang-miles` (`cb05a44f3`), not `main`. Local final-head validation is complete; maintainer-triggered AMD CI remains a merge gate.

signal.title: fix(moe): narrow global expert IDs using the built runner
signal.text: ## Problem `StandardDispatcher` decides whether the AITER path keeps expert IDs global from the configured MoE backend. A quantization method may build a different runner: on ROCm, compressed-tensors W4A16 can be configured as `auto` while constructing a Triton runner. With EP=4, the dispatcher then keeps global IDs up to 383, but the Triton align kernel allocates for 96 local experts. Warmup writes outside that buffer and terminates all four ranks with an illegal-address fault. ## Solution Record the backend only after `MoeRunner` is constructed successfully. The dispatcher keeps its existing AITER inference, then uses the built runner only as negative evidence: ```text new_use_aiter_runner = old_use_aiter_runner and (runner is unknown or runner is AITER) ``` This can only disable an unsafe AITER/global-ID decision; it cannot enable one that was previously disabled. The separate `skip_local_expert_mapping` rules for FlashInfer consumers remain unchanged. A complete namespace capability for that mirror case is a separate follow-up, not part of this ROCm Triton fix. ## Validation On 4x MI350X with the two-layer Kimi-K2.5 checkpoint: - base `sglang-miles@cb05a44f3`: warmup ended in repeated `hipErrorIllegalAddress` / error 700, exit 137; - final branch head `5db65a647`: `/health_generate` became ready, `/generate` returned tokens, and the log contained no memory fault; - `test/registered/unit/lora/test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`: 39 passed (plus 4 subtests), including successful and failed runner-construction state tests; - the final combined MoE LoRA save/resume run with #34702 and Bridge #28 also completed; - SGLang pre-commit hooks passed on every changed file. The PR targets `sglang-miles`, not `main`. Local final-head validation is complete; maintainer `run-ci` / `bypass-maintenance` labels and AMD CI remain merge gates.

signal.title: [AMD] Keep the PTX-inline-asm diffusion norm fusions off on ROCm (fix FLUX warmup crash)
signal.text:
## Motivation FLUX.1-dev dies mid-warmup on ROCm, so the server never becomes ready and `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd*` fails `test_diffusion_generation[flux_image_t2i]` — see run [31519319449](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31519319449/job/93872280540), cluster R338 in [bingxche/sglang-ci-bot#164](https://github.com/bingxche/sglang-ci-bot/issues/164): ``` Warmup requests: 0%| | 0/1 [00:00= standalone files (7)` (R323, #34328), and the one failing `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd` shard is `TestLMHeadFP32::test_flag_true_bf16_activations`, identical in both runs. CUDA-side, the kernel-unit stage carrying these tests passed. That evidence came from `pr-test-amd.yml`, which no longer has a `pull_request` trigger on main (it is now the daily ROCm 7.0 shadow). This revision is rebased onto current main so the actual PR gate, `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, exercises it — same guard, same eager fallback, and the `multimodal-gen-test-1-gpu-amd-rocm720` job is the one that reported the original failure. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No effect on CUDA. On ROCm the affected sites run the eager aten chain they were already falling back to whenever the guards rejected a shape; the fused kernels were never able to execute there. The observable effect is the 49m45s → 30m32s shard time above, which is just the removed hang. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

signal.title: feat(bench): add `--insecure` to skip TLS verification
signal.text: ## Motivation Benchmarking against a server behind a self-signed certificate or an internal CA currently fails *silently*: every health check (readiness poll, model discovery, `/server_info`, cache flush) raises an `SSLError` that `wait_for_endpoint` swallows, so the bench exits with only "Server did not become ready" — no hint that TLS verification is the cause. There is no way to benchmark such servers without changing CA trust at the system level. ## Modifications - Added a `--insecure` flag to `python -m sglang.bench_serving` that disables TLS certificate verification and is propagated as `verify=False` (requests) / `ssl=False` (aiohttp connector) on every server-bound call in `serving.py`: readiness poll, cache flush, `/server_info` (x2), `/v1/models`, `/model_info`, and the per-request bench session. - `wait_for_endpoint` now surfaces the underlying exception when the server never becomes ready, so a self-signed-cert SSLError is diagnosable instead of invisible. - Added `--insecure` / `BenchArgs.insecure` to `one_batch_server.py` and threaded `verify=` through every requests call (metrics, cache flush/warmup, the request itself, `/server_info`). - Added a `verify_ssl` parameter to `endpoint.py`'s `server_is_up` / `launch_or_reuse_server` / `acquire_endpoint`. - Added `--insecure` to the standalone `python -m sglang.profiler` CLI and a `verify` parameter to `run_profile()`. - signal.title: [Feature] Restore Double Sparsity attention backend on latest main
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> The Double Sparsity (DS) attention backend was added in #1459 (Oct 2024) but has been unmaintained for ~18 months. It stopped working on latest `main` due to: 1. **Piecewise CUDA graph not disabled for DS** — `_handle_piecewise_cuda_graph` (server_args.py) had 18 auto-disable conditions for various features but DS was missing. The server crashed during `init_piecewise_cuda_graphs` because the DS backend doesn't implement CUDA graph lifecycle methods. 2. **Forward method signature drift** — `base_attn_backend.py` and `radix_attention.py` began forwarding `**kwargs` to backend forward methods (for `q_rope`, `k_rope`, `sinks`). Every other backend was updated; DS was not. 3. **KV pool memory accounting broken** — `DoubleSparseTokenToKVPool` never called `_finalize_allocation_log()` or implemented `get_kv_size_bytes()`, leaving `mem_usage` at 0 and omitting the `label_buffer` from capacity reporting. 4. **Output view dimension bug** — Sparse decode branch used `qk_head_dim` instead of `v_head_dim` for the output tensor view (latent bug, silently correct for Llama where they're equal). ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ### `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` - Add gate in `_handle_piecewise_cuda_graph` to auto-disable piecewise compile when `enable_double_sparsity` is set ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/double_sparsity_backend.py` - Add `**kwargs` to `forward_extend` and `forward_decode` signatures (matching all other backends) - Fix sparse decode output view: `qk_head_dim` → `v_head_dim` ### `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py` - Add `get_kv_size_bytes()` to `DoubleSparseTokenToKVPool` (counts k_buffer + label_buffer + v_buffer) - Call `_finalize_allocation_log(size)` at end of `__init__` ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> `python test/manual/test_double_sparsity.py` passes (MMLU score = 0.75, threshold = 0.65 ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> **Short decode (input=512, output=128):** | Config | Output tok/s | Req/s | Mean E2E (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |--------|-------------|-------|---------------|----------------| | Default (flashinfer + CUDA graph) | 3,796 | 59.6 | 999 | 16.0 | | Triton (no CUDA graph, fair baseline) | 2,950 | 46.3 | 1,270 | 20.3 | | **Double Sparsity** | 2,856 | 44.9 | 1,314 | 20.0 | **Long decode (input=512, output=1024):** | Config | Output tok/s | Req/s | Mean E2E (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | |--------|-------------|-------|---------------|----------------| | Default (flashinfer + CUDA graph) | 6,245 | 12.0 | 4,838 | 9.29 | | Triton (no CUDA graph, fair baseline) | 5,194 | 10.0 | 5,798 | 11.13 | | **Double Sparsity** | 4,565 | 8.8 | 6,495 | 12.46 | DS shows 3-12% throughput regression vs fair baseline on H100 due to `torch.gather`/`torch.topk` overhead and lack of CUDA graph support. DS is expected to be more beneficial on bandwidth-constrained GPUs, very long contexts, and larger models. Performance optimization is planned for follow-up work. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Add fmha_v2 attention backend for SM90/120
signal.text: ## Motivation Enables TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 prefill attention backend for SM90/120. This backend is more performant than the current default (FA3), and also enables skip-softmax feature, which can further boost performance for long-context / applications where attention output is sparse. ## Modifications Baseline enablement of trtllm's fmha_v2 prefill kernel for SM90/120. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 is needed for further perf improvement, and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32268 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32269 are used for the MTP accuracy reporting. ## Accuracy Tests ``` python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model /SGL/models/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8 \ --tp 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --disable-radix-cache --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 \ --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --attention-backend trtllm_mha \ --trust-remote-code --port 30000 # --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 ``` | Config | KV dtype | Score | Repeat range | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 | bf16 | 0.725 | 0.712-0.742 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | bf16 | 0.723 | 0.702-0.753 | | FA3 + MTP | bf16 | 0.734 | 0.712-0.758 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (fa3 verify) | bf16 | 0.721 | 0.707-0.732 | | FA3 | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.727 | 0.707-0.747 | | fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | **fp8_e4m3** | 0.724 | 0.682-0.753 | ### MTP Add to server launch: `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` | Config | Accept len | Accept rate | GPQA-20 score | |---|---|---|---| | FA3 + MTP (bf16) | 2.37 (2.35) | 0.46 (0.45) | 0.750 | | fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (bf16) | 2.45 (2.30) | 0.48 (0.43) | 0.700 | | pure trtllm_mha + MTP w/ XQA mask fix (bf16, 10q) | 2.20 | 0.40 | 0.70 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling The e2e performance is not improved with just this PR because it requires a large copy operation before the compute kernel to interleave KV. https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3575 and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32272 address this issue. Unit Kernel Measurements show ~15% improvement over FA3 over a variety of problem sizes, reaching 20% at small problems. ### Skip-Softmax This feature can provide additional speedup, especially for long-context inference where the attention logits are sparse. We define the threshold factor `\lambda := a / L` where a is a hyperparameter, and L is the sequence length. To demonstrate the potential speedup, we keep a = 1000 here for simplicity. | ISL | Effective threshold (1000 / ISL) | bf16 gain | fp8 gain | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k | 0.122 | +1.8% | +0.2% | | 32k | 0.031 | +5.2% | +1.7% | | 128k | 0.008 | +12.9% | + 3.5% | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: perf(vit): thread pre-computed max_seqlen to eliminate per-layer .item() sync
signal.text: ## Motivation In the ViT attention path, `max_seqlen` was computed on every attention layer via `seq_lens.max().item()`, which triggers a GPU-CPU synchronization each time. This is redundant since `max_seqlen` is the same across all layers and can be computed once upfront. ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k25.py`** - In `MoonViT3dEncoder.forward()`, change `max_seqlen = lengths.max()` to `max_seqlen = int(lengths.max().item())` so `max_seqlen` is pre-computed as a Python int once, rather than leaving it as a GPU tensor. - In `MoonViTEncoderLayer.forward()`, pass `max_seqlen=max_seqlen` to `self.attn()` so the pre-computed value is propagated down. - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/vision.py`** - In `VisionFlash3Attention.forward()` and `VisionFlash4Attention.forward()`, first attempt to retrieve `max_seqlen` from `kwargs.get("max_seqlen", None)`. Only fall back to computing it from `cu_seqlens` when the kwarg is not provided, maintaining backward compatibility. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not alter any computation logic — `max_seqlen` remains the same value regardless of whether it is pre-computed or computed per-layer. No accuracy impact expected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling with item: no item: ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(sm120): NVFP4 NaN from E4M3 scale overflow + 3D tensor shape crashes
signal.text: ## Summary Three fixes for NVFP4 quantized models on SM120 GPUs (RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000): ### 1. E4M3 Scale Factor NaN (`modelopt_quant.py`) CUTLASS FP4 GEMM kernels on SM120 produce NaN when an E4M3 scale factor has uint8 value 127 (E4M3 max = 448.0). This affects all NVFP4 models on all SM120 hardware. **Fix:** Clamp E4M3 scale factors to uint8 126 (= 416.0, <2% precision loss). Uses unconditional `.clamp()` instead of conditional `.max()` check, which also fixes CUDA graph capture (`.max()` forces GPU-to-CPU sync that crashes graph capture with `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`). ### 2. 3D Tensor Output Shape (`compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py`) `output_shape = [x.shape[0], w_n]` assumes 2D input. During serving, inputs can be 3D `[batch, seq, hidden]`, causing `RuntimeError: shape '[1, 3456]' is invalid for input of size 8709120`. **Fix:** `output_shape = list(x.shape[:-1]) + [w_n]` preserves all leading dimensions. Changed `.view()` to `.reshape()` for non-contiguous tensors. ### 3. CUTLASS FP4 MM 2D Assertion (`nvfp4.py`) `assert a.ndim == 2` in `cutlass_scaled_fp4_mm()` crashes when tensors arrive as 3D during batch processing. **Fix:** Reshape 3D inputs to 2D before the CUTLASS kernel call, reshape output back after. ## Benchmark (RTX 5090, Gemma 4 26B MoE NVFP4) | Config | Single User | 30 Concurrent Users | |--------|-------------|-------------------| | Before (crashes) | N/A | N/A | | **After (with CUDA graphs)** | **143 tok/s** | **2,783 tok/s aggregate, p95 3.2s** | Tested with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4` on RTX 5090 32GB, `--quantization compressed-tensors --fp4-gemm-backend cutlass --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16`. ## Test Plan - [x] Tested on RTX 5090 (SM120) with Gemma 4 26B MoE NVFP4 - [x] Single user generation: 143 tok/s, coherent output - [x] 30 concurrent users: 2,783 tok/s aggregate, p95 latency 3.2s - [x] CUDA graphs enabled and working - [x] No NaN in outputs across extended generation - [ ] Needs testing on non-SM120 hardware to verify no regression

signal.title: [CI] Install protoc + Rust toolchain in rerun-test-cpu
signal.text: ## Summary - `rerun-test.yml`'s `rerun-test-cpu` job was running `uv pip install -e \"python[dev]\"` without first installing `protoc` or the Rust toolchain, so builds of the bundled `rust/sglang-grpc` extension (added in #22736) failed with `Could not find \`protoc\``. - Mirror `pr-test.yml:646-652` by invoking the shared `scripts/ci/utils/install_protoc.sh` and `scripts/ci/utils/install_rustup.sh` utilities before the pip install step. ## Context Example failure: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24679201427/job/72171535463 — the CPU rerun job dies at the `Install dependencies` step with: ``` Error: Could not find \`protoc\`. ``` The CUDA rerun job already goes through `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_dependency.sh`, which installs both tools, so only the CPU path was broken. ## Test plan - [ ] Trigger a `rerun-test-cpu` run and confirm the `Install protoc` + `Install Rust toolchain` steps succeed and the subsequent pip install now builds `rust/sglang-grpc`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Fix] Land the decode mamba checkpoint depth on the tree page under DCP
signal.text: ## Motivation A donated mamba checkpoint is only reusable at a depth the radix tree can name. `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` floor the insert key with `page_aligned(tree_page)`, so a checkpoint taken off that grid is attached to the *preceding* node while its state already covers tokens past it — a later request matching that node resumes the linear-attention recurrence mid-stream and then re-consumes those tokens. Silent, no assert, wrong output. #34808 fixed this for the **extend** path with `mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page)`. The **decode** path picks its depth from `--mamba-track-interval` instead, and that arg: - has one guard, `assert mamba_track_interval % view.page_size == 0` (`server_args.py`), against the **configured** page; - is never resolved anywhere — `grep mamba_track_interval` over `arg_groups/` and `configs/` is empty. Under DCP the tree allocates on `page_size * dcp_size` (`kv_cache_builder.py`: `page_size=... else token_to_kv_pool_allocator.page_size`), so that guard stops implying the invariant. **Break condition:** `mamba_track_interval % (page_size * dcp_size) != 0`. | page | dcp | tree page | interval | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 64 | 4 | 256 | 256 | ok | | 64 | 8 | **512** | 256 | **broken** | | 128 | 4 | 512 | 256 | broken | | 256 | 2 | 512 | 256 | broken | `test_kimi_k3_b300.py::TestKimiK3B300` (`--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8 --enable-hierarchical-cache`) is on the broken row today: Kimi-K3 DCP forces `cutedsl_mla`, which pins `page_size` to 64, and `KimiK3Config.text_config` is a `KimiLinearConfig` so the tree carries a `MAMBA` component. The tree pages at 512 while decode checkpoints every 256, so every odd multiple of 256 names a depth no node carries. Every other DCP hybrid config in tree is page 64 × dcp 4, where `64 * 4 == 256` — the default interval — and the two grids line up by coincidence. That is also why the DCP HiCache KL case (#35380) cannot catch this. ## Modifications `mamba_track_grid(tree_page)` beside `mamba_checkpoint_grid` — the same `lcm`, carrying the requested interval as well: ```python def mamba_track_grid(tree_page: int) -> int: return math.lcm( mamba_checkpoint_grid(tree_page), get_exec().mamba.mamba_track_interval ) ``` Read at the sites that pick a checkpoint depth: `schedule_batch.prepare_for_decode`, the three `batch_result_processor` boundary sites, and the spec verify/prepare paths in `spec_utils`, `dspark_worker_v2`, `dflash_worker_v2`. Every one of them already holds a `ScheduleBatch`, so the page comes off `batch.tree_cache` exactly the way `_mamba_radix_cache_v2_req_prepare_for_extend` already takes it. Pure derivation — nothing is mutated, and `server_args.mamba_track_interval` keeps the value the operator typed. Going through `mamba_checkpoint_grid` rather than just rounding onto the page keeps the decode depth chunk-aligned too, which the extend path relies on: a decode-donated depth becomes the prefix of a later extend, and `_force_track_h` asserts `i % mamba_cache_chunk_size == 0` there. Two readers stay on the raw arg because they are flush/write cadence rather than checkpoint depth: `hybrid_linear_attn_backend`'s ReplaySSM force-flush mask, where a finer grid remains a superset of the snapshot steps it has to cover, and Inkling's `sconv`, which holds only a `ForwardBatch` and has no DCP coverage. ## Accuracy Tests Behaviour changes for exactly one shipped config: Kimi-K3 TP8/DCP8 + HiCache, grid 256 -> 512. That halves KDA checkpoint frequency there and is the correct frequency — the 256-boundary checkpoints were being attached to the wrong node. Verified unchanged for page 64 x dcp 4, page 32 x dcp 4 (tree 128), and every non-DCP config. New CPU unit case in `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py`, beside #34808's extend cases since it is the same invariant from the other end. **Draft because I have not run the tests** — no sglang install on the machine I wrote this on. `py_compile`, isort, ruff, black and codespell pass. Undrafting once CI runs the unit case. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32198960136](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32198960136)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32198960077](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32198960077)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix double-reduce in DeepseekV2MoE with flashinfer_cutedsl + EP + DP-attention
signal.text: ## Motivation Running `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-NVFP4` with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutedsl --enable-dp-attention --ep-size N --dp-size N` (N>1) hit two separate bugs. **Bug 1 — double-reduce on MoE output.** Pure TP and EP without DP-attention both worked; only `cutedsl × EP × DP-attention` produced gibberish. Root cause: the MoE output was reduced **twice**. 1. `DeepseekV2MoE.forward_normal` / `forward_normal_dual_stream` unconditionally ran `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` on the MoE output. 2. When `should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` was True (cutedsl + DP-attention + `EP == DP`), `LayerCommunicator._scatter_hidden_states` additionally performed `reduce_scatterv`, which also summed across TP ranks. The result was scaled by the TP world size, corrupting every token. The cutlass fp4-allgather path already had a symmetric guard (`not should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`); the cutedsl reduce-scatterv path was simply missing the same guard. **Bug 2 — `max_num_tokens` under-sized in CuteDSL wrapper under DP-attention.** With CUDA graph enabled, `ensure_cutedsl_wrapper` sized the wrapper with `max(cuda_graph_max_bs, chunked_prefill_size)`. But when `--enable-dp-attention` is set, `chunked_prefill_size` has already been divided by `dp_size` in `server_args`, while the MoE layer receives hidden states gathered across all DP ranks (i.e. per-rank tokens × `dp_size`). The mismatch crashed the worker with `ValueError: num_tokens (N) exceeds max_num_tokens (N/dp_size)` during prefill/warmup. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py`: in both `forward_normal` and `forward_normal_dual_stream`, add `and not should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` to the all-reduce guard so the reduction is only performed by `reduce_scatterv` in the communicator. The two guards are mutually exclusive by construction (`should_use_dp_reduce_scatterv()` already requires `not should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`), so no other config is affected. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py`: when `enable_dp_attention` is on, scale `max_num_tokens` back up by `dp_size` so the wrapper covers the gathered MoE input. Verified on 4×B200 with `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3-0324-NVFP4` + `trtllm_mla` (`tp=ep=dp=4 + DP-attention + cutedsl`, CUDA graph enabled): gsm8k = **0.957** (512 examples).

signal.title: perf: optimize small-M NVFP4 MoE on SM120 (v0.5.15)
signal.text: ## Motivation On GB10 / SM121 with SGLang v0.5.15, decode-heavy ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE workloads use very small token counts (typically M=1/2, with M<=8 during CUDA Graph capture). The regular FlashInfer TRT-LLM route has non-trivial dispatch setup at these sizes. This PR adds an explicit opt-in path for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 shape. It reuses the FlashInfer SM120 CUTLASS fused MoE kernel and the already packed ModelOpt W4A4 weights. The default path is unchanged. This PR targets `release/v0.5.15` because the relevant NVFP4 JIT and runner interfaces have since been refactored on `main`; a main-branch port needs separate validation against the new weight preparation path. ## Modifications - Add `nvfp4_small_moe` for BF16, M<=8, hidden size 2048, intermediate size 512, and top-k<=8. - Dispatch eligible ModelOpt NVFP4 decode calls when `SGLANG_NVFP4_SMALL_MOE=1`. - Preserve the existing TRT-LLM path for all unsupported shapes and configurations. - Support both `[Up; Gate]` and historical `[Gate; Up]` W13 layouts without copying expert weight tensors. - Reject GEMM1 clamp and per-token activation cases from the opt-in route. ## Accuracy Tests Tested on NVIDIA GB10 / SM121 with Torch 2.11.0+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.6.12. | Case | Relative L2 error vs W4A4 reference | Max abs diff | |---|---:|---:| | M=1 | 0.36% | <=8.96e-4 | | M=2 | 0.64% | <=8.96e-4 | | M=4 | 0.51% | <=8.96e-4 | Additional validation: - Five deterministic prompts produced identical outputs. - CUDA Graph capture succeeded for decode batch sizes 1/2/4. - `pytest`: 27 supported NVFP4 tests passed. - The full blockwise MoE parameterization has one pre-existing FP16 failure on SM120: the kernel explicitly supports only BF16 output. The BF16 case passes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Direct fused MoE latency: | Tokens | Latency | |---|---:| | M=1 | 80.6 us | | M=2 | 81.9 us | | M=4 | 74.8 us | End-to-end validation, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, 2048 input tokens to 200 output tokens, concurrency 1, n=20: - Output throughput: 61.07 tok/s - Mean TPOT: 15.11 ms - Mean TTFT: 267.80 ms - Success: 20/20 - Concurrency 4 smoke test: 8/8 successful These end-to-end numbers validate stability and integration; they are not presented as an isolated speedup attributable only to this dispatch change. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit (all modified-file hooks pass). - [ ] Add new CI unit tests. Existing NVFP4 tests and model-level validation are included above. - [ ] Update documentation. The path remains experimental and opt-in. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

signal.title: Fix kimi k2 tool call parsing with separate reasoning
signal.text: ## Motivation When using the Kimi K2 model with `separate_reasoning=True`, tool calls can appear inside thinking blocks (within `reasoning_text`) or after them (within `delta`). The current implementation doesn't handle this correctly, causing: 1. Tool calls inside reasoning blocks to be lost or emitted as raw text 2. Content after tool sections to be truncated in the detector 3. Partial tool tokens breaking parsing in streaming mode This fix ensures tool calls are properly extracted from both locations in both streaming and non-streaming modes. ## Modifications ### 1. `kimik2_detector.py` - Preserve content after tool section - Changed content extraction to preserve text both before and after the tool calls section - Previously only content before `<bot>` token was kept, now content after `<eot>` is also preserved ### 2. `serving_chat.py` - Add kimi_k2 mode detection and tool parsing - Added `kimi_k2_mode` detection based on `reasoning_parser == "kimi_k2"` and `separate_reasoning` #### Streaming mode changes: - **Parse tools from reasoning_text**: Tool calls inside thinking blocks are now detected and extracted before emitting reasoning content - **Parse tools from delta**: Tool calls appearing after reasoning blocks are detected and extracted - **Skip standard tool handling**: When in kimi_k2_mode, skip the default tool call handling to avoid duplication #### Non-streaming mode changes: - **Parse tools FIRST**: For kimi_k2 with separate reasoning, parse tool calls before handling reasoning content - **Skip duplicate parsing**: Avoid parsing tools again if already handled for kimi_k2 ## Checklist - signal.title: [DeepSeek V3.2] [Feat] add tensor parallel o_proj linear in context parallel nsa
signal.text: ## Motivation The current NSA context parallel partitioning causes the o_proj to be copied across all cards, resulting in each card using 10GB more VRAM compared to DeepSeek v3. Furthermore, using `cp` during the decoding phase can cause tensors to be incompatible with tensor core computation requirements, leading to padding. ## Modifications Before： After： In this approach, we will add an all-to-all calculation after the attn core calculation to change the shape in a single card from (bs*q_len, num_heads * v_head_dim) to (oproj_tp_size * bs*q_len, num_heads // oproj_tp_size * v_head_dim), in order to align the weight shape of o_proj. Then, after the o_proj computation, the reduce scatter communication operator is used to restore the output to (bs*q_len, hidden_dim) shape. ## Accuracy Tests without o_proj tp: ![metric_old](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8b45578-7e1c-4ac5-9434-3bd6f59ff0e0) with o_proj tp: ![metric_new](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7a0444c-e30b-44be-a92d-062c6637adae) ## Benchmarking and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. signal.title: Support LLGuidance Fast-Forward tokens via Speculative Decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation Add LLGUIDANCE speculative algorithm to enable fast-forward tokens (or jump-forward tokens) when processing constrained grammars (JSON, REGEX, EBNF). The speculator will automatically force new tokens whenever possible (e.g., name fields in JSON schema) without calling the models, hence improvement the token generation throughput. This speculator prefers ff-tokens instead of ff-string to guarantee correctness. There is a good article talking about the problem [here](https://github.com/guidance-ai/llguidance/blob/main/docs/fast_forward.md) ## Modifications * Add "LLGUIDANCE" field to speculative_algorithm arg * Add LlguidanceWorker * Update llguidance version to 1.4.0 ### Benchmark Results Summary We evaluated using [JsonSchemaBench](https://github.com/epfl-dlab/jsonschemabench) and achieved speedup ranging from **1.24X to 1.44X** (TPOP - signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation When deploying an **MHA** model with PD disaggregation, if the TP sizes of the prefill and decode nodes are different, KV transfer is performed by token, which leads to high TTFT. In this PR, the optimization is mainly achieved via two environment variables: 1. SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DIFF_TP_NUMPY: use NumPy vectorization to accelerate the computation of destination pointers on the prefill side. 2. SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_PAGED_SCATTER_KV: A buffer is allocated on the decode side to receive contiguous KV cache, and then a scatter operation is performed on the decode GPU to speed up KV transfer (only applicable when P-TP-Size > D-TP-Size). <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications 1. Use Numpy vectorization to accelerate dst ptr computation in send_kvcache_slice 2. Use Scatter KV Buffer to transfer [send_kvcache_slice] --> [send_kvcache + in-GPU-KV-scatter] to accelerate KV transfer <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests |
