signal.title: [ROCm] Use the AITER sparse-MLA kernel for DSA prefill and decode
signal.text: Enable with `--dsa-prefill-backend aiter --dsa-decode-backend aiter` (both flags are required; passing only one skips the ROCm default path). The default is unchanged. ## What this does On ROCm, DSA attention currently runs on TileLang for both prefill and decode. This PR adds an `aiter` backend that routes both phases to the AITER sparse-MLA kernel `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen1_gqaratio16_ps` with fp8 Q and fp8 KV. Sparse DSA prefill is structurally a very wide decode: the chunk is handed to `mla_decode_fwd` as `num_tokens` sequences of length 1 (`max_seqlen_q = 1`), so one kernel serves both phases and no separate prefill kernel is needed. Notable details: - Q must be fp8, or AITER dispatches `mla_a16w8_qh16_m16x4_n16x1_coex0_mask1_ps` instead, which is 4.2x slower. fp8 Q comes from `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, whose gate in `forward_mla.py` previously tested `dsa_backend == "tilelang"` literally. It is now a set of backends that want fp8 Q. - CUDA-only DSA backends now fall back to `tilelang` on ROCm with a warning instead of raising `ImportError: flashmla_ops`. The ROCm default is only applied when *both* backend flags are unset, so passing one previously made the other fall through to `flashmla_kv`. ## Results GLM-5.2 FP4, MI355X (gfx950) TP4, 8192 in / 1024 out, concurrency 64. Kernel time from a rocprof trace: | | TileLang | this PR | |---|---|---| | Prefill MLA, per 8192-token step | 320.2 ms | **143.7 ms** | | Prefill GPU busy, whole window | 728.4 ms | **564.8 ms** (-22.5%) | | Decode MLA, per iteration | 3.12 ms | **1.86 ms** | Everything else is unchanged within noise: MoE GEMM, dense GEMM and all-reduce all move by less than 1%. ## Correctness `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200` -> **0.945**. ## Scope ROCm only, and only when both DSA backends are set to `aiter`. CUDA backends (`flashmla_*`, `flashinfer_sparse_mla`, `trtllm`) and the ROCm default (`tilelang`) are untouched; the default remains `tilelang/tilelang`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->_Not run yet_<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:warning: **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in.<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Stop losing Kimi-K3 tool calls to reasoning, constraint conflicts, and truncation
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #34604. The issue reports ~190 `Tool call parsing error` logs/day on a Kimi-K3 agentic workload, attributed to `kimik3_detector.py`. The detector isn't the source — it uses stdlib `json` (message: `Expecting value`), the reported strings are `orjson`'s, and `detect_and_parse` already swallows every exception. Tracing it produced four distinct defects; **two of them are entirely silent, so 190/day is a floor, not the rate.** ### 1. Native-format output pushed through the JSON-array decoder `_process_tool_calls` falls through to the `required` json_schema fallback whenever the native parser finds no tool call. That decoder is wrong for detectors that constrain generation themselves: `_process_messages` deliberately attaches no json_schema constraint for them (kimi_k3 is excluded explicitly), so the text is native XTML or prose, never a JSON array. Accounts for every reported error string: | Error | Cause | |---|---| | `unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (84x) | `orjson.loads` on the model's prose | | `Input is a zero-length, empty document` (1x) | `orjson.loads("")` | | `string indices must be integers` (106x) | `orjson.loads` returned a dict, so `enumerate()` walks keys and `tool["name"]` indexes a string | The streaming path already gates this correctly; the non-stream path now matches it. ### 2. `response_format` + `required` silently discards the tool-call constraint `protocol.py` dropped the tool-call constraint with only a warning when the request also carried `response_format` / `regex` / `ebnf`. Verified: ``` response_format=none -> constraint in flight: structural_tag response_format=json_object -> constraint in flight: json_schema: {"type": "object"} response_format=json_schema -> constraint in flight: json_schema: {...} ``` The model is then *forced* to emit JSON and *forbidden* from emitting a tool call — the request cannot be satisfied, and the failure surfaces as the cryptic `string indices` TypeError above. Now a 400. `auto` keeps warn-and-continue, since it doesn't promise a call. ### 3. A tool call emitted before `<|close|>think<|sep|>` was eaten (silent) The tools-channel rescue in the kimi_k3 reasoning detector only ran when `think_end` was **absent**. With think-close present, everything before it — including a complete tools section — became `reasoning_content`. The model is free to do this: the reasoner grammar backend defers the tools constraint until think closes (`fill_vocab_mask` returns unmasked while thinking), and K3 leaves `tools` out of `think_excluded_tokens` on purpose. Now split on whichever marker comes first, in both overrides. ### 4. A truncated tools section vanished at end-of-stream (silent) `KimiK3Detector` didn't override `finish()`, so `parse_stream_end` returned nothing: a tools section cut off before its closing tag produced no call, no text, and no log. Now reported at stream end, with genuinely held-back text released the way `detect_and_parse` already does. The non-stream path had the same silent drop — a tools marker present but zero complete calls returned before any logging; it now warns on that branch too, for `auto` and `required` alike. ### Full pipeline, before → after ``` auto required 1 think+response+tools (happy) 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 2 tools only, no response channel 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 3 cut in response (no tools) 0 -> 0 err -> warn 4 cut inside reasoning 0 -> 0 err -> warn 5 cut mid tool call 0 -> 0 silent -> reported 6 JSON object (constraint dropped) 0 -> 0 err -> 400 upstream 7 tools inside think, then close 0 -> 1 0 -> 1 8 tools straight from think (no close) 1 -> 1 1 -> 1 ``` ### Not fixed here `required` still isn't a hard guarantee. EOS *is* grammar-masked until the call completes (verified by compiling the structural tag and querying the bitmask), but `max_tokens` and client `stop` sequences terminate generation on decoded text with no grammar involvement (`schedule_batch.py` `_check_str_based_finish`). Worth its own issue. The same think_end/tool_start ordering bug exists in `BaseReasoningFormatDetector` for six other detectors that set `tool_start_token`. Left alone deliberately — only demonstrated for kimi_k3, and not worth regressing six model families in this PR. ## Modifications - `serving_chat.py` — gate the json_schema fallback on detector capability; harden the fallback for parsers that do use it (bare object accepted as a one-element array, missing `parameters` defaults to `{}`, non-conforming shapes get a readable error); warn on the sync branch where a tools marker parses to zero complete calls; raw output at debug level. - `serving_responses.py` — same capability gate, including `parses_required_natively()` so muse (ATEM format) skips the JSON fallback the way it does in chat. - `protocol.py` — 400 on `required`/named + another output constraint. - `reasoning_parser.py` — kimi_k3 overrides split on the earlier of tools-open / think-close. - `kimik3_detector.py` — `finish()` reports a dropped tools section and releases held-back text. Behavior changes worth calling out: - `tool_choice=required` (or a named tool) combined with `response_format` / `regex` / `ebnf` used to drop the tool-call constraint with a warning and then fail downstream; it is now rejected with a 400. sglang has a single grammar slot, so the combination was unsatisfiable — but this is stricter than OpenAI, which tolerates the pair best-effort. `auto` keeps warn-and-continue. - For a structural-tag parser with `tool_choice=required`, a completion that happens to be a valid JSON array of tool calls used to be decoded as tool calls. It no longer is — such a model is never constrained to emit that shape, and the streaming path already returned no calls for it. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; request-path bookkeeping only. ## Tests New cases across five files, each verified to fail on pre-fix code and pass after — including follow-up coverage for the responses muse gate and the sync truncated-tool warning: ``` 8 failed, 6 passed <- pre-fix (the 6 are chunk sizes that already worked + the auto negative case) 0 failed <- post-fix ``` Full affected suites on the branch merged with latest main: 180 passed, 53 subtests passed (`test_serving_chat.py`, `test_serving_responses.py`, `test_kimik3_detector.py`, `test_kimik3_reasoning_parser.py`, CPU). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32143251812](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32143251812)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32147164327](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32147164327)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [Docker] Upgrade Python 3.12 + torch 2.11 + triton 3.7 in ROCm 7.2.4
signal.text: ## Motivation Add ROCm 7.2.4 Docker flavors on Python 3.12 with PyTorch 2.11 and Triton 3.7. PyTorch 2.11 for ROCm 7.2 is available from the PyTorch Foundation index. Its dependency initially installs `triton-rocm==3.6.0`, but this PR replaces it at the end of the build with AITER’s pinned Triton 3.7. Installing Triton last prevents later dependency resolution from reverting the validated ROCm stack. | Component | ROCm 7.2.0 flavors | ROCm 7.2.4 flavors | | --- | --- | --- | | Base image | Ubuntu 22.04 / Python 3.10 | Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.12 | | PyTorch | 2.9.1 | 2.11.0+rocm7.2 | | Triton | AITER-managed Triton | AITER-managed Triton 3.7 | | AITER | `d9e5ef7` | `d9e5ef7` | ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Add `gfx942-rocm724` and `gfx950-rocm724` stages. - Upgrade ROCm 7.2.4 to Python 3.12 and torch 2.11. - Build AITER against the installed torch 2.11 ABI. - Install AITER’s pinned Triton 3.7 as the final Python dependency step, replacing the temporary Triton 3.6 dependency pulled by torch. - Validate that torch remains a ROCm build and report the installed Triton and `triton-kernels` versions. - Use AITER commit `d9e5ef7` consistently across ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.4. - Apply the `torch.Stream` compatibility workaround to both ROCm 7.2 variants. - Preserve the ROCm IPC memory-leak workaround through `HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1`. ### `python/pyproject_other.toml` - Add ROCm 7.2.4 extras compatible with torch 2.11. - Use `compressed-tensors==0.16.0`, because 0.15.0 requires `torch<2.11`. ### CI - Reuse the existing ROCm 7.2 PR workflow instead of adding a duplicated ROCm 7.2.4 workflow. - Add a `rocm_version` input, with ROCm 7.2.4 as the default and ROCm 7.2.0 retained for fallback testing. - Extend the existing nightly and tagged-release workflows to build either ROCm 7.2.0 or 7.2.4. - When CI rebuilds AITER on ROCm 7.2.x, run AITER’s Triton installer first and fail closed if installation fails. - Preserve `amd_ci_image` overrides so candidate images can be tested before publication. - This consolidation reduced the proposed additions from 1,921 to 345 lines—an 82% reduction. ## Accuracy Tests Both new stages were built and evaluated on their target hardware. ### `gfx950-rocm724` on MI355X Built with `--build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm724` and ran the in-repo MI35x accuracy evals. Hardware-limited to 2 GPUs, so tensor-parallel = 2 and MXFP4 checkpoints are used for the large models. GSM8K unless noted, on a 200-question slice for turnaround. | Model | Test | TP | Score | Threshold | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | openai/gpt-oss-20b | `accuracy/mi35x/test_gpt_oss_eval_mi35x.py` | 2 | 0.555 | 0.47 | ✅ PASS | | openai/gpt-oss-120b | `accuracy/mi35x/test_gpt_oss_eval_mi35x.py` | 2 | 0.860 | 0.79 | ✅ PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 | `accuracy/mi35x/test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_tp2_mi35x.py` | 2 | 0.955 | 0.93 | ✅ PASS | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 | `test_qwen3p5_triton_dcp.py` | 2 | 0.930 | 0.90 | ✅ PASS | The same set was re-run against an `ENABLE_MORI=1` build of the same stage, and all four remained above threshold. MORI does build on the Python 3.12 / noble base, so the nightly and release workflows enable it as they do for the other flavors. Notes on the 2-GPU adaptation (registered test files unchanged; edits applied only to throwaway in-container copies): - gpt-oss: ran with `--tp 2` (test default is 8) and `--disable-custom-all-reduce`. - DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4: the `..._tp2_...` test is already tp=2; pointed at a local MXFP4 checkpoint. - Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4: the registered test is tp=8 + dcp=2; reduced to tp=2 / dcp=1 and pointed at a local MXFP4 checkpoint. ### `gfx942-rocm724` on MI300X Built with `--build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm724` and ran the gpt-oss evals on 8 GPUs, unmodified. | Model | Test | TP | Score | Threshold | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | lmsys/gpt-oss-20b-bf16 | `accuracy/mi30x/test_gpt_oss_eval_amd.py` | 8 | 0.505 | 0.45 | ✅ PASS | | lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16 | `accuracy/mi30x/test_gpt_oss_eval_amd.py` | 8 | 0.875 | 0.75 | ✅ PASS | All test scripts live under `test/registered/amd/`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — Docker image/dependency change only; no kernel or model forward code is modified. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- N/A: Docker packaging change --> - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32204006607](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32204006607)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32204006453](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32204006453)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end --> ## Known behavior before the first ROCm 7.2.4 nightly `amd_ci_start_container.sh` and `amd_ci_start_container_disagg.sh` carry hardcoded fallback tags only for `rocm720` and `rocm700`; `rocm724` falls through to `*)` and returns non-zero. That is deliberate — failing loudly beats silently testing a months-old image — but it does mean that between this PR merging and the first `rocm724` nightly being published, selecting `rocm724` from the `rocm_version` dropdown hard-fails at container start. Please don't file that as a bug on day one. Worth flagging for runner capacity too: this takes the nightly build matrix from 2 builds to 4 and the release matrix from 4 to 6, at roughly 2–2.6 h each.

signal.title: [dLLM] Add JointThresholdInDel algorithm for insertion & deletion decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces the `JointThresholdInDel` algorithm, which extends `JointThreshold` with structural edit token support for diffusion LLMs. It enables the model to not only fill masks and refine tokens, but also **delete** positions (block shrinks) and **insert** new positions via SPLIT (block expands). This is essential for models trained with insertion and deletion capabilities (e.g., LLaDA2.2-flash with InDel training). ## Modifications ### New Algorithm: `JointThresholdInDel` - **DELETE token**: When the model predicts a DELETE token at a position, that position is removed from the block, remaining positions shift left, and the block is padded with mask tokens. - **SPLIT (insert) token**: When the model predicts a SPLIT token, the position expands into `[mask, current_token]`, allowing the model to insert new content. - **Original mask tracking (`is_orig_mask`)**: Distinguishes masks from the initial block vs. masks introduced by DELETE padding or SPLIT expansion, ensuring correct M2T scheduling. - **Anti-loop mechanism**: Detects repeated block states and deterministically injects diversity at the lowest-confidence position via `argmin`, preventing infinite loops caused by DELETE/SPLIT cycles. - **Bounded final cleanup**: When the post-edit budget is reached or the regular-update limit is exceeded, selects every remaining non-prompt mask and suppresses MASK, DELETE, and SPLIT. If token IDs change, one additional forward is performed before emitting the request so the KV cache matches the final block. - **FDFO compatible**: All iteration state is carried in the `states` dict, fully compatible with First-Done-First-Out scheduling. ### Config Changes Added `delete_token_id` and `split_token_id` to `DllmConfig`. `JointThresholdInDel` reads them from explicit checkpoint configuration, with a compatibility entry for the official `inclusionAI/LLaDA2.2-flash` checkpoint, and rejects unsupported checkpoints at startup. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review Process 1. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. # MoE backend benchmark: `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` (baseline) vs `flashinfer_megamoe` Benchmark of the DeepSeek-V4-Flash NVFP4 model comparing two MoE backend configurations on the serving path. `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` (trtllm routed MoE runner + flashinfer A2A) is used as the **baseline**; `flashinfer_megamoe` is the compared configuration. All deltas are reported relative to the trtllm_routed baseline. ## Environment - Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4` - Parallelism: TP=4, DP=4, DP-attention enabled (`attn_dp_size=4`, so per-rank decode batch = `max_running_requests / 4`) - 1x node, same hardware for both runs ## Server commands **Baseline — `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm_routed \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer \ --max-running-requests 1024 ``` **Compared — `flashinfer_megamoe`:** ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --max-running-requests 1024 ``` ## Client command ```bash python -m sglang.bench_serving \ --backend sglang \ --model nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $((5 * C)) \ --max-concurrency C # C in {32, 128, 1024}, num-prompts = 5 x C ``` ## Results ### Output token throughput (tok/s, higher is better) | max_conc | trtllm_routed (baseline) | megamoe | Δ (megamoe vs baseline) | |---------:|-------------------------:|--------:|------------------------:| | 32 | 876.88 | 674.21 | −23.1% | | 128 | 1215.93 | 1092.54 | −10.1% | | 1024 | 3223.92 | 3245.20 | +0.7% | ### Mean TPOT (ms, lower is better) | max_conc | trtllm_routed (baseline) | megamoe | Δ (megamoe vs baseline) | |---------:|-------------------------:|--------:|------------------------:| | 32 | 34.49 | 38.77 | +12.4% | | 128 | 109.93 | 106.83 | −2.8% | | 1024 | 422.61 | 394.92 | −6.6% | ### Full metrics | config | max_conc | out_tput (tok/s) | mean TPOT (ms) | median TPOT (ms) | p99 TPOT (ms) | achieved conc | mean TTFT (ms) | |--------|---------:|-----------------:|---------------:|-----------------:|--------------:|--------------:|---------------:| | trtllm_routed | 32 | 876.88 | 34.49 | 33.32 | 102.42 | 28.76 | 421 | | megamoe | 32 | 674.21 | 38.77 | 40.27 | 78.13 | 26.53 | 321 | | trtllm_routed | 128 | 1215.93 | 109.93 | 104.71 | 395.33 | 116.12 | 797 | | megamoe | 128 | 1092.54 | 106.83 | 101.22 | 345.54 | 103.68 | 776 | | trtllm_routed | 1024 | 3223.92 | 422.61 | 343.54 | 2429.78 | 994.81 | 3142 | | megamoe | 1024 | 3245.20 | 394.92 | 322.13 | 2356.07 | 951.20 | 3261 | ## Takeaways - **Low/mid concurrency (c32, c128): `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` wins on throughput** — +23% at c32 and +11% at c128 output token throughput, with comparable or better median TPOT. It also sustains higher achieved concurrency (28.8/116.1 vs 26.5/103.7), i.e. it drains the request queue faster. - **High concurrency (c1024): the two are effectively tied on throughput** (3224 vs 3245 tok/s, +0.7% for megamoe — within run-to-run noise). At this point both are decode-bound / saturated (achieved conc < target, p99 TPOT ~7x median), so the MoE backend is no longer the bottleneck. - **TPOT crossover:** megamoe has slightly lower mean TPOT at c1024 (−6.6%) but a worse p99 tail at low load (c32: 102 ms vs 78 ms). trtllm_routed gives more consistent per-token latency at low concurrency. - **Net:** `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` is the better default for latency-sensitive / low-to-mid concurrency serving; at saturation the choice is throughput-neutral. ## FlashInfer MegaMOE env knobs This PR exposes `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE` for the FlashInfer NVFP4 MegaMOE path. It selects the cross-rank combine wire format passed to `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig.combine_dtype`. Supported values: - `bf16`: default, exact combine path. - `mxfp8`: quantized combine traffic with a small accuracy tradeoff. - `nvfp4`: lower combine traffic with a small accuracy tradeoff. Example: ```bash SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_COMBINE_DTYPE=nvfp4 \ python -m sglang.launch_server \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4 \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe ``` `mxfp8` and `nvfp4` are incompatible with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=1`; server args validation now rejects that combination early. > Note: the `flashinfer_megamoe` in-kernel FC2-reduce variant (`SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=1`) was excluded from this comparison due to a known issue and is not reflected here. Update 7/27/2026: ## MoE backend comparison — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4, TP4/DP4/EP4 Baseline: `trtllm`. Positive throughput and negative latency are both wins. Tokens/rank = per-DP-rank prefill chunk (DP attention routes each request wholly to one rank; `--chunked-prefill-size` is divided by `dp_size` internally). ## Prefill ### 2048 tokens/rank (input len 2048, concurrency 128) | Backend | Input tput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 38,884 | 3,084 | 3,233 | 4,104 | | **deepgemm megamoe** | **46,117** | **2,572** | **2,719** | **3,372** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 42,324 | 2,952 | 3,018 | 3,849 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 41,291 | 3,036 | 3,122 | 3,955 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4 | 42,408 | 2,953 | 3,044 | 3,838 | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Input tput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---|---| | **deepgemm megamoe** | **+18.60%** | **-16.59%** | **-15.88%** | **-17.84%** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +8.85% | -4.28% | -6.65% | -6.21% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +6.19% | -1.57% | -3.43% | -3.63% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4 | +9.06% | -4.23% | -5.84% | -6.48% | > Note: trtllm/deepgemm rows are 640 requests (676,871 input tokens); the flashinfer rows are > 1,280 requests (1,327,019 input tokens). Same input len and concurrency, so the rates are > comparable, but the request counts differ. ### 8192 tokens/rank (input len 8192, 640 requests, 2,665,479 input tokens, concurrency 128) | Backend | Input tput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 151,213 | 3,137 | 3,339 | 4,361 | | deepgemm megamoe | 154,359 | 3,047 | 3,286 | 4,163 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 162,342 | 2,945 | 3,159 | 4,146 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 165,658 | 2,831 | 3,018 | 3,835 | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **169,175** | **2,745** | **2,905** | **3,753** | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Input tput | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | P99 TTFT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | +2.08% | -2.84% | -1.58% | -4.52% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +7.36% | -6.10% | -5.39% | -4.93% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +9.55% | -9.73% | -9.60% | -12.06% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+11.88%** | **-12.50%** | **-13.00%** | **-13.93%** | ## Decode Input len 32, output len 1024, 10,240 requests, concurrency 8192, 5,256,337 generated tokens. | Backend | Output tput (tok/s) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---| | trtllm (baseline) | 8,783 | 795.2 | 727.4 | 2,244.7 | | deepgemm megamoe | 8,620 | **762.8** | 721.3 | **1,944.3** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | 8,832 | 783.1 | 722.0 | 2,167.6 | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | 8,849 | 780.0 | 717.7 | 2,182.1 | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **8,886** | 776.6 | **715.8** | 2,151.7 | Change vs `trtllm`: | Backend | Output tput | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT | P99 TPOT | |---|---|---|---|---| | deepgemm megamoe | -1.86% | **-4.08%** | -0.84% | **-13.38%** | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_plain | +0.55% | -1.53% | -0.75% | -3.44% | | flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_ikr | +0.75% | -1.91% | -1.33% | -2.79% | | **flashinfer_cutedsl_megamoe_combine_nvfp4** | **+1.17%** | -2.34% | -1.60% | -4.14% | ## signal.title: [NPU] Enable non-greedy MTP sampling
signal.text: ## Motivation NPU MTP verification currently uses greedy argmax for non-greedy requests. Consequently, `temperature`, `top_k`, and `top_p` do not take effect during speculative verification. With GLM-4.7-Flash on GPQA, enabling non-greedy MTP reduced the observed accuracy from approximately ~70% to ~50%. This PR enables probability-based non-greedy MTP sampling on NPU. ## Modifications - Add an explicit NPU non-greedy branch in `eagle_sample`. - Keep NPU-specific sampling logic in `srt/hardware_backend/npu/speculative/mtp_sampling.py`. - Apply temperature scaling and sequential top-k/top-p probability renormalization. - Support target-only sampling for general EAGLE trees and classic rejection sampling for `tree_topk=1` chains. - Validate input topology and probability tensors before dispatching kernels. - Preserve the existing greedy path and fail explicitly for unsupported non-greedy configurations. Sampling algorithm and kernel unit tests are covered in `sgl-kernel-npu`; no duplicate SGLang-local test is added. ## Accuracy Tests Model: `GLM-4.7-Flash` Dataset: `GPQA` | Configuration | Sampling | Before | After | |---|---|---:|---:| | NPU TP/TP+EP without MTP | `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95` | ~70% | ~70% | | NPU TP+MTP/TP+EP+MTP | `temperature=1`, `top_p=0.95` | ~50% | ~70% | | NPU MTP greedy | `temperature=0`, `top_p=1` | ~50% | ~50% | The non-greedy MTP accuracy recovered to the expected range, while existing non-MTP and greedy behavior remained unchanged. before: after: ## Speed Tests and Profiling | Check | Result | |---|---| | End-to-end throughput | No measurable performance impact | | End-to-end latency | No measurable performance impact | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #31466214974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31466214974) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #31466214842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31466214842)

signal.title: [BugFix][Qwen3.8] Support Qwen3.8-MXFP4 DCP by registing Qwen3_5 text-only archs in mamba radix cache whitelists

signal.title: [ROCm] Fix EAGLE spec-decode verify silently sampling greedy on HIP
signal.text: ## Problem On ROCm/HIP, EAGLE speculative-decode **verify silently commits `argmax` (greedy)**, ignoring `temperature`/`top_p`. The gate in `srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py::eagle_sample` is: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: target_predict = torch.argmax(...) # greedy ``` `_is_hip` is in the predicate because the sampling-verify ops (`tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`, `top_k_renorm_prob`, `top_p_renorm_prob`) are imported only under `is_cuda()/is_musa()` in `srt/layers/sampler.py`. Result: **every EAGLE spec-decode run at `temperature>0` on ROCm decodes greedy**, which on long-reasoning generations degenerates into verbatim repetition loops. Not model-specific. ## Fix Route HIP through the pure-Triton `chain_speculative_sampling_triton` (`srt/speculative/reject_sampling.py`, no CUDA deps), with a **Triton pivot binary-search top-p renorm** replacing the CUDA-only sgl_kernel renorm, and make it the **default on HIP** so users don't have to know a flag: 1. `eagle_utils.py`: factor the gate into a pure `_verify_uses_greedy(...)` helper (testable, and **byte-identical to the original predicate for every non-HIP platform**); add `_top_p_renorm_kernel` (Triton pivot search, ~5× faster than a full sort and exact, `top_p=1.0` is a true no-op) + a HIP renorm wrapper; guard the CUDA-only imports; keep both CUDA NaN probes. 2. `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py`: in `_handle_eagle_family` (resolution pipeline), **default `speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True` on HIP** for EAGLE/EAGLE3 + topk==1 + default accept-thresholds + non-deterministic. The predicate is a strict superset of the existing rejection-sampling validation's raises, so the flip can never turn a working config into an error. This makes the rejection path (which emits the draft proposal `q` the Triton chain sampler consumes) the HIP default. ### Rebase note (current `main`) `main` has since (a) renamed the spec-arg accessor `get_server_args()` → `get_spec()`, and (b) wrapped the CUDA renorm calls in `sampling_info.need_top_k_sampling` / `need_top_p_sampling` guards. The resolution keeps both: the CUDA branch is `main`'s guarded pair verbatim, and the HIP branch runs the combined `_renorm_top_k_top_p_hip` under `need_top_k_sampling or need_top_p_sampling` — which stays equivalent, since that helper already skips the top-k sort when `top_k >= vocab` and passes rows through unchanged when `top_p >= 1.0`. `main`'s new `enable_multi_layer_eagle` validation requires `topk != 1`, which the default-on gate already excludes, so the gate still cannot trigger a raise. ## Correctness - Non-HIP (CUDA/CPU/NPU/XPU/MUSA) behavior is **byte-identical** — the gate reduces to the original predicate; CUDA still uses the sgl_kernel renorm + `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`. - NEXTN is aliased to EAGLE before this hook, so GLM-5.2 (NEXTN→EAGLE, topk==1) gets the default-on. ## Testing (all pass) **`test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py`** — pure-CPU gate truth table, **4/4 PASSED**: | method | asserts | |---|---| | `test_non_hip_is_byte_identical_to_pre_patch` | gate == the original predicate for every non-HIP row of the full {CUDA,CPU,NPU,XPU}×{greedy,sampling}×{rej on/off} matrix | | `test_hip_samples_only_with_rejection_and_non_greedy` | HIP samples **iff** rejection-sampling on and batch not all-greedy | | `test_cuda_keyed_on_all_greedy_only` | CUDA behavior unchanged (keyed on `is_all_greedy`) | | `test_cpu_npu_xpu_always_greedy` | CPU/NPU/XPU still forced greedy | **`test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py`** — Triton HIP renorm vs a torch nucleus reference, **run on gfx950 (MI350X), 5/5 PASSED**: | method | asserts | |---|---| | `test_top_p_matches_nucleus` | max\|Δ\| < 1e-6 vs nucleus for top_p ∈ {0.5, 0.9, 0.95} | | `test_top_p_one_is_exact_noop` | top_p=1.0 is bit-exact (max\|Δ\| == 0) | | `test_top_k_restriction` | top-k mask honored | | `test_edge_top_p_to_zero_keeps_top1` | degenerate top_p→0 keeps the argmax token | | `test_edge_single_nonmasked_token` | single-token row | **E2E** (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, MI350X, Max effort, temp 1.0/top_p 0.95, fp8 KV): GPQA-Diamond **89.9% (178/198)** vs ~77% stock (forced-greedy); the two hard repetition-loopers terminate cleanly with correct answers at ~2.1× the spec-off throughput (full MTP speedup kept). ## Known residual gaps (pre-existing, not regressions) On HIP, EAGLE topk==1 with `--enable-deterministic-inference` or non-default accept-thresholds is intentionally *not* flipped (rejection sampling is genuinely incompatible there), and HIP **tree-draft** (topk>1) sampling remains greedy (the Triton chain sampler is chain-only). Both are out of scope here. ## Test steps (reproduce) **Environment.** 8× MI355X (gfx950), image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`. `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is the image default, which is what puts the aiter paths below in play. <details> <summary>1. Unit tests</summary> GPU devices must be passed through even for CPU-only cases — importing `sglang` pulls in `aiter`, which shells out to `rocminfo` at import time. ```bash docker run --rm --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add video \ --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 16g \ -v "$PWD:/wt" -w /wt -e PYTHONPATH=/wt/python \ lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817 \ bash -lc 'python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_eagle_gate_routing.py test/registered/spec/eagle/test_rocm_eagle_renorm.py -q -p no:randomly' ``` Red-before/green-after: re-run after `git checkout origin/main -- python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` and the new case fails. </details> <details> <summary>2. Serve GLM-5.2 (shared by the e2e steps)</summary> Use **GLM-5.2-FP8**, not MXFP4, on this image: MXFP4 is `quant_method: quark`, and the image's `quark.py` imports `declare_load_time_override` from `arg_groups/overrides.py`, which does not exist there, so the scheduler dies at weight load (`main` has since moved past that code). FP8 is also in the `("fp8","compressed_tensors","quark")` tuple, so it exercises the same routing path. ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /data/huggingface/GLM-5.2-FP8 --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --port 30000 ``` </details> <details> <summary>3. GPQA-Diamond via lm-evaluation-harness</summary> GSM8K is **not** a useful gate here — GLM-5.2 sits at ~94% on it, so it is saturated and hides routing/sampling regressions. GPQA-Diamond is the discriminating eval (model card: 91.2). Task yaml: `utils/evals/gpqa_diamond.yaml` (task `gpqa_diamond_cot_n_shot`, dataset `Idavidrein/gpqa`/`gpqa_diamond`). lm-eval pinned at `b315ef3b05176acc9732bb7fdec116abe1ecc476`. ```bash python3 -m lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \ --tasks gpqa_diamond.yaml --output_path "$RESULTS" --log_samples \ --model_args "model=$MODEL,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:30000/v1/chat/completions,api_key=EMPTY,\ eos_string=</s>,max_retries=5,num_concurrent=64,timeout=1800,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=163840" \ --limit 198 --gen_kwargs "max_tokens=98304,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95" ``` Serve with a matching `--context-length 163840`. Two things are required for a reasoning model, or the score collapses for harness reasons rather than model reasons: - lm-eval's `LocalChatCompletion.parse_generations` must fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, otherwise every graded answer is the empty string. - `Idavidrein/gpqa` is a **gated** dataset — export `HF_TOKEN` first or the load fails with `DatasetNotFoundError`. - **The token budget must be large or the score is meaningless.** GLM-5.2 routinely reasons past 32k tokens on GPQA. A response that hits `max_tokens` mid-thought never emits a final answer, so `content` is empty, the `reasoning_content` fallback hands the grader ~110k characters of raw reasoning, and the task's `(?i)\b\(?([A-D])\)?\b` filter with `group_select: -1` returns the **last** A–D match in it — usually the English article "a", scored as option A. Measured at `max_tokens=32768`: 19/60 samples truncated, and the split was **0.951 on terminated answers vs 0.526 on truncated ones**, blending to a bogus 0.817. Always split the samples jsonl by response length (a terminated answer is 1 character) before trusting a GPQA number. - `--limit 198` selects one permutation per question (`process_docs` uses `n_repeats=2`, so the full task is 396); 198 matches the 178/198 figures quoted here. </details> <details> <summary>4. Confirm verify stops committing argmax (this PR)</summary> Serve as above **with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2`**, probe which branch `eagle_sample` takes, and send a `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95` request: | build | branch taken on a non-greedy batch | |---|---| | stock | `GREEDY(argmax) branch TAKEN` ← the bug | | + this PR | `SAMPLING branch TAKEN` | Two traps when reproducing: - Probe the **first non-greedy** call, not the first call: server warmup issues a greedy request, so a naive one-shot probe reports `is_all_greedy=True` and tells you nothing. Gate the probe on `not sampling_info.is_all_greedy`. - **Output diversity is not a valid test.** Stock still returns 8/8 distinct completions at `temperature=1.0`, because the bonus token goes through the normal sampler; only the verify-side commit is forced to argmax. </details> ### Results **Re-verified on the rebased branch** (this matters: the rebase required a hand-merge of the HIP renorm branch with `main`'s new `need_top_k_sampling` / `need_top_p_sampling` guards, so the old numbers could not simply be carried over). GLM-5.2-FP8, 8x MI355X, NEXTN spec decode (`num_steps=1, eagle_topk=1, draft_tokens=2`), GPQA-Diamond 198 questions, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=98304`: | | GPQA-Diamond | |---|---| | stock (forced-greedy) | ~77% | | **this PR, original campaign** | 89.9% (178/198) | | **this PR, re-run on the rebased branch** | **0.904 ± 0.021** | 0.904 reproduces the original 89.9% within error, so the rebase preserved the fix. The `speculative_hook.py` half was confirmed live in the same run — the server logs `enabling speculative_use_rejection_sampling by default` followed by `Rejection sampling is enabled ...`, with no raise, which is the specific risk the rebase introduced (`main` added an `enable_multi_layer_eagle` validation that the auto-enable gate must stay a strict subset of). Branch routing was verified separately with a probe on a non-greedy batch: | build | branch taken | |---|---| | stock | `GREEDY(argmax) branch TAKEN` ← the bug | | + this PR | `SAMPLING branch TAKEN` | **GSM8K is not a valid gate for this PR** and is reported only as a no-regression check (0.960 vs 0.940, n=200): it runs greedy, so forced-argmax is already the intended behaviour there and the bug is invisible by construction. GLM-5.2 is also saturated at ~94% on it. *(Reproduction note: 25% of answers still fail to terminate even at `max_tokens=98304`. That subset scores 0.878 vs 0.933 for terminated ones, so the headline number is robust — unlike at `max_tokens=32768`, where the truncated subset collapses to 0.526 and the aggregate becomes meaningless. See the token-budget warning in the test steps.)*

signal.title: [AMD] Gate the ROCm 7.2.4 nightly on the MI300X/MI355X profiling probe
signal.text: > **Scope reduced.** This PR originally added the `rocm724` Dockerfile stages, a `relax_torch_triton_pin.py` metadata patch, a separate rocm724 nightly, and the tagged-release matrix entry. #30984 provides all four, has green `gfx942-rocm724` and `gfx950-rocm724` release builds, and is going in first. What it does not have is any check that a published 7.2.4 image actually traces graph-launched kernels, which is the only reason the flavor exists. That gate is all this PR is now. ## Motivation ROCm 7.2.0 drops kernel-dispatch events for work submitted through `hipGraphLaunch` ([ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), fixed in 7.2.2), and SGLang decodes from replayed graphs, so a `torch.profiler` trace shows the host-side launch with no GPU kernels under it. That is what AMD/Silo report against every `*-rocm720-*` image, and recovering it is what the 7.2.4 flavors are for. Measured on an MI355X, profiling ten decode steps of gpt-oss-20b-bf16 through `/start_profile` on an identical workload: | image | device kernel events in trace | | --- | --- | | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`, CUDA graphs on | 513 | | same image, `--disable-cuda-graph` | 3924 | | a `gfx950-rocm724` image, CUDA graphs on | 3933 | Nothing in CI would notice if a published 7.2.4 image lost that again. `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it. ## Modifications ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm720-nightly.yml` #30984 extends this nightly to build all four ROCm 7.2 flavors, and its `publish` job pushes to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` directly. This splits that push into a `promote` job and puts the probe between them: | job | runner | what it does | | --- | --- | --- | | `publish` | `amd-docker-scale` | unchanged, minus the lmsys push: builds and pushes `rocm/sgl-dev:v<version>-rocm7??-mi3?x-<date>` | | `probe` | `linux-mi300-1gpu-sglang`, `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` | runs `check_hip_graph_profiling.py` inside each 7.2.4 image, on the GPU it targets | | `promote` | `amd-docker-scale` | republishes to `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm`, requiring a passing probe for the 7.2.4 flavors | Points worth a reviewer's attention: - **Only the 7.2.4 flavors are gated.** The rocm720 images run the runtime that has the bug and would never pass; they promote exactly as before. The gate is a step inside `promote` conditioned on the flavor, not a job-level dependency, so a 7.2.4 regression cannot hold back a 7.2.0 image. - **gfx942 is probed on MI300X and gfx950 on MI355X**, because the behaviour lives in the HIP runtime rather than in SGLang and is worth confirming per device generation. - **Promotion stays per-leg.** `promote` runs under `always()`, so a leg whose build failed has no tag artifact and fails at its own download rather than blocking the legs that did publish. That preserves today's behaviour, where the lmsys push lived inside each `publish` leg. - **The probe job installs no dependencies.** It exercises the image's own torch and HIP runtime, which is the thing under test. - **`workflow_dispatch` takes a `probe_image`**, which qualifies an already-published image without a rebuild, on the GPU its `gpu_arch` selects. That is the cheap way to answer "does this candidate trace graph replay", and pointing it at a `*-rocm720-mi35x` tag is the negative control. ## Accuracy Tests No model, kernel, or image-content changes. This PR is a CI workflow only. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Recovering profiling is the point, and the gate is the measurement: the nightly refuses to promote a 7.2.4 image whose graph-replay kernels do not reach the trace. ## Test plan Local: - Workflow parses; job graph is `publish -> probe -> promote`; job names pass `scripts/lint/check_workflow_job_names.py`. - The probe matrix expression evaluated against every dispatch case. Scheduled runs and `gpu_arch=all` probe both 7.2.4 flavors; `gpu_arch=gfx950-rocm724` probes that one; `gpu_arch=gfx942-rocm720` and `gfx950-rocm720` yield an empty matrix, so the probe is skipped and the rocm720 legs promote ungated. On hardware — 8x MI355X (gfx950), KMD 6.16.13 — running the gate's command against a `gfx950-rocm724` image built from #30984's stages plus #35390: ``` eager launch: 512/512 kernels traced, 11283 us device time, 6213 trace events graph replay: 512/512 kernels traced, 4533 us device time, 1133 trace events VERDICT: PASS -- all 512 graph-replay kernels reach the trace. ``` and against the shipped rocm720 image, which is the negative control the `probe_image` dispatch is for: ``` graph replay: 448/512 kernels traced, 3983 us device time, 1005 trace events VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches trace completely but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reach it. ``` Five repeats on each gave identical counts, so the gate does not flake. Not covered: gfx942 / MI300X, for want of the hardware — the `probe` job's MI300X leg is unexercised until this runs in CI. ## Notes for reviewers - **Stacked on #30984.** It supplies the `rocm724` stages this gate probes and the four-flavor nightly this edits. Until it lands, the diff here shows its commits too. - **Also needs #35390**, which adds `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` — the gate's command — and the libdrm fix that makes `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` resolve on a 7.2.4 base. On #30984's noble base a `gfx950-rocm724` image reports `'AMD Radeon Graphics'`; see [that thread](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5336201854). - **Dropped from this PR as redundant with #30984:** the `gfx942-rocm724` / `gfx950-rocm724` stages, `scripts/ci/amd/relax_torch_triton_pin.py` (its `patch_torch_triton_requirement.py` handles `triton-rocm` and re-pins to the installed version, which is what the torch 2.11 stack needs), the standalone `release-docker-amd-rocm724-nightly.yml`, and the `rocm724` entry in `release-docker-amd.yml`. - Follow-up, not here: teach `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_start_container.sh` to resolve `--rocm-version rocm724` images, and register `check_hip_graph_profiling.py` in the AMD suites once the images run a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime, at which point it guards the behaviour on every PR rather than only at publish time. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). <!-- CI workflow only; the probe it runs is added in #35390. --> - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). <!-- Documented in #35390. --> - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). <!-- N/A --> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32194584123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194584123)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194583932](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194583932)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Qualify ROCm 7.2.4 for the profiler: HIP-graph capture probe + libdrm-amdgpu prerequisite
signal.text: ## Motivation AMD/Silo report that on every `lmsysorg/sglang*` ROCm 7.2 image (v0.5.12 through v0.5.17, `*-rocm720-*`), `torch.profiler` traces contain no GPU kernels for work launched through hipGraph, and they have been patching `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` / `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200` out of a ROCm 7.2.4 install to work around it. This PR is the ROCm 7.2.4 evaluation that request asked for: it adds the check that decides whether a candidate image traces graph-launched kernels, and fixes the one image-level prerequisite that a 7.2.4 base introduces. The report now reproduces on MI355X. Profiling ten decode steps of gpt-oss-20b-bf16 through `/start_profile`, the shipped `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x` image records 513 device kernels where a 7.2.4 image built from this branch records 3933 on an identical workload — 87% of decode kernels never reach the trace. Numbers and method are in the test plan. The report is confirmed upstream, and the fix is already released: - ROCTracer can fail to report kernel operations: [ROCm/ROCm#6102](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102), closed with "Resolved in ROCm 7.2.2". - ROCm 7.2.0's HIP runtime also has a wrong doorbell index in `dispatchGenericAqlPacketBatch` (the graph batch-dispatch path) plus an InterceptQueue ring-buffer heap corruption, both fixed in 7.2.1 ([pytorch/pytorch#177873](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/177873)). That matches the `CUDAGraph::replay` deadlock inside `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200` seen in our own CI (#34452), which is the same bug class surfacing as a hang instead of a gap. - The candidate base carries the fixed libraries: `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_*` ships `libamdhip64.so.7.2.70204` and `libroctracer64.so.4.1.70204` (`hip-runtime-amd` 7.2.26015.70200 -> 7.2.53211.70204, `roctracer` 4.1.70200 -> 4.1.70204). So the ROCm patch bump is what fixes this, and it does not require the torch/Python upgrade: AMD publishes `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1`, which matches our current rocm720 stack (Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.10, torch 2.9.1) with only the ROCm patch level changed. #30984 remains the vehicle for the rocm724 flavors; nothing here competes with it. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` — libdrm-amdgpu is a prerequisite for any 7.2.4 base The step that fixes empty `hipDeviceGetName` results skipped every `*rocm720*` flavor on the grounds that "ROCm 7.2 base images already ship these packages". That is a property of how the base installed ROCm, not of its version, and it does not hold for 7.2.4: | base image | ROCm install | AMD libdrm + `amdgpu.ids` | | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | `amdgpu-install --usecase=rocm` | yes (`/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids`, `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/20-amdgpu.conf`) | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | `apt-get install rocm` | no | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0` (used by #30984) | `apt-get install rocm` | no | Verified from the registry manifests and layer listings, and measured on an MI355X. The only `amdgpu.ids` left in a 7.2.4 image is the distro's, from `libdrm-common`, and what that costs depends on the release: | base | AMD libdrm | distro `amdgpu.ids` | `get_device_name(0)` on MI355X | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_*` (today's rocm720) | yes | 10962 B, no `74A*`/`75A*` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_*` | no | 10962 B, no `74A*`/`75A*` | `''` | | `rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_*` (used by #30984) | no | 23250 B, `74A0`/`74A1`/`74A2`, no `75A*` | `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` | Ubuntu 24.04's table does carry the MI300 series, so a noble 7.2.4 base resolves MI300X and degrades only on MI355X — and it degrades to a generic vendor string rather than an empty one, which is worse to detect because anything testing for a missing name sees a non-empty result. Either way every device-name-keyed tuned config (fused MoE Triton configs, K3 SP collective tables, `moe_front` configs) silently misses. `graphics/7.2.4` publishes the packages, and its `libdrm-amdgpu-common` lists `74A1 AMD Instinct MI300X` and `75A3 AMD Instinct MI355X`. The step now tests for `/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` and derives the graphics repo (`x.y.z`, falling back to `x.y`) plus the codename from the image itself, with an `AMDGPU_GRAPHICS_VERSION` build-arg override. Behaviour for the flavors on main is unchanged: 7.2.0 still skips, and 7.0 still installs from `graphics/7.0 jammy`. Note for #30984: it extends the skip to `*rocm724*` on a noble 7.2.4 base, which ships a `gfx950-rocm724` image reporting `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` — measured on its exact base image, details in [that PR](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30984#issuecomment-5336201854). This commit makes that arm unnecessary. ### `scripts/ci/amd/check_hip_graph_profiling.py` — the acceptance check `test/registered/profiling/test_start_profile.py` only asserts that the trace directory is non-empty, so an image whose traces contain no GPU kernels passes it. The probe closes that gap: it captures a graph, replays it under `torch.profiler`, and compares the device kernels in the exported trace against the number launched. An eager control run separates "cannot trace graph replay" from "cannot trace anything", and each phase runs in its own process under a timeout because 7.2.0 can wedge inside `hipGraphLaunch` rather than merely lose events. It also prints the ROCm version, the mapped HIP/tracing sonames, and warns when the device name does not identify the part (the libdrm gap above) — on an Instinct arch that means anything without an Instinct model in it, so the generic `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` a noble 7.2.4 base reports on MI355X trips it as surely as an empty string does. Two measured properties of the failure decide how the check is built, and getting either wrong makes the probe pass a broken image: - **The loss is partial, not total.** A 7.2.0 image that drops 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels still writes a trace full of kernels, so the verdict compares traced against launched rather than asking whether any arrived. The eager control is held to the same completeness bar, which keeps a runtime that drops events generally distinct from one that only loses graph events. - **It only appears past a graph size.** A four-node capture traces completely on 7.2.0. The default capture is 64 kernels (`--graph-nodes`), where 7.2.0 reports 448 of 512 and 7.2.4 reports 512 of 512, ten runs out of ten on each. ``` torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0.git7e1940d4 (hip 7.2.26015-fc0010cf6a), rocm 7.2.0 device: 'AMD Instinct MI355X' (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) hip/tracing libs: libamdhip64.so.7.2.70200, libhsa-runtime64.so.1.18.70200, librocprofiler-register.so.0.6.0, libroctracer64.so.4.1.70200 eager launch: 512/512 kernels traced, 11246 us device time, 6213 trace events graph replay: 448/512 kernels traced, 3983 us device time, 1005 trace events VERDICT: FAIL -- eager launches trace completely but 64 of 512 graph-replay kernels never reach it. This is the roctracer reporting failure fixed in ROCm 7.2.2 (https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/6102). Profile with --disable-cuda-graph on this image, or move to a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime. ``` Deliberately not registered in CI yet: on today's rocm720 images it is expected to fail, and (per #34452) it can take the process down with it. It should be registered in the AMD suites once the images move to a ROCm 7.2.2 or newer runtime, at which point it guards the behaviour permanently. ### `docs/docs/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.mdx` Document the known gap for users on the current images, how to check an image, and the `--disable-cuda-graph` workaround, with the caveat that decode numbers collected that way exclude the replay path. ## Accuracy Tests No model-facing code changes. The Dockerfile change affects image contents only; it makes `torch.cuda.get_device_name()` resolve on 7.2.4 bases, which restores tuned-config selection rather than altering kernels. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to the change itself. On the current 7.2.0 images the reported symptom is that decode kernels are absent from traces; the probe is the measurement that qualifies a fixed image. ## Test plan Local, without GPU access: - Every branch of the new Dockerfile shell logic exercised in a sandbox with stubbed apt: base with `amdgpu.ids` skips; ROCm 7.2.4 resolves `graphics/7.2.4`; ROCm 7.0.0 falls back to `graphics/7.0` (matching today's hardcoded values); missing version info fails with an actionable error; `AMDGPU_GRAPHICS_VERSION` overrides. Repo URLs and package availability checked against repo.radeon.com. - Dockerfile parses as a single `RUN` instruction (`dockerfile-parse`). - Probe: trace parsing validated against a real `export_chrome_trace` output plus synthetic device events, all verdict paths (pass, eager-blind, eager-incomplete, graph hang, graph crash, graph incomplete) exercised with canned phase results, and the timeout path's process-group kill verified. On a host with no GPU it reports `environment: unusable` and exits 1. On hardware — 8x MI355X (gfx950), KMD 6.16.13, this branch merged with #35398 (clean merge), plus a `gfx950-rocm724` image built from that tree: | image | ROCm | probe | graph replay | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | 7.2.0 | FAIL | 448/512 | | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818` | 7.2.0 | FAIL | 448/512 | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1` | 7.2.4 | PASS | 512/512 | | built from this branch, `gfx950-rocm724` | 7.2.4 | PASS | 512/512 | Five repeats on each SGLang image gave identical counts, so the check does not flake. The eager control traces 512/512 on both runtimes at every graph size tried (4 through 1024 nodes), which is what places the loss on graph replay rather than on profiling generally. The user-facing symptom, on a real decode rather than the microbenchmark — gpt-oss-20b-bf16, triton attention backend, `/start_profile` with `num_steps=10`. The two graph-enabled runs agree exactly on 3520 `cpu_op`, 1993 `cuda_runtime` and 63 graph replays, so only the runtime differs: | run | device kernel events in trace | | --- | --- | | ROCm 7.2.0 shipped image, CUDA graphs on | 513 | | ROCm 7.2.0 shipped image, `--disable-cuda-graph` | 3924 | | ROCm 7.2.4 built from this branch, CUDA graphs on | 3933 | That is the reported bug, the documented workaround recovering from it, and the 7.2.4 image recovering from it with graphs left on. libdrm, on the same host, and the warning that reports it: | image | device name | probe warns | | --- | --- | --- | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_*` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | no | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu22.04_*` | `''` | yes | | `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_*` | `'AMD Radeon Graphics'` | yes | | built from this branch, `gfx950-rocm724` | `'AMD Instinct MI355X'` | no | The built image takes `/opt/amdgpu/share/libdrm/amdgpu.ids` from `graphics/7.2.4` and copies it to `/usr/share/libdrm/`, where it lists both `74A1` and `75A3`. Not covered: gfx942 / MI300X, for want of the hardware. signal.title: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: make empty-batch guard tuple-aware on fused AR+quant path
signal.text: ## Problem `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x-rocm720` partition 0 (`test_qwen35_fp8_ar_fusion_mi35x.py`) has been failing deterministically on every scheduled run since 2026-08-16 12:08 UTC. The empty DP-attention batch guard added in #34474 reads `hidden_states.shape[0]` right after `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs()`: ```python if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: ``` But when the fused AR+quant path is active (`--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` + `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on a block-FP8 Qwen3.5), `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn()` returns `hidden_states` as a **tuple** produced by `forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_group()` — `(fp8, scale)` for the attention layer (`keep_bf16=False`) and `(bf16, fp8, scale)` for the GatedDeltaNet layer (`keep_bf16=True`). A tuple has no `.shape`, so the guard raises and the server dies during decode CUDA-graph capture: ``` File "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 806, in forward if not forward_batch.forward_mode.is_idle() and hidden_states.shape[0] > 0: AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'shape' [2026-08-18 00:27:54] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed. ``` The scheduler child dying takes the process tree with it, which surfaces to the test as the unhelpful `Server process exited with code -9`. This only affects the `fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant` variant (GPUs 0-3). The `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` control variant (GPUs 4-7) stays on the tensor path and is unaffected. Only `qwen3_5.py` carries this guard, which is why no other suite regressed. Failing job: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32083881457/job/95552260420 ## Fix Take the row count in a tuple-aware way, preserving the guard's original intent. This is behavior-preserving for the fused path: `prepare_attn()` short-circuits on `hidden_states.shape[0] == 0` *before* the fusion branch, so a tuple can only ever appear when the row count is already `> 0`. The new guard is therefore always `True` on the tuple path (exactly the pre-#34474 behavior), while the tensor path keeps the empty-batch protection. ## Verification Reproduced and verified end-to-end on an 8x MI350X (gfx950) node, following the CI flow exactly — same image (`rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260817`), same `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh`, same `run_suite.py --suite stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x --auto-partition-id 0 --auto-partition-size 3`. **Before** (at `91144797c`, the failing scheduled-run SHA): `AttributeError` at `qwen3_5.py:806`, byte-for-byte the same signature as the CI log. **After:** | Variant | GPUs | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | Output tok/s | Threshold | Status | | ------- | ---- | -------- | ------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------- | ------ | | fused-ar-rms-per-group-quant | 0,1,2,3 | 0.951 | 0.009 | 53.66 | 4067.56 | 0.94 | PASS | | disable-fused-ar-quant-opt-out | 4,5,6,7 | 0.940 | 0.009 | 53.85 | 4010.65 | 0.94 | PASS | ``` Ran 1 test in 176.302s OK Test Summary: 1/1 passed ``` cc @Lzy17 Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149183042](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149183042)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149298089](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149298089)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD][bugfix] Add moe_ep_size/moe_tp_size to the allreduce-fusion gate test stub
signal.text: ## Motivation `TestAiterAllreduceFusionGate` in `test/registered/ops/test_aiter_allreduce_fusion_amd.py` has been erroring on every AMD run since 2026-08-12. The hybrid EP+TP guard added in #30700 (commit `c7c03ec53`, 2026-08-11) reads two new fields at the very top of `should_fuse_mlp_allreduce_with_next_layer`: ```python parallel = get_parallel() if parallel.moe_ep_size > 1 and parallel.moe_tp_size > 1: return False ``` The AMD gate test stubs `get_parallel()` with a `SimpleNamespace` that only carries `tp_size`, so every one of the 7 gate cases now raises: ``` AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'moe_ep_size' ``` Because the guard sits before every other branch, all 7 cases fail; CI's failfast only surfaces the first one (`test_dense_tp_fuses`). This is a test-stub gap only. The aiter fused all-reduce + RMSNorm kernel itself is fine: the three GPU subtests (`test_fused_ar_rms_benchmark`, `test_fused_ar_rms_multi_hidden_dim`, `test_fused_ar_rms_residual_accuracy`) pass. Scheduled ROCm 7.2 runs on `main`, shard 3 — the guard landed at 2026-08-11T23:46Z: | run date | shard 3 | | --- | --- | | 08-09, 08-10, 08-11 17:46 | success | | 08-12 12:21 onward (every run) | failure | ## Modifications Add `moe_ep_size=1` and `moe_tp_size=1` to the `get_parallel()` stub. Both being 1 means no MoE EP and no MoE TP, so the hybrid EP+TP guard stays inactive and the aiter branch is what decides — which is what all 7 existing cases are written to exercise. No existing assertion changes meaning. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — test-only change, no kernel or model forward code touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149134311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134311)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149134025](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149134025)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Removes three elementwise kernels from the Kimi-K3 MoE path: the D2D copy of the routed output, the contiguous copy of `routed_input`, and the dtype conversion of the router correction bias. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> Three independent commits. **MoE output zero-copy.** Hooks the aiter runner into `zero_copy_context`: the caller-published buffer is passed down through a new `output` argument on `aiter.fused_moe` so the top-k sum lands there directly, dropping the trailing `latent.copy_()` in `_forward_routed`. Depends on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4617; it is probed with `inspect.signature`, so older aiter builds fall back to the copy. **Skip the `routed_input` contiguous copy.** The fused front splits gate_up / router_logits / routed_input out of a single GEMM's output, so `routed_input` is a non-contiguous view. The mxfp8 quant kernel aiter uses for K3 indexes rows by `input.stride(-2)`, so it can consume that view as is. **Skip the router bias cast.** The correction bias parameter is stored as fp32 for the CUDA kernels, but aiter's `biased_grouped_topk` `reinterpret_cast`s `gating_output` and `correction_bias` to the same template type and therefore requires them to share a dtype, and K3's `gating_output` on aiter is bf16. That costs one conversion per MoE layer per step. signal.title: [PD] Align defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori
signal.text: - RFC: [PD disaggregation: single protocol layer, per-backend transport #33861](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33861) - Staged implementation plan and PR tracking: [PD shared-protocol implementation plan #34510](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34510) - Preceding PR: [NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout #34692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34692) ## Background #34692 added the missing NIXL Prefill bootstrap timeout. This PR continues Step 1 of #34510 by aligning clear, low-risk defensive protocol behavior across Mooncake, NIXL, and Mori without changing the Common state machine, wire format, completion channel, or Transport architecture. These changes preserve the current backend structure. They only add missing behavior or fix local race/layout issues. Extracting the common protocol and Transport remains work for later stages. ## Outline This PR groups the changes into five areas: 1. Complete Mori peer/request failure detection and ABORT delivery; 2. Prevent NIXL/Mori workers from executing stale work after teardown; 3. Keep Mooncake/NIXL control loops serving after malformed messages; 4. Align Mori MHA/MLA KV layout planning; 5. Fix the initialization race before the Mooncake control thread starts. ## 1. Mori peer and request failure handling Related commits: - `b285ea79ce` — `align Mori Decode heartbeat` - `62c13f66ba` — `align Mori abort handling with common protocol` Mori Decode did not start the existing Common heartbeat checker, so a dead Prefill would not trigger route/cache eviction or active-room failure. This PR only wires in the existing `_start_heartbeat_checker_thread()`, matching Mooncake and NIXL. Common Receiver sends an `ABORT` frame without a Mori guard, while Mori Prefill previously validated `MORI_GUARD` first and discarded ABORT as malformed. This PR recognizes the existing Common ABORT frame before guard validation: - Mark an active room as `Failed`; - Continue to ignore Success/unknown rooms; - Drop only the current message when ABORT is malformed. This only fixes ABORT delivery. It does not define ACK, cancel, or quiescence semantics. Terminal-state and safe-release behavior remains deferred to the later RFC stages. ## 2. Skip stale work after room teardown Related commit: - `46056556a5` — `skip cleared rooms in NIXL and Mori workers` Chunks already queued do not disappear when the Sender clears a room. - NIXL previously allowed a missing room to bypass its Failed check and then enter the exception path at the `transfer_infos` assertion; - Mori could continue into `add_transfer_request()` and subsequent terminalization. Mooncake already checks at `transfer_worker()` entry whether the room still exists or is `Failed`. On a match, it finishes the current chunk trace, removes residual `_staging_outstanding` state, and continues without reading that room's transfer metadata. This PR makes the other two backends discard queued tasks for missing rooms at worker entry: - NIXL aligns with Mooncake's missing-room/Failed guard, removes the room's residual `_staging_outstanding` count, and continues; - Mori uses an equivalent early return because chunk execution lives in Sender `_run_chunk()`. The stale task therefore cannot read deleted `transfer_infos`, submit to the Transport, advance state, or trigger terminalization. Existing `clear()` paths remain responsible for normal room cleanup; these guards only consume queue items that arrive after teardown. When the common protocol is extracted, this should be replaced by unified idempotent room teardown/tombstone semantics. For now, the backend-local guards avoid expanding the scope into Common state-machine changes. ## 3. Isolate malformed control messages Related commit: - `a716ceaac7` — `harden Mooncake and NIXL control message parsing` Mooncake/NIXL control loops serve multiple rooms, but previously indexed, decoded, or unpacked frames directly. An empty message, truncated ABORT, invalid guard, or unexpected frame count could terminate the long-lived thread. Mori already treats one message as the exception boundary: its Prefill bootstrap loop and Decode status loop validate guard/frame input inside `while True`, log an error for the current message, and continue receiving the next one. A bad frame therefore does not remove control-plane service from later rooms. This PR aligns Mooncake and NIXL with that behavior by adding minimum frame/tag/guard validation at the Mooncake Prefill/Decode and NIXL Prefill/Decode-staging message entries. Empty messages, truncated fields, and invalid encodings are logged and skipped without terminating the long-lived control thread. ## 4. Align Mori KV layout planning Related commits: - `48c5e1569d` — `align Mori speculative MHA layout with common planner` - `081186c4c8` — `align Mori same-PP and hybrid MLA layout planning` Together, these commits fix Mori descriptor slicing that differed from the existing Common planner. The first part handles Decode-only speculative KV layout: ```text [K_main..., V_main..., draft_K..., draft_V...] ``` Mori previously split descriptors in half and could select a draft region as main V. This PR uses the same V-offset rule as `get_mha_kv_ptrs_with_pp()`. The second part adds: - Same-PP peer descriptor lists are already aligned local layouts and must not have the global layer offset applied again; - Hybrid MLA uses MLA descriptor slicing instead of falling through to the regular MHA path. These fixes remain inside Mori for now because they operate on Mori `MemoryDesc` lists, and planner/materialization are still coupled in Mori Manager. A later stage can extract target/draft, same-PP, and MHA/MLA logical layer selection into a Common helper, leaving Mori responsible only for mapping the common plan to `MemoryDesc` and `batch_write()`. ## 5. Initialize Mooncake state before starting the control thread Related commit: - `12a88dbcfe` — `initialize Mooncake session state before control thread` Mooncake Prefill previously started its receive thread before creating state that the thread accesses: ```text session_failures failed_sessions session_lock ``` If Decode registration arrived immediately after thread startup, it could hit an initialization race. This PR only moves these three fields before `start_prefill_thread()` while preserving all other queue, worker, probe, and receive ordering. This is intentionally a minimal ordering fix rather than a Step 1 reorganization of backend thread lifecycle. When the common Manager/Transport is extracted, control-thread initialization, startup, shared state, and shutdown should be managed together. ## Testing CPU red/green regression tests are kept on a dedicated test branch: ```text branch: https://github.com/jambow0320/sglang/tree/rfc-pd-test path: test/registered/unit/disaggregation/rfc-test/ ``` Coverage includes: - Mori ABORT delivery before guard validation; - Cleared-room stale work in NIXL/Mori; - Malformed control-message isolation in Mooncake/NIXL; - Mori speculative MHA descriptor selection; - Mooncake session-state initialization order. The tests pass with the fixes and reproduce the original failures against the corresponding unfixed source. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32110778332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32110778332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32110778109](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32110778109)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
