signal.title: [Quant] Load compressed-tensors quantized lm_head instead of value-casting it
signal.text: ## Motivation compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize `lm_head` (e.g. FP8 per-channel weights targeted via `re:.*lm_head`) currently load as gibberish: `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` returns `None` for `ParallelLMHead`, so the head falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod` — the packed fp8 weight is value-cast into a bf16 parameter and `lm_head.weight_scale` is silently dropped (`Parameter lm_head.weight_scale not found in params_dict` at load). ## Modifications - `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method`: add a `ParallelLMHead` branch that resolves a linear scheme and returns `CompressedTensorsLinearMethod` (mirroring the existing ModelOpt handling); unquantized heads keep the current embedding default. - New `get_lm_head_scheme`: the head is treated as quantized only when a config target names it by layer name (exact, `re:` regex, or dotted suffix) and it is not in `ignore`. Module-type targets like `Linear` are not consulted, so checkpoints following the common convention (head unquantized and unmentioned) are unaffected. The resolved target is passed through to `get_scheme_dict` so suffix matches are not re-derived by the stricter `find_matched_target`. Block-FP8 heads are rejected with a clear error (the vocab-parallel weight loader cannot shard `vocab/block_n` weight scales). - Unit test: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_lm_head.py` (CPU, `base-a-test-cpu`). No other changes needed: the vocab-parallel weight loader already shards `output_dim=0` params, the model loader already runs `process_weights_after_loading` on the head, and the logits path already routes through `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method`. Known limits: models that construct `ParallelLMHead` without a `prefix` keep today's unquantized-head behavior (the empty layer name never matches a target); `update_weights_from_disk` with a quantized head is untested; speculative-decoding draft paths that borrow the target head are a separate follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests A/B on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with a Qwen3.8-27B mixed-precision compressed-tensors checkpoint (NVFP4 MLPs, FP8 per-channel `lm_head`), identical flags, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200`: | | GSM8K | Invalid | |---|---|---| | main | 0.000 | 0.850 | | this PR | 0.955 | 0.000 | On main, greedy decoding degenerates into repetition loops on any prompt; with this PR the head loads through `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` and the `weight_scale` warning is gone. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No impact on unquantized-head checkpoints (resolution happens once at init). A quantized head replaces a bf16 matmul with the standard fp8 linear path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: Avoid materializing GDN QKV tensors during target verification
signal.text: ## Summary This PR removes redundant Q/K/V materialization from compatible GDN speculative target-verification paths. `causal_conv1d_update` already produces packed QKV. Previously, every GDN layer launched `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to copy that output into three contiguous tensors before Triton target verification. Triton accepts explicit token strides, so it can consume zero-copy `torch.split`/`view` tensors instead. The optimization is route-aware: - Triton and ReplaySSM target verification use strided Q/K/V views. - Prefill, FlashInfer, CuTeDSL, and other routes requiring contiguous inputs retain materialization. - Model arithmetic, recurrent-state updates, speculative acceptance, logits, and sampling are unchanged. This eliminates one memory-copy kernel launch per GDN layer on every compatible target-verification pass. ## Profile evidence Matched H200 CPU/GPU traces using Qwen3.5-4B, ReplaySSM, and NEXTN T=3: | Target-verification metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | QKV-split launches/pass | 24 | 0 | **-100%** | | QKV-split GPU time/pass | 56.946 us | 0 | **-56.946 us** | | CUDA-graph kernels | 452 | 428 | **-24** | | CUDA-graph span | 8,132.684 us | 8,040.898 us | **-91.786 us / -1.129%** | The graph-span reduction's approximate 95% interval was **79.732-103.841 us**. ## Standardized GSM8K benchmark 3 alternating baseline/QKV pairs ran on the same H200 with fresh servers, seed 0, empty prefix cache, and a 30-second cooldown. The benchmark used its defaults: 200 questions, five shots, 512 maximum output tokens, temperature 0, and parallelism 64. ### Pair 1 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,433.642 tok/s | 6,762.467 tok/s | **+5.111%** | | Latency | 5.379 s | 5.145 s | **-4.350%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7374 ms | 9.4735 ms | **-2.710%** | ### Pair 2 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,202.258 tok/s | 6,366.221 tok/s | **+2.644%** | | Latency | 5.470 s | 5.401 s | **-1.261%** | | Engine TPOT | 10.2534 ms | 9.7761 ms | **-4.655%** | ### Pair 3 | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,496.073 tok/s | 6,669.102 tok/s | **+2.664%** | | Latency | 5.270 s | 5.134 s | **-2.581%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.3372 ms | 9.4393 ms | **+1.093%** | ### Three-pair aggregate | Metric | Baseline | Patch | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput | 6,377.324 tok/s | 6,599.263 tok/s | **+3.480%** | | Latency | 5.373 s | 5.227 s | **-2.723%** | | Engine TPOT | 9.7760 ms | 9.5630 ms | **-2.179%** | | Accuracy | 87.667% | 87.500% | -0.167 pp | ## Reproduction Server: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ PYTHONPATH=<sglang-source>/python \ sglang serve /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --port 30000 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --language-only \ --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}' \ --context-length 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \ --random-seed 0 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B/ \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --enable-linear-replayssm-spec ``` Benchmark: ```bash python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \ --data-path /data/gsm8k/test.jsonl ``` Dataset SHA-256: ```text 3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14 ``` ## Validation - Exact target-verification output and recurrent-state parity. - ReplaySSM ring/fold parity and routing coverage. - Contiguous-input behavior retained for unsupported routes. - 31 affected H200 tests passed, covering 46 parameterized cases. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32203074330](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203074330)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32203074047](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32203074047)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Support Kimi-K3 ModelOpt mixed NVFP4/FP8 checkpoint
signal.text: ## Motivation The official [nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4) checkpoint is a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint: - routed MoE experts use NVFP4 with SiTU (`beta=4`, `linear_beta=25`); - supported attention projections use weight-only `FP8_PB_WO` with 128x128 block scales. Current `main` cannot serve this checkpoint with the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE backend. It rejects gated `situ` during startup, and it does not instantiate/load the checkpoint's block-FP8 attention scales. The K3 fused-front also needs to pass its row-strided FP32 router output through the stride-aware precomputed-routing interface. ## Modifications - Add gated `ActivationType.Situ` support to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP4 runner. - Pass the model-provided SiTU coefficients as GEMM1 alpha/beta and keep the W13 up-dequant scale inside the SiTU activation, avoiding double application through `g1_scale_c`. - Route K3 SiTU fused-front output through SGLang's stride-aware FP32 precomputed-routing path while keeping fused-front enabled. - Dispatch ModelOpt `FP8_PB_WO` layers to SGLang's native serialized block-FP8 linear method with dynamic activation quantization and 128x128 weight blocks. - Load ModelOpt's logical 4-D block scales into SGLang's 2-D `weight_scale_inv` parameters, including fused MLA projections and TP-sharded KDA projections. - Dequantize the FP8 MLA `kv_b` weight before K3's post-load absorption. - Dequantize only K3's small `f_a`/`f_b`/`b` projections once after loading into BF16 buffers for the existing fused tiny-GEMM path; the main KDA projections remain on native block-FP8 GEMMs. - Compile the KDA recompute kernel for the BF16 activation/parameter dtype rather than the serialized FP8 weight dtype. - Add regression coverage for the SiTU scale contract, `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch, block-scale dequantization, and the fused B/F_a path. ## Accuracy Tests Validated the released checkpoint on 8x GB300 with TP8: - GSM8K-200: **197/200 = 0.985** - `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm` - `trtllm_mla` prefill and decode attention backends - fused-front enabled - K3 all-reduce fusion enabled - prefill CUDA Graph enabled; decode CUDA Graph enabled for batch sizes 1/2/4 - concurrency 4 - no fused-front-disable environment workaround Both raw completion and chat-completion smoke tests produced coherent, correct answers before the evaluation. The validation used the final patch contents in this PR. The branch was then rebased onto `eafbe2cb6f` from `main`; the intervening upstream commits do not touch this PR's files. Targeted checks: - 13/13 ModelOpt NVFP4 SiTU scale tests passed. - The ModelOpt mixed `FP8_PB_WO` dispatch test passed. - The K3 B/F_a fused-path tests passed, including CUDA Graph replay and block-FP8 dequantization. - Black, Python 3.12 `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not measured. This PR is a correctness and checkpoint-compatibility change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32202731802](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202731802)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32202731542](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202731542)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Support MiniMax-H3 GGUF DiT checkpoints
signal.text: ## Summary - Load an explicit local or Hugging Face MiniMax-H3 GGUF DiT file and execute standard/K-quant linears with the existing SRT CUDA GGML kernels. - Support both the original timestep MLP and AdaLN-pruned curve-table architecture, including TP-aware QKV loading, sequence parallelism, and residency offload. - Auto-detect Comfy AdaLN-pruned BF16 and pruned_fp8_scaled checkpoints, while rejecting unsupported ConvRot INT8 checkpoints before weight loading. ## Scope and limitations - GGUF replaces only the DiT. The Qwen3-VL text encoder and VAEs continue to load from MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3. - The initial GGUF path is CUDA-only and does not support FSDP inference. TP degrees must preserve GGML quantization-block alignment. - A concrete GGUF file must be selected; bare repositories are rejected because they can contain multiple variants and quantization levels. - quality=high continues to require the audited official BF16 transformer. ## Documentation - Add a cookbook support matrix and complete commands for Comfy pruned BF16, Comfy pruned FP8, and Unsloth Q4_K GGUF. - Document supported repositories, CLI behavior, parallel/offload compatibility, and unsupported formats. ## Coverage - Add focused unit coverage for GGUF metadata and tensor decoding, curve interpolation, URL/path resolution, custom checkpoint iteration, FP8 marker dispatch, TP QKV loading, FSDP rejection, and quality-mode admission. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32202695640](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202695640)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32202695216](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32202695216)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [VLM] Route every multimodal processor through the worker pool's call site
signal.text: ## Motivation `process_and_combine_mm_data` is the function the multimodal processor worker pool actually runs (`MultimodalProcessorExecutor.run(self.process_and_combine_mm_data, ...)`). **33 of the 37 call sites called it directly**, so those models can never use the pool: with `--mm-processor-worker-num > 1` they build the thread pool and its `deepcopy`'d processor clones at startup and then route every request straight past them. The failure is silent — the model just serves at one-worker speed. That is why PaddleOCR-VL preprocessed pages single-threaded from the day it was added: opting it in (#35318) moved 32-way concurrent throughput from 6.7 to 10.9 req/s on an H200, purely by letting an 87 ms/page preprocess overlap. Only `qwen_vl`, `kimi_k25`, `kimi_k3` and `muse_glimmer` were on the right call site. ## Modifications Mechanically rewrite the 33 sync call sites to `await self.process_and_combine_mm_data_async(...)`, and add a test that pins the invariant. **This is an identity transform, not a behavior change:** - `process_and_combine_mm_data_async` delegates straight to the sync function when `self.mm_processor_executor is None`, which is the case for every model that has not opted into concurrency. - Awaiting a coroutine that never itself suspends does not yield to the event loop, so request interleaving is bit-for-bit unchanged. Only `await loop.run_in_executor(...)` — reached solely when an executor exists — introduces a suspension point. So nothing about scheduling moves until a model sets `supports_mm_processor_concurrency`. What this PR buys is that opting a model in becomes a three-line change instead of a call-site migration plus an audit. ## Verification The migration was generated and checked by AST, not by hand: - 33 sync call sites before, **0** after; 37 async call sites after. - Every call site sits inside an `async def`, before and after — so each edit is exactly `await` + `_async`. - Each of the 33 changed lines differs from its original **only** by that rename (0 deviations, checked mechanically against the diff). - Every touched file compiles; `isort` / `black` / `ruff` clean. `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py` re-runs the same scan as a CPU test, so a processor added later cannot quietly opt out of the pool again. It reports 37 call sites on this branch and would have reported 33 offenders before it. ## Notes for reviewers Turning concurrency *on* for a given model is deliberately **not** part of this PR. That decision is per-model and needs measurement, for two reasons: - The executor is a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, so a model only benefits if its preprocessing releases the GIL (PIL / numpy / torch C code does; pure-Python preprocessing would not). - More workers spread request arrivals, which fragments GPU prefill batches — the tradeoff `qwen_vl` documents when it picks 2 workers, and which showed up in measurement as `--mm-processor-worker-num 8` being slower than 4 on PaddleOCR-VL. `muse_glimmer` is already on the async call site but has no capability flag, so it is the one existing model that could opt in for free once measured. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add a test (`test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_processor_async_call_sites.py`) - [x] Verify the change is an identity transform rather than benchmarking it (there is nothing to benchmark: behavior is unchanged until a model opts in) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32150110753](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32150110753)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32150110283](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32150110283)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.author: caiwenwen11

signal.title: [PD] Fall back to cpu_tensor when host-pool retraction cannot fit
signal.text: ## Motivation `resolve_decode_retraction_backup`, added in #34801, picks the PD decode retraction backend on capability alone — mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, priority preemption, pool class. Whether the host pool fits never comes up, and it has to: `host_pool` mirrors the device KV pool 1:1 on every scheduler, while the only capacity check sits downstream in `pool_host/base.py`, well past the point of no return. On a GB300 tray that check can never pass. Four Blackwell Ultra GPUs hold 1110 GiB of HBM against 955 GiB of Grace LPDDR5X, so a KV pool sized to fill HBM cannot be mirrored into host RAM — a hybrid-SWA model at TP4 wants 1059.80 GB against ~854 GB free: ``` ValueError: Not enough host memory available. Requesting 117.76 GB but only have 98.90 GB free. ``` No workload or freed page cache gets there, and any node whose HBM rivals its DRAM lands the same way. An inferred default that cannot be satisfied should step aside; one asked for by name should still fail loudly. ## Modifications The inferred choice degrades to `cpu_tensor` with a warning naming both figures. Explicit `host_pool` still hard-fails, since the gate sits inside the `backend is None` branch. The budget reads `available` — what `HostKVCache.__init__` itself gates on. `_agree_across_ranks` all-reduces MIN over the world CPU group, shaped after `sync_fixed_hicache_size`, so no rank diverges. Reaching it needs a rank-uniform predicate, which splits the eligibility test: mode, DCP, decode radix cache, KV offload, and priority preemption come from the config bags and gate the estimate, while `supports_host_pool` is per-rank and only picks the backend. Prefill, embedding, and non-PD servers skip the estimate entirely. Three sizing fixes: - `_local_scheduler_count` mirrors the launcher's `pp_size_per_node * tp_size_per_node` plus the classic-DP replica factor. `tp_size // nnodes` undercounts past `pp_size > 1` and can reach zero. Reads `configured_tp_size()` / `configured_pp_size()`, which don't assert before process-group init. - MTP/EAGLE draft pools count, since the mirror packs them into its own `layer_num`. - `_kv_pool_bytes` takes both `get_kv_size_bytes` shapes. It tests for the `(k, v)` pair rather than the scalar: MLA returns `numpy.int64`, which `isinstance(size, int)` misses. `hicache_ratio` keys off the pre-fallback verdict, so the gate cannot enlarge the pool it just rejected. Deliberately not keyed off "a host pool gets built anyway", which would cut 2.0 to 1.0 for hierarchical-cache users on the decode-radix-cache path. The gate and the normalisation cover different cases — reverting the normalisation alone on 4×GB300: | Configuration | Normalisation | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | non-PD MLA | reverted | starts — the gate excludes it | | non-PD MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | | PD decode MLA | reverted | crashes in `_kv_pool_bytes` | | PD decode MLA | present | starts, `/health` 200 | The estimate is a lower bound; the per-rank gate stays authoritative. Page round-up and SIDECAR draft pools are unmodelled, because reproducing host-pool sizing here would go stale quietly. That belongs in a shared sizing helper, along with the scalar/tuple split and the unified pools — they return `(0, 0)` while subclassing MHA/SWA, so they would leave the gate inert rather than loud. Unreachable today: `--enable-unified-memory` with PD is MLA hybrid-Mamba only. ## Accuracy Tests Outputs are untouched — this resolves startup configuration, not the retraction path. `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_capacity.py` is new and CPU-registered, covering the PP and DP rank arithmetic, fits and doesn't-fit, the reserve, draft-pool accounting, both accessor shapes, the scope, and the ratio invariant driven through the resolver itself. Each fix was mutation-checked by reverting it: | Reverted | Result | | --- | --- | | ratio keyed off the post-fallback backend | 1 failure, `AssertionError: 2.0 != 1.0` | | reduction re-gated on the per-rank predicate | 2 failures, `_agree_across_ranks` called 0 times | | shape normalisation | 3 failures | | config-uniform gate | 2 failures | 166 tests pass across that file, `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`, and `test_server_args.py`; 20/20 under the `unittest` runner; pre-commit clean. On 4×GB300, a hybrid-SWA PD decode server falls back with identical figures on all four ranks and no deadlock, an MLA server starts clean both non-PD and PD decode, and a plain non-PD server never reaches the estimate. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The gate runs once per scheduler at startup, only for a config-eligible decode server, and the steady-state decode path is unchanged. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). signal.title: [DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel
signal.text: > Generated by Claude. **Stacked on #35041.** GitHub cannot use that PR's branch as a base here (its head lives in the fork, and a cross-fork PR's base must be a branch of the base repo), so this targets `main` and carries #35041's commit underneath. **Review only the second commit** (`[DSA] Route the ragged prefill top-k to the v2 kernel`); the diff collapses to it once #35041 merges and this is rebased. ## Motivation The extend-shaped `RAGGED` transform is the last DSA top-k path still served by the legacy sgl-kernel kernel (`topk_transform_prefill_ragged_kernel`), even though it is the cheapest one to serve. The DeepGEMM contiguous-KV indexer emits columns that are already absolute positions in the batch's flattened KV, so unlike the paged path there is no page table to gather through -- the entire transform is a per-row add. That is exactly v2's raw-index mode (added in #35041) plus a bias. ## What this does - **`TopKProblem` gains a `bias` field (default 0)** that `emit` adds to every selected index. Every pre-existing construction site omits it, so the compiler constant-folds the add away — see the SASS check below. - **`topk_ragged_kernel`** selects inside `[row_starts[b], row_starts[b] + seq_lens[b])` and emits `position + out_offsets[b]`. One block per row, and **no cluster path**: the cluster split exists to spread one very long row across blocks, which only pays off for the few-row decode shapes; prefill has thousands of rows. - **Unaligned window starts.** The window start is an arbitrary token offset, so the read base is rounded down to a 4-float boundary and the ≤ 3 columns that pulls in are masked to `-FLT_MAX` in place. They are a preceding request's columns *of the same row* — real finite scores that would otherwise win the selection. The row belongs to this block alone and the score buffer is dead after the top-k, so the write races with nothing. It lands after the PDL wait (the indexer rounds its own KV base down to 4 as well and would otherwise overwrite the mask) and is published by the `__syncthreads()` that every `forward()` already runs before it reads any score. - Rows with `seq_len <= topk` keep a trivial path that never reads the scores, so alignment never arises there. It cannot reuse `trivial_transform`, whose `-1` padding would pick up the bias. - `dsa_topk_backend` routes the RAGGED branch to it; prefill-CP (`batch_idx_list is not None`) stays on the legacy kernel, since its `topk_indices_offset` is built from `cu_seqlens_q` rather than the KV bases. ## The existing kernels are untouched Built the JIT module before and after and diffed the SASS per function (`cuobjdump -sass`, 12 kernels / 56648 instructions): | kernel | result | |---|---| | `topk_main_kernel` × {level 0..3} × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_small_batch_kernel` × {INDICES, PAGE_TABLE} | byte-identical | | `topk_plan` | byte-identical | | `topk_persistent_cluster_kernel` | same instruction count (2808); `+1 IMAD.MOV.U32 / -1 NOP` | `cuobjdump -res-usage` is identical field for field on all 12 (`REG:32 STACK LOCAL:0 SHARED CONSTANT`). The new kernel itself is `REG:32 STACK:0 SHARED:20224 LOCAL:0`, no spill. To keep it that way, the ragged bias must be set through its own construction path — assigning a runtime bias in `TopKPagedParams::problem()` would put a real `IADD` in every mode's `emit`. ## Tests `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py`: **278 passed** (234 existing + 44 new). The new cases cover every `row_start % 4` residue against each template band (trivial / Register2 / Register4 / Streaming), mixed lengths in one launch, the selection boundaries (`seq == k`, `k+1`, 8192/8193, 16385), long context, `row_starts=None`, and an offset distinct from `row_starts`. Everything outside a window is filled with a score that beats every in-window value, so a leak shows up as a wrong selection; each case also asserts that nothing outside the masked head was written. Also checked, unchanged from the base branch: `test_dsa_indexer.py` (same pass/fail set) and `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` (3 pre-existing `impl='trtllm'` hardware-gate failures, per `KNOWN_FAILURES.md §B`). And the v2 output matches the legacy kernel exactly when driven through `DSATopKBackend`, across aligned/unaligned starts and both the trivial and radix paths. ## Benchmark `bench_topk.py` gains a ragged benchmark alongside the paged one (this also un-shadows `benchmark_paged`, which a duplicate function name had replaced with a body-less stub). B200, k=2048, µs: | seq_len | batch | jit_v1 | **jit_v2** | flashinfer | torch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4096 | 1 | 4.10 | **4.03** | 6.37 | 34.27 | | 4096 | 128 | 7.35 | **4.34** | 7.07 | 45.34 | | 4096 | 1024 | 24.61 | **16.52** | 28.20 | 147.51 | | 65536 | 1 | 37.52 | 20.35 | **13.15** | 71.30 | | 65536 | 128 | 39.40 | **21.52** | 37.48 | 157.22 | | 65536 | 1024 | 175.84 | **103.70** | 195.88 | 923.18 | 1.3–1.8× over the legacy kernel, except the single-row 64K shape where the cluster split flashinfer/the paged path use still wins — not a prefill shape (prefill's row count is the extend-token count). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32041510984](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32041510984)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32201823455](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201823455)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Kimi-K3 MoE front optimization
signal.text: ## Motivation 1. The weight of routed expert down proj and routed expert up proj is now bf16. Enabling MXFP4 online quantization for routed expert down proj and routed expert up proj can reduce memory overhead in high-concurrency/large-batch scenarios. Now enable MXFP4 quant when M > 2048 (basically enabled at the prefill stage). 2. MoE front is now using a torch.mm fallback to calculate the MoE front GEMM (shared expert gate up + routed expert down proj + gate); dispatch this to the aiter tuned GEMM instead. This part depends on aiter PR https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4834. ## Modifications 1. quantize latent MoE projections to MXFP4 on large batches (b801b07046) - New sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/latent_mxfp4_aiter_hip.py: pack bf16 weights to MXFP4 (pack), run the quantized GEMM (run), and gate availability on gfx950 (supported). - KimiK3MoE._prepare_moe_latent_mxfp4(): builds MXFP4 copies of the latent down_proj/up_proj weights at weight-load time (bf16 originals stay live for small batches). Handles all three front-merge layouts (three-way fused, EP [gate | latent down] pair, unmerged). - New env var SGLANG_K3_MOE_LATENT_MXFP4 (opt-in) and _MOE_MXFP4_MIN_TOKENS = 2048 threshold; above that token count, _forward_unfused and _forward_fused route the down/up projections through the MXFP4 GEMM instead of the bf16 ReplicatedLinear. 2. use tuned kernel for moe front bf16 kernel (56ce1f2198) - _k3_bf16_gemm now dispatches to aiter.tuned_gemm.tgemm on HIP (when SGLANG_USE_AITER is set and no output buffer is requested), in addition to the existing cutedsl path. ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k 1319: 0.947, reduced ~0.008 due to mxfp4 quantization ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Constrained] Support MistralCommon tokenizers in the XGrammar backend
signal.text: Serving a Mistral model whose tokenizer resolves to `MistralCommonBackend` disables structured output entirely. XGrammar cannot build `TokenizerInfo` from it, so we log a warning, fall back to `grammar_backend="none"`, and every `json_schema` / `regex` / `ebnf` request is rejected with a 400. Neither alternate backend helps: outlines fails to compile any schema on this vocabulary, and llguidance refuses a non-fast tokenizer outright. The cause is that `MistralCommonBackend.get_vocab()` is keyed by decoded text, so byte-level pieces collide and most ids come back as 0 — 130044 usable entries for a 131072 vocabulary. The raw byte pieces are only reachable through the inner Tekkenizer, so `patch_mistral_common_tokenizer` now attaches the `init_xgrammar` hook that `xgrammar_backend.py` already looks for (the same escape hatch `tiktoken_tokenizer.py` uses) and builds the ordered vocabulary directly. mistral_common stays responsible for encoding and chat templating; only what the grammar backend sees changes. The second commit is related but separable: mistral_common validates conversation structure and rejects, for example, an assistant turn with empty content. That escaped as a 500 even though the Jinja path already mapped equivalent template errors to 400, so both paths now share one tuple of client-error types. Verified end to end on `Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B` (tp 4, `--tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral`): no fallback warning, `json_schema` returns 200 and is actually enforced (a prose-style prompt with a strict schema still yields conformant JSON), the empty-assistant request returns 400 instead of 500, and plain chat is unchanged. One caveat for reviewers: the hook reads `_vocab_size`, `_all_special_tokens` and `id_to_byte_piece` from mistral_common's Tekkenizer, two of which are private. If a future release changes them, `init_xgrammar` returns `(None, None)` and today's graceful fallback resumes rather than crashing. That path is covered by a unit test. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32144736824](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144736824)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32144736445](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144736445)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kernel] Use Cake source Router GEMM for DeepSeek, GLM, and Mistral
signal.text: ## Motivation Use FlashInfer's source-built Cake Router GEMM for the small-token router projections used by DeepSeek V2/V3, GLM-4 MoE/Lite, and Mistral Large 3 on SM100/SM103. This fills the M=1..16 shape boundary while preserving the existing SGLang fallbacks. Dependencies and trackers: [FlashInfer #4594](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4594), [Cake !581](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/cake/cake-dev/-/merge_requests/581), [Cake issue #11](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/cake/cake-dev/-/issues/11), and [FlashInfer issue #4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254). ## Modifications - Add a lazy Router GEMM adapter that only activates when the Cake source backend from FlashInfer #4594 is present on SM100/SM103. - Preserve SGLang's caller-owned row-major output ABI and pass the model's row-major `[N, K]` parameter as the column-major `[K, N]` transpose view expected by FlashInfer. - Route the supported model gates through the adapter before their existing fallbacks, excluding DeepSeek V4. - Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_FLASHINFER_ROUTER_GEMM=0` as a kill switch. | Model path | Shape | Input / weight | Output | M range | |---|---|---|---|---:| | DeepSeek V2/V3 | K=7168, N=256 | BF16 / BF16 | FP32 | 1..16 | | GLM-4 MoE/Lite | K=6144, N=256 | BF16 / BF16 | FP32 | 1..16 | | Mistral Large 3 | K=7168, N=128 | BF16 / BF16 | BF16 | 1..16 | Missing source APIs, unsupported shapes/dtypes/layouts/devices, and a disabled kill switch return to the existing model-specific path. ## Accuracy Tests - `pytest -q test/srt/test_flashinfer_router_gemm.py`: 12 passed. - GB300/SM103 public-API matrix: 96/96 passed (3 APIs x M=1..16 x PDL on/off); maximum absolute difference `1.90735e-6`. - Real DeepSeek-V3-0324 FP8 checkpoint (163 shards), TP4/EP4 on 4x GB300: M=1..16 source prewarm passed against FP32 reference at `atol=rtol=1e-2`; maximum absolute difference `1.22070e-4`. - Eight fixed 64-token prompts produced the same first greedy token for baseline and candidate (8/8). At 32 generated tokens, 4/8 sequences remained exactly equal; later divergence is retained in the evidence because autoregressive decoding amplifies contract-valid Router GEMM rounding differences. ## Speed Tests and Profiling DeepSeek-V3-0324 FP8, TP4/EP4, 4x NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), 16 concurrent requests, 64 input IDs and 64 output tokens per request, five measured rounds after warmup: | Metric | Baseline | Cake Router GEMM | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Median output throughput | 77.445 tok/s | 81.474 tok/s | 1.0520x | | Profiler GPU active-union | 16,302.874 ms | 14,635.903 ms | 1.1139x | | Attributed Router path | 113.482 ms | 99.124 ms | 1.1449x | The candidate trace contains 14,848 `kernel_cake_blackwell_router_gemm_m16_k7168` launches. The baseline has 14,848 old Router main launches plus 14,848 attributable split-K reduction launches; the Cake path removes that reduction. Run: Slurm `3138717`, SGLang `20127f12c92c0eb7cf4182bd1b1f02158f84dba5`, FlashInfer source `2cbaf76fbcb90ce7befc0ef6dc5e4cfd70e43102`. ## Checklist - [x] Format the changed files with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Document the environment switch and fallback behavior inline. - [x] Provide accuracy, speed, and profiler results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32201569541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201569541)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32201569312](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32201569312)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
signal.text: ## Summary Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`** - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once. - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native). - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`, falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`. - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact) and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch (only 2 model files differ). Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q 8 passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.947 | | 2 | 0.943 | 0.943 | | 3 | 0.937 | 0.944 | | **avg** | **0.941** | **0.945** | Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | patched (tok/s) | Δ | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | |------------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:-----:|:---:|:---:| | 4 | 216.38 | 219.66 | **+1.5%** | 17.507 | 17.242 | | 8 | 367.65 | 372.98 | **+1.4%** | 20.715 | 20.423 | | 16 | 568.64 | 579.04 | **+1.8%** | 26.460 | 25.960 | | 32 | 792.79 | 800.70 | **+1.0%** | 38.165 | 37.808 | | 64 | 1033.97 | 1042.04 | **+0.8%** | 58.854 | 58.412 | ### Commands used ```bash # Accuracy python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 # Performance (per concurrency C in 4 8 16 32 64) python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] New unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py` passes (8 passed; gfx95 numerical). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.945 vs 0.941, invalid 0.000). - [x] Output throughput improves +0.8%–1.8% at concurrency 4–64 (TP4, 8k/1k), TPOT reduced. - [x] Falls back to unfused hc_post + hc_pre when no fused kernel fires (non-gfx95 / import failure). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32085370546](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085370546)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32085370376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32085370376)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kernel] Add H200 FP8 MoE configs for recent Qwen models
signal.text: ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for recent Qwen FP8 models: - Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP1, with separate up/gate and down-projection tables - Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, dynamic FP8, TP1 - Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8: `E=512,N=256`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP8 per rank in the verified H200 TP8 x PP4 recipe The tuned up/gate configs reduce kernel latency by 3.5% to 19.6% across the original measured token counts. The Qwen3.5 down-projection table adds a 4.9% to 17.9% incremental reduction over reusing the up config and includes decode sizes 1-128 required for stable serving. Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 BF16 share `E=256,N=512`; an H200 BF16 table already exists in `triton_3_7_1`, and Triton 3.6 falls back to it, so no duplicate non-quant config is added. Qwen3.8 BF16 has no H200 deployment recipe because the approximately 4.8 TB checkpoint does not fit the supported H200 topology. No official Qwen3.7 release was found. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `7f51e6bba096348a7eb27f31ef0e3f5946786d2c` - Up/gate token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Qwen3.5 down token counts: 1, 4, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape - Real-model validation: SGLang v0.5.17, ten 200-question GSM8K runs per side ## Results | Model | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 256 | 255.43 | 220.90 | 1.156x | 13.52% | | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 512 | 265.41 | 242.75 | 1.093x | 8.54% | | Qwen3.5 FP8 | 1024 | 284.93 | 274.94 | 1.036x | 3.50% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 256 | 245.56 | 218.58 | 1.123x | 10.98% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 512 | 282.61 | 231.81 | 1.219x | 17.98% | | Qwen3.6 FP8 | 1024 | 303.11 | 260.82 | 1.162x | 13.95% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 256 | 1058.83 | 851.62 | 1.243x | 19.57% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 512 | 1077.81 | 876.50 | 1.230x | 18.68% | | Qwen3.8 FP8 | 1024 | 1138.28 | 999.70 | 1.139x | 12.17% | Each tuned config was also run on both H200s. Both GPUs selected the same configs and produced closely matching latency. ### Qwen3.5 down-projection kernel The dedicated down table was tuned with expert routes captured from the real Qwen3.5 checkpoint on a standard GSM8K prompt. The incremental column compares the dedicated down config with the runtime's previous behavior of reusing the up/gate config. | Tokens | Generic default (us) | Up-config fallback (us) | Tuned down (us) | Reduction vs generic | Incremental reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 8.41 | 7.75 | 7.34 | 12.73% | 5.24% | | 4 | 15.65 | 11.83 | 11.26 | 28.08% | 4.88% | | 16 | 30.08 | 21.48 | 20.30 | 32.52% | 5.48% | | 32 | 41.05 | 28.33 | 26.83 | 34.64% | 5.27% | | 64 | 49.27 | 35.54 | 33.43 | 32.14% | 5.93% | | 128 | 66.23 | 49.63 | 46.91 | 29.16% | 5.47% | | 256 | 78.51 | 62.99 | 57.25 | 27.07% | 9.11% | | 512 | 96.06 | 85.86 | 74.59 | 22.35% | 13.13% | | 1024 | 113.29 | 107.87 | 88.59 | 21.80% | 17.87% | ### Real-model SGLang v0.5.17 GSM8K Checkpoint: `/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49` Both sides used SGLang v0.5.17 commit `29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`, seed 0, one H200, the same server settings, a 20-question warmup, and ten repetitions of SGLang's standard `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py` with 200 questions. | Metric | Baseline | Tuned up + down | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Median latency | 11.8005 s | 11.5760 s | -1.90% | | Mean latency | 11.8812 s | 11.6347 s | -2.07% | | Median output throughput | 3045.77 tok/s | 3183.42 tok/s | +4.52% | | Mean output throughput | 3032.40 tok/s | 3184.10 tok/s | +5.00% | | Mean GSM8K accuracy | 0.8295 | 0.8150 | -1.45 pp | | Invalid outputs | 0 | 0 | unchanged | The accuracy ranges overlapped across runs (baseline 0.810-0.845, tuned 0.805-0.830), but the lower tuned mean is reported rather than hidden. This is a performance result, not an accuracy-improvement claim. The first down-only table covered only 256/512/1024 and completed three runs, but eventually exposed a serving stall when a decode batch reused the 256-token TMA config. That table was rejected. Adding independently tuned 1/4/16/32/64/128 decode entries removed the stall and completed all ten final runs. Up-projection TMA was also audited and rejected because the exact v0.5.17 runtime does not support `USE_TMA` in the up config; compatible no-TMA alternatives were within noise of the existing up table. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODELS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-model-configs RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full searches: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen35-fp8-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen35-fp8-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen35-fp8" \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen35-fp8-tp1/tune.log" & CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen36-fp8-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen36-fp8-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen36-fp8" \ --tp-size 1 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen36-fp8-tp1/tune.log" & wait CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen38-fp8-tp8/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-qwen38-fp8-tp8/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODELS/qwen38-fp8" \ --tp-size 8 \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/qwen38-fp8-tp8/tune.log" ``` Baseline and tuned validation was run three times for each model. The command below was used first with the generated config absent, then repeated after copying that model's generated JSON into `triton_3_6_0`: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$GPU" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL_CONFIG" \ --tp-size "$TP_SIZE" \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$OUTPUT_DIR/$PHASE-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` The concrete validation invocations were: ```bash /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen35-fp8" 1 fp8_w8a8 qwen35-fp8-tp1 \ 'E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json' /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen36-fp8" 1 fp8_w8a8 qwen36-fp8-tp1 \ 'E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json' /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_qwen_h200_tuning.sh \ 1 "$MODELS/qwen38-fp8" 8 fp8_w8a8 qwen38-fp8-tp8 \ 'E=512,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json' ``` Concurrent dual-H200 validation for each model: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL_CONFIG" \ --tp-size "$TP_SIZE" \ --dtype fp8_w8a8 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$DUAL_GPU_OUTPUT/gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Real-route capture and Qwen3.5 down-projection search: ```bash RUN=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-tuned VENV="$RUN/venv-tuned" MODEL=/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49 DATA="$RUN/data/gsm8k_test.jsonl" ROUTES="$RUN/qwen35-real-topk" UP_CONFIG="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0/E=256,N=512,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128, 128].json" # The route-capture server must be launched with # --enable-return-routed-experts. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation/capture_qwen35_routes.py \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \ --dataset "$DATA" \ --model-config "$MODEL/config.json" \ --output-dir "$ROUTES" \ --min-tokens 1024 run_down_tuning() { local gpu=$1 output=$2 shift 2 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" \ PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" \ "$VENV/bin/python" "$RUN/tune_qwen35_down_real_routes.py" \ --kernel down \ --tuner "$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton/tuning_fused_moe_triton_sep.py" \ --model "$MODEL" \ --topk-ids-dir "$ROUTES" \ --up-config "$UP_CONFIG" \ --output-dir "$RUN/qwen35-down-tuning/$output" \ --batch-sizes "$@" \ --tune-iters 30 \ --validation-iters 100 \ --validation-repeats 3 } run_down_tuning 0 small-a 1 16 64 & run_down_tuning 1 small-b 4 32 128 & wait run_down_tuning 0 m256 256 & run_down_tuning 1 m512 512 & wait run_down_tuning 0 m1024 1024 ``` Matched SGLang v0.5.17 server and standard GSM8K commands: ```bash RUN=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation MODEL=/shared/public/elr-models/Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8/0b2752837483aa34b3db6e83e151b150c0e00e49 DATA="$RUN/data/gsm8k_test.jsonl" # Run once with the baseline worktree/venv and once with the tuned worktree/venv. ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-tuned VENV="$RUN/venv-tuned" # Use PHASE=baseline-10 when ROOT/VENV point to the baseline tree/venv. PHASE=tuned-decode-aware CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python" "$VENV/bin/python" \ -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path "$MODEL" \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 30000 \ --trust-remote-code \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --random-seed 0 COMMON=( --num-shots 5 --data-path "$DATA" --max-new-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --top-p 1 --parallel 64 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 --backend srt ) PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python" "$VENV/bin/python" \ "$ROOT/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \ "${COMMON[@]}" --num-questions 20 for repeat in $(seq 1 10); do PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python" "$VENV/bin/python" \ "$ROOT/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \ "${COMMON[@]}" \ --num-questions 200 \ --result-file "$RUN/qwen35-gsm8k-standard/$PHASE/result-$repeat.jsonl" \ --raw-result-file "$RUN/qwen35-gsm8k-standard/$PHASE/raw-$repeat.jsonl" done ``` The local GSM8K file contains all 1,319 canonical test examples: `/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-v0.5.17-real-validation/data/gsm8k_test.jsonl`, SHA-256 `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-qwen-h200-tuning-results/qwen-h200-configs.patch ```

signal.title: fix: guard self.model access in Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights
signal.text: Fixes #23063 ## Problem When launching a Qwen3-VL-MoE model in `--encoder-only` mode, the server crashes during weight loading with `AttributeError: 'Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration' object has no attribute 'model'`. In encoder-only mode, `self.model` is not initialized by the parent class (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.__init__` only sets `self.model` when `config.encoder_only` is `False`). However, `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` unconditionally accessed `self.model` in: ```python and hasattr(self.model, "start_layer") ``` Python evaluates `self.model` before `hasattr` can handle the missing attribute, causing the crash. ## Solution Add `hasattr(self, "model")` check before accessing `self.model`, matching the pattern already used in the parent class `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` in `qwen3_vl.py` (line 1322): ```python and hasattr(self, "model") and hasattr(self.model, "start_layer") ``` ## Testing The fix is minimal (1 line added) and directly mirrors the existing guard pattern in the parent class. Encoder-only mode now safely skips the `start_layer`/`end_layer` layer-skipping logic when no language model is initialized, while normal (non-encoder-only) mode is unaffected.

signal.title: [Quantization] Extract shared checkpoint quant metadata resolver
signal.text: ## Summary - add a lightweight, pure-data `CheckpointQuantSpec` for serialized checkpoint metadata - resolve `quantization_config`, `text_config.quantization_config`, and `compression_config` through one shared helper - make SRT's existing quant loader consume the helper without changing backend selection, overrides, or file fallback - deep-copy checkpoint metadata so loader-only fields do not mutate the Hugging Face config ## Scope This is intentionally a small foundation PR (`+329/-12`, 341 lines of churn). It does not add a quantization format or change component loading. The resolver lives in `sglang.checkpoint_quantization`, and importing it does not load `sglang.srt.model_loader` or runtime quantized-layer implementations. `CheckpointQuantSpec.declared_method` is the checkpoint's raw `quant_method`; backend-specific method inference remains in each consumer. Follow-up PRs will migrate those consumers incrementally. ## Validation - 9 focused resolver tests, including ModelOpt metadata without `quant_method` - production regressions for both incomplete `modelopt_mixed` fallback cases and complete inline metadata - verified packed-module mapping and KV metadata preservation - `isort`, `ruff`, `black`, `py_compile`, and changed-file commit hooks <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32132809467](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132809467)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32132809226](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132809226)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Unified Tree] Support Branching-Point Caching for the SWA Component
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation With out-of-window SWA slot freeing now enabled by default in [#34653](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34653), chunked prefill releases SWA states outside the last sliding window. This significantly reduces swa memory usage, but later requests branching from an earlier shared prefix may still have reusable Full KV while the corresponding swa state is no longer available, forcing unnecessary prefix recomputation. ## Modifications Reuse most of the existing mamba branching for SWA: and preserve the SWA cache at that boundary when releasing out-of-window slots, and has no effect when the `SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS` is disabled. ``` ■■ SWA slots retained □ SWA slots released P SWA branching point 1. signal.title: fix: add explicit barrier for DP-attention in scheduler to prevent race conditions
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #23022. When serving a multimodal model (e.g. Qwen2-VL, Qwen3.5-VL) with **PD disaggregation** and **`dp_size > 1` + `--enable-dp-attention`**, the scheduler crashes with `FileNotFoundError` on POSIX shared memory segments for DP1+ ranks. **Root Cause:** Under DP-attention, `work_reqs` are broadcast on `attn_tp_cpu_group` (not `tp_cpu_group`). The broadcast source rank returns the original objects immediately, while receiver ranks are still in `pickle.loads → __setstate__ → shm_open`. Without a barrier scoped to `attn_tp_cpu_group`, the source rank can call `materialize() / shm_unlink()` before receiver ranks have opened the shared memory segment. The subsequent `control_reqs` broadcast on `tp_cpu_group` is on a **different** process group and does **not** guarantee that `attn_tp` receiver ranks have completed `shm_open`. The previous guard only added a barrier for the non-DP-attention path, leaving the DP-attention path unprotected. ``` scheduler DP0 source rank │ broadcast work_reqs on attn_tp_cpu_group │ returns immediately with original objects │ unwrap_shm_features → materialize() → shm.unlink() ❌ UNLINKS SHM │ scheduler DP0/DP1 receiver ranks (still deserializing) │ pickle.loads → __setstate__ → shm_open(psm_xxx) 💥 FileNotFoundError ``` ## Modifications Added an explicit barrier on `attn_tp_cpu_group` in `recv_requests()` for the DP-attention path, symmetric with the existing barrier on `tp_cpu_group` for the non-DP-attention path. The barrier is guarded by: - `enable_dp_attention` is set - The request contains shared memory features (`has_shm_features`) - The model is multimodal (only multimodal requests use `ShmPointerMMData`) - `attn_tp_size > 1` (no cross-rank race when there is only one rank) This ensures all ranks in `attn_tp_cpu_group` have completed `shm_open` before any rank proceeds to `materialize() / shm_unlink()`. **File changed:** `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py` ## Checklist - signal.title: fix(disagg): support per-GPU JSON mapping in --disaggregation-ib-device
signal.text: ## Summary - `_validate_ib_devices()` now passes through JSON per-GPU mappings and `.json` file paths to the downstream `get_ib_devices_for_gpu()` parser, which already supports these formats. - Enables rail alignment on multi-rail HPC fabrics where GPU indices don't match NIC indices (standard on HGX H100/H200 platforms). - Without this, users must pass a flat comma-separated list which gives every GPU access to all devices, causing mooncake's internal QP selection to pick NICs non-deterministically across peers, leading to cross-rail RDMA failures in PD disaggregation. ## Details On rail-optimized clusters (e.g., 8-GPU + 8-NIC nodes), PCIe slot ordering (NICs) typically differs from NVLink group ordering (GPUs). For example, `nvidia-smi topo -m` on HGX-style nodes shows GPU 0 pairs with NIC 4 at PIX level, not NIC 0. The correct mapping for mooncake's RDMA transport is: ``` {"0":"mlx5_4","1":"mlx5_5","2":"mlx5_6","3":"mlx5_7","4":"mlx5_0","5":"mlx5_1","6":"mlx5_2","7":"mlx5_3"} ``` `get_ib_devices_for_gpu()` in `mooncake_transfer_engine.py` already parses this JSON format and resolves per-GPU device names. But `_validate_ib_devices()` in `server_args.py` runs first and rejects anything that isn't a literal IB device name after splitting on commas. The fix adds a 2-line early return that detects JSON content (`{...}`) or `.json` file paths and passes them through unchanged.

signal.title: [diffusion] Per-request lossy accelerations: Cache-DiT, CFG gating, attention backend override
signal.text: ## Motivation Lossy accelerations should be **per-request** switches, not process-wide env vars / server args: one deployment should be able to mix accelerated and lossless requests. SGLang-Diffusion already follows this for TeaCache (`enable_teacache`), Spectrum, progressive resolution, and `quality="high"` — but Cache-DiT was ~20 process-wide `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_*` env vars, CFG gating was a process-wide `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CFG_GATE_STEP` float, and approximate attention (SageAttention) was only selectable server-wide. Design rule going forward: anything whose state is request-scoped, or process-level but safely switchable at a batch boundary, belongs in `SamplingParams` (participating in the dynamic-batch signature). Env vars remain as server-wide defaults for unset requests, and are planned to be deprecated/removed later. ## Modifications **1. Cache-DiT (`enable_cache_dit` / `cache_dit_params`)** - `SamplingParams.enable_cache_dit: bool | None` — `None` follows the `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED` server default; `True`/`False` opt this request in/out (explicit `False` is a kill switch, winning even over MiniMax-H3 `quality="high"`). CLI `--enable-cache-dit true|false`; OpenAI image/video APIs accept both fields via `extra_body`. - `SamplingParams.cache_dit_params: dict | None` — per-request DBCache/SCM knob overrides on top of the env defaults, with a nested `secondary` dict for dual-DiT models (unset secondary keys inherit the request primary, then `SECONDARY_*` env). Unknown keys fail the request (`resolve_cache_dit_request_overrides`). - `DenoisingStage` generalizes MiniMax-H3's quality-transition logic: at each batch boundary it unmounts/remounts hooks when a request opts out or changes knobs, and keeps the cheap `refresh_context` path when settings are unchanged. - MiniMax-H3 generic mode honors the request switch; LTX-2's TI2V suppression now reports "not requested" so hooks mounted by a prior text-only request actually unmount (previously they silently stayed active during image-conditioned requests — the stale-activation hazard its comment warns about). Progressive-resolution SCM preset honors the per-request override. **2. CFG gating (`cfg_gate_step`)** - `SamplingParams.cfg_gate_step: float | None` — fraction of steps after which the cached cond−uncond residual is reused instead of running the unconditional branch. `None` follows the `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CFG_GATE_STEP` server default; `1.0` disables for this request. Its state was already rebuilt per denoising loop, so no transition logic is needed. CLI `--cfg-gate-step`; APIs via `extra_body`. **3. Attention backend override (`attention_backend_override`)** - One server can serve exact and approximate attention side by side: requests switch the DiT denoise attention backend among the exact/drop-in dense kernels (`fa`, `torch_sdpa`, `sage_attn`, `sage_attn_3`). CLI `--attention-backend-override`; APIs via `extra_body`. - The attention layers (`UlyssesAttention` / `LocalAttention` / `USPAttention`) keep their impl ctor kwargs and a per-backend impl cache; switching is two-phase (prepare every layer's impl first — may raise, mutates nothing — then flip all), so a rejected request leaves the transformers untouched. Non-default impls are built lazily: dual residency costs a few plain Python objects per layer, no GPU memory (sage/fa step metadata is empty/None). - **Fail-fast**: incompatible server settings reject the request with a server log instead of silently falling back — breakable CUDA graphs and `torch.compile` bake the kernel into a captured/traced graph; sparse server backends can't be mixed with per-request dense switching; ring parallelism requires a ring-capable target; unknown/unsupported/unavailable targets are refused (including silent selector fallbacks). All three fields participate in the dynamic-batch signature, so requests with different settings never share a batch and every transition happens at a batch boundary. No new env vars or server args are added. ## Test - New `test/unit/test_cache_dit_per_request.py`: request-param validation, overrides-key change detection, mount→refresh→unmount→remount transitions, explicit-disable-wins-over-env, secondary inheritance, warmup gating. - New `test/unit/test_attention_backend_override.py`: switch/restore/fast-path orchestration, all fail-fast rejections (BCG, compile, sparse, ring, unknown/non-switchable names, no layers), two-phase atomicity, layer prepare/apply including silent-fallback refusal. - Extended `test_cfg_gating.py`: request fraction overrides env default, request `1.0` disables an env-enabled gate, invalid request fraction rejected. - Updated fakes in `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py` / `test_minimax_h3_admission.py` for the new SamplingParams fields. - Docs: `cache_dit.mdx` rewritten around per-request usage; `attention_backends.mdx` gains a per-request override section; perf-tuning skill table updated. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32160110319](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32160110319)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32160109959](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32160109959)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Quantized lm_head silently produces uninitialized logits with compressed-tensors (ParallelLMHead not dispatched)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. - [x] Please use English. ### Describe the bug A compressed-tensors checkpoint with a quantized `lm_head` loads without error and then emits **uninitialized logits** — every request returns repeated token 0 (`!!!!!!...`). `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` dispatches on two layer types and returns `None` for everything else: ```python if isinstance(layer, LinearBase): ... if isinstance(layer, FusedMoE): ... return None ``` `ParallelLMHead` subclasses `VocabParallelEmbedding`, not `LinearBase`, so it gets `None` and falls back to `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`. That creates a plain `weight` parameter, while the checkpoint supplies `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` — which nothing reads. The parameter is never filled, so the head multiplies by uninitialized memory. It is silent: the server starts, reports no error, and serves garbage. **vLLM handles this case** (SGLang's file is marked `# Adapted from vLLM`). In `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/compressed_tensors.py`: ```python if isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead): quant_scheme = self.get_scheme(layer=layer, layer_name=prefix) ... return CompressedTensorsLinearMethod(self) # ParallelLMHead subclasses VocabParallelEmbedding but is handled above as # a linear; only true embedding lookups land here. if isinstance(layer, VocabParallelEmbedding): ... ``` The adaptation appears to have dropped that branch. Note `ParallelLMHead` already calls `quant_method.create_weights` with the `LinearMethodBase` signature (`input_size_per_partition=embedding_dim`, `output_partition_sizes=[num_embeddings_per_partition]`), so the linear method works unmodified. This is **not hardware-specific** — the dispatch has no device branching. It reproduces anywhere a compressed-tensors checkpoint quantizes `lm_head`. Secondary point: with the dispatch added, scheme matching also needs `lm_head` in `config_groups.*.targets`, otherwise it raises `ValueError: Unable to find matching target for lm_head in the compressed-tensors config.` That is checkpoint-side and matches what llm-compressor emits. ### Reproduction Any compressed-tensors checkpoint whose `lm_head` is quantized (i.e. not in `ignore`, and listed in `config_groups.*.targets`): ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <compressed-tensors ckpt with quantized lm_head> curl localhost:30000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"...","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17*23?"}],"max_tokens":30}' # -> "!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" ``` Leaving `lm_head` in the `ignore` list produces correct output, which isolates it to the head. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.13 GPU 0: Radeon 8060S Graphics (gfx1151) # incidental — the bug is device-independent PyTorch: 2.13.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260422 sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g3f048c80b.d20260513 sglang-kernel: 0.4.2.post1 triton: 3.7.0 transformers: 5.6.0 ```

signal.title: fix(openai): avoid IndexError when continue_final_message empties messages
signal.text: ## Problem In `_apply_jinja_template`, the DeepSeek encoding branch (`chat_encoding_spec` in `dsv4`/`dsv32`) runs: ```python messages, assistant_prefix = self._handle_last_assistant_message(messages, request) if messages[0]["role"] != "system": messages.insert(0, {"role": "system", "content": ""}) if request.tools: messages[0]["tools"] = [...] ``` When `continue_final_message=True` and the request contains only a single trailing assistant message, `_handle_last_assistant_message` does `messages = messages[:-1]`, leaving an empty list. `messages[0]` then raises `IndexError: list index out of range`. `_validate_request` only rejects an originally-empty `messages`, so this empties *after* validation and isn't caught. ## Fix Guard the system-prompt insertion against an empty list: ```python if not messages or messages[0]["role"] != "system": messages.insert(0, {"role": "system", "content": ""}) ``` An empty list now gets the empty system prompt inserted, so the subsequent `request.tools` indexing is safe too. ## Test Added `test_dsv_encoders_handle_continue_final_message_only_assistant` to `test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py` (CPU unit test), covering both `dsv4` and `dsv32`: a lone assistant message with `continue_final_message=True` is processed without raising. I could not run the suite locally (this dev box is Windows and `sglang.srt.utils.common` imports the Unix-only `resource` module, so the package fails to import). I verified `python -m py_compile` on both files and reproduced the fix logic in isolation (the stripped list is empty → the old guard raises `IndexError`, the new guard inserts the system message). Relying on CI for the full unit test run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #27764086139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27764086139)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #27764085944](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27764085944)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: add padding handling in multi-layer EAGLE draft extend CUDA graph runner
signal.text: ## Motivation The multi-layer EAGLE draft extend CUDA graph runner (`multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`) lacks padding handling in `init_replay_state()` when the CUDA graph capture batch size (`bs`) exceeds the actual batch size (`raw_bs`). The single-layer version (`eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py`) already has this padding logic, but it was not ported to the multi-layer version. When `bs > raw_bs`, the padding region `[raw_bs:bs]` in buffers like `req_pool_indices` retains stale values from previous calls, causing: 1. **IndexKernel.cu:111 assertion failure**: Stale `req_pool_indices` values cause out-of-bounds indexing in `req_to_token` lookup during `init_forward_metadata_replay_cuda_graph()`. 2. **Missing `extend_seq_lens_cpu` padding**: The `[raw_bs:bs]` region of `extend_seq_lens_cpu` is not filled, potentially causing incorrect attention metadata computation. ## Modifications Added padding handling in `init_replay_state()` of `multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` that mirrors the existing single-layer version: - Fill `seq_lens` with `seq_len_fill_value` - Zero `out_cache_loc`, `positions`, and `req_pool_indices` - Fill `accept_length` and `extend_seq_lens` with `num_tokens_per_bs` - Pad `extend_seq_lens_cpu` for the `[raw_bs:bs]` region ## Accuracy Tests N/A - this fix only affects padding regions in CUDA graph buffers that are discarded after replay. The actual inference results (within `[:raw_bs]`) are unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with MiMo-V2-Flash + `--enable-multi-layer-eagle` (MTP=3) + PD disaggregation on 2x AWS P5EN (H200 x8 per node): | Test | Configuration | Result | |------|--------------|--------| | Stability | 500 prompts x 10 rates (1-8), 16K/1K | **4000/4000 successful**, 0 crashes | | Peak throughput | rate=8, 16K input/1K output | **4,004 tok/s** output | | Throughput scaling | rate 1→8 | 987→4,004 tok/s (linear scaling) | Without this fix, the server crashes within minutes of MTP decoding under load. ## Checklist - [x] Format code - [ ] Add unit tests (this is a padding/safety fix, testing requires multi-GPU MTP+PD setup) - [ ] Update documentation - [x] Benchmark results provided above - [x] Follow SGLang code style

signal.title: Add NVFP4 per-expert weight loading for Gemma 4 MoE models
signal.text: ## Summary Adds NVFP4 per-expert weight loading for Gemma 4 MoE models in both `gemma4_mm.py` and `gemma4_causal.py`. ### Problem NVFP4 checkpoints (e.g. `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`) store MoE expert weights in unfused per-expert format: ``` moe.experts.{id}.{gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj}.{weight,weight_scale,weight_scale_2,input_scale} ``` SGLang's existing `expert_params_mapping` only handles the fused format (`experts.gate_up_proj`, `experts.down_proj`). Without the per-expert mapping, NVFP4 expert weights silently fail to load, resulting in uninitialized weights and garbage output. ### Fix Add `nvfp4_expert_params_mapping` that maps per-expert checkpoint tensors to SGLang's fused `w13_`/`w2_` parameter format. The mapping runs before the existing fused expert mapping so it doesn't interfere with standard checkpoints. Applied to both model files: - `gemma4_mm.py` (multimodal variant) - `gemma4_causal.py` (text-only variant) ### Files Changed - `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_mm.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/gemma4_causal.py` ## Test Plan - [x] Tested with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4` on RTX 5090 - [x] All expert weights load correctly (no "weights not initialized" warnings for MoE params) - [x] Model produces coherent output - [x] Standard (non-NVFP4) checkpoints still load correctly via existing fused mapping

signal.title: fix(jit_kernel): add missing <cassert> include   in awq_dequantize.cuh
signal.text: ## Summary `awq_dequantize.cuh` uses `assert(false)` as a fallback for unsupported CUDA architectures (lines 73 and 102), but the `<cassert>` header is not included. This causes JIT compilation failures when loading AWQ quantized models in certain environments (e.g., specific GCC/CUDA toolchain versions where `assert` is not transitively included). ## Motivation When loading AWQ quantized models (e.g., `Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-AWQ`) with SGLang, the JIT compilation of `awq_dequantize.cuh` fails with an `identifier "assert" is undefined` error. This issue was identified during a deployment on NVIDIA A800-SXM4-80GB. Adding the explicit include ensures the kernel compiles correctly across all standard-compliant toolchains. ## Modifications - Added `#include <cassert>` to `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/gemm/awq_dequantize.cuh`. - This is a header-only fix with no behavioral or logic changes. ## Accuracy Tests N/A. This fix only resolves a compilation error and does not affect numerical outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A.
