signal.title: [Perf] PaddleOCR-VL: overlap page preprocessing, pack the ViT, enable prefill CUDA graph
signal.text: ## Motivation PaddleOCR-VL served a 1080p page in **235 ms** and saturated at **6.7 req/s** on an H200 while the GPU sat idle. Profiling put almost none of that in the model's own compute: | what | why it was slow | |---|---| | Image processor ran **single-threaded** | `QwenVLImageProcessor` grants concurrent workers only to an explicit `model_type` allowlist that `paddleocr_vl` is not on. An 87 ms/page preprocess caps throughput at ~11 req/s no matter how much GPU is left. | | **Prefill CUDA graph was off** | Breakable CG is the CUDA default, but the generic "multimodal model" rule disables it for every multimodal arch. PaddleOCR-VL's config always carries a `vision_config`, so even *text-only* prefill lost the graph. | | ViT recomputed and re-synchronized **per image** | A device-side `max()` for the rope table, one host sync per image to slice the encoder output, a bilinear position-embedding interpolation per image per forward (the LFU cache written for it was never called), and a full projector pass per image. | | `quant_config` accepted and **dropped** | `--quantization` was a silent no-op for both the LM and the vision tower. | ## Modifications - `multimodal/processors/paddleocr_vlm.py` — opt into concurrent preprocessing (4 workers, 16 IO threads). A document page is a far heavier preprocessing unit than a chat image. - `configs/model_config.py` — allowlist the arch for breakable prefill CUDA graph, the way the Kimi archs are. Embed-carrying batches are still rejected at replay and run eager, so this is a text/mixed-traffic win. - `models/paddleocr_vl.py` — run the vision tower packed: grids stay on the host, the encoder output stays concatenated, the 2x2 merge writes into one buffer, and the two projections run once for the batch instead of once per image. Wire up the position-embedding LFU cache that was already written but never called. Pass `quant_config` through. Take `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold+matmul path for the patch embedding (kernel == stride, zero padding). - `models/ernie4.py` — give `Ernie4Model` a `get_input_embeddings`, replacing a `hasattr` + `types.MethodType` patch at the PaddleOCR-VL call site. - Cookbook page for PaddleOCR-VL / 1.5 / 1.6 (identical `config.json`, so one recipe serves all three), plus the `supported-models` row. ## Accuracy Every arm was gated on output equality before it was measured: five page geometries x two task prompts under greedy decoding, compared against the pre-change baseline. - packed ViT: **10/10 byte-identical** (text and token counts) - \+ four concurrent preprocessing workers: **10/10** - \+ transformers-native image processor: **10/10** - \+ the final scheduling recipe: **10/10** CPU unit tests pin the packed vision math to a per-image reference implementation at fp64 (packed 2x2 merge, batch invariance, the position-embedding cache vs uncached interpolation, LFU eviction, conv-vs-matmul, packed 2D position ids), and a second file pins the two allowlist memberships, which are exactly the kind of setting a refactor drops silently. ## Benchmark One H200, PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, 1080p JPEG pages (~2700 image tokens), 128 output tokens, prefix + multimodal caches disabled, **median** TTFT, arms interleaved within a single run, 2-3 reps. | workload | before | after | |---|---|---| | 1080p page, 1 stream (TTFT) | 235.1 ms | **119.6 ms** (1.97x) | | 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 6.67 req/s | **12.26 req/s** (1.84x) | | 2704-token text, 1 stream (TTFT) | 16.1 ms | **11.5 ms** (1.40x, from the prefill graph) | Against vLLM 0.27.1 on the same box, same caches-off settings: | workload | sglang | vLLM | |---|---|---| | 2704-tok text, 1 stream TTFT | **11.5 ms** | 15.9 ms | | 2704-tok text, 32 concurrent | **95.4 req/s** | 81.8 req/s | | 1080p page, 1 stream TTFT | **119.6 ms** | 137.5 ms | | 1080p page, 32 concurrent | 12.26 req/s | **12.77 req/s** | The one remaining loss is saturated page throughput, ~4% behind. It is GPU-bound in the vision tower (full attention over ~10.7k patches, `head_dim=72`); `fa4`, `triton_attn`, `cuda_ipc` feature transport, more processor workers, PD-multiplexing and every chunked-prefill size were all measured and none of them helped. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code and run lint locally - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/models/test_paddleocr_vl_vision.py`, `..._serving_defaults.py`) and an e2e server test (`test/registered/vlm/test_paddleocr_vl_server.py`) - [x] Benchmark on real hardware with accuracy verified against the pre-change baseline - [x] Update documentation (cookbook page + supported-models row) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32176324134](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32176324134)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32176324019](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32176324019)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] GLM-5.2-FP8 (DeepSeek-V3.2 / DSA block-fp8) produces wrong output on gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X): aiter gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle is numerically incorrect
signal.text: ## Summary On **gfx950** (MI350X / MI355X), block-fp8 DeepSeek-V3.2-architecture models (validated with **GLM-5.2-FP8**, `glm_moe_dsa`) produce **numerically wrong output**: in-context reasoning is broken (GSM8K accuracy **0.000**, 72% unparseable) even though the server runs without error and simple factual prompts often look fine. Root cause: sglang's block-fp8 linear (`aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`) routes all weight shapes outside a small hard-coded triton allowlist to the aiter **`gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`** CK kernel (with weights preshuffled at load). On this gfx950 + ROCm 7.2 build that kernel is numerically inaccurate — it introduces a small error in **every** linear layer that compounds across all 78 layers. Switching to the plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` kernel (what vLLM uses) fully fixes it. The code already carries a warning about this kernel: ```python # layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:65 # ROCm 7.0 hipcc miscompiles gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle on gfx95 (#23319). _use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = _use_aiter_gfx95 and get_hip_version() >= (7, 2, 0) ``` It is gated to ROCm ≥ 7.2 on the assumption the miscompile is fixed, but it is **still wrong** on ROCm 7.2 / gfx950. ## Environment - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13.post1-rocm720-mi35x` (ROCm 7.2, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` baked in) - HW: AMD MI350X (gfx950), TP=4 - Model: `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8` (block-fp8, 128×128 weight scales) - Flags: `--dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang` (DSA), `--kv-cache-dtype bfloat16` (cliff is deterministic in bf16; fp8 KV adds non-determinism but is also wrong) ## Reproduction / evidence Greedy in-context induction prompt — `"The capital of France is Paris. The capital of Germany is"`: - **stock**: `" Paris. The capital of France is Paris..."` (WRONG, deterministic) - vLLM (`rocm/vllm-dev:nightly`, same HW/model/quant, `--linear-backend aiter`): `" Berlin. The capital of Italy is Rome..."` (correct) GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot, `few_shot_gsm8k.py`): | | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---| | stock (bpreshuffle) | **0.000** | 0.72 | | plain CK (fix below) | **0.925** | 0.00 | Cross-engine per-layer residual-stream cosine vs vLLM (pos 1) confirms a **gradual, compounding** divergence, not a single bad layer: | layer | 0 | 16 | 32 | 48 | 77 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | stock | 0.96 | 0.96 | 0.89 | 0.53 | **0.10** | | fix | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | **1.00** | Ruled out as causes (all verified correct on stock): DSA indexer top-k selection, RoPE (fused / optimized / native), the absorbed-MLA attention core (`cos = 1.0` vs a torch reference on identical inputs), the `w_kc` absorption GEMM, fp8 activation-quant granularity (`SGLANG_USE_AITER_FP8_PER_TOKEN`). The only thing that fixes it is changing the block-fp8 GEMM kernel. ## Root cause detail `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` (`layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:764`): - gfx950 + ROCm≥7.2 ⇒ `_use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = True` - For shapes **not** in `use_aiter_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned_gfx950` (a 14-entry allowlist) ⇒ kernel = `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, and weights are preshuffled at load (`fp8.py:567`, `shuffle_weight`). - vLLM (`model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/aiter.py: AiterFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`) instead uses `triton_gemm_a8w8_blockscale` (its own tuned allowlist) **or plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale`** — never the bpreshuffle variant. So most of GLM-5.2's layers run on a different (and, on gfx950, broken) kernel than vLLM. Scope: **gfx950 only** (`is_gfx95_supported()`); gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X) takes `use_triton=True` and is unaffected. ## Fix / workaround One-line correctness fix — disable the bpreshuffle path so block-fp8 falls back to the plain CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale` (and the load-time preshuffle is skipped, since `fp8.py` imports the same flag): ```python # layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py:66 _use_aiter_bpreshuffle_gfx95 = False # was: _use_aiter_gfx95 and get_hip_version() >= (7, 2, 0) ``` With this, GLM-5.2-FP8 on gfx950 matches vLLM: GSM8K 0.925, per-layer cosine ≈ 1.0, and **EAGLE/MTP acceptance recovers to 2.65–3.77** (was ~1.3) — i.e. the bpreshuffle bug was also the cause of the previously-reported poor MTP acceptance on gfx950. Possible upstream resolutions (maintainer call): 1. Disable `bpreshuffle` on gfx950 for correctness until the aiter CK kernel is fixed (perf regression for the shapes where it currently works), or 2. Fix `aiter`'s `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` on gfx950/ROCm 7.2 (the real fix; cf. #23319), or 3. Expand `use_aiter_triton_gemm_w8a8_tuned_gfx950` to cover these shapes (route them to the working triton kernel), or 4. Add an env flag to disable bpreshuffle (none currently exists). A correctness gate (option 1/3) is preferable until the kernel is verified, given the severity (silently wrong output, GSM8K 0.0). ## Note There is currently **no runtime flag** to avoid this — it requires a source change — so all current `*-mi35x` images serving block-fp8 DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM-5.2 on gfx950 are affected.

signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug While I was setting up my developer environment, I noticed that I cannot edit the files. After looking at the devcontainer.json and Dockerfile, it looks like we need to change the UID and GID value to the one from the host. After changing, the docker image build step fails as the user and group already exists. A better solution is to check if the user/group exists or create new one. I already have a fix in my forked repo ([fix commit](https://github.com/irshadcc/sglang/commit/668e3f592c837301ff580f04116c8336cb837e93)) and look forward for your suggestions ### Reproduction Change the UID and GID values to the host user and group. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Mar 23 2026, 19:04:32) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.1, V13.1.115 CUDA Driver Version: 590.48.01 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 sglang: 0.5.13 sglang-kernel: 0.4.3 flashinfer_python: 0.6.12 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.12 flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.8.1 torchao: 0.17.0 numpy: 2.3.5 aiohttp: 3.14.1 fastapi: 0.136.3 huggingface_hub: 1.19.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.37.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.2 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 uvicorn: 0.49.0 uvloop: 0.22.1 vllm: Module Not Found xgrammar: 0.2.1 openai: 2.6.1 tiktoken: 0.13.0 anthropic: 0.109.1 litellm: Module Not Found torchcodec: 0.11.1 NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X 0-15 0 N/A Legend: X = Self SYS = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes (e.g., QPI/UPI) NODE = Connection traversing PCIe as well as the interconnect between PCIe Host Bridges within a NUMA node PHB = Connection traversing PCIe as well as a PCIe Host Bridge (typically the CPU) PXB = Connection traversing multiple PCIe bridges (without traversing the PCIe Host Bridge) PIX = Connection traversing at most a single PCIe bridge NV# = Connection traversing a bonded set of # NVLinks ulimit soft: 1024 ```

signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B text rerank returns identical scores on NGC 26.05
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] This is a bug report, not a general question. - [x] The report is in English. ### Describe the bug `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B` appears to be broken for text-only reranking on `nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang:26.05-py3` (internal SGLang version reported in the live run: `0.5.11+05fb6a52`). The NGC build has native VL-reranker support in `/v1/rerank`: the serving code auto-detects this model family and returns the expected guidance to relaunch without `--is-embedding`. However, in generation mode the text-only rerank results are not discriminative: all documents receive the same score. Verified live excerpts from the DGX Spark activation run: ```text /v1/rerank: all documents scored identically: 0.4494 ``` The server log shows the likely failure point in prompt assembly: ```text Warning: More image data items provided than corresponding tokens found in the prompt ``` The same run showed each document prefill entering as one token: ```text #new-token: 1 ``` `/v1/score` was also not a usable workaround on this build. It ignored `label_token_ids` and returned a uniform distribution: ```text /v1/score: uniform 1/2048 distribution despite label_token_ids ``` This looks like the text-only path for the multimodal reranker is constructing or tokenizing the multimodal prompt incorrectly, causing both `/v1/rerank` and `/v1/score` to lose the query/document content. ### Reproduction Hardware/context: - NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 - Architecture: aarch64 - GPU target: SM121 - Container image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/sglang:26.05-py3` - Internal SGLang version observed: `0.5.11+05fb6a52` - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B` Request shape was a normal text-only rerank call: one text query and multiple text documents, with one obviously relevant document and one junk/irrelevant document. The exact request/response pairs and pod logs are available if useful; I am keeping this issue to verified excerpts rather than fabricating a minimal traceback. Observed behavior: - `/v1/rerank` returns identical scores for relevant and irrelevant text documents (`0.4494` in the captured run). - Server logs include `More image data items provided than corresponding tokens found in the prompt`. - Per-document prefill is logged as `#new-token: 1`. - `/v1/score` ignores `label_token_ids` and returns uniform `1/2048` probabilities. Expected behavior: - Text-only rerank should produce different relevance scores for clearly relevant vs irrelevant documents. - Text-only inputs should not trigger image-token mismatch warnings. - `/v1/score` should respect `label_token_ids` or fail explicitly if that mode is unsupported for this family. ### Additional context The model card documents Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B as a multimodal reranker that supports text inputs as well as image/video/mixed inputs. The same cluster has `Qwen3-Reranker-4B` (text) working correctly on SGLang 0.5.12.x via formatted `/v1/score`, so this appears specific to the VL reranker path in the NGC 26.05 / 0.5.11 build rather than a general reranking deployment issue.
signal.author: VitrineApps

signal.title: [Bug] --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass + FP8 weights crashes with AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner'
signal.text: ### Summary When launching sglang with an FP8 quantized MoE model and explicitly selecting `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, the server passes startup and CUDA graph capture cleanly, but **crashes on the first forward pass** with: ``` AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner' ``` The combination is silently accepted at config time and only fails when an actual request arrives, which is a poor user experience. The expected behavior is either: 1. A clear `NotImplementedError`/`ValueError` at server startup explaining that `flashinfer_cutlass` is not supported on the FP8 path (and pointing users at `--moe-runner-backend cutlass` instead), **or** 2. A real implementation of FP8 + flashinfer cutlass MoE. The lightweight first option would already remove a sharp edge for users. ### Environment - sglang: main HEAD (commit `10219bd9d` at time of repro) - flashinfer: 0.6.3 - torch: 2.9.1 / triton: 3.5.1 - transformers: 5.8.1 - Hardware: 1× NVIDIA H200 (SM 9.0) - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8` ### Reproducer ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --port 31103 ``` Then any request: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:31103/generate -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"text": "Hello", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 8}}' ``` ### Server log (truncated to the relevant frame) ``` File "sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 1447, in apply if self.runner.runner_backend.is_deep_gemm(): ^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'Fp8MoEMethod' object has no attribute 'runner' ``` ### Root cause analysis In `sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py`, `Fp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner` only assigns `self.runner` for a limited set of backends: ```python # python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py (main HEAD, ~line 1779) if ( moe_runner_backend.is_deep_gemm() or moe_runner_backend.is_triton() or moe_runner_backend.is_aiter() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm_routed() ): self.runner = MoeRunner(moe_runner_backend, moe_runner_config) else: # TODO(cwan): refactor other backends pass ``` When the user passes `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, none of the `is_*()` checks match, so the `else: pass` branch silently runs and `self.runner` is never set. Later in the same module, `Fp8MoEMethod.apply()` (~line 1938 on main) dispatches by reading `self.runner.runner_backend`: ```python if self.runner.runner_backend.is_deep_gemm(): ... elif self.runner.runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() ...: ... ``` Hitting `self.runner` then raises `AttributeError`. Note: the FP8 path already has a separate `cutlass` branch a few lines earlier that uses sglang's native `cutlass_fused_experts_fp8`: ```python if get_moe_runner_backend().is_cutlass(): output = cutlass_fused_experts_fp8(...) return StandardCombineInput(hidden_states=output) ``` So the working path for FP8 + cutlass is `--moe-runner-backend cutlass`, not `flashinfer_cutlass`. Users hitting the bug are likely confused by the BF16 path, where `flashinfer_cutlass` is the right (and now well-tuned, since #26496) choice. ### Suggested fix (minimal) Add an explicit failure mode in `Fp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner` so the incompatibility surfaces at startup, not at first request: ```python if ( moe_runner_backend.is_deep_gemm() or moe_runner_backend.is_triton() or moe_runner_backend.is_aiter() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm() or moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_trtllm_routed() ): self.runner = MoeRunner(moe_runner_backend, moe_runner_config) elif moe_runner_backend.is_flashinfer_cutlass(): raise NotImplementedError( "FP8 MoE does not currently support --moe-runner-backend " "flashinfer_cutlass. Use --moe-runner-backend cutlass for FP8 " "(sglang's native cutlass_fused_experts_fp8 implementation). " "flashinfer_cutlass is currently only supported on the BF16 " "path (unquant.py)." ) else: # TODO(cwan): refactor other backends pass ``` This is a strictly user-experience fix; the underlying implementation gap (no FP8 path through flashinfer's cutlass MoE kernel) is a separate discussion. ### Related - PR #26496 ("Changes for SM120 perf and usability for NVFP4", merged 2026-06-04) recently re-enabled `flashinfer_cutlass` in the FlashInfer autotune allowlist, restoring a 4.7-8.4× speedup on H200 BF16 models when users explicitly request `flashinfer_cutlass`. This is excellent — but it also makes it more likely users will reach for `flashinfer_cutlass` on FP8 models, which is exactly the path that hits this AttributeError. See our independent validation: PR #26496 with FP8 attempt also crashes the same way (would have validated this issue earlier if we'd tried FP8 first). ### Discovery context Found while benchmarking sglang BF16 vs FP8 throughput on H200 with a deterministic bench harness. The BF16 path with `flashinfer_cutlass` worked beautifully (5-8× over the triton default once #26496-style autotune is enabled); migrating the same flag to FP8 produced this crash. Happy to share the per-regime benchmark numbers and the bench-spec setup if that helps narrow down the failure mode. ### Willingness to contribute I'm happy to send a PR for the minimal user-experience fix (option 1 above) if maintainers agree that's the right framing. The real implementation (option 2) is out of scope for me — I don't know whether flashinfer's cutlass MoE has a working FP8 path on Hopper that sglang could plug into.
signal.author: gujialiang123

signal.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash on ROCm MI350X fails during weight loading: `ModuleNotFoundError: deep_gemm`; `sgl-deep-gemm` wheel requires `libcudart.so.13`
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug I am trying to serve `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` on a **single AMD Instinct MI350X 288GB / gfx950** using SGLang ROCm images. The model reaches weight loading, but then crashes in the DeepSeek-V4 loader because `deep_gemm` is imported during weight post-processing: ```text from deep_gemm import transform_sf_into_required_layout ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'deep_gemm' ``` When I try to install `sgl-deep-gemm`, the package installs, but import fails because the wheel is CUDA-linked and requires `libcudart.so.13`: ```text RuntimeError: Failed to load dynamic shared library .../deep_gemm/_C.so libcudart.so.13: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory ``` This suggests that the ROCm / MI350X DeepSeek-V4 path is still entering a CUDA DeepGEMM dependency path during weight post-processing. I also tried the latest relevant `rocm/sgl-dev` images listed on Docker Hub: <https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/sgl-dev/tags> The same `deep_gemm` import problem appears across the tested images. ### Reproduction ### Model ```text deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash ``` The checkpoint is used as shipped from Hugging Face. No manual quantization is applied. ### Images tested I tried the latest relevant images from the Docker Hub page: <https://hub.docker.com/r/rocm/sgl-dev/tags> Including MI35x / ROCm 7.2 / DeepSeek-V4-oriented tags such as: ```text rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0610-dsv4 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260609 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm700-mi35x-20260609 rocm/sgl-dev:rocm720-mi35x-da28108-20260609-DSv4 rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260608 rocm/sgl-dev:rocm720-mi35x-da28108-20260608-DSv4 rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0605-fix-2 rocm/sgl-dev:sglang-0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x-mori-0605-fix ``` I also tried upstream ROCm SGLang images: ```text lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x-20260611 ``` ### Minimal launch command The current launch is single-GPU TP=1: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4-flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8002 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --context-length 262144 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \ --schedule-policy lpm \ --attention-backend triton \ --allow-auto-truncate \ --enable-metrics \ --enable-cache-report \ --watchdog-timeout 3600 ``` I also tested a larger config with: ```bash --context-length 1048576 --max-running-requests 2 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --enable-mixed-chunk --enable-hierarchical-cache ``` but the same error occurs before serving starts. ### Docker Compose fragment ```yaml services: deepseek-v4-flash-mi350x: image: lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13-rocm720-mi35x container_name: deepseek-v4-flash-mi350x ipc: host shm_size: "64g" ports: - signal.title: [Feature] Reduce Mamba/GDN verify cache memory overhead in DFLASH speculative decoding
signal.text: Checklist - [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation DFLASH speculative decoding can introduce a large target-verify cache overhead for hybrid Mamba/GDN models. Today, for a DFLASH verify block of size `D`, the target side keeps intermediate recurrent state snapshots for each draft position. For Mamba/GDN, this is much heavier than ordinary per-token KV cache because each draft position stores a full recurrent SSM state. The intermediate SSM cache is roughly: ```text [num_mamba_layers, num_request_slots, D, recurrent_state_shape...] For a Qwen3Next/Qwen3.5-style GDN model, using: ~36 linear/GDN layers DFLASH block size D = 16 SSM dtype = fp32 conv dtype = bf16 max_running_requests = 48 the extra DFLASH verify cache is approximately: normal Mamba/GDN state per request slot: ~73.7 MiB DFLASH intermediate SSM cache per request slot: ~1152 MiB DFLASH intermediate conv cache per request slot: ~10 MiB total extra per request slot: ~1162 MiB So the full DFLASH intermediate cache is about 15.8x the normal Mamba/GDN state per request slot. Estimated extra cache per GPU: ┌─────────┬───────────────────────────┐ │ TP size │ extra DFLASH verify cache │ ├─────────┼───────────────────────────┤ │ TP=1 │ ~55.6 GiB │ │ TP=2 │ ~27.8 GiB │ │ TP=4 │ ~13.9 GiB │ │ TP=8 │ ~7.0 GiB │ └─────────┴───────────────────────────┘ Most of this comes from intermediate SSM snapshots. If we cache only the first K verify steps and replay/ recompute the accepted tail before commit, the overhead can be reduced substantially: ┌────────────────┬────────────────────────┐ │ cached steps K │ TP=1, 48 request slots │ ├────────────────┼────────────────────────┤ │ 16 │ ~55.6 GiB │ │ 8 │ ~28.1 GiB │ │ 4 │ ~14.3 GiB │ │ 1 │ ~3.9 GiB │ │ 0 │ ~0.5 GiB │ └────────────────┴────────────────────────┘ Related work: - #27658 Feat: add compact linear spec cache replay to reduce intermediate cache memory](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27658) - #26520: GDN MTP cache mode for final-state recompute (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26520) - #28695: GDN ReplaySSM ring spec-verify (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28695) - #28451: ReplaySSM buffered output-only decode for Linear Attention (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28451) Related PR: - #28010: Add DFLASH Mamba/GDN reduced-cache replay (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28010)
signal.author: jianuo-huang

signal.title: [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Add fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold
signal.text: # [RFC][NPU][DLLM] Fused tracker and coreset kernels for LLaDA2 JointThreshold ## Summary Two NPU-only fused kernels for the LLaDA2.1-mini dLLM JointThreshold decode path on Ascend, replacing per-layer small-op swarms in MoE expert tracking and coreset keep-mask selection with single kernels, behind a runtime flag with a pure-Torch fallback. On GSM8K (n=50) they deliver **+5.14% output throughput at identical accuracy (92.0%)**. This RFC proposes kernel placement and the kernel → release → integration upstream sequence. ## Motivation In the JointThreshold decode loop, two operations run per MoE layer per denoising forward: 1. the history-gate tracker max + EMA update, and 2. the per-call coreset keep-mask selection (softmax-sum score → group-balanced top-q). On NPU these are dispatch-bound: each is a handful of small kernels whose host launch cost dominates their compute, so the device idles between launches. Fusing each path into one kernel removes those launches from the decode critical path without changing the selection semantics. ## Proposed kernels 1. **`moe_gate_max_update`** — fuses the per-expert running-max update and the EMA update into one NPU kernel (replaces a `torch.maximum(...)` + `mul_`/`add_` pair per layer). 2. **`moe_shortlist_mask`** — computes the per-call coreset selection (bf16-rounded softmax-sum score; exact top-q-per-group with lowest-index tie-break, matching `torch.topk(q)`), writes the keep-set, and masks dropped experts, in one HBM round-trip (replaces ~6–10 small vector ops per layer). Both are NPU-only and shape-specialized to the current LLaDA2 MoE (E=256, 8 groups). The Python integration uses them only when enabled; otherwise the existing Torch path runs unchanged. ## Upstream sequence (kernel / release / integration) Kernel source and the SGLang Python caller land as separate PRs because the kernel package is released separately: 1. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Kernel source PR** — add the two ops + bindings + a correctness test. 2. **[sgl-kernel-npu] Release** — a maintainer ships a release containing the new ops. 3. **[sglang] Python integration PR** — env-gated NPU-only call sites with Torch fallback, depending on the sgl-kernel-npu release that contains the ops. Target repos: kernels → `github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu`; Python → `github.com/sgl-project/sglang`. ## Guarded-fallback design (integration PR) The integration is NPU-only and guarded; CUDA/default execution is structurally untouched because the kernels are NPU-only. The call site checks: `device.type == "npu"`, fp32 dtype + contiguity, op availability (`hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "moe_gate_max_update")` / `"moe_shortlist_mask"`), and the runtime flag — otherwise it runs the existing Torch path. The model still loads and serves when the kernels are not present; the Torch path simply runs. ## Evidence GSM8K (n=50), Ascend 910B3, LLaDA2.1-mini, SGLang dLLM JointThreshold. Control runs the identical recipe and runtime-flag stack with the two new kernels off (`TRACKER_MAX_UPD_KERNEL=0`, `PERCALL_KEEP_KERNEL=0`). | Run | Accuracy | Output TPS | Elapsed | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Control (kernels off) | 46/50 = 92.0% | 355.107 | 42.68 s | | + tracker-max-update + coreset-keep kernels | 46/50 = 92.0% | 373.346 | 40.60 s | Δ = **+18.24 tok/s (+5.14%)** at identical accuracy. Next: extend to n ≥ 100 and add a per-op fallback equivalence test. Excluded from this RFC: cbout, maxfold, tracker sum-update, and deferred-flush variants. They were tested locally but were not reproducible release candidates. ## Environment | Component | Version | | --- | --- | | NPU | Ascend 910B3 | | CANN | 9.0.0 (V100R001C10SPC001B250) | | torch / torch_npu | 2.10.0 / 2.10.0 | | dtype / attention / max-running-requests | bfloat16 / ascend / 1 | ## Open questions 1. Should these kernels live under the existing `sgl-kernel-npu` layout, or a dLLM-specific submodule? 2. What is the release/version mechanism for sgl-kernel-npu — how should the integration PR pin the release that contains these ops? ## Reviewers / references NPU backend: @ping1jing2 @iforgetmyname @whybeyoung · DLLM: @ClawSeven @btw616 Style references: #27127 (guarded NPU-only fallback), #21094 (before/after dLLM throughput evidence), #18485 (how-to-run + benchmark evidence), #27144 (concise NPU dLLM PR with GSM8K evidence).

signal.title: [Feature] Per-request Observability: TTFT Breakdown + HiCache Metrics
signal.text: ## Problem Currently, SGLang lacks per-request observability in two key areas: 1. **TTFT cannot be decomposed** — there's no way to know how much of TTFT is queue wait, schedule delay, or GPU forward time. Operators can only see total TTFT, making prefill performance tuning guesswork. This problem exists regardless of whether HiCache is enabled. 2. **HiCache tier performance is invisible** — with three-tier KV cache (GPU→CPU→NVMe) enabled, L2 DMA time, L3 prefetch I/O time, and per-tier hit/miss counts are not available per-request. No Prometheus metrics exist for cache hit rates, prefetch latency distributions, or eviction pressure. ## Proposed Solution A lightweight per-request trace + Prometheus metrics system covering both TTFT decomposition and HiCache observability, implemented across 5 files. ### Part A: Per-request Trace (JSON log, debug level) One JSON line per request at `logger.debug` level. The TTFT fields work universally; HiCache fields are gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache`: ```json { "rid": "b3f3e0e1...", "prompt_tokens": 136921, "input_tokens_cache_hit": 119040, "input_tokens_no_cache_hit": 17881, "output_tokens": 4096, "L1_hit": 0, "L1_hit_pct": 0.0, "L2_hit": 119040, "L2_hit_pct": 86.9, "L3_hit": 0, "L3_hit_pct": 0.0, "L3_pf_alloc_ms": 0, "L3_pf_io_ms": 0, "L3_pf_tree_ms": 0, "queue_ms": 9.9, "schedule_ms": 2.4, "forward_ms": 1174.6, "TTFT_ms": 78907.9 } ``` #### TTFT Decomposition (universal — works with or without HiCache) `TTFT ≈ queue_ms + schedule_ms + forward_ms` | Field | Source | Meaning | | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | | `queue_ms` | `time_stats.scheduler_recv_time → wait_queue_entry_time` | Tokenizer → enqueue | | `schedule_ms` | `time_stats.wait_queue_entry_time → forward_entry_time` | Wait in queue + chunk waits | | `forward_ms` | `time_stats.forward_entry_time → prefill_finished_time` | GPU prefill compute | #### HiCache Fields (gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache`) Per-tier hit token counts with percentages, L3 prefetch phase breakdown. > **Why no L2 DMA time?** `cache_controller.load()` is asynchronous — it allocates GPU memory and queues the DMA operation, then returns immediately. The actual DMA runs on a CUDA stream in a background thread (`start_loading()`). CPU-side `time.perf_counter()` cannot capture the DMA completion time. Since DMA bandwidth is fixed (PCIe 5.0 × 16 ≈ 64 GB/s), the transfer time is a known constant: `L2_hit_tokens × 48 KB/token ÷ 64 GB/s`. L2 token count alone is sufficient to characterize L2 performance. **L3 prefetch phase breakdown** (key finding made possible by this instrumentation): | Phase | P50 | Meaning | | ---------------- | ----- | ---------------------- | | `L3_pf_alloc_ms` | 0.1ms | Host memory allocation | | `L3_pf_io_ms` | 91ms | Pure NVMe→CPU I/O | | `L3_pf_tree_ms` | 0.4ms | Radix tree insertion | Without this breakdown, the total L3 prefetch time is often conflated with scheduler queue delays (~2.4s vs actual I/O ~91ms). ### Part B: Prometheus Metrics 6 Histograms + 2 Counters exposed at `/metrics`: | Metric | Type | Description | | -------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------ | | `sglang:hicache_l1_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L1 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l2_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L2 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l3_hit_tokens` | Histogram | L3 hit tokens per request | | `sglang:hicache_l3_prefetch_seconds` | Histogram | L3→L2 prefetch total duration | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_alloc_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: alloc phase | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_io_wait_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: I/O phase | | `sglang:hicache_l3_pf_tree_insert_seconds` | Histogram | L3 prefetch: tree insert phase | | `sglang:hicache_cached_input_tokens_total` | Counter | Cumulative cached tokens | | `sglang:hicache_uncached_input_tokens_total` | Counter | Cumulative uncached tokens | ### Part C: Eviction Metrics `RadixCacheMetricsCollector.increment_eviction_num_tokens()` called from cache eviction code paths (previously unused in `HiMambaRadixCache`): - L1→L2 eviction counter (tokens evicted from GPU to CPU) - L2→L3 eviction counter (tokens evicted from CPU to NVMe) > Write-back timing is excluded for the same reason as L2 DMA — `cache_controller.write()` is also asynchronous. ## Implementation Scope 5 files, ~100 lines of instrumentation total: | File | Change | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `scheduler.py` | `_hicache_trace_one_request()` method: trace JSON + metrics observe | | `metrics_collector.py` | 7 HiCache Histograms + 2 Counters | | `hi_mamba_radix_cache.py` | L2/L3 timing in `load_back`/`write_backup`/`evict`/`evict_host` | | `hiradix_cache.py` | Same for MHA models | | `cache_controller.py` | `_page_transfer` I/O timing via `try/finally` | ## Compatibility - TTFT decomposition fields work universally (no flag required). HiCache fields gated by `--enable-hierarchical-cache` - Trace output at `logger.debug` level only (no overhead at default `info` level), `tp_rank == 0` only - HiCache metrics guarded by `enable_metrics` and `--enable-hierarchical-cache` - No breaking changes to existing APIs ## Related - [#10916](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/10916) — Unified Observability Interface proposal (tracing + metrics + TimeStat). This proposal can serve as a concrete implementation of that unified interface for TTFT and HiCache. - [#13511](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/13511) — Request Tracing Roadmap. This proposal fills the "HiCache tracing" item under "Tracing for uncovered engine components." - PRs #13152, #17862 — trace-level/module unification (compatible approach)

signal.title: [Bug] HiCacheFile file backend: single flat directory causes ENOSPC at scale (millions of cached pages)
signal.text: ## Describe the bug The local file storage backend (`HiCacheFile`, `--hicache-storage-backend file`) writes every cached page as an individual `.bin` file **directly under a single flat directory** (`SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR`). On a long-running single-replica deployment this directory accumulated **~7.5M files**, at which point writes began failing with: ``` OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device: '.../<hash>.bin.tmp...' ``` …even though the filesystem had **~24 TB free and ~456M free inodes** (`df` and `df -i` both healthy). The cause is the **ext4 per-directory index (htree) limit**: a single directory can only index a bounded number of entries, and once that is hit the kernel returns `ENOSPC` regardless of free space/inodes. **Effect:** the L3 (restart-survival) cache tier silently stops persisting new pages (~8.3k failed writes/hour in our logs). Evicted/restarted sessions then miss the prefix cache and pay a full re-prefill. Secondary issue: `batch_exists` / `_collect_existing_component_keys` performs a full `os.scandir(self.file_path)` **per call**, i.e. O(total cached files) — a per-request scan over the entire cache directory at scale. ## Reproduce Run with `--hicache-storage-backend file` and drive enough distinct prefixes that the storage dir accumulates millions of `.bin` files. Writes fail with `ENOSPC` while `df`/`df -i` show ample free space and inodes. ## Environment Latest `main` is affected — `hicache_storage.py` still writes flat (`os.path.join(self.file_path, f"{key}.bin")`), `clear()` uses a one-level `os.listdir`, and `_collect_existing_component_keys` scandirs the whole directory. ## Proposed fix Shard files into 2-level hash-prefix subdirectories (`<ab>/<cd>/<name>.bin`, derived from the leading hex of the filename) so no single directory accumulates unbounded entries, and switch the batch-existence check from a full-dir scandir to per-key `os.path.exists` (O(keys)). PR coming.

signal.title: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (dense, hybrid GDN): intermittent silent decode degeneracy — tiny-output loop + decode-throughput collapse (extra_buffer, A100)
signal.text: ### Describe the bug Serving **`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` (dense, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet)** on a single **A100 80GB**, the server **intermittently** degenerates. It is **non-deterministic on byte-identical input**, **worsens over server uptime**, and **clears on a fresh restart/redeploy**. Two manifestations, both in the same bad windows: 1. **Tiny-output loop.** The model emits a burst of short, non-progressing completions — `completion_tokens` ~80–225 with `reasoning_tokens` collapsed to ~15–90 (vs ~260–690 in healthy completions), every one stopping on `finish_reason {matched: 248046}`, `num_retractions: 0`. An agentic ReAct loop on top of this cannot make progress and hits its recursion limit in ~20–48 s while producing nothing. 2. **Decode-throughput collapse.** A single request's decode drops to **~0.02 tok/s** while the GPU is pinned at **100% util and power-capped** (`clocks_event_reasons.active = 0x4` SW Power Cap, ~304 W vs 72 W idle), with `#running-req: 1`, `full token usage: 0.06`, `mamba usage: 0.03`, `cuda graph: True`. The GPU is busy but our decode does not advance. Crucially, **nothing is logged as an error** — no OOM, no KV-cache retraction, no NaN, no watchdog fire, no traceback, no restart. The model *successfully* returns degenerate output that looks like a normal `stop`. The same prompt that loops in a bad window produces a correct multi-hundred-token answer minutes earlier/later. ### What we ruled out (on the pod) - **GPU hardware:** ECC all-zero (volatile + aggregate SRAM/DRAM), no thermal slowdown, 29–39 °C. - **Server crash / OOM / KV retraction / NaN:** server log clean across hours of uptime; no restart. - **KV / mamba pool pressure:** `full token usage` 0.02–0.13, `mamba usage` ~0.03 (KV pool ~362 K tokens, single request). `num_retractions: 0` throughout. - **#23687 (FP8 weight_scale_inv dropped at load):** does not apply — the checkpoint loads with no `gate_gate_up_proj.weight_scale_inv not found` warnings and produces coherent output in good windows. The combination (GPU pinned 100% + power-capped + ~0.02 tok/s decode + short stop-token-248046 completions, no error) points at the **GDN / mamba decode path** entering a degenerate runtime state, not memory/cache or hardware. ### Reproduction Intermittent, so not reliable on demand. It surfaces under a sustained **agentic / multi-turn workload with long reasoning traces** (thinking enabled), typically within ~30 min of a fresh start; fixed-prompt and short-conversation probes run clean in a *healthy* window (so a one-shot repro proves nothing). We can attach server-side `--log-requests` captures of the degenerate `Finish:` lines + the `Decode batch` throughput-collapse lines + `nvidia-smi` from the moment. ### Environment - SGLang **0.5.13.post1** (official `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` image), CUDA 13.x, FlashInfer attn/sampling, xgrammar. - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` (dense hybrid GDN), `max_model_len` 262144, KV bf16. - GPU: 1× **A100 80GB PCIe** (SM80). Shared host (load avg ~16–28 from neighbours). - Launch flags: `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 262144` (radix cache on; no speculative decoding; `disable_piecewise_cuda_graph=True`). ### Questions for maintainers 1. Is this a known GDN/Gated-DeltaNet (or `extra_buffer` mamba-scheduler) decode-path degeneracy on Ampere, and is there a fix on `main` / a dev tag not yet in a released version? 2. Would `--mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer` avoid it? (We use `extra_buffer` specifically to avoid the `no_buffer`+flashinfer SSM-state aliasing / accuracy regression — #20791 — so this is a trade-off, not a clean toggle; `--disable-radix-cache` is rejected with `extra_buffer`.) 3. Any recommended `mamba_ssm_dtype` / `mamba_backend` / `max_mamba_cache_size` setting for stability on A100?

signal.title: [Bug] MiniMax-H3 FL2VA + Turbo LoRA: `slice_lora_b_weights` crashes on merged/QKV linear layers with TP>1
signal.text: ## Environment - **SGLang version**: 0.5.17 (latest PyPI release) - **torch**: 2.11.0+cu130, **CUDA driver**: 13.2 - **GPU**: 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm_120, 97.9 GB each), connected via **PCIe (no NVLink)** - **Host**: 251 GB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04 - **Model**: MiniMax-H3 FL2VA (`MiniMaxH3Pipeline`, `--model-variant fl2va`), local Diffusers checkpoint - **LoRA**: `larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora` → `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors` ## Launch command ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --num-gpus 2 \ --tp-size 2 \ --performance-mode memory \ --dit-layerwise-offload \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 20 \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --lora-path /path/to/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora \ --lora-weight-name minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors \ --lora-nickname h3-turbo-v4 \ --lora-scale 1.0 ``` (TP=1 also works for loading but OOMs at video-generation warmup; TP=2 is required for the model to fit.) ## Error 1 — 3D indexing on a 2D LoRA tensor During warmup / first forward: ``` IndexError: too many indices for tensor of dimension 2 File ".../sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/lora/linear.py", line 530, in slice_lora_b_weights return B[:, start_idx:end_idx, :] ``` Full stack: ``` layer.set_lora_weights(...) -> merge_lora_weights() (linear.py:361) -> _merge_lora_into_data() (linear.py:203) -> slice_lora_b_weights() (linear.py:530) return B[:, start_idx:end_idx, :] # 3 indices on a 2-D tensor ``` The offending method is `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.slice_lora_b_weights` (~line 522). It always assumes `B` is 3-D (`[out, in, rank]`), but for MiniMax-H3's gated-FFN merged layers the Turbo LoRA `lora_B` is 2-D (`[out, rank]`). The base class `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.slice_lora_b_weights` (~line 503) already handles 2-D correctly with `B[start_idx:end_idx, :]`. ## Error 2 — per-head vs linear sharding for QKV-merged layers After locally patching `slice_lora_b_weights` to do 2-D slicing on the first dim, a second mismatch appears: ``` RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (10752) must match the size of tensor b (3584) at non-singleton dimension 1 ``` 10752 = 3×3584 is the QKV-merged output (q+k+v). `slice_lora_b_weights` computes the shard as `output_partition_sizes[0]` (the width of a **single** logical weight, e.g. Wq = 1792 under TP=2) and slices only that much, but a QKV-merged LoRA `lora_B` spans **all** logical weights (q+k+v), so the correct per-rank slice is `sum(output_partition_sizes)` = 5376 under TP=2 — not 1792. The same issue affects `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA` (gated FFN, 2 logical weights). ## Expected behavior Turbo LoRA (`larryvrh/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora`, and presumably `lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo`) should load and run on MiniMax-H3 with TP>1. It currently only loads with TP=1 (which then OOMs for video generation on 97.9 GB cards). ## Additional note The SGLang cookbook's MiniMax-H3 LoRA recipe (https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3) references these exact LoRAs, but the documented hardware (B200/H100/H200) likely does not exercise the merged/QKV LoRA sharding path the way RTX PRO 6000 does here. This looks like a genuine bug in `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA` / `QKVParallelLinearWithLoRA` slicing semantics for 2-D LoRA adapters under TP.

signal.title: [Spec] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector
signal.text: ## Motivation Two additions to the DFlash draft, both switched on by the checkpoint. A DFlash checkpoint declares neither and takes the path it always took. **Grouped dynamic depthwise convolution** inside each block, so a proposal position can see the ones before it without another backbone pass. `out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`, taps zero across the block boundary. Wraps each sublayer in and out from one projection of its input. On when `conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` are set. **Candidate selector.** Instead of an independent argmax per slot, keep the target head's top-K per slot, score adjacent transitions `edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`, and walk the best path from the verified anchor. At T>0 it walks by inverse CDF and returns q over the K candidates for the lossless verify. On when `selector_rank` and `selector_top_k` are set. ## Modifications ``` srt/models/dflash.py the convolution, the selector, the walk kernel srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py four config fields srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py the proposal and the T>0 verify ``` The selector's decode is folded into the draft CUDA graph, greedy and sampled alike. The walk is one Triton program per request: a slot's K scores stay in registers, greedy rows take the argmax and emit a one-hot q, and the slot-to-slot dependency is a loop inside the program rather than a kernel per slot. No new server args, no new env vars, nothing outside DFlash touched. ## Accuracy Tests ``` python -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py ``` `4 passed` and `5 passed`. `test_dflash_logits.py` covers the selector's sampled path end to end, the mixed greedy/sampling batch — each row identical to running it alone, with greedy rows asserted to carry a one-hot q — and the rejection of a quantized target LM head. Lossless decoding is the property that matters here and it is structural: greedy walks emit the point mass at the token they take, and sampled walks return the realized q over the K candidates, so the verify sees the proposal distribution it actually drew from. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Published evaluation for [`z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2) on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`: SGLang on one H200 with FlashAttention 3, block size 8 (seven draft tokens per verification step), Qwen3.8's recommended sampling (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) at `xhigh` reasoning effort, 4096 max new tokens, prompts formatted by [`z-lab/dflash`](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash). Compared against the target's built-in MTP and a community DSpark drafter, [`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark), both also proposing seven tokens per step. ### Acceptance length Per-request mean of completion tokens over verification steps. | Dataset | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 | |---------|----:|-------:|---------:| | GSM8K | 5.02 | 4.36 | **5.46** | | MATH-500 | 4.72 | 3.92 | **5.28** | | HumanEval | 3.91 | 3.30 | **4.39** | | MBPP | 3.99 | 3.51 | **4.79** | | MT-Bench | 3.74 | 3.01 | **4.10** | ### Throughput, GSM8K Output tokens over end-to-end wall time, with speedup over autoregressive decoding. | conc | autoregressive | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 | |------|---------------:|----:|-------:|---------:| | 1 | 68.9 | 178.5 (2.59×) | 185.3 (2.69×) | **236.1 (3.43×)** | | 8 | 467.2 | 1,022.1 (2.19×) | 1,040.8 (2.23×) | **1,328.7 (2.84×)** | | 32 | 1,329.8 | 1,381.1 (1.04×) | 1,506.5 (1.13×) | **1,922.5 (1.45×)** | Full tables for the other four datasets, and for [`z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2) against Meta's published DFlash assistant, are on the model cards. ### What it costs The convolution and the selector are the whole difference between a DFlash draft and a DFlash 2 draft, so their cost is what a step loses by having them. Measured against Meta's published DFlash assistant on the same target, [`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B), block 16, GSM8K, four H200 shards. `cost` is `(1 + accept gain) / (1 + throughput gain) - 1` — the throughput gain the extra acceptance would have produced had the step stayed the same length, against the gain it actually produced. | conc | acceptance | throughput | cost | | acceptance | throughput | cost | |------|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|---|-----------:|-----------:|-----:| | | **T=0** | | | | **T=1** | | | | 1 | +13.6% | +11.7% | 1.7% | | +24.4% | +21.1% | 2.7% | | 8 | +14.0% | +11.4% | 2.3% | | +24.5% | +21.5% | 2.5% | | 32 | +14.1% | +11.9% | 2.0% | | +24.0% | +21.2% | 2.3% | | 64 | +14.0% | +12.3% | 1.5% | | +24.3% | +22.2% | 1.7% | So 1.5–2.7%, and it falls as the batch grows: the target verify grows with the batch while the selector's work does not keep pace. It falls as the target grows for the same reason. Acceptance enters this table only as a ratio between the two drafts, both measured the same way — as total accepted tokens over total verification steps, where the model card reports a mean over per-request ratios. The two statistics differ on absolute values but nearly cancel in the gain: +24.3% here at concurrency 64 against the card's +21.0% for the same pair of checkpoints. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32199057265](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199057265)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32199057143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199057143)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [P/D disagg] Decode-side radix cache for SWA hybrid models (unified radix tree)
signal.text: <!-- codex-pr-description:start --> This PR enables device-resident decode-side radix reuse for hybrid SWA models on the experimental unified radix tree. It keeps full-attention KV reusable while transferring a fresh SWA window, reducing repeated P/D KV transfer without introducing HiCache or Mamba support. ### How This Was Implemented - Caps the reused full-attention prefix at the SWA window boundary and allocates only the fresh SWA tail. - Caches an unfinished request's computed prefix, deduplicates overlapping full-attention KV, then repoints the live request to the cache-owned slots. - Carries SWA lock boundaries through rejection paths, including when the cap reduces a matched prefix to zero. - Requires the unified radix tree and rejects hierarchical cache, Mamba/SSM, DSA, and SWA-compress variants. - Adds registered device-only gpt-oss-20b P/D coverage. ### Before and After | Unfinished-request state | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Full-attention KV is device-resident but the old SWA window is tombstoned | The normal full+SWA match can return zero indices after insertion has deduplicated the request's full KV. Repointing then fails `new_prefix_len <= len(new_indices)`; continuing would leave the request referencing freed duplicate slots. | This one lifecycle path requests the full device-resident match, rewrites the request table to the cache-owned full-KV slots, and transfers its lock to the deepest full-resident node. Normal scheduler matching remains SWA-window-safe. | <details> <summary>Walkthrough</summary> #### Mental model Full-attention KV remains reusable across turns, while SWA KV is valid only for the current live window. ```mermaid flowchart LR P["Prefill delta"] --> D["Decode admission"] M["Unified-tree prefix match"] --> D D --> F["Reuse full-attention KV"] D --> W["Allocate fresh SWA tail"] F --> C["Cache unfinished request"] W --> C ``` #### Why a full-device match is required `cache_unfinished_req` is named for the request lifecycle, not for a single pointer operation: it commits the current prefix of a request that will continue running. It inserts the prefix into the shared radix tree, deduplicates request-owned full-KV slots that the tree already owns, resolves the canonical cached slots, rewrites the live request's token table, and moves the request's tree lock. For a four-token reused prefix: ```text request-owned full KV before insert: R0 R1 R2 R3 cache-owned full KV: C0 C1 C2 C3 cache-owned SWA KV: tombstoned insert result: prefix_len = 4; duplicate R0-R3 are released normal match: [] because SWA is tombstoned full-device match: [C0 C1 C2 C3] canonical slots for repointing ``` The normal match would make the safety check `4 <= 0` fail. The full-device match makes it `4 <= 4`, so the request is repointed to `C0-C3` before it continues; `return_full_match` defaults to false and is enabled only at this repoint call, so admission and reuse decisions still require an SWA-valid match. #### Request lifecycle Decode matches and locks the device prefix, caps reuse at the SWA window boundary, checks both full and SWA pool budgets, and allocates the remaining full pages plus the live SWA tail. Admission rejection releases the original matched-node lock even when capping reduces the usable prefix to zero; unfinished caching then commits the live prefix, tombstones out-of-window SWA positions, repoints full-attention slots, and transfers the request lock. #### Boundaries and limitations This change is device-only. SWA decode radix combined with hierarchical cache is rejected, and Mamba/SSM, DSA, and SWA-compress models remain unsupported. </details> ### Validation - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_radix_lock_ref.py -v` — 6 passed. - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` — 1,818 ran; 758 skipped; OK. - Mocked `build_kv_cache` smoke — device-only path succeeds; SWA + hierarchical cache raises. - `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files ...` — passed. - Targeted `/rerun-group disaggregation` — SWA decode-radix passed on 8×H20; hybrid-attention passed on 8×H200. <!-- codex-pr-description:end --> ## Motivation Extend the decode-side radix cache (P/D disaggregation, #19746) to **sliding-window-attention (SWA) hybrid models** such as gpt-oss, which are currently rejected at startup. With this, a decode worker can **reuse a cached prefix's full-attention KV across requests/turns** and request only the delta from the prefill worker, instead of receiving the entire prefix KV every time. The feature is gated to the **experimental unified radix tree** (`SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE`). The default `SWARadixCache` and the Mamba/SSM pools remain unsupported on this path, as do DSA (DeepSeek-V4) and SWA-compress (Gemma/MiMo) variants. > Supersedes #26218, which took the same feature through the default `SWARadixCache`. We're standardizing on the unified tree for SWA decode-radix, so that path is dropped here. ## Background: why SWA needs special handling A hybrid SWA model keeps **two** KV caches with different lifetimes: - **Full-attention layers** — keep KV for every token, as long as it's cached. Large, sticky. - **Sliding-window layers** — keep KV for only the last *W* tokens; older slots recycle as the window advances. Bounded. So on the decode worker the prefix's **full-attention** KV can be reused directly, but its **sliding-window** KV cannot — by reuse time the original writer's window has slid past it. Such a node is a **tombstone** (full KV present, SWA recycled). This is normal and harmless for correctness: a reuser only needs the window for its *own* current position, which it gets fresh. ## What this PR does - **`kv_cache_builder.py`** — allow SWA + `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` **only when the unified tree is active**; otherwise raise (DSA / SWA-compress still blocked even under unified). - **`decode.py`** — decode-side SWA mechanics: cap full-attention prefix reuse at the sliding-window start so the window lands in the fresh delta; `alloc_extend_swa_tail` on radix hits; mark the non-window prefix `swa_evicted_seqlen` (SWA tombstone); SWA-aware budget/eviction accessors; thread the SWA lock uuid through prefix lock/release. - **`unified_radix_cache.py` + `swa_component.py` + `base_prefix_cache.py`** — two `UnifiedRadixCache` fixes this path needs: 1. **SWA pool leak.** `SWAComponent.prepare_for_caching_req` only forwarded `swa_evicted_seqlen` when `is_finished=True`; on the unfinished path the out-of-window prefix tokens were inserted as *live* SWA and counted as `swa_evictable`, so at idle `available + evictable` exceeds the pool. Forward it on both paths so they become tombstones (`0` on the aggregated path → unchanged there). 2. **`cache_unfinished_req` repoint.** The dedup/repoint operates on full-attention cards but was sized by the SWA-window-safe match. On a reused, tombstoned prefix the window-safe match collapses to `0` while the cards number in the hundreds, tripping `assert new_prefix_len <= len(new_indices)`. Add `MatchPrefixParams.return_full_match`: `_match_prefix_helper` returns the deepest device-resident node, `_match_post_processor` returns the full cards + that node. The unified `inc_lock_ref` already skips tombstones, so no lock change is needed. No `swa_radix_cache.py` changes — the old path is intentionally not supported. ## Usage ``` --disaggregation-mode decode \ --disaggregation-transfer-backend {nixl|mooncake} \ --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache \ --page-size 64 # with SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 in the env ``` ## Test `test/manual/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_decode_radix_cache_swa.py` (gpt-oss-20b; manual because the model isn't in the CI pool) launches with the unified tree via `extra_*_env` and runs the shared decode-radix mixin (multi-turn cache-hit + 2-pass gsm8k). Validated on `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, 1P1D on 2×L40S, `--page-size 64 --attention-backend triton`, strict idle + per-iteration memory checks: | Check | Result | |---|---| | Multi-turn prefix reuse (decode cache hit) | cached tokens grow across rounds (0 → 1792 → 3584) | | gsm8k, 500 ex, 2 passes (2nd hits the cache) | 0.532 / 0.572 | | SWA-pool leak / `cache_unfinished_req` assert | **0 / 0** | ## Deep dive Writeup of the two `UnifiedRadixCache` bugs hit while enabling this path — exact errors, root causes, fix walkthrough, before/after validation: https://gist.github.com/ishandhanani/ed3cd2082381f31d848a7f6fcac977c6 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32199795172](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199795172)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32199794974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32199794974)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Docs]: clarify chunked_prefill_size and max_prefill_tokens semantics
signal.text: ## Motivation `--chunked-prefill-size` and `--max-prefill-tokens` are both per-batch token budgets that are decremented together as requests are admitted, but the existing docs describe them as independent limits with no mention of their interaction. Additionally, `--chunked-prefill-size` silently gets divided by `dp_size` when `--enable-dp-attention` is set, and neither this behavior nor the truncation semantics are documented. Raised in #20018. ## Modifications - `docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.md`: extended the descriptions of `--chunked-prefill-size` and `--max-prefill-tokens` to clarify (1) both are shared per-batch budgets, not per-request caps; (2) `--chunked-prefill-size` additionally triggers truncation of individual requests; (3) whichever budget is tighter bounds the batch; (4) the effective value of `--chunked-prefill-size` is `chunked_prefill_size // dp_size` when DP attention is enabled. - `docs/advanced_features/hyperparameter_tuning.md`: added a note in the OOM tuning bullet pointing readers to the server arguments reference for the interaction between the two parameters. Docs-only change.
