signal.title: [AMD][CI] Add the Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x nightly, and stop running two Qwen jobs that are not paying for themselves
signal.text: ## Motivation Two related changes to AMD nightly Qwen coverage: add the missing Qwen3.8 job, and stop spending runner time on two Qwen jobs that are redundant or dead. **Add Qwen3.8.** [Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8) shipped with [day-0 SGLang support](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-12-qwen3-8-day0-support/) and a [day-0 AMD Instinct recipe](https://www.amd.com/en/developer/resources/technical-articles/2026/day-0-support-for-qwen-3-8-on-amd-instinct-gpus.html), but the AMD nightly has no coverage for it. The model reuses the Qwen3.5 architecture (the checkpoint reports `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`), so it runs today with no model-code changes — which is exactly why nothing currently guards it. A change to the shared Qwen3.5 hybrid path or to the AITER MXFP4 MoE kernels can silently degrade Qwen3.8 output quality or throughput on ROCm with no signal. The new job follows the single-node MI355X cell the cookbook publishes ([`hw=mi355x`, `quant=mxfp4`, `strategy=balanced`, `nodes=single`](https://lmsysorg.mintlify.app/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8#hw=mi355x&variant=default&quant=mxfp4&strategy=balanced&nodes=single)). **Stop running the Qwen3-235B jobs.** They duplicate `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` coverage that survives elsewhere, including per-commit. ### Why MXFP4 and not the FP8 checkpoint directly At 2.4T parameters FP8 is ~2.4 TB, against 8 x 288 GB = 2.30 TB on an MI355X node, so the FP8 checkpoint has no single-node AMD recipe at all — the cookbook serves it as MI300X TP8 x PP2 across two nodes, and the AMD nightly runners are single-node. Single-node on AMD therefore means FP4. The job serves [`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4), AMD's Quark quantization **of `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`** (~1.2 TB, ~150 GB per GPU). Only the routed experts are quantized — attention, the shared expert, the MoE gate and `lm_head` stay at source precision — so AMD measures the same **97.49** GSM8K as the FP8 baseline (100% recovery). The FP8 checkpoint's quality is what this job is gating; MXFP4 is just the packaging that fits one node. ## Modifications ### New: Qwen3.8 MXFP4 MI35x job **`test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen38_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`** (new) — two phases in one file, registered to the `nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4` suite (`est_time=14400`, `nightly=True`): - `test_a_gsm8k_accuracy` — GSM8K few-shot at TP8, gated at 0.93. - `test_b_serving_perf` — serving benchmark over batch sizes 1/8/16/64 at 1024 in / 1024 out, reported through the shared `generate_simple_markdown_report`. Both phases launch from a single `SERVER_ARGS`, which reproduces the recipe published on the AMD model card: ``` --tp 8 --attention-backend aiter --page-size 1 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --trust-remote-code --watchdog-timeout 1200 \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' ``` with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and the eval runs `run_eval` gsm8k over the test split at 512 threads, `max_tokens=2048`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`. **Why accuracy and perf share a suite** rather than splitting into `nightly-amd-accuracy-*` and `nightly-perf-*`: sharing one `SERVER_ARGS` means the throughput numbers describe the exact configuration the accuracy gate covers, and a flag change cannot drift one out from under the other. Perf is also skipped unless accuracy passed (`accuracy_passed` class flag, with ordering from unittest's alphabetical method sort): a server that decodes garbage still benchmarks fine, so publishing its throughput would be worse than publishing nothing. Two flags in `SERVER_ARGS` are load-bearing rather than restatements of a default, and are commented as such in the file: - `--page-size 1` — `_page_size_default` bumps the default to 64 on HIP when the container sets `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, so the measured geometry only holds if the page size is pinned. - `--attention-backend aiter` — no arg override picks a backend for `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM` on ROCm, so the AITER path has to be named. The server deliberately runs with **no `--reasoning-parser`**: the scorer extracts the last number in the reply, so a `<think>` block still scores when reasoning stays in `message.content`. With a reasoning parser on, it would be split into `reasoning_content`, leaving `content` empty and scoring 0. The model path is overridable via `QWEN38_MXFP4_MODEL_PATH` for hosts with a local copy. **`.github/workflows/nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`** — new `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` job on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`, wired into `job_select` and `check-all-jobs`. ROCm 7.2 only: MXFP4 needs gfx95x, and the model card pins ROCm 7.2.0 for MI350/MI355. There is no MI30x counterpart — gfx942 has no hardware MX matmul, and the FP8 checkpoint it would otherwise serve needs two nodes. It is a single step rather than the usual accuracy/perf pair, because both phases live in the same suite. `timeout-minutes: 420` / `--timeout-per-file 21600` budget two loads of the 1.2 TB checkpoint, one per phase, which dominate wall time well before either the eval or the benchmark starts; `ENABLE_CACHE_HOST: "1"` keeps the weights on the runner cache so steady-state nights are far cheaper than the first. **`test/run_suite.py`** — register the new suite under `NIGHTLY_SUITES[HWBackend.AMD]`. ### Removed: the Qwen3-235B nightly jobs Only the workflow jobs go. No file under `test/` is touched — the tests, their launch recipes and their thresholds stay exactly as they are, so re-enabling is re-adding the job, and `run_suite.py --suite nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` still works by hand in the meantime. (Marking the tests `disabled=` was considered and rejected: on top of removing the job it changes no behavior, and it would make that manual re-run silently skip.) **All three Qwen3-235B jobs** — `test_qwen3_instruct.py` (BF16), `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py` (FP8) on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, and `test_qwen3_instruct_mxfp4.py` (`amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`, TP4 + EP2) on MI35x, across *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` is well covered without them: - **Per-commit, on both ROCm lanes**, `test/registered/quant/test_quark_mxfp4.py` runs on `linux-mi35x-gpu-1` in the `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x` suite, quantizes `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507` with `--quantization mxfp4` and asserts `gsm8k >= 0.89`. That suite is dispatched by `pr-test-amd.yml` (ROCm 7.0 container) *and* `pr-test-amd-rocm720.yml` (`--rocm-version rocm720`), so the MXFP4 MoE kernels for this architecture's shapes are checked on every PR against both ROCm versions, not once a night against one. This is why the removal applies to the ROCm 7.0 nightly as well as 7.2: neither lane is left without a substitute. - **Nightly**, `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py` and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. - Serialized Quark MXFP4 *checkpoint loading* is covered by the Qwen3.8 job added here plus the DeepSeek-R1, GLM-5 and Kimi-K3 nightlies. What loses its substitute is the combination rather than any single ingredient: a pre-quantized Quark checkpoint on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale over TP4 + EP2. The per-commit test quantizes online at TP1, and expert parallelism survives nightly only through the MiniMax jobs — no Qwen job exercises EP after this. That is the deliberate trade for four 8-GPU jobs per night — two per nightly, each capped at `timeout-minutes: 120`, two on the `linux-mi300-8gpu-sglang` pool and two on `linux-mi35x-gpu-8`. The jobs removed are `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b[-rocm720]` and `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, along with their `job_select` options and `check-all-jobs` dependencies in each workflow. Their three test files then join the other registered-but-undispatched AMD nightly tests noted below. ### Out of scope After this change, a scan turns up **36 AMD nightly test files** registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — the three Qwen3-235B tests above plus 33 pre-existing ones, mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left untouched here. One is worth calling out for whoever picks that up: `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` is not merely dormant but unrunnable — `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has no `setup_profile_directory()` and `run_benchmark_for_model` takes no `enable_profile=`, so `test_b_perf` would `AttributeError` on its first line, and its model paths are runner-local `/data/amd/` directories rather than HuggingFace ids. It is deliberately left unmodified by this PR. ## Accuracy Tests **Validation run:** [Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2) #32196787596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196787596) — dispatched on this branch's head with `job_select: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720`, so it covers both the accuracy and perf phases. Job selection resolves as intended: `nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720` is the only active job, the other 45 are skipped, and no `qwen3-235b` job exists at this SHA, confirming the removal took effect. An earlier dispatch (#32185767315) predated the perf phase and was cancelled in its favour. Expect a long run: the 1.2 TB checkpoint has to be fetched onto the runner cache, and both nightlies fire at `30 17 * * *` and drain the same `linux-mi35x-gpu-8` pool, so a manual dispatch queues behind their MI35x backlog. The gate is `ACCURACY_THRESHOLD = 0.93`, ~5% below AMD's published 0.9749 — the same relative tolerance the sibling Qwen3.5 MI35x evals allow (`Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.yaml` uses `rtol: 0.05` against 0.9704, i.e. a 0.922 floor). The threshold is inherited from AMD's measurement rather than from a run on the CI fleet, so if the dispatch lands materially off 0.9749 on the CI image, the number should be recalibrated to the observed run the way the Kimi-K3 job was. No model or kernel code is touched by this PR, so there is no output-affecting change to validate beyond the job itself. Static checks, run locally without GPUs: both workflows parse and every `check-all-jobs` dependency resolves to a defined job, with no `job_select` option pointing at a removed one; the AST registry parser resolves the new file to `backend=AMD, suite='nightly-amd-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4', nightly=True, est_time=14400` and no file under `test/` other than the new one differs from `main`; the suite string matches across all three files with no stale references to the pre-rename name; and every symbol the new test imports exists in its source module. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py`, `check_no_bare_pytest_main.py`, isort, black, ruff and codespell all pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The perf phase is the speed coverage this PR adds; it publishes a latency / input-throughput / output-throughput / ITL table to the job summary rather than asserting a threshold, so it reports regressions without becoming a flaky gate. Batch sizes and sequence lengths are overridable through the usual `NIGHTLY_BATCH_SIZES` / `NIGHTLY_INPUT_LENS` / `NIGHTLY_OUTPUT_LENS` environment variables. Net runner impact: one new MI35x job added, four 8-GPU jobs removed (two per nightly, split across the mi300 and mi35x pools). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — the Qwen3.8 cookbook page already documents this recipe; no doc change needed. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - The nightly job can be re-run at any time via `workflow_dispatch` on `Nightly Test (AMD ROCm 7.2)` with `job_select: nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen38-mxfp4-rocm720`. 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32192821926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32192821926)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32192821399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32192821399)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(encode-server): do not forward None video metadata to the processor
signal.text: ## Motivation `MMEncoder._flatten_and_load_videos` guards the `video_metadata` kwarg with `if video_metadata:`, which tests the list for **emptiness** rather than for content: ```python videos, video_metadata = map(list, zip(*video_processed)) video_processor_kwargs["do_sample_frames"] = False if video_metadata: video_processor_kwargs["video_metadata"] = video_metadata ``` `preprocess_video` returns `(video, None)` whenever its input is not a `VideoDecoderWrapper` — i.e. for video that was already decoded upstream and handed over as frames. The guard then sees `[None]` (or `[None, None, ...]`), finds it truthy, and forwards it. transformers' `make_batched_metadata` converts the value only when it is `None` (synthesizing defaults), or when it is a list whose first element is a `list` or a `dict`. A list holding `None` matches neither branch and is returned unchanged, so the consumer dereferences `None`. Measured against transformers 5.12.1: ``` video_metadata=None -> [VideoMetadata(total_num_frames=4, width=8, height=8, frames_indices=[0, 1, 2, 3], ...)] video_metadata=[None] -> [None] -> .fps raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fps' video_metadata=[{...}] -> [VideoMetadata(..., fps=24.0)] ``` So omitting the kwarg is strictly *better* than forwarding `None`s: transformers then derives `total_num_frames`, `width`, `height` and `frames_indices` from the video itself. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py`: forward `video_metadata` only when every entry is present. The list is positionally parallel to `videos`, so individual entries cannot be dropped without misaligning the rest — hence `all(...)` rather than `any(...)`; a partially-populated list is omitted entirely. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_encode_server_video_metadata.py` covering all-`None`, all-real, mixed, and ordering (CPU, no model or GPU required). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. When metadata is present the behavior is unchanged; when it is absent the processor now receives no kwarg instead of `None` entries. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one pass over a list whose length is the number of videos in the request. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1. New unit test against the shipped `encode_server.py`: **2 failed, 2 passed** — the failures are exactly `test_all_none_metadata_is_not_forwarded` and `test_mixed_metadata_is_not_forwarded`, while the real-metadata and ordering controls pass. After the fix: **4 passed**. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196854673](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854673)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196854541](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196854541)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(multimodal): let load_video accept an already-constructed decoder
signal.text: ## Motivation `load_video` returns a `VideoDecoderWrapper` for a URL/path/bytes source, but rejects one on the way in. `_normalize_video_input` has no case for that type and returns `None`, so the call raises `ValueError: Unsupported video input type`. The function is therefore not idempotent with respect to its own return value. This blocks any caller that constructs the decoder itself — a custom decode backend, or a caller that fetched the bytes under its own network policy and wants SGLang to keep owning frame selection via `smart_nframes`. Today such a caller has to pre-sample frames and hand over a bare `ndarray`, which takes the `not is_video_obj` early return in `preprocess_video` and bypasses the `video_config` policy (`fps` / `nframes` / `min_frames` / `max_frames`) entirely. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: pass a `VideoDecoderWrapper` through, next to the existing `list`/`tuple`/`Tensor`/`ndarray` passthrough, and widen the type hint. Unsupported types still raise. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_load_video_passthrough.py` (CPU, no decoder backend needed — `VideoDecoderWrapper` is patched with a stub). ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to model outputs. This only widens accepted input types on the decode path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one `isinstance` check on a non-hot path. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1: ``` BEFORE RAISED ValueError: Unsupported video input type: <class 'Stub'> AFTER passthrough returned Stub, is-same: True ``` New unit test: 2 failed / 2 passed before the fix (the two failures being the passthrough cases, the passes being the regression guards for the existing types), 4 passed after. Also reproduced on `v0.5.16-cu130-runtime` and `v0.5.17-cu130-runtime`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196807882](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196807882)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196807536](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196807536)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(multimodal): resolve image token counts for decoded image tensors
signal.text: ## Motivation `BaseMultimodalProcessor.resolve_image_token_counts` reads `image.height` / `image.width`, which only exist on PIL images. But `gpu_image_decode` is `True` by default (`base_processor.py`), and `load_image` routes JPEG payloads through `torchvision.io.decode_jpeg(..., device="cuda")`, which returns a CHW `uint8` tensor. So the **default** configuration feeds this method a value it cannot read: ``` AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'height' ``` The failure is easy to miss because the call site wraps the block in `except Exception` and logs: > `Due to {e}, falling back to decode+retokenize, which may change prompt length (token drift).` The practical effect is that `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` — whose entire purpose is to avoid that drift — silently does nothing for JPEG images whenever GPU decode is on. It degrades to a warning rather than an error, so the feature looks enabled while never taking effect on the most common image format. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/base_processor.py`: add a small `_image_height_width` helper that reads the trailing two axes for a `torch.Tensor` (decoded image tensors are channels-first, so the spatial dims are always last) and keeps the PIL attribute path otherwise. `resolve_image_token_counts` uses it. - Added `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_resolve_image_token_counts_tensor.py` (CPU, no model or GPU required). Mixed lists of PIL images and tensors are handled, and a degenerate tensor (`ndim < 2`) raises `ValueError` rather than silently producing a wrong size. ## Accuracy Tests This change *restores* accuracy rather than affecting it: with the fix, `SGLANG_MM_AVOID_RETOKENIZE` can keep the user's exact tokens for JPEG images instead of falling back to decode+retokenize, which is the path that can change prompt length. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — an `isinstance` check per image, off the hot path. It does avoid an unnecessary retokenize when the flag is enabled. ## Validation Verified against `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260818-c0b6474b` by patching the image's own source tree at `/sgl-workspace/sglang` (editable install, so source and binaries match), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1: ``` BEFORE RAISED AttributeError: 'Tensor' object has no attribute 'height' AFTER [7] ``` New unit test: fails to even import before the fix, 6 passed after. Also reproduced on `v0.5.16-cu130-runtime` and `v0.5.17-cu130-runtime`. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — not applicable, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32196829036](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196829036)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32196828914](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32196828914)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion. This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in: ```bash --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 ``` The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged. Related work: - SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816 - FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738 ### FlashInfer version requirement This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP. The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI. The new option therefore requires both: - `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18` - `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change. GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431. ## Modifications ### Runtime selection and compatibility - Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`. - Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90. - Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior. - Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths. - Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI. - Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility. ### Weight preprocessing - Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing. - Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer. - Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2. - Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules. - Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range. - Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path. ### Kernel invocation Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API: 1. FC1 folded weight block scales 2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation 3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale 4. FC2 folded weight block scales 5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale. ### Tests and benchmark - Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with: - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales - EP rank with global expert IDs - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18 - Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare: - SGLang Marlin W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16 - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 - Update the server-argument documentation. ## Accuracy Tests The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed: ```bash python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v ``` ```text 18 passed, 1 skipped ``` The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \ --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`. ```bash PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \ python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --port 30000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 \ --api chat \ --max-tokens 1024 \ --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 \ --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl ``` | MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s | | W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s | W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU. The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \ FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \ python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py ``` Results on NVIDIA H20-3e: | Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x | | 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x | | 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x | | 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x | | 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x | | 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x | | 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x | | 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x | FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed. ## Scope and Limitations - The implementation is SM90-only. - It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path. - A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions. - [x] Update server-argument documentation. - [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18. - [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result. - [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085259](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085259)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31955085154](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31955085154)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Fix overlap scheduler for embedding/classification/reward models
signal.text: ## Motivation Two fixes that make overlap scheduling usable for prefill-only (non-generation) models: embeddings, classifiers, and reward models. Both bugs are hit immediately once overlap scheduling is enabled for such models and a batch goes big enough to trigger `batch_is_full`. ### Bug 1 — FutureMap allocated but unused `FutureMap` tracks future tokens emitted during the decode step. Embedding, classification, and reward models produce their output in a single forward pass and never consume the map, but `init_overlap` allocates one as long as `enable_overlap=True`. For a non-generation deployment, this is pure wasted memory. ### Bug 2 — `batch_is_full` never resets for prefill-only batches `get_new_batch_prefill` flips `self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True` when admission control kicks in on a large batch. For generation models this is fine — the flag is reset when the prefill batch is merged into `running_batch` on the next iteration. Prefill-only batches (embedding / classification / reward) are **never merged** into `running_batch`, so the flag stays `True` forever and the scheduler stops admitting new batches for the rest of the server's lifetime. ## Modifications `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`: - `init_overlap`: skip `FutureMap` allocation and return early when `self.is_generation` is False. - Main scheduling loop: add an `elif self.last_batch.is_prefill_only:` branch that resets `self.running_batch.batch_is_full = False` in the same place we'd normally merge the last batch. ## Accuracy Tests No numerical changes — the fixes only affect admission control and memory allocation. Verified existing embedding/classification tests pass with `--disable-overlap-schedule` **and** without it (i.e. overlap now actually works end-to-end for non-generation models). ## Benchmarking and Profiling Measured on `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, bs=256, input=512 tokens, H100: | Config | RPS | HFU | GPU util | |---|---|---|---| | Overlap disabled (`--disable-overlap-schedule`) | 18.1 | 27.4% | 87% | | Overlap enabled (with this fix) | **20.9** | **31.4%** | **98%** | **+15.5% throughput, +13.4% lower latency.** Before this fix, enabling overlap on an embedding server would freeze admission after the first large batch, so this benchmark wasn't even reachable. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed. - [x] Provide test results, including accuracy and performance analysis. - [x] For reviewers: follow the [Code Review Guide](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/code_review_guide.html).

signal.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for Encode Prefill Disaggregation
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR adds CI test coverage for encoder disaggregation features on Ascend NPU. Specifically, it validates the `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder` parameter, which allows a language-only VLM server to intelligently route single‑image requests locally while dispatching multi‑image requests to remote encoder servers. The tests ensure that the Ascend backend correctly supports: - `--encoder-only` and `--language-only` disaggregated deployments. - The `zmq_to_scheduler` and `zmq_to_tokenizer` transfer backends. - Adaptive dispatch logic that prevents single‑image requests from attempting to contact an encoder server (allowing safe use of dummy encoder URLs for validation). Without these tests, encoder disaggregation behavior on NPU could regress silently. ## Modifications Added the following test scripts under `test/registered/ascend/basic_function/EPD/`: 1. **`test_npu_adaptive_dispatch_to_encoder.py`** - Contains `TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoder` and `TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoderMultiImage`. - Validates single‑image local processing and multi‑image remote forwarding with `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder`. 2. **`test_npu_disaggregated_vlm.py`** - Contains `TestDisaggregatedVLM` (base) and `TestDisaggregatedVLM_ZMQ_Tokenizer`. - Provides foundational tests for `--encoder-only` + `--language-only` disaggregated VLM deployments on NPU. Both scripts set `SGLANG_MM_SKIP_COMPUTE_HASH=True` to work around Ascend’s lack of `_local_scalar_dense` support for `UInt64` in multimodal hash computation. This test suite implements the validation plan for the following encoder disaggregation parameters: - `--encoder-only` / `--language-only` - `--encoder-transfer-backend` - `--encoder-urls` - `--enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder` Additionally, the PR includes the existing `TestDisaggregatedVLM` base class and its `zmq_to_tokenizer` variant, which were previously added and serve as foundational tests for disaggregated VLM deployments on NPU. ## Accuracy Tests All tests are implemented in the scripts listed above and use deterministic settings (`temperature=0`) with a fixed inline image to guarantee reproducible results. - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_language_only_text_generation`** Validates that the language‑only server correctly answers a text‑only prompt (`"The capital of France is"` → `"Paris"`). - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_encoder_processes_image_via_language_server`** End‑to‑end image description through the encoder → language pipeline. - **`TestDisaggregatedVLM.test_encoder_processes_multi_images_via_language_server`** Similar validation with two images. - **`TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoder.test_single_image_processed_locally`** Ensures a single‑image request succeeds without a real encoder server, confirming local processing. - **`TestAdaptiveDispatchToEncoderMultiImage.test_multi_image_forwarded_to_encoder`** Ensures a multi‑image request succeeds when a real encoder server is available, confirming remote dispatch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable – this PR adds functional correctness tests only; no kernel or runtime changes that affect performance. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre‑commit. - [x] Add unit tests (via CI registration for NPU nightly suites). - [ ] Update documentation – encoder disaggregation flags are already documented; adaptive dispatch documentation will be tracked separately. - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks – not required for test‑only changes. - [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

signal.title: [release] install rust toolchain in release docker images
signal.text: ## Summary Adds a rustup install to the four release-image Dockerfiles that perform a source install of sglang at image build time: - \`docker/diffusion.Dockerfile\` - \`docker/npu.Dockerfile\` - \`docker/xeon.Dockerfile\` - \`docker/xpu.Dockerfile\` Images that already install rust (\`docker/rocm.Dockerfile\`, \`docker/gateway.Dockerfile\`) are left untouched; \`docker/sagemaker.Dockerfile\` inherits from the main image. ## Why Once the native Rust gRPC crate is bundled into the main sglang wheel via \`setuptools-rust\`, each of the release image builds invokes \`cargo\` during \`pip install .\` (or the \`[all_npu]\` / \`[diffusion]\` variants). Split so each Dockerfile change is independently reviewable and the release-image nightly workflows can be re-run separately. ## Test plan - [ ] Rebuild each affected image and confirm \`rustc --version\` / \`cargo --version\` succeed in the final image. - [ ] Verify a \`pip install\` path that pulls in a setuptools-rust-built crate succeeds inside each image. signal.title: feat(scheduler): adaptive warm reserve for chunked prefill
signal.text: ## Summary Adds `--prefill-reserve-budget N` so waiting requests with small uncached-prefill length can interleave into the **same forward pass** as an in-flight chunked cold-prefill request. 0 disables the feature; default is 0, so server behavior is unchanged out of the box. **Motivation:** long-context multi-turn agentic workloads on PD-disaggregation prefill engines. When a cold long request enters chunked prefill, it monopolizes the per-step token budget via ``add_chunked_req``, head-of-line blocking short-compute waiters for many chunks. This change lets the scheduler reserve a slice of the budget so those waiters finish in one step. **How it works:** before calling ``add_chunked_req``, the scheduler peeks at the top-K (8) waiting-queue requests and sums the page-aligned uncached-prefill length (``len(origin_input_ids) - len(prefix_indices)``) of any whose contribution fits in the reserve budget. The sum is passed as ``max_chunk_tokens`` to ``add_chunked_req``; the existing ``add_one_req`` loop then admits those waiters into the leftover budget. No changes to the PD state machine — ``KVSender`` / bootstrap / inflight queues are untouched and ``is_chunked`` is decremented per forward regardless of chunk size. **Also in this PR:** defensive fix for the ``chunked_req`` singleton invariant. Prior to this change, the assertion in ``get_new_batch_prefill`` was satisfied only by the accident of ``add_chunked_req`` consuming the entire ``rem_chunk_tokens``. Once we leave leftover budget, both ``PrefillAdder.add_one_req`` and ``PrefillAdder.add_one_req_ignore_eos`` chunked-promotion branches must explicitly reject promotion when ``has_chunked_req=True``. **Safety:** - Reserve is ceil-page-aligned; effective budget is further floored at ``chunked_prefill_size - page_size`` so the chunked request always retains at least one page of forward progress. - Config validation rejects ``prefill_reserve_budget >= chunked_prefill_size``. - Disabled path (``prefill_reserve_budget = 0``) short-circuits on the first line of the helper — byte-identical to ``main`` scheduler decisions. ## Test plan - [x] ``python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py -v`` — 14/14 passing (6 new + 8 existing). Verified on CPU-only venv. - [ ] E2E on PD-disagg prefill: set ``--prefill-reserve-budget`` to a nonzero value, send a cold long request mid-chunk plus several short-context requests, confirm the short ones interleave in the same forward pass and cold progression slows by roughly ``chunked_prefill_size / (chunked_prefill_size - budget)``. - [ ] Regression: run existing ``per-commit`` suite with flag at default (0); expect byte-identical scheduler decisions vs ``main``. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
signal.author: Kangyan-Zhou

signal.title: [Tracking] Host allocator: page-aligned allocation with host-side bookkeeping
signal.text: ## Motivation The KV allocator keeps its source of truth on device. Freeing KV therefore reads device state back -- `torch.unique(free_index // page_size)` with a data-dependent output shape, and on the SWA side the `full_to_swa_index_mapping` gather plus its `> 0` liveness filter -- each forcing a stream synchronization on the scheduler's stream. Under the overlap scheduler these syncs queue behind the WAR barrier, so the CPU parks until the in-flight forward drains. On workloads where requests finish every step (e.g. PD decode), this is a measurable throughput loss. None of that information needs a device read: it is host-known at allocation time. Target design (validated end-to-end by the #31335 spike): - Allocation is planned host-side in whole pages; each request tracks a page-ceiled allocated extent (`req.kv.kv_allocated_len`) with a single writer. - `free()` receives whole pages by construction -- no dedup, no liveness filter, no data-dependent shapes. `torch.unique` survives only behind a legacy API for truly scattered index sets. - Device tables (`req_to_token`, `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, `free_pages`) become write-only projections consumed by kernels; the scheduler never reads them back. ## Prior work **Landed** - #29427 / #29429 / #29432 -- `req.kv` container: owned-KV lifecycle and bookkeeping coupled to real allocations - #32701 -- free KV pages by segment in the paged allocator without a device sync (non-SWA) - #33475 / #34067 -- free-group batching and aliasing fix (hardening the deferred-free machinery the sync-free path relies on) - #35265 -- page-align the DFLASH decode KV reservation (toward the invariant: every writer keeps `kv_allocated_len` page-aligned) - #35286 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor at PD decode prealloc (I2: SWA liveness boundary invariant) - #35382 -- share the page-aligned decode alloc lens between EAGLE and DFLASH (dedup; the watermark loop becomes the single writer of kv_allocated_len) **Closed** - #31335 (with CI companion #31194) -- the original spike validating the full shape - #25500 -- early PoC: unify page allocation estimation on `kv_allocated_len` - #33907 / #34783 -- SWA free without a device sync via segment liveness contracts; closing in favor of the host-bookkeeping approach (the `swa_alive_from` contract only holds on the chunk-cache path; page-aligned extents remove the need for it) ## In flight - #35396 -- assert the page-aligned SWA evict floor on the second PD decode prealloc path, and drop the fixture that mocked an unaligned tail length - #35401 -- write the `req_to_token` page tail so a row stays valid over every page the allocator handed out; widen the row headroom to `page_size - 1` for every paged config. Prerequisite for page-ceiling `kv_allocated_len`: without it, anything slicing a row by a page-ceiled length reads the previous occupant's indices

signal.title: [diffusion] Warmup-calibrated auto residency promotion in performance-mode auto
signal.text: ## Motivation Under `--performance-mode auto`, component placement is decided **before load** from static per-model thresholds (`keep_resident_min_available_gb`). On GPUs with ample free VRAM this leaves components needlessly offloaded — e.g. a layerwise-offloaded text encoder on an 80–140 GB card pays a full H2D reload every request for VRAM nobody else uses — and fixing it by hand requires per-model, per-GPU flag tuning. This PR makes `auto` mode **calibrate residency from the server warmup it already runs**: measure real memory behavior, then promote implicitly offloaded components to GPU-resident when the default workload provably fits, before the server turns ready. Frozen after `/health`; no changes after startup. ## Modifications **Measurement** - Server warmup forwards record `peak_reserved` + a pre-forward baseline on **every rank** (previously output-rank only). - Video warmup (which caps frames to bound startup) adds one extra small-frame **calibration forward**; a two-point affine fit in workload units (`batch × W × H × frames`) separates constant (weights/buffers) from linear (activation) memory and extrapolates the default-workload peak with a 1.2× margin on the linear part only. Image warmup already runs the default shape, so it is a direct measurement, no extrapolation. - The loader now records real weight/buffer sizes alongside the GPU-load delta (`memory_usages` is ≈0 for exactly the offloaded components residency decisions are about). **Decision + promotion (between last warmup req and ready)** - All ranks all-gather `{estimated peak, budget, candidates}` and compute one deterministic plan: candidates are implicitly offloaded, known-size, native CUDA components only; ranked by per-request H2D savings (layerwise DiT counts default denoise steps); promoted greedily while `estimated_peak + promoted_bytes + reserve ≤ budget`, with `reserve = max(10 % budget, 4 GiB)` and `budget = free + torch-reserved` (min across ranks; excludes other processes on shared GPUs). - Promotion reuses existing primitives: component-offload → resident via `require_component_resident`, layerwise via `disable_offload()`; the strategy cache is invalidated explicitly. - A **re-warm forward** after promotion re-establishes compile/kernel caches and proves the promoted layout actually serves; any failure rolls every rank back to the original strategy (only a rollback failure aborts startup). - Excluded paths: explicit placement / `manual` mode, FSDP, diffusers backend, quantized DiT (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4, SVDQuant), Cache-DiT, breakable CUDA graph, realtime/disagg, `batching_max_size > 1`, any warmup failure. Kill switch: `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_DISABLE_AUTO_RESIDENCY=1`. **Fixes and unification along the way** - Warmup frame caps now run the pipeline's `adjust_num_frames`: LongLive2's server warmup was silently a no-op (17 capped frames → 5 latent frames, not divisible by `num_frames_per_block=8`, error swallowed by fail-open). - The post-request residency hint (`get_can_stay_resident_components`) now shares the promotion's candidate collection and H2D ranking — it previously read the ≈0 `memory_usages`, making the recommendation meaningless, and could recommend FSDP/custom-strategy components. - Logs narrate the adjustment: decision summary (`target/measured/estimated_peak/reserve/budget/promoted`), per-component `mode -> resident` with the **equivalent `--component-residency` flags** users can pin, and the kill switch. ``` Server warmup complete; adjusting component residency for the default workload (--performance-mode auto). Auto residency: target=1024x1024x1f steps=9, measured=[1024x1024x1f=17.4GiB], estimated_peak=17.4 GiB, reserve=13.3 GiB, budget=133.5 GiB, promoted=[text_encoder(layerwise-offload, 6.8 GiB)] Auto residency: adjusted text_encoder: layerwise-offload -> resident. Equivalent server args: --component-residency text_encoder=resident. ... ``` The optimization target is the model-default workload (default resolution/frames, batch 1). Larger or batched workloads should pin residency explicitly; the reserve bounds the blast radius. Static model deployment configs remain as the fallback when calibration is skipped. No numerics change for non-promoted paths; promoted components run identical code at a different placement. ## Test - `test/unit/test_auto_residency.py`: estimation (same-shape, single-point, two-point fit, negative-slope fallback, covering measurement), plan (skip propagation, reserve, cumulative fit, ranking), multi-rank worst-casing, promotion/rollback on stub modules, eligibility gates, LongLive2 frame alignment, applied-changes log, hint/promotion ranking consistency. - H200, Z-Image-Turbo serve: text encoder (layerwise, 6.8 GiB) promoted; warmup 9.15 s, decision <1 s, post-promotion re-warm 0.15 s; `/health` stays 503 until after promotion. - 2×H100, Wan2.1-T2V-14B: VAE promoted; text encoder correctly refused (estimated 65.6 GiB + 6.5 GiB TE > 70.2 GiB budget). Single-GPU 14B correctly refuses all promotions (72.6 vs 72.8 GiB). - Steady-state E2E improved on promoted image cases; no OOM observed in any validated case, including the refusal boundaries. ## Post-submission hardening (adversarial review pass) A 10-angle review over the diff surfaced and fixed, in `harden auto residency against review findings`: - **Measurement**: per-forward `empty_cache` + peak reset (allocator-pool carryover flattened the calibration slope → under-estimate → post-ready OOM); calibration forward moved after the main warmup so one-time allocations can only steepen the slope (safe direction); only `is_warmup` requests are measured (compile prewarm ran a different layout); failed warmups are recorded on every exit path; **`--enable-torch-compile` is excluded** — its warmup deliberately runs a stripped memory layout (layerwise DiT + evicted aux components) whose peaks are not serving peaks; unknown default workloads skip instead of trusting the capped peak. - **Distributed/rollback**: everything before the first all-gather is fenced into a skip report (a raise there parked peer ranks in the collective); error gathers filter on `is not None` with never-empty error strings; a failed in-apply rollback now surfaces as `rollback_failed` (aborts startup) instead of masquerading as rolled back; `disable_offload` re-arms hooks when `load_all_layers` fails; mechanism/mode mismatches from the `offload_during_compile` window are excluded and guarded; `_required_resident_components` tracks an owner feature so rollback cannot release loader hard-requirements. - **Startup contract**: apply-RPC failures honor the warmup fail-open contract; the post-rollback restore warmup keeps `--warmup-resolutions`' fail-closed contract; the calibration request shares `auto_residency_skip_reason` (the kill switch and excluded configs no longer pay for a measurement they never consume); warmup records are consumed exactly once (one-shot handler); re-warm passes no longer double-advance the warmup progress bar. - The warmup/target frame contract (cap → `adjust_num_frames` → `num_gpus` latent alignment) is now one shared helper extracted from `SamplingParams._adjust_visual_fields`, used by real requests, warmup requests, and the workload resolver. Known accepted conservatisms (documented in code): the budget check double-counts bytes of a component already partially on GPU at the measured peak (safe direction), and the reserve stays at `max(10 %, 4 GiB)`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32195701226](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195701226)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195700967](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195700967)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [PD] Enforce the request waiting timeout in disaggregation mode
signal.text: ## Motivation `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT` and `SGLANG_REQ_RUNNING_TIMEOUT` are only checked in `Scheduler.get_next_batch_to_run`, which the PD disaggregation event loops never call. In PD mode both timeouts are silently ignored, so a request stuck queued on a prefill worker can wait forever and abort-on-timeout never reaches the client. ## Modifications **Prefill — waiting = bootstrap queue + waiting queue.** `_abort_on_prefill_waiting_timeout` (called from `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run`) measures staleness from bootstrap-queue entry, i.e. arrival on the prefill worker, and scans both queues, making `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT` a bound on the total pre-compute wait. `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` remains the separate bound on handshake stalls. Two details: - **Rank consensus.** Both queues feed rank-aligned `poll_and_all_reduce` lists, so a per-rank clock decision could drop a request on one attn rank but not another and misalign the collectives. The stale verdicts are MIN-reduced across attn-tp/attn-cp ranks (new `all_reduce_min_attn_cp_tp_group` helper, same idiom as `poll_and_all_reduce_attn_cp_tp_group`) so every rank drops the same requests in the same iteration. - **Peer notification.** A timed-out request frees its metadata buffer slot and calls `disagg_kv_sender.abort()` so the decode peer observes `KVPoll.Failed` instead of blocking until its own transfer timeout. **Decode — deliberately no waiting abort.** By the time a request reaches the decode waiting queue, its prefill and KV transfer are already paid for — the worst point to shed load. Decode-side stalls all have owners: transfer stalls → `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT`, scheduled requests → the running timeout (now enforced in `get_next_disagg_decode_batch_to_run`; its `to_finish` mark is consumed by the decode/prebuilt result paths). This also avoids a spurious-abort hazard for resumed retracted requests, whose waiting stamp dates from the original KV arrival. **Shared abort helper.** The waiting-queue abort bookkeeping shared by `abort_request` and the timeouts is factored into `Scheduler._abort_waiting_request`. This fixes two client-abort leaks: the KV sender of a *bootstrapped* prefill request was never aborted (previously only pending-bootstrap senders were, leaving the decode peer hanging), and decode-side HiSparse state was never released. The prefill loop does not enforce the running timeout: its `running_batch` is structurally empty (the PD prefill loop never merges finished extends into it). The PP disagg prefill loop is unchanged and still has no timeout enforcement, as before. Note: like the existing non-PD path, timestamps are per-rank, but the consensus reduce makes the abort decision rank-consistent by construction. ## Testing `test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_timeouts.py` (CPU CI): - Prefill clock starts at arrival and spans both queues (a fresh waiting-queue stamp does not shield an old arrival); unstamped requests are never dropped. - The MIN-reduced consensus verdict gates rank-local staleness. - Timed-out prefill requests free their metadata buffer and abort the KV sender. - Decode planner enforces only the running timeout; prefill planner enforces the waiting timeout. - Client aborts of queued PD requests release role-specific resources (decode KV + HiSparse, prefill metadata + sender). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with `pre-commit run --all-files`. - [x] Add unit tests <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32184150957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32184150957)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32184150747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32184150747)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] DCP: reject fa3 for MLA and stop defaulting to it on Hopper
signal.text: > Stacked on #35298 (base: `fix-dcp-args-validation`). This PR's own diff is the last commit; GitHub will retarget it to `main` once #35298 merges. ## Motivation `fa3` has no DCP decode path for MLA models: it returns no LSE for the cross-dcp-rank reduction, so `forward_mla`'s `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` unpacks two values from a single return and a `--dcp-size > 1` run dies at decode cuda-graph capture with `ValueError: too many values to unpack` — far from the actual misconfiguration. `fa3` is also the **Hopper MLA auto-default**, so every Hopper DCP launch without an explicit `--attention-backend` hits this. Blackwell is unaffected because its MLA default is already `flashinfer`, which carries the DCP metadata. ## Modifications - `_handle_dcp_validation`: reject an explicit `fa3` (`--attention-backend` or `--decode-attention-backend`) with `dcp_size > 1` on MLA models, naming DCP-aware alternatives. Prefill-only disaggregation workers are exempt — they never run the DCP decode path. - `_get_default_attn_backend`: Hopper MLA under DCP defaults to `flashinfer` instead of `fa3`, matching the Blackwell branch. No working configuration changes behavior: the rejected combination previously crashed at capture, and the default change replaces a guaranteed crash with a backend that works. ## Verification - Reproduced on 4x H200 with Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (`tp=4 dcp=4`): the capture crash on the fa3 auto-default, and a clean start on `flashinfer`. - **Unit tests** (`TestDcpAttentionBackend`): verified red on pre-fix code, green post-fix. Negative branches pin that prefill-only workers and MHA models still accept fa3, and that the non-DCP Hopper MLA default stays `fa3`. - `pre-commit run` passes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [ ] Update documentation as needed. - [x] Provide verification results. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194002702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194002702)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194002504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194002504)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Add configurable decode interval after prefill
signal.text: [by Codex] ## Motivation With DP attention, each rank schedules attention work locally while all ranks still participate in the same MoE collective. A rank with repeated chunked-prefill continuation work can therefore keep winning SGLang's prefill-first scheduling decision and starve decode work on peer ranks. In the AgentX workload this left requests waiting while the actual decode batch remained small. The DP-attention MLP-sync all-gather already exposes whether any rank selected an EXTEND batch. Use that globally synchronized signal to enforce a rank-consistent decode interval after prefill. ## Modifications - Add `--prefill-decode-interval N`, defaulting to `0` (disabled, so existing behavior is unchanged). - After an EXTEND batch, defer new prefill scheduling for the next `N` scheduler rounds so the running batch can decode. - Under DP attention, arm the interval from the existing globally synchronized `is_extend_in_batch` flag. Under non-DP scheduling, use the local forward mode. - Validate non-negative values and add focused scheduler/server-argument unit tests. No AIPerf source change is required. The benchmark prototype used the existing per-session routing behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes batch selection cadence only; it does not change model math or sampling. - Added unit coverage for disabled, non-DP, globally synchronized DP, and decode/non-rearm behavior. - Added server-argument validation coverage. - `python -m py_compile` passed for all modified Python/test files. - The focused pytest command could not collect on the development VM because its base Python environment does not include `torch`/`numpy`; the new tests are registered in `base-a-test-cpu`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The equivalent scheduler prototype was evaluated with full 3,600-second DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 AgentX runs on 8x B200 using TP8/DP8/EP8, DP attention, MTP3, and an interval of 16: | Concurrency | Interactivity (tok/s/user) | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) | Cache hit | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 56 | 30.75532 | 23,559.05865 | 95.945% | | 84 | 23.24221 | 26,110.24296 | 94.703% | The c84 run completed 7,096 profiled requests with zero request errors. These results validate the equivalent prototype on SGLang v0.5.17; this PR ports the behavior onto current `main` using the existing global DP EXTEND flag. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32117588164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32117588164)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32117587921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32117587921)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Do Not Merge][BCG]Use piecewise cuda graphs
signal.text: ## Motivation Inspired by SGLang's work on breaking graphs into piecewise CUDA graphs, we've built a small, standalone pure-Python package -- piecewise-cuda-graphs (https://github.com/meta-pytorch/piecewise-cuda-graphs). Our goal is to make it easily reusable across the PyTorch community, so that projects don't each have to maintain their own version. This PR swaps SGLang's in-tree piecewise CUDA graph code for the new PyTorch annex package. The behavior is identical in the context of SGLang. We'd love it if you could run your CI on this to see how it holds up in your setup. Whether or not it's a fit to merge is entirely your call -- we completely understand if you'd rather keep it in-tree, and no worries either way. Happy to iterate on anything, and thanks for taking a look! ## Modifications **Code (commit 1).** The `breakable` prefill backend's hand-maintained segmented-capture engine is replaced with the library, called directly at every site: | in-tree (removed) | `piecewise_cuda_graphs` | | --------------------------- | ----------------------- | | `BreakableCUDAGraph` | `CUDAGraphSequence` | | `BreakableCUDAGraphCapture` | `piecewise_graph` | | `eager_on_graph` | `no_graph` | | `break_graph` | `force_no_graph` | `piecewise-cuda-graphs==0.1.0` is added as a dependency. Backend name, config, and CLI flags are unchanged (still `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`). **Docs (commit 2).** Updates the Breakable CUDA Graph page for the new package. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3-8B scores **0.840** on mgsm_en with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=breakable` (the integration test threshold is 0.80) -- unchanged from the in-tree engine. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No regression from the swap. Benchmarked with `bench_one_batch` on H100, this branch vs. its parent (the in-tree engine), on identical shapes (input 512, output 8, batch 1/4/16) across five models: gpt-oss-120b, Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8 (tp8), Llama-3-70B-Instruct (tp4), Llama-3-8B-Instruct, and MiniMax-M2.7 (tp4). Every prefill delta -- the only path this swap touches -- is within **+/-1.6%** and mixed in sign. Decode runs on the unchanged `full` backend. Repeating a fixed config on one build puts the harness's run-to-run variance at **~3% std**, which exceeds every prefill delta, so nothing here is distinguishable from noise. ## Limitation after rebase Rebasing onto main picked up four breakable features that `piecewise-cuda-graphs==0.1.0` cannot yet express: `barrier_fn` and `capture_stub` (both #31987), CUDA graph segment dedup (`SGLANG_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH_DEDUP`, default off), and XPU (#30273) all dropped here and intended as follow-ups on the package side. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32177332303](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32177332303)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32177331705](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32177331705)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec] Deduplicate the max_running_requests=48 default into one helper
signal.text: ## Motivation The identical five-line block that defaults `max_running_requests` to 48 (plus its warning) is copied verbatim into all five per-algorithm hooks in `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` (dflash, dspark, frozen-kv-mtp, eagle family, standalone). signal.title: [Spec] Route weight updates through the _draft_model_runners() guard
signal.text: ## Motivation `BaseSpecWorker.update_weights_from_disk` and `update_weights_from_ipc` iterate `self.draft_worker.draft_runners` directly. This dereference is unguarded: - **NGRAM** has no draft worker → `AttributeError` on any weight-update request while ngram speculation is enabled. - **DFlash family** exposes `model_runner` rather than `draft_runners`, so the current loop targets the wrong attribute there too. `BaseSpecWorker` already owns the correct abstraction for exactly this case: `_draft_model_runners()` returns `()` for ngram / frozen-kv-mtp / absent draft worker and maps the dflash family to its `model_runner`. ## Modifications Both update paths now iterate `self._draft_model_runners()` instead of `self.draft_worker.draft_runners` (2-line change, no new code paths): - ngram / frozen-kv-mtp: weight updates no longer crash; they correctly no-op over zero draft runners and return success. - dflash: the update reaches the actual draft `model_runner`. ## Accuracy Tests No model-forward changes; behavior is identical for the EAGLE family (where `_draft_model_runners()` returns exactly `draft_worker.draft_runners`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable (control-path only, executed once per weight-update request). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with `pre-commit run --all-files` - [x] Two-line change reusing an existing guard; no new dependencies 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_015bz4X1Dc9F6SQoV26ribYP <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32195486495](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195486495)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32195486153](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32195486153)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for multi-item scoring
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces a multi-item scoring feature for the `/v1/score` endpoint via the new server argument `--multi-item-scoring-delimiter`. The feature allows batching a single query with multiple items into one forward pass by concatenating them with a user-specified delimiter token. This avoids multiple independent inference calls, substantially improving throughput when evaluating many query–item pairs. The change is especially beneficial for scoring tasks (e.g., reward modeling, classification, or multiple-choice evaluation) where a single query is paired with a list of candidates. ## Modifications - Added `--multi-item-scoring-delimiter` (type `int`) to the server arguments. - The specified token ID is used to separate the query from items and items from each other in the constructed input sequence. - Enforces that `--disable-radix-cache` and `--chunked-prefill-size -1` are set when the delimiter is used (otherwise the server raises an error). - Extended `/v1/score` handling to accept either text strings or pre-tokenized integer lists for `query` and `items`. - Modified the tokenizer manager and scheduler output processor to: - Build a single sequence: `query + <delimiter> + item1 + <delimiter> + item2 + <delimiter> ... + itemN + <delimiter>`. - Extract logprobs only at the delimiter positions that correspond to the end of each item. - Return scores for each label token ID specified in `label_token_ids`. - Added comprehensive unit tests for Ascend NPU CI (`test_npu_multi_item_scoring_softmax.py`): - `test_softmax_true_text_input`: validates `apply_softmax=True` produces proper normalized probabilities and correct semantic ordering. - `test_softmax_false_tokenized_input`: validates `apply_softmax=False` returns raw scores in `[0, 1]` and confirms difference from softmax output. - `test_item_first_flag`: verifies that the `item_first` parameter is ignored (as expected) in multi-item scoring mode. ## Accuracy Tests All tests pass on NPU (Ascend) hardware using the Qwen3-32B model. The correctness of softmax normalization and semantic ordering is verified with a simple arithmetic reasoning task ("1 plus 2 equals 3"). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable for this PR (the feature is an API enhancement that reduces the number of forward passes from N to 1, which inherently improves throughput; exact speedups depend on batch size and model size). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(Documentation update will follow in a separate PR)* - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [Test] Tighten the DCP HiCache KL threshold to 0.005
signal.text: ## Motivation `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` (Kimi Linear + DCP4 + HiCache L2 + UnifiedRadixCache) has gated at `kl_threshold = 0.01` since it landed in #33112. Every other fp8 hybrid cache-hit KL case in the same directory gates at 0.005: | case | threshold | | --- | --- | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_mamba.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_cp.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dsv4.py` | 0.005 | | `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py` | **0.01** | A looser threshold tolerates float noise and small state bugs alike, and the thing this case exists to catch — a missing DCP logical→physical translation handing back another rank's KV on a cache hit — is exactly what slack hides. This PR tries the house value so the DCP translation path is held to the same bar as the non-DCP ones. This is an experiment: the point is to find out whether the DCP path actually holds at 0.005 in CI. If it flakes, the measured headroom tells us either to keep 0.01 with a comment recording why (the way the mamba case documents its own 0.003 → 0.005 bump) or that there is real divergence worth chasing. ## Modifications One line: `kl_threshold` 0.01 → 0.005 in `test/registered/radix_cache/unified_radix_tree/test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`. No source changes. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output changes. The case is registered as `stage="extra-b"`, `runner_config="4-gpu-b200"`, so it needs the extra CI stage to actually exercise the new threshold. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A — test threshold only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32183451677](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183451677)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32183451328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183451328)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
