signal.title: [Bugfix] Kimi-K3: fix vision-DP rank-local indexing into global grid_thws_host
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving Kimi-K3 with vision-DP sharding (observed on `--tp-size 8 --dcp-size 8` with DSPARK speculative decoding, image `nightly-dev-cu13-20260817-d91c3682`), the first `/v1/chat/completions` request that carries **two or more images with different geometries** kills the scheduler: ``` ValueError: Kimi-K3 deferred GPU preprocessing produced wrong grids ``` The request returns 500 and the server never recovers — every subsequent request fails until the container is restarted. Single-image requests, and multi-image requests whose images share one NaViT grid, are unaffected — which is how this survives typical smoke tests. ## Root cause In `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py`, `materialize_item_features(image_indices)` receives the **global** image indices assigned to this vision-DP rank, but the deferred-preprocessing block indexes `grid_thws_host` — a global tensor with one row per image in the batch — with the rank-**local** enumerate positions: ```python expected_grids = grid_thws_host[indices] # local idx into global tensor ... patch_counts = [int(grid_thws_host[index].prod().item()) for index in indices] # same bug ``` On any rank whose assigned images are not the global prefix `[0..k)`, the expected grids and patch split counts are read from the wrong rows. If the wrongly-read row happens to hold a different grid, the `torch.equal` sanity check fires and raises, taking the scheduler down. (The non-DP path passes `list(range(len(items)))`, where local == global, so it never triggers.) ## Fix Translate the local enumerate positions through the closure's `image_indices` before indexing `grid_thws_host`, in both the expected-grid comparison and the `patch_counts` split. No numeric effect on correct batches — the check now compares each produced grid against the row it was actually produced from. ## Accuracy Tests Deterministic repro: one chat completion with two images, 504×504 and 1344×756 (different NaViT grids), against a TP8/DCP8 B300 deployment. - **Before:** request returns 500, scheduler dead (`/health` times out until restart) — reproduced 2/2. - **After:** request returns 200 (14.8s cold) with a correct description of both images; `/health` stays 200; subsequent multimodal and text traffic unaffected. Model outputs for previously-working requests are unchanged: the patch only affects index bookkeeping inside a validation check, not any computed feature. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — two list-indexing expressions inside the deferred-preprocessing validation branch; no hot-path change. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (black/codespell clean; ruff `F401,F821,UP037` and isort report zero *new* findings vs the base revision of this file) - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (A unit test for this path needs multi-GPU vision-DP; validated with the deterministic E2E repro above. Happy to add a mocked test if maintainers prefer.) - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (n/a) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194807740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194807740)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194807547](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194807547)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Realtime ASR: bounded long audio with encoder-window caching
signal.text: ## Summary This PR adds an experimental, opt-in realtime ASR path for long audio items. It bounds the acoustic work submitted by each update, reuses completed audio encoder windows through SGLang's existing multimodal cache, and publishes decoder progress through the existing append-only transcription delta event. The current realtime path re-submits all audio accumulated for an item every 2 seconds. This preserves full acoustic context, but both prefill and memory grow with the session. On long items, per-update latency eventually dominates realtime playback. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, the opt-in path works as follows: 1. Keep the existing cumulative path through the first 60 seconds. 2. On the first update after 60 seconds, establish a one-way handoff from the cumulative transcript to encoder-window continuation. 3. Keep at most eight complete model-native 8-second audio windows plus the current incomplete tail in each later request. 4. Reuse complete-window embeddings through the existing MM cache; always recompute the mutable tail. 5. Carry older semantic context in a bounded, confirmed transcript prefix and generate only the new suffix. 6. Stream decoder progress through the existing `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` event. No client schema or new event type is added. The default remains `cumulative`. Encoder windowing is currently enabled only for an explicitly declared English session on a local single-GPU runtime. Unsupported models, languages, and topologies keep the cumulative path and its 60-second safety boundary. ## Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Client appends PCM] --> B[2-second inference boundary] B --> C{Received audio over 60 seconds?} C -- No --> D[Submit audio from 0 to current end] D --> E[Cumulative transcript reconciliation] C -- Yes, first handoff --> F[Submit full audio once] F --> G[Create bounded confirmed-text prefix] C -- Yes, steady state --> H[Choose 8-second-aligned rolling range] G --> H H --> I[Up to 8 complete windows plus mutable tail] I --> J[Complete windows: existing MM embedding cache] I --> K[Mutable tail: encode, do not retain] J --> L[Decoder prefix plus new suffix generation] K --> L E --> M[Reconcile decoder updates] L --> M M --> N[Emit only append-safe delta text] N --> O[Existing transcription.delta event] O --> P[Advance absolute PCM cursors and compact old audio] ``` The first windowed request intentionally includes the full handoff audio. Once the handoff succeeds, steady-state requests retain no more than 64 seconds of complete encoder windows plus an incomplete tail shorter than 8 seconds. For example, a steady-state request near 130 seconds looks like this: ```text Older audio represented by confirmed text | v text: [bounded decoder prefix] audio: [w0][w1] ... [w7][tail] encoder: [cache hits / misses][encode] decoder: [prefix] + [rolling acoustic context] -> new suffix only wire: -> append-only stable deltas ``` ## Encoder-window reuse Qwen3-ASR declares its independent encoder geometry in the multimodal processor. For Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one complete window is 8 seconds and produces 104 encoder tokens. The generic audio-window builder: - extracts complete windows independently from the mutable tail; - expands one audio placeholder into per-window token ranges; - hashes the exact feature, attention mask, modality, and token geometry; - marks complete windows as cacheable; - marks the mutable tail `use_embedding_cache=False`; and - provides an explicit encoder batch key for variable-width audio features. A cache miss or eviction simply re-encodes the window. Cache reuse is therefore a performance optimization, not persistent session state and not a correctness dependency. The cache is model-owned only through declarative capability data: ```text Transcription adapter -> activation threshold, language gate, text-prefix limits Multimodal processor -> independently encodable window geometry Generic audio-window builder -> feature extraction, MM items, identity, cacheability Existing MM scheduler/cache -> lookup, miss batching, embedding assembly ``` There is no ASR-specific scheduler session, cache service, GPU lease, or model forward API. ## Append-only decoder streaming Each backend ASR request now uses `stream=True` when the realtime endpoint provides a callback. Partial decoder text is stripped of model-specific output markers, reconciled against cumulative or windowed transcript state, and sent only when it extends the text already published for that request. This is decoder-token-driven stable delta streaming, not a guarantee of one WebSocket event per tokenizer token. Local Agreement and suffix holdback may release several tokens together. If a completed decode revises a prefix that was already emitted, the request fails closed rather than sending a conflicting append-only transcript. No client changes are required. The wire protocol remains: ```text conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed ``` ## Enablement ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B \ --asr-long-audio-strategy encoder_window \ --asr-max-buffer-seconds 1800 ``` The client uses the existing realtime transcription session format and must declare a supported language before sending audio: ```json { "type": "session.update", "session": { "audio": { "input": { "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 16000}, "transcription": { "model": "qwen3-asr", "language": "en" }, "noise_reduction": null, "turn_detection": null } } } } ``` `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` is the total accepted duration of one client item. Resident PCM is independently compacted after the encoder-window handoff. ## Alternatives evaluated Before selecting this implementation, four approaches were run under the same controlled setup: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B, one RTX 4090, Triton attention, identical native audio, 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, and 2-second flood-mode appends. Processing time is measured from the first send to the completed event; it measures server work rather than realtime playback. "Word error" is the normalized edit distance from the published reference; lower is better. | Approach | Long-audio behavior | Result | Decision | |---|---|---|---| | Cumulative | Re-submit all received audio every 2 seconds | 178.5 seconds of audio took 153.240 seconds; 291.1 seconds did not finish within 300 seconds | Keep as the unchanged default for normal items | | PCM tail slicing | Submit a bounded PCM tail plus 2-second overlap | 178.5 seconds took 109.735 seconds with 39.81% word error; longer cases did not finish | Rejected: bounded audio alone did not bound decoder-prefix work or preserve quality | | Encoder-aligned rolling context | Reuse complete windows and continue from confirmed text | Completed 291/593/908/1687-second inputs in 16.947/31.721/51.097/90.195 seconds | Selected: fastest completed long-stream approach and no client protocol change | | Independent segment finals | Finalize disjoint segments without a cross-segment prefix | Completed the same inputs in 18.804/35.343/55.127/98.233 seconds | Not selected: slower and requires replaceable snapshot semantics | The long-input comparison was: | Input | Cumulative | PCM slicing | Encoder windows | Independent segments | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | LongLibriHeavy 178.5 s | 153.240 s, 12.04% error | 109.735 s, 39.81% | 9.911 s, 11.30% | 11.586 s, 11.30% | | TED Al Gore 291.1 s | >300 s, incomplete | >300 s, incomplete | 16.947 s, 3.87% | 18.804 s, 4.66% | | LongLibriHeavy 592.6 s | >405 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 31.721 s, 7.95% | 35.343 s, 7.74% | | TED Craig Venter 907.8 s | >405 s, incomplete | >405 s, incomplete | 51.097 s, 4.50% | 55.127 s, 4.75% | | Earnings22 EXCOF 1686.7 s | >397 s, incomplete | >397 s, incomplete | 90.195 s, 12.80% | 98.233 s, 10.55% | ## Current-head GPU validation Environment: - Commit: `135eb6cf66` - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090, 24,564 MiB - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B`, snapshot `5eb144179a02acc5e5ba31e748d22b0cf3e303b0` - Attention backend: Triton - Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.8.1 - 16 kHz mono PCM16 WebSocket input, 2-second appends - `--mem-fraction-static 0.75`, 100 MiB MM cache, 1800-second item cap All reported accuracy and performance cases below are complete, unmodified published source rows or source files. No reported audio was concatenated, cropped, padded, or silence-extended. For every successful WebSocket case: ```text concatenate(all transcription.delta text) == completed transcript snapshot events == 0 ``` Selected native-audio results on the current head: | Input | Duration | Server processing time | Reference word error | Result vs pre-streaming encoder-window path | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | Qwen English demo | 15.1 s | 0.814 s | no published reference | Byte-identical | | LongLibriHeavy | 75.0 s | 4.245 s | 11.02% | Same normalized output and error rate | | LongLibriHeavy | 93.4 s | 4.899 s; fresh rerun 5.222 s | 7.98%; rerun 7.45% | One-word first-run variation; rerun matched baseline | | TED Al Gore | 291.1 s | 16.837 s | 3.87% | Normalized-exact | | TED Barry Schwartz | 1104.6 s | 58.373 s; rerun 58.485 s | 2.39% both runs | Normalized-exact, full opening and ending | | Earnings22 EXCOF | 1686.7 s | 88.901 s; rerun 88.367 s | 12.80% both runs | Full opening and ending; 0.20-0.22% run-to-run text variation | The 28-minute Earnings22 run issued 844 backend requests. Of 888,608 prompt tokens, 511,624 were cache hits (57.6%); uncached prompt work was 376,984 tokens. The server remained healthy after every request. ### Paced streaming receipt The 15.05-second Qwen demo was also sent at realtime pace instead of flood mode: - 8 backend ASR requests; - 37 existing `transcription.delta` events; - 0 snapshot events; - the joined deltas were byte-identical to the completed transcript; and - the first six deltas arrived between 2.171 and 2.208 seconds after the run began, while 4 seconds of audio had been sent. This confirms that output is emitted while one backend decode is still running, while preserving the endpoint's append-only transcript contract. ## Public audio sources - Qwen English demo: <https://qianwen-res.oss-cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/Qwen3-ASR-Repo/asr_en.wav> - LongLibriHeavy: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/inesc-id/longlibriheavy> - TED-LIUM long form: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/tedlium-long-form> - Earnings22: <https://huggingface.co/datasets/distil-whisper/earnings22> The benchmark manifest records dataset revisions, row ids, decoded-audio SHA256, wire-PCM SHA256, duration, sample rate, and reference text. Every result reported above uses one native source row or source file without local audio construction. ## Implementation | Area | Responsibility | |---|---| | `realtime/asr_processor.py` | Selects cumulative/windowed requests, reconciles decoder updates, advances absolute cursors, and compacts PCM | | `realtime/audio_buffer.py` | Maintains the per-item absolute PCM timeline | | `realtime/decoder_suffix.py` | Reconciles bounded decoder-prefix continuations without fuzzy deletion | | `realtime/session.py` | Owns WebSocket lifecycle and emits existing append-only events | | `streaming_asr.py` | Runs backend streaming generation and model-specific partial-output processing | | Transcription adapter | Declares activation, supported languages, decoder-prefix limits, and streaming postprocessing | | `audio_encoder_windowing.py` | Builds complete-window and mutable-tail multimodal items | | Base/Qwen multimodal processors | Provide generic construction plus model-config-derived window geometry | | `MultimodalDataItem` / `mm_schedule.py` | Support opt-in cacheability and producer-declared compatible miss batching | | `server_args.py` | Adds the off-by-default `encoder_window` strategy | ## Validation ```text 37 focused CPU tests passed 20 parameterized subtests passed py_compile passed git diff --check passed Ruff format check passed PR-file pre-commit hooks passed (black-jupyter skipped; no notebooks changed) GPU: 15-1687-second unmodified native-audio regression complete TED-LIUM and Earnings22 long-form recordings 1105- and 1687-second long-form reruns realtime-paced decoder-streaming trace ``` ## Limits - Encoder windowing is experimental, off by default, English-only for Qwen3-ASR, and currently limited to a local single-GPU runtime. - Operators must raise `--asr-max-buffer-seconds` above 60 seconds for the strategy to activate. - Stable deltas are driven by backend token streaming, but Local Agreement may group tokens. This is not raw one-event-per-token passthrough. - `finish_reason=length`, irreconcilable streamed-prefix revisions, and unsafe no-word-boundary continuation fail closed. - No timestamps, forced aligner, model-native streaming state, distributed encoder cache, or scheduler-owned ASR session is introduced. - Validation is bounded to Qwen3-ASR-0.6B on one RTX 4090 and does not establish universal multilingual quality or production capacity. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32194510888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194510888)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32194510769](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32194510769)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sglang-miles] RDT/NIXL weight sync support for Ray scheduler actors
signal.text: ## What sglang-side support for **RDT (Ray Direct Transport / NIXL) weight sync** — lets the [miles](https://github.com/radixark/miles) trainer push RL weights to rollout engines via a zero-copy RDMA pull instead of NCCL broadcast. Paired with the miles-side PR (radixark/miles#1313), which has the perf write-up. ## Changes - **`ray/scheduler_actor.py`** — add `pull_weights()`, which uses `ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref` to RDMA pre-sharded weight buckets directly into the model's `param.data` buffers (no intermediate receive buffers / copies). - **`ray/engine.py` + `ray/data_parallel_controller.py`** — register `SchedulerActor`s as **detached** named actors with the http **port** baked into the name, so the trainer (a different Ray job) can discover them via `list_named_actors` even when several engines share a node; raise `max_concurrency` so a concurrent `pull_weights` is not starved while `run_event_loop` blocks; set `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1` so the absolute GPU id from `get_accelerator_ids()` stays valid. - **`server_args.py`** — add `enable_engine_info_bootstrap` to start the engine-info bootstrap server and register per-rank parallelism config **without** the mooncake/verbs P2P transfer-engine seeding. - **`entrypoints/engine.py` + `model_executor/model_runner.py`** — honor `enable_engine_info_bootstrap`; make the P2P transfer-engine memory registration non-fatal so EFA/verbs clusters where it fails don't crash the scheduler (RDT only needs the parallelism config). - **`model_loader/loader.py`** — make `post_load_weights` public so the RDT path can invoke it. - **`pyproject.toml`** — require `ray>=2.55.1` (`ray.experimental.set_target_for_ref`). ## Notes Targeting the `sglang-miles` integration branch; rebased onto current `sglang-miles` (#28001, #29339). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32193574872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32193574872)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32193574518](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32193574518)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [ray] expose get_scheduler_actor_name so callers can look up the schedulers
signal.text: ## Motivation `RayEngine` names each `SchedulerActor`, but the name format is inlined in `_create_scheduler_actor`. A process outside the engine that wants handles to those schedulers — e.g. an RL trainer that supplied the placement group and wants to push weights straight into the scheduler actors — has no supported way to address them, and ends up scanning `ray.util.list_named_actors()` for substring matches. ## Modifications - Extract the name format into `get_scheduler_actor_name(*, rank0_node_ip, dp_rank, pp_rank, tp_rank, port, bundle_idx)` and call it from `_create_scheduler_actor`. - Re-export it from `sglang.srt.ray`. - Key the name by the engine's http port instead of `_pg{hex}`. The placement-group id is only knowable inside `RayEngine`, so an external caller cannot reproduce it; the port is assigned per host, so `(node ip, port)` uniquely identifies an engine and keeps engines co-located on one node distinct. With this, a caller that knows the node ip, ranks, port and bundle indices it handed to `RayEngine` can rebuild the name and `ray.get_actor()` directly. Note this does change the actor names `RayEngine` produces (`_pg{hex}` → `_port{port}`). Nothing in-tree reads the names — `_create_scheduler_actor` was the only place the format appeared. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code - [x] No new dependencies <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31641744701](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31641744701)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31641744995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31641744995)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(cake_gemm): add Cake batch DeepGEMM FP8 backend
signal.text: ## Real-weight inference validation Model: [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324) using all 163 real safetensors shards with native FP8 weights. Both runs used 4x NVIDIA GB300, TP4/EP4, the same server configuration, and the same deterministic inputs. ### Accuracy parity Here, accuracy means backend numerical/decoding parity, not a downstream model-quality benchmark such as MMLU. Token exact match is `matching generated token IDs / 48`; sequence exact match requires every generated token in a prompt to match. | Check | FlashInfer/DeepGEMM reference | Cake | Result | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Greedy prompts | 3 | 3 | same inputs | | Generated tokens per prompt | 16 | 16 | 48 tokens compared | | Token exact-match accuracy | 48 | 48 | **48/48 = 100%** | | Sequence exact-match accuracy | 3 | 3 | **3/3 = 100%** | | Finish reasons | 3 | 3 | **3/3 exact** | | Non-finite output logprobs | 0 | 0 | **pass** | | Maximum output-token logprob absolute difference | — | — | **0.0** | ### Steady-state SGLang E2E SGLang's serving benchmark used 64 requests per round, exact 16-token inputs and 128-token outputs, concurrency 8, request rate `inf`, seed 42, and three rounds per backend. A separate 16-request x 32-output-token warmup ran first. Model loading, server startup, JIT compilation, and warmup are excluded; the reported metric is steady-state end-to-end request wall clock. The harness invoked `sglang.benchmark.serving.run_benchmark` directly. This is the CLI-equivalent command sequence used once against the reference server and once against the Cake server; the measured loop runs three rounds: ```bash python - <<'PY' import json from pathlib import Path rows = [ { "conversations": [ {"value": f"Deterministic serving benchmark prompt number {i} for real weight inference."}, {"value": "Deterministic benchmark response."}, ] } for i in range(128) ] Path("random-corpus.json").write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n") PY BENCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:31000 # reference; use :32000 for Cake CORPUS_PATH=./random-corpus.json # fixed 128-row deterministic corpus COMMON_ARGS=( --backend sglang --base-url "$BENCH_URL" --dataset-name random --dataset-path "$CORPUS_PATH" --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 --random-input-len 16 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 8 --seed 42 --disable-tqdm ) # Excluded warmup. curl -fsS -X POST "$BENCH_URL/flush_cache" python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --num-prompts 16 --random-output-len 32 # Three measured rounds. run_benchmark performs its own one-request warmup # before its benchmark_start_time; the explicit cache flush is also outside it. for BENCH_ROUND in 0 1 2; do curl -fsS -X POST "$BENCH_URL/flush_cache" python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" --num-prompts 64 --random-output-len 128 done ``` | Round | Reference duration (s) | Cake duration (s) | Reference output tok/s | Cake output tok/s | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 0 | 378.054856 | 204.302219 | 21.668813 | 40.097460 | **1.850469x** | | 1 | 377.507678 | 202.967479 | 21.700221 | 40.361146 | **1.859942x** | | 2 | 372.968888 | 205.485857 | 21.964299 | 39.866491 | **1.815059x** | | Three-round median metric | Reference | Cake | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Duration | 377.507678 s | 204.302219 s | **1.847790x** | | Output throughput | 21.700221 tok/s | 40.097460 tok/s | **1.847790x** | | Total throughput | 24.412748 tok/s | 45.109642 tok/s | **1.847790x** | | Mean E2E latency | 47,185.254 ms | 25,534.840 ms | **1.847877x** | | Median E2E latency | 47,198.526 ms | 25,529.890 ms | **1.848756x** | | Mean TTFT | 1,112.430 ms | 592.937 ms | **1.876137x** | | Median TTFT | 1,028.638 ms | 546.565 ms | **1.882004x** | | Mean TPOT | 362.778 ms | 196.393 ms | **1.847206x** | | Median TPOT | 363.052 ms | 196.489 ms | **1.847700x** | Reference output-throughput CV: `0.745%`. Cake output-throughput CV: `0.617%`.

signal.title: [HiSparse] Fix inflated full token usage for DeepSeek V4
signal.text: ## Motivation When HiSparse is enabled for DeepSeek V4, an empty KV cache can report a high `full token usage` immediately after startup. For example, with the following pool sizes: - Full logical capacity: 5,445,376 tokens - C4 device capacity: 272,268 compressed tokens - Compression ratio: 4 The previous implementation calculated available full-token capacity as: ```python min(logical_available, device_available * compress_ratio) ``` This limited the reported capacity to 1,089,072 tokens and caused an empty logical pool to appear approximately 80% occupied. after: before: --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32112853651](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32112853651) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32112853286](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32112853286)

signal.title: [Fix] Stop unparsed Kimi K3 template syntax from leaking into responses
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi K3 emits its channels (`<|open|>tools<|sep|>`, `<|open|>call ...`, `<|close|>message<|sep|>`, ...) as literal text, so any path that does not run the tool-call parser hands that syntax straight to the client. Two such paths exist today: - **Parsing disabled.** With `tool_choice="none"` or no tools, `serving_chat` / `serving_responses` skip the parser and `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream` returns `full_text` verbatim. Measured on a K3 deployment: ~10% of `tool_choice="none"` completions came back containing a raw tools section. - **Truncation.** `KimiK3Detector.has_tool_call` is `self.bot_token in text`, so output cut mid-marker (`...<|open|>too`) misses detection and `parse_non_stream` again returns the raw text. With small `max_output_tokens` this reproduced in 97-100% of samples. Separately, `ResponsesRequest._normalize_input_item_for_validation` defaults the SDK-required `input_image.detail` only under `item["content"]`. Tool-output items carry their parts under `item["output"]`, so an image tool result without `detail` (what Codex sends) fails validation with a 400. ## Modifications - `base_format_detector.py`: two identity-by-default hooks, `strip_template_artifacts(text, reasoning_separated)` and `strip_template_markers(text)`. Formats whose tool channel is literal text override them; every other detector is unaffected. - `kimik3_detector.py`: implements both. Artifact stripping cuts from an unparsed `TOOLS_OPEN` / `CALL_OPEN` onward, drops the think channel when a reasoning parser already routed the trace to its own field, unwraps the response channel, and removes whole and cut-off markers. Marker stripping only removes syntax, keeping the text it wrapped — used for reasoning content. - `kimik3_format.py`: `ALL_MARKERS`, `ARGUMENT_OPEN`, and a `min_len` on `partial_suffix_len` so a reply legitimately ending in `<` is not truncated. - `function_call_parser.py`: the two paths that returned `full_text` unchanged (no tools, detection missed) now route it through `strip_template_artifacts`. - `serving_chat.py` / `serving_responses.py`: apply the hooks to non-streaming assistant text and reasoning content, regardless of whether parsing ran. A Responses turn whose text was nothing but syntax still emits an `output_text` item (empty) rather than an output array with no message. - `utils.py`: `align_token_logprobs_to_text`. The cleanup is pure span deletion, so the cleaned text is a subsequence of the concatenated tokens; entries whose token was removed are dropped, and the array becomes `None` if the two cannot be reconciled rather than being returned misaligned. Applied only when cleanup actually changed the text, so logprobs on paths this PR does not touch are unchanged. - `protocol.py`: normalize `input_image.detail` under `output` as well as `content`. Streaming is out of scope: the chunk handlers can still emit markers verbatim, and fixing that needs cross-chunk marker buffering. ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward or kernels — this only affects post-generation text handling in the OpenAI entrypoints. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A; the added work is a few regex passes over the response text. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191148180](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191148180)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191147947](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191147947)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(constrained): reject NUL bytes in grammar specs to stop an xgrammar segfault
signal.text: ## Motivation A single `POST /v1/chat/completions` whose `regex` begins with a NUL byte kills the whole server. xgrammar's regex converter appends its own NUL terminator and indexes past it, raising **SIGSEGV** rather than an exception — and a signal is below the interpreter, so the `except RuntimeError` in `dispatch_regex` cannot catch it. The scheduler dies with `exit code -11` and every later request from every client is refused until restart. ```python python3 -c 'import xgrammar; xgrammar.Grammar.from_regex(chr(0))' # SIGSEGV ``` Two details, both measured: - The trigger is a **leading** NUL, not control characters generally — `\x01`, `\x02`, `\x1f` and a non-leading NUL all compile fine. So the guard is scoped to NUL; rejecting all control characters would break valid patterns like `[\t\n]+`. - A **JSON schema reaches the same converter via `pattern`**, at any depth, where the NUL can be written as the escape `\u0000` — no NUL byte in the request body at all. Guarding only the raw `regex` field leaves that path live. No version bump helps: every xgrammar wheel installable on aarch64 (0.2.0–0.2.4) segfaults identically, 0.2.5 has no aarch64 wheel, and xgrammar has no fix upstream. ## Modifications - `base_grammar_backend.py`: add `_grammar_key_contains_nul()` and call it at the top of `_init_value_dispatch`, returning `InvalidGrammarObject` on a hit. For `json` / `structural_tag` the spec is decoded and walked, so an escaped `\u0000` in a nested `pattern` is caught too; malformed JSON falls through to the backend's own error. Placed at the dispatcher, not in `xgrammar_backend.py`, because the JSON path reaches the same native code and a segfault cannot be caught after the fact. - `test_base_grammar_backend.py`: `TestNulByteGrammarRejection` — NUL specs are rejected without the backend being called (`regex` and JSON `pattern`, raw and escaped, plus a non-leading `a\x00b` so the guard can't be narrowed to `startswith()`), and valid patterns, non-NUL control characters and malformed JSON still dispatch normally. A NUL has no meaning in a regex, schema or grammar, so no legitimate request is affected — the crash becomes the same clean error an invalid pattern already returns. Verified on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260811-d59c1ddf` (aarch64, GB200): the file passes **33 tests / 17 subtests** with no regressions; the new cases fail 8/8 without the guard; and on a live server the two crashing payloads go from killing the process to **HTTP 400**, with `/health` still 200 and no segfault markers. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — no change to kernels or the model forward path. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — one substring check per uncached grammar compilation (for JSON, a parse the backend already performs). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — N/A, no user-facing API change. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — N/A, see above. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190389520](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190389520)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190389395](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190389395)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: model_loader: only open the MTP-head shards for a NextN/MTP draft load
signal.text: ## Motivation An EAGLE/MTP **NextN draft** is loaded from the **same combined checkpoint** as the target, so `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` hands it **every shard in the safetensors index** — the whole checkpoint — even though the draft consumes only the appended NextN layer: - `embed_tokens` / `shared_head.head` are **shared from the already-resident target** (`deepseek_weight_loader` skips them: `if "shared_head.head" in name or "embed_tokens" in name: continue`), not read from disk; - every other tensor is skipped by the NextN weight loader (`if not name.startswith(layer_prefix): continue`) **after** the iterator has already opened the file. Net: a small draft head **re-opens the full multi-hundred-GB checkpoint** — wasted I/O, and a misleading full-checkpoint-size weight-load progress bar on the draft. On a real MTP model (`GlmMoeDsa*`-family, 78 layers + 1 NextN layer, FP4, EAGLE), the NextN head lives in **3 of 47 shards** but the draft opened all 47. ## Modifications Add `maybe_filter_nextn_shards` (weight_utils.py), called right next to `maybe_add_mtp_safetensors` in `DefaultModelLoader._get_weights_iterator`. For a **draft** config it restricts the shard list to just the shard(s) holding the MTP head. Deliberately conservative: - **Draft-only** — acts only when the architecture ends in `NextN` / `MTP`; **target loads are untouched**. - **Checkpoint-discovered MTP layer** — finds the MTP layer by the NextN-only modules it carries (`eh_proj` / `enorm` / `hnorm` / `shared_head`), **not** config arithmetic, since some archs rewrite `num_hidden_layers` (e.g. Longcat resets it to the nextn count). A wrong guess can **never drop needed weights**: no markers / no index / no reduction ⇒ the list is returned unchanged. - **Keeps index-undescribed files** — e.g. a separately-added `mtp.safetensors` (the `maybe_add_mtp_safetensors` path) is never dropped. Runs before the weights iterator is chosen, so it benefits every safetensors load path for NextN drafts. ## Accuracy Tests No output impact: the NextN draft loads the **identical** head weights — the same tensors the loader already kept. This change only avoids *opening* shards whose tensors the NextN loader already skips (target body / main-model layers), so the resulting model state is unchanged. Verified in production: the draft reaches ready and serves normally. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on a production MTP deployment (`GlmMoeDsa*` FP4, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE`, 8×B200, cold node), before vs after this change — **same target, same node class**: | Phase | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Target (`role=main`) load | 47.83 s | 47.79 s (unchanged) | | **Draft (`role=draft`) load** | **41.51 s** | **4.29 s** (**9.7× faster**) | | Draft shards opened | 47 / 47 | **3 / 47** | | Draft weight-load bar total | 433 GB | **23.4 GB** | The log confirms the narrowing: > `NextN draft load: restricting 47 checkpoint shard(s) to the 3 holding MTP layer(s) ['78'] (target body skipped).` The target load is unchanged (confirming the filter is draft-only); the draft speedup comes entirely from not re-reading the target body. The win scales with checkpoint size and node coldness. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit (pre-commit run passes: black / isort / ruff / codespell). - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_weight_utils.py::TestMaybeFilterNextnShards`): draft → MTP-only shards, target untouched, `num_hidden_layers`-rewrite safety, separately-added `mtp.safetensors` kept, no-marker / no-index no-ops. - [ ] Update documentation — n/a (internal loader optimization, no user-facing flags). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. --- *Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); validated in production as shown above.* <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191339576](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191339576)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191339452](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191339452)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat: add KV cache CPU backup for sleep/wakeup radix tree preservation
signal.text: Add --enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup flag that preserves the prefix cache radix tree across sleep/wakeup cycles. Changes: - server_args.py: new --enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup flag with validation - radix_cache.py: export_snapshot() and import_snapshot() methods (iterative DFS to avoid recursion limit on large trees) - scheduler_update_weights_mixin.py: snapshot before pause(), restore after resume(); pre-flight CPU memory check (hard reject at 1.2x safety margin, soft warning at 1.5x); graceful exit on insufficient memory via ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput(success=False, message=...) - memory_pool.py: enable_kv_cpu_backup param threaded through KVCache and all subclasses (MHA, MLA, NSA, DoubleSparse, HybridLinear, HiSparseNSA) - model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py: pass enable_kv_cpu_backup in all pool creation calls - io_struct.py: ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput gains success/message fields for graceful failure reporting - test/srt/test_kv_cache_cpu_backup.py: complete test suite (313 lines) ## Motivation During sleep/wakeup cycles (e.g., `release_memory_occupation` / `resume_memory_occupation` for weight updates like RLHF), the KV cache radix tree is flushed, causing prefix cache hits to be lost after wakeup. This forces full prefill for all subsequent requests, degrading performance. This PR adds `--enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup` which preserves the prefix cache radix tree across sleep/wakeup cycles by serializing it before `pause()` and restoring it after `resume()`, enabling prefix cache hits to work immediately after wakeup without re-prefill. ## Modifications ### Core feature - **`radix_cache.py`**: Added `export_snapshot()` (iterative DFS to avoid recursion limits on deep trees) and `import_snapshot()` methods for serializing/deserializing the radix tree topology and slot assignments. Comprehensive error handling with descriptive messages for node rebuild failures, topology wiring errors, and allocator free-list restoration failures. - **`scheduler_update_weights_mixin.py`**: On `release_memory_occupation`, snapshots the radix tree before `pause()`. On `resume_memory_occupation`, restores it after `resume()`. Also added a pre-flight CPU memory check: hard reject at 1.2x safety margin, soft warning at 1.5x, preventing `cudaMallocHost` OOM kills. - **`io_struct.py`**: `ReleaseMemoryOccupationReqOutput` gains `success: bool` and `message: str` fields for graceful failure reporting. - **`memory_pool.py`**: Threaded `enable_kv_cpu_backup` through `KVCache` base class and all subclasses (`MHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolFP4`, `MLATokenToKVPool`, `MLATokenToKVPoolFP4`, `NSATokenToKVPool`, `DoubleSparseTokenToKVPool`, `HybridLinearKVPool`, `HybridReqToTokenPool`). Each `_create_buffers()` passes `enable_cpu_backup=self.enable_kv_cpu_backup` to `memory_saver_adapter.region()`. - **`hisparse_memory_pool.py`**: `HiSparseNSATokenToKVPool` passes `enable_kv_cpu_backup` to parent. - **`model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py`**: Propagates `enable_kv_cpu_backup` to all KV pool creation calls across all cache backends. - **`server_args.py`**: Added `--enable-kv-cache-cpu-backup` flag with validation: requires `--enable-memory-saver` and is incompatible with `--disable-radix-cache`. - **Container-aware memory check**: `_get_container_available_memory_bytes()` reads cgroup v2/v1 memory limits first (correct for Docker/K8s), falling back to `psutil.virtual_memory().available` for non-containerized hosts. ### Tests - **`test/srt/test_kv_cache_cpu_backup.py`**: Complete test suite (313 lines) covering: - Unit tests: empty tree export, snapshot round-trip, prefix match after restore, allocator free-list update, disabled/empty snapshot handling. - Integration tests: basic sleep/wakeup correctness (output consistency, GPU memory drop/recovery), prefix cache restoration (cached_tokens > 0 after wakeup). ## Accuracy Tests - **Output consistency**: Verified that generation output before sleep matches output after wakeup across multiple cycles (TP=1 and TP=2). - **Prefix cache restoration**: Verified that `cached_tokens > 0` after wakeup, confirming the radix tree snapshot is correctly restored and prefix cache hits fire. - **Radix tree integrity**: Unit tests confirm `total_size()` and `match_prefix()` results are identical before/after snapshot round-trip. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Sleep/Wakeup Timing (Qwen3-32B, NVIDIA A100, TP=1) | Metric | First cycle | Subsequent cycles | |--------|------------|-------------------| | Sleep (KV only) | ~2.1s | ~0.9s | | Wakeup (KV only) | ~0.36s | ~0.35s | | Sleep (KV + Weight) | ~24s | ~9.5s | | Wakeup (KV + Weight) | ~3.85s | ~3.85s | ### Sleep/Wakeup Timing (Qwen3-32B, NVIDIA A100, TP=2) | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | Sleep (KV + Weight) | ~32.5s | | Wakeup (KV + Weight) | ~3.9s | ### Stability - 10× consecutive sleep/wakeup cycle test passed with no crashes, no memory leaks, and consistent generation output across all cycles. - Pre-flight memory check correctly rejects release requests when available CPU memory is below 1.2x the required pinned memory size, preventing process kills from `cudaMallocHost` failures - signal.title: [SM100] Fuse bias addition into fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm epilogue
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In FP8 blockwise linear layers the bias addition (output += bias) is currently a separate element-wise kernel launch after GEMM, which incurs extra global memory round-trip and kernel launch overhead on SM100 GPUs. Fusing bias into the CUTLASS epilogue eliminates this overhead. ## Modifications - **`sgl-kernel/csrc/gemm/fp8_blockwise_gemm_kernel.cu`**: Added `launch_sm100_fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_with_bias` template function that uses `ElementC = ElementD` (non-void) in the CUTLASS `CollectiveBuilder`, passes bias pointer with broadcast stride `(0, 1, 0)` along M dimension, and sets `alpha=1.0, beta=1.0` in epilogue arguments. Updated `sm100_fp8_blockwise_dispatch_shape` to dispatch to the bias-fused variant when bias is provided. Added explicit rejection of bias for SM90 and SM120+ code paths. - **`sgl-kernel/csrc/common_extension.cc`**: Extended `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm` op schema with optional `Tensor? bias=None` parameter. - **`sgl-kernel/include/sgl_kernel_ops.h`**: Updated C++ declaration accordingly. - **`sgl-kernel/python/sgl_kernel/gemm.py`:** Forwarded new `bias` kwarg through Python binding. - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`**: In `cutlass_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`, detect SM100 via device capability and pass bias into the fused path; non-SM100 GPUs fall back to the existing separate `output += bias`. - **`sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_blockwise_gemm.py`**: Added `_test_accuracy_once_with_bias` and parametrized `test_accuracy_with_bias` covering M ∈ {1,3,5,127,128,512,1024,4096}, N ∈ {128..14080}, K ∈ {512..16384}, both bf16 and fp16, gated by SM100 skip condition. ## Accuracy Tests Added `test_accuracy_with_bias` test comparing fused-bias output against reference (`baseline_scaled_mm` with bias) at `rtol=0.02, atol=1`. Test is gated to run only on SM100 GPUs via `@pytest.mark.skipif`. ## Speed Tests and Profiling running the following benchmark code using B200 gpu: ```python3 """Benchmark: SM100 FP8 blockwise GEMM with fused bias vs. separate bias-add. Compares two paths: - Fused: fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm(..., bias=bias) [epilogue alpha=1,beta=1] - Separate: out = fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm(...); out += bias [two kernel launches] Usage: python bench_bias_fusion.py """ import torch import triton from sgl_kernel import fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm def _is_sm100(): if not torch.cuda.is_available(): return False major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability() return major == 10 and minor in (0, 3) def cdiv(a, b): return -(a // -b) def scale_shape(shape, group_shape): return tuple(cdiv(shape[i], group_shape[i]) for i in range(len(group_shape))) @triton.testing.perf_report( triton.testing.Benchmark( x_names=["M"], x_vals=[256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384], x_log=True, line_arg="mode", line_vals=["fused", "separate"], line_names=["Fused (bias in epilogue)", "Separate (gemm + add)"], styles=[("green", "-"), ("red", "--")], ylabel="ms", plot_name="fp8_blockwise_gemm_bias_fusion", args={}, ) ) def benchmark(mode, M, N, K, out_dtype): fp8_info = torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn) fp8_max, fp8_min = fp8_info.max, fp8_info.min a_fp32 = (torch.rand(M, K, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda") - 0.5) * 2 * fp8_max a_fp8 = a_fp32.clamp(min=fp8_min, max=fp8_max).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) b_fp32 = (torch.rand(N, K, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda") - 0.5) * 2 * fp8_max b_fp8 = b_fp32.clamp(min=fp8_min, max=fp8_max).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).t() scale_a_group_shape = (1, 128) scale_b_group_shape = (128, 128) scale_a_shape = scale_shape(a_fp8.shape, scale_a_group_shape) scale_b_shape = scale_shape(b_fp8.shape, scale_b_group_shape) scale_a = torch.randn(scale_a_shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.001 scale_b = torch.randn(scale_b_shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.001 scale_a = scale_a.t().contiguous().t() scale_b = scale_b.t().contiguous().t() bias = torch.randn(N, device="cuda", dtype=out_dtype) * 0.01 # Warmup _ = fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm(a_fp8, b_fp8, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype) _ = fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm(a_fp8, b_fp8, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype, bias=bias) torch.cuda.synchronize() quantiles = [0.5, 0.2, 0.8] def run_fused(): return fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm( a_fp8, b_fp8, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype, bias=bias ) def run_separate(): out = fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm( a_fp8, b_fp8, scale_a, scale_b, out_dtype ) out += bias return out if mode == "fused": ms, min_ms, max_ms = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph( run_fused, quantiles=quantiles ) elif mode == "separate": ms, min_ms, max_ms = triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph( run_separate, quantiles=quantiles ) return ms * 1000, max_ms * 1000, min_ms * 1000 if __name__ == "__main__": if not _is_sm100(): print("SKIP: bias fusion is only supported on SM100/SM103 GPUs") exit(0) test_shapes = [ # (N, K, out_dtype) — representative DeepSeek-V3 MoE / Qwen FP8 shapes (7168, 7168, torch.bfloat16), (7168, 16384, torch.bfloat16), (16384, 7168, torch.float16), (14080, 16384, torch.bfloat16), # typical FFN dim (8192, 8192, torch.float16), ] for N, K, out_dtype in test_shapes: print(f"\n{'='*60}") print(f"N={N}, K={K}, dtype={'bf16' if out_dtype==torch.bfloat16 else 'fp16'}") print(f"{'='*60}") try: benchmark.run(print_data=True, N=N, K=K, out_dtype=out_dtype) except Exception as e: print(f" ERROR: {e}") print("\nBenchmark finished!") ``` here is the result: ```bash signal.title: [Bug Fix] Fix EAGLE draft worker overwriting global server_args for MLA models
signal.text: ## Summary Fix a bug where the EAGLE3 draft model's `ModelRunner` initialization overwrites shared `server_args` fields (`disable_chunked_prefix_cache`, `use_mla_backend`), causing `AssertionError` crashes on long-context requests for MLA models (e.g. Kimi-K2.5) with chunked prefix cache enabled. The draft model (non-MLA) runs `model_specific_adjustment()` which sets `disable_chunked_prefix_cache = True` and then overwrites `global_server_args.use_mla_backend = False`, corrupting the target model's configuration. Guard these operations with `if not self.is_draft_worker:`. Fixes #22682 ## Test plan - [x] Deploy Kimi-K2.5 + EAGLE3 (DPA, TP=8), send 4 concurrent 200K-token requests — previously crashes, now completes - [x] Verified no performance regression after the fix <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #26176984151](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26176984151)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #26176984022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26176984022)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [CI] Skip fast-fail for scheduled stages
signal.text: ## Summary - Skip the cross-job PR health fast-fail when a reusable test stage is invoked with `scheduled: true`. - Keep the existing skip behavior for explicit health-check bypasses, parallel dispatches, and run-all requests. ## Root cause Release Branch Cut invokes the nightly workflow through `workflow_dispatch`. The reusable stage therefore cannot rely on `github.event_name == 'schedule'`. Although the nightly workflow passes `scheduled: true`, `SKIP_PR_TEST_HEALTH_CHECK` previously ignored that input, so later nightly jobs could cascade fast-fail after an earlier failure. ## Impact Nightly and weekly stages using `inputs.scheduled` will continue running to collect all failures. Regular PR stages retain fast-fail behavior. ## Validation - Evaluated the workflow expression for regular PR, scheduled, explicit skip, parallel dispatch, and run-all inputs. - Ran `actionlint -ignore SC2086 .github/workflows/_pr-test-stage.yml`. - Ran repository pre-commit checks. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190496623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190496623)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190496419](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190496419)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: perf(sgl_kernel): migrate `moe_fused_gate` from AOT sgl-kernel to JIT
signal.text: ## Motivation ref: #17865. The `moe_fused_gate` kernel was previously compiled AOT and shipped inside the `sgl-kernel` wheel. This PR migrates it to the JIT path under `sglang.jit_kernel`, following the same pattern as the recent `cast` and `rmsnorm` migrations. Benefits: - Removes the AOT CUDA object from `sgl-kernel` (~4.6 MB wheel size reduction). - No Cutlass dependency — the `.cuh` file uses only native CUDA types, so it compiles cleanly through the lightweight TVM-FFI JIT path. - Identical runtime semantics: same sigmoid + bias-add + group-filter + top-k + renorm logic, same numerical results. ## Modifications **New files** | File | Description | |---|---| | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/moe/moe_fused_gate.cuh` | Self-contained CUDA header. Templated fast path for known configs (256/8, 256/16, 128/4, 128/8); dynamic fallback for arbitrary expert/group counts. | | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/moe_fused_gate.py` | Python JIT loader. Wraps `moe_fused_gate_detail::MoeFusedGateKernel::run` via TVM-FFI. | | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_moe_fused_gate.py` | Correctness tests (1 188 parametrized cases). | | `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_moe_fused_gate.py` | Latency benchmark vs. PyTorch reference. | **Modified files** | File | Change | |---|---| | `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py` | Replace `from sgl_kernel import moe_fused_gate` with `from sglang.jit_kernel.moe_fused_gate import moe_fused_gate`. Remove the now-unnecessary `torch.library.register_fake("sgl_kernel::moe_fused_gate")` stub. | ## Accuracy Tests The test compares JIT kernel output against a pure-PyTorch reference (`biased_grouped_topk_ref`) on identical inputs. Two properties are checked per test case: 1. **Expert indices** — per-row sort then exact integer match (selection order within a row is unspecified by the kernel). 2. **Weights** — `torch.allclose(rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-3)` (tolerance covers fp16/bf16 rounding). **Test matrix — 1 188 cases, all passed** | Axis | Values | |---|---| | `seq_length` | 1–9 (every value), 16, 128, 1024, 4096 | | MoE config `(E, G, topk_group, topk)` | (128,4,2,4) · (256,8,4,8) · (512,16,8,16) | | dtype | `float32`, `float16`, `bfloat16` | | `num_fused_shared_experts` | 0, 1, 2 | | `apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output` | `True`, `False` | ``` python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_moe_fused_gate.py 1188 passed (9.91 s) ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Environment**: NVIDIA H20, CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128 **Config**: DeepSeek V3 / R1 — `num_experts=256`, `num_expert_group=8`,`topk_group=4`,`topk=8`, `routed_scaling_factor=2.5`, `bfloat16` **Measurement**: `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`, median latency | seq\_length | PyTorch reference (μs) | JIT kernel (μs) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 000 | 97.9 | 16.6 | **5.9×** | | 2 000 | 156.1 | 20.9 | **7.5×** | | 4 000 | 264.9 | 27.6 | **9.6×** | | 8 000 | 485.6 | 40.7 | **11.9×** | | 16 000 | 925.8 | 64.8 | **14.3×** | | 32 000 | 1 807.8 | 120.3 | **15.0×** | | 64 000 | 3 599.2 | 225.6 | **16.0×** | The speedup grows with batch size because the PyTorch reference materialises several intermediate tensors (group scores, group masks, gathered weights), while the JIT kernel keeps all intermediate state in registers and completes the full routing pipeline in a single GPU pass. ## Checklist - [x] Format code — all 5 changed files pass `pre-commit run` (isort, ruff, black, clang-format, codespell). - [x] Add unit tests — `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_moe_fused_gate.py`, 1188 parametrized cases. - [x] Documentation — N/A, no new public API surface. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmark results — see sections above. - [x] Code style

signal.title: [Kernel] Tune Kimi-K3 Marlin MoE block sizes on H200
signal.text: ## Summary Tune the Marlin MoE `BLOCK_SIZE_M` selector for the documented Kimi-K3 H200 deployment topologies: - TP16 / EP16: 896 global experts, 56 local experts per rank, top-k 16 - TP32 / EP32: 896 global experts, 28 local experts per rank, top-k 16 Kimi-K3's H200 recipes explicitly use `--moe-runner-backend marlin`, so Triton fused-MoE JSON configs are not consulted. This change adds H200-only Marlin block-size tables while preserving the existing heuristic for every other device and shape. Base commit: `955704544c` ## Environment - 2x NVIDIA H200 - PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime `13.0` - CUDA compiler `13.1` - Triton `3.6.0` - Python `3.12` ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH=python export CPATH=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12 cd "$ROOT" ``` ## Tuning commands The benchmark uses random packed MXFP4 weights with Kimi-K3's exact rank-local dimensions: - hidden size: 3584 (`routed_expert_hidden_size`) - intermediate size: 3072 - global experts: 896 - top-k: 16 - remote expert ids mapped to the standard dispatcher's `-1` sentinel - three repetitions per candidate; each repetition is the median of 30 timed calls after 10 warmups Both H200s were used concurrently: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 1 4 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --blocks 8 16 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 30 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-extended-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 1 4 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --blocks 8 16 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 30 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-extended-tp32.json ``` Large-token fallback validation: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 8192 16384 \ --blocks 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 5 \ --iterations 20 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-tail-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 8192 16384 \ --blocks 32 48 64 \ --alignments global \ --warmup 5 \ --iterations 20 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-tail-tp32.json ``` ## Final baseline versus tuned validation The baseline forces the previous heuristic's block. The tuned path calls the selector normally, including the new H200 table. SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu0 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_kimi_k3_marlin_tuning.py \ --tuner /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp16-ep16 \ --tokens 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 50 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-final-tp16.json CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=/shared/user/vjhaveri/.cache/sglang-jit-kimi-gpu1 \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/validate_kimi_k3_marlin_tuning.py \ --tuner /shared/user/vjhaveri/tune_kimi_k3_marlin_block_size.py \ --shape k3-tp32-ep32 \ --tokens 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 \ --warmup 10 \ --iterations 50 \ --repeats 3 \ --output /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-kimi-h200-results/k3-final-tp32.json ``` ### TP16 / EP16 | Tokens | Baseline block | Tuned block | Baseline (ms) | Tuned (ms) signal.title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Nemotron-3.5
signal.text: ## Summary Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16`: - TP1: `E=128,N=1856` - TP2 per rank: `E=128,N=928` Both shapes previously used the generic fallback config. The tuned configs reduce kernel latency by 32.2% to 39.6% across the measured token counts. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA H200 - GPUs available: 2 - Torch: `2.11.0+cu130` - CUDA runtime: 13.0 - Triton: 3.6.0 - SGLang tuning commit: `c2c1c4d3ebc42402264002f6ec57f90fee58c30c` - Token counts: 256, 512, 1024 - Validation repetitions: 3 baseline and 3 tuned per shape ## Results | TP | Tokens | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup | Latency reduction | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 256 | 1435.44 | 930.48 | 1.543x | 35.18% | | 1 | 512 | 1550.47 | 967.20 | 1.603x | 37.62% | | 1 | 1024 | 1694.77 | 1023.66 | 1.656x | 39.60% | | 2 | 256 | 734.74 | 493.07 | 1.490x | 32.89% | | 2 | 512 | 780.75 | 529.32 | 1.475x | 32.20% | | 2 | 1024 | 845.91 | 548.78 | 1.541x | 35.13% | The TP2 per-rank config was also run concurrently on both H200s. Both ranks selected the same configs; their measured means were within 0.6% to 1.0%. ## Reproduction commands The upstream tuner imports Ray only for scheduling. Ray was not available in the test environment, so the same worker was executed directly by `tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py`, one process per GPU. ```bash ROOT=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning VENV=/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/venvs/sglang-v0.5.16-cu130 MODEL=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-model-configs/nemotron35-lightning RESULTS=/shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results export PATH="$VENV/bin:$PATH" export PYTHONPATH="$ROOT/python:$ROOT/benchmark/kernels/fused_moe_triton" export CPATH="/shared/user/qwen35-9ms-sla/system-deps/python3-devel/root/usr/include/python3.12${CPATH:+:$CPATH}" ``` Full TP1 and TP2 searches: ```bash mkdir -p "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp1/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 1 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & ( cd "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \ TRITON_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/triton" \ TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR="$RESULTS/cache-nemotron-tp2/torch" \ "$VENV/bin/python" /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" \ --tp-size 2 \ --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ --tune \ 2>&1 | tee tune.log ) & wait ``` Baseline and tuned validation, repeated three times for each TP size: ```bash for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/baseline-repeat-$repeat.log" done CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/configs/triton_3_6_0" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/E=128,N=1856,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" cp "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/E=128,N=928,device_name=NVIDIA_H200.json" "$CONFIG_DIR/" for repeat in 1 2 3; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 1 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp1/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ 2>&1 | tee "$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2/tuned-repeat-$repeat.log" done ``` Concurrent dual-H200 TP2 per-rank validation: ```bash for gpu in 0 1; do ( CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$gpu" "$VENV/bin/python" \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/tuning_fused_moe_triton_no_ray.py \ --model "$MODEL" --tp-size 2 --batch-sizes 256 512 1024 \ >"$RESULTS/nemotron-tp2-dual-rank-gpu$gpu.log" 2>&1 ) & done wait ``` Patch checks: ```bash git diff --check git apply --check --reverse \ /shared/user/vjhaveri/sglang-h200-tuning-results/nemotron35-lightning-h200-configs.patch ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32191091618](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191091618)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32191091591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32191091591)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Add JoyAI-LLM Flash NextN support for speculative decoding
signal.text: ## Motivation JoyAI-LLM Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 48B total parameters and only 2.7B active parameters, achieving a substantially higher sparsity ratio than contemporary models of comparable scale. Pretrained on 20 trillion tokens and optimized through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), and large-scale reinforcement learning with the novel FiberPO algorithm, it delivers strong performance while maximizing token efficiency. The model further incorporates dense Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) and Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) under a joint training–inference co-design to improve inference throughput. See it on HF: https://huggingface.co/jdopensource/JoyAI-LLM-Flash Technical Report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03044 ## Modifications - Support dense NextN speculative decoding for MTP ## Benchmarking and Profiling JoyAI-LLM Flash speculative decoding acceptance rate analysis on H200 using SPEED-Bench. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26992578814](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26992578814) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26992578669](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26992578669)

signal.title: Improve M3 performance on MI350
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Improve M3 performance on MI350. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications MI350X (gfx950) decode/prefill optimizations for MiniMax-M3 and M3-VL. Measured on TP8 / MXFP8 / 80k context: **1144 -> ~2035 tok/s decode** (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at the higher batch), GSM8K unchanged (88.55% before and after at the same budget; 95.3-95.7% at a 2048-token budget). ### MXFP8 / dense GEMM - AITER FlyDSL MXFP8 MoE support: pre-shuffled gate/up weights, E8M0 scales, OAI-SwiGLU activation handling, and fused shared-expert execution. - `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16`: dequantize MXFP8 weights once at load and run BF16 hipBLASLt linear. - `SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`: convert *dense* weights to block-FP8 `[128,128]` at load while MoE stays on the native per-1x32 MX path (the block-scale MoE kernel does not support SwiGLU-OAI). ~+35% prefill. - `SGLANG_OPT_MXFP8_DENSE_PTPC_DECODE_M` (default 128): rowwise-FP8 (ptpc) dense fast path for skinny-M decode, falling back to the block-FP8 GEMM above it. The old cap of 8 silently disabled both this path and the quant fusions below at bs16; raising it was +14.2%. - Allows `--moe-runner-backend aiter` for MXFP8 on gfx950, and errors early if `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` is not set. ### Fusions - Per-token FP8 quantization fused into the Gemma fused-add-RMSNorm Triton kernel, so the ptpc decode GEMM consumes `(fp8, scale)` directly. Uses an explicitly rounded `1/448` reciprocal (Triton `/` lowers to a fast reciprocal on ROCm, which cost 1 ULP vs AITER). - MoE all-reduce fused into the next layer's norm + qkv quant (`forward_with_allreduce_fusion_quant_per_token`), opt-in per model via `enable_fused_ar_quant_per_token` so it cannot fire for unrelated AITER GemmaRMSNorm models. - Shared-expert append folded into the Triton fused MoE gate (`nfse` handling fixed - the previous path double-appended the shared expert and dropped a routed one). - Shared-expert compute overlapped onto an alternate stream when the routed path forces fusion off. - Small-batch MoE sorting + MXFP8 quant kernel (`moe_sorting_small`), replacing a two-kernel path at decode shapes. ### Router GEMV - New Triton split-K router GEMV (`kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`) with in-kernel split-K fixup (no separate zero-init launch), per-M-bucket configs (BK 512, BN by batch), and the gate weight read once per decode batch. ~+2.8% then +5.5% on top. ### Sparse attention (ATOM port) - Gluon-based paged sparse prefill (`minimax_sparse_ops/atom_prefill.py`), default on via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_ATOM_PREFILL`, with Triton fallback for unsupported shapes and a scratch-size cap that falls back rather than OOMs. - Score-only index kernel at every page size: the per-page slot addressing is now a `PER_PAGE_SLOTS` constexpr chosen from `block_size_k // page_size`, instead of gating the whole (~1.6x) kernel behind `page_size >= 16`. - Index top-k shared across every N sparse layers, `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ` (default 2, ROCm only, never under two-batch overlap) - it changes which KV blocks skip layers attend, so it is an accuracy knob. - Decode top-k written straight into the reuse buffer; per-forward caches keyed on the owning `ForwardBatch` so they are TBO-safe. - JIT radix top-k unblocked under CUDA graphs (`kMaxNumBlocks` 4096 -> 16384). ### Dense decode attention - ROCm decode-attention KV tile 32 -> 64 tokens and a software-pipelined KV loop (`num_stages` 2) for `Lk <= 128`: 690 -> 285 us/launch, ~+7% e2e. - Decode `kv_indices` build parallelized across sequence spans. - Skips redundant sparse KV-cache writes when fusion already populated the cache, and top-k id sanitization when EP is off. ### Defaults and memory accounting - On ROCm gfx950, `--prefill-attention-backend` defaults to `aiter` (ck-tile fmha) while decode stays on Triton. Decode on the AITER backend costs ~3 points on AIME25, so it is not defaulted. - Replaced the blanket `mem_fraction_static *= 0.85` for the AITER backend at `context_len > 8192` with an exact charge: the paged-decode split workspace is fp32 and linear in context length (~4 GiB at 128k) and is allocated after the KV pool, so `KVCacheConfigurator` now re-solves the budget once with the measured size (`aiter_attn_workspace_bytes`) subtracted. The old flat haircut over-reserved ~28 GB. - MiniMax-M3-VL gets the same ROCm shared-expert support; EP/DeepEP guards preserved. ### Launch recipes ### Higher-accuracy dense path Keeps dense weights on the native MXFP8 path with the original per-1×32 scales. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend bf16 \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ### Fast decode path Converts dense weights to block-FP8 at load and selects the automatic block-FP8/PTPC dispatch. MoE remains on native MXFP8. ``` SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \ SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1 \ sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path /persistent/models/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \ --reasoning-parser auto \ --tool-call-parser auto \ --tp 8 \ --quantization mxfp8 \ --moe-runner-backend aiter \ --fp8-gemm-backend auto \ --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` ## Accuracy Tests baseline ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 227.1s | 1485 tok/s | 337K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.61% truncated_rate = 10.39% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` this pr ``` == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 119.9s | 2862 tok/s | 343K tokens * score = 88.55% stop_rate = 89.69% truncated_rate = 10.31% [warn: hitting max_tokens] error_rate = 0.00% ``` <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling MI350X, TP8, MXFP8 MiniMax-M3. ### Dense-path configurations (bs1 / il8192) | Configuration | Decode | Prefill | | |---|---:|---:|---| | Native MXFP8 dense, `--fp8-gemm-backend bf16` (higher-accuracy dense) | 131 tok/s | 22.1k tok/s | reference | | Dense block-convert only (`SGLANG_FORCE_MXFP8_BLOCK_CONVERT_DENSE=1`) | 92.5 tok/s | 29.9k tok/s | **+35% prefill, -30% decode** — the CK a8w8 blockscale kernel is a prefill kernel, ~2.5x worse than bf16 hipBLASLt at M=1 | | Block-convert + PTPC decode fast path + the rest of this PR (fast decode) | 169 tok/s | ~46k tok/s | **+29% decode, +2.1x prefill** vs the first row | The two rows the launch recipes above expose are rows 1 and 3; row 2 is why the skinny-M PTPC path exists at all. ### Concurrency sweep (TP8) | CC | baseline tok/s/user | baseline tok/s/GPU | high accuracy tok/s/user | high accuracy tok/s/GPU | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 49.8 | 6.2 | 131.1 | 16.4 | | 2 | 48.9 | 12.2 | 126.0 | 31.5 | | 4 | 47.9 | 23.9 | 120.5 | 60.3 | | 8 | 46.5 | 46.5 | 112.4 | 112.5 | | 16 | 42.0 | 83.9 | 92.9 | 186.1 | | 32 | 36.8 | 147.3 | 73.9 | 296.0 | | 64 | 30.9 | 247.3 | 57.1 | 457.3 | | 128 | - | - | 41.7 | 667.0 | | 256 | - | - | 29.0 | 929.9 | ### Long-context decode (bs16-32 / il80000) 1144 -> 2035 tok/s (13.98 -> 15.72 ms/step at bs32) across the MXFP8 decode-M cap (+14.2%), the router GEMV M-keyed configs (+5.5%), the fmoe atomic reduce pick (+4.3%), the dense decode-attention tile+pipelining (+3.6% and +7.2%), and the ATOM sparse port. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: fix(sm120): MoE GEGLU activation support + FP4 block scale NaN clamp
signal.text: ## Summary Two fixes for `cutlass_moe_fp4()` that affect NVFP4 MoE models on SM120 GPUs (RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000): ### 1. GEGLU Activation Support `cutlass_moe_fp4()` hardcodes `silu_and_mul()` as the activation function. Models that use GEGLU (like Gemma 4 26B MoE) produce incorrect output from every MoE layer because the wrong activation is applied between GEMM1 and GEMM2. **Fix:** Add `activation` parameter to `cutlass_moe_fp4()`. When `activation="gelu_tanh"`, uses `gelu_tanh_and_mul()` instead. Defaults to `"silu"` for backward compatibility. ### 2. MoE Block Scale NaN Clamp Same E4M3 uint8=127 NaN bug as in linear layers, but in the MoE path. Block scales from `scaled_fp4_experts_quant()` can contain uint8 value 127 which triggers NaN in the CUTLASS FP4 group GEMM kernel on SM120. **Fix:** Clamp block scales to uint8 126 after both `scaled_fp4_experts_quant()` calls (GEMM1 activation scales and GEMM2 intermediate scales). ## Benchmark (RTX 5090, Gemma 4 26B MoE NVFP4) Without these fixes, Gemma 4 NVFP4 MoE layers produce garbage output (wrong activation) and/or NaN (unclamped scales). With fixes applied: | Config | Single User | 30 Concurrent Users | |--------|-------------|-------------------| | **NVFP4 fused MoE + CUDA graphs** | **143 tok/s** | **2,783 tok/s aggregate, p95 3.2s** | ## Test Plan - [x] Tested on RTX 5090 (SM120) with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4` - [x] Verified coherent output (correct GEGLU activation) - [x] No NaN with block scale clamping across extended generation - [x] 30 concurrent users benchmark passes - [ ] Needs testing on non-SM120 to verify no regression - [ ] Needs testing with SiLU-based MoE models to verify default path unchanged
