Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation In local Cursor-style tool-use workflows, GLM5.1 could emit valid tool calls, but it often failed to continue from successful tool results. From the user side, this showed up as Cursor being unable to reliably use tools such as `Shell` to read code, because the model kept re-issuing low-value tool calls instead of consuming the returned results and moving on. During debugging, we ruled out several alternative explanations: - it was not a temperature issue - tool calls were being emitted correctly - Cursor was actually executing the tools - tool results were successfully returned to the model - the `glm47` tool-call parser was not corrupting the generated tool call The key observation was that the same tool result content became usable immediately once it was fed back to GLM5.1 in a different continuation format. This suggests the issue is not in tool execution itself, but in how GLM5.1 consumes tool-result turns in this workflow. ## Modifications This PR adds a GLM5.1-specific chat template override so tool-result turns are rendered in a continuation-style format that works more reliably for GLM5.1 in Cursor-style OpenAI tool-use flows. Specifically: - add a GLM5.1-specific template override at `python/sglang/srt/managers/templates/glm5_1_tool_result_as_user.jinja` - update `python/sglang/srt/managers/template_manager.py` to apply this override only for GLM5.1 - leave the existing HuggingFace chat template behavior unchanged for other models - keep an environment variable gate `SGLANG_GLM51_TOOL_RESULT_TEMPLATE_FIX` so the behavior can be explicitly disabled if needed This is intended as a targeted compatibility fix for GLM5.1 behavior in this workflow, and can serve as a practical workaround while a more semantically aligned tool-result template path is evaluated. ## Accuracy Tests Manual debugging and behavior verification were performed in local Cursor-style tool-use testing. The following were confirmed: - tool calls were emitted correctly - tool execution succeeded - tool results were returned to the model - after this change, GLM5.1 was able to continue normally from tool results instead of repeatedly re-issuing similar tool calls ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [AMD][CI] Prune dead Qwen coverage from the AMD nightly
signal.text: ## Motivation Two pieces of AMD nightly Qwen coverage that are not paying for themselves. **1. `test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py` has never run and could not run.** It registers the suite `nightly-amd-accuracy-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen35-mxfp4`, and that name appears nowhere else in the repo — no workflow dispatches it by `--suite`, no job invokes the file by path, and it is absent from `NIGHTLY_SUITES`. Consistent with never having executed, it is also broken as written: the perf phase calls `runner.setup_profile_directory()` and passes `enable_profile=` to `run_benchmark_for_model`, and `NightlyBenchmarkRunner` has neither, so it would `AttributeError` on the first line of `test_b_perf`. It additionally points at local `/data/amd/` checkpoints rather than HuggingFace ids, so it would not resolve weights on a fresh runner either. **2. The MI30x Qwen3-235B job duplicates architecture coverage that survives elsewhere.** `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` runs `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507` in BF16 and FP8 on an 8-GPU mi300 runner, in *both* the ROCm 7.0 and ROCm 7.2 nightlies, for ~1h each. `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` keeps a nightly heartbeat without it — `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` runs TP8 in `test_qwen3_moe_eval_mi35x.py`, and `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507` runs in the mi30x GSM8K sweep. ## Modifications **Deleted** `test/registered/amd/accuracy/mi35x/test_qwen35_mxfp4_eval_mi35x.py`, plus `test/registered/amd/test_qwen3_instruct.py` and `test_qwen3_instruct_fp8.py`, which fed the removed suite. Removing the job without removing its test files would just move them into the registered-but-undispatched pile rather than out of it. **Removed** the `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b` / `nightly-8-gpu-qwen3-235b-rocm720` job from `nightly-test-amd.yml` and `nightly-test-amd-rocm720.yml`, along with its `job_select` option and `check-all-jobs` dependency in each. **Kept** the MI35x MXFP4 job (`nightly-8-gpu-mi35x-qwen3-235b-mxfp4[-rocm720]`, serving `amd/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-mxfp4`). It is the only coverage of MXFP4 on `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` anywhere in the AMD nightly — the other MXFP4 jobs pair that quantization with DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Qwen3.5-family architectures — and the only Qwen MoE job exercising `--ep 2`. The section comments were retitled from `8-GPU Qwen3-235B (MI30x + MI35x MXFP4)` to `8-GPU Qwen3-235B-MXFP4 (MI35x only)` with a note recording why the MI30x half went away. ### What this trades away The removal gives up `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM` at 235B scale and its FP8 path, in exchange for roughly 2h of 8-GPU mi300 time per night across the two nightlies. That is the deliberate call here rather than an oversight; if the FP8 path at scale turns out to matter, the cheaper restoration is a single mi300 job in the ROCm 7.2 nightly only, not both. ### Out of scope While verifying that these removals did not orphan anything, a broader scan turned up **32 other AMD nightly test files** that are registered but reachable by neither `--suite` nor direct path — mostly dormant mi30x and mi35x DeepSeek / GLM / Kimi / MiniMax evals. Those are left alone here. Unlike the file deleted in this PR they are not known to be broken, and several look deliberately parked for occasional manual dispatch. Worth a follow-up pass to either wire them up or retire them, but not mixed into this change. ## Accuracy Tests No product code is touched; this only removes CI jobs and test files. Verified locally: both workflows still parse as YAML; no `check-all-jobs` dependency references a job that no longer exists; no `job_select` option references a missing job; no reference to the removed suite, jobs, or deleted filenames remains anywhere in the tree; and the three deleted files were confirmed against `origin/main` to have never been invoked by path from any workflow. `check_registered_tests.py`, `check_workflow_job_names.py` and codespell pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable. The net effect is ~2h/night less 8-GPU mi300 occupancy. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — removal-only PR; no new tests. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing docs cover these CI jobs. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Misc] Fix version detection to use ancestor tags and strip .postN
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #22034 Two fixes to `python/tools/get_version_tag.py` for correct setuptools-scm version resolution: - **Use ancestor tags (`git tag --merged HEAD`)** instead of listing all tags globally. When the ancestor tag is the latest, use it directly (fixes checkout-between-releases showing wrong version). When a newer global tag exists (main branch where release tags live on release branches), use the global tag via merge-base distance. - **Strip `.postN` suffixes** from tags before passing to setuptools-scm. The `guess-next-dev` scheme bumps the last integer, so `v0.5.10.post1` would produce `0.5.10.post2.devN` (wrong). signal.title: [HiCache] Support DCP with DSpark
signal.text: ## Motivation DCP + HiCache + DSpark is currently rejected during server argument validation. Removing that guard exposed a draft HiCache sidecar sizing bug: draft indices inherit the target cache's DCP-wide logical index space, while the draft host pool was sized from only the target's physical per-rank rows. Once L1 eviction reached the uncovered range, the draft host transfer failed with `CUDA error: invalid argument`. ## Modifications - Allow DSPARK with HiCache when `--dcp-size > 1`, while retaining the guard for other speculative algorithms. - Size full draft HiCache sidecar pools from the target host pool's logical capacity. - Apply the same logical-capacity sizing to the legacy draft HiCache path. - Add a regression test for DCP-expanded draft sidecar sizing. ## Accuracy Tests Validated on RunPod node 5 with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs using a Kimi-K3 target and RadixArk Kimi-K3 DSpark draft model, TP8/DCP8, A2A, HiCache L2, and the normal CUDA graph path. - Eviction stress test: 64 requests x 16,384 input tokens, concurrency 48. - Result: 64/64 successful; 1,048,576 input tokens and 512 output tokens processed in 52.00 seconds. - Post-run `/health_generate`: HTTP 200. - No scheduler exceptions or CUDA errors after the fix. - `test_server_args.py`: 144 passed, 15 subtests passed. - `test_hybrid_pool_assembler.py`: 4 passed. [TODO] more advanced tests involving DeepSWE ## Speed Tests and Profiling This is a capacity/correctness fix rather than a kernel-path performance change. The eviction stress test above observed approximately 20,164 input tokens/s. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). signal.title: fix(moe): handle bf16 DeepEP low_latency dispatch (a_scales=None) in cutlass W4A8
signal.text: ### Problem `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_ll()` unconditionally calls `fp8_per_token_to_per_tensor_quant_triton(x_scale=a_scales, ...)`. Under DeepEP **low_latency**, the cutlass W4A8 backend dispatches in **bf16** (its default; also forced by `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype bf16`), so the dispatch returns bf16 tokens with **no per-token fp8 scales** — `a_scales is None`. The unconditional call then dereferences `None`: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'size' ``` at decode cuda-graph capture → scheduler dies (exit -3). Hit on Kimi-K3-W4AFP8 with `--deepep-mode auto` (normal prefill + low_latency decode), cuda-graph ON. ### Fix When `a_scales is None`, quantize the bf16 masked tokens to per-tensor fp8 in-place with the static input scale via `per_tensor_quant_fp8(...)` — byte-for-byte the same quantization `cutlass_w4a8_moe_deepep_normal()` already applies to its bf16 input. Forcing fp8 dispatch instead is not a general fix: the per-token triton kernel asserts `hidden % 1024 == 0`, which fails for models whose routed-expert hidden size isn't 1024-divisible (e.g. Kimi-K3 = 3584). ### Validation mini-K3 (2 nodes, EP16, `--deepep-mode auto`, cuda-graph ON) passes decode capture and serves completions without the crash. Draft pending upstream CI + a full multi-node run. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32190125293](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125293)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32190125037](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32190125037)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] Two SM10x-gated cluster/tcgen05 kernels fail on B300 (sm_103): cutedsl TGV BF16 GEMM raises Xid 13 CGA "CTA Not Present", trtllm-gen MoE finalize hangs silently
signal.text: Both are reached because `is_sm100_supported()` is a *family* check (`major == 10`), so sm_103 takes SM100-specific paths. Each was identified by name from a CUDA coredump, not inferred. They are separable — happy to split into two issues if preferred — but they share one gate and one diagnostic, so filing together. ## Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8× NVIDIA B30Z, compute capability **(10, 3)** / sm_103 | | Model | Kimi-K3, TP=8, `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`, decode CUDA graphs on | | sglang | `0.0.0.dev1+g6c7498113` (commit `6c7498113`, 2026-08-07, Kimi-K3 branch) | | torch / driver | 2.13.0+cu130 / 580.159.04 | | flashinfer | 0.6.15.post1, cubin cache verified complete (17372 files, 0 missing) | | workload | offline eval harness, ≤10 concurrent, mixed text and 512×512 images | Everything else is stock: attention backend left unset (auto-selects `trtllm_mla`), `mamba_backend=triton`, CUDA graphs on. I am on a Kimi-K3 branch, so please confirm whether `main` carries the same gating — the code quoted below is from this tree. ## How both were found `kill -9` on a wedged server destroys the evidence, and neither failure prints anything useful on its own. What worked, every time, was reading the CUDA coredump that `--crash-dump-folder` produces: ```bash cuda-gdb -batch -ex "target cudacore core.cuda.<pid>" -ex "info cuda kernels" ``` **The signature: seven ranks hold only a collective kernel and one holds something else. That one is the culprit.** It held for both bugs below. I attributed each from symptoms first and was wrong both times. (Note for anyone reproducing: `cuda-gdb` is often absent, and the conda `cuda-gdb` package ships only the wrapper script — the real `cuda-gdb-minimal` / `cuda-gdb-python3.X-tui` binaries are not in it. The NVIDIA apt `.deb` extracts fine with `dpkg-deb -x`, no system install needed.) --- ## Bug 1 — `TgvGemmCuteExtKernel` (cutedsl BF16 GEMM) faults with Xid 13 ### Symptom All ranks hang forever in `process_batch_result_decode` → `result.copy_done.synchronize()` → `cudaEventSynchronize`, with **zero CUDA errors raised in-process**. SGLang's 300 s watchdog eventually aborts. Twice, on different days and **different GPUs**: | | 2026-08-10 09:55 | 2026-08-10 11:44 | |---|---|---| | 7 ranks holding | `all_reduce_pull_res_kernel` | `all_reduce_pull_res_kernel` | | outlier rank | **device 3**, sm 145 | **device 5**, sm 109 | | outlier kernel | `TgvGemmCuteExtKernel_cta64x16x128_2cta1_pdl1_bias0_tensorptrbf16…` | same | | launch geometry | GridDim (112,1,1), BlockDim (256,1,1), **cluster dim (2,1,1)** | identical | Different GPUs with an identical kernel and geometry rules out one bad board. ### The Xid For the 11:44 crash, the host kernel log has: ``` NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:a7:00): 13, Graphics SM Cga Exception on (GPC 0, TPC 8, SM 1): CTA Not Present ``` `cuda-gdb` reports device 5 as PCI `a7:00.0` — the same device it found holding the kernel. **CGA is the thread-block cluster**, and this kernel launches 2-CTA clusters, so "CTA Not Present" names the launch shape exactly. Worth flagging for others hunting this: dmesg on our host is a ~73 minute ring buffer, so the Xid for the earlier crash was already gone by the time we looked. The coredump is the durable artifact. ### Why it runs on sm_103 ```python # srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:91 if backend_str == "auto" and is_sm100_supported(): backend_str = "cutedsl" ``` ```python # srt/utils/common.py:286 is_sm100_supported = lru_cache(maxsize=1)( partial(_check_cuda_device_version, device_capability_majors=[10], cuda_version=(12, 8)) ) ``` `device_capability_majors=[10]` accepts **any** 10.x, so sm_103 (and sm_110) pass. Measured on this box: ``` torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) -> (10, 3) is_sm100_supported() -> True ``` And the selected kernel is explicitly SM100 two-SM: ```python # kernels/ops/gemm/cutedsl_bf16_gemm.py:149-152 if use_2cta: self.cluster_shape = (2, 1, 1) self.mma_tiler_mn = (cta_m * 2, cta_n) self.cta_group = tcgen05.CtaGroup.TWO self.tma_op = cute_ext.OperationTypeEnum.SM100_TMA_LOAD_2SM ``` 2-CTA clusters and `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` depend on SM-pairing topology, which is not identical between SM100 and SM103. ### Workaround `--bf16-gemm-backend torch`. **No measurable throughput cost** here — aggregate went from 297–610 tok/s (noisy) to 595–666 tok/s, which makes sense since Kimi-K3's compute is dominated by MXFP4 MoE, not unquantized BF16 GEMM. --- ## Bug 2 — `moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernelVecLoad` (trtllm-gen MoE) hangs With Bug 1 worked around, the Xid stopped and a **different** signature appeared after 73 min of serving (2026-08-10 20:35): | rank | resident kernel | |---|---| | device 1–7 | `all_reduce_pull_norm_kernel` — waiting in the collective | | **device 0** | **`moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernelVecLoad`**, GridDim (24,1,1) — never returns | All eight Python stacks in `process_batch_result_**prefill**` → `synchronize` → `cudaEventSynchronize`; SGLang's 300 s watchdog fired and dumped every rank. **No Xid, no CUDA error, nothing in dmesg.** The kernel does not fault, it simply never completes — so without the coredump this is indistinguishable from a scheduler deadlock, and it looks a lot like #26454 while having a different cause. Contrast the two: | | Bug 1 | Bug 2 | |---|---|---| | Xid | 13, CGA / CTA Not Present | **none** | | nature | kernel faults | kernel hangs | | Python frame | `process_batch_result_decode` | `process_batch_result_prefill` | | time to failure | 20 min – 2 h | 73 min and 3 h 07 min | ### Arch coverage `moe_runner_backend=auto` selects `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM10x when the trtllm-gen SiTU cubin pool is present. That pool ships prebuilt binaries, and its sm_103 coverage is thin: | kernel set | sm100f | sm103a | sm103a share | |---|---:|---:|---:| | trtllm-gen **MoE** cubin pool (`20260617_v0613rc1`) | 1636 | 60 | **3%** | | trtllm-gen FMHA cubins | 11248 | 1892 | 14% | flashinfer exposes `gen_cutlass_fused_moe_sm103_module` but only `gen_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_**sm100**_module` — no sm_103 generator for this path. ### Workaround `--moe-runner-backend marlin`, which SGLang's own Kimi-K3 override already suggests (`srt/arg_groups/overrides.py:574`). Marlin is compiled from source in `sgl_kernel` for the local arch and launches no clusters. Measured cost: | | trtllm-gen | marlin | |---|---|---| | single stream (`#running-req: 1`) | ~103 tok/s | ~84 tok/s (−18%) | | aggregate at 9–10 concurrent | ~705 tok/s | ~385 tok/s (−45%) | --- ## Result With `--bf16-gemm-backend torch --moe-runner-backend marlin` and everything else stock: - **11 h+ of continuous serving, zero restarts, zero new Xids**, versus a 20 min – 3 h failure cadence before. - A full 63-configuration benchmark sweep (9 tiers × 7 tasks × 10 trials) completed on it, including image-heavy multi-turn workloads. ## Suggested fix Both kernels look like they want the treatment `cutlass_mla_decode` already gets in this tree — hard-gated to `sm_version == 100` with a comment that half the accuracy tests fail on SM103a (#27384). Concretely: 1. Gate the cutedsl `use_2cta` path (or the whole cutedsl BF16 GEMM) to `sm_version == 100`, falling back to `torch` on sm_103 rather than trapping. 2. Do the same for trtllm-gen MoE selection when no sm_103a cubin exists for the required kernel, falling back to marlin — which the code already knows how to suggest, just not automatically. 3. More generally: `is_sm100_supported()` reads as a capability check but is a family check. Anywhere it guards SM100-specific cluster/tcgen05 features, an exact-arch predicate seems more appropriate. Happy to send a PR for (1) and (2) if the approach sounds right. ## Related - #27384 — sibling tcgen05 kernel already hard-gated to `sm_version == 100` ("On SM103a, half of the accuracy tests are failing"); the ungated sibling traps. - #21904 — any model hangs at high concurrency on (G)B300 (SM103) with TRTLLM attention. - #25564 — flash-attn-4 cute kernel arch check rejects sm_103 (the *opposite* direction: a gate too narrow, where these two are too wide). - #25574 — `topk_transform_512_v2` fused-cluster kernel crashes on B300. - #26454 — frame-identical `copy_done.synchronize()` hang, but GB200/sm_100 and no Xid; likely a different cause from either of these. - #30010 — closest in shape to Bug 2: a MoE kernel (`moeA2ACombineKernel`) deadlocking with all ranks spinning, under CUDA graphs. Different kernel and different configuration, but the same "one MoE kernel never returns and the collective piles up behind it" pattern. - vllm-project/vllm#50880 — independent corroboration outside SGLang: B300 hard hangs under concurrency, and changing the attention backend does not help because it leaves the MoE expert path untouched. I have the coredumps, per-rank py-spy dumps and full server logs for all three crashes and can share whatever is useful.

signal.title: [Bug] deepep FP8 MoE on GB300/sm_103 crashes in DeepGEMM m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous —   UE8M0 scale-format mismatch (CUDA 719 / smxx_layout.cuh:131 assert)
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On GB300 (sm_103), serving a DeepSeek MoE with the `deepep` a2a backend + FP8 crashes on the **first real request** with an opaque `CUDA error 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)` inside DeepGEMM's `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1`, the 719 unmasks to a device-side assertion: ``` Assertion failed: deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/smxx_layout.cuh:131, condition: (values[j] & 0x807fffffu) == 0 ``` `0x807fffff` masks the fp32 sign + 23 mantissa bits, so the kernel is asserting the scale factors are **UE8M0** (power-of-two, exponent-only). Instrumenting the call site shows the two operands are in **different scale formats**: ``` a_sf (activation scale) = torch.int32 # UE8M0-packed b_sf (weight scale) = torch.float32 # raw, NOT UE8M0 m=768 n=2816 k=2048 num_groups=16 ``` No single `disable_ue8m0_cast` reconciles a mixed pair, so the kernel asserts. **This is not a DeepGEMM/hardware limitation** — DeepGEMM's grouped fp8 kernel runs correctly on sm_103 in isolation (see below). It's a scale-format inconsistency in SGLang's Blackwell deepep-fp8 path: the **MoE expert weight scales are not UE8M0-requantized** while the activation scales are. **Note:** startup + DeepGEMM warmup **succeed** because the warmup uses trivial `torch.ones` scales, which are coincidentally UE8M0-valid (1.0 is a power of two). Only the **first real request** — whose per-block scales are not powers of two — trips the assertion. ## Root cause `srt/layers/quantization/utils::should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0(...)` gates whether FP8 weight scales get UE8M0-requantized at load. On this path the **MoE expert weight scales stayed `float32`** (the requant did not fire), while the activation-scale path produced `int32` UE8M0-packed scales — so the two operands handed to `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous` disagree. This is the same family as #34340 (`is_sm100_supported()` is a `major == 10` check, so sm_103 takes SM100 paths inconsistently). ## DeepGEMM is not at fault (isolation evidence) DeepGEMM's own tests pass on sm_103 for the exact kernels SGLang uses, with **both** the bundled `0.1.5.post3` and current `2.6.1`: - `tests/test_fp8_fp4.py::test_gemm` (plain), `test_m_grouped_gemm_contiguous`, `test_m_grouped_gemm_masked` → all PASS, ~3.5 PFLOPS fp8, 0 errors. So the kernel correctly *rejects* malformed (mixed-format) input; it is not missing sm_103 support. ## Attempted fix (partial — confirms the direction) Packing the weight scale to int32 UE8M0 per-group and calling with `disable_ue8m0_cast=True` gets **past** the UE8M0 assertion but then hits a layout assertion: ``` Assertion (layout.hpp:97): sf.size(-2) == ceil_div(mn, gran_mn) ``` i.e., packing is **necessary but not sufficient** — the packed weight scale must be in the **mn-major, TMA-aligned grouped layout** (via `get_mn_major_tma_aligned_packed_ue8m0_tensor` / the load-time `requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm` path), not a naive per-group stack. This is why the correct fix belongs at weight-load, using SGLang's own UE8M0 helpers. ## Suggested fix Ensure MoE **expert** weight scales are UE8M0-requantized (with the correct grouped TMA-aligned layout) whenever the DeepGEMM runner will be used for the deepep path on Blackwell — i.e., make the weight-load requant fire for this path so it matches the activation scale format. More generally (per #34340): `is_sm100_supported()` reads as a capability check but is a family check; SM100-specific format assumptions should be exact-arch aware for sm_103. ## Workarounds - **MoE serving on GB300 today:** vLLM/Dynamo (do not route through this DeepGEMM path). - Possibly `--moe-runner-backend <alt>` (as #34340 uses marlin for its trtllm-gen MoE bug) — untested for the deepep path here; SGLang's deepep may not register an alternate runner. ## Related #34340 (same sm_103 SM10x MoE gating class), #20776 (auto-fallback when scale_fmt not UE8M0), #29993 / #29954 (UE8M0 scale-pack assert family, B200), #29038 (Blackwell DeepGEMM accuracy), #27384 (sibling sm_103 device-assert). We have full logs and the instrumented dtype trace, and a standing GB300 repro cluster — happy to test a fix. ### Reproduction Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite`, single node, TP=4 / EP=4, deepep + FP8. Launch the server (device-side assertions on, so the 719 shows its real cause): ```bash CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --trust-remote-code --quantization fp8 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal --attention-backend triton \ --disable-cuda-graph --moe-dense-tp-size 1 ``` Server starts and the DeepGEMM warmup completes (`Uvicorn running` / `Application startup complete`). Then send one request: ```bash curl -s localhost:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text":"The capital of France is","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8}}' ``` → the scheduler crashes on this first request (empty response). Without `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1` it appears only as `CUDA error 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)` in `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`; with them, the `smxx_layout.cuh:131` UE8M0 assertion above is shown. ### Environment ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3: NVIDIA GB300 GPU 0,1,2,3 Compute Capability: 10.3 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88 CUDA Driver Version: 580.173.02 PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130 sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+gc0b6474b4 sglang-kernel: 0.4.6.post1 flashinfer_python: 0.6.17 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.17 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.17+cu130 triton: 3.7.1 transformers: 5.12.1 numpy: 2.3.5 fastapi: 0.141.1 huggingface_hub: 1.27.0 outlines: 0.1.11 pydantic: 2.13.4 uvicorn: 0.52.3 xgrammar: 0.2.1 vllm: Module Not Found NVIDIA Topology: GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3 NIC0 NIC1 NIC2 NIC3 NIC4 CPU Affinity NUMA Affinity GPU NUMA ID GPU0 X NV18 NV18 NV18 SYS SYS NODE NODE SYS 0-55 0 N/A GPU1 NV18 X NV18 NV18 SYS SYS NODE NODE SYS 0-55 0 N/A GPU2 NV18 NV18 X NV18 NODE NODE SYS SYS NODE 56-111 1 N/A GPU3 NV18 NV18 NV18 X NODE NODE SYS SYS NODE 56-111 1 N/A NIC Legend: NIC0: mlx5_0 NIC1: mlx5_1 NIC2: mlx5_2 NIC3: mlx5_3 NIC4: mlx5_4 ulimit soft: 1048576 ``` Additional context not in `check_env`: - `deep_gemm` version: `0.1.5.post3` (bundled in the image). - Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`. Cluster: K8s DRA (GPUs via `gpu.nvidia.com`, ComputeDomain for MNNVL); single node, 4× GB300 / sm_103.

signal.title: [PD] Deferred decode-side KV release for the NIXL backend
signal.text: ## Motivation #35049 added env-gated **deferred decode-side KV release** — on abort, hold an in-flight request's KV pages/req-slot until the prefill confirms its transfer drained (or a timeout fires), so a still-landing write can't corrupt the next request that reuses those pages. It wired the prefill ack for **mooncake only**. Two reasons NIXL needs it: 1. **There is a latent footgun today.** The decode side is backend-agnostic, so enabling `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_DEFERRED_DECODE_KV_RELEASE` on a NIXL deployment *already* holds pages (`NixlKVManager(CommonKVManager)`, `NixlKVReceiver(CommonKVReceiver)` inherit the abort/tracker machinery). But NIXL never sends `ABORT_ACK` and had no path to receive one, so `is_abort_release_safe` is never satisfied and **every abort waits out the full timeout** — safe (holding is the safe direction), but fully degraded, pinning KV and back-pressuring new requests under abort load. 2. **The hazard is arguably worse than mooncake's.** NIXL transfers are inherently asynchronous — `agent.transfer(handle)` posts and returns, and the worker polls `check_xfer_state(handle)` for `DONE` — so there is always a real in-flight window. Mooncake's *default* path is the synchronous `batch_transfer_sync`. `nixl/conn.py::_handle_abort_notification` even carried a `TODO` for exactly this mechanism. ## Modifications **Shared (`common/conn.py`)** — one ack implementation for both backends: - Hoist `_prefill_unique_rank`, `_send_abort_ack`, `_maybe_ack_drained_abort` and the `_deferred_ack_targets` map from `MooncakeKVManager` to `CommonKVManager`; add `register_deferred_ack_target()` documenting the mark-`Failed`-first ordering. Mooncake behavior is unchanged (now inherited). `CommonKVSender.clear()` already drops held targets, so NIXL gets that cleanup for free. **NIXL (`nixl/conn.py`)**: - `_handle_abort_notification`: parse the return address the decode already sends (`_send_abort_notification` has always included ip/port — NIXL just ignored it), register the held ack **after** the status flip for an active room, and ack a concluded room immediately. It never acks an active room from the bootstrap thread: a chunk dequeued but not yet counted would race the ack. - `transfer_worker`: ack at the skip site (nothing was written for the aborted room) and after the existing `while handles: check_xfer_state == DONE` barrier (writes have landed). NIXL's drain point is actually *cleaner* than mooncake's — no sibling-future hazard. Deliberately **no** ack on the exception path: that barrier bails on the first `ERR`, so sibling handles may still be writing; the room falls back to the decode timeout. **Closing two ack-stranding windows (both backends — both were present in #35049):** Previously the ack was driven only by worker visits, so two sequences left a registered target that nobody ever acked, falling back to the decode timeout (safe, but losing the fast path exactly when you want it): 1. the owning worker could pass its `Failed` skip point *between* the status flip and the target registration (ack attempt a no-op, then the target lands and strands); 2. a room whose enqueued chunks had all drained with no further chunk coming (`is_last_chunk` unseen) is never revisited by the worker at all. The root cause was that `outstanding == 0` was not a quiescence predicate: chunks were counted *after* the `Failed` status check, so a chunk could be dequeued and about to write while the counter still read 0 — which is why the ack could not safely be sent from the bootstrap thread. Now chunks are **counted at dequeue, before the status check**, so a chunk either writes (counted) or skips (uncounted), never both, and `Failed and outstanding == 0` genuinely means nothing can still write. With that predicate the abort path attempts the ack once after registering, covering both windows. Counting slightly earlier is strictly more conservative for the existing `poll()` Success hold and teardown condition (increments/decrements still pair). - Decode: generalize the staging-only ZMQ thread into a decode **listener** that also handles `ABORT_ACK`, started when staging *or* deferred release is enabled. A dedicated thread ingests acks even while the decode is idle — NIXL notifs would **not**, since the decode agent runs with `num_threads=0` and only drains notifs inside a live receiver's `poll()`, which early-returns once `conclude_state` is set on abort. Off by default; when disabled, both backends behave exactly as before. ## Tests New `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_deferred_kv_release.py`: ack held until outstanding drains, fires at most once, unregistered-room no-op, rank formula matches the Success-sync formula, abort-notification registration (active / concluded / feature-off / legacy 2-frame abort / non-ABORT passthrough), and per-rank ack aggregation. Existing NIXL fixtures that build a manager via `object.__new__` now set `enable_deferred_decode_kv_release = False` (they cover the legacy no-ack behavior). Verified in the `lmsysorg/sglang` container on a CPU VM: ``` test_nixl_deferred_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_nixl_backend_basic Ran 43 tests OK test_deferred_decode_kv_release Ran 12 tests OK test_decode_queue_cleanup Ran 6 tests OK test_nixl_sender_failure_cleanup Ran 1 test OK test_disaggregation_wire Ran 23 tests OK test_kv_transfer_replica_metric Ran 3 tests OK ``` (The mooncake-side suites are included deliberately: the dequeue-counting change touches shared worker logic.) ## Not covered / follow-ups - **No live NIXL PD run.** The state machine and wiring are unit-tested; an end-to-end abort-mid-transfer run on a real NIXL deployment (and the fast-ack-vs-timeout ratio) is not yet measured. Same gap as #35049's, which validated on mooncake. - Multi-node / TP>1 dummy-rank fan-out unvalidated (the `len(bootstrap_infos)` denominator is dummy-proof by construction, but untested where the real multi-queue concurrency lives). - The mamba/state path (`maybe_send_extra`) is not routed through drain-aware waiting on either backend — carried over from #35049. ## Checklist - [x] Format with pre-commit (black/isort) - [x] Add unit tests - [ ] Accuracy/speed benchmarks (N/A — abort-path correctness; no kernel/throughput impact, no-op when disabled) - [x] Code style Related: #35049, #32564, #27372 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32167618366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32167618366)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32167618173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32167618173)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: docs(cookbook): Qwen3.6 config-driven deployment + measured speed benchmarks
signal.text: Migrates the Qwen3.6 cookbook page to the **config-driven Deployment/Playground engine** (as for DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3.5) and adds **measured speed benchmarks**. The legacy `qwen36-deployment.jsx` generator is removed. ## Config — `configs/qwen/qwen3.6.jsx` (44 cells) `h100/h200/b200/b300` × `{35B-A3B (MoE), 27B (Dense)}` × `{bf16, fp8, +nvfp4 on Blackwell}` × `{low-latency, high-throughput}`, plus **Xeon `balanced`** (27B/35B-A3B × bf16/fp8). low-latency = MTP/EAGLE + mamba radix-cache v2; high-throughput = MTP off; Xeon = spec unsupported → single `balanced` recipe (`--device cpu`, tp 3/6). GPU cells tp=1 single-node. ## Faithfulness - Cells reproduce the generator command **verbatim** — verified by executing `generateCommand()` across the matrix: **42/44 exact**. Parsers (`--reasoning-parser`/`--tool-call-parser`) omitted (Playground-only; DSv4 convention). - The 2 non-verbatim cells are **b300 35B-A3B NVFP4**, adding `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass`: the generator's default moe runner crashes on that model on 0.5.16, and this is exactly how b300 was measured. - Bench = `bench_serving` random isl 8192 / osl 1024, `--random-range-ratio 1.0 --warmup-requests 64 --flush-cache`; LL @ conc 1+16, HT @ conc 1024+4096. `tokens_per_sec_per_gpu = output_throughput / tp × (isl+osl)/osl`. ## Coverage — 32/44 measured - Measured: **B200 (12) @ 0.5.15, H200 (8) + B300 (12) @ 0.5.16**. - Pending (render "pending"): **H100 (8)** — no 8×H100 capacity this run; **Xeon (4)** — no CPU box (Deploy command shown, no speed). - Blackwell NVFP4 version note: b200 on 0.5.15 (default moe runner works → plain command), b300 on 0.5.16 (needs the flag) — **each cell matches its own bench**. ## Follow-ups - Bench H100 (8) once capacity frees. - Re-bench b200 35B-A3B NVFP4 on 0.5.16 with `flashinfer_cutlass` to unify the Blackwell backend. - Apply the +13% mem0.92 tune to h200 35B-A3B bf16 HT (clean conc 1024+4096 re-bench). Supersedes the prose-table approach in #23798. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32179796223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32179796223)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32179795888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32179795888)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Add Agentic-Aware Tail-Optimized LRU eviction to the unified radix cache
signal.text: ## Motivation Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU, [NeurIPS 25](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15152)) keeps only as much of a conversation cached as its next prefill needs to stay under a TTFT SLO budget, and frees the rest of the tail before falling back to recency order, so newer requests can be admitted. On agentic traces the tail is what a plain LRU protects at the expense of every other conversation's tail latency by up to 43%. The policy is opt-in and off by default; `lru` remains the default and its code path is unchanged. ## Modifications ``` --radix-eviction-policy tlru --tlru-threshold N # xi, in tokens --tlru-next-prompt-estimate M # Q_hat, in tokens ``` Concretely: a conversation or agentic turn with history length `L` whose next prompt is expected to add `Q_hat` tokens only needs `L + Q_hat - xi` tokens resident to keep its next prefill inside a TTFT budget `xi`. Everything past that point is "TEL-safe" — evicting it cannot worsen tail latency, because the recompute it causes still fits the budget. T-LRU frees those tokens first (phase 1) and continues in plain recency order once they run out (phase 2). Implemented as a priority function rather than a second eviction pass: a TEL-safe node reports as infinitely old, so the existing device and host eviction drivers produce both of the paper's phases unchanged. ```python budget = max(node.convo_length + self.next_prompt_estimate - self.threshold, 0) cached_without_this_node = node.depth - len(node.key) tel_safe = cached_without_this_node >= budget return (-1 if tel_safe else 0, node.last_access_time) ``` The conversation's history length (`convo_length`) is tracked as a monotone high-water mark separate from its resident depth, maintained on insert and split. Deriving it from what is still cached would leave a trimmed conversation over budget on every later pass and walk it down to nothing instead of stopping after `xi - Q_hat` tokens. Thresholds are expressed in tokens, unlike the paper's blocks (multiply the paper's values by `page_size` to convert), and startup rejects the two configurations that would silently reduce the policy to LRU (`xi <= Q_hat`, and use without the unified radix tree). **Choosing `xi` and `Q_hat`.** Only the difference `delta = xi - Q_hat` reaches the policy (the protected budget is `max(L - delta, 0)`), so the two are stated separately only because each is independently interpretable. `xi` is the tolerated recompute cost in tokens: pick a TTFT budget in seconds and divide by `alpha`, the measured per-uncached-token prefill cost of the system under test (~64 us/token here), giving `xi = 14592` — p5 of the trace's context-length distribution. `Q_hat` is the expected next-prompt size, taken from the trace's per-turn prompt-growth distribution rather than guessed: `2304`, its p60 (median growth is 1,731). Both are workload-relative token counts, so porting them to a new workload means re-deriving: re-measure `alpha` and re-apply the SLO, or match the freed share `F(delta) = sum(min(delta, ctx_i)) / sum(ctx_i)` (7.4% of served context at our setting) and solve for the new `delta`. Files touched (325 insertions, 7 deletions): | file | change | | --- | --- | | `mem_cache/evict_policy.py` | `TLRUStrategy` | | `mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py` | `convo_length` bookkeeping on insert/split | | `mem_cache/cache_init_params.py`, `kv_cache_builder.py`, `utils.py` | plumb the two params | | `srt/server_args.py` | flags, choices, validation | | `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_tlru_eviction_policy.py` | 9 unit tests | ## Accuracy Tests No change to model forward computation or kernels: the policy only reorders which cached prefixes are evicted, and an evicted prefix is recomputed exactly on its next request, so model outputs are unchanged by construction. The default `lru` path is untouched when the flag is not set. Policy behaviour is covered by 9 CPU-only unit tests (`test_tlru_eviction_policy.py`, no GPU required): - frees exactly the tail budget on a fresh conversation, and stops there - conversations under the threshold are entirely free - phase 1 spreads across conversations, then falls back to LRU - degenerates to exact LRU when `Q_hat` reaches `xi` - an oversized tail node is protected rather than partially freed - a compacted branch keeps its shared prefix protected - budget clamps at zero; priorities stay finite and orderable ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, 4x B300, TP4/EP4/DP-attention, HiCache DRAM ratio 4, on the SemiAnalysis agentic trace via aiperf, 3,600 s measured after 600 s cache-pressure warmup, `xi=14592` / `Q_hat=2304`. C=32: 5 LRU / 12 T-LRU runs; C=40: 4 LRU / 5 T-LRU. **Methodology.** The client seed is pinned, so both arms replay identical trajectories; requests are matched across arms on `(conversation_id, turn_index)` and compared as a paired sample (~6,000+ matched requests per concurrency), which removes workload variance. Comparisons use the middle 80% of each run's measured window (opening/closing 10% trimmed from both arms alike) to exclude the residual warm-up transient and client-drain. And the trace is using [semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126](https://huggingface.co/datasets/semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126) on HuggingFace: 9,843 real Claude Code sessions (98,827 turns) captured by WEKA's kv-cache-tester. The actual generator code lives in the aiperf fork inside [InferenceX](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX), checked out at dd237099. **Paired quantile deltas, T-LRU vs LRU on identical requests (lower is better):** C=32: | metric | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TTFT | -3.2%| -5.3% | -4.7% | -6.9% | -8.6% | | ITL | +2.2%* | -0.7% | -8.7% | -17.2% | -43.9% | C=40: | metric | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 | p99 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TTFT | +5.1% | +2.4% | +2.1% | -4.3% | -13.6% | | ITL | +0.2% | +0.8% | -0.6% | -2.7% | -11.0% | The shape matches the mechanism: the decode tail is where retention pays off, and the effect grows monotonically toward the tail at C=32 (ITL -8.7% at p90 to -43.9% at p99), alongside TTFT body improvements. The cost is small and in the body: ITL p50 +2.2% at C=32 and TTFT p50 +5.1% at C=40 (both corroborated by run-level exact rank tests). **Throughput** (arm-level medians, higher is better) is unchanged — every delta is inside its replicate spread. The policy reshapes the latency distribution without moving aggregate throughput or the prefix hit rate. | C | metric | LRU | T-LRU | delta | replicate spread | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 32 | tok/s/GPU | 28,580 | 28,228 | -1.2% | 12.2% | | 32 | tok/s/user | 23.45 | 22.89 | -2.4% | 4.9% | | 32 | GPU prefix hit | 96.04% | 96.07% | +0.04 pp | 0.5 pp | | 40 | tok/s/GPU | 30,117 | 30,558 | +1.5% | 8.0% | | 40 | tok/s/user | 20.06 | 19.72 | -1.7% | 9.8% | | 40 | GPU prefix hit | 95.70% | 95.79% | +0.09 pp | 0.3 pp | Note: this configuration is well-provisioned (working set ~0.28x of KV capacity, 96% prefix hit rate vs a 97.7% ceiling), so these numbers are a lower bound on what a cache-pressured deployment shows; and `xi`/`Q_hat` are workload-relative token counts — copying our values onto a different context distribution will not reproduce this behaviour (only `xi - Q_hat` reaches the policy). **Write-back study.** There is a nuance in the analogy to a CPU cache: in a CPU, SRAM caches are *write-back* to DRAM; here, DRAM itself is the second-level cache (backing GPU HBM), and it runs write-back in an "allocate on eviction" sense. That is: a KV page gets its DRAM copy only at the moment it is demoted out of HBM, never proactively. Thus, the *write-back rate* is exactly the *eviction rate*. **Measured write-back and load-back rates** (median per run, 3,600 s window, from run counters): | arm | C | written back to DRAM | rate | load-back from DRAM | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | LRU | 32 | 30.0M tokens | ~8.3k tok/s 10 MB/s | 0.7M tok (~0.2 MB/s) | | LRU | 40 | 38.9M tokens | ~10.8k tok/s 13 MB/s | 3.3M tok (~1.1 MB/s) | | T-LRU | 32 | 48.1M tokens | ~13.4k tok/s 16 MB/s | 17.4M tok (~5.7 MB/s) | | T-LRU | 40 | 58.3M tokens | ~16.2k tok/s 19 MB/s | 22.8M tok (~7.5 MB/s) | Implied size is ~1.2 KB per token, consistent with MLA's compressed KV — this model is unusually cheap to demote. **Two main readings** 1. *Average bandwidth is trivial*. 10–20 MB/s sustained against an HBM↔DRAM link measured in hundreds of GB/s is negligible — write-back traffic is not a bandwidth concern here, even with T-LRU's 1.6× amplification (visible directly: e.g., T-LRU writes 48M vs LRU's 30M at C=32, and the ~17M difference is its load-back volume). Any latency cost from the demotion path arises from the moment copies happen — bursty, under memory pressure, on the eviction path while a prefill waits — not from the total data moved. 2. *The tier is write-heavy and read-light under LRU* (e.g., 30M written vs 0.7M read back at C=32, a 43:1 ratio). This is exactly when write-back is the right policy: write-through would have pre-copied everything for almost no read benefit. T-LRU narrows the ratio to ~3:1 by design — it deliberately evicts things that come back. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #32166634910](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166634910) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #32166634309](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166634309)

signal.title: [Bug][Spec] fix startup crash and reduce CUDA graph memory usage for speculative adaptive
signal.text: ## Motivation Three separate problems show up when `--speculative-adaptive` is enabled: 1. **Startup crash.** `ModelRunner.max_decode_logits_rows()` sizes the shared logits buffer from the *static* `decode_num_tokens_per_req()`, but adaptive speculative decoding replays runners built for larger draft-token widths. The buffer is too small and the server fails to start. (mentioned in #30549) 2. **IMA on the first replay.** `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` looked up `on_after_cuda_graph_warmup` on `self.model_runner.attn_backend` instead of on the backend this capture actually ran against (`attn_backend` from `capture_prepare`). For the runner the `ModelRunner` owns these are the same object, but adaptive speculative decoding builds extra runners bound to their own freshly created backend while `model_runner.attn_backend` still points at the active one. Hooking the wrong backend leaves this capture's warmup-upgraded metadata (raw→full, FlashMLA scheduler meta) frozen into the graph, which produces an illegal memory access on the first replay. 3. **Redundant CUDA graph memory.** Each capture pass opened `graph_capture()` without a stream, so every pass captured on a fresh stream. The caching allocator partitions the graph pool's segments **by stream**, so each pass re-reserved the pool's MoE / DeepEP scratch instead of reusing what an earlier pass left inactive. With adaptive speculative decoding that is one pass per candidate step × three runners — tens of GB of segments that all read back `inactive`. ## Modifications 1. `max_decode_logits_rows()` now derives `num_tokens_per_req` from `max_speculative_num_draft_tokens`, so the shared logits buffer is sized for the widest adaptive graph. (Same fix as #30554.) 2. `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1226-1237` — resolve `post_warmup_hook` from the capture-local `attn_backend` rather than `model_runner.attn_backend`, with a comment recording why. 3. Added `get_or_create_global_graph_capture_stream()` in `runner_utils/pool.py` (a named stream lease in the `Resources` tier, alongside the existing process-wide graph memory pool) and used it as the `graph_capture(stream=...)` argument in both `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture` and `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture`. All capture passes therefore share one stream and reserve that scratch exactly once. Captures are strictly serial (`Scheduler.init_all_cuda_graphs` runs target and draft workers in turn; the adaptive controller builds one runtime state at a time), so a single shared stream is safe. Also added a CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_graph_capture_resources.py` covering both the pool and the new capture-stream lease. ## Accuracy Tests Server launched following the cookbook: ```bash sglang serve \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --tp 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \ --speculative-adaptive \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Evaluated on the three datasets shown in the cookbook: | | GPQA Diamond | AIME25 | GSM8k | | -------- | ------------ | ------ | ----- | | cookbook | 88.1 | 95 | 96.13 | | before | 88.13 | 98.33 | 96.89 | | after | 88.04 | 97.29 | 96.97 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling No throughput change is expected; the win is memory. With the launch command above and the default adaptive speculative decoding parameters, CUDA graph memory drops from **14.4 GB → 10.13 GB**. With my own serving config and adaptive speculative decoding parameters, it drops from **44.3 GB → 16 GB**, which frees the corresponding capacity for the KV cache. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bug] Multimodal CUDA IPC transport auto-selected on WSL2, where CUDA IPC is unsupported — scheduler crashes with no hint at --mm-feature-transport
signal.text: ## Summary On WSL2, any multimodal model fails to start because the scheduler dies in the CUDA IPC multimodal feature transport. **WSL2 does not support CUDA IPC** (`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle` / `cudaIpcGetMemHandle` are unsupported there), but `_handle_multimodal_feature_transport` auto-selects `cuda_ipc` for any multimodal model on single-node CUDA. The workaround is `--mm-feature-transport cpu`, but nothing in the error output points to it. ## Reproduction RTX 5090, Windows 11 + WSL2, Docker, image `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b`. ```bash docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g -p 30000:30000 \ -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \ --ipc=host lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b \ sglang serve --trust-remote-code \ --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --attention-backend flashinfer --max-running-requests 1 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 ``` ## Actual behaviour The HTTP server comes up, then the scheduler crashes on the first request: ``` Failed to deserialize from cached pooled CUDA IPC handle (CUDA error: invalid resource handle Search for `cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle' in ... ). Invalidating cache entry and retrying uncached. Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 500, in reconstruct_on_target_device ) = self._reconstruct_from_ipc_extra( File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 416, in _reconstruct_from_ipc_extra storage = _pool_handle_cache_get_or_open(cache_key, redirected_handle) File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 75, in _pool_handle_cache_get_or_open storage = _open_pooled_storage_uncached(pool_handle) File "sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py", line 66, in _open_pooled_storage_uncached return torch.UntypedStorage._new_shared_cuda(*pool_handle) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid resource handle ``` Setting `SGLANG_USE_IPC_POOL_HANDLE_CACHE=0` does not help — the uncached path uses the same unsupported CUDA IPC calls. ## Expected behaviour Either: 1. **Auto-detect WSL2** in `_handle_multimodal_feature_transport` and resolve to `cpu` instead of `cuda_ipc`, the same way multi-node and PD-disaggregated deployments already fall back; or 2. **Point at the fix in the error.** The current traceback names no flag. A message such as `CUDA IPC is unavailable (common on WSL2). Pass --mm-feature-transport=cpu.` would save a lot of time. Option 1 seems consistent with the existing auto policy in `server_args.py`, which already narrows `cuda_ipc` to cases where it is known to work. WSL2 can be detected by checking for `microsoft` / `WSL` in `/proc/version` or `uname -r`. ## Workaround ``` --mm-feature-transport cpu ``` Confirmed working: the server starts, text and vision requests both succeed, and a 190K-token prompt completes without issue. The only cost is routing image features through host memory. ## Environment - GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32 GB) - OS: Windows 11 + WSL2, kernel `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2` - Docker image: `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b` - Model: `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (multimodal, hybrid GDN) ## Related Other CUDA IPC transport fallback issues, though neither covers WSL2: #33687, #29687

signal.title: [DSV4] Split mixed-chunk attention: route decode tokens to the fp8 paged MLA kernel
signal.text: ## Motivation With `--enable-mixed-chunk`, every step in the high-concurrency steady state is a mixed batch (prefill chunk + one decode token per running request), and all tokens go through the bf16 sparse-prefill workspace path. This forces two `_dequantize_k_cache_paged` calls per layer covering every running request's SWA window (~16.9 ms/step at conc 2048 on 8xB300), and the fp8-native decode kernel is never used in steady state. ## Modification `mix_with_running` appends decode requests after prefill requests (one token each), so decode tokens are the contiguous tail of the batch. Split at that boundary: - decode tail -> fp8-native `flash_mla_with_kvcache` (row-sliced topk indices, no dequant); - prefill head -> existing bf16 sparse path, with `SparsePrefillChunkCache` built over the prefill requests only, shrinking the dequant workspace. Controlled by `SGLANG_OPT_MIXED_SPLIT_DECODE_ATTN` (default on; set to 0 to fall back to the previous behavior). ## Results 8xB300, DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, 8k1k, conc 2048 (megamoe + dp-attention + mixed-chunk), radix cache enabled with forced misses, num_prompts = 6x conc, warmup = 2x conc. Back-to-back A/B on the same machine with byte-identical launch commands; the only variable is this commit (feature default-on for the comparison): | | Without this commit | With this commit | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput (tok/s) | 8983.25 | **9828.27** | **+9.4%** | | Median TPOT (ms) | 196.25 | 177.20 | -9.7% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 196.89 | 178.37 | -9.4% | | Median TTFT (ms) | 26925 | 24517 | -8.9% | | Successful requests | 12288/12288 | 12288/12288 | — | GSM8K under concurrency (mixed steps active): 0.970 with the flag vs 0.980 without, within noise (n=200). ## TODO (draft) - Done: `num_mixed_decode_tokens` is recorded by `mix_with_running` and plumbed through `ForwardBatch`. A temporary cross-check assert against a tail-scan of `extend_seq_lens` ran clean over 16k requests (~4.7k mixed steps) and has been removed. - Full GSM8K (1319) + a long-context eval; conc 1024 regression check. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31791518956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31791518956)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31791518814](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31791518814)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(openai): Accept the input_audio content part in chat completions
signal.text: ## Motivation OpenAI's Chat Completions API carries inline audio as an `input_audio` content part, holding base64 data plus a format label. SGLang accepts audio only as `audio_url`, an sglang extension whose payload is a URL or a data URI. A request written against the OpenAI spec therefore fails schema validation with a 400 before it reaches the model, on every audio-capable model served through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Inkling, Gemma 4, MiMo-V2.5, and others). ## Modifications - `ChatCompletionMessageContentAudioPart` becomes an annotated union of two concrete variants: the existing `audio_url` part, and a new `input_audio` part. - An `AfterValidator` rewrites an `input_audio` part into the equivalent `audio_url` data URI as it validates, using the registered media type for the declared format (`wav` → `audio/wav`, `mp3` → `audio/mpeg`). - Nothing downstream changes. The conversation parser, the chat-template parser, and the multimodal loader continue to handle `audio_url` alone, so both spellings share one code path and a client's choice between them stops being visible past validation. - Existing `audio_url` requests are unaffected: the variant passes through untouched, for both HTTP(S) URLs and data URIs. - The cookbook pages that describe the audio content-part format (Inkling, Inkling-Small, Gemma 4) now name `input_audio` alongside `audio_url`. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable; this is request-schema validation only and does not affect model outputs. Inline audio is rewritten to the data URI form that `audio_url` already accepted, so the decoded waveform and the resulting prompt are identical to those of an equivalent `audio_url` request. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable; the added work is one dict lookup and one string concatenation per audio content part, at validation time. ## Test Plan 8 new unit tests: 7 protocol cases covering conversion for both formats, `audio_url` passthrough for a URL and a data URI, rejection of an unsupported format, rejection of a missing payload on either variant, and that the JSON schema advertises both spellings; plus one end-to-end case in the conversation-parser tests, built from raw dicts so the parts go through validation the way a request body does, confirming inline audio arrives as a data URI at a parser that only knows `audio_url`. ``` python -m pytest \ test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py \ test/registered/unit/parser/test_conversation.py \ test/registered/unit/parser/test_jinja_template_utils.py # 139 passed ``` Both test files are already registered on `base-a-test-cpu`, so the new cases run in CI without registry changes. ## Checklist - [x] Format the code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests. - [x] Update the documentation: the cookbook pages describing the audio content-part format now name `input_audio`. - [x] Accuracy and speed benchmarks are not applicable. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32057038950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32057038950)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32057038648](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32057038648)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse the ROCm DSA indexer q/k prep into aiter's single kernel
signal.text:
## Summary On ROCm the DSA indexer spends 11 kernels per decode layer on q/k prep. This PR collapses most of that into one aiter kernel. * `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` does k LayerNorm + RoPE + fp8 quant + paged index-k store, q RoPE + fp8 quant, and the head-gate scale in a single launch — six kernels become one. Like the CUDA fused path it drops the Hadamard rotation, which is logit-preserving and only shifts fp8 quantisation error. Prefill drops it too, since prefill writes the index-K cache decode reads back and the two must agree on basis. * `wk` and `weights_proj` are folded into one `wk_weights_proj` GEMM. This needs only the concatenated weight, no fused kernel, but was gated on CUDA; it now runs on CUDA or HIP and is numerically identical to the split projections. * The aiter kernel is tuned for decode's one-token-per-sequence shape and costs about twice what it replaces at prefill widths, so it is gated to decode. It also requires gfx95x, `SGLANG_USE_AITER`, and an aiter build exporting the symbol — a capability probe, not a preference: anything outside the envelope falls back to the existing path. CUDA and NPU are unchanged. Decode indexer on GLM-5.2 / MI355X: **11 kernels / 70.8 us per layer → 5 kernels / 41.4 us (−41.5%)**, which closes the MI355X-vs-B200 indexer gap from 2.55x to 1.49x. Drive-by fix: define the module-level `_use_dsa_indexer_fusion` that `lora_manager.py` already imports but nothing defined, so an indexer-targeted LoRA adapter raised `ImportError` instead of the intended `ValueError`. ## Test plan MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, fp8 KV, `chunked_prefill=16384`, DSA backend triton, i8192 / o1024, one run per point. Baseline is the same AMD GLM-5.2 stack without this PR (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324, #32888, plus ROCm/aiter#4453). | conc | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 323.3 → 335.9 (+3.9%) | 10.61 → 10.16 (−4.2%) | 366.7 → 367.6 (+0.2%) | | 8 | 465.3 → 482.3 (+3.6%) | 14.02 → 13.43 (−4.2%) | 379.1 → 379.8 (+0.2%) | | 16 | 731.5 → 762.9 (+4.3%) | 15.73 → 14.86 (−5.5%) | 378.0 → 383.3 (+1.4%) | | 32 | 1044.3 → 1081.1 (+3.5%) | 19.39 → 18.37 (−5.3%) | 393.7 → 389.5 (−1.1%) | | 64 | 1342.4 → 1382.2 (+3.0%) | 25.33 → 24.03 (−5.1%) | 631.6 → 615.6 (−2.5%) | ITL improves −4.2% to −5.5% at every concurrency, matching the 29.4 us/layer the kernel table predicts over the 21 layers that run the indexer (0.62 ms per decode forward). TTFT is flat, which is the check that matters given the kernel is decode-only. GSM8K (1200 questions): 0.928 baseline, 0.934 this PR. The index-K cache is bit-exact against the unfused path across both `preshuffle` and `scale_fmt`; the q fp8 payload differs by 1 ULP on 0.10% of elements, because aiter multiplies by the reciprocal rather than dividing.
Per-layer decode indexer kernels, and why the aiter kernel is decode-only | baseline | us | this PR | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (wk) | 6.59 | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (merged wk_weights_proj) | 6.50 | | `hgemm_16x64x64x6` (weights_proj) | 5.30 | — | — | | `Layernorm2dFwd` | 4.19 | `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` | 5.60 | | `kn_entry_2c_sbhd_cached_indirect` (RoPE) | 8.78 | | | | `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` | 4.43 | | | | `_hadamard_quant_kernel` | 4.55 | | | | `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 4.19 | | | | `triton_poi_fused_mul_unsqueeze_0` | 4.18 | | | | `wv_splitk_small` (q proj) | 5.70 | `wv_splitk_small` | 5.95 | | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.34 | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.46 | | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.60 | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.93 | | **total** | **70.8** | **total** | **41.4** | Of the 29.4 us/layer saved, 5.4 is the merged projection and 21.3 is six kernels becoming one; downstream topk and logits move by 0.1–0.3 us, which is noise. With the aiter kernel enabled for prefill too, the prefill indexer went from 1614.5 up to 1780.5 us/layer: the fused kernel alone costs 300.4 us/layer against the 162.8 of the six it replaces, and drags downstream topk and logits ~8% each. Gating it to decode gives prefill 1519.6 us/layer (−5.9%), since prefill still benefits from the merged projection and from dropping the Hadamard.

signal.title: ci: prefetch HF snapshots and skip redundant metadata calls to survive 429s
signal.text: ## Summary CI 429s against the HF API (example: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/24707205487/job/72263640803) happen when a runner has an incomplete cache for a test's model — the offline-mode guard falls through to online, the server launch issues `HfFileSystem.ls()` → `repo_info` (`python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py:502-503`), and one saturated 5-min window 429s every concurrent job. This PR closes the leak: - **`_try_enable_offline_mode_if_cache_complete`** (`python/sglang/test/test_utils.py`) used to bail to online mode whenever the cache was missing or incomplete. Now calls the new `_ci_prefetch_snapshot` which does a full `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download` with `max_workers=1` (NFS `.incomplete` safety), 3-retry 429 handling that honors `Retry-After`, and recovers a 429 signal from `str(e)` when the error has no `response` object. With the snapshot populated, offline mode is enabled for the server subprocess so the failing `fs.ls()` — which is gated on `not HF_HUB_OFFLINE` — is skipped entirely. Matches the vllm pattern of per-launch snapshot fetches; no manifest to maintain, new test models just work. - **`scripts/ci/utils/prevalidate_cached_models.py`**: parallelize the per-snapshot validation with `ThreadPoolExecutor(16)`. Each worker assembles its full log block as a single string to avoid interleave; the main loop wraps `future.result()` in try/except so one worker raising doesn't abort the whole pass (matches prior serial `FAIL (error)` behavior). Expected runtime on a 221-snapshot cache: ~47s → a few seconds. Failure path on a persistent 429 window is preserved (best-effort: prefetch gives up after 3 retries and falls through to online, same as today). ## Test plan - [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` — clean on touched files. - [ ] Re-trigger the failing job (`stage-b-test-2-gpu-large (0)` on PR #23281) and confirm the `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` server launch now enables `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` instead of 429'ing. - [ ] Verify prepare_runner.sh `Prepare runner` step drops from ~60s to ~15-20s on a warm cache (221 snapshots). - [ ] Spot-check log output: per-snapshot blocks remain intact (each `[idx/total] model` header is immediately followed by its PASS/FAIL/SKIP line, even with 16 concurrent workers). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: WIP: [Speculative] Add draft-DP mode to eliminate allreduce/all-to-all during draft multi-step decode
signal.text: ## Motivation In speculative decoding with MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-R1 with MTP), the draft model's multi-step decode phase incurs significant collective communication overhead (allreduce, all-to-all) across TP/EP ranks. Since the draft model is much smaller than the target model, running it with full TP/EP parallelism is wasteful — the communication cost dominates the compute savings. This PR introduces `--speculative-draft-dp`, which runs the draft model with data parallelism (tp_size=1, ep_size=1 per rank), so each rank loads all draft experts locally and skips all collective communication during draft decode steps. ## Modifications - **`server_args.py`**: Add `--speculative-draft-dp` flag with validation logic (auto-sets `--speculative-moe-a2a-backend=none`, warns if tp/ep=1). - **`parallel_state.py`**: - Extend `patch_tensor_parallel_group` with `also_patch_attn_tp` parameter for full TP+ATTN_TP patching. - Add `patch_moe_parallel_group` context manager to temporarily override `_MOE_EP` / `_MOE_TP`. - **`spec_utils.py`**: Add `draft_dp_full_context` (patches TP+ATTN_TP+MOE_EP+MOE_TP) and `create_draft_dp_group` (creates a single-rank GroupCoordinator per rank). - **`eagle_worker.py`**: - Draft init: patch parallel groups so draft model weights are loaded with tp=1, ep=1; allgather target's embed/lm_head for the draft model. - Draft forward: wrap multi-step decode, draft extend, and draft extend-after-decode with `_draft_forward_context` to patch MoE A2A backend. - Support both draft-DP + DPA (recommended) and draft-DP standalone paths. ## Benchmark Results **Setup:** 8×B200, DeepSeek-R1 MTP, FP8, same prompt and parameters. ### Throughput & Latency | Metric | DPA Baseline | Draft DP | Change | |--------|-------------|----------|--------| | Avg throughput | 97.1 tok/s | 101.7 tok/s | **+4.7%** | | Avg latency | 2.65s | 2.53s | **-4.5%** | | Avg accept_len | 2.64 | 2.65 | ≈0 (correctness verified) | ### Profile (same workload) | Metric | Baseline | Draft DP | Change | |--------|----------|----------|--------| | Total communication | 5838ms (38.1%) | 4672ms (31.2%) | **-20%** | | Total GPU time | 15343ms | 14980ms | **-2.4%** | | NCCL AllGather | 2827ms | 2137ms | **-24%** | | custom allreduce 2stage | 1708 calls | 1152 calls | **-32.5%** | | FP8 GEMM (bmm) | 1877ms | 2139ms | +14% (draft computes more experts) | | fused_moe | 154ms | 253ms | +64% (8 vs 1 expert/rank) | **Key takeaway:** Draft-DP trades a small increase in per-rank compute (each rank runs all draft experts) for a large reduction in communication overhead, resulting in a net **4.7% throughput improvement** and **4.5% latency reduction**. Accept length remains unchanged, confirming correctness. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Loading `amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4` with MTP (speculative EAGLE) fails during weight loading: ``` File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py", line 314, in load_weights super().load_weights(weights, is_nextn=True) File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2339, in load_weights self.do_load_weights(weights, is_nextn) File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 361, in do_load_weights future.result() ... File "sglang/srt/layers/linear.py", line 271, in weight_loader assert param.size() == loaded_weight.size() ``` **Root cause:** `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN.hf_to_sglang_mapper` maps **all** `model.layers.61.*` weight names to `model.decoder.*`. This is correct for decoder sub-modules (self_attn, mlp), but incorrect for NextN-specific weights (`eh_proj`, `embed_tokens`, `enorm`, `hnorm`, `shared_head`) which live directly under `model`, not `model.decoder`. This causes the quark quantization exclude list to be incorrectly transformed: | Checkpoint name | Mapped name (before fix) | Actual param prefix | Correct? | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `model.layers.61.eh_proj` | `model.decoder.eh_proj` | `model.eh_proj` | No | | `model.layers.61.embed_tokens` | `model.decoder.embed_tokens` | `model.embed_tokens` | No | | `model.layers.61.enorm` | `model.decoder.enorm` | `model.enorm` | No | | `model.layers.61.hnorm` | `model.decoder.hnorm` | `model.hnorm` | No | | `model.layers.61.shared_head` | `model.decoder.shared_head` | `model.shared_head` | No | | `model.layers.61.self_attn.*` | `model.decoder.self_attn.*` | `model.decoder.self_attn.*` | Yes | | `model.layers.61.mlp.*` | `model.decoder.mlp.*` | `model.decoder.mlp.*` | Yes | Because `should_ignore_layer("model.eh_proj", ["model.decoder.eh_proj", ...])` fails to match, `QuarkLinearMethod` creates FP4-packed parameter ## Modifications - Update `hf_to_sglang_mapper` in `DeepseekV3ForCausalLMNextN` to add explicit longer-prefix mappings for NextN-specific weights (`eh_proj`, `embed_tokens`, `enorm`, `hnorm`, `shared_head`). Since `WeightsMapper` sorts by substring length (longest first), these specific entries take priority over the generic `model.layers.61 -> model.decoder` fallback. - After this fix, the quark exclude list is correctly mapped, `should_ignore_layer` properly identifies `eh_proj` as excluded, and `UnquantizedL ## Accuracy Tests **DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4 launch cmd** ```bash sglang serve --model-path /dockerx/data2/models/amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4-MTP-MoEFP4/ \ --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size=8 \ --chunked-prefill-size=32768 \ --mem-fraction-static=0.8 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --num-continuous-decode-steps=4 \ --max-prefill-tokens=32768 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs=256 \ --attention-backend aiter \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \ --speculative-num-steps 3 \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 ``` **GSM8K evaluation cmd** ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --port 30000 ``` | Model | GSM8K acc | Output throughput | | --- | --- | --- | | dpsk-r1-0528-mxfp4-mtp-moefp4 (mtp, before fix) | CRASH | N/A | | dpsk-r1-0528-mxfp4-mtp-moefp4 (mtp, after fix) | **0.960** | 582.3 tok/s | ## Related Model Tests | Model | Config | GSM8K Accuracy | Throughput | Status | |--------|--------|--------|--------|--------| | DeepSeek-R1-0528 | no MTP | 0.955 | 676.8 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528 | EAGLE + external NextN draft | 0.975 | 999.5 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 | EAGLE (built-in MTP) | 0.935 | 1621.3 tok/s | PASS | | DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 | EAGLE + external NextN draft | 0.935 | 1369.5 tok/s | PASS | | GLM-5.1-MXFP4 | EAGLE (built-in MTP) | 0.965 | 687.9 tok/s | PASS | ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist -
