signal.title: [NPU] Add CI tests for Dynamic Batch Tokenizer
signal.text: ## Motivation This PR introduces comprehensive NPU-side test coverage for the --enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer feature and its associated parameters (--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size, --dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout). The dynamic batch tokenizer significantly reduces tokenization overhead under high concurrency by asynchronously batching incoming requests, which is especially beneficial for deployments with many short-prompt requests. The added test suite verifies correctness and stability under various configurations (batch size 1 and 64, different timeouts), concurrency patterns, mixed prompt lengths, streaming, varied sampling parameters, and compatibility with disabled radix cache. It also includes an accuracy regression test using the GSM8K benchmark to ensure no degradation in generation quality. In addition, a utility helper send_concurrent_requests is added to test_ascend_utils.py to enable true concurrent HTTP load generation using threading (avoiding asyncio limitations with blocking I/O). The new test is registered for the NPU nightly CI suite. ## Modifications 1. **Dynamic Batch Tokenizer Logic:** - Implemented an `AsyncDynamicBatchTokenizer` that maintains an internal async queue. - A background task `_dynamic_batch_loop` continuously collects incoming requests. - Supports dynamic batching based on `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size` and `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout`. - Utilizes a single-threaded `ThreadPoolExecutor` to handle blocking tokenizer calls safely. 2. **Server Arguments:** - Added `--enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer` to activate the feature. - Added `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size` (default: 32) to control the maximum batch window. - Added `--dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout` (default: 0.002s) to balance latency and throughput. 3. **Utility Enhancement:** - Added `send_concurrent_requests` in `test_ascend_utils.py` to facilitate reliable concurrency testing for NPU environments. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K accuracy is measured for both configurations using run_eval with 200 examples and max_new_tokens=512. The threshold is set to 0.86. Observed scores in NPU CI runs: Configuration GSM8K Score Latency (s) Throughput (tok/s) batch_size=64, timeout=0.001 ~0.87–0.88 ~12.5 ~620 batch_size=1, timeout=0.005 ~0.87–0.88 ~11.8 ~650 The accuracy remains well above the 0.86 baseline, confirming that the dynamic batch tokenizer does not degrade model output quality. ## Speed Tests and Profiling While this PR focuses on correctness testing, the GSM8K runs also provide indicative performance metrics. The throughput and latency numbers above are collected from actual NPU hardware (Atlas A3 4-card TP=4). signal.title: [Bug Fix] Fix actor name and port collision in RayEngine for multi-replica deployments
signal.text: ## Motivation When deploying multiple SGLangServer replicas on the same node via Ray Serve, two bugs cause replica initialization to fail: 1. **Actor name collision**: Named actors in `RayEngine` are keyed only on `rank0_node_ip + pp_rank + tp_rank`. When multiple replicas share the same host, they generate identical actor names, causing: `ray.exceptions.ActorAlreadyExistsError: The name sglang_scheduler_rank0node=<IP>_pp0_tp0 is already taken.` 2. **Port collision**: The torch.distributed rendezvous port is derived from `server_args.port + ZMQ_TCP_PORT_DELTA`, which is the same across replicas on the same host, causing: `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: address already in use (EADDRINUSE)` ## Modifications 1. **Actor name**: Prefixed with `port{server_args.port}` — since each replica must listen on a unique HTTP port, this disambiguates actor names across replicas on the same node without requiring a UUID. 2. **Port collision**: Use `get_free_port()` to atomically grab a free OS port at `RayEngine` construction time, the same way `nccl_port` is already allocated. ## Tests Validated on a single node with 2x A10G GPUs using Ray Serve with `min_replicas=2`, `max_replicas=2`. Both replicas initialize successfully on the same node with no actor name or port collisions. Autoscaler and MultiNode test in progress. ![sglang-ray-multiserver](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df74464d-6149-47e0-afbb-5ae20b0f917d) ## Related - Ray issue: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/62480 - Ray PR: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/62504

signal.title: [bugfix]  Fix unnecessary recompilation in fla l2norm_fwd_kernel by removing constexpr from runtime T
signal.text: ## Motivation This kernel is invoked by GDN / KDA / RWKV-style linear-attention layers on every forward pass, so the recompilation penalty hits every request in production serving. In `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/l2norm.py`, the `l2norm_fwd_kernel` declares `T: tl.constexpr`. However, `T` represents the total number of input rows (`num_tokens` × `num_heads`), which is a **runtime-dynamic** value that changes on every batch during inference. In Triton, a `tl.constexpr` parameter is treated as a compile-time constant. Every distinct value of `T` triggers a full JIT recompilation of the kernel (~90 ms each on L20Y). During online serving, `T` varies continuously across batches, causing: - **Repeated unnecessary recompilations**: each new `T` value compiles a new kernel variant - **Unbounded compilation cache growth**: hundreds of kernel copies accumulate - **Latency spikes**: compilation overhead (~90 ms) dwarfs the kernel execution time (~0.03 ms) The upstream FLA library has already addressed this by using `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])` with `T` as a plain parameter: https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/fla/modules/l2norm.py `T` is only consumed by `tl.make_block_ptr(shape=(T, D), ...)` for shape description and boundary masking; it never participates in control flow, loop bounds, or constant folding. Therefore removing `constexpr` cannot change generated PTX semantics — only the specialization key. ## Modifications Two-line change in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/l2norm.py`: 1. `@triton.jit` → `@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])` 2. `T: tl.constexpr` → `T` (plain parameter) ```diff -@triton.jit +@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"]) def l2norm_fwd_kernel( x, y, eps, NB: tl.constexpr, - T: tl.constexpr, + T, D: tl.constexpr, BT: tl.constexpr, BD: tl.constexpr, ): ``` Added test file: `test/manual/layers/test_fla_l2norm.py`---- — this is a verification script for reviewers to reproduce the fix, and is not intended to be merged into the main codebase. Feel free to remove it before merging. ## Accuracy Tests Both kernel variants (constexpr `T` vs runtime `T`) tested against a pure-PyTorch L2 norm reference implementation (float32 accumulation) with `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2` on bfloat16 inputs. 10 different `T` values with fixed `D=128`: | T | constexpr T | runtime T | |-----|-------------|-----------| | 16 | PASS | PASS | | 37 | PASS | PASS | | 64 | PASS | PASS | | 100 | PASS | PASS | | 128 | PASS | PASS | | 200 | PASS | PASS | | 256 | PASS | PASS | | 333 | PASS | PASS | | 500 | PASS | PASS | | 777 | PASS | PASS | Both variants produce numerically identical results. The change does not affect computation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Environment**: NVIDIA L20Y (80 GB, SM90), CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.9.1, Triton 3.5.1 **Test methodology**: Two independent kernel copies defined in the test file (one with `T: tl.constexpr`, one with plain `T`). Same inputs, same launch parameters. The only difference is the `T` declaration. **Experiment parameters**: - `D=128` (fixed, typical `head_k_dim` for GDN/KDA models) - `dtype=bfloat16` - `BT=16, BD=128, NB=1, num_warps=8` (all fixed `constexpr`) - `T` is the **only** varying parameter across calls ### Compilation count (10 different T values, NB=1 for all) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | New compilations | 10 | 0 | | Cache growth | 1 → 11 | 1 → 1 | ### End-to-end latency (20 batches, T=16,32,...,320) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |---------------|-------------------|-------------------| | Total time | 1335.14 ms | 0.60 ms | | Per-batch avg | 66.76 ms | 0.03 ms | | **Speedup** | — | **2224x** | > Note: the 2224x figure reflects steady-state inference where the old version recompiles on nearly every batch. The cold-start table below (10.7x) reflects the worst case where the new version still pays one compilation. ### Cold-start latency (fresh kernels, 10 batches, T=16,66,...,466) | | constexpr T (old) | runtime T (fixed) | |---------------------|-------------------|-------------------| | Total time | 903.9 ms | 84.5 ms | | Compilations | 10 | 1 | | Per-batch avg | 90.4 ms | 8.4 ms | | **Speedup** | — | **10.7x** | | Wasted compile time | ~819 ms | — | ## Reproduce ```bash python test/manual/layers/test_fla_l2norm.py ``` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). *(N/A — internal kernel optimization, no user-facing API change)* - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Kernel] Support wider rows in mega_moe_pre_dispatch
signal.text: ## Motivation `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` assigns one thread to each 8-element input chunk, so a single CUDA block can only cover hidden dimensions up to 8192. Wider shapes are rejected before launch. ## Modifications - Cap the block size at the CUDA 1024-thread limit and process wider rows in strided chunks. - Recompute quantization-group indices for each chunk while preserving the UE8M0 scale layout. - Keep a separate single-chunk kernel specialization so existing shapes retain the same instruction path. - Reject wide shapes whose tail would split a warp-level reduction. ## Accuracy Tests - Verified bitwise FP8 output and UE8M0 scale bytes against a reference implementation for hidden dimensions 3584, 5632, 8192, 12288, and 16384. - Verified exact top-k copies and idle-slot padding. - Verified that hidden dimension 8320 fails with the expected full-warp alignment error. - JIT-compiled the ported CUDA header successfully. ## Speed Tests and Profiling - The single-chunk specialization produces the same SASS instruction stream as the previous kernel. - CUDA-event microbenchmarks showed no measurable regression for shapes that already fit in one chunk. ## Original commits - `d7c54c96f5` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). signal.title: HotFix EAGLE3 target/draft global ServerArgs mix-up in chunked prefix cache path
signal.text: Fixes #22780 ## Summary This PR fixes a bug in the EAGLE3 speculative decoding path where target-side execution can observe draft-side runtime configuration inside the same scheduler process. This can break MLA target models such as `Kimi-K2.5` and eventually cause crashes like: ```text AssertionError ... assert not get_global_server_args().disable_chunked_prefix_cache ``` The investigation and local validation for this fix were done with the help of Codex. ## Root cause The target model (`kimi_k25`) and the EAGLE3 draft model (`LlamaForCausalLMEagle3`) use different attention architectures. - target model: MLA - draft model: non-MLA During draft worker initialization, `ModelRunner.model_specific_adjustment()` may set: ```python server_args.disable_chunked_prefix_cache = True ``` The investigation showed two layers of the problem: 1. The draft worker could overwrite target-side settings when the same `ServerArgs` object was reused. 2. Even after isolating the draft worker with a copied `ServerArgs`, runtime forward paths still relied on `get_global_server_args()`, so target execution could still read draft-side configuration if the active process-global state was left pointing at the draft side. Later, the target model could enter the chunked prefix cache path and hit a hard assertion because target execution was reading the wrong process-global runtime configuration. ## Fix This PR applies a scoped fix in `eagle_worker_v2.py`: - keep draft and target `ServerArgs` isolated - restore the correct target-side global runtime configuration before entering target execution paths - restore the correct draft-side global runtime configuration before entering draft execution paths With this change: - the draft worker can still apply its own model-specific adjustments - those settings remain local to the draft side - target execution runs with target-side global configuration - draft execution runs with draft-side global configuration - `disable_chunked_prefix_cache` is no longer incorrectly observed from the wrong side during target execution ## Why this is the minimal fix The deeper architectural issue is that some runtime forward paths still depend on process-global `ServerArgs`. A broader cleanup would replace those global reads with runner-local configuration. This PR intentionally does not attempt that larger refactor. Instead, it provides a focused and low-risk fix in `eagle_worker_v2.py` that prevents target/draft global configuration mix-ups in the observed failing path. ## User-visible impact This prevents crashes for configurations such as: - `Kimi-K2.5` - `EAGLE3` - long context - high KV-cache pressure In particular, it fixes the case where `kv cache full` is followed by a later assertion in the FlashAttention chunked-prefix path.[](url) I use Codex to help prepare and verify the fix during local debugging.

signal.title: [Spec] Add LFM2 and LFM2-MoE DSpark speculative decoding support
signal.text: ### What Adds DSpark speculative-decoding support for the LFM2 hybrid (ShortConv + attention) family: both the dense **LFM2** and MoE **LFM2-MoE** targets. Follow-up to #30261 (DSpark), now that it has landed on `main`. Two commits: 1. **Interleaved RoPE in the fused-KV kernel** - the fused RMSNorm+RoPE materialization only handled neox rotation. Adds an `IS_NEOX` constexpr selecting the pairing (neox: `(i, i+rotary/2)`; interleaved/GPT-J: `(2i, 2i+1)`); no change for existing neox drafts. LFM2 draft exports rotate interleaved and need this. 2. **LFM2 / LFM2-MoE target support** - the draft is a DSpark checkpoint (Qwen3-style GQA backbone, markov + confidence heads) exported with interleaved RoPE. It registers as its own `Lfm2DSparkDraftModel` arch (a thin `DSparkDraftModel` subclass, mirroring `Qwen3DSparkModel`) so the LFM2 draft can gain LFM2-specific layers - e.g. ShortConv/conv1d - later without touching the shared classes. Interleaved RoPE and the confidence head come from the checkpoint config; the kernel change handles the rotation. Only the target side needs code beyond that: aux-hidden capture + ShortConv block verify/rollback in `lfm2.py`/`lfm2_moe.py`, hybrid-state commit after verify in the DSpark worker (mirrors the DFlash worker so decoding stays lossless), routing the draft KV injector through the fused-KV path, and marking the LFM2 archs eligible for the `extra_buffer` mamba radix strategy that spec-v2 rollback needs. Net: 7 files, +422/-23, no changes to existing DSpark behavior. Base LFM2-MoE serving parity (the attention-backend / radix-cache override tables for `Lfm2MoeForCausalLM`) is independent of DSpark and is in its own PR: #30780. Pair with it for the 8B target's serving defaults. ### Speedup 1xH100 80GB, bs=1, temperature 0, block size 7, accept length / speedup vs the same server minus spec flags: | dataset | LFM2.5-1.2B + 5L | LFM2.5-8B-A1B + 3L | |---|---|---| | math500 (chat math) | 4.82 / **2.10x** | 5.42 / **2.21x** | | aime (competition math) | 4.36 / 1.95x | 6.20 / **2.42x** | | humaneval (code) | 4.41 / 1.93x | - | | mbpp (code) | 4.45 / 1.95x | 4.80 / 1.96x | | gsm8k (grade-school math) | 3.73 / 1.49x | 3.51 / 1.24x | | mtbench (multi-turn chat) | 2.35 / 1.05x | 5.87 / **2.32x** | Floor is short chat on the small dense target (~1.05x); ceiling is long reasoning on the MoE (2.3-2.4x, accept near the block-7 limit). Accuracy at parity with baseline on every scoreable bench. Note: interleaved RoPE (commit 1) is not optional for these drafts. Serving them neox collapses accept length to ~1.9 vs ~5.1 interleaved. ### Public draft checkpoints - dense: https://huggingface.co/tugot17/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-DSpark-5L (target `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct`) - MoE: https://huggingface.co/tugot17/LFM2.5-8B-A1B-DSpark-3L (target `LiquidAI/LFM2.5-8B-A1B`) ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path LiquidAI/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path tugot17/LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct-DSpark-5L \ --speculative-draft-attention-backend flashinfer ``` ### Testing Validated in serving on 1xH100 across the benches above (dense + MoE, draft depths 2L/3L/5L). The MoE ShortConv decode uses the same CUDA `causal_conv1d_update` kernel as dense (an earlier triton swap was removed after confirming identical accept, 5.936 both ways). Happy to add a gated CI test under `test/registered/spec/dspark/` against the public checkpoints. Supersedes #30776, which was opened against the DSpark PR branch before it merged; rebased onto `main`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #30454618242](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30454618242)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #30454620279](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30454620279)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [SM12x] Drop the 64-head TP pad on the DSv4 MLA prefill path
signal.text: ## Problem With `attn_tp_size=2`, `MQALayer` builds a **64-row** query tensor, writes only `[0:n_local_heads]` (= 32), runs attention on all 64 rows, and discards half the output via `o = o[:, tp_slice, :]`. ```python # FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel only specializes h_q for {64, 128}. padded_num_heads = 64 if self.n_local_heads <= 64 else self.n_heads ``` That comment is true of `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` — the `else` branch at `deepseek_v4_backend.py:1774`, which SM12x never takes. On SM12x the kernel is FlashInfer's, and the decode/prefill split happens **by row count** inside the FlashInfer entry (`B <= _DECODE_MAX_TOKENS`, `flash_mla_sm120.py:558`), **not by forward mode**. So a wide prefill chunk is dispatched to the paged/prefill kernel, which takes arbitrary `h_q`, and the pad buys it nothing. MLA is the one place where this is pure waste rather than a wash: 64 query heads share a **single** latent KV (`num_key_value_heads = 1`), so head-sharding saves compute without saving KV bandwidth. Prefill (many query rows, compute-bound) scales with head count; decode (few rows, KV-bandwidth-bound) does not. ## Fix Gate the pad off for wide prefill chunks only, behind `SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_UNPAD_PREFILL_MLA_HEADS` (default on, SM12x only). - **row term — this is the one that selects the kernel.** Strictly above `_DECODE_MAX_TOKENS`, read from FlashInfer (`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py`; 64 in every flashinfer release to date) rather than hardcoded, so the gate and the dispatch fork at `flash_mla_sm120.py:558` are provably the same number. If FlashInfer ever raised that cutoff, a hardcoded 64 here would unpad rows that still route to the decode kernel — a silent kernel-family swap, not a crash. That is what the import buys. - **mode terms — scope, not legality.** `is_extend_or_draft_extend_or_mixed()` (an allowlist, *not* `is_extend()`, which is also `True` for `TARGET_VERIFY`), plus `_original_forward_mode` because DP padding can rewrite a verify batch into `EXTEND`. To be explicit about what these do and do not do: FlashInfer's SM120 decode kernel is instantiated for `num_heads ∈ {8,16,32,64,128}` as well (`_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH`), so unpadding is *legal* on both sides of the row fork. The mode terms exist to keep `TARGET_VERIFY` and large-`bs` `DECODE` — both CUDA-graph-captured — on exactly the kernel instantiation they run today. I would rather change one path at a time here than two. - Because the gate reads `forward_mode`, which is not part of a captured graph's shape key, it bails under `is_in_breakable_cuda_graph()`. That is a consequence of the mode terms, not an independent requirement; a row-count-only gate would not need it (and would also work under `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill=breakable`, where this PR is a no-op). Supporting changes: - `sm120_flashmla_decode_max_tokens()` exposes the threshold instead of duplicating the constant. On an import failure it returns a value no batch can exceed, so the gate fails **closed** (everything keeps the pad). It returns `0` when the backend is not FlashInfer — there the triton and torch fallbacks read `h_q` off the query shape, so there is no floor to respect and the gate is free to fire. - `_local_attn_sink()` takes an optional `num_heads`. The narrowed sink is a **prefix view** of the cached padded tensor, not a second allocation, so a device pointer baked into a captured decode graph stays valid; and when `num_heads` is `None` or already equals the stored width, the *same object* is returned. `DSparkAttention` (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py:246`) calls it with no argument and is unchanged — the DSPARK draft block stays padded. ## Measurements 2× DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, TP=2 across two nodes. - **MLA prefill lane: −49.7%** - Kernel instantiation goes from `sparse_mla_prefill_mg_dual_kernel<(ModelType)1, (ComputeMode)1, 64, ...>` to `<..., 32, ...>`, verified from an in-server profile rather than inferred from the launch flags. That profile is also the evidence that the gate actually fired. - That matches the geometry the reference vLLM deployment of this model runs on the same box (`<..., 32, 128, ...>`, grid `[4072,1,1]` vs ours `[4096,1,1]`, block `[384,1,1]`). Decode, `TARGET_VERIFY`, and the DSPARK draft block are untouched and stay padded. ## Correctness — what is and is not established - GSM8K 500 questions: 0.944 → 0.948, `Invalid: 0.000`. **This is the wrong instrument and I am not claiming it as evidence of equivalence.** Attention is per-`(token, head)` independent and the dropped heads were fed `new_empty` garbage and then sliced away, so the surviving heads *should* be bit-identical and the score *should* have been unchanged. A 2-in-500 delta means either the two runs differed in more than this flag, or the `NUM_HEADS=32` and `NUM_HEADS=64` template instantiations are not bit-identical on the heads that survive. **A gate-ON/gate-OFF greedy text-exact comparison is owed and I will post it.** - Shape safety on the path this PR changes is enforced by FlashInfer, loudly: `TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(attn_sink.size(0), num_heads)` and a compiled `switch (num_heads)` whose `default:` returns false into `TVM_FFI_ICHECK`. Nothing on the prefill path fails silently. ## Known gaps - **No head-count legality guard, and the head envelope is flashinfer-version-dependent.** The FlashInfer prefill dispatch is a closed `switch (num_heads)`. The `case 8:` instantiation landed with flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380 (merged 2026-08-08) — **after** the `v0.6.17` release branch was cut, so the version this repo pins (`flashinfer_python==0.6.17`) ships without it; the first releases carrying it are the `v0.6.18` nightlies. On the pinned wheel the prefill head set is `{16, 32, 64, 128}`: at `attn_tp_size = 8` (`n_local_heads = 8`) the unpadded path would abort where the padded path worked. `attn_tp_size ≥ 16` is already non-functional for this model for an unrelated reason (`o_groups = 8` ⇒ `n_local_groups = 0`). A `n_local_heads in (16, 32, 64, 128)` term in the gate would close this (16 as the floor while 0.6.17 is pinned); I would like a view on whether the allowlist or a capability probe is preferred. (Same-breath note, independent of this PR: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380 is also what adds the `topk ∈ {192, 256}` decode instantiations that SM12x DSPARK — topk fixed at 192 — needs, so stock `v0.6.17` fails that path regardless of head count.) - No test. The gate is a pure predicate over `(rows, forward_mode, _original_forward_mode, env, graph flag)` and is testable on CPU with `_is_sm120` and the threshold monkeypatched; happy to add it. - The pre-existing comment at `deepseek_v4.py:1362` attributes the `{64,128}` restriction to "FlashMLA's fp8 sparse decode kernel" without saying which kernel. It is correct for `sgl_kernel.flash_mla` and stale for the FlashInfer kernel SM12x calls. Say the word and I will amend it in this PR. ## Notes Only sm120/sm121 hardware was available; the gate is `is_sm120_supported()`-scoped and defaults off everywhere else. Note that `is_sm120_supported()` is `cc_major == 12`, so it also covers (12,0) parts I could not test — the row-threshold argument transfers because they take the same FlashInfer entry. CI: the red on `base-b-test-1-gpu-large (4)` is `test/registered/quant/test_awq.py::TestAWQMarlinBfloat16::test_mmlu` (`0.82421875 not greater than 0.83`), which is unrelated to this change and is currently flaky at its threshold on unrelated branches too — #34477 raised `num_examples` 64 → 256 without re-calibrating the bound. The CPU `build-test` and AMD failures reproduce on `main`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: [Spec] Generalize hybrid SWA MTP draft pool routing
signal.text: ## Motivation Multi-layer draft KV pools for hybrid sliding-window models are currently selected through Inkling-specific architecture checks. Other hybrid SWA models can expose the same per-depth attention pattern and should use the same SWA/full pool routing and memory accounting. ## Modifications - Detect hybrid SWA multi-layer drafts from generic configurator state instead of an architecture name. - Route each draft depth to the SWA or full-attention pool using the model's attention-layer metadata. - Account for full-capacity draft SWA rings from optional `mtp_local_layer_ids` metadata across hybrid SWA architectures. - Simplify comments that described the previous model-specific behavior. ## Accuracy Tests This changes KV-pool configuration only. The relevant upstream unit suites pass: ```text test_pool_configurator.py: 32 passed, 2 subtests passed test_mamba_donated_alloc_ratio.py: 8 passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked independently. This generalizes existing pool routing and memory accounting without changing the runtime attention kernels. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required for this allocator-configuration change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32183055554](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183055554)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32183055236](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32183055236)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: correct YaRN RoPE mscale calculation for models with mscale/msca…
signal.text: ## Motivation When deploying Ministral3ForCausalLM (e.g., `baidu/ERNIE-T2I-PE`) via the SRT engine, the model produces repetitive output ("repeater" phenomenon). The same model works correctly when loaded through HuggingFace's `AutoModelForCausalLM` in the `multimodal_gen` pipeline. Root cause: The SRT engine's `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` ignores the `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` parameters from `rope_parameters` in the model config. For Ministral3 (`mscale=1.0`, `mscale_all_dim=1.0`, `factor=16.0`), HuggingFace correctly computes `attention_factor = get_mscale(16, 1.0) / get_mscale(16, 1.0) = 1.0`, but the SRT engine was computing `mscale = yarn_get_mscale_simple(16.0) ≈ 1.277`, incorrectly scaling positional encodings by 27.7% and causing degraded attention quality and repetitive generation. ## Modifications - **`factory.py`**: Added `"mscale"` and `"mscale_all_dim"` to the `extra_kwargs` extraction in the `yarn` branch, so these parameters are passed through to `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` and `YaRNScalingMRotaryEmbedding`. - **`yarn.py`**: `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding.__init__` now accepts `mscale` and `mscale_all_dim` parameters. When both are provided, computes `mscale = yarn_get_mscale(factor, mscale) / yarn_get_mscale(factor, mscale_all_dim)` matching HuggingFace's logic. Falls back to the original `yarn_get_mscale_simple(scaling_factor) * attn_factor` when neither is provided, ensuring full backward compatibility. - **`mrope.py`**: `YaRNScalingMRotaryEmbedding` synced with the same fix. Added `yarn_get_mscale` to imports. ## Accuracy Tests Deployed `ERNIE-T2I-PE` on a single H800 GPU with the fix applied: ```bash curl http://localhost:8877/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "ERNIE-T2I-PE", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "{\"prompt\": \"a cat sitting on a windowsill\", \"width\": 1024, \"height\": 1024}"}], "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0.6, "top_p": 0.95 }' ``` Results: - **Before fix**: Model produces repetitive/looping text output - **After fix**: Model generates coherent, detailed visual descriptions without repetition. `finish_reason: "stop"` at EOS token correctly - Tested with multiple prompts (cat, sports car, sunset) and different temperatures (0.6, 1.0) — all produce correct output ## Speed Tests and Profiling This fix only changes the mscale value used in the RoPE cos/sin cache computation (computed once at initialization). No impact on inference speed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [Spec] Avoid multi-layer EAGLE SWA scheduler synchronization
signal.text: ## Motivation Paged sliding-window KV eviction performs a data-dependent uniqueness pass for request segments that are already complete and page-aligned. Multi-layer EAGLE also leaves the scheduler without the final draft graph's shared-read completion event, forcing a broader stream synchronization before the shared buffers can be reused. ## Modifications - Add a fixed-shape SWA segment-free path for page-aligned request prefixes, with the existing token path retained for page size 1 and unified allocation. - Route sliding-window eviction through that path when the allocator supports it. - Publish `shared_read_done_event` after the final multi-layer draft graph step, including the single-graph replay path. - Point the worker's last shared-read runner at the final draft runner. - Add allocator and CPU event-publication regression tests. ## Accuracy Tests No model-output behavior changes. The relevant unit suites pass: ```text 14 SWA allocator tests passed (plus 15 subtests) 14 SWA eviction-boundary tests passed 2 shared-read event tests passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked independently. The allocator change removes a device-side uniqueness operation from complete page-aligned SWA segments, and the event publication lets the scheduler use its event-scoped shared-read barrier for multi-layer EAGLE. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation is not required for this internal implementation change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). -Robot <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32182552708](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182552708)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32182552201](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182552201)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model Loader] Harden startup weight-load overlap and expand model coverage
signal.text: ## Summary This is the hardening and coverage follow-up to #32017. It keeps startup weight-load overlap opt-in while making the path safer to extend, adding an opt-in automatic fallback mode, and validating the overlap path on hybrid/VLM and MoE/EP models. - Replace implicit support checks with a structured, deterministic admission plan and rejection report. - Add `--startup-weight-load-mode=auto`: supported configurations use overlap, while rejected configurations retain serial startup. - Verify resolved checkpoint sources before capture-safe model mutation. If `auto` discovers PT or secondary weights, it reuses the already allocated model and resolved sources for serial loading rather than allocating the model twice. - Freeze graph-visible parameter, buffer, and explicitly registered derived-tensor storage across real-weight commit. - Fail closed when real loading leaves capture-safe sentinel values behind. - Report complete startup-overlap phase timings and assign `ModelRunner.weight_load_time` only after the real commit. - Harden best-effort checkpoint prefetch failure/cancellation behavior. - Add narrowly validated Qwen3.5 dense-hybrid, Qwen3.5 MoE-hybrid, and Qwen3 MoE EP profiles. The default remains `serial`. Explicit `overlap` still fails during preflight with deterministic reasons when unsupported; `auto` logs those reasons and follows the serial path. ## Supported profiles | Profile | Validated configuration | | --- | --- | | Native dense | Native `LlamaForCausalLM`, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`, or `Qwen3ForCausalLM`; FP16/BF16; TP1/TP2 | | Qwen3.5-family hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` (including Qwen3.6 dense checkpoints); BF16; TP2/TP4; Triton linear attention; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM | Native `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE and linear attention; standard EP path; breakable or disabled prefill CUDA graphs | | Qwen3 MoE EP | Native `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`; BF16; TP2+EP2; Triton MoE runner; standard EP path (`moe_a2a_backend=none`) | Quantization, speculative decoding, DP/PP/CP, LoRA, offload, DeepEP/other MoE A2A backends, EPLB, redundant or elastic experts, and unvalidated model implementations remain outside the overlap matrix. Qwen hybrid FullCG prefill is also excluded after an H100 probe reproduced an existing hybrid linear-attention replay failure during capture. `auto` sends these configurations through serial startup. ## Design details `StartupWeightLoadAdmission` separates side-effect-free config preflight from model-class resolution. The preflight only resolves/imports the native implementation after all cheap rules pass, so `auto` can select serial without remote-code imports, exception-driven control flow, or model mutation. Checkpoint format and secondary weights are only known after source resolution. That second fallback boundary remains before sentinel initialization. The default loader can therefore serial-load the real weights into the initialized model from the already resolved sources, preserving normal iterator prefetch/multithread behavior without a second model allocation. `ModelStorageManifest` records tensor identity, pointer, shape, stride, dtype, device, and storage offset after dummy post-load preparation. Finalization verifies that real loading refreshed the existing storage rather than rebinding anything captured by CUDA graphs. Models can explicitly enumerate graph-visible derived tensors through a per-module hook without a recursive attribute scan. Real-weight commit failures after capture-safe preparation are terminal startup failures. `auto` intentionally does not attempt an in-process serial retry after the model has been mutated or CUDA graphs have captured its storage. Page-cache prefetch remains best-effort: a failed worker falls back to the normal checkpoint reader, and late failures are reported without invalidating a successful real load. Both Scheduler startup and `bench_one_batch` route lifecycle hooks from the manager actually selected by admission, rather than from the requested mode string. ## H100 validation ### Qwen3.6 dense hybrid VLM `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B@6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`, BF16, TP2, FA3, Triton GDN, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. Three cold-cache trials per mode after one JIT warmup: | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 34.48 s | 28.05 s | -18.7% / 1.23x | | Process ready | 43.93 s | 37.48 s | -14.7% / 1.17x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 14.62 s | 7.59 s | -48.1% | Correctness covered BS1, BS2, long-prefix branching, and an image request. Text, token IDs, and output logprobs matched exactly; maximum absolute output-logprob difference was `0.0`. ### Qwen3.5 MoE hybrid VLM `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE and linear attention, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. Both modes started from zero resident checkpoint pages across 14 safetensors shards (71.9 GB): | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 149.70 s | 48.14 s | -67.8% / 3.11x | | Process ready | 158.52 s | 56.96 s | -64.1% / 2.78x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 126.61 s | 24.46 s | -80.7% | This is an end-to-end mode comparison, not a claim that CUDA-graph overlap alone exceeds the `t1 + t2 -> max(t1, t2)` bound. The overlap mode also coordinates checkpoint page-cache prefetch across TP ranks, so the result includes cold-storage I/O deduplication and a hot-cache real-weight commit. A serial+coordinated-prefetch arm is still needed to isolate the incremental graph-overlap contribution. Serial, overlap, and auto produced identical token IDs and output logprobs across three text prompts, a BS2 request, and an image request (six responses total). `auto` selected the `qwen3_5_moe_hybrid_vlm` profile. ### Qwen3 MoE with expert parallelism `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`, BF16, TP2+EP2, FA3, Triton MoE, standard EP, breakable prefill graph, decode FullCG. The checkpoint has 16 safetensors shards totaling 61.1 GB. Five alternating cold-cache trials (three overlap, two serial) kept JIT caches warm and evicted only checkpoint pages before each run: | Metric | Serial | Overlap | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Scheduler startup | 51.11 s | 28.66 s | -43.9% / 1.78x | | Process ready | 60.33 s | 38.07 s | -36.9% / 1.58x | | Exclusive `load_weight` attribution | 31.59 s | 8.23 s | -73.9% | Both ranks passed storage-manifest and sentinel validation while each rank loaded 64 local experts. Correctness covered a BS4 prompt set with different routes plus a long-prefix seed and two branches (seven responses total). Text and token IDs matched exactly; maximum absolute output-logprob difference was `0.0`. ## Tests - Focused startup-weight-load unit suite passed on the development superset (`52 passed`); the submitted diff removes three GLM-only tests/hooks after deferring that unvalidated runtime profile. - `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/test_server_args_migration.py::TestServerArgsAnnotatedCli::test_startup_weight_load_mode` (`1 passed`) - The registered one-GPU parity test compares both `overlap` and `auto` with default serial startup. - `black --check`, `isort --check-only`, and `ruff check --select F401,F821,UP037` on all changed files - `python3 -m py_compile` on all auto-fallback implementation and test files - Registered-test, bare-pytest, and package-registration lint checks - `git diff --check` ## Follow-up This PR intentionally keeps `serial` as the default. Follow-up work can add separately validated profiles for GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and Kimi linear/K3; define capture-stable contracts for quantized/repacked weights; add a serial+coordinated-prefetch benchmark arm for clean overlap attribution; and, after broader operational evidence, make automatic overlap selection the default. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32182075332](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182075332)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32182074978](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32182074978)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Performance] Reduce idle DP work in breakable prefill CUDA graphs
signal.text: ## Motivation Under DP attention with breakable prefill CUDA graphs, idle DP ranks may be rewritten into fabricated `EXTEND` batches so that all ranks can follow the same execution sequence. Previously, the fabricated rows were counted as real tokens. As a result: - MoE top-k and dispatch treated dummy rows as valid tokens. - Busy ranks performed unnecessary expert work for tokens from idle ranks. - Attention was executed even when a rank had no real tokens. - Prefill BCG forced all DP ranks to use `MAX_LEN`, which can introduce significant padding when the per-rank token distribution is skewed. The padding overhead is particularly visible in multi-turn and agentic workloads, where cache affinity, tool calls, and uneven turn arrival times frequently leave some DP ranks idle. ## Changes ### Skip dummy-token work on idle DP ranks For idle non-hybrid models: - Keep `num_token_non_padded` at zero after creating the fabricated `EXTEND` batch. - Prevent dummy rows from being dispatched to MoE experts. - Skip attention when the rank has no real tokens. - Zero skipped attention outputs before returning to avoid propagating uninitialized values. Hybrid SSM models retain the previous behavior because their state update requires the fabricated row. ### Allow per-rank prefill graph buckets with MegaMoE MegaMoE can safely use per-rank `SUM_LEN` buckets because its symmetric dispatch buffers are sized from `num_max_tokens_per_rank`, and its NVLink barrier depends on the number of ranks rather than each rank's local token count. This PR therefore allows MegaMoE DP ranks to select different prefill CUDA graph buckets instead of forcing all ranks to use `MAX_LEN`. The optimization is intentionally disabled for: - DeepEP and other MoE A2A backends. - DSA prefill context parallelism. - MLA prefill context parallelism. These paths continue to use the existing `MAX_LEN` behavior. ## Benchmark Configuration: - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash - TP / DP / EP: 4 / 4 / 4 - Prefill CUDA graph backend: `breakable` - Router: DP-aware, cache-aware - Maximum concurrency: 64 ### Single-turn workload For both DeepEP and MegaMoE, the single-turn high-concurrency workload mainly improves TTFT. End-to-end throughput remains approximately unchanged because all DP ranks stay busy for most of the benchmark, leaving few idle-rank opportunities. MegaMoE results below are the mean of three runs: | Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Mean TTFT | 11.50 s | 10.01 s | -13.0% | | Median TTFT | 9.85 s | 7.99 s | -18.9% | | Mean E2E latency | 34.99 s | 34.86 s | approximately unchanged | | Input throughput | 60.84k tok/s | 60.96k tok/s | within run-to-run variance | ### Multi-turn MegaMoE workload The multi-turn workload creates more skewed per-rank prefill batches and more idle DP ranks. | Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | QPS | 4.749 | 5.361 | +12.9% | This matches the intended optimization target: the gain becomes visible when the workload frequently contains idle or lightly loaded DP ranks. ## Correctness and compatibility - DeepEP retains its existing `MAX_LEN` behavior. - Non-MegaMoE A2A backends retain their existing behavior. - DSA and MLA prefill CP retain their existing synchronization behavior. - Hybrid SSM models continue counting the fabricated row as a real token. ## Test Plan - [x] `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py` - 2 passed - [x] `test/registered/dp_attn/test_dp_attention_bcg_kl.py` - 48 samples - Prefill and decode cache-hit KL: 0.0 - Passed in 163.655s - [x] DeepSeek-V4-Flash service startup with DeepEP - [x] DeepSeek-V4-Flash service startup with MegaMoE - [x] Breakable prefill CUDA graph capture and replay - [x] DP-aware Router smoke test - [x] Single-turn DeepEP benchmark - [x] Single-turn MegaMoE benchmark, three runs - [x] Multi-turn MegaMoE benchmark <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31138477171](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31138477171)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31138477123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31138477123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [feature] Add response-level input/output token ids to chat completions via SglExt
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> Exact token ids behind a completion cannot reliably be recovered by retokenizing the response. Returning exact prompt and sampled token IDs is currently unsupported for `v1/chat/completions` streaming responses (#30917 added `return_token_ids`, but chat streaming rejects it, and its streaming shape interleaves per-chunk id deltas into every choice). This PR exposes both input and output token IDs on the response-level `sglext` extension, delivered once per response, and is opt-in per request or server-wide. ## Modifications <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> - `protocol.py`: add `return_input_ids` / `return_output_ids` request flags and `sglext.input_ids` (shared prompt) / `sglext.output_ids` (per choice) response fields. - `server_args.py`: add `--return-input-ids` / `--return-output-ids` to force the behavior for every request; also settable per request via `x-sglext-return-input-ids` / `x-sglext-return-output-ids` headers. - `serving_chat.py`: - Non-streaming: ids are attached to the response's sglext field. - Streaming: ids are delivered exactly once, in a final response-level sglext chunk before [DONE] - Unit tests in test_serving_chat.py covering streaming/non-streaming, n>1, both streaming modes, and abort paths. ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.author: amykchang

signal.title: [4/N] elastic-ep: Scale at DP-attention replica granularity
signal.text: ## Summary This PR follows the Elastic EP CUDA graph recapture PR [#33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723) and removes the scale-up topology restriction `dp_size == tp_size == ep_size`. Scale-up now admits complete DP-attention replicas. For example, with fixed `attn_tp_size=2`, a deployment can scale from **DP2/TP4 to DP3/TP6 to DP4/TP8**, adding two physical EP ranks and one logical DP replica per step. The scale API continues to use physical EP sizes. The scheduler, DP controller, and tokenizer use the corresponding logical DP size. ## Changes - Derive the replica width as `attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size` and track the live DP size as `elastic_ep_size / replica_width`. - Size scheduler workers, DPC capacity, joiner offsets, and tokenizer routing in logical DP units. - Keep scale targets and Mooncake/NIXL membership in physical EP-rank units. - Admit and health-check complete replicas instead of individual ranks. - Create fixed attention and DCP groups for joiners using their global rank offset; only Mooncake WORLD grows during scale-up. - Handle the newly exercised MLP synchronization, empty embedding batch, and DCP KV-padding paths. ## Configuration Primary and joiner groups must use the same fixed topology: ```text attn_tp_size attn_cp_size dcp_size moe_dense_tp_size=1 ``` The target EP size must be divisible by `attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size`. ## Known Limitations - Attention TP, attention CP, and DCP sizes cannot change during scale-up. - This PR does not negotiate topology between the primary and joiners. - `moe_dense_tp_size == attn_tp_size` cold launch is outside this PR; `moe_dense_tp_size=1` remains required. - The scale-direction and recovery limitations of the existing Elastic EP scale-up path are unchanged. ## Test Plan The eight-GPU test adds one complete two-rank attention replica per step: | Stage | Physical topology | Logical DP size | | --- | --- | ---: | | Launch | DP2 / TP4 / EP4 | 2 | | First scale | DP3 / TP6 / EP6 | 3 | | Second scale | DP4 / TP8 / EP8 | 4 | It uses fixed `attn_tp_size=2`, `dcp_size=2`, `attn_cp_size=1`, and `moe_dense_tp_size=1`. ```bash python -m pytest -v -s \ "test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUpDP2TP4ToDP4TP8::test_scale_up_on_demand" ``` Validated results: - Eager DP2/TP4 -> DP3/TP6 -> DP4/TP8: passed, GSM8K **63.28%**. - FULL decode CUDA graphs on the same topology: passed, GSM8K **64.45%**. - Existing width-one EP4/DP4 -> EP5/DP5 -> EP6/DP6: passed, GSM8K **64.06%**. - Existing width-one EP4/DP4 -> EP5/DP5 with CUDA graphs: passed, GSM8K **62.50%**. - Focused topology, process-group, utility, and embedding tests: **37 passed**. ## References - [PR #33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723) - CUDA graph recapture after scale-up - [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up - [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31022864688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31022864688)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31022864287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31022864287)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: zackyoray

signal.title: SGLang scale-down number of processes.
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang's upstream elastic-EP supports **scale-up** (adding ranks) and **fault recovery** (recovering a rank that crashed), but not runtime **scale-down** (retiring live ranks from a serving deployment). This PR adds a Mooncake-native scale-down path, layered on top of upstream's existing elastic-EP infrastructure, and stabilizes end-to-end shrink + grow flows against Mooncake C++'s runtime constraints. The design principle is simple: at launch, allocate `--max-ep-size` ranks and immediately **pre-shrink** to the operator's desired starting size. Every subsequent scale-up is then treated as a *grow-into-retired-slot* operation via upstream's v1 recovery path, and every scale-down is a retirement of a contiguous suffix of live ranks. This unifies scale-up and scale-down under one contract (the `active_ranks` bitmask), keeps the mask size stable across the lifetime of the deployment, and lets us reuse upstream's `maybe_recover_ep_ranks` machinery unchanged. ## What this PR adds ### 1. Scale-down finite state machine (new) `ElasticEPStateManager` gains a scale-down phase graph: ``` serving ──POST /scale_elastic_ep(target<current)──▶ waiting_for_retire │ ▼ drain (admission gate; drain in-flight batches) │ ▼ flip_mask (survivors clear active_ranks[retiree]; retirees run local Mooncake quiesce + os._exit(0)) │ ▼ reconfig (Mooncake update_ep_member; broadcast_global_expert_location_metadata) │ ▼ local_cleanup (rearm EPLB, reset expert distribution recorder) │ ▼ serving_shrunk ``` Driver lives in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/scale_down_state.py` (new) with per-tick callbacks (`on_prepare` / `on_flip_mask` / `on_reconfig` / `on_exit`) implemented on `ModelRunner`. The scheduler + tokenizer manager gate new admissions on the phase. ### 2. NIXL retire barrier (new) A TCPStore-backed elected-leader epoch derivation coordinates the `flip_mask` transition across the surviving cohort. Handles rank-drift, arrival-counter rollback, catch-up busy-polling, and the same-tick DRAIN fold. Full implementation in `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py::nixl_retire_barrier_{post,check,consume}`. ### 3. Two-cycle Mooncake retire primitive (new) `try_retire_ranks(retirees)` fences via `cuda.synchronize()`, clears `active_ranks[retiree]=0` on every launch-time PG, calls `mooncake_ep.update_ep_member(WORLD, active_ranks)`, and awaits a completion barrier. Retirees separately execute `_retire_and_exit(...)` which quiesces Mooncake buffers and calls `os._exit(0)` — deliberately *not* `sys.exit(0)`, so we avoid pytest atexit hooks that would re-enter the Mooncake destructor and hang. ### 4. Grow-into-retired-slot via v1 recovery (new integration) When the operator POSTs `/scale_elastic_ep` with `target > effective_ep_size`, the scheduler now populates `ElasticEPStateManager.pending_recover_ranks` from `active_ranks == 0` slots, and `maybe_join_ep_ranks` routes through upstream's `try_recover_ranks` + `_finalize_scale_recover` instead of `try_admit_scale_ranks`. Retired slots stay in the Mooncake peer table for exactly this reason, so no new joiner subprocess needs to negotiate a wider WORLD. The joiner subprocess (`server_args.ep_join_mode="recover"` + non-zero `ep_join_rank_offset`) initializes elastic-EP state via `ModelRunner.__init__` before `initialize()`, gets its `active_ranks` mask flipped ON, and syncs the random seed from the survivor cohort via TCPStore (paired write in `_finalize_scale_recover`, `is_source=True`). ### 5. Runtime stabilization - **`retire_barrier_consume` skips `Work.wait()` when the TCPStore counter confirms all ranks posted** — Mooncake's async collective can hang here asymmetrically after retiree exit; the counter is the authoritative signal. - **Same-tick DRAIN fold**: `scale_down_state.py` no longer returns to the scheduler between DRAIN-posted and DRAIN-consumed on the same tick, avoiding a 30s stall in the NIXL a2a barrier. - **TCPStore initialization for Mooncake WORLD**: `_create_global_tcp_store` runs unconditionally when elastic-EP is enabled (previously NIXL-only), so the elected-leader epoch works uniformly. - **`_finalize_scale_up` writes `self.dp_size = target_size`**: `update_dp_attention_post_scale` only updates module globals; downstream consumers reading `ModelRunner.dp_size` (DP-attention-aware kernels, DPC-side elasticity accounting) would otherwise see the stale launch value. - **`maybe_join_ep_ranks` silent-skips on `has_scaled` when `pending_size is None`**: upstream's original called `fail_recovery` which sets `scale_phase="recovery_unsupported"` and blocks every subsequent scale request. Our design needs scale-up and scale-down to remain requestable after any prior scale, so we return silently. - **Local timeout check** (per-rank `time.monotonic()` on `pending_since`) instead of upstream's `dist.all_reduce(WORLD, MAX)`: our WORLD may include `os._exit(0)`'d retirees whose Mooncake slot has not yet reconnected, and NCCL/Gloo would deadlock waiting for peers that will never respond. ### 6. Test coverage (new) - **Manual end-to-end** (`test/manual/ep/test_mooncake_scale_down.py`, 3.7k lines): MC01–MC14 cover single-node + multi-node scale-down and grow-back on both NIXL and Mooncake a2a backends. MC06 uses deterministic inference (`--enable-deterministic-inference` + fixed seed + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds) and asserts byte-identical scores across three post-shrink rounds. MC11 is intentionally skipped (Mooncake C++ `join_group(WORLD)` deadlock on join-then-shrink is a separate upstream issue). MC13 (shrink-below-primary after append) is env-gated behind `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN` as a compatibility valve for older container images; on the default nightly (Mooncake 0.3.12+) MC13 passes. - **Unit tests** (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`, new): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections (max-ep-size / initial-size / recover-only-with-mooncake), wiring between `ElasticEPStateManager` ↔ scheduler ↔ tokenizer manager. ### 7. Runtime environment - Default container in sweep scripts: nightly ≥ 2026-07-29 (bakes Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, which resizes P2PProxy peer arrays dynamically). Older containers still work for MC01–MC12/MC14 but need `SGLANG_MC13_FORCE_RUN=0` (the default) to skip MC13. ## Design constraints worth calling out for reviewers **Mooncake P2PProxy peer arrays.** In Mooncake versions before 0.3.12 the peer arrays were fixed-width at construction time. Our pre-shrink pattern (allocate at `--max-ep-size`, immediately retire down to the operator's desired starting size, grow back into retired slots) neatly sidestepped that constraint. Mooncake 0.3.12+ resizes these arrays dynamically (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#2623), so the constraint no longer applies at runtime — but we keep the pre-shrink design because it also gives us a stable `active_ranks` mask size, keeps every scale-up on the same code path (upstream's recovery path), and lets us keep retired slots addressable in the Mooncake peer table for future refill. **Asymmetric `Work.wait()` on Mooncake WORLD backend.** Some ranks return instantly from `handle.wait()`, others hang for 30s+. On NIXL this doesn't matter (all ranks tick at the same rate), but on Mooncake a2a it corrupts subsequent C++ collectives (`EPBuffer.update_ep_member` hangs). We ship a NIXL-first design; Mooncake a2a scale-down carries this documented limitation and is out of scope for this PR. **Fault recovery + scale coexistence.** Upstream's original `maybe_join_ep_ranks` calls `fail_recovery` when a runtime recovery attempt is detected on a scaled cohort, permanently blocking every subsequent scales. Our design supports iterative shrink/grow cycles, so we return silently on that path and preserve the ability to request future scales. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests (`test/srt/unit/elastic_ep/`): FSM transitions, boot-guard rejections, and admission-gate wiring. - [x] Full MC01–MC14 × 5 baseline sweep on NIXL a2a: **PASS**. - [x] MC01 smoke on the layered-port rebase: **PASS** (GSM8K parity 62.50% → 61.72%, within 10% tol). - [x] MC06 deterministic smoke: byte-identical scores across all three post-shrink rounds. - [x] All 11 commits pass `python3 -m py_compile` at every snapshot. ## Commit-by-commit walkthrough (11 commits) Rebased on top of `sgl-project/sglang:main` as of 2026-07-31. Each commit passes tests standalone. | # | Commit | Summary | |---|---|---| | 1 | `e38192f08e` | **Layer scale-down on top of upstream elastic-EP.** New `scale_down_state.py`, `try_retire_ranks`, retire barrier, FSM entry points on `ModelRunner`, scheduler + tokenizer-manager admission gates, `pending_recover_ranks` plumbing, `is_ep_offset_joiner` predicate. | | 2 | `b2197ff6d1` | Unit + manual test coverage (MC01–MC12, unit tests). | | 3 | `f9e7d340b6` | Stabilize scale-down on NIXL a2a: retire barrier busy-poll, TCPStore epoch derivation, arrival-counter rollback handling. | | 4 | `9d55cf89e8` | Fix recover-mode joiner MoE storage sizing (joiner slot count from `ep_join_rank_offset + tp_size`, not `elastic_ep_initial_size`, to support partial regrow). | | 5 | `4085745e18` | Wire scale-down FSM + partial-recovery grow-back through `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 6 | `3f74440ec6` | MC14 (`4→3→5` shrink-recover-then-append) + skipped MC13 regression trigger. | | 7 | `6f7c2cd19d` | Env-gate MC13 on Mooncake ≥ 0.3.12 P2PProxy fix. | | 8 | `19b9fa11e2` | Harden scale-down FSM: same-tick DRAIN fold, backend-conditional `Work.wait()` skip, TCPStore for Mooncake WORLD, `_finalize_scale_up::dp_size`, local timeout in `maybe_join_ep_ranks`. | | 9 | `078bf87c26` | Pre-PR cleanup: barrier arrival-counter leak, dedup, doc drift. | | 10 | `0c12260b21` | Dedup `ModelRunner` methods after layered port; **reorder methods to match upstream order** (reviewer-friendly diff shape, drops 603 lines of `git diff` phantom-move noise). | | 11 | `8ec48f0cae` | Make MC06 deterministic: exact-equality across post-shrink rounds via `--enable-deterministic-inference` + `--random-seed 42` + serial GSM8K + KV-cache flush between rounds. | ## Diff shape 29 files changed; net `+9,731 / -236`. Two files carry most of the surface: - `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py`: `+1507 / -123` after the reorder in commit 10. All upstream methods stay at their upstream line numbers; new scale-down/retire methods append at the class tail as a clean additive block. - `python/sglang/srt/elastic_ep/elastic_ep.py`: `+1559 / -33`. Mostly honest additions (NIXL retire barrier, retire primitives, FSM state). signal.title: [RFC] Orchestrator-facing Elastic EP lifecycle contract
signal.text: ## Motivation Dynamo is designing Kubernetes-managed Elastic EP in [Dynamo DEP #13121](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13121). SGLang's merged scale-up path is already close to what an external reconciler needs: it accepts an absolute EP target, distinguishes effective and pending size, lets joining cohorts wait for admission, and exposes asynchronous status. To turn that into a reliable Kubernetes lifecycle, the orchestrator must be able to recover after a controller restart or request timeout, identify the joining or retiring cohort for one operation, and know when capacity is safe to delete. The goal is not to standardize SGLang's internal topology; it is to make the boundary used by an external process orchestrator explicit and queryable. ## Proposed orchestrator-facing contract ### Resize identity and status - Accept an absolute target and associate it with an operation ID or generation. - Treat a repeated request for the active or in-progress target as the same operation. - Report a stable runtime instance ID, operation ID, effective size, pending target, documented phase, and operation-scoped error. - Make it possible to distinguish an engine restart from an operation that is still progressing. A conceptual status shape is: ```json { "instance_id": "server-7", "operation_id": "resize-42", "effective_ep_size": 4, "pending_ep_size": 6, "phase": "waiting_for_cohort", "last_error": null } ``` ### Joining-cohort identity For scale-up, expose enough information to associate externally launched joiners with one operation: - cohort or operation ID; - expected rank range and ready-rank count; - a topology/configuration fingerprint; - explicit mismatch and timeout errors. This prevents a stale joiner from a failed operation from being admitted into a later resize that happens to reuse the same rank offset. ### Scale-down and process ownership For scale-down, separate topology commit from external process termination. The surviving coordinator should report the retired ranks and when they are safe for the orchestrator to terminate: ```json { "phase": "serving_shrunk", "effective_ep_size": 4, "retired_ranks": [4, 5], "safe_to_terminate_ranks": [4, 5] } ``` A mode where retired ranks quiesce and wait for external termination would integrate more cleanly with Kubernetes than unconditional process exit. If ranks exit themselves, the contract should still define how the surviving coordinator proves the smaller topology committed, because Kubernetes may restart exited containers. ### Machine-readable scale mapping and capabilities The native API can remain expressed in physical EP ranks. An external autoscaler nevertheless needs a machine-readable mapping from logical serving replicas to physical targets, especially with the DP-attention replica granularity proposed in [#33728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33728). Useful capability fields include: - effective and maximum physical EP size; - logical DP size; - replica width and target granularity; - supported scale directions; - relevant topology constraints or a configuration fingerprint. For the topology in #33728: ```text replica_width = attn_tp_size * attn_cp_size physical_ep_target = logical_dp_target * replica_width ``` ## Kubernetes capacity consideration The scale-down design in [#33111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33111) proposes launching `max_ep_size` ranks and pre-shrinking to the desired initial size. Requiring maximum physical GPU capacity at cold start would limit pay-as-you-grow deployments. If possible, it would be preferable to reserve maximum-sized metadata/buffers while launching only the initially active ranks, then add or recover the remaining slots on demand. ## Related work - Original Elastic EP RFC: [#22788](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) - Merged scale-up: [#30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - Scale-down draft: [#33111](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33111) - CUDA graph recapture: [#33723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33723) - DP-attention replica granularity: [#33728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33728) Would this kind of external-orchestrator contract fit SGLang's intended Elastic EP direction?

signal.title: Fix context-boundary max_new_tokens clipping
signal.text: ## Motivation Requests that fit the advertised context length are silently clipped by two tokens in the scheduler. With `--context-length 4096`, `ignore_eos=True`, and `max_new_tokens=16`: ```text input=4078, requested=16, actual=16 input=4079, requested=16, actual=15 input=4080, requested=16, actual=14 input=4081, requested=16, HTTP 400 ``` This reproduces on both Qwen3-0.6B and the hybrid GDN/linear-attention Qwen3.5-0.8B path, so it is not model-specific. SGLang's public validation permits requests whose total length is exactly the model context length: ```text input_len + max_new_tokens <= context_len ``` This boundary was explicitly adopted in #22546 after the same behavior was reported in discussion #16020. The scheduler uses a different internal length. In [`TPModelWorker.get_worker_info`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/604d3561b012816aa4cec2fb89c522f819f68af8/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py#L514-L519), `max_req_len` is already defined as: ```python max_req_len = min( context_len - 1, effective_max_total_num_tokens * dcp_size - 1, ) ``` However, `Scheduler.init_req_max_new_tokens` applies another subtraction: ```python max_req_len - input_len - 1 ``` When the context-length bound is active, this expands to `context_len - input_len - 2`, explaining the two-token clipping. The execution invariant is that generating `N` output tokens forwards the prompt and only the first `N - 1` generated tokens. The final token is sampled and returned, but is never forwarded in another decode step. Therefore: ```text input_len + max_new_tokens - 1 <= max_req_len max_new_tokens <= max_req_len - input_len + 1 ``` EOS does not require a separate reserved slot: when sampled, it is itself one of the generated tokens. The page-rounded global KV admission bound remains a separate safety constraint. ## Modifications - Use `max_req_len - input_len + 1` for the per-request context bound. - Keep the page-rounded global KV admission bound added by #25126 unchanged. - Update the existing scheduler property tests to encode the forward-length invariant. - Add a focused regression for a request exactly at the public context boundary. The regression fails on the parent commit with `14 != 16` and passes with this change. After the change: ```text input=4078, requested=16, actual=16 input=4079, requested=16, actual=16 input=4080, requested=16, actual=16 input=4081, requested=16, HTTP 400 ``` ## Accuracy Tests This changes only scheduler length accounting, not model forward computation, logits, or sampling math. End-to-end validation used Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B on an RTX 3070 with the Triton attention backend. All accepted requests through total length 4096 returned the requested token count; total length 4097 remained rejected with HTTP 400. The exact boundary also passed with Qwen3.5 NEXTN/EAGLE speculative decoding, including its four reserved token slots; one token beyond it returned HTTP 400 and the server remained healthy. Focused unit results: ```text 9 passed, 542 subtests passed ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling No hot inference path changes. The patch replaces one integer expression during request initialization, so no speed impact is expected. Local `pre-commit run --all-files` passed all Python formatting, lint, registered-test, and repository checks. Rust-only hooks could not run because this WSL environment does not have `cargo` or `rustup`; this PR does not modify Rust files. No user-facing documentation change is required; the scheduler comment now documents the corrected forward-length invariant. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Fix] Skip padded state slots in the chunked GDN kernel
signal.text: _forward_metadata poisons padded request rows with state index -1, and the decode kernel already skips them (fused_recurrent: `if idx >= 0`). The chunked extend kernel had no such guard, so -1 reached `initial_state + index * stride_init_state` for both the initial-state load and the in-place final-state store, addressing before the state pool. boundary_check does not help: it validates against the declared block shape, not the allocation. Under breakable-CUDA-graph prefill with DP attention an idle DP rank replays an extend with an all-padded batch, so every row carries -1 and the kernel faults with cudaErrorIllegalAddress. Reproduced on Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3.5-397B on pristine main; a single request against --dp 4 is enough. No per-commit suite covers a linear-attn hybrid with DP attention, which is why this went unseen. Add a regression test in the existing base-b (1-GPU, per-commit) kernel suite; it fails without the guard. <!-- Thank you for your contribution! signal.author: Fridge003

signal.title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 tool call parser fails ~8x/hour in production: TypeError 'string indices must be integers' and json 'unexpected character'
signal.text: ## Describe the bug Running Kimi-K3 with `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3` in production (agentic coding workload, Claude-Code-style tool loop), the tool call parser raises on a significant fraction of model outputs. Over a 24h window with moderate traffic we counted **~190 parser failures**: - 106x `Tool call parsing error: string indices must be integers` (TypeError — a parsed call is indexed like a dict but is a str) - 84x `Tool call parsing error: unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` (json.loads on a non-JSON argument payload) - 1x `Tool call parsing error: Input is a zero-length, empty document` Logged from `serving_chat.py` ("Tool call parsing error") — the request then falls back to returning the raw text instead of a structured `tool_calls` entry, so the client sees a turn without tool calls and the agent loop degrades or retries. ## Environment - SGLang 0.5.17-tree, ROCm (8x MI350X, gfx950), `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --enable-strict-thinking`, grammar backend xgrammar - Failures occur both with streaming and non-streaming chat completions ## Analysis `function_call/kimik3_detector.py` extracts calls via `_CALL_RE`/`_ARG_RE` and then: - `json.loads(raw_value)` on each argument value — raises `unexpected character` when the model emits an unquoted/partial value (this is exactly the second error class), and - downstream consumers index `call["name"]`/`call["arguments"]` — the `string indices` TypeError suggests a code path where the parsed call is still a plain string (e.g. malformed/partial `<|open|>call ...` block that the regex only partially matches). ## Expected behavior Malformed tool-call blocks from the model should be handled defensively (skip the malformed call and/or return it as text with a warning), never raise inside the parser. Given Kimi-K3 is explicitly advertised for agentic workloads, hardening this parser has outsized impact — at our traffic every ~7-8 minutes an agent turn silently loses its tool call. ## Reproduction We do not yet have a captured raw failing sample (the error log does not include the payload). We are happy to add debug logging in production and attach concrete failing model outputs if that helps — please tell us the preferred capture point. ## Checklist - [x] Searched existing issues — found tool_call_id-related PRs for kimi-k3 but nothing covering these parser exceptions.
