signal.title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Fix NPU Ring Attention varlen dispatch & restore 2-NPU CI testcase
signal.text: ## Motivation Ring Attention on Ascend NPU currently breaks when execution reaches the packed variable-length FlashAttention fallback (added for Minimax-H3 support). The shared Ring Attention path uses `flash_attn_varlen_func` for variable-length packed sequences, but that entry point did not have an NPU implementation. As a result, Ring Attention regressed on NPU in the current `main` branch. This PR implement the NPU path by adding Ascend support for packed variable-length attention and wiring it into both the generic FlashAttention compatibility API and the diffusion Ascend attention backend. The implementation is based on the Ascend varlen attention work from [#33569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33569), extracted here as a focused Ring Attention compatibility fix. ### Before ### After This PR fix this behavior by implementing this fallback: ## Modifications ### Ascend packed variable-length attention - Add `ascend_fused_infer_attention_varlen`, backed by `torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score`. - Use the Ascend `TND` layout with packed sequence boundaries supplied through `actual_seq_lengths` and `actual_seq_lengths_kv`. - Validate Q/K/V layout, device placement, dtype, head dimensions, and cumulative sequence lengths. - Support optional host-side cumulative sequence lengths to avoid unnecessary device-to-host synchronization when they are already available. - Handle empty packed segments and non-contiguous Q/K/V views. - Support returning softmax LSE when requested. ### `flash_attn_varlen_func` NPU dispatch - Route NPU tensors from the generic `flash_attn_varlen_func` compatibility API to the Ascend packed-attention implementation. - Explicitly reject FlashAttention options that are not supported by the Ascend implementation instead of silently producing incorrect behavior. - Leave the existing CUDA/FlashAttention v3 path unchanged. ### Diffusion Ascend attention backend - Implement `AscendFlashAttnImpl.forward_varlen`. - Use the shared fused `TND` implementation for non-causal packed attention. - Preserve sequence boundaries for causal attention by processing each packed segment independently through the existing Ascend attention path. ## Accuracy Tests - **Before this PR:** the packed variable-length fallback used by Ring Attention does not have a working NPU implementation. - **After this PR:** the same Ring Attention path successfully dispatches through the Ascend varlen implementation. ## Speed Tests and Profiling This PR is primarily a correctness and dispatch fix; no standalone end-to-end performance benchmark was collected. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Spec] Drop the unconditional stream sync from spec-prefill H2D copies
signal.text: ## What `torch.tensor(python_list, device="cuda")` lowers to `memcpy_and_sync()` — a `cudaMemcpyAsync` followed by an **unconditional** `cudaStreamSynchronize`. In both spec workers, the `ctx_lens` / `draft_seq_lens` copies are issued a few statements after `target_worker.forward_batch_generation(...)`, which does not synchronize before returning — so the host blocks on the **entire target prefill forward** for an 8-byte copy. `torch.tensor(...).to(device, non_blocking=True)` performs the same copy without draining the stream. Four sites — the same two lines in both spec workers: | file | tensors | |---|---| | `speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py` | `ctx_lens`, `draft_seq_lens` | | `speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py` | `ctx_lens`, `draft_seq_lens` (verbatim twin of the above) | Within each file the two lines must change together: the sync drains the queue, so converting only the first would just make the second one the payer. ## Why this is safe Both tensors have exactly one consumer on this path: `compute_position` → `compute_position_triton`, which reads them with `tl.load` on the current stream. Every CUDA/HIP attention backend takes that branch (`support_triton()`); nothing reads the values back on the host, and there is no stream switch or synchronization primitive anywhere between the copy and the kernel. The `torch_native` / `intel_amx` fallback (`compute_position_torch`) does host-read them — still correct, because the implicit `.item()` synchronizes the same stream the copy was enqueued on; those backends simply see no win. This is the same idiom the non-spec prefill path already uses for the same two quantities (`forward_batch_info.py` builds `extend_seq_lens` / `extend_prefix_lens` with `torch.tensor(...).to(device, non_blocking=True)`), and the same fix #34782 (merged) applied to the DSpark decode path. ## Scope change from the first revision The first push also converted two more `torch.tensor(list, device=...)` sites, in `mem_cache/allocation.py` and `speculative/frozen_kv_mtp_utils.py`. Both dropped: neither is reachable in the configuration where the drain was observed (the `allocation.py` sentinel is on the dLLM-only kv-reuse branch; the `frozen_kv_mtp_utils.py` site is Frozen-KV-MTP-only), and the right fix for the `allocation.py` sentinel is the on-device `torch.full((1,), -1, device=...)` that #32575 already applied to its sibling line — that belongs in its own follow-up, not riding along unmeasured here. ## Honest scoping — please read before treating this as a perf PR On the setup where this was found (2× DGX Spark / GB10 sm_121 / DeepSeek-V4-Flash / TP=2 across two nodes), **prefill is ~99.4% GPU-bound**: 27.0 ms idle out of a 4409 ms window. That caps the host-side upside at **~0.6%**, and I could **not** demonstrate an end-to-end improvement above run-to-run noise. One more caveat in the same spirit: for pageable sources the CUDA sync-behavior appendix leaves the driver latitude to stage an "async" copy through an internal stream sync ("might be synchronous with respect to host"). If this driver takes that path, the change removes PyTorch's explicit post-copy drain and inherits an implicit one in the same position. So the case for this patch is **"remove a sync that serves no purpose on these call sites, and align them with the idiom the surrounding code already uses"**, not a measured speedup. A deployment whose prefill is less GPU-bound, or one where one of these syncs lands next to a long-running kernel, could see more — the cost of a sync has no intrinsic magnitude, only a position on the stream. Filing as draft; happy to close it if the maintainers would rather not carry a change without a demonstrated win. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32168567081](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168567081)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32168566642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32168566642)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] feat: per-layer TP shard planner for DiT linears (--dit-tp-plan)
signal.text: ## Motivation #29774 shards the Qwen-Image DiT across TP ranks, and the follow-up commits there showed the best per-layer layout is **not** uniform: the text-branch FFN should stay replicated at tp=2 (−8% e2e) but sharded at tp=4 (+1.1% if replicated), the image FFN should be replicated only for small workloads (−18% at 512², regression at ≥1024²), and none of it transfers blindly to other models (the identical change on FLUX's `ff_context` measures +0.8%). Hardcoding these crossovers per call site does not scale across **TP sizes × machines × models × workloads**. This PR adds a small planner that owns those decisions. **Why not an analytic cost model?** We tried. Isolated comm/GEMM microbenchmarks mis-rank layouts in both directions: replicating the attention out-projs looks like −8.5% on isolated per-step timings but is e2e-null (+0.8%, mixed-sign ABAB paired diffs — substituting an all-gather for an all-reduce buys nothing); meanwhile the txt_mlp win is far larger than its isolated all-reduce cost (eliminating the collective also removes a sync point and a compile graph break). End-to-end measurement is the only signal that ranked every case correctly, so the design is built around measured rules plus an e2e tuner, not FLOP/bandwidth formulas. ## Design `--dit-tp-plan {auto | full | aggressive | <plan.json>}` resolves each DiT linear through four levels (first match wins): 1. **Plan-file rules** (`{"rules": {"*.txt_mlp": "replicate"}}`, glob-matched per layer) — exact control; also the output format of the new tuner. 2. **Structural rules** — attention out-projs always shard (their contraction dim is head-sharded; replicate = collective substitution = measured null; ColumnParallel+gather = strictly worse). 3. **`MEASURED_RULES` registry** — per-`(model_family, branch)` defaults that passed e2e ABAB validation, gated on TP degree and (for `aggressive`) the expected workload from `--dit-tp-plan-workload WxH`. Every entry carries its evidence string. 4. **Conservative fallback** — full shard for any un-measured model. The FLUX negative result is the reason this is the default: no blanket architecture rules. `tools/tune_dit_tp_plan.py` covers machines/models we haven't measured: it boots candidate plans ABAB-interleaved on the actual hardware, compares paired e2e latencies, and emits a plan JSON with provenance (so `--dit-tp-plan tuned.json` is auditable). `QwenImageTransformerBlock` is the first consumer — its `txt_mlp`/`img_mlp` layouts now come from the planner (replacing the hardcoded `tp<=2` gate, same defaults). ## Measured basis (2×H100, e2e ABAB ×3, single-request) | setting | full-shard | txt_mlp replicated | |---|---|---| | qwen 1024² tp=2 | 5.58 s | **5.12 s (−8%)** | | qwen 512² tp=2 | ~5.04 s | **4.54 s (−9%)**; +img_mlp → **4.11 s (−18%)** | | qwen 1536² tp=2 | 10.23 s | 10.28 s (+0.4%) | | qwen 1024² tp=4 | **6.04 s** | 6.11 s (+1.1%) | | flux 1024² tp=2 (`ff_context`) | **4.41 s** | 4.44 s (+0.8%) | ## Usage ```bash # defaults: measured rules for known models, full-shard for unknown sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 --tp-size 2 ... # pinned small-resolution deployment: also replicate the image FFN sglang serve ... --dit-tp-plan aggressive --dit-tp-plan-workload 512x512 # new machine / new model: tune once, then load the plan python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.tune_dit_tp_plan \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 \ --serve-args "--num-gpus 2 --tp-size 2 --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile" \ --workload 1024x1024 --candidate full --candidate auto --output tuned.json sglang serve ... --dit-tp-plan tuned.json ``` ## Validation - `test/unit/test_tp_shard_planner.py`: 14 tests covering the decision chain (registry gates on tp/workload/mode, plan-file override + unsupported-scheme rejection, conservative default, plan loading). - Smoke on 2×H100: `auto` resolves text-FFN→replicate / image-FFN→shard and serves requests; `full` resolves everything→shard; `aggressive --dit-tp-plan-workload 512x512` adds image-FFN→replicate. Decisions are logged once per layer group with their evidence. - Perf parity: `auto` at tp=2/tp=4 reproduces exactly the layouts validated in the #29774 measurements above (same module classes, same defaults). ## Notes Rebased onto `main` now that #29774 has merged — the diff is a clean single commit (planner + `--dit-tp-plan`/`--dit-tp-plan-workload` + qwen wiring + test + offline tuner). Default `auto` reproduces #29774's merged behavior exactly (qwen text-FFN replicate at tp<=2, image-FFN sharded), now expressed as an evidence-carrying measured rule instead of a hardcoded gate. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32175385071](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32175385071)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32175384557](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32175384557)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: ci: bundle in_process_group tests into one python3 -m unittest invocation
signal.text: ## Motivation `run_unittest_files` invokes one fresh `python3 file.py -f` per test file in a partition. Each invocation pays ~10 s of `import sglang.*` + CUDA init before doing any test work. For a partition with N pure module-level tests, that's ~10×N seconds of pure overhead. Measured locally on the attention-backend unittest suite (27 files): | Invocation | Wall time | |---|---| | `python3 file.py -f` × 27 (current CI loop) | **~5 min** | | `python3 -m unittest -f <27 mods>` (one process) | **~50 s** | The savings exist for any test set where the import cost dominates the actual test work. For a typical 8-12-file partition of pure module-level tests, this can cut wall time by 3-5×. ## Architecture context GitHub Actions stages run `partitions[suite]` jobs in a matrix; each partition is a separate GHA runner with its own checkout + install + warmup. Inside one partition, `run_unittest_files` loops the partition's files sequentially. That's the natural scope for amortizing imports — one warm Python per partition. But `auto_partition` LPT-bin-packs files by `est_time`, so the 27 attention files would normally end up scattered across 8 partitions (~3-4 per). Without grouping at the partitioner, savings shrink proportionally. ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_register.py` * New kwarg-only `in_process_group: Optional[str]` on every `register_{cuda,cpu,amd,npu,xpu}_ci`. Persisted as `CIRegistry.in_process_group` (defaults to None → existing behavior unchanged). * New `CIBundle` dataclass: `group_key`, `members: List[CIRegistry]`, `est_time`. Acts as a single atomic bin-pack unit. * `_bundle_in_process_groups()` rolls members with the same group key into a `CIBundle` **before** `auto_partition` runs LPT. The whole group always lands in one partition. Bundle `est_time`: - prefers grouped `live_est["group:<key>"]` from a prior measurement; - falls back to `sum(member.est_time) - (N-1) * _BUNDLE_IMPORT_COST_SEC` (each extra member avoids one cold `import sglang`). * `auto_partition()` return type widens to `List[Union[CIRegistry, CIBundle]]`. ### `python/sglang/test/ci/ci_utils.py` * `_filename_to_module()` — converts `registered/foo/test_x.py` → `registered.foo.test_x` for the unittest CLI argv (cwd is `test/` per `_pr-test-stage.yml:157`). * `_run_one_bundle()` — handles one bundle: builds `python3 -m unittest -f <mod1> <mod2> ...`, runs under `run_with_timeout`, credits/discredits members en bloc, supports the existing retry-on-flake loop. Per-bundle timing recorded under `file_elapsed["group:<key>"]` so `live_est` picks up grouped wall time for future bin-packing. * `run_unittest_files()` per-iteration loop dispatches `CIBundle` units to `_run_one_bundle` and continues; `CIRegistry`/`TestFile` units take the existing per-file `Popen(["python3", file, "-f"])` path unchanged. * `units_passed_count` so the "Test Summary" line reports unit counts (not member counts). * `_repo_relative_path()` returns `group:<key>` verbatim so TIMINGS JSON keys are stable across runner layouts. ### No test files change `in_process_group` is opt-in. The first consumer (attention-backend unittest suite, PR #26517) will add the field in a follow-up commit on that branch. ## How a suite opts in ```python register_cuda_ci( est_time=25, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200", in_process_group="attention_unittest", # ← single new kwarg ) ``` All files with the same group value run together as one `python3 -m unittest -f <mods>` invocation in whichever partition `auto_partition` picks for the bundle. ## Risks + mitigations | Risk | Mitigation | |---|---| | Members of a group share a Python interpreter — one file's monkey-patch could affect another | Opt-in. Authors mark their group only when they've confirmed shared-interpreter safety. Out of the box, no test files are marked. | | One file crashing kills the whole bundle | v1 fails the whole bundle and credits the bundle's error to every member. Per-member fallback re-run on failure is a follow-up. | | Group too large for any partition's timeout | `bundle_timeout = max(timeout_per_file, est_time * 2 + 60)` — generous slack, but extremely large groups still need to be split manually for now. | | `live_est` from before rollout is per-file → bundle bin-packing overestimates | Acceptable for first run; once grouped runs land, `live_est["group:<key>"]` takes over and packing tightens. | ## Accuracy Tests * Parsed all 779 registered test files (1051 registries) with the new field — unchanged behavior, `in_process_group=None` everywhere, no regressions in `collect_tests` / `auto_partition` for existing tests. * End-to-end synthetic bundle: 2 stub test files registered with `in_process_group="bundle_validation"`, `auto_partition` produces a `CIBundle`, `run_unittest_files` runs `python3 -m unittest`, bundle key recorded in TIMINGS with `passed: true`, summary line `1/1 unit(s) passed`. ## Speed Tests | Path | Today | With this PR (attention suite, 27 files marked) | |---|---|---| | One partition handling 3-4 attention files mixed with others | ~5×10 s import overhead | n/a — group always lands in one partition | | One partition handling the whole attention bundle | n/a | one `python3 -m unittest -f <27 mods>` → ~50 s total | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests) — validated via synthetic bundle end-to-end. - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) — inline docstrings on `CIBundle`, `in_process_group`, `_run_one_bundle`. - [x] Provide accuracy results (above). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32090148143](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090148143)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32090148015](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32090148015)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Split TRTLLM MHA decode batches by KV sequence length
signal.text: ## Motivation TRTLLM-GEN decode attention can pay a large tail-latency tax when requests in the same batch have very different KV sequence lengths. On GB300, a matched mixed-context profile attributed `8.377 ms` of a `9.822 ms` decode-step delta to attention, with `7.601 ms` coming from the main SM100 variable-sequence FMHA kernel. At BS44/rank on a 148-SM GB300, the unsplit launch has only one KV CTA per request and selects the persistent kernel. Long requests then form the tail of the shared wave. Splitting a fixed-query-length batch into length-sorted groups increases CTA parallelism and prevents the longest requests from delaying the short groups. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MHA_DECODE_SEQ_LEN_SPLITS`, with default `1` preserving the existing single-call behavior. - For values above one, sort requests by KV length, form equal-count groups, gather their query/page-table/length metadata, invoke TRTLLM MHA per group, and scatter outputs back to request order. - Reuse the same helper for ordinary fixed-query decode and frozen-KV MTP target verification, including NVFP4 KV-cache scaling. - Validate the split count and cap it at the request count. The ragged-query path is unchanged. - Extend two existing TRTLLM-MHA test cases to cover split eager decode and frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph replay; no new test method or module is added. The refreshed commit is rebased onto current upstream `main@f019f0b064`. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, 200 requests, 5-shot chat evaluation on `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`: | Metric | Result | |---|---:| | Accuracy | **0.985** (197/200) | | CUDA graph request fraction | 1.0 | | Retractions | 0 | | Error markers | 0 | Acceptance was generated naturally; no simulated-accuracy path was enabled. Targeted GB300 correctness coverage on the refreshed upstream commit: - existing eager dense-decode case with two sequence-length groups; - existing frozen-KV MTP CUDA-graph case with two groups; - `2 passed`, covering `5` subtests. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Feature isolation: no split versus two groups Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, FP8 KV cache, TP8/DP8/EP8, TRTLLM MHA, NEXTN draft length 6, BS44/rank on GB300: | Workload | Splits=1 | Splits=2 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Mixed ISL decode iteration | 57.485 ms | 51.639 ms | **-10.17%** | | Uniform 92k, exact matched points | 49.907 ms | 50.008 ms | +0.20% | | q_len=1 attention micro | 0.757 ms | 0.637 ms | **-15.9%** | | q_len=6 attention micro | 1.066 ms | 0.711 ms | **-33.3%** | The mixed run held batch size, average context, request count, and draft settings constant. Length splitting closed `75.5%` of the isolated mixed-ISL attention tax without a material steady-state regression on uniform lengths. ### Production split-count tuning AgentX 393-trace workload, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4, 24 GB300 GPUs, 4P+1D, concurrency 896. Exact-shape matching used each arm's independently aligned formal `180-900 s` window. | Metric | Split-3 | Split-4 | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Exact-shape output TPS/User | 67.352353 | 70.623070 | **+4.8561%** | | Strict matched TPS/running request | — | — | **+1.82848%** | | ITL | — | — | **-4.0306%** | | Full decode duration | — | — | **-3.6644%** | Both arms had CUDA graph fraction `1.0` and zero retractions. This second table is split-count tuning enabled by the PR, not an additional additive estimate on top of the no-split comparison. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The opt-in setting is documented inline at its declaration. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Bug] HiCache NIXL L3 cleaner group-key parsing misses hybrid pool suffixes, so eviction is not atomic per logical entry
signal.text: ## Describe the bug The L3 cleaner's design guarantee is that eviction is atomic per logical cache entry: all physical shards of one entry (per-rank files, K/V splits, hybrid pool components) are grouped and deleted together, preserving the cluster-wide all-or-nothing `batch_exists` invariant (`_GroupInfo` docstring, `nixl_cleaner.py:28-37`). `_parse_group_key` (`nixl_cleaner.py:40-55`) only handles two name shapes: - a trailing bare `_k` or `_v` (`_KV_SUFFIXES`, line 23) - a trailing `_{tp_rank}_{tp_size}` (`_RANK_SUFFIX_RE`, line 22) But `_get_hybrid_component_keys` (`hicache_nixl.py:200-219`) generates physical names of the form `{hash}{config_suffix}{component}` where `{component}` is: - `_{pool}_temporal` and `_{pool}_conv_{i}` for Mamba pools - `_{pool}_k` / `_{pool}_v` for two-component pools - `_{pool}_{i}` for other multi-component pools - `_{pool}` for named single-component pools (`_get_component_key`, `hicache_nixl.py:188-193`) None of these strip, and because the component sits after the rank suffix, the rank suffix (anchored with `$`) never strips either. Concrete outcomes for one logical page of a hybrid model with `config_suffix = "_model_0_8"`: ```python _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8") # "page-a_model" (intended group) _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_swa_k") # "page-a_model_0_8_swa" _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_mamba_temporal") # "page-a_model_0_8_mamba_temporal" _parse_group_key("page-a_model_0_8_mamba_conv_0") # "page-a_model_0_8_mamba_conv_0" ``` One logical entry fragments into many "groups": per rank, per pool and (for Mamba) per physical file. ## Impact Under watermark pressure the cleaner deletes fragments independently in mtime order, so a hybrid entry can lose its temporal file while its conv/K/V files survive (or lose rank 3's shard while ranks 0-2 survive). `batch_exists` then reports the entry missing while most of its bytes still occupy disk, which is the worst of both: the space is not reclaimed proportionally and the entry is gone. The grouped-delete design exists precisely to prevent this, and the class docstring's compatibility claim ("MHA, MLA, and DSA naming", `nixl_cleaner.py:75-76`) does not hold for hybrid naming. The existing unit test only covers the bare shapes (`test_hicache_nixl_cleaner.py:43-48`), which is how this slipped through. ## Reproduce CPU-only: the four `_parse_group_key` calls above, or extend `TestHiCacheL3Cleaner` with hybrid names and observe one logical entry spread across multiple `_GroupInfo` groups and deleted partially by `_tick`. ## Proposed fix (happy to send a PR) Options, in my order of preference: 1. **Pass the naming down instead of guessing it back.** `HiCacheNixl` knows its `config_suffix` and the exact component-suffix set it generates; hand both to `HiCacheL3Cleaner` at construction so grouping strips exact known suffixes by construction. New pool types then cannot drift out of sync with the parser. 2. **Extend the parser's stripping rules**: strip a known component tail (`_(k|v|temporal|conv_\d+|\d+)$` then an optional `_{pool}` for pool in the `PoolName` values) before the rank suffix. Smaller diff, but the parser has to chase key-generation changes forever. 3. **Group by hash prefix alone** (`name.split("_", 1)[0]`; hashes are hex and cannot contain `_`). Simplest and future-proof, but it couples eviction across models sharing a mount: same-hash entries of other instances would be evicted together, which has the same shared-mount courtesy problem as #32693. Related: #32693 (unscoped `clear()` on shared mounts) and the tenant-aware L3 directory layout discussed on #26693; a namespaced layout would make both this grouping and scoped clears trivial. ## Environment Found by code inspection on main @ 5f33000; affects any hybrid model (Mamba, SWA, DSA multi-component naming) using `--hicache-storage-backend nixl` with the L3 cleaner enabled.
signal.author: aaltinsoy

signal.title: Fix NIXL cleaner grouping for hybrid cache keys
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #32702. The NIXL FILE L3 cleaner must evict every physical shard of a logical cache entry atomically. `_parse_group_key()` removed only a trailing `_k`/`_v` and then a trailing TP-rank suffix, but hybrid names append their pool component after the rank (for example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k`), so the anchored rank match failed and one entry was split into independently evicted groups. ## Modifications - Build the hybrid pool-name pattern from `PoolName`, ordered longest-first for overlapping names such as `swa` and `draft_swa`. - Strip the generated hybrid component shapes (`_{pool}`, K/V, indexed, Mamba temporal, and Mamba convolution suffixes) before applying the existing K/V and TP-rank parsing. - Add CPU regression coverage for every component shape and for `_tick()` deleting legacy K/V files, hybrid components, and TP ranks as one logical group. For example, `page-a_model_0_8_swa_k` previously grouped as `page-a_model_0_8_swa`; it now groups as `page-a_model`, together with the entry's other ranks and components. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: this changes only background disk-eviction grouping and does not modify cache contents, transfer logic, or model computation. Focused CPU unit test: **9 passed, 8 subtests passed**. The test was run in a dependency-light Python 3.10 harness because this macOS checkout cannot install SGLang's CUDA-only runtime dependencies. Cleaner module coverage from the focused test is **76%**. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable: this is outside the inference hot path. The suffix regex is compiled once at module import and adds one match per file during a watermark-triggered background scan. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Fix] Transformers-fallback (GPT-NeoX) + KV pool config (DeepSeek-VL2)
signal.text: ## Summary Three small fixes surfaced by consecutive downstream accuracy runs. All three are one-liners (plus comments); the first two live in the Transformers-fallback layer, the third in `ModelConfig`. ### 1. `hf_to_sglang_mapper` — map `gpt_neox.` and `embed_out.` `GPTNeoXForCausalLM` has no native SGLang impl → falls back to `TransformersForCausalLM`. The fallback calls `AutoModel.from_config(config)`, which returns the bare `GPTNeoXModel` backbone (`embed_in`, `layers`, `final_layer_norm`) as `self.model`; `self.lm_head` is materialized separately by `CausalMixin`. Pythia / NeoX checkpoints were saved from `GPTNeoXForCausalLM.state_dict()`, so keys carry a `gpt_neox.` wrapper prefix for the backbone and a top-level `embed_out.` for the LM head. The base mapper has no rule for either, so the catch-all `""` → `"model."` fires and produces `model.gpt_neox.embed_in.weight` — which the loader can't find (`ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.gpt_neox' ...`). **Fix:** add two prefix rules alongside the existing `"transformer.": "model."` (GPT-2 analogue): - `"gpt_neox.": "model."` — strip the wrapper prefix so backbone keys land under `self.model.*`. - `"embed_out.": "lm_head."` — route the LM head to SGLang's `self.lm_head` slot. ### 2. `skip_substrs` — skip GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` causal-mask buffer Older GPT-NeoX checkpoints include a persistent causal-mask buffer named `gpt_neox.layers.N.attention.bias`. Newer transformers versions register the same buffer with `persistent=False`, so it is absent from the constructed model's tree. `self.skip_substrs` already skips GPT-2-style `.attn.bias` / `.attn.masked_bias` (attention module named `attn`), but not GPT-NeoX-style `.attention.bias` (attention module named `attention`). Result: `ValueError: No module or parameter named 'model.layers.0.attention.bias' ...`. **Fix:** add `.attention.bias` to the skip list. The already-present `.masked_bias` catches the fill-value counterpart regardless of attention module name. ### 3. `ModelConfig.v_head_dim` — treat `0` as unset (fixes DeepSeek-VL2 non-MLA V-cache) `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny`'s `language_config` sets `use_mla=False` **and** `v_head_dim=0` — the `0` is an MLA-disabled sentinel from the checkpoint's DeepseekV2-flavored config, not a real head dimension. `ModelConfig.__init__` currently substitutes `head_dim` for `v_head_dim` only when the attribute is `None`, so a `getattr` that returns `0` slips through into `self.v_head_dim`. `pool_configurator.py` then reads `model_config.v_head_dim` directly in the non-MLA branch, and per-slot V-buffers get allocated with last dim = 0. The first extend prefill fails: ``` File ".../mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 192, in _set_kv_buffer_impl v_cache[indices] = v RuntimeError: shape mismatch: value tensor of shape [432, 10, 128] cannot be broadcast to indexing result of shape [432, 10, 0] ``` DeepSeek-VL2 explicitly selects the standard (non-MLA) `DeepseekForCausalLM` language model when `use_mla=False` (`sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py`), which produces real V with the usual `num_kv_heads * head_dim` layout — the attention layer is correct; the pool is what's mis-sized. **Fix:** swap the guard to `if not self.v_head_dim:` so both `None` and `0` fall back to `self.head_dim`. MLA architectures are unaffected — their architecture-specific `elif` branches later in the same block overwrite `self.v_head_dim` with the real value from the text config. ## Test plan - [x] `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — passes locally for all three files. - [x] `EleutherAI/pythia-12b` (TP=2, triton) — reproduces the missing-mapper failure on `main`; loads through with fix 1. - [x] `EleutherAI/gpt-neox-20b` (TP=2, triton) — with fix 1 applied, reproduces the missing-skip failure on `main`; loads through with fix 2, warmup succeeds, first `POST /generate` returns 200. - [x] `deepseek-ai/deepseek-vl2-tiny` (TP=1, triton, `--disable-radix-cache`, mem-fraction 0.55) — reproduces the `_set_kv_buffer_impl` shape-mismatch on `main`; with fix 3, KV cache allocates `K size = V size = 3.38 GB` (previously `V size = 0.00 GB`), text `POST /generate` returns 200 with valid tokens. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32173524564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173524564)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32173523738](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173523738)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] feat: load GGUF transformer checkpoints (MiniMax-H3)
signal.text: ## Motivation MiniMax-H3's transformer is 61.7 GiB in BF16, and the FL2VA partition is 135 GiB in total. Layerwise offload already lets that run on a consumer card, so the barrier for those users is not VRAM — it is the download and the host memory that offload pins. This adds GGUF as a diffusion quantization family so the transformer can come from a single community-quantized file: **17.5 GiB instead of 61.7 GiB** for the same model. That shrinks the download, the pinned host memory, and the bytes streamed per layer, all by ~3.5x. It is complementary to `kitchen_int8` (#34581) rather than an alternative: that path is faster, but quantizes online and therefore still needs the full BF16 checkpoint on disk and in host RAM. **GGUF does not reduce peak VRAM** — peak is set by the offload buffers and VAE decode, not the weight dtype. There is also a large existing ecosystem of community GGUF checkpoints for other DiTs (Qwen-Image, Wan, FLUX), which this makes reachable. ## Modifications `--model-path` stays the base model; `--transformer-weights-path` takes the `.gguf`. A local path, `owner/repo/file.gguf`, or `owner/repo:QUANT_TYPE` all resolve. `--quantization gguf` is deliberately *not* the selector — the quantization is read from the file header. ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --transformer-weights-path leejet/MiniMax-H3-GGUF:Q4_K_M \ --num-gpus 1 \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --port 30010 ``` **New:** - `runtime/loader/gguf_weights.py` — header reader, tensor-layout metadata, weights iterator, Hub reference resolution. - `runtime/layers/quantization/gguf.py` — `GGUFConfig` + `GGUFLinearMethod`. Weights stay packed on device and are dequantized per use via the in-tree `ggml_dequantize`; `F.linear` broadcasts the DiT's N-D activations. **Changed:** - `loader/fsdp_load.py` (+10) — optional `weights_iterator` so a caller whose checkpoint is not safetensors can supply its own source. - `loader/transformer_load_utils.py` — GGUF resolution and the constraint checks. - `loader/component_loaders/transformer_loader.py` — routes the GGUF branch. - `models/dits/minimax_h3.py` (+6) — skip the qkv reorder, which translates the safetensors layout; GGUF already stores `[q_all, k_all, v_all]`. - `pipelines_core/lora_pipeline.py` — reject LoRA on packed weights before offload is disabled. The packed byte shape of every tensor is read from the header *before* the model is constructed, so `create_weights` registers each parameter with its exact packed shape. The generic weight loader's cast to the meta parameter's dtype is then a no-op on an already-`uint8` parameter, which is why **`linear.py` is untouched** and no lazily-materialized parameter is needed. **Rejected at startup**, rather than misbehaving later: non-CUDA, `--tp-size > 1`, FSDP for the loading component, LoRA (including a dynamic `set_lora`), `--quantization`, `--enable-svdquant`, the H3 AdaLN cache/online flags, a non-native byte order, and a tensor whose element count is not a whole number of 256-element super blocks (the K-quant/IQ dequantize kernels have no bounds check; IQ4_NL and IQ4_XS round the block count up and would write out of bounds). ## Accuracy Tests Dequantized weights compared tensor-by-tensor against the BF16 reference checkpoint (shard 1, all 54 shared tensors): | GGML type | tensors | min cosine | max rel. err | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | F32 | 9 | 1.00000 | 0.00000 | | BF16 | 24 | 1.00000 | 0.00000 | | Q4_0 | 3 | 0.99738 | 0.072 | | Q4_K | 18 | 0.99686 | 0.079 | End to end on 1× RTX 5090, `t2va` at 1344×768 × 107 frames: valid MP4 (H.264 + AAC 32 kHz stereo, clean full decode), output bit-identical across runs at a fixed seed. 36 CPU unit tests in `test/unit/test_gguf_diffusion.py`, passing with and without a visible GPU. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GGUF is not a speed optimization — it pays one dequantization per linear per denoise step. Measured on 1× RTX 5090, same checkpoint and request, showing the VAE offload trade-off (output bit-identical either way): | `--layerwise-offload-components` | Peak VRAM | Denoise | VAE decode | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `dit,text_encoder` | 26.3 GiB | 39.0 s | 9.5 s | | `dit,text_encoder,vae` | 19.6 GiB | 39.0 s | 57.2 s | Adding `vae` saves 6.7 GiB of peak at ~6x the decode time, because the decoder is re-streamed per tile. The docs give both rows so the choice is explicit. **Not validated:** other quantization types, the `ref2va` partition, multi-GPU (sequence parallelism is not rejected, since it shards activations rather than weights, but it is untested), Cache-DiT and `torch.compile` combinations. Pruned community checkpoints that fold the AdaLN branches into a low-rank table change the module structure and are not loadable by this path. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32173149796](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173149796)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32173149595](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173149595)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(diffusion): add OmniDreams autoregressive video world model
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Adds NVIDIA **OmniDreams** — a 2B distilled autoregressive driving-video world model (Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B based, production runtime = FlashDreams) — to `multimodal_gen`. Given a first frame + a per-frame HD-map (lane lines + actor boxes) control signal, it rolls out a temporally-coherent driving video via 2-step Self-Forcing flow-match denoising over a rolling block KV cache. Served both one-shot (HTTP `/v1/videos`) and realtime (WebSocket `/v1/realtime_video/generate`). Relates to #27214. Cookbook: [/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams/OmniDreams). ## Modifications - **DiT model:** OmniDreams 2B — 3D NeoX RoPE (44:42:42) with `shift_t` chunk positioning, AdaLN-LoRA modulation, flat-checkpoint loading (570-key `.pt`). - **AR pipeline (3 stages):** text/i2v/HD-map pre-encode → block-causal rollout (`BlockKVCache`: sink + rolling window) → seam-free Wan-2.1 VAE decode (clean per-chunk latents concatenated and decoded in one pass so the causal 3D cache flows across chunk boundaries). - **Conditioning:** 2-step flow-match scheduler (sigmas `{1.0, 0.8036, 0.0}`, shift=5.0) with first-frame i2v pinning; Cosmos-Reason1-7B `full_concat` text embedding; per-frame HD-map raster sequence VAE-encoded as one causal clip and sliced into per-chunk latent groups. - **Pure-Python runtime (no custom CUDA):** the vendored native CUDA FP8 DiT extension tree was removed; the runtime is now eager bf16 DiT + weight-only FP8 (pre-quantized E4M3 weights dequantized to bf16, cached for reuse), with an optional FP8-compute path (`torch._scaled_mm`). Self-attention uses SDPA; a SageAttention-3 FP4 backend and a CUDA-graph capture of the steady-state AR step are split out into separate follow-up PRs. The DiT file tree follows the single-file convention every sibling DiT uses (9 helper files → 4). - **Realtime online serving:** WebSocket `/v1/realtime_video/generate` streaming adapter (per-chunk HD-map control events + incremental frame output); `OmniDreamsRealtimeAdapter` reuses the `RealtimeModelAdapter` base class. Open-loop today (repeats last HD-map frame when the client lags); closed-loop per-chunk conditioning is planned. - **Serving:** TP via `Column/RowParallelLinear` head sharding (cross-view attention scaffolded, fail-loud gated off for single-view); HTTP API `hdmap_path` / `num_views`, with a guard rejecting local FS paths over HTTP (only `http(s)://` / `data:`) to close an arbitrary-file-read vector. - **Docs:** OmniDreams cookbook (`docs_new/cookbook/diffusion/OmniDreams/OmniDreams.mdx`) + card in the diffusion cookbook overview. ## Accuracy Tests Two fixes were needed to match the reference distribution and produce sharp output: - **Text encoder runs without an `attention_mask`** — the checkpoint is trained (FlashDreams' `CosmosReason1TextEncoder`) on the full padded sequence unmasked, and the DiT cross-attends over all 512 token embeddings (valid + padding). Adding a mask pushes padding-token conditioning OOD → washed-out rollouts (measured: normalized latent std collapses to ≈0.52 vs ≈0.84 unmasked). - **Clean first-frame re-injected during context-noise KV writes** so the pinned frame-0 doesn't accumulate noise in the rolling cache. **Distribution match:** after the text-conditioning fix the generated rollout's normalized latent std recovers `0.52 → 0.84`, matching real GT `≈0.84` — sharp, temporally coherent (no washed-out collapse). **Generalization, not memorization:** stays sharp across unseen seeds, mismatched first-frame/HD-map pairings, and a held-out scene; gen-vs-GT PSNR declines monotonically with rollout depth (`40.8 dB` @f1 → `23.6 dB` @f29). **CPU unit tests** — 101 cases in one file `test_omnidreams.py` (117 passed, 4 skipped with the lighttae/lightvae checkpoints available): ``` python -m pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_omnidreams.py -q ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling **rtx6kd (RTX 6000D 85GB, sm_120) — 13 frames, 2 denoise steps, default WanVAE:** | Path | Config | Denoise | Total | Peak VRAM | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | offline eager | `native_dit_acceleration=disabled` | 2.93s | 7.08s | 44.8GB | bf16 baseline | | offline **fp8_compute** | `native_dit_acceleration=fp8_compute` | 3.03s | 6.99s | 45.8GB | real FP8: 196 linears on `torch._scaled_mm`, weights stay FP8, SDPA attention. Faster than eager. | | offline `weight_only_fp8` (cold-start) | `native_dit_acceleration=weight_only_fp8` | 40.4s | 44.6s | 48.1GB | **dequant fallback**: loads the offline FP8 `.pt` then dequantizes to bf16 (~36s one-time, cached) and runs eager. For GPUs without FP8-compute; not the headline FP8 path. | | online `sglang serve` + `/v1/videos` | eager + WanVAE | 2.93s | 7.26s | 44.8GB | HTTP one-shot | Output is sharp across all paths (per-frame std ~48–52, frame-to-frame meandiff ~1.9, no gray-mush), numerically identical between eager and fp8_compute. **Two FP8 modes (both consume the offline-quantized `omnidreams_fp8_dit.pt` artifact):** - `fp8_compute` — the proper offline-quantization path: weights quantized to FP8 E4M3 (per-output-channel) and kept FP8 in VRAM; GEMMs via `torch._scaled_mm` (rowwise) + SDPA attention. Faster than eager on Blackwell. This is the recommended FP8 path. - `weight_only_fp8` — a fallback that dequantizes the offline FP8 weights back to bf16 and runs the eager DiT. It trades a one-time ~36s dequant (cached for the process lifetime) for a smaller checkpoint on disk, with no VRAM or steady-state speed benefit. Use it only on GPUs without FP8-compute support. **Benchmarks still missing:** - [ ] Warm-serve fp8_compute latency + realtime per-chunk latency (the SageAttention-3 backend + CUDA-graph capture were split out into follow-up PRs; will re-bench the warm/realtime paths once those land). - [ ] Multi-GPU / TP scaling (rtx6kd is single-GPU; needs a multi-GPU host). Sample inputs: `nvidia/omni-dreams-samples` (gated). HD-map is mandatory — without it the rollout goes OOD and collapses to gray after ~2 frames (expected). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) (OmniDreams cookbook + cookbook-overview card). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed) — partial (see Speed section: eager / fp8_compute / weight_only_fp8 done; warm-serve + realtime + TP scaling pending). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32173051147](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173051147)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32173050971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32173050971)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix(model-gateway): accept token ID prompts in /v1/completions
signal.text: ## Motivation The Python OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API accepts pre-tokenized prompts as `List[int]` and batched token prompts as `List[List[int]]`. The Rust model gateway currently models `prompt` as a string or an array of strings only. As a result, valid token-ID completion requests are rejected by Axum during request deserialization with HTTP 422 before they can be forwarded to the backend. This creates an API compatibility gap between the Python server and the Rust model gateway. ## Modifications * Extend the Rust completion prompt representation to accept: * text prompt * batch of text prompts * single token-ID sequence * batch of token-ID sequences * Preserve token-ID prompts when forwarding requests to workers. * Update completion batch-size detection for token-ID batches. * Add regression coverage for unified and PD routing paths. This PR only adds request parsing/forwarding compatibility. Token-ID prompts bypass the current text-based cache-aware routing; token-ID-aware radix/cache routing is intentionally left to a separate follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests This change does not modify model computation or model outputs. Route-level regression tests cover: * existing text completion * single `List[int]` token prompt * batched `List[List[int]]` token prompts * PD batch request semantics Before this change, a real Axum `/v1/completions` request with a token-ID prompt returns HTTP 422. With this change, the same request is accepted and forwarded successfully. Validation: * focused Rust tests: passed * `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`: passed * `cargo fmt --check`: passed * patch/apply check against upstream main: passed No GPU is required for this protocol-level fix. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. This is a request-schema and routing compatibility fix and does not change the inference execution path. ## Checklist * [ ] Format your code according to the [[Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). * [x] Add unit tests according to the [[Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). * [x] Update documentation according to [[Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing behavior beyond restoring existing Python API compatibility.) * [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [[Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [[Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (No performance benchmark needed for this protocol-only change.) * [x] Follow the SGLang code style [[guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance)](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32171702497](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32171702497)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32171702123](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32171702123)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(kv-events): Add component_types field to BlockStored for per-component placement tracking
signal.text: ## Motivation KV-aware routers consume `BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` to track which blocks live on which tier. On hybrid models the unified radix tree keeps several independent KV components on one node — full attention, sliding window, mamba state — and evicts and restores them independently. A `BlockStored` today only says "this block is on GPU". That is ambiguous once SWA has been tombstoned off an internal node while its full KV stays resident: the router still believes the block is fully reusable and routes a request that then has to recompute the window. This adds an opt-in per-component placement dimension so a consumer can tell what is actually resident at a given medium, following the same shape as #18205 which added the `medium` field. ## Modifications Gated behind `--enable-kv-events-component-types`, off by default. 1. **Schema.** A trailing `Optional[list[str]]` on `BlockStored` plus the `KV_COMPONENT_FULL/SWA/MAMBA` wire names. `BlockRemoved` stays whole-block — a removal always means the base (full) component left the tier, so there is nothing partial to express. 2. **Plumbing.** The flag flows from `ServerArgs` through `CacheInitParams` into the cache builder, and is documented in the server arguments reference. The UMBP subscriber logs the component dimension but does not forward it; its external-KV API is keyed by `(hashes, tier)` only. 3. **Emission.** `KVCacheEventMixin` gains a `_component_types_for_page` hook defaulting to `None`; `UnifiedTreeCore` overrides it and reports residency off live tree state, anchoring the single per-leaf mamba state to the leaf's last page. 4. **Tests.** 20 unit tests in `TestUnifiedRadixCacheComponentPlacementEvents`, plus wire-layout tests in `test_kv_events.py`. Three ordering constraints shaped the implementation and are worth flagging for review: - *Gains defer, losses do not.* SWA and Mamba attach device values through barrier-applied actions (`SWARebuild`, `MambaEvictExcessPathStates`), so a node's component set is not final until those apply. Inserts collect nodes in `_InsertWalkState` and emit one snapshot per node in the TAIL step; evictions are final when the component is dropped and emit immediately. - *Emission is root-first.* SWA splits the fresh leaf at commit time, so nodes are noted in neither tree nor creation order. `_record_store_event` seeds a node's lazily computed hash chain off its parent's hash, so announcing a child first would publish it as a root block under a hash no other code path reproduces. - *Partial eviction restates, never removes.* When SWA or Mamba is tombstoned while full survives the block has not left the tier, so we restate the smaller component set. Whole-block teardowns (`_demote`, host-leaf eviction) keep emitting `BlockRemoved` and never restate. `commit_load_back` also moves its emit after every component restores, unioning each component's `nodes_to_load`; emitting on full's list alone reported a promoted block as full-only. ## Subscriber compatibility `BlockStored` is a msgspec `array_like` struct, so every field is always encoded positionally — an unset `component_types` is a trailing `nil`, not an omitted slot (pinned by `test_component_types_is_the_trailing_slot`). With the flag **off** that `nil` is exactly what a positional decoder reads for an absent optional, so subscribers are unaffected; verified against both in-tree decoders, sgl-router (which drains unknown trailing fields, `experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/kv_events/wire.rs:420`) and dynamo's kv-router. With the flag **on**, the slot holds a list. sgl-router still ignores it. dynamo's kv-router, however, shares one positional layout with vLLM in which that slot is `lora_name` (a string), so it rejects the whole event batch. This is exactly why the feature is opt-in, and enabling it against a dynamo subscriber is not supported today. Aligning the two representations — dynamo already models this as one event per KV-cache group tagged with `kv_cache_spec_kind` — is a larger cross-project change and deliberately out of scope here. Only component-aware caches honour the flag; the mixin hook returns `None` elsewhere, so `radix_cache`, `hiradix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `mamba_radix_cache` and `hi_mamba_radix_cache` are untouched. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable — observability only. This touches no kernel, no model forward path, and no cache eviction or placement decision; it changes what is reported about placement, never the placement itself. Unit tests run locally across page_size 1/4/16/64/128 and the FULL, FULL+SWA, FULL+MAMBA and FULL+SWA+MAMBA configurations (`test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_kv_events.py`, and the radix/hiradix/swa/mamba mem_cache units): 1113 passed, 1030 skipped (config-conditional), 140 subtests passed. `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` is one of the 12 files currently deferred at module level by #31812 during the ServerArgs config-namespace migration, so those cases will not run in CI until that skip is lifted upstream; the run above was done locally with the module skip removed. signal.title: [Metrics] Discount queued prefill load by recent cache hits when waiting-queue matching is off
signal.text: ## Motivation `get_num_waiting_uncached_tokens` counts each waiting request's full `seqlen` when waiting-queue prefix matching is unavailable (cache-agnostic policy without fast prefix matching, or LPM past its 128-request queue limit). On cache-friendly multi-turn workloads this overstates queued prefill demand by an order of magnitude, inflating autoscaling signals derived from the load snapshot exactly when the queue is deep. ## Modifications - Track a token-weighted prefill cache-hit rate over a recent window in the scheduler metrics reporter (`SGLANG_CACHE_HIT_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS`, default 15s). The exported `cache_hit_rate` stats keep their per-report semantics. - `SchedulePolicy.waiting_queue_prefix_matched` reports whether waiting-queue requests carry exact `num_matched_prefix_tokens`. - When matching is on, waiting requests keep their exact uncached counts; when it is off, each waiting request is estimated as `seqlen * (1 - recent_cache_hit_rate)`. The active chunked request always uses its exact count. ## Test plan - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_load_inquirer.py` (new): policy predicate incl. the LPM queue-limit boundary; estimated vs exact waiting-token accounting. - `test/registered/unit/observability/test_forward_pass_metrics.py`: windowed hit-rate accounting incl. 15s expiry boundary. - Both pass locally (CPU-only). ## Original commits - `66221f5666` - `8fe5d4fcd3` - `681a9ba283` - `a930d560f9` - `d66a732a3b` ## Checklist - [x] Format your code with pre-commit - [x] Add unit tests <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32100733359](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32100733359)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32100818431](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32100818431)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
signal.author: hanming-lu

signal.title: [Fix] Handle aborts before assembling streaming logprobs in OpenAI endpoints
signal.text: ## Motivation Both OpenAI streaming handlers assemble logprobs *before* reading `finish_reason`, so a terminal chunk that carries `finish_reason: abort` and no logprob keys raises `KeyError` inside the handler instead of being emitted through the existing error path. A client streaming with `logprobs` enabled sees a handler crash rather than the abort error chunk. **Which aborts produce such a chunk:** `Req.set_finish_with_abort()` (`schedule_batch.py`) is the only place that clears `Req.return_logprob`. It is called from pre-enqueue validation — bad session id, prompt too long, grammar compile failure, multimodal prompt overflow after token expansion — not from running-request aborts. Clearing the per-request flag only matters if it also flips the batch-level flag, which is `any(req.return_logprob for req in reqs)`; the output streamer leaves `input_token_logprobs_val` at `None` when that batch flag is False, and `TokenizerManager.convert_logprob_style` early-returns on `None`, so `add_logprob_to_meta_info` never runs and the chunk has no `output_token_logprobs_length`. That second condition — no *other* request in the same batch asking for logprobs — is why this reproduces intermittently under load. Mid-flight aborts are not affected: OOM abort and retraction failure go out as `AbortReq`, which `_handle_abort_req` handles with `add_logprob_to_meta_info`, and the running-request timeout sets `req.to_finish` without touching `return_logprob`, so its arrays are `[]` rather than `None`. ## Modifications - `serving_chat.py` / `serving_completions.py`: hoist the `finish_reason` read above logprob handling and skip logprob assembly when `finish_reason_type == "abort"`. The abort chunk is then emitted through the existing error path unchanged. - Unit tests extended to cover the abort-with-logprobs chunk in both handlers (`test_serving_chat.py`, `test_serving_completions.py`). Note on the guard: `finish_reason_type != "abort"` is a proxy for "the logprob keys are absent". It is exact for the `set_finish_with_abort` path, which sets both, but it is broader than the crash — a running-timeout abort carries `finish_reason: abort` *with* valid logprob keys, and those logprobs are now dropped from the terminal chunk. Happy to narrow it to a presence check on `output_token_logprobs_length` instead if reviewers prefer that the guard track the actual invariant. This fix has been running in production on a high-traffic OpenAI-compatible deployment since late July. ## Accuracy Tests N/A — error-path fix, no model-output changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling N/A. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

signal.title: [XPU] Fix device assumptions and the ComfyUI passthrough denoise path
signal.text: > Supersedes #35365 and #35366, which were the same changes split by area. Combined here at the author's request; both are fallout from the same XPU test bring-up. The PR still needs CODEOWNER approval from **both** areas it touches — `/python/sglang/multimodal_gen` and `/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache` — and the two concerns are kept as separate commits so they can be reviewed (or reverted) independently. ## Motivation Bringing up the SGLang unit tests on XPU surfaced two classes of failure. Neither is XPU-only in nature: one is code that hard-codes CUDA where a device is already available, the other is device-independent bugs that only the XPU run happened to execute. **1. CUDA-hardcoded paths** (`srt`, mamba/GDN state and weight loading). The Triton kernels and pool allocations involved are not CUDA-specific, but they name CUDA explicitly, so they fail off CUDA. One of these is a latent bug on *any* device: the XPU `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` wrapper never passes `stride_h0_source`, which the shared kernel in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py` takes as a required argument (the CUDA caller passes it), so the wrapper cannot reach the kernel at all. **2. The ComfyUI passthrough denoise path** (`multimodal_gen`). This pipeline feeds pre-encoded embeddings straight to the transformer, so it runs neither `TextEncodingStage` nor timestep preparation — but three downstream consumers assume those stages have run: - `require_text_seq_lens()` reads `batch.prompt_seq_lens`, which only `TextEncodingStage` populates. - `DenoisingStage` reads `batch.scheduler`, which is left unset without timestep prep. - `ComfyUIPassThroughScheduler.step()` increments `self._step_index`, but `DenoisingStage` clears it to `None` before the loop, so the increment fails on the first step. These three are device-independent; the passthrough pipeline could not complete on CUDA either. ## Modifications ### Commit 1 — `[XPU] drop CUDA assumptions from the mamba/GDN and weight-load paths` - `srt/hardware_backend/xpu/kernels/fla/fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent.py`: pass `stride_h0_source=initial_state_source.stride(0)` (0 when the source is `None`). Envelope-strided state pools have a per-slot pitch `!= HV*K*V`, so the stride has to come from the caller. - `kernels/ops/mamba/mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`: `fused_mamba_state_scatter_with_mask` and `fused_conv_window_scatter_with_mask` rejected any tensor that was not `.is_cuda`. They now share a `_require_triton_device()` helper enforcing a common, non-CPU device — the guarantee the Triton kernels actually need. Error messages now name the calling function. - `srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py`: three `MambaPool` buffers were allocated with `device="cuda"` while every sibling allocation in the same methods uses the configured device. They now use it too. - `srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`: `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` / `synchronize()` after rebinding the embedding and LM head become `current_platform` calls. - `test/registered/model_loading/test_load_weights_from_remote_instance.py`: `torch.cuda.set_device/synchronize/empty_cache` become `current_platform` equivalents, the 2-GPU precondition uses `get_device_count()`, and `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE` / `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE` are only set on cuda-alike platforms. The `init_process_dst` `set_device` moved below `base_gpu_id` so it can use it — previously it called `set_device(rank * tp_size)` and then recomputed the same value. ### Commit 2 — `[diffusion] unblock the ComfyUI passthrough denoise path` - `comfyui_latent_preparation.py`: back-fill `batch.prompt_seq_lens` / `batch.negative_prompt_seq_lens` from the incoming embeddings, since there is no `TextEncodingStage` to do it. - `denoising.py`: resolve the scheduler through `get_or_create_request_scheduler()` instead of reading `batch.scheduler` directly. - `scheduling_comfyui_passthrough.py`: re-seed `_step_index` from `_begin_index` when `DenoisingStage` has cleared it. - `configs/pipeline_configs/base.py`: add `PipelineConfig.seq_lens_from_prompt_embeds()` — the "seq lens from maskless embeddings" rule (2-D means `batch=1`), previously inline in `TextEncodingStage`. - `text_encoding.py`: use the shared helper, so the new back-fill and the text-encoding path share one definition. - `test_flux_pipeline.py`: use `current_platform.device_type` instead of hard-coded `"cuda"`, and pass a zeroed `neg_pooled_embeds` when `negative_prompt_embeds` is set — Flux `time_text_embed` needs a pooled projection on every CFG branch. - `component_residency_strategies.py`: offload synchronously on XPU. An async copy into pageable host memory can reach the backend memcpy with a null argument there, and cannot overlap anything anyway. ## Accuracy Tests Nothing here changes model math on the existing CUDA paths: - `current_platform.empty_cache()` / `synchronize()` / `set_device()` dispatch to the `torch.cuda` equivalents on CUDA. - The `device="cuda"` → configured-device changes are no-ops when the configured device is CUDA, which it was in every path that previously worked. - `_require_triton_device()` only relaxes a precondition; the accepted CUDA inputs and the kernel bodies are untouched. - The `text_encoding.py` change is intended as a pure no-op refactor: `seq_lens_from_prompt_embeds()` reproduces the removed `ndim == 2` / else branches exactly. Two behavioral changes, both in paths that previously could not run: - `stride_h0_source` makes the XPU wrapper match the CUDA caller, which already passes the same expression. - The Flux passthrough test's CFG negative branch previously supplied no pooled projection at all. Local test logs are not attached yet. `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` is registered CUDA/AMD CI, so its existing coverage exercises the loader refactor directly — please trigger CI, and I will add XPU `test_flux_pipeline.py` output. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No expected impact. No kernel body, launch configuration, grid, or allocation shape changes; `stride_h0_source` is computed once per call from an existing tensor. The XPU offload change trades an async copy for a synchronous one on XPU only, where the async path could not overlap work regardless — CUDA offload behavior is unchanged. The remaining diffusion changes are one-time per-request setup, not per-step work. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — `black`, `isort`, `ruff` (repo rule set) and `codespell` all clean on the 12 files. - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — covered by the existing registered `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance` and by `test_flux_pipeline.py`, which is updated here; no new test file added. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — n/a, no user-facing API or flag change. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — rationale above; numbers to follow if reviewers want them. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32169094379](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32169094379)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32169093830](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32169093830)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Add MiniMax H3 cube sparse attention
signal.text: ## Summary - add a FlexAttention-based cube sparse attention backend for MiniMax H3's 3D visual streams - wire H3 packed-sequence metadata and denoise-step sparsity schedules into the native pipeline - keep text, audio, standalone reference images, and the text-only token refiner on dense attention - document the component-scoped command and add numerical, CUDA, admission, and parallelism coverage ## Behavior Select the backend only for the H3 transformer: ```bash --component-attention-backends transformer=cube_sparse_attn \ --attention-backend-config '{"local_cube_size":[4,4,4],"topk_ratio_list":[1.0,1.0,0.8,0.7,0.6,0.5,0.5]}' ``` A ratio of `1.0` uses H3's native FlashAttention path. Ratios below `1.0` use approximate cube sparsity. Ring parallelism is rejected because its attention exchange does not compose with this backend; Ulysses remains supported. ## Recommended `attention-backend-config` For `num_inference_steps=50` (49 denoise updates), use: ```json { "local_cube_size": [4, 4, 4], "topk_ratio_list": [ 1.0, 1.0, 0.55, 0.45, 0.35, 0.35, 0.30, 0.25, 0.25, 0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 0.05 ] } ``` Pass this JSON through `--attention-backend-config` alongside the component-scoped backend selection above. ## Implementation Note The Cube sparse attention backend in this PR is a reference implementation built with PyTorch FlexAttention. For higher performance on supported NVIDIA hardware, future work may explore replacing it with cuDNN Frontend's Block Sparse Attention ([cudnn-frontend/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention at main · NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/tree/main/python/cudnn/block_sparse_attention)) operator. Broader hardware support and backend-specific optimizations are left to future community contributions. ## Performance On 2×H100 with the 1344×768, 4-second, 8-step TP2 workload: - dense FlashAttention denoise: 16.51s - aggressive all-`0.05` sparse schedule: 13.32s (19.3% faster) - mixed `[1.0, 1.0, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5]` schedule: 19.67s The mixed schedule is slower on this short sequence because FlexAttention routing overhead outweighs the sparse-kernel savings, so the feature remains opt-in and the cookbook calls out the tradeoff. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32163799691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32163799691)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32163799272](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32163799272)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
