signal.title: [Diffusion] Candidate-trajectory execution contract (phase 1: types + validation)
signal.text: ## Summary Implements the candidate-trajectory execution contract proposed in #35331 as a real, opt-in path -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/pipelines_core/candidates.py`): - `CandidateTrajectorySpec` -- `count` / `reducer` / `return_candidates` / `seed_policy`, with eager validation: `count=1` must use `reducer="none"` (provably identical to the existing non-candidate path), `count>1` requires a real registered reducer. - `CandidateGroup` -- stable, sorted, unique `candidate_ids` per `request_id`. - A reducer registry (`"none"`, `"mean"`, plus `register_candidate_reducer()` for model-owned rules). - `derive_candidate_generators()` -- one `torch.Generator` per candidate, derived from `(base_seed, candidate_id)` via a splitmix64-style bit mixer. - `validate_candidate_admission()` / `reduce_candidates()` -- atomic group admission and partial-failure-safe reduction. **Real integration**: - `SamplingParams.candidate_spec`, validated against `num_outputs_per_prompt` -- the RFC's premise is that `num_outputs_per_prompt`'s existing outputs *become* the candidate axis, not a separate count, so `candidate_spec.count` must equal it. - **`InputValidationStage._generate_seeds`** (the real per-request seed/generator construction used by every model) now uses `derive_candidate_generators` instead of the existing naive `base_seed + i` scheme whenever `candidate_spec` is set. This is the RFC's core RNG-independence safety requirement, not a nicety -- plain addition can produce visibly correlated draws for nearby seeds. When `candidate_spec` is `None` (the default), behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. The actual candidate-reduction *application* point (averaging N action outputs down to one served result) needs real per-model tensor-shape knowledge -- e.g. Cosmos3's `action_latents` layout -- that can't be added correctly without a real model and weights to validate against. That's left for the model-adapter phase the RFC's own rollout plan describes (step 2: "Add a Cosmos3 action adapter"); the RNG-derivation wiring above is what's provably safe to land now. ## Test plan - **30 tests** in `test_candidate_trajectory.py` (27 original + 3 new), covering: - RFC required-tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (count=1 identity, sequential/batched seed equivalence, reducer parity, stable candidate IDs across co-batched requests, no partial-aggregate on failure). - The exact multi-prompt aggregation pattern `_generate_seeds` now uses: prompt-major/candidate-minor flattening order, cross-prompt independence, single-prompt equivalence to bare `derive_candidate_generators`. - Requirements 5, 6, 8 (CFG-parallel candidate membership, TP/SP reconstruction before reduction, conditional video-branch skip) still need a real model/pipeline adapter and are out of scope until that phase. All 30 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend. `input_validation.py` itself has a heavy import surface (`torchvision`, which isn't installed on this machine, plus a deep `pipeline_configs`/`platforms`/`server_args` chain) that makes it impractical to instantiate `InputValidationStage` directly in a local sandbox, so the new branch's logic is validated at the level of the RNG derivation it calls into (already exhaustively tested) rather than via a live call through the stage class; CI's full dependency stack can exercise that path directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35331. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166068209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166068209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166067961](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166067961)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Compile-plan trajectory promotion gate
signal.text: ## Summary Implements the data model and validation flow proposed in #35333: connects SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support (`DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` in `runtime/utils/torch_compile.py`) to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models -- turning "compile succeeded" into "this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature." - `CompileWorkloadSignature` -- the exact workload regime (model revision, dtype, backend, parallel signature, latent shape regime, step count, CFG/cache mode, state schema version) a compiled plan is valid for, with a stable sha256 `digest()` for use as a manifest key. - `TrajectoryGate` -- declares checkpoints and per-checkpoint tensor-parity thresholds (`cosine_similarity` as a *minimum*, `mae`/`mse`/`rmse`/`max_abs`/`l2` as *maximums*), plus a slot for model-specific output-quality metrics the framework deliberately does not compute itself. - `CompiledPlanManifest` -- the offline/CI artifact recording whether a compile plan was promoted (`"validated"`/`"rejected"`) for a signature. - `run_trajectory_gate()` -- warms and runs both an eager reference and a compiled candidate through a caller-supplied stepping function across a *full checkpoint schedule* (not a single isolated forward, per the RFC's core argument that one forward isn't enough to validate a stateful rollout), scores each declared checkpoint, and rejects on the first threshold miss. - `select_validated_plan()` -- the runtime-side lookup: does an incoming workload signature match a validated manifest, or fall back to eager. The manifest is an offline/CI artifact; the runtime never reruns the full reference rollout per request. `compute_tensor_metrics()` mirrors the metric semantics of the existing `tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` (cosine similarity, MAE/MSE/RMSE, max-abs, L2), reimplemented locally rather than imported, so this module carries no diffusion-specific dependencies (no `imageio`, no model loading) and stays independently testable. ## Scope Data model, validation, and the promotion decision itself -- matching the RFC's explicit non-goals ("this RFC does not enable [compile] globally"; "runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request"). Wiring an actual SGLang Diffusion model/pipeline through this gate as part of CI is follow-up work. ## Test plan `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_compile_trajectory_gate.py`, 18 tests, all passing: - Signature digest determinism and sensitivity to every field. - `TrajectoryGate`/`CompiledPlanManifest` validation (empty/duplicate checkpoints, missing threshold entries, invalid status). - `compute_tensor_metrics()` correctness (identical tensors score perfectly, shape mismatches raise). - **`run_trajectory_gate()` against a real `torch.compile` call** -- not mocked tensors: a toy stateful iterative `nn.Module` (linear + tanh, hidden state carried across steps, standing in for a denoising step) is wrapped with `torch.compile(backend="aot_eager")`, and both the eager and compiled versions are actually run through a multi-step rollout: - the compiled candidate's trajectory is confirmed `"validated"` against the eager reference at declared checkpoints; - a deliberately diverging candidate (same shape, shifted values, standing in for a broken/miscompiled plan) is confirmed `"rejected"`; - a checkpoint schedule that never visits a declared checkpoint, and a step function returning `None` for a declared checkpoint, both raise `CompileGateError` rather than silently passing. - `select_validated_plan()` -- matching signature returns the manifest, mismatched signature falls back to `None`, and a `"rejected"` manifest is never selected regardless of signature match. All 18 tests were run on the **Apple Silicon MPS backend** (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved `DEVICE`, not a silent CPU fallback -- so the `torch.compile` calls and tensor-metric computations are exercised on a real accelerator, not just plain Python logic. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35333. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166481922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481922)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166481726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166481726)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSV4] Fix SWA state pool over-allocation by using storage page size instead of model window
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation For DeepSeek-V4 models, DSV4PoolConfigurator sizes the c4 compressed-state pool using the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size = 128), while the runtime addresses that same pool using the pool's SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size = 256). These two values differ by 2x, causing capacity waste. <!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. --> ## Modifications Align the state-pool paging to the SWA storage page size (server_args.page_size), consistent with how DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool and CompressStatePool address the pool at runtime: self.swa_storage_page_size = mr.server_args.page_size # 256 c4_state_ratio = self.c4_ring_size / self.swa_storage_page_size c4_state_pool_size = swa_tokens // self.swa_storage_page_size * self.c4_ring_size A comment is added to disambiguate this storage page size from the model's SWA window (cfg.window_size / SWA_WINDOW = 128). This is not a correctness bug — the runtime already divides by 256, so the smaller pool stays within bounds; it purely recovers wasted capacity. <!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. --> ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling Validated on GB200 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP4 / DP4, default config, mem-fraction-static unconstrained). signal.title: [Diffusion] Step-reuse execution contract for iterative denoising models
signal.text: ## Summary Implements the step-reuse execution contract proposed in #35332 as a real, opt-in skip-forward strategy usable today -- not just a standalone contract module. **Contract layer** (`runtime/cache/step_reuse.py`): - `StepReusePolicy` -- declares `observation_point`, `history_size`, `max_skip_steps`, forced real-forward points (`first_one`, `first_two`, `terminal`), and the `state_scope` axes a policy is keyed by. - `StepReuseState` -- per-scope lifecycle: last real prediction, bounded similarity history, remaining skip budget, and metrics. - `StepSideEffectContract` -- lets a model declare that the terminal step must always run a real forward (e.g. to commit a persistent KV/session write). - `StepReuseController` -- multiplexes independent `StepReuseState` lifecycles across arbitrary `scope_key` tuples (request / modality / CFG branch / ...), enforces the skip budget and forced points, and never feeds a *reused* prediction back into the similarity history. **Real integration** (this is now wired into the actual serving path, not just tested in isolation): - `SamplingParams.enable_step_reuse` (+ `StepReuseParams`), mutually exclusive with `enable_teacache`/`enable_spectrum`. - Threaded through the OpenAI-compatible API surface: `protocol.py`'s Image/Video request schemas, `image_api.py`, `video_api.py` (both JSON and multipart form paths) -- mirrors every existing `enable_teacache` call site. - `StepReuseMixin` mixed into `CachableDiT` alongside `SpectrumMixin`/`TeaCacheMixin`, so any DiT model can opt in. - **`WanTransformer3DModel.forward()`** (`wanvideo.py`) actually calls it: a real, working alternative to the existing TeaCache call sites (should-skip check, block loop, cache/retrieve), gated by `enable_step_reuse`. A model-tuned threshold (like TeaCache's per-model `teacache_thresh` coefficients) would need real benchmarking against actual model output that isn't possible without GPU hardware and model weights, so `step_reuse_params` stays a single generic default on the base `SamplingParams` rather than a fabricated per-model number -- matching `teacache_params`' own convention (`None` at the base class, populated per model in `configs/sample/wan.py`). Per-model calibration is legitimate, separable follow-up work; it doesn't block the mechanism itself from being real and correct. ## Test plan - `test_step_reuse.py` -- 19 tests on the pure `StepReuseController`/`StepReusePolicy` contract (skip windows, forced points including the new `first_one`, side-effect contract, scope isolation, reset, metrics, validation). - `test_step_reuse_mixin.py` -- **5 new integration tests** wiring `StepReuseMixin` exactly the way `WanTransformer3DModel` does: real torch tensors, the real `set_forward_context` context manager, a toy DiT-like module. Covers reset-on-new-request, forced first/terminal steps, and CFG positive/negative branch isolation. - This test caught a real bug during development: copying `TeaCacheMixin`'s reset guard verbatim (`current_timestep == 0 and not self.is_cfg_negative`) is only correct if the negative CFG branch is always dispatched first at each timestep. Calling positive before negative silently double-reset and dropped state. Fixed with an order-independent "reset armed" flag instead of relying on that branch-order assumption. All 24 tests pass on the Apple Silicon MPS backend (`torch.backends.mps.is_available()`), confirmed via the test module's resolved device. Full production imports (the real `sglang.multimodal_gen.*` module tree) require this project's CUDA-only extras (`flashinfer`, `cuda-python`, etc.) that cannot install on this machine, so `test_step_reuse_mixin.py` was additionally verified against an isolated sandbox containing only the real source files it imports before being placed in the real test tree, where CI's full dependency stack runs it directly. Also verified clean against the repo's `black`, `isort`, and `ruff --select=F401,F821,UP037` configuration. Closes/relates to #35332. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166805209](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166805209)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166804905](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166804905)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Complete dots.note.omni support with native encoders, video preprocessing, and MTP decoding
signal.text: <!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. --> ## Motivation Merge dots.note.omni model ## Modifications This PR completes the SGLang integration of dots.note.omni, including: - Native in-process vision and audio encoders - Train-consistent native video preprocessing - Full-sharing MTP/NextN speculative decoding - DP/TP/EP execution support, including overlap scheduling - Correct KV-cache sizing for the hybrid sliding-window draft model ## How dots.note.omni differs from existing models dots.note.omni does not fit several assumptions made by existing multimodal and speculative-decoding paths. ### Multimodal architecture Unlike models that reuse standard Hugging Face vision/audio encoders, dots.note.omni uses: - A custom MoE vision transformer - A Whisper-derived audio encoder with a model-specific convolutional frontend and token-length calculation - Model-specific image and audio placeholder expansion - **A native video pipeline that jointly samples and interleaves frames, timestamps, and audio segments under a token budget** The video representation must match the training-time flattening algorithm. Applying a generic uniform-frame video processor changes the modality ordering, sampling strategy, and token allocation, which causes an inference/training mismatch. ### Language-model attention (**Introduce dots_hybrid_attn_backend**) The dots3 language model combines: - MLA - Full-attention and sliding-window layers with different attention geometry - Optional DSA indexing on full-attention layers - Head-wise or element-wise attention gates Therefore, its full-attention and SWA layers cannot always share the same attention path or KV-cache accounting. ### MTP structure the standard single-layer EAGLE/NextN execution path with an ordinary SWA-capacity, MLA-based draft layer. ## Model-specific changes ### Native vision and audio towers This PR migrates the dots.note.omni encoders into SGLang: - Adds the dots MoE ViT implementation - Adds the dots audio model and Whisper-derived speech encoder - Uses SGLang FA3 and fused MoE kernels - Loads encoder weights directly from the model directory - Removes runtime imports and compatibility shims for mm_encoder_server - Honors --language-only, allowing encoder/LLM disaggregation and text-only deployments without loading the multimodal towers ### Train-consistent video preprocessing This PR vendors the required dots video flattening pipeline and integrates it with the OpenAI chat API. The processor: - Accepts a native video_url - Decodes and processes remote video payloads entirely in memory - Uses the tokenizer loaded from the served model - Produces interleaved timestamp, image, and audio content matching training - Uses a deterministic seed derived from the video and question - Reserving the context budget for each video input - Falls back to visual-only processing if audio would exceed the configured token budget - Records per-request preprocessing latency The following request-scoped controls are added: | Field | Purpose | |-------|---------| | seq | Total sequence budget used by the video flattener | | audio_cap | Maximum fraction of the input budget assigned to audio | | audio_sr | Audio sample rate | | k_mode | Deterministic evaluation/sampling mode | These options are request-scoped because evaluation jobs with different context budgets may share one server. Current native-video limitations: - One video per request - A native video cannot currently be mixed with separate image or audio inputs in the same request ### Full-sharing MTP/NextN A dedicated Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN draft model is added. For draft-model loading, the dots3 configuration is rewritten before attention shapes and KV-cache geometry are derived: - The draft architecture becomes Dot3NoteForCausalLMNextN - Exactly one recursively shared MTP layer is exposed - The layer uses the dots3 SWA attention geometry - A checkpoint-provided MTP embedding is retained when present - The target LM head is shared with the draft model Target verification and draft extension use the paged, absorbed SWA-MLA path. The expanded SWA-MHA path remains limited to prefill, where its logical-tail metadata is available. ## Shared SGLang changes and why they are needed The changes below are implemented in shared infrastructure because the underlying correctness conditions are not specific to one model name. ### 1. Hybrid SWA draft KV-cache accounting The existing hybrid pool configurator charged all EAGLE/NextN draft layers as full-attention layers. That is incorrect for dots3 because its shared draft layer is an ordinary SWA layer with: - SWA latent-vector geometry - SWA token capacity rather than full-attention capacity The speculative auxiliary configuration now records how many draft layers are SWA layers. The hybrid pool configurator separately accounts for: - Full-capacity full-attention draft layers - Ordinary SWA draft layers using the target SWA capacity - Full-capacity SWA-shaped draft layers, such as the existing Inkling case This prevents both under-allocation and unnecessary loss of target KV-cache capacity. The logic is generic for hybrid-SWA models using EAGLE-family draft models. ### 2. DP dummy-row normalization for overlap MTP With DP attention and overlap scheduling, an idle rank must still participate in MLP and attention collectives. SGLang creates dummy rows for this purpose. For speculative decoding, attention metadata may be planned before DP synchronization adds those rows. This previously left the following structures with inconsistent request dimensions: - GPU and CPU extend-length metadata - Prefix-length metadata - Draft cache locations - Positions and hidden states - Dense attention page tables - Draft logits returned to the speculative worker This PR normalizes speculative dummy rows before draft buffers are allocated, keeps the CPU and GPU metadata aligned, preserves the normalized output rows on idle ranks, and exposes a backend hook to refresh row-dependent attention metadata after DP padding. The backend hook defaults to a no-op. Only backends whose metadata can be safely rebuilt opt in, so pre-planned sparse/DSA schedules remain untouched. ### 3. Attention page-table normalization A shared helper is added to align a pre-planned page table with a DP-normalized batch. It truncates extra rows or appends zero-valued dummy rows. Both the dots hybrid backend and the FA3 SWA-MLA fallback use this helper. This avoids model-name checks and makes the invariant explicit at the attention-backend boundary. ### 4. FA3 SWA-MLA fallback dots3's MTP layer is both SWA-shaped and MLA-based. Target verification and draft extension already have a paged latent KV view, while the existing expanded SWA-MHA path is designed for prefill. FA3 therefore gains an absorbed SWA-MLA fallback that consumes the SWA page table and latent KV cache directly. This is exposed as a backend capability and selected by the model only when available. ### 5. OpenAI request and internal request plumbing The dots video controls and the unrendered user question are propagated through: - ChatCompletionRequest - OpenAI chat serving - GenerateReqInput - The dots multimodal processor The original question is required because the training-consistent adapter uses it for deterministic sampling and cache-key construction. It cannot reliably be recovered from the rendered chat prompt, which also contains template, role, and system tokens. The new fields retain defaults and are only consumed by the dots native-video path. ### 6. Encoder/LLM disaggregation validation Dot3NoteForCausalLM is added to the architectures allowed to use --encoder-only and --language-only. The model itself skips vision and audio tower construction in language-only mode. This avoids consuming memory needed by the language model and enables the standard encoder-disaggregation deployment pattern. ## Tests The PR adds coverage for the shared correctness changes: - The DSA K-only rotary path does not alias query and key inputs - Draft-extend dummy requests keep CPU and GPU length metadata aligned - Idle speculative batches retain normalized dummy logits and hidden states - Hybrid-SWA draft layers use SWA geometry and capacity during KV-cache sizing An EP8/TP8/DP8 launch script is also included for dots.note.omni with: - DeepEP - NEXTN speculative decoding - FA3 draft attention - Optional overlap scheduling - Optional language-only mode - Optional DSA and speculative-decoding switches ## Accuracy Tests <!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. --> ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. signal.title: fix: guard top-logprobs and token-ids logprob rows against missing data
signal.text: ## Motivation Follow-up to #34627. That PR removed the early return that dropped output logprobs when input logprobs are absent, but the removed return had also been shielding everything below it: with output-only logprob requests, execution now reaches the top-logprobs and token-ids blocks that still assume input-side data is present. - `return_logprob=True, top_logprobs_num>0` without input logprobs: the scheduler leaves `ReqLogprob.input_top_logprobs_val` at `None` when the prefill pass did not compute input-side top logprobs, and the output streamer appends that per-request `None` into the batch list. `len(recv_obj.input_top_logprobs_val) > 0` therefore passes, and `state.input_top_logprobs_val.extend(None)` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`. - `token_ids_logprob` set without input logprobs: the same shape arrives for the input-side token-ids rows (and the output-side fields can be `None` on paths that never populated them). ## Modifications Extend each side only when both the batch-level field and the per-request row are present, mirroring the guards #34627 added for the plain logprob fields: - input top logprobs: `is not None and len(...) > 0 and [i] is not None` - output top logprobs / token-ids rows: `is not None and [i] is not None` ## Verification - New regression tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_flat_raw_top_logprobs.py` (same stub style as the #34627 regression test): - `test_output_top_logprobs_without_input_logprobs` - `test_token_ids_logprobs_without_input_logprobs` - Both fail on current `main` with the predicted `TypeError` at `tokenizer_manager.py` (`extend(None)`) and pass with this change; the pre-existing tests in the file still pass (30 passed, 2 skipped locally). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32166870429](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166870429)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32166870120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32166870120)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] [Spec] Enable stochastic tree verification on ROCm
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm EAGLE verification currently routes every HIP request through greedy `argmax`, even when `temperature`, `top_p`, or `top_k` request stochastic sampling. ROCm also lacks the CUDA target-only tree-sampling kernel and its top-k/top-p renormalization operators. While validating a portable tree verifier with GLM-5.2-FP8, EAGLE top-k > 1 exposed a second blocker: DSA’s page-64 index cache received physical token-slot IDs but indexed them as page rows: ```python index_k[tgt_loc_flat] = index_k[src_loc_flat] ``` On MI355X this failed during draft cache preparation, before target verification: ```text HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION: An HSAIL operation resulted in a hardware exception (0x1016) torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure ``` Both the stochastic verifier and page-aware DSA relocation are required for a complete ROCm top-k > 1 tree path. ## Modifications ### Target-only tree verification - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/tree_sampling.py` - Add the Triton target-only stochastic tree verifier and residual bonus-token sampling. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/__init__.py` - Register the Triton tree-sampling operator for CUDA and HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py` - Route non-greedy HIP EAGLE requests to the Triton tree verifier; preserve chain rejection sampling and greedy dispatch. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py` - Enable the same target-only Triton verifier for DFLASH on HIP. - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py` - Advertise tree-kernel availability on HIP. ### Portable probability renormalization - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm.py` - Add exact threshold-based top-k/top-p pivots, tie handling, and full-sort overflow fallback. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/renorm_triton.py` - Fuse pivot application, masked reduction, and normalization for HIP. - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/sampling/__init__.py` - Select CUDA AOT, HIP Triton, or portable Torch implementations through the kernel registry. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` - Reuse the portable top-p semantics in the Torch sampler path. ### Page-aware DSA tree relocation - `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/index_buf_accessor.py` - Add overlap-safe gather/scatter kernels that move each token’s 128-byte FP8 index key and 4-byte FP32 scale by `(page, offset)`. - Preserve AITer’s 16x16 preshuffled K layout and CUDA’s row-major layout. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/index_key_cache.py` - Replace token-slot-as-page-row indexing with logical K/scale relocation. - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/dsa_cache_layer_split.py` - Remove the duplicated broken override so layer-sharded caches inherit the corrected implementation. ### Tests - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_spec_verify_distribution.py` - `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` ## Accuracy Tests ### MI355X unit tests on final PR commit ```text TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_torch_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_seeded_inputs_are_repeatable TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_dflash_sampling_integration_matches_oracle TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_branched_tree_preserves_target_distribution TestTreeSpeculativeSamplingTriton.test_matches_cuda_aot_oracle [skipped on ROCm] TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_hip_target_only_uses_triton_tree TestSpecSamplingDispatch.test_rejection_sampling_uses_triton_chain TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_chain_sampler_preserves_target_distribution TestSpecVerifyDistribution.test_greedy_verify_collapses_to_argmax TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_k_scalar_and_per_row TestPortableSpecRenorm.test_top_p_per_row_and_zero_mass TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_cross_page_overlap_and_identity TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_empty_move TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_layer_split_skips_non_owned_buffers TestDSAIndexCacheMove.test_page64_tree_prefix_tail_duplication ``` | Test file | Result | |---|---:| | `test_tree_speculative_sampling_triton.py` | 4 passed, 1 CUDA-only skip | | `test_spec_verify_distribution.py` | 5 passed, 1 sgl-kernel-only skip | | `test_dsa_index_cache_move.py` | 4 passed | | Pre-commit, all 15 changed files | Passed | CUDA-only registered renormalization oracles: ```text TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_k_fallback_matches_kernel TestSpecRenormFallbacks.test_top_p_fallback_matches_kernel ``` ### GLM-5.2-FP8 customer workload Apex Shortlist problem 4, gold answer `2618`, `n=8`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=131072`, EAGLE top-k 2 / 5 steps / 6 draft tokens. | Platform | Correct | Stop | Length | Completion tokens | Server exceptions | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | MI355X, TP8 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 317,649 | 0 | | GB300, TP4 | 7/8 | 8 | 0 | 357,376 | 0 | MI355X top-k 3 stress: 27,681 completion tokens, 0 server exceptions. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No valid end-to-end before/after comparison exists: the previous HIP path silently executed greedy verification instead of the requested stochastic algorithm, and DSA top-k > 1 page-64 serving crashed before completion. Kernel optimization will follow separately. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No semantically valid baseline exists.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. signal.author: Raiden-Makoto

signal.title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
signal.text: # [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3 ## Summary This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined. Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses: - an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access; - direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers; - asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and - a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts. The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path. ## Usage Install this branch from source before running the examples: ```bash python3 -m pip install -e "python" ``` ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash Download the tested FP4/FP8 GGUF from [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash). The benchmark used the immutable model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`. ```bash python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP4-FP8-native.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` ### Kimi-K3 Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`. ```bash hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \ --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \ --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3 ``` ```bash python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \ --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \ --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \ --max-new-tokens 200 ``` The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward. | Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** | | Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** | The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom. ## Correctness - DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts. - Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`. ## Performance The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs. ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt. | Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** | | Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** | ### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens. | Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** | | Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** | The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32151441084](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151441084)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32151440956](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32151440956)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Fix] Select custom all-reduce v2 by topology capability
signal.text: ## Motivation This fixes a regression introduced by #32541. Before that PR, custom all-reduce v2 was enabled by default and eligible TP16 groups reached the topology and allocator capability check. The added TP2-8-specific multinode policy disabled `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` for TP16 before capability detection, forcing an otherwise eligible configuration to fall back. ## Modifications - Remove the separate multinode flag and server-argument policy; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2` remains the single enable and opt-out control. - Select cross-node v2 from the actual topology, VMM allocator capability, and architecture-tuned world sizes. - Let eligible custom all-reduce inputs run before symmetric-memory PyNccl; larger inputs still fall through. - Replace the server-argument policy tests with capability and dispatch tests. ## Original commits - `fb9411abe` ## Accuracy Tests No model math changes. - `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py` — 10 passed. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No public speed benchmark was run. The change restores the eligible TP16 custom all-reduce v2 path and preserves fallback for unsupported topology or message sizes. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). Pre-commit passed for the changed files. The bare-pytest checker was run directly under Python 3.12 because its isolated hook interpreter cannot parse the `int | None` annotation used by the checker. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31978608777](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978608777)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31978608691](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31978608691)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Refactor kv cache event mixin into a recorder
signal.text: ## Motivation `.claude/rules/general-code-style.md` says to avoid mixins and prefer explicit composition. `KVCacheEventMixin` is the shape that rule is about: it carries no state and reads four attributes off whichever class inherits it (`kv_event_queue`, `enable_kv_cache_events`, `page_size`, `root_node`). Four classes inherit it, plus four more transitively, and each assembles that attribute set by hand in its own `__init__`. Missing one fails at runtime, and the contract is stated nowhere. `KVCacheEventRecorder` owns the queue and the two settings instead, so a cache holds one and calls it: ```python self.kv_events = KVCacheEventRecorder( enabled=params.enable_kv_cache_events, page_size=self.page_size ) ... self.kv_events.record_store(node, medium=StorageMedium.CPU) ``` The test suite already wanted this. `test_radix_cache_unit.py` carried a `_KVCacheEventQueue(KVCacheEventMixin)` shim whose whole body assigned the two attributes the mixin needed, only so the coalescing logic could be exercised on its own. That shim is gone and the test constructs a recorder. ## Modifications - `events.py`: `KVCacheEventMixin` becomes `KVCacheEventRecorder`, holding `enabled`, `page_size` and the queue. `_record_store_event` / `_record_remove_event` / `_record_all_cleared_event` / `_enqueue_kv_event` / `take_events` become `record_store` / `record_remove` / `record_all_cleared` / `enqueue` / `take`. - 34 call sites across 8 files now go through `self.kv_events`. - `BasePrefixCache` grows `kv_events: Optional[KVCacheEventRecorder] = None`, alongside the `metrics_collector` and `cache_controller` it already declares that way, and `take_events` delegates to it. That keeps the published `take_events` contract in one place rather than as four identical overrides. `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` is not a `BasePrefixCache`, so it declares `kv_events` and its own `take_events`. - `hiradix_cache.py` had the only read of `enable_kv_cache_events` outside the mixin. It now reads `self.kv_events.enabled`, so the flag has a single home. - `record_store` reached back into its owner for `root_node`, to tell whether a parent is the tree root and so contributes no parent hash. It asks the node instead, `node.parent.parent is None`. That is what lets the recorder be built once and left alone, since all four `reset()` implementations install a fresh `root_node` and a stored reference would need re-wiring every time. The two forms agree because a root has no parent (`TreeNode.__init__` sets `self.parent = None`, and `UnifiedTreeCore`'s sanity check reports "root has a parent pointer" as an error) and nothing in `mem_cache` clears a live node's parent. ## Accuracy The published event stream is unchanged: the emitter was compared against main over every payload branch (root-parented node, multi-page node, short last page, `cache_salt`, bigram key, GPU and CPU media, coalescing and non-coalescing removes, `AllBlocksCleared`) and produced identical events. `mem_cache` unit suite: 1119 passed, 1030 skipped, 0 failed. `flexkv_radix_cache.py` raises at import without the FlexKV package, on this branch and on main alike, so both storage integrations are covered by compile plus a static check that no old reference survives and both call sites moved. No remaining references under `python/` or `test/` to `KVCacheEventMixin`, `_record_store_event`, `_record_remove_event`, `_record_all_cleared_event`, `_enqueue_kv_event` or `kv_event_queue`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32091916969](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091916969)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32091916636](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091916636)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: preserve output logprobs without input logprobs
signal.text: ## Motivation SGLang drops generated-token logprobs in the Python Engine API path when prompt/input logprobs are not requested. `convert_logprob_style()` currently returns when `input_token_logprobs_val` is `None`, even if valid output logprobs are present. Consequently, downstream consumers such as Dynamo receive no logprobs for output-only requests like `logprobs=true, top_logprobs=0`. Downstream context: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/12820 ## Modifications - Process input logprobs only when input logprob data is present. - Process output logprobs independently when output logprob data is present. - Add a regression test for output logprobs without input logprobs. ## Before and After Launch SGLang without its tokenizer so top-logprob candidates contain token IDs and logprobs but no decoded token text: ```bash python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 \ --skip-tokenizer-init ``` SGLang returns the candidate’s token ID and logprob, but its decoded text is missing: ```json { "output_top_logprobs": [ [ [-0.42, 1234, null] ] ] } ``` Send a request for one top-logprob candidate: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:30000/generate \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "input_ids": [45764, 23811], "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1 }, "return_logprob": true, "top_logprobs_num": 1, "logprob_start_len": -1 }' ``` **Before this PR**, Dynamo could pass the incomplete candidate metadata into the OpenAI response: ```json { "token": null, "bytes": null, "logprob": -0.42 } ``` **After this PR**, Dynamo uses the candidate token ID to fill in the missing text and bytes while preserving the original logprob: ```json { "token": "A", "bytes": [65], "logprob": -0.42 } ``` ## Accuracy Tests This does not change model computation or generated text. It only preserves already-computed output logprob metadata. Validation: - New focused SGLang unit test: 1 passed. - Adjacent SGLang tokenizer-manager tests: 28 passed, 2 skipped. - Dynamo GPU end-to-end matrix passed for: - Non-streaming: `top_logprobs=0`, `top_logprobs=1`, and omitted. - Streaming: `top_logprobs=0` and `top_logprobs=1`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31640510083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31640510083)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31640509938](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31640509938)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] ComfyUI: add a MiniMax-H3 node and a generic extra-fields passthrough
signal.text: ## Summary The ComfyUI plugin's executors cover flux / qwen_image / zimage — all image models — so there was no route to MiniMax-H3 from ComfyUI. H3 does not fit the executor route. It denoises a packed video+audio sequence in one pass and routes conditioning by task (`t2va` / `fl2va` / `ref2va`), while ComfyUI's KSampler drives a single latent tensor and has no audio branch. Rebuilding that inside ComfyUI would duplicate the visual/audio/reference conditioning stages the server already runs, so this wires H3 through the server route instead. Two changes: - **`generate_video` gains `extra_fields`.** The video request schema already accepts unknown fields, so the client only needed a way to reach a model's own request surface. `extra_fields` is merged last, so a model-specific field wins over a generic default of the same name. No further change to this client is needed for the next model that adds request fields. - **`SGLDiffusionGenerateH3`** builds H3's `task` / `conditions` / `target` shape from ComfyUI-native inputs. Keyframes carry a `frame_index`; references keep request order because the prompt addresses them positionally per modality; local paths become `file://` URIs while remote URLs pass through unchanged. Output dimensions are read from the response, because H3 aligns the canvas server-side and `short_edge` alone cannot reconstruct it. ## Test plan - [x] 9 new tests drive the real node through the real client and mock only HTTP, so a change on either side of the payload contract fails. They cover the three task shapes, keyframe frame-index mapping, modality ordering for prompt tags, remote-URL passthrough, the server-resolved canvas, the task/conditioning validation errors, and `extra_fields` precedence. - [x] Run on a plain checkout and on an H200 box: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/test/test_h3_request.py --import-mode=importlib` **Not covered:** an end-to-end run against a live H3 server. The tests pin the request shape against the documented contract and the shape used by the existing H3 CI case, but nothing here has generated a video through ComfyUI yet. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32158669747](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32158669747)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32158669388](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32158669388)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion] docs: document the request-level quality parameter
signal.text: ## Motivation `quality` is documented today as a single paragraph inside the OpenAI API page, while every peer lever — attention backends, caching, progressive resolution, quantization, parallelism, encoder parallelism — has its own page. It is also the only one of those a caller sets *per request*, so it is the page a user is most likely to go looking for and not find. The bigger problem is that the one paragraph makes `high` read as a single, uniform tradeoff. It is not. ## What the page documents `high` selects whatever accelerated path the model owns, and those paths are not the same class of change: | Model | What `high` mounts | Class | | --- | --- | --- | | FLUX.1 / Qwen-Image / GLM-Image | fused linear + tanh-GELU | same math, different rounding order at BF16/FP16 | | Ideogram 4 | fused gate-RMSNorm chains | approximate — norm statistics in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 | | any pipeline on one of three gated VAE classes | re-associated decoder fast path | not bit-exact; independent of whether the model has transformer sites | | MiniMax-H3 | Cache-DiT | measured approximation — SSIM 0.931 / PSNR 28.16 dB on its audited workload | Behaviours that are easy to get wrong, documented with the guard that causes them: - an unsupported `high` is a **silent no-op** — no warning, no error, and there is no capability API to check first; the only positive signal is a `Mounted ... for quality=high` log line - FLUX.1's LayerNorm fold requires batch size 1, so it does nothing under CFG batching or multiple outputs per prompt, even when mounted - `lossless` does not mean "unfused" — the bit-exact fused kernels run at both levels - `lossless` is **not** a master off switch for Cache-DiT, quantization, progressive resolution, approximate attention, or torch.compile - on MiniMax-H3, `high` **fails closed** against an audited deployment and request shape, and sending the field at *either* level suppresses the `SGLANG_CACHE_DIT_ENABLED` path - `quality` participates in the dynamic-batch signature, so mixed-level traffic never merges - realtime sessions and the WebUI ignore the parameter entirely Every measured number is given together with the workload it was measured on. The page states plainly that only MiniMax-H3 has an in-tree acceptance measurement and that every other model is unmeasured, and gives an A/B recipe for validating drift on your own workload. ## Note for reviewers Two things I could not settle from the source tree and deliberately did not guess at: 1. **GLM-Image and Ernie-Image are left unplaced in the VAE table.** `VAELoader.load_customized` resolves the VAE class from the checkpoint's `_class_name`, so which of the gated classes they load is a property of the published checkpoints, not of the repo. If GLM-Image does load `AutoencoderKLWan`, it would be the only model taking both a transformer fusion and a VAE fusion under `high` — worth confirming against a real checkpoint. 2. **`docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx` says `lossless` output "is bit-exact against the reference implementation and the CI ground truth."** The consistency suite compares CLIP/SSIM/PSNR thresholds rather than exact equality, so this page describes `lossless` as "the reference numerics" and reconciles the two claims in a sentence rather than silently contradicting the cookbook. If the cookbook's stronger claim is backed by something I did not find, this page should be adjusted to match instead. ## Checklist - [x] Content verified against `origin/main` (`fb72a37`) - [x] Registered in `docs/docs.json` under Performance Optimization - [x] Every relative doc link and the in-page anchor resolve to existing files - [x] Follows the house conventions of the peer pages (frontmatter, `tag: "approx"`, styled tables, section order) 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31321080422](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31321080422)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31321080381](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31321080381)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [UnifiedTree] feat: support runtime attach/detach
signal.text: ## Motivation `UnifiedRadixCache.attach_storage_backend` / `detach_storage_backend` were stubs that always returned `False`, so the `/hicache/storage-backend` admin API only worked with `HiRadixCache`. This implements them for the unified tree. Preceding fix for #35081. Supersedes #35240 (same feature, developed in parallel). ## Modifications **`unified_cache/storage_attachment.py` (new).** `StorageAttachment` owns the storage backend lifecycle: policy validation, extra-config parsing, controller attach, the ordered teardown, and `apply_runtime_config()`. Keeping it beside the tree rather than inside it leaves `UnifiedRadixCache` on cache logic and gives the three entry points — startup, the admin API, and the atexit hook — one implementation. `UnifiedRadixCache` goes from 2764 to 2520 lines. `apply_runtime_config()` is the single point where storage turns on, which is why the hash backfill below lives there rather than in `attach()`. **Hash-chain backfill (correctness).** Page hashes chain off the parent's last hash, and `_add_new_node` only computes them when storage is enabled. A node built before attach therefore has no hash, and hashing its children against it restarts the chain mid-sequence — the resulting L3 keys claim to encode a full prefix but only encode a suffix, so an unrelated request starting with those tokens loads KV computed under a different prefix, silently. Reproduced end-to-end with `--page-size 64` and explicit `input_ids` (P, R, Q are 128 tokens each): request `P+R` with storage off, attach, request `P+R+Q`, flush, then request `Q+S`. | | L3 hit for the `Q`-prefixed request | |---|---| | without backfill | **128 tokens** — loaded KV computed after `P+R` | | with backfill | **0** — correctly misses | | control: same sequence after its own backup | 128 in both, so L3 itself is healthy | `UnifiedTreeCore.backfill_missing_hash_values()` walks parent-before-child so each node hashes against an already-filled parent. **`cache_controller.py`.** The storage control queues are now initialized to `None` in `__init__` instead of only existing after `_start_storage_threads()`, so a detach on a server that never attached is a clean no-op rather than an `AttributeError`. ## Accuracy Tests Output stability is asserted throughout: every scenario re-runs fixed prompts and compares them byte-for-byte against a baseline captured before any attach. ## Tests **15-scenario attach/detach state machine**, run in one server process, asserting per step that the HTTP result is as expected, the server stays healthy, output is unchanged, and `GET /hicache/storage-backend` reflects reality: - traffic → attach → traffic → detach → traffic - attach → traffic → detach - attach → attach (same backend → 200, policies updated; different backend → 400, state unchanged) - attach → detach → detach; detach before any attach - attach/detach cycled 5× with traffic in between - interleaved traffic/attach/traffic/attach/traffic/detach/traffic/detach/traffic - L3 actually used when attached (960 tokens) and unused when detached (0) - invalid policies rejected without changing state - attach onto a warm tree, then extend an existing prefix (the backfill path) - **attach/detach hammered under concurrent traffic**: 16 ops → `[200, 400×15]`, every 400 a `not idle` refusal, state never half-applied, no output drift - **8× attach + real L3 traffic + detach**: L3 hit count constant at 960 across rounds, which is the observable proof that host pages come back (the scheduler's invariant checker guards the device pool but not the host pool) Result: **157 PASS / 0 FAIL on 1 GPU and again under `--tp-size 2`** (48 attaches, repeatedly creating and destroying the prefetch gloo groups; no traceback, SIGQUIT, leak or NCCL/gloo anomaly after server ready). **Unit tests** — `TestUnifiedRadixCacheStorageAttachBackfill` pins the contract that a backfilled hash chain is identical to one hashed from the start. Verified by mutation: stubbing `backfill_missing_hash_values` to `return 0` turns two cases red; restoring it turns them green. Full file: 1046 passed, 0 failed. **Registered e2e** — `test_hicache_storage_runtime_attach_detach.py` now covers both implementations via a subclass, so the existing HiRadixCache coverage is retained rather than switched over. 2 passed. ## Notes `HiRadixCache` has the same unhashed-node issue and the same non-idempotent detach when no backend was ever attached. Both are left alone here to keep this PR scoped to the unified tree. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32144619670](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144619670)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32144619414](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32144619414)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] EAGLE/NEXTN TP=2 hangs at warmup on Intel XPU after #34238 moved the verify-decision TP broadcast out of the sampling branch
signal.text: ## Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. - [x] Please use English. ## Describe the bug On the **Intel XPU backend**, EAGLE/NEXTN speculative decoding with `--tp 2` intermittently hangs on the first decode step after warmup. The scheduler watchdog fires at 300 s and the server never becomes ready, so the test fails at setup after the 600 s launch timeout. We started seeing this after #34238 ("[AMD] Broadcast the EAGLE greedy verify decision across TP ranks on ROCm", merged 2026-08-15). It is intermittent: on the same commit, one run hung at warmup and a later run of the same command passed (GSM8K 0.920, accept len 3.18). ### Why XPU is newly exposed by #34238 #34238 did not add a new code path — it de-indented the existing TP broadcast in `eagle_sample()` out of the `else:` (sampling / rejection-sampling) branch so it now runs after **both** verify branches: ```python # python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_utils.py if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: ... # greedy verify -- XPU ALWAYS lands here else: ... # tree_speculative_sampling_target_only / chain_speculative_sampling_triton # after #34238 this runs for BOTH branches (it used to live inside `else:`) tp_group = get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() if tp_group.world_size > 1: tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` `_is_xpu` is a term in that branch condition, so **XPU can never reach the `else` branch**. These three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238 and now execute on every verify step. NVIDIA is effectively unchanged: the non-greedy path already had them, and the newly-covered all-greedy case is a semantic no-op because NCCL's all-reduce yields bitwise-identical logits on every rank. The newly-live set is ROCm (the intended fix), XPU, NPU, CPU, and CUDA-all-greedy — all at TP > 1. ### Stacks at the hang (`--tp 2`, watchdog dump) **TP1 — active, stuck on a Level Zero device event inside the draft extend that follows verify:** ``` Thread 1012034 (active): "MainThread" sched_yield (libc.so.6) 0x7214ac5fa8ed (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) 0x7214ac5fb768 (libze_intel_gpu.so.1.14.36300) ur::level_zero::urEventWait (libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0.12.0) compute_spec_mrope_positions (forward_batch_info.py:1131) init_new (forward_batch_info.py:949) prepare_for_draft_extend (eagle_worker_common.py:178) _draft_extend_for_decode (eagle_worker_v2.py:887) forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1198) run_batch (scheduler.py:3696) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1803) ``` **TP0 — idle, already past `run_batch`, waiting on the CPU-group request broadcast of the next iteration:** ``` Thread 1012033 (idle): "MainThread" pthread_cond_wait (libc.so.6) c10d::Work::wait (libtorch_cpu.so) broadcast (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3080) broadcast_pyobj (utils/common.py:2406) _broadcast_reqs_across_ranks (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:210) recv_requests (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:93) event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:1772) ``` Timeline from the log: weights loaded, `max_total_num_tokens=76412`, one warmup `Prefill batch` at 17:33:49, then no further progress; `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` on both ranks at 17:41:12-13. So the stall is on the **first decode/draft-extend step after the first verify** — i.e. immediately after the first `eagle_sample()` call. ### Hypothesis (not yet proven — maintainer input welcome) TP0 has drained and is waiting on the **CPU/gloo** group for requests, while TP1's **XPU device queue** never completes an event. That is the signature of an unmatched or stalled collective on the xccl *device* group leaving TP1's queue blocked, with the visible `urEventWait` being downstream work that can never retire. Relevant: `GroupCoordinator.broadcast()` issues a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` on `self.device_group`. That is exactly the call shape XPU deliberately avoids for all-reduce — `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` routes XPU through the `inplace_all_reduce` custom op, with this comment in `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`: > Route through inplace_all_reduce custom op so Dynamo treats this as an opaque call and does not > decompose it into `_c10d_functional` primitives (which invoke `sycl_event.wait()` and break XPU > graph capture). `broadcast()` has no such wrapper, so #34238 introduces three raw eager device-group collectives per verify step on a backend that has an explicit carve-out against them. ### What we have and have not verified - Verified: the hang and the two stacks above, on a commit that contains #34238. - Verified by code reading: the three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238. - **Not** verified: a hang-rate comparison against the parent of #34238. The failure is intermittent (1 hang, 1 pass observed on the same code), so we are still collecting runs and will post the numbers here. Attribution to #34238 is currently based on when we started seeing it plus the code reading above. ### Side issues found while filing this (happy to send PRs) 1. **`python3 -m sglang.check_env` crashes on Intel XPU**, which blocks the required Environment field of this template. `python/sglang/check_env.py` dispatches on `is_cuda_v2/is_hip/is_npu/is_musa/is_mps` with no XPU branch and no `else`, so `env` is never bound: ``` File ".../python/sglang/check_env.py", line 594, in <module> env.check_env() NameError: name 'env' is not defined ``` The Environment section below was therefore collected manually. 2. **`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` is silently ignored on XPU.** The `_is_xpu` term forces greedy verify, so the rejection-sampling kernel is never reached even when the flag is set — the test below is named for a path it does not exercise on XPU. ### Candidate fix Smallest XPU-scoped change; restores exactly the pre-#34238 XPU behavior and leaves the ROCm fix intact: ```diff - tp_group = ( - get_parallel().attn_tp_group if is_dp_attention_enabled() else get_tp_group() - ) - if tp_group.world_size > 1: - tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) - tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) + # XPU opts out: a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` decomposes to `_c10d_functional`, + # whose `sycl_event.wait()` breaks XPU graph capture (why all_reduce takes the + # `inplace_all_reduce` detour). The greedy path never ran this sync on XPU before, + # so skipping it keeps the prior behavior. + if not _is_xpu: + tp_group = ( + get_parallel().attn_tp_group + if is_dp_attention_enabled() + else get_tp_group() + ) + if tp_group.world_size > 1: + tp_group.broadcast(predict, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(accept_index, src=0) + tp_group.broadcast(num_correct_drafts, src=0) ``` If XPU does need the rank-0 sync for the same reason ROCm does, the alternative is to route the broadcast through a custom op the way XPU all-reduce already is, rather than skipping it. Happy to send whichever the maintainers prefer. ## Reproduction Model `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, 2x Intel Arc Pro B60, `--device xpu --tp 2`: ```bash pytest -sv test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_reject_sampling.py::TestQwen35EagleRS::test_a_gsm8k ``` Equivalent standalone server command (taken verbatim from the failing run): ```bash sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B --trust-remote-code --tp 2 \ --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-use-rejection-sampling \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --disable-radix-cache \ --device xpu --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 ``` Effective server args from the hanging run: `attention_backend='triton'`, `cuda_graph_config` decode=`disabled` prefill=`disabled` (no graph capture involved), `page_size=1`, `disable_radix_cache=True`, `speculative_use_rejection_sampling=True`, `enable_dp_attention=False`, `watchdog_timeout=300`, `disable_overlap_schedule=False`. The hang reproduces before the GSM8K workload starts, during server warmup, so no eval data is needed to trigger it. ## Environment Collected manually because `python3 -m sglang.check_env` raises `NameError` on XPU (see side issue 1 above). ``` sglang: 0.5.18.dev687 (source checkout containing #34238) python: 3.12.13 os: Linux-6.14.0-37-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.41 torch: 2.12.0+xpu xccl: available (torch.distributed.is_xccl_available() == True) ipex: not installed oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch: not installed xpu devices: 8x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, 24 GB each, driver 1.14.36300+8 (this repro uses 2 of them via --tp 2) ``` cc @JessicaJiang-123 @XinyuJiangCMU (authors of #34238), @Ying1123 @merrymercy @hnyls2002 @Qiaolin-Yu (CODEOWNERS for `python/sglang/srt/speculative`)

signal.title: [XPU] Skip the EAGLE verify-decision TP broadcast on XPU
signal.text: ## Motivation Fixes #35144. #34238 de-indented the `predict` / `accept_index` / `num_correct_drafts` broadcast in `eagle_sample()` out of the `else:` (sampling / rejection-sampling) branch so it covers the greedy verify path too. `_is_xpu` is a term in that branch condition: ```python if sampling_info.is_all_greedy or _is_cpu or _is_npu or _is_hip or _is_xpu: ... # greedy verify -- XPU ALWAYS lands here else: ... # tree_speculative_sampling_target_only / chain_speculative_sampling_triton ``` So XPU can never reach the `else` branch: these three broadcasts were unreachable on XPU before #34238 and now execute on every verify step. That regressed XPU. EAGLE/NEXTN at TP=2 intermittently hangs at warmup, on the first decode step after the first verify. The scheduler watchdog fires at 300 s and the server never becomes ready: ``` # TP1 -- active, stuck on a Level Zero device event in the draft extend that follows verify ur::level_zero::urEventWait (libur_adapter_level_zero_v2.so.0.12.0) compute_spec_mrope_positions (forward_batch_info.py:1131) prepare_for_draft_extend (eagle_worker_common.py:178) _draft_extend_for_decode (eagle_worker_v2.py:887) run_batch (scheduler.py:3696) # TP0 -- idle, already past run_batch, waiting on the CPU-group request broadcast c10d::Work::wait (libtorch_cpu.so) broadcast_pyobj (utils/common.py:2406) _broadcast_reqs_across_ranks (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:210) recv_requests (scheduler_components/request_receiver.py:93) ``` `GroupCoordinator.broadcast()` issues a raw `torch.distributed.broadcast` on the device group. That is the call shape XPU deliberately avoids for all-reduce — `GroupCoordinator.all_reduce()` routes XPU through the `inplace_all_reduce` custom op, per the comment in `parallel_state.py`: > Route through inplace_all_reduce custom op so Dynamo treats this as an opaque call and does not > decompose it into `_c10d_functional` primitives (which invoke `sycl_event.wait()` and break XPU > graph capture). `broadcast()` has no such wrapper, so #34238 added three raw eager device-group collectives per verify step on a backend with an explicit carve-out against them. Full stacks, environment and the reproduction are in #35144. ## Modifications Guard the sync with `if not _is_xpu:`, restoring XPU's pre-#34238 behavior. ROCm (the target of #34238), CUDA, NPU and CPU are unchanged — for them this is a pure re-indent. If maintainers would rather XPU keep the rank-0 sync, the alternative is to route this broadcast through a custom op the way XPU all-reduce already is. Happy to switch to that instead — this PR takes the minimal regression fix. ## Accuracy Tests No output change on CUDA/ROCm/NPU/CPU — the guard only excludes XPU, and the enclosing `tp_group.world_size > 1` check is untouched. On XPU, `pytest -sv test/registered/spec/eagle/test_eagle_reject_sampling.py::TestQwen35EagleRS::test_a_gsm8k` (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, `--device xpu --tp 2`, NEXTN, 2x Intel Arc Pro B60): GSM8K score 0.920, `avg_spec_accept_length=3.18`. Note the hang is intermittent, so a hang-rate table across repeated runs on this branch versus the parent of #34238 is still being collected; it will be posted on #35144. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable — this removes three small per-verify-step collectives on XPU and changes nothing on any other backend. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). No new unit test: there is no XPU multi-GPU spec-decode test in CI to extend. The only XPU-registered EAGLE test, `test/registered/spec/eagle/test_spec_eagle_parity.py::TestEagle3ParityXPU`, runs on `nightly-xpu-1-gpu`, where `world_size == 1` makes this code path a no-op. Adding `nightly-xpu-2-gpu` spec coverage would have caught this and is worth a follow-up — glad to take it if maintainers agree on the suite. cc @JessicaJiang-123 @XinyuJiangCMU (authors of #34238) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32035935575](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32035935575)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32035935436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32035935436)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Add _apply_vocab_mask_fallback to xgrammar backend.
signal.text: ## Motivation XGrammar guided decoding currently raises RuntimeError: Unsupported device when no fused token-bitmask kernel is registered for the target device. This prevents structured-output requests from running on backends that are not explicitly enumerated in the XGrammar backend adapter. ## Modifications - Add a device-agnostic fallback using xgrammar’s apply_token_bitmask_inplace. and use the fallback in both XGrammar vocabulary-mask application paths. - Emit one warning per device type when the slower fallback is selected. - Add CPU unit tests verifying that disallowed tokens are masked correctly. ## Accuracy Tests Added unit tests covering both vocabulary-mask entry points and verifying the resulting logits. This re-uses existing reference `apply_token_bitmask_inplace` and only affects a fallback path for unsupported devices. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not applicable to existing fused CUDA/NPU paths, which remain unchanged. Unsupported devices now use xgrammar’s device-agnostic implementation.
