signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Summary On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`. The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with: ```python pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64) ``` However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions. Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding. The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`. ## Affected checkpoints | Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes | | `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug | The affected 27B configs contain: ```json { "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"], "language_model_only": false, "text_config": { "attn_output_gate": true, "head_dim": 256, "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25, "rope_parameters": { "mrope_interleaved": true, "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10], "rope_theta": 10000000, "rope_type": "default" } } } ``` SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366 ## SGLang versions reviewed | Version | Commit | | --- | --- | | v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) | | v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) | | v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) | | latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) | The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`: ```text 56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b ``` ## Source-level reproduction ### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions `QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471 `ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253 For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug. ### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453 ### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled: ```python if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused( positions=positions, hidden_states=hidden_states, ) ``` https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163 There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`. ### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153 The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0. ## Minimal runtime assertion On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`: ```diff def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states): + assert positions.ndim == 1, ( + f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, " + f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}" + ) ``` Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 ``` Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel. The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`. ## Why existing validation missed it The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320 That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case. ## Expected behavior For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`. The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics. ## Actual behavior On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill. ## Suggested minimal correctness fix Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract: ```diff -if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate: +if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...) else: q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...) ``` Also fail fast in the fused wrapper: ```python if positions.ndim != 1: raise ValueError( f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, " f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}" ) ``` This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison. The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode. ## Tests requested Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache: | Case | Positions | Expected result | | --- | --- | --- | | Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance | | Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path | | Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically | An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring. ## Scope and current evidence The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path. I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions. ### Reproduction ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --port 8000 \ --tp-size 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 ``` ### Environment I use the 0.5.16+cu129 docker. ``` Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0] CUDA available: True GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0 CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86 CUDA Driver Version: 535.129.03 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129 sglang: 0.5.16 sglang-kernel: 0.4.5+cu129 flashinfer_python: 0.6.14 flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.14 flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.14+cu129 triton: 3.6.0 transformers: 5.12.1 torchao: 0.17.0+cu129 numpy: 2.4.4 aiohttp: 3.14.3 fastapi: 0.139.2 huggingface_hub: 1.24.0 interegular: 0.3.3 modelscope: 1.38.1 orjson: 3.11.9 outlines: 0.1.11 packaging: 26.2 psutil: 7.2.2 pydantic: 2.13.4 python-multipart: 0.0.32 pyzmq: 27.1.0 signal.title: [PD] Introduce runtime role switching between prefill and decode
signal.text: ## [PD] Introduce runtime prefill<->decode role switching (mori backend) ### Motivation SGLang's PD disaggregation currently **pins each instance's role (`prefill` / `decode`) at startup** with no way to change it at runtime — to re-balance the P:D ratio you must tear down and relaunch servers. This PR introduces **runtime P<->D role switching**: an operator/router can convert a prefill instance into a decode instance (or vice versa) live, without restarting the server or reloading weights. It lands as a first PoC on the **mori** transfer backend; the control plane is backend-agnostic. ### Design: in-place role flip Key enabler: **the token KV pool is role-independent** — prefill and decode allocate the same KV memory structure. Only the *role-specific* disaggregation structures differ (prefill: bootstrap queue + KV sender; decode: receiver/poll threads, bootstrap registration, role-specific queues/metadata buffers). A flip therefore does **not** reallocate the KV pool or touch model weights. It only tears down and rebuilds the small role-specific structures, then re-dispatches the scheduler event loop to the new role. Draining to idle before teardown is a correctness requirement (an in-flight decode request's KV is owned by an upstream prefill). ### API ``` POST /pd_role_switch {"new_role": "prefill" | "decode", "decode_cuda_graph_bs": [..]?} ``` Gated by `--enable-pd-role-switch` (default **off**, zero impact on existing PD). ### What's in this PR - **Control plane**: `--enable-pd-role-switch`; `PdRoleSwitchReqInput/Output`; `POST /pd_role_switch`; `handle_pd_role_switch` + teardown/rebuild in a dedicated `disaggregation/role_switch.py`; event-loop re-dispatch on flip. Hardened with an in-progress re-entrancy guard, a fail-fast "unhealthy" state on rebuild failure, and table-driven precondition checks. - **Decode CUDA graph on flip**: enable and capture the decode graph on the flip to decode; the captured batch sizes are queryable via `/get_server_info` and can be passed as `decode_cuda_graph_bs` for a size-matched capture; idempotent. - **Backend opt-in interface**: `BaseKVManager.supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`, so other transfer backends can support role switching (checked up-front in the reject path). - **mori backend**: teardown/rebuild hooks for the KV-transfer manager (worker threads are poll-based so they observe the stop flag; sockets, zmq context, RDMA registrations and the IOEngine are released). - **Radix / hicache compatibility**: release the prefix cache on flip; removes the previous `--disable-radix-cache` requirement (works with `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache`). - **Plumbing / invariants**: `disagg_service.py` (bootstrap started on role-switch instances), `tokenizer_control_mixin.py`, `model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` (role-agnostic pre-alloc), `invariant_checker.py` (leak check keyed on the pool, not the role). - **Unit tests** (CPU-only, mocked): `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`. ### Validation **Unit tests** — `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py`: **17 passed** (control-plane contract, all reject branches, same-role no-op, successful-flip orchestration, serialization, teardown thread-leak, radix-on prefix-cache release). **E2E accuracy (original)** — DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, 1P1D on 2×MI355X, mori KV transfer, TP8 (pure-TP MoE), concurrency 128, GSM8K (1319, lm_eval flexible/strict): | stage | flexible-extract | strict-match | |-------|------------------|--------------| | baseline (P=node A, D=node B) | 0.9469 | 0.9462 | | after flip (roles swapped via /pd_role_switch) | 0.9462 | 0.9454 | | after flip back (reverted) | 0.9416 | 0.9447 | **Accuracy + performance with radix cache ON (new)** — Qwen3-32B (dense, TP=8, pure-TP), mori, 1P1D on 2×MI300X; 8k1k = random 8192/1024, 320 prompts, concurrency 32, warmup 64: | state | gsm8k | out tok/s | total tok/s | TTFT med | TPOT med | |-------|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|----------| | ① baseline | 0.840 | 2680 | 24119 | 649 ms | 10.62 ms | | ② flip | 0.850 | 2655 | 23895 | 633 ms | 10.77 ms | | ③ flip-back | 0.840 | 2641 | 23772 | 679 ms | 10.69 ms | **Leak stress (new)** — 25 round-trip cycles = **100 role switches**, run once with the radix cache OFF and once ON, metrics recorded per cycle. `flip_fails=0`; weight / kvcache / graph / GPU-free / thread-count stay flat across cycles 2–25 in both configs ⇒ no resource leak. | metric (radix OFF) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |--------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.09 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=53567 D=53488 | constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2127 D=2047 | constant | | metric (radix ON) | baseline | cycles 1–25 | |-------------------|----------|-------------| | kvcache / graph (GB) | 115.05 / 1.07 | constant | | gpu_free (MB) | P=50908 D=50748 | bit-for-bit constant | | threads (lwp) | P=2519 D=2224 | ±16, non-monotonic | ### Limitations / follow-ups - Only the **mori** backend's teardown/rebuild hooks are implemented; other backends opt in via `supports_role_switch` + `teardown()`. - Validated with pure-TP MoE (`--tp-size 8`, no EP / DP-attention / MoE a2a). With `--moe-a2a-backend mori`, the a2a dispatch buffer is sized per-role at startup and is not yet rebuilt on flip — a follow-up. - Flip is driven externally (operator/router); an automatic load-based flip policy is out of scope here. ### How to use ```bash # launch both instances with the flag (add --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache to run with radix on) python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode prefill --enable-pd-role-switch python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... --disaggregation-mode decode --enable-pd-role-switch # (optional) query a decode server's captured decode-graph batch sizes curl http://<decode>:8000/get_server_info # -> internal_states[].decode_cuda_graph_bs # after draining, flip (optionally pass decode_cuda_graph_bs for a size-matched capture) curl http://<inst>:8000/pd_role_switch -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"new_role":"decode"}' ``` <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32152225473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32152225473)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32152224504](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32152224504)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bug] TypeError in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs during NEXTN TARGET_VERIFY — mamba_next_track_idx is None (hybrid-mamba + speculative decoding + lazy buffer mode)
signal.text: **Env:** SGLang 0.5.14 (pip wheel) · model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 · GPU: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24GB each) · NEXTN speculative decoding enabled **Crash:** \`TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer\` at \`schedule_batch.py:1594\` in \`set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()\` during TARGET_VERIFY. **Mechanism (from reading v0.5.14 source):** \`Req.mamba_next_track_idx\` initializes to \`None\` (schedule_batch.py:790) and is only assigned in the extend path — an assignment that lazy buffer mode skips (line ~2325, deferring to \`mamba_lazy_prealloc_at_boundary\` in \`prepare_for_decode\`). NEXTN's TARGET_VERIFY builds the track-index tensor (line 1589+) before any decode step has run for a fresh request, so the tensor build receives \`None\`. **Workaround (running stably on my machine):** for req in batch.reqs: if req.mamba_next_track_idx is None: req.mamba_next_track_idx = 0 placed immediately before the torch.tensor build. Zero is the semantically correct initial ping-pong slot per the field's own comment ("0 or 1"). A maintainer may prefer initializing at the source instead. **Context:** the same architectural class (hybrid-recurrent state index reaching a spec-decode kernel unset/unbounded) has three known instances in vLLM (vllm#43559, vllm#50021) — SGLang fails loudly with this TypeError where vLLM's analogues fault in-kernel. Downstream discussion: noonghunna/club-3090#803.

signal.title: [Perf] Avoid full-logits all-gather for TP greedy sampling
signal.text: ## Motivation Tensor-parallel generation currently materializes and all-gathers full-vocabulary logits on every rank before a strict greedy `argmax`. For greedy-only requests, each rank only needs to contribute its local maximum value and global token ID. This PR adds an experimental opt-in path that changes the logits communication from `O(batch * vocab)` to `O(batch * TP)` candidates. It is related to, but does not duplicate, #31079: that PR gathers full logits to rank 0, while this path reduces each vocab shard locally and never communicates full logits. ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_ENABLE_TP_SHARDED_GREEDY=1` (off by default). - Compute local FP32 LM-head logits and the local `(max value, global token ID)` on each TP rank. - Pack each candidate into two 32-bit lanes, all-gather the candidates, and select the global winner with the same lowest-token-ID tie behavior as full-vocabulary `torch.argmax`. - Pass the selected token IDs through `LogitsProcessorOutput` without constructing full-vocabulary logits. - Strictly fall back to the existing path for logprobs, top-logprobs, token-ID logprobs, grammars, custom logit processors, logit bias, penalties, sampling masks, speculative modes, prefill-only requests, added embeddings, unsupported LM-head layouts, and CUDA-graph logits buffers. - Add unit tests and a TP communication microbenchmark. ## Accuracy Tests ```text pytest -q test/registered/unit/sampling/test_tp_sharded_greedy.py 18 passed ``` The tests cover per-row winners, exact ties, NaNs, explicit opt-in, and all full-logits fallback gates. A fixed greedy E2E probe produced identical results with the feature disabled and enabled: ```text prompt: "Hello" output_ids: [13, 358] text: ". I" ``` The communication benchmark also checks candidate-path token IDs against full all-gather + argmax with `rtol=0, atol=0` before timing each shape. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Hardware/software: - 2x NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB (SM80), TP=2 - PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, NCCL 2.28.9 - BF16 model weights, FP32 logits - CUDA graphs disabled (the experimental path currently falls back when graph logits buffers are present) - `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` for both paths because P2P/IPC communicator initialization hangs on this PHB-connected hosted instance; both paths use the same NCCL transport Microbenchmark (`vocab_size=128256`, 100 iterations): | Batch | Full all-gather + argmax (us) | Candidate all-gather (us) | Speedup | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 213.91 | 403.08 | 0.531x | | 4 | 420.88 | 400.34 | 1.051x | | 16 | 1185.63 | 378.73 | 3.131x | | 64 | 5100.59 | 384.84 | 13.254x | E2E serving benchmark: - Model: `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` - 128 requests, random input length 256, output length 128 - concurrency 64, temperature 0, TP=2 - CUDA graphs/custom all-reduce/overlap scheduling disabled for both paths - cache flushed before every run - A/B/A ordering after kernel caches were warm | Metric | Baseline runs | Feature runs | Mean change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Output throughput (tok/s) | 1603.47, 1583.17 | 1698.81, 1717.17 | **+7.20%** | | Median E2E latency (ms) | 4892.71, 4913.26 | 4628.27, 4534.11 | **-6.56%** | | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 4962.94, 5030.94 | 4737.79, 4737.67 | **-5.19%** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 33.55, 33.93 | 31.71, 31.80 | **-5.88%** | The microbenchmark shows why the path remains experimental and opt-in: it targets medium/high-batch greedy decode, not batch 1. ## Checklist - [x] Formatted with the repository's pinned Ruff, isort, and Black versions. - [x] Added unit tests for correctness and fallback behavior. - [x] Documented the experimental environment variable inline; no public default behavior changes. - [x] Included accuracy, microbenchmark, and E2E benchmark results. - [x] Followed the existing SGLang code style. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32107422729](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32107422729)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32107422138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32107422138)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] MXFP4 KV Cache Decode for DSV4 on Hopper
signal.text: ## Summary MXFP4 KV cache for DeepSeek V4 on Hopper (SM90/H20), end to end: codec + memory pool + fused decode attention kernel + backend integration. The decode kernel is a JIT-compiled port of the FlashMLA three-stage split-KV design (scheduler metadata kernel + persistent WGMMA main kernel + combine kernel), covering all 44 layers (SWA + C4/C128 + attn_sink) in one call. The PR is self-contained: the kernel and its vendored dependencies live under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` and compile at first use via `load_jit` — no sgl-kernel wheel changes required. ## MXFP4 Layout (368 B/token) ``` [224 B packed E2M1 | 14 B E8M0 + 2 B pad | 128 B BF16 RoPE] ``` - E2M1 (4-bit FP: 1S+2E+1M) nope data, block-size 32 (14 groups) - E8M0 8-bit exponent-only scale per group (dequantized in-register via `bits << 23`) - BF16 RoPE (unquantized) - Row-major contiguous, no page tail padding; no global scale needed (unlike NVFP4) - 16-byte-aligned row (368 B = 16×23) enables 128-bit loads; the NVFP4 reference's 380 B is only 4-byte aligned Memory capacity gain vs FP8: ~+37% full-token capacity (bytes/token 7705 → 5609; the NVFP4 reference gains +31.75%). ## Decode Kernel (`kernels/jit/csrc/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90/`) FlashMLA-style fused split-KV decode for MXFP4: 1. **Scheduler metadata kernel** — 1 CTA × 1 thread computes per-SM split assignments with device-side length clamping (CUDA-graph safe: runs inside the captured graph, re-executes with replayed top-k lengths) 2. **Persistent main kernel** — 384 threads (3 warp groups: producer dequant→SMEM, QK+PV local, PV remote), WGMMA 64×64×16 / 64×256×16; E8M0 block-32 dequant via bit-shift, E2M1 via LUT+PRMT (4 instructions per 16 elements) 3. **Combine kernel** — merges split-K partials with PDL (programmatic dependent launch) Entry point: `entry.cuh` (TVM-FFI single translation unit, explicit instantiations for h_q 64/128). Python wrapper: `kernels/ops/attention/mxfp4_dsv4_decode_sm90.py` (FlashMLASchedMeta, per-geometry scratch reuse, C++-side stream resolution via `TVMFFIEnvGetStream`). ### Vendored dependencies (provenance) | Component | Source | |---|---| | `params.h`, `defines.h`, `utils.h`, `flashmla_utils.h`, `kerutils/`, `combine` | FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 | | `config.h`, `dequant.h`, `layout.h`, `components/helpers.h`, splitkv skeleton | SGLang reference PR #31269 (NVFP4) | | `splitkv_mla.cuh` (MXFP4 variant), `entry.cuh` | This PR | CUTLASS/CUTE headers come from the JIT build's `extra_dependencies=["cutlass"]` (pinned cutlass @ 147f5673, matching the reference PR). `kerutils` includes were converted to relative paths during vendoring. ## Changes - **Codec** (`srt/layers/attention/dsv4/mxfp4_k_cache.py`): quantize/dequant for the 368 B row (Triton), paged variants - **Compressor** (`compressor_v2.py`): `_forward_mxfp4` covering all 44 layers (C0/C4/C128), decode-plan boundary semantics - **Memory pool**: parameterized enablement via `--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4` (env alias with deprecation warning); pool sizing/accounting unified - **Startup guards**: HiSparse + MXFP4 combination rejected at init (incompatible sparse layout); DeepseekV4 + fp4_e2m1 on non-SM90 fails fast with a clear error - **Backend** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`): `_forward_mxfp4_decode_flashmla` — one fused call per layer; scheduler metadata shared per geometry across layers, re-created during CUDA-graph capture (top-k lengths are replayed device inputs) - **Tests**: `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` (17 kernel cases: C0/C4/C128 × flash/profiling geometries, graph replay + length clamping, invalid contracts, scheduler-refresh regressions) + `test_mxfp4_k_cache.py` (5 codec cases) + `test_dsv4_hisparse_pool.py` (3 pool-guard cases) + `test_dsv4_compress_write_pad.py` (3 restored cases); benchmark in `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_mxfp4_dsv4_decode.py` - **E2E**: `test/registered/kernels/e2e/test_mxfp4_dsv4_e2e.py` — 8-GPU H200 server + gsm8k, exercising pool configurator → compressor → CUDA-graph capture (CI stage extra-b) - Removed the first-generation standalone JIT kernel (`mxfp4_decode.cuh` + `_forward_mxfp4_decode`) superseded by the FlashMLA port ## Validation - Kernel SASS was byte-identical to the AOT (cmake) build of the same sources at port time; the subsequent refactors (V32 path removal, aligned 128-bit row loads) are instruction-level changes covered by the same unit suite - Unit: 28/28 kernel + codec + pool-guard tests pass; 8-GPU e2e integration test passes locally - End-to-end on 8×H20 (TP8, `DeepSeek-V4-Flash`), FP8 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`) vs MXFP4 (`--kv-cache-dtype fp4_e2m1 --fp4-kv-cache-recipe mxfp4`), identical server flags otherwise: | Metric | FP8 baseline | MXFP4 (this PR) | Δ | |---|---|---|---| | Decode throughput (server-side, 4k×256, conc 32) | 1013 tok/s | 980 tok/s | −3.3% | | GSM8K (1319, greedy, max_tokens 1024; truncated samples excluded) | 96.89% | 96.89% | 0.0pt | | AIME25 (480 = 30×16, greedy, max_tokens 32768; 73 truncated samples excluded from both) | 99.57% pass@1 | 99.78% pass@1 | +0.2pt | ## Known gaps / follow-ups - Small-batch (b≤8) kernel-level latency vs FP8: +8–12% (kernel-inherent scheduling granularity; end-to-end TPOT already within 5%) - Prefill-path throughput: −6.8% vs FP8 (out of scope for this PR; triton-based MXFP4 prefill) - Deep-context + high-concurrency decode (64 concurrent, 8k ctx, no rolling prefill): decode TPOT +17% vs FP8 (33.1 vs 28.3 ms); end-to-end 8k→8k throughput on par (1677 vs 1652 tok/s). One full AIME25 eval run showed −44% throughput vs FP8, but four controlled reruns (5-question replica, rolling short-prompt, 8k×8k fixed) could not reproduce it and measured MXFP4 at parity or faster — attributed to environment, not the kernel. - sm_90a-only (Hopper); no SM100 support (non-SM90 + fp4_e2m1 is rejected at startup) - HiSparse (sparse KV cache) not supported with MXFP4 — rejected at startup ## References - PR #31269 — NVFP4 KV cache for DSV4 in sgl-kernel (reference implementation for the FlashMLA three-stage decode) - FlashMLA upstream @ 05e26647 — scheduler/combine kernels and kerutils - This PR takes the jit_kernel approach (JIT CUDA via TVM-FFI) instead of AOT CUTLASS in sgl-kernel, keeping the PR self-contained --- **Status**: Ready for review — kernel + integration complete, end-to-end validated on 8×H20. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32149788831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149788831)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32149788487](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32149788487)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Prevent hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk decode over-admission
signal.text: ## Motivation Hybrid-SWA mixed-chunk scheduling admits new prefill tokens while an existing decode batch is executed in the same forward pass. The mixed-chunk path does not perform the regular decode memory check before admission. However, the existing decode batch still requires SWA KV pages immediately after admission. Since `PrefillAdder` did not reserve this SWA demand, prefill admission could consume pages required by decode. This can cause decode allocation failure under SWA memory pressure. ## Root Cause For a running batch, `new_tokens_required_next_decode()` returns the page-aligned token demand for the next decode step. The mixed-chunk admission path previously ignored this demand and initialized the SWA reservation offset to zero. The composite SWA allocator had a second issue: full-attention pages were allocated before SWA pages. If the SWA allocation failed, the full allocator had already consumed pages, leaving a partial allocation state. ## Fix Reserve the current decode batch's SWA demand during mixed-chunk admission: ```python mixed_decode_swa_tokens = ( running_batch.new_tokens_required_next_decode() if self.is_mixed_chunk and self.tree_cache.supports_swa() else 0 ) ``` Pass this value to `PrefillAdder` as the initial SWA reservation. Make hybrid SWA decode allocation preflight both underlying allocators before performing either allocation: ```python num_new_pages = get_num_new_pages( seq_lens=seq_lens_cpu, page_size=self.page_size, decode=True, ) if not self.new_pages_available(num_new_pages, num_new_pages): return None ``` This prevents full-KV pages from being consumed when the corresponding SWA allocation cannot succeed. ## Validation - Existing scheduler and allocator tests pass: `45 passed, 27 subtests passed`. - On A100, a decode batch requiring 8 new pages with only 4 SWA pages available: - before the fix, full-KV allocation consumed all 8 pages before SWA failed; - after the fix, allocation returned `None` without changing either pool. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32148300784](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148300784)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32148300620](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148300620)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Check paged KV capacity before kernel launch
signal.text: ## Summary - Check paged KV capacity before launching the extend/decode Triton allocator kernels. - Preserve the existing release-page merge behavior before the capacity check. - Add regression tests covering OOM, successful allocation, and release-page merging. ## Motivation The old implementation launched the allocation kernel and only then checked whether enough free pages were available. On an A100 with two free pages, a prefill or decode request requiring three pages returned `None` but still launched the kernel once. The kernel could read beyond the logical free-page list. This is reachable in normal serving when the KV cache is full and no more evictable pages are available. See issue #34399 for the reproducible online path and evidence. ## Validation ### Unit and allocator tests ```text 138 passed, 2 warnings, 33 subtests passed in 29.19s ``` The test command covered the new paged allocator regression tests, multi-ended allocator, paged free, SWA, HiSparse, DCP layout, KV page invariants, and decode bookkeeping tests. ### A100 validation With `NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB`, PyTorch `2.9.1+cu128`, and `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`: ```text extend_oom= True kernel_launches= 0 free_unchanged= True decode_oom= True kernel_launches= 0 free_unchanged= True ``` The same unmodified-mainline inputs launched one kernel in each path. ### OOM-path microbenchmark After warming the successful kernel path, 100 synchronous prefill OOM calls measured: ```text main: 126.14 us/call patch: 59.37 us/call ``` This is a single local failure-path measurement, not an end-to-end throughput benchmark. Successful allocation behavior is unchanged. ## Scope This patch is intentionally limited to the paged allocator capacity-check ordering. It does not change the Triton kernel interface, page numbering, or normal successful allocation behavior. Fixes #34399 <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32148286995](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148286995)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32148286714](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32148286714)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [DSV4] Support raw-index output in TopK v2
signal.text: ## Summary Allow TopK v2 to populate a raw-index output buffer. DSV4 sparse prefill internally allocates `c4_sparse_raw_indices` even when `--enable-return-indexer-topk` is disabled. The previous `raw_indices is None` gate therefore forced the InfX sparse-prefill path to fall back to TopK v1. When `--enable-return-indexer-topk` is enabled, the capture-only temporary buffer could additionally take precedence over the functional sparse-prefill buffer. This change makes the sparse-prefill buffer canonical, passes it through TopK v2, and lets the capturer copy the same result afterward. ## Changes - Pass the raw-output buffer to `topk_transform_512_v2`. - Prioritize `core_metadata.c4_sparse_raw_indices`; the capturer reads the same result afterward. - Add a regression test covering TopK v2 with sparse prefill and capture enabled. No CUDA kernel, ABI, metadata format, default, or HiSparse behavior changes. Related: #32771 contains the same buffer-ordering change; #33288 owns chunked-path metadata refresh. ## Testing - DSV4 indexer unit tests: **8 passed, 12 subtests passed** - TopK v2 GPU subset on GB300: **36 passed, 208 deselected** - `pre-commit run --all-files` A prior GB300 microbenchmark (8,192 queries, max C4 length 2,048, `topk=1024`, metadata planning excluded) measured **0.1023 ms** for v1 and **0.0646 ms** for v2 (**36.9% lower kernel latency**). Should have bigger influence on long prefix as the indexer will take more time. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32130035343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130035343)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32130034969](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130034969)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [bugfix] [NPU] fix transpose batch matmul K*B exceed 65536.
signal.text: ## Motivation `torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul` provides the numerically validated path for Kimi-K3, but it does not support shapes where the relevant dimension limit is reached. In particular, `B * K` must be smaller than `65536`. Large-prefill workloads can exceed this limit and fail at runtime. ## Changes - Use `torch_npu.npu_transpose_batchmatmul` when all shape constraints are satisfied, including `B * K < 65536`. - Fall back to the previous `torch.ops.npu.batch_matmul_transpose` implementation for unsupported large shapes. - Preserve the validated `torch_npu` path for normal Kimi-K3 workloads. - Replace the following Kimi-K3 environment variables with `ServerArgs` options: - `SGLANG_K3_SHARED_EXPERTS_ATTN_TP` → `--k3-shared-experts-attn-tp` - `SGLANG_K3_DENSE_MLP_ATTN_TP` → `--k3-dense-mlp-attn-tp` ## Accuracy gsm8k for k3 --98%(200). ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [PP&Sepc] enable dspark under pipeline parallelism (deepseek-v4 & kimi-k3)
signal.text: ## Motivation roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11857, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/30344, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32607 Our previous PR (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31139) enabled PP + EAGLE support. Testing showed DSpark speculation performs far better than EAGLE, so this PR builds on it to add DSpark + PP compatibility. This PR depends on the previous one and should be merged afterwards. DSpark's verify path is structurally different from EAGLE's (per-layer aux hidden capture, linear block verify, confidence-driven budget), so it could not reuse the EAGLE PP machinery verbatim. This PR lifts that ban and makes DSpark run under PP, targeting DeepSeek-V4-Flash + the bundled DSpark draft checkpoint. ## Modifications The core idea mirrors the EAGLE PP design — the draft model lives only on the last PP rank, every rank runs its own target verify forward, and the draft proposal is relayed across stages so each rank rebuilds an identical verify context. The DSpark-specific work is making the per-layer aux-hidden capture and the linear block verify cross the PP boundary correctly. 1. **Per-rank draft proposal carrier (`DSparkPPVerifyInputRaw`).** A new spec input type carries the last rank's draft / confidence / accounting fields (bonus tokens, draft tokens, new seq lens, confidence, accept/cap-trim/verify lens) across the PP ring. Every rank rebuilds an identical verify layout from the same source each iteration, so all PP ranks produce byte-identical verify windows. It mixes in the shared `DFlashDecodePrepareMixin` so the non-last rank's verify forward (which reads `verify_cache_loc` from `req_to_token`) pre-allocates KV headroom exactly like the last rank. Linear verify reuses the formal `req_to_token` slots, so `accept_index` is always `None` and the token-move step in `batch_result_processor` is skipped automatically. 2. **Per-layer aux hidden capture across PP stages (`deepseek_v4.py`).** DSpark's draft needs per-layer aux hidden states (`dspark_aux_hidden_states`), but each PP rank only executes layers in its own `[start_layer, end_layer)` range. The aux list is now stacked as `[L, num_tokens, hidden]`, relayed downstream under the `"dspark_aux"` key in `PPProxyTensors`, and rebuilt in global layer order on the last rank (upstream layers first, then local captures). `set_dspark_layers_to_capture` no longer early-returns on non-last ranks, so every rank registers its own capture range. 3. **PP-aware verify forward.** `pp_proxy_tensors` is threaded through `TargetVerifyExecutor.run` / `run_non_compact` so the target verify forward relay hidden states along the PP ring on every rank. `TargetVerifyResult` carries `pp_hidden_states_proxy_tensors` back to the scheduler. Logits adjustments (penalizer / vocab mask / logit bias) are now gated on `result.logits_output is not None`, since non-last ranks never sample and their logits output is `None`. 4. **Embed / weight loading split (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`).** The DSpark draft used to borrow `embed_tokens` from the target. Under PP the last rank builds its own `VocabParallelEmbedding` and only `lm_head` is shared from the target; `attach_shared_modules` now takes `embed_tokens: Optional` so the PP path passes `None` and the draft keeps its locally-built embedding. Weight-name remapping keeps `embed_tokens.weight` on the last PP rank. 5. **PP proxy buffer sizing (`base_runner.py`).** The static `pp_proxy_tensors` buffers are allocated by max token count, not batch size, so the dummy / capture buffer fits the verify-token-expanded shape `[num_tokens, *hidden]` produced under speculative decoding. 6. **Planner / draft fixes for the relayed layout.** `alloc_verify_window` and `DraftBlockProposer` derive `prefix_lens` from the verify window's anchor position instead of `batch.seq_lens`, because the last rank's re-propose pass builds the next window from post-iter seq lens while `batch.seq_lens` is still the pre-iter value. The planner forces `RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=STATIC` and non-compact (eager) verify under PP, since the confidence-driven ragged scheduler and the cuda-graph compact path only run on the last rank and cannot keep cross-rank layout identity. Supporting changes: `draft_worker_common.build_draft_tp_worker` accepts a `pp_global_random_seed` so the draft sampler on the last rank is seeded consistently with the target; `speculative_hook` replaces the blanket `pp_size != 1` ban with a narrower "PP + DP-attention unsupported" check (DP-attention partitions the batch, which conflicts with the PP requirement that every rank see an identical batch). ### Limitations asserted now - **PP + DP-attention** is rejected. Only `--dp-size 1` is permitted under PP. - **PP forces static verify and eager (non-cuda-graph) verify** ## Accuracy Tests Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 GSM8K accuracy (200 examples, 5-shot, temperature=0): | Configuration | GSM8K Accuracy (%) | |---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 98.00 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 98.50 | ## Speed Tests Setup: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, single 8*H20 node; three PP2+TP4 configs: - **PP2-TP4** — PP2+TP4, no spec (baseline) - **PP2-TP4-MTP314** — PP2+TP4 + EAGLE (`speculative-num-steps=3`, `speculative-eagle-topk=1`, `speculative-num-draft-tokens=4`) - **PP2-TP4-DSpark** — PP2+TP4 + DSpark (this PR) bench_serving: `--dataset-name random` with local ShareGPT path (`--dataset-path /datasets/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json`), `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompts 5`, `--max-concurrency 1`, `--random-output-len 1024`, `--seed 42`; 3 rounds per point, reporting the min. **TPOT (ms)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 (no spec) | 11.11 | 11.14 | 11.13 | | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 5.39 | 5.43 | 5.65 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 2.30 | 2.34 | 2.38 | **Average accepted length (tokens / iter)** | Configuration | 16k | 32k | 64k | |---|---|---|---| | PP2-TP4 + MTP314 | 2.75 | 2.90 | 2.83 | | PP2-TP4 + DSpark (this PR) | 4.91 | 4.85 | 4.87 | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to the [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to the [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32118971072](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32118971072)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32118970721](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32118970721)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feature] Workload-Signature-Based Parallelism Advisor for Diffusion Serving
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Extend SGLang Diffusion's current rule-based `auto_tune` and parallelism documentation with an evidence-producing advisor that selects a legal execution topology from a workload signature and a calibrated benchmark record. The current documentation correctly explains that CFG, TP, and SP split different axes and that more parallelism is not always faster. `auto_tune.py` already makes high-confidence memory/residency choices and can enable CFG/FSDP under guarded conditions. The missing layer is a reproducible way to answer: > For this model revision, device topology, latent shape, denoising schedule, CFG mode, and effective candidate batch, which legal plan has the best end-to-end objective without failing quality or memory gates? This matters especially for short-sequence world/action models. A wider TP degree may amortize well for a multi-candidate batch but regress a latency-first single request because fixed collective and host-dispatch costs dominate. #### Goals - Enumerate legal CFG/TP/SP/FSDP/replica plans from model and hardware constraints. - Benchmark plans end to end rather than rank them from FLOPs alone. - Key recommendations by workload signature, not just model name. - Preserve explicit user configuration as highest priority. - Add a true world-size-one serving fast path where distributed work is semantically a no-op. - Produce a machine-readable calibration report and explain every selection/fallback. #### Non-goals - Moving a live request between TP topologies mid-denoising in phase 1. - Automatically renting/allocating GPUs. - Declaring one plan globally optimal for every batch size or objective. - Replacing existing memory-safety checks. #### Data model ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class DiffusionWorkloadSignature: model_revision: str task_type: str latent_tokens: int num_inference_steps: int | tuple[int, ...] logical_batch: int candidate_count: int cfg_branches: int dtype: str cache_mode: str compile_mode: str device_topology: str @dataclass(frozen=True) class ParallelExecutionPlan: num_gpus: int cfg_parallel_size: int tensor_parallel_size: int sequence_parallel_size: int fsdp: bool data_parallel_replicas: int @dataclass(frozen=True) class CalibrationResult: signature: DiffusionWorkloadSignature plan: ParallelExecutionPlan feasible: bool latency_ms: Mapping[str, float] peak_memory_bytes: int quality_gate: str communication_summary: Mapping[str, float] ``` #### Advisor flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Sig["Workload signature
shape, steps, batch, CFG, topology"] Caps["Model + hardware capabilities"] Enumerate["Enumerate legal plans"] Filter["Static feasibility
divisibility, memory, backend support"] Calibrate["Controlled end-to-end calibration"] Gate["Quality + stability gate"] Rank["Rank by selected objective
latency, throughput, or memory"] Record["Versioned calibration record"] Resolve["Startup/request-class resolver"] Run["Selected serving pool"] Sig --> Enumerate Caps --> Enumerate --> Filter --> Calibrate --> Gate --> Rank --> Record --> Resolve --> Run ``` #### Plan enumeration and static filters Reuse existing legality rules: - total devices equal the product/composition required by CFG/TP/SP/FSDP; - attention heads and sequence dimensions satisfy divisibility constraints; - the model/backend explicitly supports each parallel axis; - estimated resident memory and temporary peak fit the least-free selected GPU; - cache/compile combinations are compatible with the plan; and - CFG parallel is proposed only for models with the required branches. Static estimates only eliminate impossible plans. They should not select the winner. #### Calibration protocol For each remaining plan: 1. launch in an isolated calibration mode; 2. run a complete warmup, separating compile/cold-start time; 3. run repeated end-to-end requests at the exact signature; 4. record p50/p95 latency, throughput, peak memory, stage times, and collective counts/bytes; 5. apply the model's accuracy/trajectory gate; and 6. store environment, code revision, model revision, driver/backend versions, and device topology. The advisor ranks only passing plans. A microbenchmark win is supporting evidence, not a substitute for end-to-end measurement. #### Runtime resolution Phase 1 should resolve at server startup or route between separately launched pools. It should not reconfigure process groups for each request. Precedence: 1. explicit user-provided parallel flags; 2. exact validated calibration match; 3. compatible conservative recipe from pipeline config; 4. existing rule-based `auto_tune` behavior; or 5. clear failure if the model cannot fit safely. The log/metrics record which tier selected the plan and why other candidates were rejected. #### World-size-one fast path The advisor should also make `num_gpus=1` an explicit serving plan, not “distributed mode with degree one everywhere.” Components should expose whether they require a process group for protocol reasons versus useful sharding. When every effective group has size one: - do not wrap the model in FSDP/sharding machinery; - do not issue rank broadcasts with no receiver; - do not construct device communicators used only by multi-rank stages; - return inputs directly from no-op collectives; and - retain only process-group state genuinely required by the server protocol. This is an execution-plan property, not a check of `dist.is_initialized()` alone. #### Suggested integration - Keep current `auto_tune.py` as the resolver/guardrail layer. - Add a separate calibration command under diffusion benchmark/profile tooling. - Store results as JSON with a schema/version and stable signature hash. - Add pipeline-config capability methods for legal degrees and topology caveats. - Add optional startup flag such as `--diffusion-parallel-plan auto:`; exact naming is open for discussion. - Expose `selected_plan`, source, rejected-plan reasons, and calibration digest in startup metrics/logs. #### Correctness tests - explicit flags always override the advisor; - illegal head/sequence/device products are rejected before launch; - exact signature match selects the recorded plan; - different candidate batch/step count does not reuse an incompatible record; - stale model/code/device revisions fail closed to a conservative path; - quality-gate failure removes a plan regardless of latency; - world-size-one plan creates no sharding wrapper or redundant broadcast; - multi-rank plans initialize every required group consistently. #### Benchmark matrix At minimum, calibrate: - logical/candidate batch `1` and one larger production-relevant batch; - CFG serial and CFG parallel where supported; - TP degrees `1/2/4` subject to legality; - one applicable SP degree for long-latent video; - cache/compile modes claimed by the final record; and - single-GPU resident execution when the model fits. Report communication time together with collective count and payload size. “Time inside all-reduce” alone does not distinguish bandwidth transfer from rank-arrival skew. #### Alternatives considered - **Static model recipes only.** Useful defaults, but cannot represent batch/shape/topology crossovers. - **Choose the widest TP that fits.** Can regress short-sequence/small-batch latency. - **Online exploration on live requests.** Risks cold compilation, OOM, and quality variation in production. - **Reconfigure topology per request.** Process-group/model-shard transitions are too expensive for phase 1; separate serving pools are safer. #### Rollout 1. Define report/signature schema and dry-run plan enumeration. 2. Add world-size-one fast-path assertions. 3. Calibrate one model across two batch regimes and publish the artifact. 4. Add startup resolver behind an explicit flag. 5. Extend model coverage only when each recommendation has end-to-end evidence. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion parallelism guide: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/parallelism.mdx - Current diffusion auto-tuning policy: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/auto_tune.py - Diffusion distributed state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/parallel_state.py - Cosmos3 pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py

signal.title: [Feature] Trajectory-Gated Regional Compilation for Stateful Diffusion Pipelines
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Connect SGLang Diffusion's regional `torch.compile` support to a reproducible, full-trajectory promotion gate for stateful iterative models. The repository already contains two strong but separate capabilities: - `DenoisingStage` / `CompiledModuleRegistry` can compile full transformers or repeated submodules; and - `compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py` can compare intermediate denoising latents and final frames between a reference and a candidate run. For a stateful video/action or world model, a single isolated forward is not enough to decide that a compiled path is safe. History length changes, cache decisions may branch, CFG changes the observation point, and a numerically small difference can accumulate across a rollout. This feature would turn “compile succeeded” into “this exact compile plan passed the declared end-to-end trajectory contract for this workload signature.” #### Goals - Represent compiled regions and their supported shape/state regime explicitly. - Warm and validate compilation through a complete request/rollout trajectory. - Separate strict tensor parity from model-level output quality thresholds. - Produce a machine-readable promotion manifest. - Fall back to eager execution when a request falls outside the validated regime. - Keep compile disabled or opt-in exactly as current model policy requires; this RFC does not enable it globally. #### Proposed data model ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CompileWorkloadSignature: model_revision: str dtype: str backend: str parallel_signature: str latent_shape_regime: tuple[int, ...] num_inference_steps: int | tuple[int, ...] cfg_mode: str cache_mode: str state_schema_version: str @dataclass(frozen=True) class TrajectoryGate: checkpoints: tuple[str, ...] tensor_thresholds: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, float]] output_metrics: Mapping[str, float] require_decision_trace_match: bool @dataclass(frozen=True) class CompiledPlanManifest: signature: CompileWorkloadSignature regions: tuple[str, ...] compile_options: Mapping[str, object] gate_digest: str status: str # validated / rejected ``` The manifest is an offline/CI artifact. Runtime does not rerun the full reference rollout for every request; it checks whether the incoming workload is covered by a validated signature and falls back otherwise. #### Promotion flow ```mermaid flowchart TD Ref["Eager reference
fixed requests and seeds"] Cand["Regional compile candidate
same requests and seeds"] Warm["Complete warmup rollout
compile + cache/state transitions"] Capture["Capture selected internal states
and public outputs"] Compare["Trajectory gate
shape, decisions, tensor metrics,
task/output metrics"] Pass{"All declared gates pass?"} Manifest["Write validated manifest
signature + regions + thresholds"] Reject["Reject plan
retain eager path + artifacts"] Runtime["Runtime signature resolver"] Compiled["Use compiled plan"] Eager["Safe eager fallback"] Ref --> Capture Cand --> Warm --> Capture Capture --> Compare --> Pass Pass -->|yes| Manifest --> Runtime Pass -->|no| Reject Runtime -->|covered| Compiled Runtime -->|uncovered| Eager ``` #### Gate semantics The framework should support three kinds of checks without pretending they are interchangeable: 1. **Structural invariants:** same step count, tensor shapes, cache/reuse decision trace, terminal side effects, and output schema. 2. **Numerical trajectory checks:** per-step max absolute error, MAE, relative error, and cosine similarity at named tensors. 3. **Public/task-level checks:** action tolerance, image/video similarity, or another model adapter metric. Some changes should be bitwise exact; others may be acceptable only under calibrated tolerances. Thresholds belong to the model/workload gate, not a global constant. Passing a final-frame metric must not hide a large early trajectory divergence unless the model's declared policy explicitly allows it. #### Full-rollout requirements A candidate must run: - one complete warmup rollout so compilation, autotuning, and state initialization occur; - at least one measured full rollout with fixed per-replan/per-request seeds; - every relevant history-length or latent-shape regime; - cache on/off and CFG serial/parallel variants if the manifest claims them; and - a reset/new-session sequence for stateful models. Cold compile time, warm steady-state latency, graph count, graph breaks, recompilations, and peak memory should be reported separately. #### Integration points - Extend `CompiledModuleRegistry` with a stable region inventory/digest. - Let `DenoisingStage._maybe_torch_compile()` receive a resolved compile plan rather than only global booleans. - Reuse trajectory-capture plumbing from `compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py`, generalized to named checkpoint adapters. - Add a small manifest loader/resolver near diffusion server configuration. - Record fallback reasons in request/server metrics. No model code should read a CI artifact directly. Model adapters declare capture points and quality metrics; the runtime owns signature matching and fallback. #### Stateful and cache-aware behavior The signature must include state/cache schema and mode because `torch.compile` may trace different control flow when a cache wrapper is mounted or when a history-length branch changes. Compiled state must remain request-owned; graphs may not capture a mutable tensor belonging to a prior request. If a compiled region mutates cache buffers, the custom-op metadata and fake implementation must declare those mutations accurately. Otherwise the plan is rejected even if one sample appears numerically close. #### Tests Unit tests: - stable signature hashing and manifest schema; - supported and unsupported shape resolution; - eager fallback on digest/revision/state-schema mismatch; - capture-point registration and missing-checkpoint failure; - mutation/alias checks for state tensors; - no cross-request reuse of captured mutable buffers. GPU integration tests: - eager vs regional compile across a complete denoising trajectory; - first request vs warmed request; - state reset and changing history length; - CFG serial vs CFG parallel where supported; - compile with cache disabled and with an explicitly validated cache mode; - intentional one-step perturbation is caught at its first named checkpoint. #### Benchmark report Each promoted plan should report: - cold compile/warmup wall time; - warm p50/p95 model and end-to-end latency; - number of compiled regions, graphs, graph breaks, and recompiles; - peak GPU memory during warmup and steady state; - per-checkpoint numerical metrics; - public output/task metrics; and - exact workload signatures covered by the manifest. #### Alternatives considered - **Use one forward-pass allclose test.** It misses accumulated drift and state transitions. - **Gate only on final media.** It cannot localize the first divergence and may hide invalid internal state. - **Compile every encountered shape dynamically in production.** This gives unbounded cold latency/memory behavior and no promotion evidence. - **Require bitwise equality for every model.** Too strict for legitimate backend/topology changes; the model adapter must declare a calibrated gate. #### Rollout 1. Generalize trajectory capture and define the manifest schema. 2. Add offline validation for one existing regionally compiled diffusion model. 3. Add runtime signature resolution with eager fallback and metrics. 4. Extend to one stateful world model with reset/history tests. 5. Consider CI promotion automation only after artifacts are stable. ### Related resources - Diffusion denoising compile integration: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - Existing trajectory comparator: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/tools/compare_diffusion_trajectory_similarity.py - SGLang custom-op/compile guidance: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/piecewise_cuda_graph.mdx - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py - Related vLLM-Omni native-step/golden-trace RFC: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/5950

signal.title: [Feature] Side-Effect-Aware Step Reuse for Stateful Diffusion Pipelines
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Define a framework-level, side-effect-aware contract for reusing a previously computed denoising prediction on selected iterative steps while continuing to execute scheduler updates and any mandatory terminal state writes. SGLang Diffusion already integrates Cache-DiT and model-specific cache policies, but recent lifecycle bugs show that “skip a transformer call” is not a complete correctness model. Stateful world models may have several independent lifetimes at once: - request-local denoising predictions; - modality-local video and action loops; - conditional/unconditional CFG branches; and - persistent session/KV state updated only by specific real forwards. An approximate step-reuse policy can be safe only if those lifetimes and side effects are explicit. This proposal adds that contract without prescribing one universal similarity metric. #### Goals - Separate reusable denoising predictions from persistent session/KV state. - Let a model define when a real prediction is similar enough to reuse and for how many steps. - Always execute the scheduler update, even when the transformer is skipped. - Never feed reused predictions back into the similarity history as new observations. - Support independent state machines for modalities or branches with different dynamics. - Force designated real forwards when model side effects must be committed. - Make reset, CFG, distributed-decision, and failure behavior testable. #### Non-goals - Replacing Cache-DiT or standardizing one cache algorithm. - Claiming exact numerical equivalence for approximate reuse. - Reusing state across requests in phase 1. - Inferring safe terminal side effects automatically from arbitrary model code. #### Proposed contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepReusePolicy: policy_name: str observation_point: str # e.g. "post_cfg_velocity" history_size: int max_skip_steps: int force_real_steps: frozenset[str] # e.g. {"first_two", "terminal"} state_scope: tuple[str, ...] # request, modality, cfg_role @dataclass class StepReuseState: last_real_prediction: torch.Tensor | None = None real_history: deque[torch.Tensor] = field(default_factory=deque) skip_remaining: int = 0 real_forwards: int = 0 reused_steps: int = 0 @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepSideEffectContract: terminal_write_required: bool = False write_tags: frozenset[str] = frozenset() ``` The model adapter supplies `observe_real_prediction(...)`, `decide_reuse(...)`, and side-effect metadata. The runtime supplies lifecycle, isolation, metrics, and distributed agreement. #### Execution flow ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["Begin request / modality loop
fresh StepReuseState"] Step["Next denoising step"] Force{"Real forward required?
warmup, no history, terminal side effect"} Budget{"skip_remaining > 0?"} Real["Run transformer"] Observe["Apply CFG, then record
real prediction only"] Decide["Model policy computes
bounded reuse budget"] Reuse["Reuse last real prediction"] Sched["Always run scheduler update"] More{"More steps?"} Finalize["Verify mandatory writes
and emit metrics"] Start --> Step --> Force Force -->|yes| Real --> Observe --> Decide --> Sched Force -->|no| Budget Budget -->|yes| Reuse --> Sched Budget -->|no| Real Sched --> More More -->|yes| Step More -->|no| Finalize ``` #### Lifecycle and isolation rules 1. State is created per logical request and per declared scope. Video and action loops do not share history unless a model explicitly declares that safe. 2. The first observations are real. A policy cannot make a similarity decision from reused values. 3. Reused predictions never enter `real_history`. 4. The scheduler advances on every configured step. 5. Terminal real-forward requirements override every reuse budget. 6. A request error, cancellation, reset, or session change destroys request-local reuse state. 7. Reuse is disabled by default and invalid policy parameters fail at configuration/admission time. #### CFG and distributed semantics The observation point must be explicit. For common two-branch CFG, a policy that compares the final guided velocity should observe *after* the conditional/unconditional merge. A policy that operates per branch must declare two independent states. All ranks participating in TP/SP/CFG parallelism must take the same execute/reuse decision. Phase 1 should compute the decision on the stage's control rank and broadcast a compact decision token, or derive it from replicated tensors proven identical. Rank-local threshold decisions are not safe because a one-ULP difference near a threshold can desynchronize collective control flow. The current Cache-DiT lifecycle issue involving serial CFG and CFG parallel is relevant evidence that reset ownership must be stated once and shared by every execution mode rather than inferred from wrapper placement. #### Integration proposal - Add a small `StepReuseController` adjacent to, not inside, the generic denoising loop. - Let existing Cache-DiT adapters remain unchanged initially. - Expose lifecycle hooks: `begin_scope`, `before_step`, `after_real_forward`, `after_scheduler_step`, and `finalize_scope`. - Add model adapters only for architectures with an explicit observation point and quality evaluation. - Keep persistent session/KV updates in model state; the controller merely enforces declared mandatory real-forward points. For LingBot-style world-action models, one adapter could create separate video and action scopes, compare FP32 post-CFG velocities, and declare a terminal real forward needed to install persistent rollout state. The framework should not embed those model-specific thresholds. #### Correctness and quality gates Required unit tests: - first `history_size` observations are real; - skip countdown is bounded and cannot underflow; - only real predictions update history; - scheduler is called for every step; - terminal write is forced after a long reuse streak; - state is isolated across requests, modalities, CFG roles, and retries; - invalid thresholds/history/budgets fail closed; - all distributed ranks receive the same decision token; - serial CFG and CFG-parallel lifecycle produces the same reset count. Required end-to-end validation: - cache off vs on with fixed seeds; - per-step real/reused trace; - public output quality metric plus internal trajectory metrics; - persistent state/KV equality after the forced terminal write where exact equality is expected; - multiple schedules and request lengths, not only one single-step sample. #### Observability Per request and per scope: - possible, real, and reused transformer forwards; - reuse streak lengths; - similarity/decision statistics (sampled or debug-only); - forced-real reason; - scheduler steps executed; - terminal-write verification result; and - fallback/disable reason. #### Alternatives considered - **A model-local boolean cache.** It cannot express independent modalities, terminal writes, or distributed decision agreement. - **Use only Cache-DiT wrapper state.** Existing algorithms remain useful, but wrapper placement alone does not define side effects and lifecycle for stateful world models. - **Skip scheduler steps together with transformer steps.** This changes the solver trajectory and is out of scope. - **Compare reused predictions recursively.** That makes self-reuse look artificially stable and can extend skipping without new evidence. #### Rollout 1. Land contract/controller tests with a synthetic iterative model. 2. Add trace-only mode that computes decisions but executes every real forward. 3. Validate one opt-in model adapter against full trajectory and public output gates. 4. Enable explicit opt-in configuration; keep defaults unchanged. 5. Generalize only after serial CFG, CFG-parallel, and session-state cases pass. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion denoising and Cache-DiT integration: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - Cache-DiT documentation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/cache_dit.mdx - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py - Related CFG lifecycle bug: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35054 - Related exact dependency-aware reuse RFC in vLLM-Omni (different reuse class): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6238
