signal.title: [Feature] Batched Candidate-Trajectory Ensembling for Stochastic Action Generation
signal.text:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Add a first-class, opt-in execution contract for generating multiple independent action trajectories from one conditioning context, executing the candidates as one physical batch, and reducing them to one served action result. SGLang Diffusion already has most of the lower-level pieces: - `Req.num_outputs_per_prompt` represents multiple outputs; - latent preparation preserves per-request RNG streams and batches the deterministic packing/scaling work; - pipeline stages can expand shared conditioning to the sample batch; and - Cosmos3 is implemented as a composed pipeline with explicit latent, timestep, denoising, action, and decode stages. What is missing is a model/runtime contract that says these outputs are *candidates for one logical prediction*, not independent public media outputs. Without that distinction, a world-action model has to implement sequential sampling or ad hoc aggregation inside model code, and the runtime cannot preserve candidate identity, enforce RNG independence, or measure the benefit of batching. This proposal is intentionally narrow. It does not propose averaging images or videos, and it does not change default `num_outputs_per_prompt` behavior. It adds an opt-in path for models whose public action output has a validated candidate reducer. #### Proposed execution contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateTrajectorySpec: count: int = 1 reducer: str = "none" # "none", "mean", or a registered model reducer return_candidates: bool = False seed_policy: str = "per_candidate" @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateGroup: request_id: str candidate_ids: tuple[int, ...] public_output: str = "action" ``` The model/pipeline adapter would declare: 1. which tensor is the candidate action trajectory; 2. whether reduction occurs before or after denormalization; 3. the supported reducer and output dtype/shape; 4. which conditioning tensors are candidate-invariant; and 5. whether video or another auxiliary branch must execute for action correctness. The runtime owns grouping, candidate identity, batching, failure handling, observability, and final response construction. The model owns the mathematical reduction rule. #### Request and execution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Req["One logical request
conditioning + candidate count N"] Validate["Validate model capability
and candidate contract"] Seeds["Create N independent
request-owned RNG streams"] Shared["Compute candidate-invariant
conditioning once"] Expand["Expand/fan out conditioning
and build candidate batch"] Denoise["One batched denoising path
candidate axis = N"] Action["Model-specific action
postprocessing"] Reduce["Validated reducer
mean or registered reducer"] Resp["One public action result
optional raw candidates"] Req --> Validate --> Seeds --> Shared --> Expand --> Denoise --> Action --> Reduce --> Resp ``` #### RNG and equivalence rules Candidate batching must not collapse stochastic independence or silently change seed semantics. - Candidate `i` receives a stable stream derived from `(base_seed, i)` or an explicitly supplied generator. - `count=1` must preserve the current output exactly. - For a fixed candidate seed list, batched execution must produce the same candidate set as the sequential reference under the model's declared equivalence rule. - Candidate ordering is stable across dynamic batching and output slicing. - Retry/fallback may rerun the whole group, but must not reuse a partially advanced generator as though it were fresh. The existing grouped latent-preparation logic is a useful precedent: it already draws request-owned random latents separately and only batches deterministic work afterward. The candidate path should retain the same property. #### Scheduler and batching behavior Phase 1 should admit a candidate group atomically when it fits the configured execution batch. If it does not fit, the runtime should fail clearly or use a documented sequential fallback; it should not silently truncate the group. A later phase may split candidates into microbatches and aggregate when all slices finish, but the request state must then track: - candidate IDs completed/pending; - seed/generator state per candidate; - partial reducer state; and - cancellation semantics for the entire logical request. Candidate-invariant conditioning should be encoded once where the stage contract permits it. An adapter may use an expanded view or an explicit attention fan-out; physical tensor replication is not required by this RFC. #### Integration points Suggested initial ownership: - request fields and validation: diffusion sampling/request data; - group identity and completion: request/scheduler state; - independent raw noise: `LatentPreparationStage`; - conditioning expansion: pipeline configuration's existing sample-batch expansion hook; - candidate reducer: a small action-output capability implemented by opt-in world-model pipelines; - metrics: candidate count, physical forwards, fallback reason, reducer time, and action-only branch time. The first model integration could be Cosmos3 action generation because SGLang already has an explicit Cosmos3 composed pipeline. The framework abstraction should not contain Cosmos-specific tensor names. #### Correctness and quality gates Required tests: 1. `count=1` is identical to the existing path. 2. Fixed per-candidate seeds produce the same ordered candidate tensors in sequential and batched modes. 3. The reduced action matches a standalone reducer applied to captured candidate tensors. 4. Candidate IDs remain stable when unrelated requests are co-batched. 5. CFG serial and CFG-parallel paths preserve candidate membership. 6. TP/SP output reconstruction happens before reduction when the action tensor is sharded. 7. Cancellation and one-candidate failure do not return a partial aggregate as a valid result. 8. Auxiliary video decode can be skipped only when the model declares it irrelevant to the action output. Quality validation must be model-specific. The framework should report candidate-level and reduced-output artifacts but should not hard-code a universal action metric or assume that a larger candidate count always improves quality. #### Benchmark plan Report, for `N in {1, 2, 4, 8, 10}`: - sequential reference latency; - batched latency and peak memory; - number of physical transformer forwards; - conditioning encode time; - candidate-reduction time; - candidate tensor parity under fixed seeds; and - model-declared action-quality metrics. Benchmark at more than one parallel topology. Wider TP may help the larger candidate batch while regressing `N=1`; the RFC should not encode one topology as universally optimal. #### Alternatives considered - **Keep aggregation in application code.** This forces repeated RPCs or model-specific server loops and prevents the runtime from preserving one logical request/candidate group. - **Treat candidates as ordinary independent outputs.** This loses the reduction contract and makes failure/cancellation semantics ambiguous. - **Always expose raw candidates.** This moves a model-system accuracy feature into every client and expands the public payload unnecessarily. - **Average videos/latents generically.** Out of scope and not semantically valid for this proposal. #### Rollout 1. Land internal types and validation with no model enabled. 2. Add a Cosmos3 action adapter and sequential-equivalence tests. 3. Add atomic candidate-group scheduling and metrics. 4. Benchmark before enabling any default. 5. Consider microbatching and additional reducers only after the initial contract is stable. ### Related resources - Cosmos3 composed pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - Latent preparation and per-request RNG handling: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/latent_preparation.py - Diffusion denoising stage and sample-batch expansion: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - vLLM-Omni request-selected output routing RFC (complementary output-branch contract): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6302

signal.title: [Distributed] Enable custom all-reduce for attention TP groups
signal.text: ## Summary Enable custom-all-reduce capability detection for derived attention tensor-parallel groups. ## Motivation With DP attention, the full TP group and attention-TP group may differ. For example, a 16-rank DP4 x attention-TP4 launch creates a full TP16 group plus four attention-TP4 subgroups. The attention groups were constructed with `use_custom_allreduce=False`, so eligible node-local subgroups could never select CustomAllReduceV2. The server-side MNNVL auto-enable logic also used the full `tp_size` as a global gate. That suppressed eligible derived groups before their own topology and world-size checks could run. ## Changes - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Remove the server-level `tp_size <= 8` gate from MNNVL auto-enable. - Leave final selection to `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2(group, device)` for each process group. - Add focused tests for TP16 launches with derived groups and attention-TP group construction. ## Behavior For a DP4 x attention-TP4 launch: - Full TP16 independently rejects or falls back downstream. - Each eligible attention-TP4 subgroup can select CustomAllReduceV2. - Explicit custom-all-reduce disable settings remain respected. ## Validation - Python syntax compilation passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Added CPU unit coverage for the changed selection behavior. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32145778328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145778328)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32145777749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32145777749)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Kimi] Enable GB300 SP collectives for attention TP4 and TP16
signal.text: ## Summary Enable tuned Kimi K3 sequence-parallel collectives on GB300 for both derived attention-TP subgroups and world-size 16. This covers: - DP4 x attention-TP4 / EP16, where the attention group is a node-local subgroup of the full TP16 group. - Attention-TP16 / EP16 across four GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment. ## Motivation SGLang already creates a separate attention-TP group when attention TP differs from full TP, but that group was constructed with `use_custom_allreduce=False`. The server-side MNNVL auto-enable logic also gated on the full `tp_size`, suppressing eligible derived TP4/TP8 groups before their own capability checks could run. World-size 16 additionally needs multinode CustomAllReduceV2 workspace support and an exact-device K3 SP tuning table. Generic TP16 all-reduces should remain on NCCL until independently tuned. ## Changes ### Process-group selection - Let derived attention-TP groups inherit the global custom-all-reduce policy. - Remove the server-level `tp_size <= 8` MNNVL gate. - Leave final communicator selection to `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2(group, device)` for each process group. - Add focused tests for TP16 launches with derived groups and attention-TP construction. ### K3 world-16 support - Admit world-size 16 CustomAllReduceV2 communicators on multinode MNNVL fabric. - Use the world-16 communicator as symmetric-workspace infrastructure for K3 SP kernels. - Keep ordinary TP16 all-reduces on NCCL. - Enable K3 SP dispatch for world size 16 when an exact-device table is available. - Add the GB300 `world=16,H=7168` reduce-scatter/all-gather tuning table. - Keep untuned attention-residual fusion entries on the existing `separate` path. - Add one-time dispatch/fallback diagnostics. ## TP4 validation Nsight Systems confirmed exactly 92 custom TP4 reduce-scatter/all-gather pairs per decode step: - NCCL reduce-scatter launches over ten steps: 930 -> 10. - NCCL all-gather launches: 940 -> 20. - Custom reduce-scatter launches: 0 -> 920. - Custom all-gather launches: 0 -> 920. Representative medians: - Reduce-scatter: 16.014 -> 6.853 us (`-57.2%`). - All-gather: 16.508 -> 7.179 us (`-56.5%`). - Aligned layers 84-87 wall time: 1883.232 -> 1753.139 us (`-6.91%`). - Full decode graph: 43.365 -> 40.259 ms (`-7.16%`). Large TP4 prefill shapes continue to fall back safely to NCCL when they exceed the default push workspace. ## World-16 tuning and correctness The table was tuned on four GB300 nodes in one NVL72 segment over global-token buckets 16 through 16384. - Every measured push/pull/direct candidate was checked against NCCL before timing. - BF16 comparison used `rtol=2e-2`, `atol=5e-2` to account for rank-16 reduction-order differences. - Every selected custom bucket was faster than NCCL. - The production table was checked under CUDA graph capture/replay at every bucket. Representative results: | Operation | Tokens | NCCL | Custom | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Reduce-scatter | 512 | 105.371 us | 17.219 us | 6.12x | | All-gather | 512 | 57.081 us | 16.824 us | 3.39x | | Reduce-scatter | 8192 | 265.358 us | 171.723 us | 1.55x | | All-gather | 8192 | 224.534 us | 171.736 us | 1.31x | ## TP16 serving and dispatch validation Workload: ISL 8192, OSL 1024, concurrency 512, 2048 requests, attention-TP16 / EP16. - Output throughput: 2872.99 -> 3029.28 tok/s (`+5.44%`). - Median TPOT: 117.64 -> 109.69 ms (`-6.76%`). - Median ITL: 55.33 -> 48.60 ms (`-12.16%`). - Aligned layers 84-87 wall time: 2398.005 -> 2100.865 us (`-12.39%`). - Eight SP collectives in that window: 369.731 -> 137.872 us (`-62.71%`). Nsight Systems confirmed, over ten rank-0 decode steps: - 920 custom reduce-scatter launches. - 920 custom direct all-gather launches. - Zero NCCL reduce-scatter launches. - Ordinary non-SP TP16 all-reduces remained on NCCL. ## Deployment note The validated world-16 production launch used: ```bash SGLANG_FORCE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2_PUSH_SIZE_KB=16384 ``` This provides the full K3 push workspace rather than clipping it at the generic all-reduce crossover. ## Local checks - Python syntax compilation passed. - JSON parsing passed. - `git diff --check` passed. - Added CPU unit coverage for the changed group-selection behavior.

This table logs those scout results. > Related: #21302 — per-version AITER(in SGLang main) feature/issue & PR readiness --- | AITER Scout Run Date | AITER Commit ID | Status | Memo | | --- | --- | --- signal.title: [Bug] sglang 0.5.17 + hierarchical cache + chunked prefill 16K: scheduler hang in DSV4 sparse prefill (watchdog abort) on DeepSeek-V4 FP8 / H20 — plus sampling device-side assert on 0.5.16+PR
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Key launch arguments ``` --tp-size 8 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 --max-running-requests 64 --page-size 256 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 3.0 --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ (speculative_num_steps=1, speculative_eagle_topk=1, speculative_num_draft_tokens=6) ``` Scheduler init line: ``` max_total_num_tokens=9027840, chunked_prefill_size=16384, max_prefill_tokens=32768, max_running_requests=64, context_len=1048576, available_gpu_mem=17.10 GB DSV4 memory calculation: bytes_per_full_token=9259.90, available_bytes=79.15 GB, full_token=9027840 ``` ## Crash A (0.5.17, primary): scheduler hang -> watchdog abort in DSV4 sparse prefill Timeline on 2026-08-08 (hicache ON, chunked_prefill_size=16384): - 12:28:02 server starts on 0.5.17 - 15:02:37 last batch log (decode batches, ~89.9K full tokens, SWA window active) - 15:08:34 all 8 TP ranks: `Scheduler watchdog timeout (self.watchdog_timeout=300, self.soft=False)` - 15:08:53 CUDA coredump attempt (`CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP` was not set), 60s wait - 15:09:53 `kill_process_tree` py-spy dump (`--native`) of the scheduler MainThread — identical shape on all ranks: ``` cuStreamSynchronize (libcuda.so.580.95.05) cudaStreamSynchronize (libcudart.so.13) at::native::_local_scalar_dense_cuda (libtorch_cuda.so) at::native::item / at::_ops::item::call torch::autograd::THPVariable_item (libtorch_python.so) build_swa_token_ids (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:241) build (dsv4/sparse_prefill_utils.py:333) _forward_prefill_sparse (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1794) forward (deepseek_v4_backend.py:1710) forward (deepseek_v4.py:1287 / 1698 / 2423 / 2615) _execute_extend (runner/eager_runner.py:331) _forward_prefill (dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py:412) run_batch (scheduler.py:3594) -> event_loop_overlap -> run_scheduler_process ``` The main thread is blocked in `.item()` inside `build_swa_token_ids`, i.e. `cudaStreamSynchronize` never returns: a kernel enqueued during sparse prefill apparently never completes (device-side hang). The watchdog then aborts all 8 scheduler processes. There is no Python-level exception; the server simply freezes and stops serving. ## Crash B (0.5.16 + PR patches): device-side assert in sampling (NaN/Inf in probs) Observed twice with the same chunked-prefill-16K config: - 2026-08-05 14:15:50, hicache **ON** — preceded by a large prefix-cache hit (`#cached-token: 178176`), matching the signature of issue #33656 (hicache restores target-side KV/SWA but not the DSpark draft-side SWA state -> SWA KV written at wrong positions -> NaN logits). dmesg shows all 8 GPUs raised Xid 43 in cascade. - 2026-08-06 18:02:24, hicache **OFF** — same assert, so the plain radix-cache large-prefix path seems able to trigger it too (or a related SWA/prefix-reuse bug remains). All 8 TP ranks die with: ``` Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed. (_assert_async_cuda_kernel, /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109) ... File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py", line 448, in _forward_prefill ctx_lens = torch.tensor(batch.extend_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered ``` (reported asynchronously at the H2D copy; the asserting kernel is multinomial sampling, i.e. the model produced NaN/Inf logits/probs.) Note: the Aug 5 occurrence looks like issue #33656, whose fix (PR #30393) only landed in 0.5.17. The Aug 6 occurrence had hicache disabled, which #33656 does not explain. ## Previously observed, resolved (for completeness, logs omitted) On 0.5.16 + PR patches we also hit a plain CUDA OOM inside deep_gemm `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (~7 GiB transient workspace). It disappeared after lowering `--mem-fraction-static` and has not recurred; we believe it is unrelated to the two failures above. ## Reproduction notes - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ## Questions 1. Any known issue in the DSV4 sparse prefill path (`sparse_prefill_utils.build` / `build_swa_token_ids`) that can deadlock/hang the CUDA stream with chunked prefill 16K + hierarchical cache on 0.5.17 (i.e. *with* PR #30393 included)? The `.item()` sync in the hot path also looks fragile — should this be pre-computed on CPU? 2. Crash B on Aug 6 reproduced with hicache OFF, which issue #33656 / PR #30393 does not cover. Is there another known NaN source in the DSV4 / DSPARK prefix-reuse path (0.5.16 era), and is a fix included in 0.5.17? 3. We are also aware of issue #31023 (compact-verify TP8 + overlap IMA instability); we run the default static ragged-verify mode, so it should not apply — but mentioning it in case it is related to Crash A. Full (sanitized) log excerpts attached: `sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt` [sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30889446/sglang_crash_logs_sanitized.txt) ### Reproduction - Long-context serving workload (tens to hundreds of K tokens per request), high prefix reuse (hicache hits of 100K+ tokens). - Crash A: once on 0.5.17. Crash B: twice on 0.5.16+PR (hicache on and off); not yet seen on 0.5.17, but only one day of traffic so far. - No minimal repro yet. For the next occurrence we will set `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `CUDA_ENABLE_USER_TRIGGERED_COREDUMP=1`; happy to add extra logging if advised. ### Environment - sglang: **0.5.17** (released 2026-08-08; installed 12:16 and crashed the same day). 0.5.17 includes PR #30393 (HiCache packed/sidecar draft caches, the fix for issue #33656), yet the hang below still occurred with hicache ON. - The two earlier crashes (Aug 5-6) below were on **0.5.16 + local PR patches** (local patches only touch the decode-stage grammar vocab mask; they predate the upstream fix PR #30393). - torch 2.11.0, triton 3.6.0, flashinfer-python 0.6.15.post1, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.5.post1, apache-tvm-ffi 0.1.11, sglang-kernel 0.4.5, transformers 5.12.1 - GPU: 8x NVIDIA H20-3e (139.80 GiB each), driver 580.95.05 - Model: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, FP8 weights, KV cache fp8_e4m3, context_len = 1048576 - OS: Linux, Python 3.12

signal.title: [Model] Support Ling-3.0-flash (BailingMoeV3)
signal.text: ## Motivation Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support. ## Modifications - `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN). - DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing. - KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification. - `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers. - BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell. - Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests. ## Validation All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`. ### Quantized checkpoints Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU. | GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 | | H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 | | B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 | | B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 | INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts. BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate. ### Speculative decoding Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`: | spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate | |---|---:|---:|---:| | DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% | | MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% | Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops. ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI. - [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200. - [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:no_entry_sign: [Run #32095333446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32095333446)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32095333328](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32095333328)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Fix inflated row pitch when a CP round-robin shard has a single row
signal.text: ## Motivation `dsa_cp_round_robin_split_data` can hand downstream kernels a shard whose row pitch is `cp_size` times too large, which on DeepSeek-V4 prefill context parallelism causes a GPU memory fault. The last line of the function is ```python return input_.view(-1, cp_size, *input_.shape[1:])[:, cp_rank].contiguous() ``` When a prefill chunk holds exactly `cp_size` tokens, every rank's shard has a **single row**. A size-1 outer dimension imposes no contiguity constraint, so `is_contiguous()` returns `True` regardless of `stride(0)` — and `.contiguous()` becomes a no-op. The shard keeps the `cp_size`-inflated row pitch, `cp_size * row_numel` instead of `row_numel`. Any kernel that takes its row pitch from `stride(0)` then treats the shard as `cp_size` times larger than it is. On DeepSeek-V4 (`hc_mult=4`, `hidden_size=7168`, `cp_size=8`) the pitch is `229376` instead of `28672`; aiter's `mhc_pre` sizes its buffer descriptors from it and addresses past the tensor: ``` Memory access fault by GPU node-N on address 0x... (8 GPUs, 8 distinct addresses) Fatal Python error: Aborted deepseek_v4.py:1541 hc_pre -> aiter/ops/mhc.py:372 mhc_pre ``` ### Reproducer (deterministic, no GPU fault needed) ```python import torch HC, HID, CP = 4, 7168, 8 for tokens in (8, 16, 24): x = torch.randn(tokens, HC, HID, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") # contiguous out = x.view(-1, CP, *x.shape[1:])[:, 7].contiguous() # the current line print(f"tokens={tokens:3d} m={out.shape[0]} stride0={out.stride(0):7d} " f"expected={HC*HID} is_contiguous={out.is_contiguous()}") ``` ``` tokens= 8 m=1 stride0= 229376 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True <-- no-op, pitch is 8x tokens= 16 m=2 stride0= 28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True tokens= 24 m=3 stride0= 28672 expected=28672 is_contiguous=True ``` ## Modifications Compare the shard's row pitch against the parent's and copy with `clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)` only when they differ, plus a comment explaining why `.contiguous()` cannot be used here. Copy behaviour versus the current code (`row_numel = prod(shape[1:])`): | `cp_size` | shard rows | current | this PR | note | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | any | no copy | **no copy** | shard is genuinely contiguous | | >1 | 1 | **no copy** (pitch stays `cp_size * row_numel`) | copy | this is the bug being fixed | | >1 | >=2 | copy | copy | unchanged | So the only added copy is the one that is required for correctness, and it copies a single row. An unconditional `clone()` would also have copied for `cp_size == 1`, where `.contiguous()` correctly does nothing, so the pitch comparison is used instead. Values are unchanged in every case. Verified alternatives that also work: `torch.empty(shape).copy_(shard)`, `shard.reshape(-1, *shard.shape[1:])`. Does **not** work: `.contiguous()`, and `input_[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous()`. ## Accuracy Tests Values are bit-identical to the current code in all cases (the change only affects the layout of a shard whose contents are already correct): ``` tokens= 8 rank=0: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 8 rank=7: m=1 old_stride0=2272 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 16 rank=0: m=2 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True tokens= 24 rank=7: m=3 old_stride0= 284 new_stride0=284 torch.equal(old, new) = True ``` Separately, feeding a strided shard to the affected kernel produces wrong results, which is what this fix prevents downstream (same logical values via a strided view vs a compacted copy, DeepSeek-V4 dims): ``` m=2 cp=8 max|diff| in y = 7.42 m=4 cp=8 max|diff| in y = 10.31 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling The copy runs only for single-row shards. Measured on MI355X, `(1, 4, 7168)` bf16 = 56 KB: ``` clone(memory_format=contiguous_format) on (1, 4, 7168) bf16 = 56 KB : 0.1 us per call observed frequency: 8 calls per ~5,200 mhc_pre calls in a 3600 s run => ~1 us added per hour-long run ``` The `m >= 2` path is unchanged — `.contiguous()` already copied there — and `cp_size == 1` still copies nothing. ### End-to-end validation 1P1D DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on MI355X, prefill TP8/EP8/**CP8** (`interleave`), decode TP8/EP8/DP8, agentic trace replay. Instrumented runs logging every `mhc_pre` shard's strides, before the fix: | runs | mhc_pre calls | shards with the inflated pitch | GPU memory faults | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 7 runs | ~45,000 | 0 | 0 | | 1 run | 5,240 | **8** (one per CP rank) | **8** | The condition is rare by default because a request's tail chunk is `extend_len % chunked_prefill_size`, so at 8192 a chunk small enough to leave a rank with one token occurs for roughly 1 request in 1000. Forcing it with `chunked-prefill-size 256` raises the rate to ~3%: | run | forced | fix | single-row shards | inflated pitch | faults | outcome | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | A | yes | no | yes | **8** | **8** | crash after ~15 min | | B | yes | **yes** | **8** | **0** | **0** | no fault | Same trigger and the same number of single-row shards; the fix removes the inflated pitch and the faults. ## Related observation (not changed here) `python/sglang/srt/layers/utils/cp_utils.py:194` has the same pattern: ```python input_ids = input_ids[cp_rank::cp_size].contiguous() ``` I verified this `.contiguous()` is also a no-op for a single-element shard (it leaves `stride(0) == cp_size`). It is not known to cause a failure today — `input_ids` is consumed by ops that honour strides — so I left it alone to keep this PR focused, but it may be worth the same treatment. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests. — the function calls `get_parallel()` and needs a distributed context, so the reproducer above is given instead; happy to add a test if you can point me at the right harness. - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations. — not applicable. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32010474564](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010474564)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32010474245](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32010474245)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion] Optimizing MiniMax-H3 for consumer-level GPUs: INT8 Linear + pluggable DiT attention backends
signal.text:
## Summary Runs MiniMax-H3 text-to-video-and-audio on one 24GB GPU and cuts denoise wall clock by **1.34× with exact attention**, up to **2.48×** with opt-in approximate attention backends. 1344×768 · 107 frames · 20 NFE · same process: warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), timed only: | Config | timed e2e | Denoise | vs BF16 | PSNR vs BF16 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | BF16 + FlashAttention (baseline) | 405.6 s | 370.2 s | 1.00× | — | | **`kitchen_int8` + FA** — new default | **303.3 s** | 273.7 s | **1.34×** | 24.81 dB | | `kitchen_int8` + `sol_attn` | 223.9 s | 203.9 s | 1.81× | 24.44 dB | | `kitchen_int8` + `sage_attn` | 174.9 s | 154.2 s | 2.32× | 23.51 dB | | `kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid | **163.8 s** | 143.1 s | **2.48×** | 23.04 dB | | *(external reference)* ComfyUI INT8 workflow | 318.1 s | 297.4 s | 1.28× | 16.43 dB | ComfyUI is the reference workflow for H3 on 24GB, included as a yardstick only. Its 1.05× gap to INT8+FA is mostly node-graph wrapper overhead (~19.7 s). ## Motivation H3's DiT weights are **~60+ GiB in BF16**, so a 24GB card requires layerwise offload, and the DiT runs at **T ≈ 32,700 tokens** — a single `FlashAttnFwdSm80` call averages **202 ms**. It runs, but at 405.6 s end-to-end. Nsight Systems (timed pass only, BF16) shows **two operator classes own ~76% of GPU activity**: | Category | Share | | --- | --- | | **Attention (FlashAttention)** | **41.8%** | | **DiT Linear GEMM (BF16 cuBLAS)** | **34.4%** | | H2D memcpy (layerwise offload) | 11.2% | | VAE / FP16 GEMM | 8.8% | | Other | 3.8% | Everything else is ruled out by measurement: - **PCIe is not the bottleneck.** Compute-stream stall waiting on weight transfers is **0.00–0.09 s per forward**; bandwidth runs at **12%** of the measured pinned-H2D ceiling (3.34 of 27.0 GB/s). Optimizations that only reduce transferred bytes buy **zero** time. - **Compute is already at roofline** — BF16 GEMM and attention both at 140–148 TFLOP/s against ~165 peak. - **Elementwise is 1.6%** of a step; **framework overhead is ~0** (microbench 19.31 s/step vs 19.26 s in-framework, within 2%). So there are two levers, pulled in this order: quantize Linear (numerics only), then revisit attention. That ordering matters — after INT8 lands, attention rises to **~51%** of GPU activity while DiT GEMM falls to **~11%**, which is what motivates doing both here. --- ## Modifications ### 1. `kitchen_int8` quantization method Targets the 4 GEMMs per DiT block (45.3% of a step). Forward calls `torch.ops.comfy_kitchen.int8_linear`, a single fused op doing rotation → dynamic per-row activation quantization → INT8 tensor-core GEMM → fused dequant epilogue → bias. - **Quantization happens online at load time** from the Hub BF16 weights (data-free, no calibration), not from an offline INT8 checkpoint. - **`create_weights` is identical to `UnquantizedLinearMethod`**, so H3's custom qkv loader and `MergedColumnParallelLinear` sharding work unmodified — no loader changes. - **Per-layer CPU→GPU→CPU round-trip quantization** (≤294 MiB resident at a time) rather than `needs_device_weight_postprocess`, which would move all 60 GiB on-device and OOM. - **Layers whose input dim isn't divisible by the group size fall back to BF16** instead of raising. H3's AdaLN projections (in=2688) take this path; they are 0.2% of step time. Load log: `quantized 209 linear layers (37.38 GiB BF16 -> 18.69 GiB INT8), left 51 in BF16`. No observable added load time (192.8 s vs 206.8 s for BF16).
Why online quantization rather than an offline checkpoint (correctness, not convenience) The quantization is data-free (`int8_tensorwise` + ConvRot, groupsize 256, no calibration), so it is exactly reproducible from BF16 — verified against an externally quantized reference at scale relative error ~1e-7. The decisive reason is **layout**. H3 stores `qkv` grouped (`[head, q+k+v per group]`) and SGLang reorders it to `[Q_all; K_all; V_all]`. Quantizing inside `process_weights_after_loading` sees the post-reorder, post-TP-shard weights, so there is no ambiguity. Consuming a pre-quantized external checkpoint mismatches on `qkv` — we measured dequantized error 1.20 versus 2.68e-03 until the reorder was accounted for — which is a **silent** correctness bug, not a loud failure. Layerwise offload interaction was audited and is safe: the per-layer CPU buffer is keyed by dtype (so int8 weights, fp32 scales and bf16 norms coexist), and quantization runs before `configure_layerwise_offload()`, so the offload snapshot captures post-quantization dtype/shape.
### 2. Row-splitting for large-M INT8 GEMMs The fused kernel mis-selects its CUTLASS configuration for `qkv_proj` at M=32700, costing 1.81× over pure IMMA. Splitting M into 4 chunks pushes the heuristic back to the right config: `qkv_proj` 26.51 → **17.94 ms** (1.48×), per-block total 69.28 → 59.14 ms (1.17×). Predicate is `rows > 8192 and out_features >= 8192`, overridable via `SGLANG_KITCHEN_INT8_MAX_ROWS` / `SGLANG_KITCHEN_INT8_MIN_SPLIT_N`.
Root cause: Stream-K selected for a shape that has 168 full waves Overhead over pure IMMA was very uneven (`qkv_proj` 1.81×, others 1.19–1.27×), grew **superlinearly in M** (1.12× at M=4096 → 1.34× at 16384 → 1.83× at 32700), and forcing the cuBLAS fallback made `qkv_proj` *faster* (19.42 vs 26.50 ms) with bit-identical output — all pointing at configuration selection rather than the quantization epilogue. `select_fused_int8_config(m, n, k)` is a hand-written threshold tree: - `qkv_proj` (M=32700, N=21504, K=5376): `n <= 24832` holds → small-problem branch → `m*k` (175.8M) `> n*5675` (122.0M) → **config 13** - `mlp.fc1` (M=32700, N=28672): `n > 24832` → other branch → **config 0** Both use the **same tile shape** (128×256×64); config 13 additionally uses `ThreadblockSwizzleLeanStreamK`. Stream-K exists to balance load when tiles can't fill the GPU — but `qkv_proj` at M=32700 launches **21,504 CTAs, i.e. 168 full waves over 128 SMs**, so the balancing is worthless and its workspace plus fixup reduction is pure overhead. Splitting M into 4 chunks puts the shape back under config 0's threshold (`M <= n*5675/k = 22700`), which matches the measured M sweep. End-to-end A/B (only difference between runs): steady per-forward 14.35 → **13.73 s**, denoise stage **276.4 → 270.0 s** (−2.3%), peak memory unchanged.
### 3. Pluggable DiT attention backends FlashAttention is at roofline, so further speedup needs a different algorithm. Selected via `--attention-backend`; **default remains `fa`**, and the text encoder always stays on `torch_sdpa` (only DiT attention is substituted). | Backend | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `fa` (default) | exact-attention baseline | | `sol_attn` | Ada Triton sparse (SM89, `int8_qk=True`); first `dense_steps=10` dense, rest sparse | | `sage_attn` | SageAttention 2.2.0, approximate throughout | | hybrid | `sol_attn` with `dense_backend=sage_attn` — Sage for the dense prefix, Sol sparse tail | Includes an API compatibility shim for `sol_attn` (filters arguments it doesn't accept, e.g. `kv_splits`; enables `int8_qk` automatically on Ada). --- ## Accuracy Tests Same prompt and seed (42), 20 NFE. First pair isolates **quantization** (both exact attention); second pair shows the **approximate attention** tiers. **BF16 + FA — baseline, 405.6 s** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19551677-532e-46c9-a104-b8844ba2303c **`kitchen_int8` + FA — new default, 303.3 s** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/442021c1-766c-443f-901f-2361546cbe50 **`kitchen_int8` + `sol_attn` — 223.9 s** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f12eb91b-f539-4537-b421-97b37860fe8a **`kitchen_int8` + Sage→Sol hybrid — 163.8 s** https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ef3c2e2-3434-4558-95df-4069899960ee --- ## Example Quality tier (new default) — INT8 Linear with exact FlashAttention, on one 24GB card: ```bash pip install comfy-kitchen # required only for --quantization kitchen_int8 sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend fa \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` Note that `--layerwise-offload-components` deliberately omits `vae` (see change 4). For the **BF16 baseline**, drop `--quantization`; everything else is identical. Speed tier (opt-in) — same offload recipe, Sage→Sol hybrid on the DiT only: ```bash sglang generate \ --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \ --model-variant fl2va \ --quantization kitchen_int8 \ --attention-backend sol_attn \ --attention-backend-config dense_backend=sage_attn,dense_steps=10 \ --component-attention-backends text_encoder=torch_sdpa,transformer=sol_attn \ --performance-mode memory \ --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder \ --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 \ --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 0 \ --enable-torch-compile false \ --prompt "A cat walking on a sunny beach, gentle waves." \ --save-output ``` --- ## Benchmarking and Profiling RTX 4090 D 24GB · driver 595.58.03 · CUDA 13.0 · PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 · 1344×768 / 107 frames / euler / 20 NFE · `torch.compile` and step caching **disabled** · same process: load → warmup (seed 0) → timed (seed 42), **only the timed pass reported**. Results are in the table at the top. Steady-state per-forward times: BF16 18.5 s → INT8 13.3 s → `sol_attn` 13.8 s dense / 6.8 s sparse → `sage_attn` 7.8 s → hybrid 7.9 → 6.6 s. Text encoding (~1.2 s) and decode (~15 s) are off the denoise path and unchanged. At the kernel level the 4 GEMMs in a DiT block go from BF16 **171.74 ms** to **68.88 ms** (**2.49×**). Worth noting that this is **kernel quality, not "using INT8"** — with the same INT8 weights, `torch._int_mm` is 0.46–0.90×, i.e. *slower* than BF16, and a Triton INT8 implementation lands at roughly parity. Memory: quantized DiT linear weights 37.38 → **18.69 GiB**, bytes streamed per forward 60.12 → **42.19 GiB**, CPU resident ~60 → **~25 GiB**. GPU peak stays ~18 GB either way, since under streaming offload it is set by offload buffers and VAE decode, not weight dtype. --- ## Checklist - [ ] Format code with pre-commit hooks - [ ] Unit tests added: `test_comfy_int8_linear_method.py`, `test_comfy_int8_row_split.py` - [ ] Document `--quantization kitchen_int8`, `--attention-backend`, and the 24GB offload recipe (including why `vae` must stay out of `layerwise_offload_components`) - [ ] Benchmark and accuracy results included above - [ ] Confirm the BF16 default path is unchanged when `comfy-kitchen` is not installed --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #32106865028](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32106865028) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32106864858](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32106864858)

signal.title: [SM120] Add optional b12x PCIe all-reduce (one-shot + fused RMSNorm + FP8 DMA ring)
signal.text: ## Motivation On Blackwell workstation / server parts (SM120 & SM121 — RTX PRO 6000, RTX 6000D, RTX 50-series, GB10) the GPUs are connected over PCIe with no NVLink. The per-layer tensor-parallel all-reduce therefore dominates both decode latency and long-prompt prefill: on 8x RTX 6000D running GLM-5.2-NVFP4, NCCL needs 45 us for a 4 KB all-reduce and 344 us for 64 KB, which is most of the per-token budget at low batch sizes. [`b12x`](https://pypi.org/project/b12x/) (Apache-2.0) is an SM120/SM121-only CuTe DSL kernel library that ships IPC-backed PCIe all-reduce runtimes for exactly this topology. This PR wires two of them into SGLang behind an opt-in flag. ## What this adds A new `B12xPCIeCommunicator` and a three-tier dispatch inside `GroupCoordinator._all_reduce`: | message size | path | |---|---| | `<= 8 MB` | b12x PCIe **one-shot** all-reduce (decode-sized hidden states) | | `8 MB .. 256 MB` | b12x PCIe **DMA ring**, optional FP8 wire format (prefill chunks) | | otherwise | existing NCCL path, unchanged | The one-shot runtime also exposes a fused `all-reduce + residual add + RMSNorm`, plugged into the existing `fused_allreduce_rmsnorm` coordinator hook that AITER already uses (`layers/communicator.py` + `layers/layernorm.py`). That kernel is specialized for `<= 36` rows, so the dispatch helpers cap on token count and fall back when it does not apply — including an explicit all-reduce fallback in `_forward_with_allreduce_fusion`, since the caller has already skipped its own all-reduce when it takes the fusion path. ## Safety / blast radius - Off by default: `SGLANG_B12X_PCIE_AR` and `SGLANG_B12X_PCIE_DMA` are `EnvBool(False)`. - The communicator is only constructed for the **tensor-parallel** group (other groups would just pin IPC buffers). - `b12x` is an optional dependency; when it is not installed the setup logs a warning and everything stays on NCCL. No changes to any default code path. - Every tier re-checks dtype / contiguity / size and returns to NCCL when the kernel declines. ## Results GLM-5.2-NVFP4, 8x RTX 6000D (SM120, PCIe), driver 595.71.05, KV cache FP8, greedy, prefix caching off. **Kernel microbenchmark** (8 ranks, NCCL vs b12x one-shot): 4 KB 45.0 -> 7.3 us (6.1x), 12 KB 58.5 -> 15.3 us (3.8x), 64 KB 344.5 -> 38.5 us (8.9x). **TP8 decode** (ISL 1 / OSL 256), median TPOT / output tok/s: | bs | baseline (NCCL) | + b12x | |---|---|---| | 1 | 23.9 ms / 41 | **14.7 ms / 66** | | 8 | 70.6 ms / 112 | **29.8 ms / 264** | | 32 | 105.8 ms / 300 | **69.2 ms / 457** | **TP8 e2e 8K** (ISL 8192 / OSL 64), median TTFT: `6103 ms -> 1384 ms` (DMA ring tier). **TP4xPP2 + MTP, 64K** (ISL 65536 / OSL 1024), bs1: TTFT `11.5 s -> 9.3 s`, TPOT `10.3 ms -> 9.5 ms`, accept length 3.00. **Accuracy**: GSM8K (20 questions) stays at 0.900 for both TP8 and TP4xPP2+MTP — identical to the NCCL baseline — with `Invalid 0.000`, and greedy output matches token-for-token on a fixed prompt. ## Test plan - [x] TP8 and TP4xPP2(+MTP) launch with both tiers active (8/8 ranks report one-shot + DMA enabled, no init failures) - [x] Communicator is built for the TP group only (`world=4` under TP4xPP2, PP group untouched) - [x] GSM8K 0.900 / Invalid 0.000, greedy output matches baseline - [x] decode (bs 1/8/32), e2e 8K, 64K sweeps as above - [x] Gate off (default): unchanged NCCL behaviour ## Notes for reviewers - Requires `pip install b12x` (plus `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, pulled in as a wheel dependency; kernels are JIT-compiled on first use). - The DMA ring allocates a scratch slab sized by `SGLANG_B12X_DMA_MAX_BYTES` (default 256 MB); on memory-tight setups this competes with the KV pool, so raise `--mem-fraction-static` accordingly when enabling it together with speculative decoding. - `_FUSED_MAX_ROWS = 36` mirrors the current kernel limit and is duplicated in `communicator.py` as `_B12X_FUSED_MAX_ROWS`; happy to expose it from the package instead if maintainers prefer. - This is orthogonal to #30775 (PP x speculative decoding). Stacking both is what produces the 64K number above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32143670090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32143670090)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32143669597](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32143669597)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Scheduler] Cap prefill-delayer queue target by admission capacity
signal.text: ## Motivation The prefill-delayer queue trigger caps its accumulation target with `max_prefill_bs`, an observed high-watermark that can remain near one under trickle arrivals. This allows each request to immediately satisfy the trigger and keeps prefills fragmented. ## Modifications - Cap the queue target with the configured `prefill_max_requests`. - Fall back to the observed `max_prefill_bs` when no request limit is configured. - Update the server-argument documentation to describe the cap and fallback. ## Tests - `pytest -q test/registered/scheduler/test_prefill_delayer.py -k test_negotiate` — 1 passed. - OSS SGLang pre-commit hooks passed for all changed files. - Added a scheduler regression case covering a low observed watermark with a larger admission capacity. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable. This changes scheduling behavior without modifying model computations. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [formatting guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [testing guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to the [documentation guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide relevant speed benchmark results. - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32091007940](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091007940)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32091007742](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32091007742)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fix registered HiCache host pointer aliases
signal.text: ## Motivation Registered HiCache host allocations can have different CPU and GPU virtual addresses. This is observable on MI355X, where `hipDeviceAttributeCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is false. Passing the CPU VA to a custom kernel causes a GPU memory fault even though runtime copy APIs can still accept that address. The affected paths include AOT/JIT HiCache transfers, Mamba transfers, HiSparse copies, and host-pool pointer tables. CPU-side storage and disaggregation metadata must continue to expose the original CPU VA. ## Modifications - Add a target-device-aware `get_device_accessible_ptr` AOT API using `cudaHostGetDevicePointer` / `hipHostGetDevicePointer`. - Resolve direct registered-host tensor operands at AOT and JIT kernel launch boundaries while preserving the caller's current device. - Build CUDA/ROCm host-pool kernel pointer tables from device-accessible aliases for MHA, MLA, K-only, DSV4 paged/state, and DSA pools. - Keep raw CPU addresses for unregister, contiguous-buffer metadata, page metadata, and storage/disaggregation consumers. - Preserve unpinned, NPU, and MUSA pointer behavior. - Add registered-mmap regressions for pointer domains, AOT/JIT transfers, and CUDA graph capture/replay. ## Accuracy Tests ROCm 7.2 / MI355X (`gfx950`), Docker image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260813`: - Fresh ROCm AOT build: passed. - `test_hicache_page_first_write_back.py`: `15 passed`. - `test_transfer_mamba.py`: `16 passed`. - `test_hisparse.py`: `16 passed, 2 skipped`. - `test_mem_pool_host.py`: `9 passed`. - Registered-mmap post-rebase regressions: `3 passed`. - Native HIP runtime comparison: alias matches `hipHostGetDevicePointer`; wrong-device input is rejected; current device is restored. - Repository pre-commit hooks over the rebased PR diff: passed. CUDA validation in `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130` (compile-only because this host has no NVIDIA GPU): - HiCache, Mamba, and HiSparse JIT modules compiled and loaded for SM90. - Modified AOT `transfer.cu` and `common_extension.cc` translation units compiled for SM90. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not run. This is a correctness fix for registered-host pointer address domains; it does not change kernel bodies or transfer algorithms. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing documentation change required.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Correctness results above; no performance-sensitive algorithm change.) - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32092731671](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32092731671)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32092731528](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32092731528)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: route decode wo_a bf16 batched matmul to aiter batched_gemm_bf16
signal.text: # [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: route decode wo_a bf16 batched matmul to aiter `batched_gemm_bf16` ## Summary On the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm decode path, the MLA output-absorb (`wo_a`) bf16 GEMM runs `torch.einsum("tgd,grd->tgr", o, wo_a)`, which dispatches to a **rocBLAS/Tensile `Cijk_*` batched GEMM** — one of the larger kernels in the DSV4 decode attention region. aiter ships a tuned `batched_gemm_bf16` for exactly this shape, and the reference ATOM stack uses it for the same op. This PR routes the einsum to `batched_gemm_bf16` on gfx95, behind a new opt-in env flag, with an einsum fallback. **What this change is:** a 1:1 kernel replacement that aligns the sglang decode `wo_a` op with the kernel the reference stack uses. The trace confirms the replacement; in raw GPU time the aiter kernel is **at parity** with the Tensile kernel (see Validation). End-to-end this shows a **marginal (~2-3% total tok/s)** effect in repeated pure-TP runs — this is an ATOM-alignment / kernel-parity change, **not** a large throughput win. ## Motivation Attributing the DSV4 decode attention region kernel-by-kernel (torch-profiler External-id + enclosing python stack) shows the `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_*_MT16x16x1024` Tensile kernel is launched by `aten::bmm` from the `wo_a` bf16 einsum. The same logical op in the reference stack is aiter's `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel`. Routing sglang to that kernel matches the reference kernel choice for this op. ## What changed - `deepseek_v4.py`: new module helper `_apply_wo_a_bf16_matmul(o, wo_a, is_decode)`. Eligibility (opt-in flag `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, the global `SGLANG_USE_AITER` switch, HIP, and gfx95) is folded into `_wo_a_aiter_gemm_eligible(...)` and evaluated **once at module import** into `_wo_a_aiter_batched_gemm_enabled`; the aiter kernel is **pre-imported** into `_wo_a_batched_gemm_bf16` at import as well. This keeps the per-token decode critical path free of `EnvBool.get()` and function-local imports. - On the decode path, when enabled and not runtime-disabled, it calls aiter `batched_gemm_bf16` (`Y[i] = X[i] @ W[i]^T`): `XQ = o.transpose(0,1)` `[G,T,D]`, `WQ = wo_a` `[G,R,D]` -> `[G,T,R]` -> transpose back to `[T,G,R]`. Otherwise (prefill, any gate off, or after a failure) it uses the einsum. The `wo_a` else-branch calls this helper, passing `forward_batch.forward_mode.is_decode()`. - Restricted to **decode** — the kernel was benchmarked/validated for decode; prefill keeps the einsum. - Gated on the global `SGLANG_USE_AITER` switch, so the reroute cannot activate when aiter is disabled even if the opt-in flag is set. - **Two-stage fallback** — an import failure disables the reroute at module load (logged once); a kernel that imports but raises at runtime flips a process-global and falls back to the einsum for the rest of the process (logged once), instead of retrying/re-logging on every layer/token. - `environ.py`: new `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM = EnvBool(False)`. No behavior change unless the flag is set. CUDA, non-gfx95, and prefill paths are untouched. ## Validation (MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8) **Numerics** — model-free bit-check of `batched_gemm_bf16` vs the einsum across `T/G/D/R` shapes: max relative error <= 5e-4 (bf16 rounding; mostly exactly 0.0). The unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_wo_a_bf16.py` (registered on `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) exercises the aiter kernel on-device and covers static eligibility, dispatch/prefill gating, the runtime-failure fallback, and the numerics check. **Accuracy** — 5-shot GSM8K, 1319 questions, `--parallel 1319`, cuda-graph on: einsum (flag off) 0.952 / aiter (flag on) 0.946 — same 0.946-0.952 fp4-MoE run-to-run band, no regression. **Coherence** — server generates correctly with the flag on (`capital of France is` -> "Paris. The capital of Germany is Berlin."). **Kernel swap (trace-confirmed, same scope)** — total GPU time for all launches of the kernel in the profiled decode window, flag off vs on: - off: `Cijk_Alik_Bljk_*_MT16x16x1024` 2.04 ms x244 - on: `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel_*` 2.07 ms x244 (aiter); `Cijk` drops 248->4 launches So the kernel is replaced 1:1 (~8.4 us vs ~8.5 us per launch) — the aiter kernel is at **parity** in raw GPU time, marginally higher, within noise. The trace demonstrates *kernel replacement*, not a kernel-time reduction. **Profiling** Before After **Throughput** (DSV4-Pro fp4, MI355X, TP8, **pure-TP eager**, `random` ISL 512 / OSL 1024, N=4 reps/point, fixed seed; flag off (einsum) vs on (aiter)): Output tok/s (mean / p50 / pop-std): | conc | off (mean / p50 / std) | on (mean / p50 / std) | d mean | d p50 | |------|------------------------|-----------------------|--------|-------| | 4 | 36.0 / 36.0 / 0.00 | 36.0 / 36.0 / 0.00 | +0.00% | +0.00% | | 32 | 288.0 / 288.0 / 0.00 | 294.0 / 288.0 / 10.39 | +2.08% | +0.00% | | 64 | 576.0 / 576.0 / 0.00 | 576.0 / 576.0 / 0.00 | +0.00% | +0.00% | Total tok/s (mean / p50) — output tok/s is quantized to fixed steps in this harness and hides sub-step movement: | conc | off (mean / p50) | on (mean / p50) | d mean | d p50 | |------|------------------|-----------------|--------|-------| | 4 | 52.0 / 52.0 | 53.3 / 53.3 | +2.53% | +2.48% | | 32 | 416.7 / 417.0 | 425.5 / 426.0 | +2.12% | +2.16% | | 64 | 817.2 / 817.5 | 842.8 / 842.8 | +3.13% | +3.10% | Reading: on the quantized output-tok/s metric the off/on bands overlap at every concurrency (the lone conc=32 outlier is +2.08% mean but d p50 = 0 with std 10.4 — within run-to-run variance). On total tok/s there is a consistent, small **+2-3%**. Under DP-attention / high concurrency it is expected to be ~neutral (comm-bound). Honest framing: kernel-parity / ATOM-alignment change with a marginal (~2-3%) end-to-end effect, not a confirmed output-tok/s win. **DeepSeek-V4-Pro GPTQ** — not available in this environment, so not tested (documented as an environment limitation). The reroute is dtype-agnostic for correctness: `wo_a` is a bf16 batched matmul (`o` and `wo_a` are bf16 regardless of the MoE quant scheme), so the einsum-vs-aiter swap is numerically identical across fp4/GPTQ; the fp4 GSM8K accuracy plus the model-free bit-check cover the numerical contract. ## How to enable ``` SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 ``` Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` on gfx95 (MI355X). Applies to the decode path only. ## Checklist - [x] Numerically validated (bf16-equivalent vs einsum; on-device unit test) - [x] Coherent end-to-end on MI355X TP8 - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved - [x] Opt-in (default off); CUDA / non-gfx95 / prefill unchanged - [x] Flag + kernel cached at module import (no per-token `EnvBool.get()` / import) - [x] Repeated-run A/B (mean / p50 / std), reframed as kernel-parity + marginal effect --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #32097452107](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32097452107) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32097451926](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32097451926)

signal.title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up
signal.text: ## Summary This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up. Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before the new EP size is committed. The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged. ## Changes - Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the expanded world. - Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask. - Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture configuration before recapture. - Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all ranks before committing the scale operation. - Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path. - Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization path. ## Configuration Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings: ```text --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 ``` The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR. ## Known Limitations - Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph recapture are outside this PR. - Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph configuration and effective capture sizes. - Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the scale-finalization pause. - The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3. - Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture. - The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the base scale-up PR still apply. ## Test Plan The manual Elastic EP tests cover direct, single-rank, mixed-cohort, and repeated scale-up: - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To6CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To8CudaGraph` - `TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph` Each test captures decode batch sizes `1 2 4 8 16` and checks post-scale generation, routed joiner traffic, input logprobs, and GSM8K correctness. ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \ python -m pytest -v -s \ test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph::test_scale_up_on_demand ``` The repeated 4-to-5-to-6 and direct 4-to-6 validations passed with all five decode graph sizes captured on every participating rank. ## References - [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) - EPLB after scale-up - [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up - [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32138752782](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752782)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32138752466](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32138752466)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: Amd/dsv4 shared experts fusion top6
signal.text: # [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: fix shared-experts fusion for top-6 ## Summary Enabling shared-experts fusion (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) for DeepSeek-V4 on MI355X (gfx950) crashed at startup. Two independent issues in the fused topk / append path assume DeepSeek-V3 conventions (fp32 correction bias, power-of-two topk) that DeepSeek-V4 (bf16 correction bias, **top-6** routing) violates. This PR fixes both so the fused path runs, and shows it is a **~+8–11% output-throughput win at low concurrency with accuracy preserved**. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`** — in `biased_topk_jit_kernel_impl`, cast `correction_bias` to `float32` before calling `moe_fused_gate`. DeepSeek-V4 stores `e_score_correction_bias` in bf16 (for the aiter sqrtsoftplus topk path), but `moe_fused_gate` asserts a float32 bias (`AssertionError: bias must be float32`). Only the fused-gate branch (taken when `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`) is touched. - **`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`** — `_fused_append_shared_experts_kernel` indexed the routed/shared lanes with `tl.arange(0, K)` / `tl.arange(0, S)`, which Triton only accepts for power-of-two ranges. DeepSeek-V4 routes top-6 (`K=6`), so it failed with `ValueError: arange's range must be a power of 2`. The kernel now iterates over `next_power_of_2(K)` / `next_power_of_2(S)` blocks with masking, mirroring the existing `_fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights_kernel` sibling. Behavior is unchanged for power-of-two `K`. - **`test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py`** — new unit test covering non-power-of-two `K`/`S` (incl. the DSV4 `K=6` case) against a pure-torch golden reference. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`. Baseline = `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, Fusion = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`. ### Unit test ``` $ python3 -m pytest test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py -q 3 passed, 7 subtests passed ``` ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 2000 questions × 3 runs) | run | baseline | fusion | |----:|:--------:|:------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.943 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.937 | | 3 | 0.936 | 0.940 | | **avg** | **0.939** | **0.940** | Invalid ≈ 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy is preserved (within run-to-run noise). ### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput) | concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | fusion (tok/s) | Δ | |------------:|:----------------:|:--------------:|:-----:| | 1 | 69.59 | 77.06 | **+10.7%** | | 2 | 122.31 | 135.33 | **+10.6%** | | 4 | 216.26 | 238.91 | **+10.5%** | | 8 | 366.29 | 403.37 | **+10.1%** | | 16 | 569.47 | 613.60 | **+7.7%** | ### Commands used Server (per config; `$FLAG` = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` or `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`): ```bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend dsv4 --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 --max-running-requests 16 \ --context-length 10240 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 $FLAG ``` Accuracy: ```bash python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200 ``` Performance (per concurrency `C` in 1 2 4 8 16): ```bash python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos ``` ## Test plan / Checklist - [x] `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` no longer crashes for DeepSeek-V4 (top-6) on gfx950. - [x] New unit test `test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py` passes (non-pow2 K/S incl. K=6). - [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.940 vs 0.939). - [x] Output throughput improves ~+8–11% at concurrency 1–16 (TP4, 8k/1k). - [x] Power-of-two `K` behavior unchanged (regression guard in the unit test). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32142107014](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32142107014)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32142106609](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32142106609)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 destination offset overflow in CUTLASS MoE pre-reorder
signal.text: ## Motivation `pre_reorder_triton_kernel_for_cutlass_moe` loads `dst_idx` from the `src2dst` mapping as an `int32` and uses it to calculate the destination address: ```python dst_ptr_offs + dst_idx * hidden_size ``` Because `dst_idx` is 32-bit, `dst_idx * hidden_size` can overflow signed 32-bit arithmetic when the destination activation buffer contains more than `2**31` elements. For example, with `hidden_size = 6144`, the first overflowing destination row is: ```text ceil(2**31 / 6144) = 349,526 ``` This is reachable during large expert-parallel prefill workloads. The wrapped offset can cause a CUDA illegal memory access or write to an incorrect GPU address. ## Modifications Promote `dst_idx` to `tl.int64` immediately after loading it: ```python dst_idx = tl.load(token_src2dst_ptr + idx).to(tl.int64) ``` This ensures that the multiplication by `hidden_size` and the destination pointer offset are evaluated using 64-bit arithmetic. The `src2dst` mapping remains `int32`; only the address calculation is widened. ## Accuracy Tests The change only affects destination address arithmetic. Outputs below the signed 32-bit offset boundary remain unchanged. The overflow boundary can be validated with an FP8 destination buffer using: - `hidden_size = 6144` - `dst_idx = 349,526` - A destination element offset greater than `2**31` - One BF16 input row converted and written to the selected FP8 row Expected behavior: - Before the fix: CUDA illegal memory access or an incorrect destination write. - After the fix: the selected destination row matches the FP8-converted input row. Large-offset validation requires a CUDA GPU with enough memory for a contiguous allocation larger than 2 GiB. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. The change adds one scalar `int32`-to-`int64` conversion for each valid routed destination. It does not change the number of loads, stores, kernel launches, or transferred elements. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Documentation changes are not required for this internal kernel fix. - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32141555496](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32141555496) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32141554828](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32141554828)

signal.text: ### Summary Adds the native **ProductionDebtRadixCacheGate** and cryptographic **TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger** under `sglang/srt/mem_cache/production_debt.py`. ### Problem Solved As enterprise AI architects and Forward Deployed Engineers deploy high-throughput multi-turn agentic systems and reasoning workloads (e.g. DeepSeek R1, Chatbot Arena models) with SGLang across multi-GPU Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell (B200) clusters, engineering organizations require real-time controls over **Enterprise SGLang RadixCache & Chunked Prefill Production Debt & Technical Due Diligence**: 1. **RadixCache Debt Index (RDI <= 12.0)**: Scoring radix trie tree execution for orphaned trie node memory fragmentation, multi-GPU chunked prefill pipeline stalls, structured decoding regex token mask overhead, and trie lookup/eviction latency degradation. 2. **Trie Tree Memory Sprawl Multiplier (TTMM <= 1.08x)**: Monitoring peak utilized prefix cache memory against physical HBM limits to eliminate LRU eviction thrashing. 3. **P99 Trie Lookup & Eviction Latency Ceiling (<= 2.8ms)**: Enforcing sub-millisecond prefix hit traversal and block allocation boundaries across continuous batching loops. 4. **Deterministic Mutation Boundaries**: Enforcing `never_equate_intent_to_approval` across state-mutating trie node splittings, parent-child link mutations, and structured grammar token masks. 5. **Cryptographic Technical Due Diligence Action Ledger**: Emitting immutable, SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL receipts providing audit-ready evidence for VC/PE Technical Due Diligence, M&A evaluations, and enterprise production readiness reviews. ### Features Added - `sglang.srt.mem_cache.production_debt.TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger`: - `record_radix_event()`: Cryptographically links each trie tree allocation and prefix eviction event into an immutable SHA-256 chain. - `verify_ledger_integrity()`: Validates hash-chain continuity. ### Testing & Validation - Added `test/srt/test_radix_debt.py` with 3 automated unit tests validating clean RadixCache trie tree operations, degraded memory fragmentation failure detection, and cryptographic ledger integrity (3/3 tests passing). ### Upstream & Commercial Context Maintained by [A2Z SOC](https://a2zsoc.com) for AI Forward Deployed Engineering, SGLang RadixCache Hardening, and Technical Due Diligence. signal.title: [VLM] Add video input support for Kimi-K3
signal.text: ## Motivation Kimi-K3 has a temporal MoonViT3d vision stack, but its SGLang multimodal processor currently handles still images only. Although the OpenAI-compatible protocol can carry `video_url` content, Kimi-K3 requests cannot route decoded video frames through the checkpoint's media processor and vision tower. This adds video input support for Kimi-K3 while preserving the existing image path. Video frames are processed; audio tracks are not. The implementation targets the current Kimi multimodal pipeline. This is related to the earlier Kimi-K2.5 attempt in #21023, which was closed after that older processor pipeline was replaced. ## Modifications - accept Kimi-K3 `video_url` inputs from server-accessible URLs, local paths, and Base64 data URLs - sample frames with the checkpoint media configuration and split them into timestamped temporal chunks for MoonViT3d - preserve mixed image/video ordering and enforce one-to-one visual placeholder mapping - reuse the Kimi image placeholder token while carrying temporal `grid_thw` metadata through preprocessing and model execution - map image grids globally for encoder-DP execution - keep image artifact caching unchanged; video requests intentionally use the uncached path - expose video token usage in non-streaming Chat Completions responses - document video request examples and the no-audio limitation - add focused OpenAI protocol, processor, model, and DP regression tests ## Accuracy Tests Unit tests: ```text pytest test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_chat.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k25.py \ test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_vision.py 162 passed ``` Real-model smoke tests used Kimi-K3 with TP8 on one 8x NVIDIA B300 node: - video URL, local path, and Base64 data URL inputs - mixed image/video input ordering - Chat Completions streaming - Responses API - image-only regression A 5.16 MB MP4 produced HTTP 200 and correctly identified one restaurant scene with roughly six people dining and conversing. The request used 43,969 prompt tokens, including 43,200 visual tokens. An extracted 49.4 KB frame produced HTTP 200 and correctly described the two foreground diners. The request used 1,282 prompt tokens, including 1,170 image tokens. ## Speed Tests and Profiling There is no before/after video latency comparison because Kimi-K3 video requests were unsupported before this change. Cold end-to-end measurements on the TP8 B300 deployment, with `reasoning_effort=low`, `max_tokens=256`, and no cached prompt tokens: | Input | End-to-end latency | Completion tokens | |---|---:|---:| | 5.16 MB MP4 | 6.361 s | 115 | | 49.4 KB image | 1.343 s | 127 | The text path is unchanged. The existing image artifact-cache path remains active for image-only requests; videos bypass it because the cache currently stores image artifacts only. ## Limitations - video audio tracks are not processed - separate audio input is not added by this PR - video preprocessing intentionally bypasses the image artifact cache ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32139310022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139310022)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32139309596](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32139309596)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->
