signal.title: [AMD] Add ROCm 7.15 (gfx942 / gfx950) stages to the ROCm Dockerfile
signal.text: ## Motivation ROCm 7.15 publishes no `rocm/pytorch` base image, so its stack has to be assembled from AMD's ROCm pip channels on top of `ubuntu:24.04`. That places the SDK in `site-packages` instead of `/opt/rocm`, which the existing ROCm 7.0 / 7.2 stages of `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` assume throughout. This PR adds gfx942 and gfx950 ROCm 7.15 stages built that way, plus the adjustments the pip-SDK layout forces on the existing build and CI steps. The SDK pin is a nightly (`7.15.0a20260712`) because 7.15 never had a stable release: the line ran from `7.15.0a20260626` to `7.15.0a20260728` and was then renumbered 10.0. This specific build is the one the gfx1250 7.15 image also pins, so all three arches share a single 7.15 SDK. Note for sequencing with #32754 (`[AMD] Enable gfx1250 Support`): that PR adds its own copy of a 7.15 pip-SDK stage, which could instead reuse the shared `rocm715-base` stage introduced here. Both PRs also introduce the same `rocm_legacy` / `rocm_rock` extras in `python/pyproject_other.toml`. Whichever lands second will need to be reconciled against the first. ## Modifications ### `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` - Added a shared `rocm715-base` stage: `ubuntu:24.04` + Python 3.12 in a venv + the ROCm 7.15 pip stack — `rocm[libraries,devel,device-gfx942,device-gfx950]==7.15.0a20260712`, `torch==2.11.0`, `torchvision==0.26.0`, `triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6`, from the ROCm nightlies and devreleases indexes. - Added two thin per-arch stages, `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15`, which only set build flags (`BUILD_VLLM`, `BUILD_TRITON`, `BUILD_LLVM`, `BUILD_AITER_ALL`, `BUILD_MOONCAKE`, `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT`). Both arches' torch device wheels go into the shared base; `GPU_ARCH_LIST` still narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for. - torch and torchvision device wheels are named as separate specs rather than combined device extras. Several device extras in one spec (`torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]`) silently installs only the first, and the missing arch then fails at runtime with `hipErrorInvalidImage`. - Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.14: `st_attn==0.0.7`, `vsa==0.0.4`, `petit_kernel==0.0.2` and `wave-lang==3.8.2` publish wheels only up to cp313 and no sdist, so on 3.14 pip has no candidate at all for `srt_hip`. - Path fixups for the non-`/opt/rocm` SDK: `ROCM_HOME` / `ROCM_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` / `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` point at the site-packages `_rocm_sdk_devel` tree; a `/opt/rocm` symlink because AITER shells out to `/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/amdgpu-arch` to pick `DEFAULT_GPU_ARCH` and the rest of this Dockerfile refers to `/opt/rocm`; and a `/usr/lib64/libc.so` symlink because the SDK's `hsakmtTargets.cmake` hardcodes that path from its own build host. - libdrm: skip the apt install for `*rocm7_15*`, since libdrm ships with the pip SDK. - amdsmi: install it for `*rocm7_15*` (same branch as 7.2), since the pip SDK does not pre-install it. - MORI: point the build at the SDK's vendored `lib/rocm_sysdeps` tree via `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` / `CPATH` / `LIBRARY_PATH` plus an `ldconfig` entry, for NUMA (`hsakmt-config.cmake` calls `find_dependency(NUMA)`) and libdrm (`rocm_smi.h` includes `<libdrm/drm.h>`, `mori_application` links `-ldrm`/`-ldrm_amdgpu`). Guarded on the directory existing, so the apt-based ROCm 7.x images keep their current behaviour. - nixl: remove `libabsl-dev` before configuring, because nixl's meson wants an abseil providing `absl_log` and refuses its bundled subproject while Ubuntu 24.04's older `libabsl-dev` (20220623) is visible. Only `-dev` packages are removed; `libabsl20220623t64` stays so the Mooncake binaries built earlier keep the shared library they linked against. - Second commit: removing `libabsl-dev` also removes `libgrpc-dev` and `libgrpc++-dev`, which depend on it, so all three are reinstalled once nixl is built. The image's own MORI is built before this point and is fine, but the CI install script rebuilds MORI inside the image, and without `libgrpc++-dev` that rebuild configures without gRPC and silently drops symbols the Python side imports — `mori.umbp` then fails on `CacheRemoteAdmission` and `test_umbp_store` errors out. - The SGLang install now selects a `compressed-tensors` extra: `rocm_rock` for `*rocm7_15*`, `rocm_legacy` otherwise. ### `python/pyproject_other.toml` - Moved `compressed-tensors` out of `srt_hip` into two new mutually exclusive extras, `rocm_legacy = ["compressed-tensors==0.15.0"]` and `rocm_rock = ["compressed-tensors==0.16.0"]`. 0.15.0 requires `torch<2.11` and 0.16.0 requires `torch>=2.10`, so the correct pin depends on which torch the ROCm SDK generation ships rather than on the platform. Pinning the wrong one leaves pip trying to replace the image's ROCm torch with a PyPI build, which it cannot do, and the resolve then fails. Neither extra is pulled automatically — the Dockerfile and the CI install script append one. ### `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` - Detect the ROCm version inside the CI container and append the matching `compressed-tensors` extra (`rocm_rock` for >= 7.15.0, else `rocm_legacy`) to `EXTRAS`. - Apply the same `rocm_sysdeps` handling to the in-image MORI rebuild, kept scoped to that build instead of exported image-wide because `rocm_sysdeps/include` also carries `zlib.h` / `expat.h` / `elf.h`, which would shadow the system headers for every other component. - Keep ROCm 7.15's own Triton (`INSTALL_AITER_TRITON=false` for HIP `7.15*`, matching `BUILD_TRITON=0` on the new stages). AITER's `install_triton.sh` resolves its wheel index from `dpkg -l rocm-core`, which does not exist for a pip-installed SDK, so it would fall back to the ROCm 7.2 index and drop a 7.2-built Triton into a 7.15 image. Verified in the built image that `dpkg-query` finds no `rocm-core` and that `torch.version.hip` reports `7.15.0`. ### `.github/workflows/release-docker-amd-rocm7_15-nightly.yml` - Added `gfx942-rocm7_15` and `gfx950-rocm7_15` to the build matrix, and replaced the single-arch `if` with a `case` mapping them to the `rocm7.15-mi30x` and `rocm7.15-mi35x` tags. - Build args: dropped `GPU_ARCH_LIST_ARG` and `SGLANG_VERSION`, neither of which this Dockerfile consumes, and pass `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION`, which is what the SGLang install actually reads. ## Accuracy Tests All of the following was run on an MI300X host (gfx942). - `gfx942-rocm7_15` builds end to end (46GB image). - In-image smoke test: torch `2.11.0+rocm7.15.0a20260712`, `torch.version.hip` `7.15.0`, `gcnArchName` `gfx942:sramecc+:xnack-`, a bf16 matmul on device returns finite values, and `aiter`, `mori`, `tilelang`, `nixl`, `amdsmi` and `sglang` all import. - The real CI flow was run against the image: `scripts/ci/amd/amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` exits 0, and `test/run_suite.py --hw amd --suite stage-a-test-1-gpu-small-amd` reports **6/8 passed**. That matches a ROCm 10 image baseline run on the same host on 2026-08-17, which was also 6/8. The two failures are `test_basic_sanity.py` and `test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, both `huggingface_hub.errors.GatedRepoError: 401` on `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` because this host has no `HF_TOKEN` — identical to the baseline and unrelated to this change. - Known gap: the `gfx950-rocm7_15` stage has **not** been built or run. It shares `rocm715-base` with gfx942 and differs only in the AITER / sgl-kernel compile targets, but it is unverified. The host is MI300X, so gfx950 runtime tests were not possible here. ## Speed Tests and Profiling <!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. --> ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #32132588829](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588829)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32132588628](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132588628)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Model] Add Boogu-Image base T2I support
signal.text:
## Motivation Add sglang inference support for **Boogu-Image** ([boogu-project/Boogu-Image](https://github.com/boogu-project/Boogu-Image)). The base model is a 10 B DiT (40 layers = 8 double-stream + 32 single-stream, plus 3 refiner groups), conditioned on Qwen3-VL-8B instruction features, decoded via the FLUX.1-dev `AutoencoderKL`. It ships with a bespoke ascending-time flow-match Euler scheduler that has no direct diffusers equivalent, so this PR wires everything needed to run it end-to-end. Scope of this PR: **base T2I only**. Edit / reference-image, Turbo, and the instruct-reasoner variants are intentionally out of scope and will follow separately. ## Modifications - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — DiT: `BooguRMSNormZero` / `BooguLayerNormContinuous`, double-stream + single-stream blocks, 3-axis 3D RoPE (`text / ref-image / noise`) with per-sample windows via `BooguRopeBundle` (msgspec.Struct). Batch is folded into the token dim before rotary so sglang's Triton kernel receives 2D `[num_tokens, head_dim//2]` cos/sin; padded rows use the identity rotation (`cos=1, sin=0`) to match upstream `position_ids=0` semantics. 4D↔5D squeeze at the `ImagePipelineConfig` boundary since Boogu is image-only. - `runtime/models/schedulers/scheduling_boogu_flow_match.py` — flow-match Euler on an **ascending** time axis (`t: 0 → 1`, `prev = sample + (t_next − t) · v`), fundamentally different from `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler`. Ports the upstream v1 logistic shift (`mu = lin(seq_len)` with `x1=256, y1=0.5, x2=4096, y2=1.15`) and v2 shift (`t / (m − mt + t)` with `m = sqrt(seq_len)/120`). - `configs/pipeline_configs/boogu_image.py` — `BooguImagePipelineConfig`. Chat template routes empty instruction → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DROP`, non-empty → `SYSTEM_PROMPT_4_T2I` (upstream `system_prompt_follows_task_type=False`, no images). Postprocess reads `.last_hidden_state` (norm-applied); `BooguTextEncodingStage` overrides `_forward_text_encoder` to call `text_encoder.model(...)` because the outer `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward` returns a causal-LM output without `last_hidden_state`. `BooguQwen3VLArchConfig` mirrors the `PretrainedConfig` defaults (`output_attentions=False` etc.) that the HF Qwen3-VL `config.json` doesn't ship. - `runtime/pipelines/boogu_image_pipeline.py` — `_load_config` remaps the on-disk `mllm` / `processor` slots to `text_encoder` / `tokenizer` (via `component_paths` redirect) and relabels the non-diffusers `transformer_boogu` / `scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete_time_shifting` module strings so the loader library-string assertions pass (`ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls` keys on the class name). - `configs/models/vaes/boogu_image.py` — subclass of `StableDiffusion3VAEArchConfig` (the SD3 arch config *is* the diffusers `AutoencoderKL`), with FLUX.1-dev's `scaling_factor=0.3611`, `shift_factor=0.1159`. - `configs/models/dits/boogu_image.py`, `configs/sample/boogu_image.py` — DiT and sampling defaults (50 steps, guidance 4.0, 1024²). - `configs/models/fsdp.py`, `registry.py` — `is_boogu_image_layer` FSDP predicate; register `BooguImagePipelineConfig` / `BooguImageSamplingParams` behind a `"boogu-image"` path detector. - `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/text_encoding.py` — **the only shared-path change in this PR.** `align_negative_batch_dim` was applied to both negative embeddings and negative masks, but its 2-D branch is only valid for embeddings: a 2-D *embedding* is `(seq, dim)` with no batch axis, so it must gain one (`unsqueeze(0).repeat(B, 1, 1)` — the Z-Image single-prompt case the branch was written for), whereas a 2-D *mask* is already `(batch, seq)` and must be broadcast in place. Conflating them turned a `[1, S_neg]` mask into `[B, 1, S_neg]`, so any consumer reducing over the sequence dim gets a list of lists instead of one length per request — for Boogu that is an HTTP 500 out of the RoPE builder for every dynamically-batched request (`TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "int") to list`). At batch 1 the broadcast is a no-op (`target_batch == 1` returns the tensor unchanged), which is why the one-shot `generate` path never surfaced it. The helper now takes a kw-only `batchless_2d` flag; both mask call sites pass `batchless_2d=False`. - `runtime/models/dits/boogu_image.py` — `@torch.compiler.disable` on `BooguRopeEmbedder.forward`, which is what makes `--enable-torch-compile` usable for this model. Dynamo's polyfill calls `cls.__new__(cls, *args)` and msgspec's C-level `__new__` rejects it, so compiling the DiT raised from the RoPE embedder's `BooguRopeBundle` return value. Position ids depend only on sequence lengths and image sizes, never on the latents, and the call is ~0.5 ms, so keeping it out of the graph costs nothing and lets the remaining 40 layers compile. - `test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py` — new. A shared `[1, seq]` negative mask stays 2-D when broadcast to a batch (and still reduces to one length per request); a 2-D `(seq, dim)` embedding still gains a batch axis; batch 1 is unchanged. Follows [`no-getattr-defensive`](.claude/rules/no-getattr-defensive.md), [`no-dataclasses`](.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md) (new containers are `msgspec.Struct`; config classes are grandfathered `@dataclass`), [`general-code-style`](.claude/rules/general-code-style.md). ## Accuracy Tests - Scheduler: bit-identical to upstream across `static-v1` / `dynamic-v1` / `dynamic-v2` / `do_shift=False` × steps ∈ {50, 40, 28}, and `step()` integration over 40 steps (max delta `0.0`). - Weight loading: 942 checkpoint keys → 888 model params, 0 missing / 0 unexpected / 0 shape mismatch. - Single-GPU T2I end-to-end (1024×1024, guidance 4.0, seed 0): output image aligns with the reference `inference_simple.py` prompt (elderly scavenger + trash can + red traffic light + Leica street-photography aesthetic). - Unit tests: `pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_text_encoding_negative_batch.py -q` → **3 passed**. Shared negative-conditioning / CFG paths re-run to confirm no other model regressed (`test_text_encoding_cache.py`, `test_cfg_gating.py`, `test_sampling_params.py`, plus the new file) → **36 passed, 8 subtests passed**. - Server end-to-end: the benchmark below produced 10 images (1 warmup + 3 sequential + 2 concurrent + 4 concurrent) with zero exceptions in the server log, at scheduler-reported batch sizes 1 / 2 / 4. - The `text_encoding.py` fix is shape-only and a no-op at batch 1, so single-request output is unchanged by construction; the batched shapes are locked by the new unit tests. `@torch.compiler.disable` keeps the RoPE builder in eager rather than altering it, so it does not move numerics either. - 50-step parity vs the upstream diffusers reference (same `seed=42`, cyberpunk prompt / gallery row 1): injecting byte-identical initial noise **and** conditioning into both stacks leaves the initial latent bit-identical (max abs diff `0.0`) and the step-1 latent within **0.53%** rel-L2 (cosine `0.99997`) — a single denoise step is numerically equivalent across backends. Over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 this compounds to step-50 latent rel-L2 ≈ 72% and final-image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40 (see the Qualitative Comparison section), i.e. benign last-bit bf16 kernel drift (FlashInfer/fused vs SDPA), not a structural difference. ## Qualitative Comparison (upstream diffusers vs sglang native) Same weights, `seed=42`, 1024×1024, 50 steps, `guidance_scale=4.0`. Images are width-limited to 320px; click any cell to view full 1024×1024. | Prompt | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | |---|---|---| | A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon reflections on wet streets | | | | A cute orange tabby kitten sitting in a field of sunflowers, golden hour lighting, photorealistic | | | | A serene Japanese garden with a red maple tree, koi pond and stone lantern in autumn | | | | A steaming bowl of ramen with a soft-boiled egg and chopsticks, close-up food photography | | | | An astronaut riding a horse on Mars, dramatic cinematic lighting | | |
Parity note (same-seed divergence is expected, not a bug) Feeding byte-identical initial noise **and** identical conditioning embeddings into both stacks: step-1 latent rel-L2 = 0.53% (cosine 0.99997), step-50 = 72%, final image PSNR 12.3 dB / SSIM 0.40. A single denoise step is numerically equivalent between the two backends; the divergence is compounding bf16 kernel drift amplified over 50 CFG steps at guidance 4.0 — a different-but-valid sample from the same distribution, not a structural difference.
## Speed Tests and Profiling H20 (95.6 GiB), bf16, `Boogu-Image-0.1-Base` (10.29B DiT, 40 layers), `guidance_scale=4.0`, `seed=42`, fixed prompt set. Sections 1–3 are 1024²/50 steps with the upstream diffusers pipeline as reference (identical weights, sglang on GPU 2, diffusers on GPU 0); section 4 uses vllm-omni's published 512²/28-step config. The native-backend gate was verified on every sglang run (no `diffusers backend` / `Loaded diffusers pipeline` in any log). Shared env: `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`.
Commands sglang one-shot and server. `serve` opens its HTTP port *before* warmup runs (`/health` answers 200 while the GPU is still warming), so readiness is gated on the `fired up and ready to roll` log line: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main generate \ --backend=sglang --model-path $MODEL --prompt "$PROMPT" \ --width 1024 --height 1024 --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4.0 \ --seed 42 --save-output --warmup --dit-cpu-offload false \ --perf-dump-path outputs/diffusion_benchmarks/$LABEL.json \ [--enable-torch-compile] [--enable-cfg-parallel] python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31000 \ --batching-max-size 4 --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false curl -x '' -s http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1/images/generations \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"'"$PROMPT"'","width":1024,"height":1024, "num_inference_steps":50,"guidance_scale":4.0,"seed":42,"n":1}' ``` Upstream diffusers reference. `device=cuda:0` must be exported *before* importing `boogu` — it gates upstream's own fused RMSNorm and fused SwiGLU, so leaving it unset understates the reference. One 50-step warmup pass is discarded: ```python import os; os.environ["device"] = "cuda:0" # before the boogu import import torch from boogu.pipelines.boogu.pipeline_boogu import BooguImagePipeline pipe = BooguImagePipeline.from_pretrained(MODEL, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).to("cuda:0") # str -> batch 1; list -> batch_size = len(list) (pipeline_boogu.py:2743) pipe(instruction=PROMPT, negative_instruction="", height=1024, width=1024, max_input_image_pixels=1024 * 1024, max_input_image_side_length=2048, num_inference_steps=50, text_guidance_scale=4.0, generator=torch.Generator("cuda:0").manual_seed(42)) ``` Section 4, sglang side — the in-tree benchmark client, one server lifetime per config. With `--enable-torch-compile` *and* `--batching-max-size > 1` the sweep runs twice and only the second, compile-warm pass is reported; see the section 4 caveats for why `--warmup-requests` cannot cover it: ```bash python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.entrypoints.cli.main serve \ --model-path $MODEL --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 \ --batching-max-size {1,4} --batching-delay-ms 100 \ --enable-batching-metrics --dit-cpu-offload false --enable-torch-compile true for conc in 1 2 4; do python python/sglang/multimodal_gen/benchmarks/bench_serving.py \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31011 --dataset random --task text-to-image \ --width 512 --height 512 --num-inference-steps 28 \ --num-prompts 10 --max-concurrency $conc --warmup-requests 4 \ --disable-tqdm --output-file c$conc.json done ``` vllm-omni side (their own harness and config, model repointed at our local checkpoint, baseline assertion replaced by `skip-performance-assertion`): ```bash python -m pytest tests/dfx/perf/scripts/run_diffusion_benchmark.py \ --test-config-file tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_h20_local.json -s -v ```
### 1. Optimization stack vs upstream diffusers, one-shot latency The diffusers reference is repeated per row so each sglang config is compared to the closest diffusers configuration — 68.65 s eager (its own fused RMSNorm / SwiGLU / FA on) for the non-compile rows, 66.51 s (+ `torch.compile`) for the compile rows. Head-dim padding and CFG parallel have no equivalent there. | config | diffusers (upstream) | sglang (native) | sglang speedup | sglang vs diffusers | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | eager, 1 GPU | 68.65 | 69.49 | 1.00× | 0.99× | | + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | 59.87 | **1.16×** | **1.11×** | | + head-dim padded to FA bucket, eager | 68.65 | 64.67 | **1.07×** | **1.06×** | | + head-dim padded + `--enable-torch-compile` | 66.51 | **54.54** | **1.27×** | **1.22×** | | + `--enable-cfg-parallel`, 2 GPU | 68.65 | 34.79 | **2.00×** | **1.97×** | | + CFG parallel ×2 + compile | 66.51 | **29.93** | **2.32×** | **2.22×** | - Eager baselines agree within 1.2%, so the ports are at parity before any lever. - `torch.compile` buys diffusers only 3.1% (68.65 → 66.51, fast paths already on) but 1.16× here — and is reachable only via the `@torch.compiler.disable` change in this PR. Compile × CFG-parallel stacks cleanly: 2.01 × 1.16 = 2.33 predicted vs 2.336× measured. - Best single-GPU 54.54 s is **1.22×** diffusers' own best; CFG-parallel ×2 + compile 29.93 s is **2.22×**. - Head-dim padding routes Boogu's head_dim=120 through FlashAttention by zero-padding Q/K/V to 128 (softmax_scale pinned to 1/√120) and slicing back — the trick `sana_wm_components._sana_wm_sdpa` already uses for head_dim=112. Kernel test matches SDPA within bf16 noise (rel-L2 = 3.9 × 10⁻⁵). The two padding rows were re-measured as a four-cell A/B on one commit, the only variable being `_padded_head_dim` (128 vs `self.head_dim`, which makes the selector reject FA at head size 120 and fall back to `torch_sdpa` — confirmed per cell from the `Attention backends for transformer` log line); all four cells reproduce the table within 0.21%. The gain is resolution-dependent: attention is 22.5% of DiT GPU time at 1024²'s 4352 joint tokens but roughly a third of that at 512²'s 1280, since attention FLOPs grow as S² and the linear layers as S, so the same A/B at 512² returns only +0.27% (section 4). ### 2. Server mode with dynamic batching Warmup is `server warmup req (1024x1024, 2/50 steps)` = 6.12 s, then `fired up and ready to roll` — 210 s from launch. Batch sizes are the scheduler's own `Dynamic batch dispatch` metric, not the request count. Compile rows are compile-warm (first request at a new batch dim recompiles: 315 s at batch 2). SDPA eager (= section 1's `eager, 1 GPU`): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 70.48 / 70.00 / 70.77 → median **70.48** | 70.48 | 0.0142 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 137.01 / 137.01 | 137.02 | 0.0146 | 1.03× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 271.18 ×4 | 271.19 | 0.0148 | 1.04× | Padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` (= section 1's best single-GPU row): | concurrency | scheduler dispatch | per-request latency (s) | wall (s) | img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `size=1/4 delay` | 55.44 / 55.15 / 55.15 → median **55.15** | 55.44 | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | `size=2/4 delay` | 110.51 / 110.51 | 110.52 | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | `size=4/4 config_cap:4` | 218.16 ×4 | 218.17 | 0.0183 | 1.01× | Serving overhead is small — 70.48 s through HTTP + ZMQ + scheduler vs 69.49 s one-shot, **+1.4%**. Padded FA + compile is **1.28× / 1.24× / 1.24×** faster per request at concurrency 1 / 2 / 4, matching section 1's 1.27×. ### 3. Batching headroom at this resolution, vs diffusers | batch | diffusers ms/forward | diffusers img/s | vs 1 | sglang (SDPA) img/s | vs 1 | sglang (padded FA + compile) img/s | vs 1 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 683.3 | 0.0146 | 1.000× | 0.0142 | 1.000× | 0.0181 | 1.000× | | 2 | 1331.9 (1.95×) | 0.0150 | 1.027× | 0.0146 | 1.03× | 0.0181 | 1.00× | | 4 | 2617.5 (3.83×) | 0.0152 | 1.046× | 0.0148 | 1.04× | 0.0183 | 1.01× | diffusers' per-forward scales 1.00 / 1.95 / 3.83 — essentially linear — so one 1024² image (4096 image + 256 instruction = 4352 joint tokens) already saturates the H20 and batching is worth ~1–4% for any implementation. All three curves agreeing on the flat shape is the result: this PR makes batching *correct*, and section 1's multi-GPU path is where throughput comes from. Peak memory, per engine: sglang 29 950 / 34 558 / 44 794 MB (server's own `Peak memory usage`), diffusers 36.91 / 38.54 / 42.54 GiB (`torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated`). ### 4. Cross-engine check against vllm-omni, on the same GPU vllm-omni [PR #4995](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/4995) ports the same model, but on different hardware, so its published numbers support no claim about either implementation. Their stack was installed (own uv venv, `vllm 0.26.0` + vllm-omni at upstream main `67c54777`, torch 2.11.0+cu130) and **their harness and their published config were run on the same H20, GPU 1** — the card our own sweep used. That config is `tests/dfx/perf/tests/test_boogu_image_vllm_omni.json` (512×512, 28 steps, 10 prompts, `max-concurrency` 1/2/4, 4 warmup requests at concurrency 4, negative prompt on, guidance 4.0 with CFG on), **not** the 1024² command in their PR body. Their pipeline profiler costs 0.5–1.0%, so their profiler-off numbers are quoted. 30/30 requests succeeded per run. Medians are used throughout: at 10 prompts / concurrency 4 the run is only 2.5 waves, so the partly-empty first wave biases every mean, while medians match Little's Law within 0.15%. Each engine at its own best. Both harnesses share a client lineage and emit the same fields (`throughput_qps`, `latency_median`), so the rows line up directly: latency is the median of 10 requests at concurrency 1, throughput the best over concurrency 1 / 2 / 4. | engine | best config | per-image latency (s) | throughput (img/s) | |---|---|---:|---:| | vllm-omni | compile on by default; request batching unavailable | 8.502 | 0.1192 | | sglang (this PR) | padded FA + `--enable-torch-compile` | **8.259** | **0.1341** | | ratio (sglang / vllm-omni) | | **1.029×** | **1.125×** | The two sglang figures come from different `--batching-max-size` values — 8.259 s at `maxb 1`, 0.1341 img/s at `maxb 4` — because batching trades 0.115 s of single-image latency (the `--batching-delay-ms 100` window, with nothing to merge at concurrency 1) for +10.7% throughput at concurrency 4. Run `maxb 4` when loaded, `maxb 1` when latency-bound. - **They compile the DiT by default** (`Regional compilation applied to 42 module(s) for repeated blocks [...]`, no flag); our defaults are eager and `batching_max_size = 1` (`server_args.py:355`). Default vs default **we lose 11.6%**, and only this PR unblocks the flip — worth 1.16× here, the same as section 1's 1024² figure. Compile vs compile with batching off the two engines are within 1.6%: the denoising loops are at parity, and the gap above comes from the levers around them. - **Their concurrency curve is flat for a structural reason, not a batching result.** `pipeline_boogu_image.py:201` sets `supports_request_batch = False`; `diffusion_engine.py:205` raises `ValueError` for any `max_num_seqs > 1`; the alternative `--step-execution` path needs `prepare_encode()` / `denoise_step()` / `step_scheduler()` / `post_decode()`, none of which their pipeline implements. Their log confirms `max_num_seqs=1 max_wait_ms=0.0`, `batch_size=1`. Per-pipeline gap, not an engine limit: `qwen_image`, `sd3`, `flux`, `ltx2` all set `supports_request_batch = True`. - **Head-dim padding is nearly free at this resolution** — +0.27% against +7.5% / +9.7% at 1024² in section 1. A 1280-token joint sequence spends far less of its time in attention than a 4352-token one. | lever | sglang (this PR) | vllm-omni Boogu | upstream diffusers | |---|---|---|---| | `torch.compile` on the DiT | 1.16× at both resolutions, unblocked here | on by default | 1.03× | | request batching | +10.7% qps at concurrency 4 | unavailable | +4.6% at batch 4 | | CFG parallel, 2 GPU | **2.00×** | unavailable | unavailable | | stacked | **2.32×** | — | — | Caveats: single run per point. For the `maxb 4` figure the sweep was run twice against one server and the second, compile-warm pass reported — with `--enable-torch-compile` the first request at a previously unseen batch dim recompiles inside the measured window, so cold pass 1 at concurrency 2 reads qps 0.0560 with p99 116.4 s against a 15.51 s median. Their harness posts t2i to `/v1/chat/completions` while `bench_serving.py` posts `/v1/images/generations` (each engine's documented path). All four GPUs carried an external tenant at ~80% utilization throughout, applying to both engines equally — the point of measuring on one box. ## Follow-up work (not in this PR) Called out so reviewers know the current boundary; these will land separately: - **Sequence parallelism (Ulysses/SP).** `--ulysses-degree 2` does not yet work for this model — the latent `rearrange` is over 5 dims and the 7 KV heads do not divide by the SP degree, so it needs a `shard_latents_for_sp` override in `base.py` and a fix to the head-count assert at `usp.py:263`. CFG parallelism in section 1 is unaffected and is the multi-GPU path that works today. - **Cache-DiT (step-layer caching, ~1.5–2× lossy).** Boogu is not yet registered in `_CUSTOM_BLOCK_ADAPTER_SPECS`; the adapter carries a single block-list attribute while Boogu has two (`double_stream_layers` = 8, `single_stream_layers` = 32), so registration has to handle both. Gated on a PSNR/SSIM check since it is lossy. - **Warm up serving benchmarks at the real step count.** `bench_serving.py:591` pins warmup requests to `num_inference_steps=1` because the server overrides them anyway (`warmup_request_builder.py:394` → `Req.set_as_warmup`), and issues them serially — so warmup pre-warms neither the real denoise shape nor a batch dim, and under `--enable-torch-compile` with `--batching-max-size > 1` the first request at each new batch dim recompiles inside the measured window. vllm-omni's harness avoids this by warming at `warmup-num-inference-steps=28, warmup-concurrency=4`. Section 4 works around it by reporting the second of two passes; the fix is to let warmup requests carry the benchmark's step count and concurrency. - **I2I / edit and reference-image** (and Turbo / instruct-reasoner), per the scope note in Motivation. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30752695530](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695530) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30752695446](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30752695446) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32132256761](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132256761) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32132256539](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32132256539)

signal.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8 DSpark forced-reject is not lossless: accumulated GDN state drift vs Base decode
signal.text: ### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug Summary With RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark, I can reproduce a deterministic correctness divergence between ordinary Base decode and DSpark TARGET_VERIFY even when every speculative draft token is deliberately rejected and only the target model's own argmax token is committed. The failure is cumulative rather than context-local: Base decode is deterministic across independent processes with a fixed seed. Under gamma=1 forced rejection, DSpark initially matches Base but later diverges. Rebuilding the same prefix through normal prefill restores the correct Base result at the divergence context. Using FP32 Mamba/SSM persistent state delays the divergence substantially, but does not eliminate it. This suggests accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift somewhere in the TARGET_VERIFY / intermediate-state / commit path. Possibly related to the state-correctness work tracked in #34899 and #34297. Environment SGLang: SGLANG_BUILD_COMMIT=c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5 SGLANG_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260814-c4271c3f CUDA 13.0 TP=1 attention backend=triton linear attention backend=triton Target model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 revision: 52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854 Draft model: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark revision: 923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda Diagnostic configuration: max_running_requests=1 gamma=1 verify_num_draft_tokens=2 SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static CUDA graph disabled prefill CUDA graph disabled seed=123456789 Triton GDN backend Model weights are not modified. Forced-rejection diagnostic SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 by itself is not a semantically valid forced-rejection test because it changes correct_len without recomputing the naturally selected target bonus token. For gamma=1 I therefore used this local diagnostic patch in dspark_verify.py: if self._simulate_acc_len > 0: - correct_len = self._simulated_correct_len( - bs=bs, dtype=correct_len.dtype, device=correct_len.device + target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view( + bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens ) + correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) + bonus = target_predict[:, 0] + cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len) The resulting request reports: spec_accept_rate=0.0 spec_num_correct_drafts=0 spec_num_proposed_drafts=95 spec_verify_ct=95 spec_accept_histogram=[95] Thus every first draft is rejected and the committed output token is the target model's own argmax. Exact request The same exact 24 input_ids are used for every run: INPUT_IDS = [ 248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11, 10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046, 198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271, ] Input verification: count: 24 SHA256: f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0 The SHA256 is computed as: hashlib.sha256( ",".join(map(str, INPUT_IDS)).encode() ).hexdigest() Sampling: temperature: 0 top_p: 1 top_k: -1 max_new_tokens: 96 ignore_eos: true Example request: payload = { "input_ids": INPUT_IDS, "sampling_params": { "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0, "top_k": -1, "max_new_tokens": 96, "ignore_eos": True, }, "stream": False, } Server configuration Relevant arguments: sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend triton \ --context-length 16384 \ --max-total-tokens 16384 \ --max-running-requests 1 \ --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \ --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \ --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \ --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \ --disable-cuda-graph \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \ --random-seed 123456789 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 30000 Environment: SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 For the FP32-state diagnostic I additionally use: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 Results 1. Base oracle is deterministic Base-only greedy decode is deterministic across independent server processes with seed 123456789. Original BF16 Base oracle SHA256: a935dafc6111c5acf3280bb9fa1d545f39abf5c9ba92285ba29d39949e971848 2. Original TARGET_VERIFY + forced rejection With gamma=1, static verify, CUDA graph disabled, and the forced-rejection diagnostic: first divergence: output index 13 Base token: 1070 DSpark token: 836 Indices 0..12 match Base. 3. Concrete beta precision mismatch One concrete numerical difference exists between Base packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY. Base rounds beta through the beta tensor's source dtype, while TARGET_VERIFY originally keeps the sigmoid computation in FP32. Diagnostic patch: - b_beta = 1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-b_b)) + b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32) With only this change: first divergence: 13 -> 23 Indices 0..22 now match Base. This appears to be a real numerical contributor, but not the complete cause. 4. Fresh-prefix localization Using the beta-aligned path, I rebuilt a fresh request consisting of: original input IDs + exact Base output IDs [0:22] No text was retokenized. The request reported: cached_tokens=0 Expected next Base tokens: [2438, 5306] Generated: [2438, 5306] Exact match. Therefore the long-request divergence at index 23 is not a direct TARGET_VERIFY failure at that context when recurrent state is freshly rebuilt through ordinary prefill. It requires accumulated speculative-state evolution. 5. FP32 persistent SSM state Using the same beta alignment but changing both Base and DSpark to: --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 results are: FP32 Base SHA256: 5557ae475bafcb00ff5ea564e14954f5590cf8e77535edec878a7203225561fc FP32 DSpark SHA256: a982aa8b26b5e7f51d11669da7b42a730d839d721d0d386944c3a964321a2fcb first divergence: index 38 Base token: 6338 DSpark token: 2279 So increasing persistent SSM precision changes: BF16 SSM + beta alignment: index 23 FP32 SSM + beta alignment: index 38 but does not eliminate the divergence. This suggests BF16 persistent-state storage is an error amplifier rather than the sole root cause. 6. KV precision control With FP32 SSM and beta alignment, changing target KV cache from FP8 E4M3 to BF16 moved first divergence only: 38 -> 39 This suggests full-attention KV precision is not the primary cause of the remaining drift. Other isolation work Delta reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's delta projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation did not improve correctness: beta + Base-layout delta projection: first divergence = 6 Output reduction layout Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's output projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation also regressed: beta + Base-layout output projection: first divergence = 6 Softplus expression TARGET_VERIFY originally evaluates: beta_x = softplus_beta * x softplus_x = tl.where( beta_x <= softplus_threshold, (1.0 / softplus_beta) * tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(beta_x)), x, ) Runtime parameters were confirmed as: softplus_beta=1.0 softplus_threshold=20.0 Changing only this expression to Base's literal form: softplus_x = tl.where( x <= 20, tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(x)), x, ) regressed the FP32 test: first divergence: 38 -> 6 Because the two forms are algebraically equivalent for the actual runtime parameters, this appears to demonstrate sensitivity to Triton floating-point/codegen behavior rather than identify the root cause. Convolution state A source audit found persistent conv state and TARGET_VERIFY intermediate conv windows use the same default BF16 dtype and the expected post-anchor snapshot/scatter semantics for gamma=1. Attempting the independent diagnostic: SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float32 cannot currently be used as a clean control because the current implementation hits: RuntimeError: Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match, got Float for the destination and BFloat16 for the source. ReplaySSM The current build exposes: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec but DSPARK/DFLASH explicitly rejects this path for Qwen3.8 GDN: ValueError: --enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires a KDA (kimi_linear) model; got a non-KDA model. So I could not use ReplaySSM as a GDN DSPARK correctness control. Current hypothesis The strongest evidence is: forced reject + repeated TARGET_VERIFY rounds -> divergence fresh prefill of the exact same prefix -> correct again higher persistent SSM precision -> divergence substantially delayed KV precision change -> almost no effect My current hypothesis is that a small difference enters a committed/intermediate GDN recurrent state during repeated TARGET_VERIFY reject/commit rounds and accumulates until it changes the target argmax. For gamma=1, I also audited the reject/commit indexing: candidate row 0 = anchor/current token commit_lens = 1 last_correct_step_indices = 0 and the committed conv window appears to correspond to the post-anchor state as expected. The remaining high-value localization would therefore seem to be the SSM state boundary rather than further source-expression A/B tests. Expected behavior Under this diagnostic every speculative draft token is rejected and only the target model's own greedy token is committed. I would expect DSpark to preserve the same greedy token sequence as ordinary Base decode. If exact Base equivalence is intentionally not guaranteed for GDN TARGET_VERIFY because the recurrent numerical paths differ, clarification on the intended correctness invariant/tolerance would also be useful. Questions Is this accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift a known limitation or bug in the current DSpark TARGET_VERIFY path? Is there an existing GDN state-commit / TARGET_VERIFY correctness patch that should be tested on this Qwen3.8 path? Would the most useful next instrumentation be a per-layer/per-round comparison of: Base persistent SSM state before decode TARGET_VERIFY input persistent SSM state TARGET_VERIFY intermediate step-0 SSM state post-commit/scatter persistent SSM state Is the beta source-dtype rounding difference described above expected, or should TARGET_VERIFY match Base packed decode here? If exact Base equivalence is not expected between packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY, what correctness invariant should speculative decoding enforce for recurrent GDN models? signal.title: [Speculative] Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference
signal.text: ## Motivation Classic EAGLE/NEXTN rejection sampling draws each draft proposal with `fast_sample()`. Although target sampling and verify-side rejection coins support request-local seeds, this proposal draw used the global PyTorch RNG (`exponential_()`), so `--enable-deterministic-inference` still changed outputs with batch shape and CUDA graph replay. This is the draft-worker follow-up documented in #30822. Before this change, Qwen3.5-9B NEXTN rejection sampling produced 12 unique outputs in 12 changing-batch trials with a fixed sampling seed. ## Modifications - Add an optional deterministic path to `fast_sample()` keyed by: - request sampling seed - absolute sequence position - draft step / MTP layer - vocabulary entry - Domain-separate draft proposal randomness from target sampling and verify-side rejection coins. - Convert MurmurHash32 output to open-interval uniforms with midpoint binning, then use exponential-race categorical sampling in float64. - Preserve the existing RNG-backed fast path when deterministic inference is disabled. - Plumb request seeds and positions through eager and CUDA-graph EAGLE/NEXTN workers. - Support both ordinary and multi-layer EAGLE, including the single-CUDA-graph multi-layer draft-extend path. - Keep deterministic rejection sampling guarded on non-CUDA-compatible devices because this implementation uses a Triton hash kernel. - Add sampler tests for replay, batch permutation/splitting, seed/position/step separation, hash endpoints, CUDA graph updates, and categorical distribution sanity. - Add dedicated deterministic E2E smoke tests without changing the existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP test configurations. - Add a reproducible seeded/unseeded sampling microbenchmark. ## Accuracy Tests ### Regular EAGLE/NEXTN Qwen3.5-9B, TP2, NEXTN, rejection sampling, temperature 1.0, sampling seed 42: | Version | Changing-batch trials | Unique outputs | |---|---:|---:| | Before | 12 | 12 | | After | 12 | 1 | The deterministic harness also passed changing batch sizes, prefix batching, bitwise logprob comparison, and radix-cache consistency. Post-rebase validation on B200: ```text 7 passed, 16 warnings, 2 subtests passed Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1 OK ``` The unit suite includes 100,000 distinct seeded draws from `[0.1, 0.2, 0.7]` and verifies that observed frequencies are within 0.01 absolute tolerance. ### Multi-layer EAGLE `stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash`, TP8 on 8x B200, FA4, three MTP layers, single-CUDA-graph draft extend: ```text Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1 MULTI_LAYER_EAGLE_REJECTION_SAMPLING_IS_DETERMINISTIC ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling B200, vocabulary size 163,840, CUDA-graph replay: | Batch | Unseeded | Seeded | Slowdown | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 31.9 us | 47.2 us | 1.48x | | 8 | 38.0 us | 63.5 us | 1.67x | | 32 | 54.5 us | 131.9 us | 2.42x | | 128 | 138.9 us | 544.1 us | 3.92x | Peak allocated memory for batch 128 and vocabulary 163,840: ```text Input probabilities: 80.00 MiB Baseline allocated: 80.00 MiB Peak allocated: 321.25 MiB Incremental seeded peak: 241.25 MiB ``` The deterministic mode is opt-in. A fused hash/exponential/argmax kernel can be considered separately if end-to-end profiling shows that the materialized hash and score matrices materially affect serving throughput. ## Checklist - [x] Format code and pass Ruff / `git diff --check`. - [x] Add unit and registered E2E tests. - [x] Preserve existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP coverage. - [x] Provide accuracy, latency, and peak-memory measurements. - [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance. - [x] No documentation update is needed; this fixes an existing flag combination without adding user-facing options. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:white_check_mark: [Run #31581112407](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31581112407)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31581112329](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31581112329)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [sglang-miles] Fix p2p weight registry: draft worker overwrite, fused indexer mapping, registration retries
signal.text: Three fixes found while verifying miles p2p (RDMA) weight updates on GLM-5.2 744B fp8 with MTP enabled. Companion miles PR: radixark/miles#2605. **Draft worker overwrites the target model's registry** (`model_runner.py`) With speculative decoding, the draft worker's `ModelRunner.initialize()` also calls `maybe_register_and_publish_weight_info()`. The EngineInfoBootstrapServer stores registrations as `dict[tp_rank]`, last write wins, and the draft registers after the target — so the p2p client receives the draft model's weight table and RDMA session for every rank: ordinary target params (`input_layernorm`, `o_proj`, ...) appear missing on the remote and every write bucket fails. The draft is not trained, so it is now excluded from registration. (If draft weight updates are ever needed, the registry key should become `(tp_rank, worker)`.) **Fused DSA indexer weights unmappable by ParameterMapper** (`deepseek_v2.py`) With `use_dsa_indexer_fusion`, the model has one bf16 `indexer.wk_weights_proj` per layer and no `indexer.wk` / `indexer.weights_proj` params. The checkpoint loader folds the unfused names via `_load_fused_indexer_wk`, but `ParameterMapper` — built from `stacked_params_mapping` and used by the p2p staging path — had no entry, so every indexer wk/weights_proj tensor sent by the trainer was silently dropped and the engine's indexer weights went stale. Added the two stacked entries, gated on the fused param existing. Checkpoint loading is unaffected: when fusion is on, the fold helper consumes these names before the stacked loop runs; when fusion is off, the gate keeps the entries out. **Registration was one-shot and swallowed failures** (`remote_instance_weight_transporter.py`) A transient connection failure while PUTting to the bootstrap server was logged and forgotten; the missing rank then surfaced minutes later as a 404 at the first weight update, far from the cause. Both registrations now retry (60 x 5s, timeout 30s) and raise after exhaustion. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32131323240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32131323240)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32131322909](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32131322909)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: fix: avoid TRT-LLM DSV4 DP mixed-chunk deadlock
signal.text: This is a rebased follow-up to #30805 that reproduces and fixes the B200 failure from [job 94626280851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31751166329/job/94626280851?pr=30805). The failing recipe combines TRT-LLM DSV4 attention, DP attention/DeepEP, and mixed-chunk scheduling. Uneven cached-prefix batches can leave DP ranks in different live forward modes, after which rank-coupled DeepEP collectives deadlock. The failure appeared as uneven scheduler queues followed by the DeepEP CPU receive timeout and a 0.1 GSM8K score. This follow-up takes a correctness-first approach and disables mixed-chunk scheduling only for TRT-LLM DSV4 with DP attention. Breakable prefill CUDA graphs remain enabled. It also updates the backend option for current `main` by registering `dsv4_attn_backend` in the executor-kernel configuration namespace and reading it through `get_exec().kernel`. The newly added backend module also used whole-response edit distance and exact generated-string equality across two different FP8 cache formats. Observed answers remained semantically correct while harmless formatting and continuation choices tripped those assertions. This draft replaces them with explicit known-answer and domain-term invariants, including the cached-prefix replay, so semantic corruption still fails the test. Validation on one 8xB200 AIHub node with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`: - `TestDSV4FlashFP4BreakableCudaGraphB200`: 8 tests passed, 1 skipped; GSM8K 0.960. - `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced`: 9 tests passed; GSM8K 0.970. - `TestDSV4FlashFP4NonMTPB200`: 8 tests passed; GSM8K 0.970. - New `test_dsv4_fp8_trtllm_backend.py` module on current `main`: 11 tests passed; GSM8K 0.965. - Repository-wide pre-commit passed, including the static ratchets, Rust formatting, and clippy. The speculative TP4 recipe did not reach serving readiness on the validation image even with a validation-only 900-second watchdog; all ranks remained in TRT-LLM FP4 cubin loading/GEMM warmup. This is separate from the reproduced DP runtime deadlock. No workflow was manually dispatched for this draft. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #31782874946](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31782874946)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #31782874832](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31782874832)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Diffusion][AMD] Add gfx1250 detection and stop silent CPU fallback for diffusion
signal.text: # [Diffusion][AMD] Add gfx1250 detection and stop silent CPU fallback for diffusion ## Motivation #32754 enables gfx1250 for the SRT path. `multimodal_gen` has its own platform-resolution and aiter-gating modules, so it needs the equivalent plumbing before diffusion models can be brought up on gfx1250. ## Changes **1. `srt/utils/common.py` — add `is_gfx1250_supported()`** Alongside the existing `is_gfx95_supported()` / `is_gfx942_supported()`, same pattern and `lru_cache`. Note #32754 introduces an identical helper; whichever lands second should drop its copy. Kept here so this PR is self-contained if it lands first. **2. `multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/aiter.py` — expose `USE_AITER_GFX1250`** So diffusion code can gate arch-specific aiter paths the way it already does for gfx942 and gfx95x (`USE_AITER_GFX942`, `USE_AITER_GFX95`). **3. `multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/__init__.py` — don't silently fall back to CPU** This is the substantive fix. `rocm_platform_plugin()` decided ROCm-vs-CPU solely on whether `import amdsmi` and `amdsmi_get_processor_handles()` succeeded: ```python except Exception as e: logger.debug("ROCm platform is unavailable: %s", e) ``` `amdsmi` is an optional dependency and is absent from several ROCm container images. When it is missing, the exception is swallowed into a `logger.debug` and platform resolution falls through to `CpuPlatform`. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32130274749](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130274749)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #32130274417](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32130274417)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Perf] Evaluate enc-dec cuda-graph gate on encoder_lens_cpu mirror
signal.text: ## Problem The enc-dec CUDA-graph admission gates in `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` — `can_run_graph()` and `_can_run_ragged_verify_graph()` (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) — evaluated `torch.all(forward_batch.encoder_lens > 0)` (a CUDA tensor) as a Python bool. That bool conversion is an implicit device-to-host sync on the scheduler/forward thread once per decode step, and it forces a drain of every kernel queued on the stream before the sync can complete — on a busy stream the drain dominates and costs far more than the bare sync (bare sync window is on the order of a few hundred µs; exact numbers are workload-dependent). ## Fix Both gates now go through `_encoder_lens_all_positive(forward_batch)`, which evaluates the same all-positive predicate on the CPU mirror `forward_batch.encoder_lens_cpu` when it is available (host-side `all()`, no device traffic), falling back to the original device-tensor check only when the mirror is `None`. The mirror is built from the same Python list as the device tensor, and the gates that consult it run before DP padding appends any device-only zero rows, so when present the predicate result is identical at those gates. ## Tests New tests in `test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` cover both gates: the mirror is consulted and the device tensor is never materialized into a bool on the happy path (spy), the fallback path when the mirror is `None`, and a disagreeing-mirror case (mirror all-positive, device tensor containing a zero) pinning that the mirror takes precedence by design — if they ever disagree, the device tensor is the stale one. 18 passed, 21 subtests passed on CPU (the GPU-marked parity test is deselected without a GPU). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32129182645](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32129182645)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32129182614](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32129182614)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse compress+norm+rope, emit bpreshuffle scale natively, keep kv_score in bf16
signal.text: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4 decode a good part of each attention layer goes to kernels that only move or re-lay-out data rather than compute anything. Three of them run on every layer of every step: 1. On CSA layers (`compress_ratio` 4) compress, norm and rope are three separate launches. Each is 4-8 us, which is small enough that dispatch rather than the work sets the cost. 2. The fp8 quant path writes its scale tensor in one layout and then a second kernel transposes it into the layout the bpreshuffle GEMM actually wants — 152 extra launches per decode step. 3. The compressor takes fp32, so the bf16 `wkv_gate` output is widened by a separate elementwise copy before it can be consumed — 92 extra launches per decode step. None of these carry information the surrounding kernels don't already have, so each can be folded into its neighbour without changing the math. ## Modifications Three independent optimisations, each behind its own env gate. **`SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE`** — new `fused_compress4_norm_rope.cuh` folds compress, norm and rope into a single kernel for CSA layers. The fused kernel maps one token per 64-lane wavefront rather than two; that takes it from 85 to 47 VGPRs and lifts occupancy from 5 to 8 waves/SIMD, which is what makes the fused kernel actually cheaper than the three it replaces instead of merely equal to them. **`SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE`** — the quant kernel writes the scale tensor directly in the physical layout bpreshuffle wants (column-major in M), so the separate transpose pass is not needed. **`SGLANG_OPT_KV_SCORE_BF16`** — `c4_v2.cuh` and `c128_v2.cuh` gain a `SrcFloat` template parameter, kept separate from the compute dtype so `score_bias` stays fp32. The compressor then widens the `wkv_gate` output as it loads it and the fp32 copy in front of compress is never materialised. `compress_forward()` only widens on the XPU path, and `compressor.py` calls `linear_kv_score` where it previously called `linear_bf16_fp32`. **On the defaults.** All three gates default to on. They are separable on purpose — each can be turned off on its own with `=0` if it regresses a shape I did not measure — but the numbers below are all with the three together, which is the configuration the defaults select. Happy to ship any or all of them off by default instead if maintainers would rather see soak time first. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, on the environment below. | Run | Gates | Accuracy | Invalid | |---|---|---|---| | Baseline | all off | 94.7% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 1 | all on | 94.5% | 0.000 | | Patched, pass 2 | all on | 94.8% | 0.001 | Baseline and patched are the same build on the same image, gates flipped by env var only. The patched arm was run twice because temperature 0 is not bit-deterministic here — batching order moves with arrival timing — so a single number cannot separate a real accuracy change from run-to-run noise. The two patched passes differ from each other by 0.3 points and bracket the baseline, which is the most that can be claimed: no accuracy change is visible above run-to-run noise at this sample size. ```bash MODEL= FUSE=1 NATIVE_SCALE=1 KVBF16=1 \ NUM_QUESTIONS=1319 NUM_SHOTS=5 MAX_NEW_TOKENS=512 PARALLEL=1200 \ bash bench/gsm8k_item4_517.sh # FUSE=0 NATIVE_SCALE=0 KVBF16=0 for baseline ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Environment | | | |---|---| | GPU | 8x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) | | ROCm | 7.2.0 | | Image | `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260812` | | Model | DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 61 layers | | Shape | 8k in / 1k out, `--random-range-ratio 1.0` | Server: ```bash sglang serve --model-path "$MODEL" --port "$PORT" \ --tensor-parallel-size $TP $DP_ARGS \ --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs "$CONC" --max-running-requests "$CONC" \ --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --page-size 256 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --context-length 16384 \ --chunked-prefill-size $((ISL * TP)) \ --disable-shared-experts-fusion --watchdog-timeout 1800 # DP_ARGS for the conc-64 shape: # --dp $TP --enable-dp-attention --enable-prefill-delayer --enable-two-batch-overlap ``` Client: ```bash python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port "$PORT" --model "$MODEL" \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" --max-concurrency "$CONC" ``` ### Throughput Each shape is measured A B B A and the pairs averaged, so drift over the sweep cancels instead of being charged to whichever arm happened to run second. | Shape | Baseline (tok/s) | Patched (tok/s) | Gain | |---|---|---|---| | conc 4, TP4 | 174.23, 174.85 -> 174.54 | 180.96, 179.99 -> 180.48 | **+3.40%** | | conc 8, TP4 | 302.63, 302.48 -> 302.56 | 314.70, 314.41 -> 314.56 | **+3.97%** | | conc 64, TP8 + DP8 | 1600.37, 1593.98 -> 1597.17 | 1645.41, 1643.07 -> 1644.24 | **+2.95%** | Within-arm spread is 0.05-0.40% on baseline and 0.09-0.54% on patched, comfortably under the gap between arms, so the gain is not sweep-order drift. ### Profile Decode window, 8k1k conc 64 TP8 + DP8, per layer on rank TP-0: | Per layer | Baseline | Patched | |---|---|---| | CSA kernels | 55 | **48** | | HCA kernels | 43 | **40** | | Elementwise, CSA / HCA | 8x / 6x | **3x / 3x** | | bf16->fp32 copy, CSA / HCA | 2x / 1x | **0x / 0x** | The widening copy that fed compress is gone from both layer types, and the 48 / 40 counts hold on all seven ranks that captured a full decode window. The compress kernels take bf16 directly — the fourth template argument is the source dtype: - CSA `flash_c4_decode_norm_rope<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, 0, false, true>` - HCA `flash_c128_decode<512l, float, float, __hip_bfloat16, float, false>` The three elementwise launches left per layer are two same-dtype `direct_copy` (bf16->bf16, fp32->fp32) and one bf16 residual add. None is a dtype conversion and none sits in front of compress. One caveat worth stating: CSA layer time drops 6.1% while HCA is flat at -0.07% even though HCA also loses three kernels. A single five-step profiler window carries a few us of per-layer drift, which is the same order as the effect being measured, so the throughput sweep above rather than this table is the measurement of record. ### Unit tests ```bash python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c4_v2.py \ test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_c128_v2.py -q # 110 passed ``` `test_c4_v2.py` and `test_c128_v2.py` are parametrised over a new bf16 source dtype: 55 of the 110 are those new cases. The `SrcFloat` path had no coverage before, and the bf16 arm was confirmed to actually reach the new specialisation (the dispatcher was observed compiling with `dtype_src=torch.bfloat16`) rather than being quietly widened somewhere above the kernel. All four compress specialisations (c4/c128 x fp32/bf16 source) were also checked to compile. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations) — no user-facing surface changed; the three gates are internal env switches. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32128957260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32128957260) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32128957002](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32128957002)

signal.title: [AMD][Fix] Route MoRI through the Qwen MoE all-to-all path
signal.text: ## Motivation Serving **Qwen3.5 MoE** (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) with `--moe-a2a-backend mori` on MI355X/ROCm (DP=1 / TP=2, EP=2) produced near-zero accuracy — gsm8k **0.006**. The Qwen2/Qwen3 MoE gates key on `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`, which recognises **only** pure DeepEP. MoRI is a DeepEP-class backend and needs the same per-rank EP expert layout, so under MoRI the block silently fell through to the plain-TP path: - the shared expert stayed sharded by TP=2, so each token computed only one shared-expert shard and lost the other half of the contribution; - `can_fuse_shared_expert` still allowed the fusion, placing the shared expert in a **global** slot that the per-rank EP layers never allocate; - the block never entered `_forward_deepep()`, so the routed experts never went through the MoRI dispatch/combine at all. The corrupted first token then poisons everything generated after it. This PR is the correctness follow-up to #31793 (which only disabled the global-slot shared-expert fusion to get MoRI past the init crash). ## Modifications Add `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_mori()` alongside the existing `is_deepep()` at the four gates in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2_moe.py`: `can_fuse_shared_expert` (`:153`), the shared-expert TP override (`:328`), the EP layout branch (`:347`), and the forward dispatch (`:563`). MoRI now uses the correct per-rank EP expert layout, replicates the shared expert per rank (`tp_rank=0, tp_size=1`), enters `_forward_deepep()`, and each token receives the full shared-expert output. The remaining DeepEP-class backends (Mooncake, PPLX) are deliberately **not** included — they have no Qwen MoE coverage to validate against, so `is_mori()` keeps the change byte-identical to `main` for the CUDA-side backends this PR does not exercise. A CPU unit test in `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` pins that `can_fuse_shared_expert` refuses for both `deepep` and `mori`, and still fuses on plain TP. ## Two earlier changes have been removed from this PR On-hardware re-validation no longer shows either of the two bugs they targeted. ### Decode CUDA graph disable (`server_args.py`) — removed MoRI normal mode **is** CUDA-graph safe, as @Duyi-Wang said. `mori_cpp.build_args` returns an args struct whose values (input/indices pointers, `curRankNumToken`, and the preallocated shmem buffer pointers) are snapshotted per graph node by `hipModuleLaunchKernel`, and every comm buffer has fixed capacity and a stable address. The earlier "serial gsm8k 1.000 eager → 0.000 graph" reading was a misattribution of the routing bug above. With the routing gates reverted, gsm8k is **0.000 in both eager and graph** — no code state produces the eager/graph split that motivated the guard: | routing gates | decode CUDA graph | gsm8k (40q serial) | |---|---|---| | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | on | 0.000 (invalid 0.625) | | broken (`is_deepep()` only) | **off (eager)** | **0.000** (invalid 0.600) | | fixed (this PR) | on | 0.967 (60q) | The clincher: the eager number this PR originally reported (**0.935** @ parallel 200) matches the graph number measured now (**0.932** @ parallel 200) — at 2.2x the throughput. If graph replay were misrouting experts, accuracy would collapse, not match to three decimals. Disabling the decode graph also costs spec-decode acceptance, which is what regressed `test/registered/amd/test_moriep_small.py::TestMTP::test_gsm8k` (2.51 against a 2.8 bar; passes on `main` at 3.0077). Reproduced independently on Qwen3.5 with EAGLE MTP — same server, only the graph flag differs: | decode CUDA graph | accept length | |---|---| | on | **3.47 – 3.59** | | off | 2.59 – 2.91 | ### AITER eager-metadata buffer capacity (`aiter_backend.py`) — removed The `Target sizes: [111] / Tensor sizes: [112]` crash no longer reproduces, and the sizing change did not fix the remaining high-concurrency fault: with it applied, Qwen3.5 + MTP at 64 running requests still dies with `Memory access fault by GPU node-N`, and it does so exactly when the log shows `mamba usage: 1.00` — linear-attention state pool exhaustion, not `kv_indptr` overflow. That is a separate bug and is tracked outside this PR. ## Accuracy Tests Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4, 2x MI355X, TP2 / EP2, `--moe-a2a-backend mori` (deepep_mode normal), aiter attention, fp8 KV cache, decode CUDA graph **on**: | Questions | Parallel | Accuracy | |---|---|---| | — | — | 0.006 (before fix) | | 60 | 30 | 0.967 | | 400 | 64 | 0.925 | | 1000 | 200 | **0.932** | With EAGLE MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), 200 questions / parallel 30: accuracy **0.935**, accept length **~3.5**. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GSM8K 1000 questions / parallel 200, same config: **1552.6 tok/s** output throughput (vs 691 tok/s with the decode graph disabled). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Feat][GLM-5.2] Shared KV Cache for Prefill and Decode
signal.text: ## Summary > **Supersedes [#31435](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31435).** This PR continues its GLM-5.2 Prefill CP Shared KV work and replaces it with a unified mixed Prefill/Decode implementation, adding Demand Cache, optional Shared Indexer, and EAGLE support. Add an opt-in DSA Shared KV cache for GLM-5.2 TP8/Attention-CP8 serving(CP8TP8), with CP Prefill and TP Decode on the same workers. In the tested **H20-3e** configuration, token capacity is about **3.1x–4.8x** Base and **TPOT overhead is < 2 ms**. Persistent Main KV and, by default, Indexer pages keep one owner-sharded copy per CP group. Main KV uses a local Demand Cache for FlashMLA-KV, while Shared Indexer reuses the existing full-batch Indexer compute path. The Base path is unchanged when the feature is disabled, and **EAGLE** is supported. ## Motivation Regular CP8 keeps eight physical Main KV and Indexer replicas for one logical cache. Shared KV stores one owner-sharded copy across the CP group and maps it into a common CUDA VMM address space. - LayerSplit: layer owner → **per-layer NCCL broadcast** → local full-layer scratch → attention - Shared KV: page owner → common VMM view → **local HBM read or demand peer-memory load** → attention Demand loading is intentionally simple: - **owner-local** rows are read directly - a ready local cache row is consumed as a **hit** - on a **miss**, FlashMLA-KV consumes the authoritative peer VMM row and opportunistically fills the local Demand Cache - a **collision or in-progress fill** does not wait; it falls back to the authoritative row Decode keeps current rows in a small local shadow. Shared Indexer materializes only the active shared pages into a reusable local buffer before running the existing full-batch Indexer compute. EAGLE Decode/verify uses the same Shared + Demand path; only draft-model KV remains local and replicated. ## Usage Add `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache --max-running-requests N` to the existing GLM-5.2 Attention-CP FlashMLA-KV command. `N` is configurable in `[1, 32]` and determines the preallocated Decode Demand workspace. Add `--disable-dsa-shared-indexer-cache` to share Main KV while retaining the replicated Indexer. <details><summary>Benchmark launch script</summary> The two simulation variables below are benchmark-only. Production serving must leave both unset. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail MODE=${1:?base|main-only|full} MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:?set MODEL_PATH} case "${MODE}" in base) SHARED_ARGS=() ;; BATCH=32; EXPECTED_CACHED=0; POPULATE_LEN=0 ;; 100k-prefix90-b8) INPUT_LEN=102400; BATCH=8; EXPECTED_CACHED=92160; POPULATE_LEN=92224 ;; 256k-prefix90-b16) INPUT_LEN=262144; BATCH=16; EXPECTED_CACHED=235904; POPULATE_LEN=235968 ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac mkdir -p "${OUT}" bench() { local name=$1 input_len=${2:-${INPUT_LEN}} output_len=${3:-1024} local num_prompts=${4:-${BATCH}} python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30080 \ --dataset-name random-ids --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \ --random-input-len "${input_len}" --random-output-len "${output_len}" \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --max-concurrency "${num_prompts}" \ --warmup-requests 0 --seed 20260820 --tokenize-prompt \ --disable-tqdm --output-details --cache-report \ --extra-request-body '{"ignore_eos":true,"temperature":0}' \ --output-file "${OUT}/${name}.jsonl" >"${OUT}/${name}.log" 2>&1 } validate() { python3 - "$1" "${INPUT_LEN}" "${BATCH}" "${EXPECTED_CACHED}" <<'PY' import json, sys p, input_len, batch, cached = sys.argv[1], *map(int, sys.argv[2:]) d = json.loads(open(p).readline()) assert d["completed"] == batch and d["max_concurrency"] == batch assert d["total_input_tokens"] == input_len * batch assert d["total_output_tokens"] == 1024 * batch assert all(x == cached for x in d["cached_tokens"]) assert not any(d["errors"]) assert abs(d["accept_length"] - 3.0) < 0.02 assert all(1020 <= len(x) <= 1023 for x in d["itls"]) PY } # Disjoint JIT warmup; its KV is flushed before measurement. bench warmup 4096 1 1 curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30080/flush_cache >"${OUT}/flush-after-warmup.json" for round in round1 round2; do curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30080/flush_cache >"${OUT}/${round}-flush.json" if (( POPULATE_LEN > 0 )); then bench "${round}-populate" "${POPULATE_LEN}" 1; fi bench "${round}" validate "${OUT}/${round}.jsonl" done ``` The Prefix populate lengths include one extra 64-token page because the radix cache withholds its final page.
