signal.title: [dLLM] Cut per-step host overhead in the dLLM extend path
signal.text: ## Motivation dLLM inference disables the overlap scheduler (each denoise step has a hard input dependency on the previous step's result), so every bit of host time between steps is exposed directly as device idle. Profiling LLaDA2 at bs=128 on Ascend 910B3 showed three host-side costs on the per-step path, none of which needed to be there: 1. `AscendAttnBackend.init_forward_metadata` took two D2H syncs to obtain values the scheduler already holds on the host (`seq_lens_max`, `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int`). 2. `NPUGraphRunner` re-read `forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` before every replay, a blocking D2H behind whatever is queued on the stream, while the same host mirror was already available. 3. `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse` (the dLLM FDFO retained-KV path) re-read each reuse row's retained block with its own slice + cast kernel, and pulled every scheduling scalar out of CPU tensors one element at a time. Both costs grow linearly with batch size. ## Modifications **`hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py`** — take `seq_lens_max` from `seq_lens_cpu` and build `extend_seq_lens_cpu_int` from `extend_seq_lens_cpu`. Gated on `forward_mode.is_dllm_extend()`, so the decode/prefill path is byte-identical. **`hardware_backend/npu/graph_runner/npu_graph_runner.py`** — use `forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu` when present, falling back to `.cpu()` when it is not. This one is **not** dLLM-gated and affects every non-DeepSeek-DSA/V4 model on this path, so it is worth stating why it is equivalent: `seq_lens_cpu` is already the authoritative host mirror here — the Ascend attention backend derives its own `seq_lens_cpu_int` from it for every forward mode, and likewise adds the draft width on target-verify. Reading the device tensor in the graph runner made the two components disagree on their source for the same forward; this aligns them. The `is_target_verify()` adjustment is unchanged, and the two former branches collapse into one because they now differ only by that addition. **`mem_cache/allocation.py`** — three changes inside `_alloc_extend_loc_with_kv_reuse`, which is reached only via `if batch.is_dllm()` in `alloc_for_extend`, so non-dLLM requests never enter it: - Add `_gather_reused_block_locs`: the retained blocks all share one length, so fetch them with a single flat index op instead of one slice + cast kernel per row. It replaces one kernel launch per row with a fixed index build + H2D, so it wins on wide batches and loses on narrow ones. The gate is the reuse-row count, re-evaluated every round, so a batch that shrinks falls back on its own — a small-batch latency deployment keeps the per-row path without configuring anything. The threshold defaults to the backend's measured break-even (8 on Ascend, where break-even is ~6) and is unset on backends where it has not been measured, so those keep today's behavior. `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` overrides it: a row count to retune, or `-1` to disable the batched path outright for A/B and rollback. Rows of non-uniform block length keep the per-row path regardless. The resolved default is logged once at INFO. - Replace the per-element `int(cpu_tensor[i])` reads with one `.tolist()` per tensor. Unconditional: strictly less work at any batch size. At bs=128 the old code did roughly 770 of these, each allocating a temporary 0-dim tensor. - Hoist the `torch.tensor([-1], device=...)` filler out of the `last_loc` comprehension. Unconditional for the same reason. Every empty-prefix row was allocating its own identical device tensor; the list is consumed by `torch.cat`, which copies, so one shared tensor is equivalent. ### Configuration One new environment variable, `SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` (`EnvInt(None)` in `environ.py`), the minimum number of dLLM FDFO reuse rows at which the retained blocks are gathered in one flat index op. Nothing needs to be set for the intended behavior on either an Ascend or a non-Ascend deployment: | Value | Behavior | When to use | | --- | --- | --- | | unset (default) | Ascend: batch at 8+ reuse rows. Other backends: always per-row. | Normal serving, both latency and throughput. | | `N` (>= 0) | Batch at `N`+ reuse rows. | Enabling it on a backend after measuring its break-even, or retuning Ascend. | | `-1` | Never batch. | Production A/B and quick rollback. | ```bash # enable on a non-Ascend backend after measuring its break-even SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=8 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... # roll back to the per-row path without redeploying SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=-1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ... ``` The resolved default is logged once at INFO: ``` dLLM retained-block gather: batching enabled above 8 reuse rows (Ascend default). Override with SGLANG_DLLM_BATCHED_GATHER_MIN_ROWS. ``` ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs — all three changes are host-side bookkeeping that produce the same values (the same slot indices, the same metadata) by different means. Verified with LLaDA2-mini on gsm8k (zero-shot, full 1319 samples): accuracy unchanged. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on Ascend 910B3 at bs=128 (LLaDA2-mini, 32-token dLLM blocks), microbenchmarking each site against the code it replaces: | Site | Before | After | Saved | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Retained-block gather (128 reuse rows x 32) | 5671 us | 309 us | **5.4 ms** | | ~770 scheduling scalar reads | 3849 us | 54 us | **3.3 ms** | | `init_forward_metadata` (idle stream) | 251 us | 83 us | 168 us | | Graph replay `seq_lens` (idle stream) | 44 us | 6 us | 38 us | The gather is the dominant one and the only part that changes complexity: the per-row path costs about 44 us per reuse row (one kernel launch each) and scales linearly, while the batched path is roughly constant at about 270 us. That constant is why it is row-gated rather than unconditional — below the break-even the per-row path is genuinely faster: | reuse rows | per-row | batched | | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 1 | 120 us | 305 us | per-row path taken | | 4 | 196 us | 269 us | per-row path taken | | 6 | 279 us | 271 us | break-even | | 8 | 362 us | 268 us | Ascend default threshold | | 32 | 1449 us | 277 us | | | 64 | 2762 us | 268 us | | | 128 | 5671 us | 309 us | | | 256 | 11466 us | 353 us | | The `last_loc` hoist is not in the table because its benefit depends on how many requests have an empty prefix: each such row was allocating a device tensor at about 70 us, so it saves that times the number of empty-prefix rows in the batch (up to 8.9 ms at bs=128 when every row is fresh, and nothing when every row has a cached prefix). On Ascend at bs=128 this removes about 8.7 ms per step out of the box, against a step time of about 98 ms. On a backend where the gather threshold is unset it removes about 3.5 ms (the scalar reads plus the two D2H syncs); the gather itself is one env var away once its break-even has been measured there. ## Unit Tests `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dllm_reused_block_gather.py` (CPU-only, no server) pins the flat index arithmetic in `_gather_reused_block_locs` against per-row slicing. Each case covers a way the gather can be heterogeneous across rows, which is where a "looks equivalent" rewrite goes wrong: distinct per-row start offsets, unsorted pool indices, and a block ending exactly at the row boundary. Changing `row * width` to `row * block_len` in the implementation fails all three. These are deliberately not a re-test of the happy path. `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` covers that already in principle, but its reuse rows all share one prefix length and ascending pool indices, so an implementation that broadcast row 0's offset across every row would still pass it. (It is also module-level skipped today, and its fixtures no longer match `alloc_for_extend` — un-skipping it raises `SimpleNamespace has no attribute out_cache_loc_dsv4` — so it is not currently guarding anything either way.) The two D2H changes have no new tests: they need an NPU, and their equivalence is structural (`seq_lens_cpu` is the mirror of `seq_lens`, which the same backend already relies on). ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32126343375](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126343375)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32126343182](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126343182)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: feat(srt): add ProductionDebtInferenceGate and TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger
signal.text: ### Summary Adds the native **ProductionDebtInferenceGate** and cryptographic **TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger** under `python/sglang/srt/production_debt.py`. ### Problem Solved As enterprise AI architects and Forward Deployed Engineers deploy high-throughput RadixAttention serving, structured programs, and multi-turn agentic workflows in SGLang (LMSYS), engineering organizations require real-time controls over **Enterprise GPU Inference Production Debt & Technical Due Diligence**: 1. **SGLang Debt Index (SDI <= 12.0)**: Scoring inference batches for RadixTree KV cache thrashing, speculative rollback debt, and latency degradation. 2. **Radix KV Cache Eviction Multiplier (REM <= 1.08x)**: Monitoring peak Radix tree cache memory against allocated GPU RAM to eliminate memory fragmentation and OOM crashes. 3. **P99 Time-To-First-Token Ceiling (<= 0.65s)**: Enforcing strict TTFT boundaries across complex structured programs and speculative decoding batches. 4. **Deterministic Mutation Boundaries**: Enforcing `never_equate_intent_to_approval` across state-mutating SGLang tool execution and external API calls. 5. **Cryptographic Technical Due Diligence Action Ledger**: Emitting immutable, SHA-256 hash-chained JSONL receipts providing audit-ready evidence for VC/PE Technical Due Diligence, M&A evaluations, and enterprise production readiness reviews. ### Features Added - `sglang.srt.production_debt.ProductionDebtInferenceGate`: - `evaluate_inference_batch()`: Evaluates batch memory, Radix KV cache ratios, and TTFT latency, returning a normalized Production Readiness Score (0–100) with critical smell warnings. - `sglang.srt.production_debt.TechnicalDueDiligenceLedger`: - `record_inference_event()`: Cryptographically links each serving event into an immutable SHA-256 chain. - `verify_ledger_integrity()`: Validates hash-chain continuity. ### Testing & Validation - Added `test/srt/test_production_debt.py` with 3 automated unit tests validating clean inference batches, degraded Radix sprawl failure detection, and cryptographic ledger integrity (3/3 tests passing). ### Upstream & Commercial Context Maintained by [A2Z SOC](https://a2zsoc.com) for AI Forward Deployed Engineering, GPU Serving Hardening, and Technical Due Diligence. For engineering organizations and investors requiring codebase due diligence or production debt triage: - **Instant Audit ($499):** https://a2zsoc.com/productized-services#instant-audit-tripwire - **Technical Due Diligence ($25K–$50K) & Production Debt Remediation Sprints ($50K–$100K):** https://a2zsoc.com/consultation <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32127712761](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32127712761)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32127712630](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32127712630)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [AMD] Fuse Kimi-K3 MLA Q and cache preparation
signal.text: ## Summary - Fuse Kimi-K3 identity-RoPE Q materialization, Q concat, and latent KV-cache write through AITER's per-head MLA cache operator. - Support BF16-Q/BF16-KV, FP8-Q/FP8-KV, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV mixed output for Triton decode. - Dispatch only on gfx950 decode/idle batches with contiguous covered inputs; DCP and unsupported contracts fail closed to the existing split/cat/cache path. ## Runtime configuration ```bash export SGLANG_K3_AITER_MLA_Q_CACHE_FUSION=1 ``` Validated FP8-KV configuration: ```bash sglang serve \ --model-path /path/to/Kimi-K3 \ --tp-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend triton \ --prefill-attention-backend triton \ --decode-attention-backend triton ``` BF16 KV is also covered. The larger measured gain is with BF16-Q + FP8-KV. ## AITER dependency This SGLang integration requires AITER #4342 / commit `770790cd` or newer `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` semantics, including the `compute_all_q_rope` behavior used for correct batch-64 execution. The AITER revision currently pinned by main (`d9e5ef7`) is insufficient: its old schema rejects the new argument, and a 14-argument compatibility call produces incorrect token-64 output. This PR intentionally documents rather than changes the AITER pin. ## Accuracy Tests - Focused operator tests: `9 passed` - GSM8K 1319: `0.955` - Invalid responses: `0.001` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Historical matched results for the same integration: - BF16 KV: C32 `+0.63%`, C64 `+0.53%` - FP8 KV: C32 `+3.26%`, C64 `+3.57%` - FP8-KV median TPOT: approximately `-4%` ## Test plan - [x] BF16/BF16, FP8/FP8, and BF16-Q/FP8-KV operator tests at token counts 1 and 64 - [x] Negative slot handling - [x] CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs - [x] Narrow support/fallback predicates - [x] Full GSM8K 1319 with Triton prefill/decode and FP8 KV - [ ] Re-run after the target branch updates its AITER pin AITER prefill was not used in the full-model test because 12-head AITER attention-backend enablement is maintained separately; this fusion acts on the decode path. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com) <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32125303049](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125303049)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32127602006](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32127602006)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Spec][DSV4] perf: Skip inactive target-verify metadata tails
signal.text: ## Motivation DSV4 MTP target verification captures metadata buffers for a 1M-token maximum context. On every CUDA-graph replay, `_page_table_positions_kernel` and `_init_compressed_attn_metadata_kernel` traversed the full capture capacity even when the current sequence was short. This made two memory-bound metadata kernels a measurable part of target-verify GPU time. ## Modifications - Add CUDA-graph-safe live-prefix execution to both Triton metadata kernels. Launch grids stay static, while blocks beyond device-side live lengths exit without rewriting inactive tails. - Preserve scalar metadata updates and the required C128 sentinel for empty sequences. - Enable the optimization only for the validated default SM100 path. Alternative indexer, top-k, HiSparse, and non-CUDA paths retain full-tail initialization. - Add focused B200 replay and poisoned-tail consumer tests, plus a local non-CI CUDA-graph benchmark. ## Accuracy Tests ```bash sgl-eval run gsm8k \ --base-url http://localhost:30000/v1 \ --num-threads 32 Run directory: /root/.sgl_eval/sgl_eval_gsm8k_20260727-052647 gsm8k: 100%|█████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████████| 1319/1319 [03:58<00:00, 5.53it/s, acc=96.44%] == gsm8k == 1319 examples (single-shot) | 238.6s | 738 tok/s | 176K tokens * score = 96.44% stop_rate = 100.00% truncated_rate = 0.00% error_rate = **0.00%** ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Local B200 benchmark, verify width 4 and fixed capture capacity 1,048,577. Each request contributes four causal metadata rows, so `metadata rows = BS × 4`. signal.title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4 MI355X: eliminate bpreshuffle fp8-scale relayout copy in dense w8a8 linear
signal.text: ## Summary On MI355X (gfx950) the CK bpreshuffle w8a8 blockscale GEMM consumes the per-group activation scale in **column-major** `[num_groups, tokens]` layout. `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` quantizes the activation row-major and then relays the scale out with `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale` = `.t().contiguous().t()` — a real relayout **copy per dense w8a8 GEMM** (the MLA q/kv/o projections and MoE), one of the larger ELEWISE deltas in the DeepSeek-V4 MI355X decode breakdown. `aiter_per1x128_quant` already supports `transpose_scale=True`, which emits the exact `[num_groups, tokens]` byte-order directly. This PR asks for that and reinterprets the strides with a zero-copy view, removing the copy on the fresh-quant path. ## What changed - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`** — in the fresh-quant branch of `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear`, pass `transpose_scale=emit_bpreshuffle_scale` to `aiter_per1x128_quant` and consume the result via the shared `view_aiter_fused_rms_transposed_fp8_scale` helper (the `as_strided((1, M))` metadata repair that landed on main in #31727) instead of `materialize_bpreshuffle_fp8_scale`. Guarded `M >= 2`; the M==1 single-row case keeps the materialize path, which for a contiguous `[1, G]` input is a **no-op view** anyway (the `[1, G]` and `[G, 1]` byte orders coincide, so `.t().contiguous().t()` shares storage and launches no copy kernel). Bit-identical output; removes one relayout copy on the M>=2 path. The pre-existing Triton row-major-view branch is routed through the same helper too, so the transposed-scale repair lives in one documented place rather than as duplicated inline `as_strided` expressions. ## Tests - **CPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_scale.py`) — the shared-helper stride/no-copy contract, and the `M == 1` materialize fallback: values intact on the natural `(G, 1)` stride (the no-op-view layout, not `(1, 1)`), sharing storage. - **MI35X GPU** (`test_fp8_bpreshuffle_dense_linear_mi35x.py`, `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`) — exercises the **real** kernels: (1) `aiter_per1x128_quant` with `transpose_scale` True vs False, asserting identical quantized bytes, equal scale values, the `(1, M)` stride (M>=2) / `(G, 1)` no-op (M==1), and zero-copy sharing; (2) end-to-end `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` new path vs the original path (forced by patching quant→row-major + relayout→materialize), asserting **bit-identical** GEMM output over M ∈ {1, 2, 8, 16} (M==1 exercises the materialize fallback), and **spying the GEMM dispatch to assert the CK `gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle` path is taken (not Triton)** so a future tuned-shape-list change can't silently void the coverage. This is the direct real-path evidence the fabricated-layout CPU test could not provide. ## Validation Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP8. Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260731`. Baseline = image tree; Patched = image tree + this patch. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton`. **Correctness:** GEMM output bit-identical vs the materialize path (`gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle`, max-abs-diff 0.0). ### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 2 runs) | run | baseline | patched | |----:|:--------:|:-------:| | 1 | 0.942 | 0.941 | | 2 | 0.939 | 0.947 | Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise); the bit-identical correctness check above is the primary guarantee. ### Perf (random 8k/1k, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, seed 42, num-prompts = conc×10) — preliminary **Single-shot, one run per arm — preliminary, not an established speedup.** The Δ below (≈ 0.9–2.0%) is not yet backed by repeated A/B runs, so I'm presenting it as directional rather than a confirmed win; the trend (larger at lower concurrency, i.e. more launch/latency-bound) is consistent with removing a per-GEMM relayout copy but isn't proven by these numbers alone. The correctness/no-regression guarantee is the **bit-identical GEMM output** check above. Happy to add repeated-run A/B (mean/p50/variance) if a throughput claim is wanted. | conc | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) | ΔTPOT | baseline total tok/s | patched total tok/s | Δtot | |-----:|:------------------:|:-----------------:|:-----:|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|:----:| | 16 | 19.48 | 19.10 | −2.0% | 6500.2 | 6613.0 | +1.7% | | 32 | 24.63 | 24.22 | −1.7% | 9685.3 | 9821.3 | +1.4% | | 64 | 35.03 | 34.60 | −1.2% | 12819.0 | 12935.7 | +0.9% | Coherent, zero dropped requests. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32115420885](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32115420885)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32115420264](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32115420264)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [ROCm] Fuse per-token fp8 activation quant into RMSNorm for per-chann…
signal.text: This PR fuses the per-token FP8 activation quantization into the preceding RMSNorm for **per-channel dynamic** FP8 attention projections on AMD gfx95 (validated on MI355X with Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4). By emitting a pre-quantized `(fp8, scale, orig_dtype)` tuple straight from the norm, it removes the standalone per-token quant kernel before each attention projection, improving throughput by up to ~3.5% with no accuracy change. ## Motivation For per-channel fp8 attention projections on gfx95, the per-token activation quant runs as a standalone `_per_token_group_quant_8bit` launch immediately before each projection (`fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, `kv_b_proj`). Profiling shows this as a separate kernel that can be folded into the preceding RMSNorm. ## Change Fold the per-token fp8 quant into the preceding RMSNorm, so the projection receives a pre-quantized `(fp8, x_scale[m, 1], orig_dtype)` tuple consumed directly by `gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle` in `apply_fp8_linear`. The standalone quant kernel is eliminated. The tuple carries the original activation dtype so the GEMM output preserves it (FP16 stays FP16; not promoted to BF16). Fusion sites, each emitting a per-token whole-row scale `[m, 1]`: - **Entry proj** (`fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`): fold into `input_layernorm`, covering the fused all-reduce + RMSNorm path (`custom_fused_ar_rms_quant`) **and** the post-all-reduce path used by large-batch prefill. - **Decode `q_b_proj`**: fold into the fused q/kv RMSNorm (`fused_qk_rmsnorm`, `quant_type=per_Token`). - **Prefill `q_b_proj` / `kv_b_proj`**: fold into the single-tensor RMSNorm (`rmsnorm2d_fwd_with_dynamicquant`, `group_size=0`). ## Testing - **`test/registered/unit/models/test_pertoken_fp8_eligibility.py`** (CPU) — unit tests for the fold-eligibility predicate `_is_per_channel_dynamic_fp8`. Asserts the layout contract is read from the layer's own state: the explicit `_fp8_weight_preshuffled` marker (not the global gfx95 flag), `input_scale is None` (dynamic), and `weight_scale.numel()` equal to the projection's real output-channel count (`output_size_per_partition` else `output_size`), 1-D `[N]` or 2-D `[N,1]`. Covers eligible per-channel (1-D/2-D) vs. rejected per-tensor, static-input-scale, block-scale, non-fp8, missing-marker, and a scale sized to the input dim `K` (must be rejected). - **`test/registered/kernels/test_pertoken_fp8_fold_parity.py`** (MI35x) —GEMM-level parity: the pre-quantized `(fp8, scale)` tuple path vs. the standard `apply_fp8_linear` path produce identical output, and the carried dtype is preserved (FP16 stays FP16; a 2-tuple falls back to `pre_quant_output_dtype` / BF16). - **`test/registered/kernels/test_pertoken_fp8_quant_method_routing.py`** (MI35x) — drives the folded tuple **through the real quant method** rather than `apply_fp8_linear` directly: `test_quark_scheme_routes_tuple` runs the actual Quark `W8A8Fp8` `apply_weights` for the entry (2112), q_b (12288), and kv_b (16384) widths at M=1 (decode) and M>1 (prefill), BF16/FP16, asserting parity and dtype preservation; `test_unwrapped_per_token_scale_does_not_assert` guards the native `Fp8LinearMethod` / compressed-tensors unwrap path (`apply_fp8_linear(input=qx, input_scale=scale[M,1])`) that previously asserted `numel == 1` and failed for M>1. - **`test/registered/kernels/test_pertoken_fp8_layer_routing.py`** (MI35x) —genuine layer-path regression test: builds a real `ColumnParallelLinear`, quantizes and preshuffles its weight via the real Quark scheme (`create_weights` → load → `process_weights_after_loading`, which sets the marker), then calls `layer.forward()` — exercising the full production routing (`ColumnParallelLinear.forward → quant_method.apply → scheme.apply_weights → apply_fp8_linear → gemm_a8w8_bpreshuffle`). Asserts the preshuffle marker landed, the folded-tuple forward matches the plain-activation forward, and dtype is preserved (q_b/kv_b, M=1 and M>1, BF16/FP16). All four pass on MI355X (gfx950); the CPU eligibility test also runs on CPU CI. ## Accuracy test **Accuracy (GSM8K)** — neutral, within run-to-run noise: Results (MI355X / gfx950, Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4) | parallel | 100 | 300 | 600 | 1200 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | original | 0.951 | 0.953 | 0.942 | 0.950 | | fold_quant | 0.947 | 0.946 | 0.947 | 0.951 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **Throughput / GPU (tok/s)** — consistent improvement: Results (MI355X / gfx950, Kimi-K2.7-Code-MXFP4) | Conc | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 | 128 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | original | 906.82 | 1491.25 | 2128.38 | 2955.05 | 3925.4 | 5048.96 | | fold_quant | 932.15 | 1511.13 | 2203.48 | 2992.39 | 3983.7 | 5084.88 | | Δ | +2.79% | +1.33% | +3.53% | +1.26% | +1.49% | +0.71% | original profiling: fold_quant profiling: ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [diffusion] Allow per-role attention backend override
signal.text: ## Motivation Currently one can choose a global attention backend or a specific backend per component. This PR adds support to choose attention backend per component for each role. That is, a different backend for self-attention and cross-attention. The motivation here is that when using quantized attention backends, there's a quantization overhead prior to running the lower precision kernel. This overhead is mostly worth it in self-attention, but cross-attention calls are often so light that the overhead can be enough for the entire call to be slower than the un-quantized counterpart. The backend can be chosen via the component backend selection: ``` --component-attention-backends.transformer.self=backend_1 -component-attention-backends.transformer.cross=backend_2 ``` The backend choice tree is as follows: 1. selected_attention_backend - explicit arg passed directly into `get_attn_backend()` 2. Global forced backend - `get_global_forced_attn_backend()`, set via `global_force_attn_backend()` (programmatic override) 3. Component + role override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend_for_role(attention_role)`, i.e. the config key transformer.cross / transformer.self 4. Component-wide override - `get_component_forced_attn_backend()`, i.e. the config key transformer (no role suffix) 5. CLI global - `--attention-backend` flag 6. `default_attention_backend` 7. Platform default - if everything above is None, platform picks This now only adds the choice via the `--component-attention-backends`. If desired, I can also add a `--cross-attention-backend` flag. ## Modifications - Enhances the component-attention-backend to support self/cross attn as well - Adds AttentionRole enum used to specify self/cross role (can support others, like joint, as well, if needed) - Refactors all is_cross_attention checks to use the new AttentionRole value instead - Wires AttentionRole to Attention modules, so they can pick the correct backend ## Accuracy Tests Here the self was `torch_sdpa` and cross is `aiter`. Both are used as expected. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c90da006-421a-42d8-b923-301210e0cb4e Output is good. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. signal.title: [Fix][Profiler] Stop freezing the scheduler thread while the chrome trace is written
signal.text: ## Motivation `SchedulerProfilerManager._stop_profile()` writes the chrome trace out inline on the scheduler thread. The rank is frozen for the entire write: no batch is scheduled, in-flight requests stall, and `/health_generate` calls that land in the window fail, so a router in front of the rank can take it out of rotation for a profile the operator asked for deliberately. This addresses the second of the two defects reported in #34943. The first one in that report — the by-stage predicate counting `TARGET_VERIFY` batches as prefill, so a stage window terminates on a later request — is a separate change and is **not** touched here, so this PR intentionally does not close the issue. Measured on one rank, `Qwen2.5-0.5B` at tp1, a 20 s profile window under steady load from the same driver in every arm: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | longest gap between request completions | 108.5 s | **32–36 s** (3 runs) | | `/health_generate` failures in the window | 5 consecutive 503s | 1 | The residual is worth stating plainly, because this PR does not remove it. Splitting the stall by phase gives `torch_profiler.stop()` = 21.0 s and kineto's `export_chrome_trace()` = 13.9 s. The latter holds the GIL inside C++ for its whole duration, so moving it to another thread cannot hide it, and the former is torch's own teardown. What actually comes off the critical path is the gzip write of the staged json, which for this window is ~3 GB in and ~118 MB out. ## Modifications Two changes, and nothing else. **1. The export runs on a flush thread, and an explicit `/stop_profile` is answered when the trace is on disk.** `_stop_profile()` submits the write to a single-worker executor and hands the deferred reply along with it; `Scheduler.send_control_output()` is extracted so the flush thread can send that one reply. The scheduler loop reaps finished writes via `check_pending_flush()`, and `run_scheduler_process`'s `finally` calls `drain_pending_flushes()` so a shutdown mid-write still answers and still finishes the file. At most two flushes may be pending: a third stop waits for the oldest to finish, which is no worse than what every stop does today. And if the executor is already gone — shutdown has drained it — the export runs inline, exactly as it does now, rather than dropping the trace. Deliberately unchanged: `torch.distributed.barrier(dp_tp_cpu_group)` stays synchronous in its original position, because that group also carries grammar `all_gather_object` and multimodal `broadcast_object_list` at rank-symmetric points; and `merge_profiles=True` stays fully synchronous, draining pending flushes first, because `ProfileMerger._discover_trace_files()` globs `f"{profile_id}*.trace.json.gz"` and would otherwise race a trace this rank is still writing. **2. The gzip write is chunked.** `_export_trace()` is torch's own staging block with one line changed: `shutil.copyfileobj(fin, fout, 4 MiB)` instead of torch's `fout.writelines(fin)`. torch's version needs the GIL once per line, which is precisely what makes the write unhideable from a worker thread — in a contention experiment, writing a 1.6 MB trace that way from a background thread while the scheduler spun took 142.9 s. Chunked, it is 6.8× faster under that contention, 1.2× faster uncontended, and the resulting archive is byte-identical. On MPS the export stays inline, because a Metal trace is written alongside it under a name derived from the same path. ### Behaviour change An explicit `/stop_profile` reply now means "this rank's trace is on disk", not "every rank's". Deferring the reply per rank is what buys the unblocking; restoring the old meaning would require the reply to cross the barrier above, which has to stay where it is. Relatedly, a follower rank whose export fails is now reported with `logger.error` rather than raising — before this change that raise would have taken the rank down. Predicate-driven stops (`--profile-by-stage`, step-count stops) reply to nobody and are unaffected. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: no model, kernel or forward-path code is touched. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The table above; the driver applies identical load in every arm and times the `/stop_profile` round-trip. The produced trace was checked rather than assumed: it parses, carries 7,205,111 events in 117,824,756 bytes, its gzip header stores the trace's own name (not the staged json's), it is mode `0644`, and no staged json is left behind in the temp directory. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — 17 tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_profiler_manager_async_export.py`, covering the deferred reply, the shutdown drain, back-pressure, the inline fallback, the merge path, the MPS bypass, and the staged-json location and cleanup. - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing documentation change; the one behaviour change is described above. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32126389138](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126389138)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32126388800](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126388800)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [dLLM] Fix KV leak on FDFO abort and cap the staging token-budget fallback at one block
signal.text: ## Motivation Two device-agnostic dLLM correctness fixes found while running LLaDA2 FDFO at large batch sizes. Both reproduce on any backend (no device-specific branches involved). ### Bug 1: KV leak when aborting FDFO requests with unresolved blocks `RadixCache.cache_finished_req` slices `req_to_token` by `len(origin_input_ids + output_ids)`, but an FDFO request's unresolved denoise block exists only in `dllm_incomplete_ids` — its committed KV slots lie **beyond** that length. The tail free never sees those slots, so every aborted incomplete request orphans one block of KV, and the pool never recovers. **How to reproduce** (radix cache on, i.e. default): ```bash # 1. Launch a dLLM server; strict idle check turns the leak warning into a hard error. # --dllm-algorithm is the only required dLLM flag (FDFO and radix cache are on by # default; the attention backend is auto-resolved per platform). SGLANG_ENABLE_STRICT_MEM_CHECK_DURING_IDLE=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini --trust-remote-code \ --dllm-algorithm LowConfidence # 2. Send concurrent long generations and hard-disconnect the clients mid-generation # (client-side timeout closes the connection -> server aborts the request while # its current denoise block is still unresolved) python3 - <<'EOF' import concurrent.futures, requests def hit(i): try: requests.post("http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate", json={"text": "Write a very long story.", "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 2048}}, timeout=5) except requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: pass with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(128) as ex: list(ex.map(hit, range(128))) EOF # 3. Wait for the server to go idle ``` Before this PR: once the server goes idle, the invariant check fails (crash under strict mode, repeated warnings otherwise): ``` File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3662, in on_idle self.invariant_checker._report_leak("pool", "\n".join(messages)) File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/invariant_checker.py", line 428, in _report_leak raise_error_or_warn( ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=635008, available=32, evictable=634944, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0 ``` The accounting pins it down: `available + evictable + protected + session_held + uncached = 634976`, which is short of `total = 635008` by exactly **32 tokens = one denoise block** — this trace had one aborted incomplete request. The pool shrinks by one block per aborted incomplete request and never recovers (bisected with per-abort allocator accounting). After this PR: the idle check passes; the pool returns to full size after every abort wave. ### Bug 2: uncapped staging token-budget fallback crashes the denoise reshape `PrefillAdder._get_dllm_remain_tokens` falls back to `rem_dllm_tokens` when `rem_total_tokens` is exhausted. `rem_total_tokens` charges `max_new_tokens` upfront for every staging row on every scheduling round, so long-output workloads drive it negative long before the KV pool actually fills — the fallback is then the common path, and it is uncapped: a staging row can be granted more than `block_size` tokens (e.g. a mid-prompt prefill row's whole remaining prompt). That produces a variable-length row, which crashes the denoise algorithms' uniform-block reshape (`view(B, block_size)`). **How to reproduce**: ```bash # 1. Launch as above (strict-mode env not needed) python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model inclusionAI/LLaDA2.0-mini --trust-remote-code \ --dllm-algorithm LowConfidence # 2. Long-output workload at full batch (bench_serving defaults to port 30000, # matching the server default) python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 512 --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 2048 --random-range-ratio 1 ``` Before this PR: once `rem_total_tokens` goes negative (reliably within the run), the scheduler admits an over-sized staging row and the server crashes in the denoise step with `RuntimeError: shape '[B, 32]' is invalid for input of size N`. After this PR: a single staging grant is capped at one block, every row stays uniform, and the run completes. ## Modifications - `mem_cache/radix_cache.py`: slice `kv_indices` by `kv_len_to_handle` instead of `len(token_ids)`, matching the chunk-cache (radix-disabled) branch which already frees by KV length. For non-dLLM requests `kv_len_to_handle` never exceeds `len(token_ids)` (AR requests finish with `kv_committed_len < len(origin_input_ids + output_ids)`), so the slice is byte-identical and AR behavior is unchanged. - Note: the same slicing pattern exists in `mamba_radix_cache`, `swa_radix_cache`, `pure_swa_radix_cache`, `unified_radix_cache`, and `radix_cache_cpp`; those are unreachable by dLLM today (latent only) and are left as-is. - `managers/schedule_policy.py`: cap the fallback at `min(rem_dllm_tokens, dllm_block_size)` so a single staging grant can never exceed one block. The fallback itself is kept — removing it would stall in-flight denoise blocks once `rem_total_tokens` goes negative; it is only clamped. AR never reaches this function (`_get_dllm_remain_tokens` is only called on `dllm_config is not None` paths). ## Unit Tests Two CPU-only regression tests (`base-a-test-cpu`, no GPU/server), both verified **red on the pre-fix code and green on the fix**: - `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_dllm_abort_free.py` — the aborted-FDFO case fails pre-fix with the unresolved block's KV slots unaccounted (`[] != [108..111]`), plus an AR-invariance case pinning the new kv-length slice byte-identical to the old behavior for autoregressive requests. - `test/registered/unit/managers/test_dllm_staging_token_budget.py` — the exhausted-budget fallback returns one block instead of the whole `rem_dllm_tokens` (pre-fix: `4096 != 32`), does not inflate a sub-block budget, and leaves the normal budget path unchanged. ## Accuracy Tests No effect on model outputs by construction (memory-reclaim / scheduling-budget only). Verified with LLaDA2-mini on gsm8k (zero-shot, full 1319 samples): accuracy unchanged before/after. ## Speed Tests and Profiling No measurable throughput change; both fixes are off the hot path (abort cleanup, and a clamp on an already-taken fallback branch). The repros above are the before/after evidence: the abort wave now passes the idle pool invariant check, and the 512-in/2048-out full-batch run completes instead of crashing. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32126326452](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126326452)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32126326246](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32126326246)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [diffusion][Model] Support MAGI-2-preview
signal.text: ## Motivation Relate #35011 Adds native support for [MAGI-2-preview](https://huggingface.co/sand-ai/MAGI-2-preview), SandAI's 114B MoE model that generates a video and its synchronized stereo soundtrack in one denoising trajectory. About 6B parameters are active per token. Audio is not a second pass over finished video: video and audio latents share one packed sequence and one denoise loop. Text-to-video and image+text-to-video are both supported. The checkpoint ships two DiTs. A preview model denoises the clip, and a refiner then takes that result to 1920x1088; the words "preview" and "refiner" below always mean those two. Serving it today means standing up a second stack. The reference implementation launches under `torchrun`, depends on SandAI's own kernels ([MagiAttention](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiAttention), [MagiCompiler](https://github.com/SandAI-org/MagiCompiler), FlashAttention 3) and so ships as a [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/sandai/magi-2-preview), and its checkpoint has no `model_index.json`. This PR builds it against SGLang's own layers so it is served like every other family in `sglang.multimodal_gen`. ## Modifications ### New code Four pieces the tree did not already have. Everything else goes through existing machinery. - **Multi-head MoE** (`runtime/layers/moe_multihead.py`). MAGI-2 routes 12 independent heads over 256 experts each, top-6, where the tree's MoE assumes one routing head. Viewing tokens as `[N * 12, 256]` instead of `[N, 12, 256]` makes it a standard MoE with `hidden_size=256` and `num_experts=3072`, so srt's Triton `fused_experts` runs unmodified. MAGI-2's activation, which it calls `swiglu7`, is a sigmoid-gated GELU approximation clamped to ±7 and maps onto that kernel's existing `gemm1_alpha` and `gemm1_clamp_limit`. - **Attention sinks** (`runtime/layers/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`). Both DiTs use one always-attended sink token per sequence, and the FlashAttention backend accepted no `sinks` argument, so those logits were dropped silently. Now plumbed through, along with `window_size`. - **Block-window local attention** (`runtime/layers/attention/magi2_block_grid_attention.py`). Every refiner layer restricts video-to-video attention to a radius-(2,2,2) ball on the 3-D latent block grid, which no `(left, right)` flash window can express, so it is carried as a `flex_attention` `BlockMask` built from tile occupancy rather than through `create_block_mask` and its dense intermediate. The same mask is also expressed as token-range pairs for MagiAttention's `flex_flash_attn_func`, which is used when that package is importable and is 1.78x faster on the refiner's shape; without it the `flex_attention` path runs unchanged. - **Multi-stream hyper-connections**, mHC (`runtime/models/dits/magi2_mhc.py`). The preview DiT's residual is 4 parallel streams of 3072 rather than one of 12288, mixed by a per-block matrix that Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization keeps doubly stochastic. ### Reused from the tree Both DiTs are wired to the existing optimizations rather than reimplementing them: - **Ulysses sequence parallelism** carries the packed sequence. Rows are sharded once per forward and gathered at the end, and pad rows from an uneven split get their own varlen segment so real tokens cannot attend to them. - **Expert parallelism** shards the MoE head axis with one all-to-all, through the same `ep_group` plumbing srt's MoE uses. - **Layerwise and CPU offload** via `LayerwiseOffloadableModuleMixin` and `layer_names`, so `--dit-layerwise-offload` and `--cpu-offload-components` work without model-specific code. - `AutoencoderKLWan` for the video VAE (which is what MAGI-2 ships), the UniPC scheduler, FSDP sharding through `_fsdp_shard_conditions`, and the `PipelineStage` / `Req` / `OutputBatch` contracts. ### Structure Eleven stages under `runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/magi2/`. Two orderings matter and are easy to break in review: Image encoding runs **before** text encoding, because each conditioning image needs a `<Figure N>` phrase present in the prompt; pooling that phrase's embedding runs **after**, because it needs the encoded prompt. A conditioning image is not the clip's first frame — it is VAE-encoded, parked past the clip on the rope time axis, and bound to the prompt through that pooled embedding. The denoise loop is model-owned rather than delegated to `DenoisingStage`, because video and audio carry separate guidance scales and separate multistep scheduler state, which the shared loop's single-latent contract cannot represent. Compile, residency and warmup still come from the base stage. ### Parallelism `--num-gpus` must divide every head axis, since a rank owns whole heads on all of them: 24 preview attention heads, 12 preview MoE heads, 32 refiner attention heads, 8 refiner GQA key/value heads. The refiner's 8 bind, so the two-stage tier admits 2 or 4 and preview-only admits 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. All four axes are checked in `validate_server_args`, so a bad count fails at launch instead of inside a collective. 8 GPUs divides three axes but not the preview's 12 MoE heads. The reference handles that by padding the head axis to 16 and giving the spare ranks zero-weight experts; this PR rejects the configuration instead, rather than waste two ranks of expert capacity. `--enable-cfg-parallel` is rejected — the denoise loop already runs both branches itself, so splitting CFG across ranks would double-apply the guidance. Expert parallelism is what lets the weights fit, not merely what makes them fast: the preview partition is 228 GB in BF16 and only its expert tensors shard, while the 6.7B refiner is replicated per rank. ### Deliberate divergences from the reference Both are marked at the site in the code. **The refiner's residual accumulates in BF16, not FP32.** The reference promotes it at the first `down_proj` and holds FP32 through all 30 layers. Matching that roughly doubles the residual's footprint across 30 layers at the 1080p sequence length, which the two-stage tier does not have to spare. The refiner's QK-norm likewise stores in BF16 while reducing in FP32, where the preview DiT can afford FP32 through the rotary. **Expert-parallel head padding is not implemented**, as described under Parallelism. ### Docs `docs/cookbook/diffusion/MAGI/MAGI-2.mdx` covers the quality tiers, the parallelism rules, offload recipes, and the stage timings below. Added to the compatibility matrix. ### Known limitations - Only 1920x1088 and 896x512 are accepted, rejected before denoising otherwise. 1088 rather than 1080 because the VAE stride forces multiples of 16. - 10-second clips only; the model was trained for one duration. - `--enable-torch-compile` must be paired with `--regional-compile`. On its own it compiles the whole transformer, and inductor autotuning then fails on the multi-head MoE GEMMs, asking more shared memory than sm90 has (`triton_mm Required: 262144, Hardware limit: 232448`). With `--regional-compile` the expert GEMMs stay out of the compiled region and both DiTs compile per block. - `--tp-size` and `--ring-degree` are rejected, per the speed tests below. - FlashAttention only. Sinks and the packed varlen path exist nowhere else, so `sage_attn` is rejected rather than silently degraded. - The two-stage tier wants `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`. Its decode asks for one large block while both DiTs are resident, which otherwise tends to fail on fragmentation well into a run. A startup warning fires when it is unset. ## Accuracy Tests ### Side-by-side with the reference implementation Three pairs, each generated twice on the same box with the same weights, the same seed 42, and the same 1920x1088 two-stage tier — once by the reference implementation and once by this PR. The prompts are the reference repository's own long structured captions, used verbatim so nothing depends on prompt wording. **Pair 1, text-to-video.** An 8895-character caption describing a 10-second Japanese-anime-style sequence: a young girl walks from a dark, mist-filled forest into a bright clearing over the ocean, with one deliberate camera cut near the climax. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b734f741-c01f-43ac-bde9-8634b447fb1a - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05fccde8-111a-4162-91ba-4eb31f974b67 **Pair 2, image-to-video.** The same caption as pair 1, plus a still frame as the conditioning image. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fdab8b3-a4f4-4569-983f-5c9087891e51 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19f6148-4c93-4dca-8ef1-c3714fa4242d **Pair 3, image-to-video.** A 10931-character caption describing a stop-motion clay animation — a small clay figure searches a room for a lost red ball and finds it at his feet — plus its conditioning still. - Reference: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9444c586-ebae-4daa-901a-bd7161e36858 - This PR: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f8638fd-90cd-4ee1-b824-e3334f99d964 The two are not bit-identical and are not meant to be. This PR runs SGLang's own attention, MoE and VAE paths rather than the reference's kernels, and it accumulates the refiner residual in BF16 where the reference uses FP32 — see Deliberate divergences. The clips are the thing to look at. ### Prompt coverage Eight prompts in one process, all at 1920x1088 with joint audio, seed 42 — static and fast-moving subjects, interior and exterior, one non-English: - Calm mountain lake at sunrise, mist over still water — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed79a0e-4a39-42da-a144-fe77765f3ffe - Busy night market in the rain, neon reflected in puddles — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed94afe5-4337-44ce-949a-78abc5f0ae20 - Cellist in an empty concert hall, dust in a shaft of light — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2abb3374-184d-4278-ac9a-0ebb6976df38 - Golden retriever bounding through deep snow, powder spraying — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/728e9d78-5577-4ec3-8eae-d524f9fc66bc - Timelapse of storm clouds over wheat fields — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a677bb13-efca-4aba-932e-ebfdf250e98e - 一位老人在清晨的公园里练太极，动作缓慢舒展 — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e8bbc7-6970-4007-815b-0b4d0ab987d9 - Blacksmith hammering glowing steel, sparks arcing — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b39855-3163-48eb-af15-677dd499bf0b - Sea turtle gliding over a coral reef, sunlight rippling — https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a876691-8373-423b-8ad1-c7096c1bec23 All eight ran without a restart. Every output verified h264 1920x1088 at 25 fps, 249 frames, AAC 44100 Hz stereo, 10.0s. The audio tracks its prompt rather than being generic ambience — the blacksmith clip is 66% silence between strikes, the lake clip is continuous and low-frequency. ### Unit tests 59 unit tests, 51 of which need no GPU: the MoE router and expert layout, mHC normalization, rope construction and partial rotation, the coordinate builder, packed-sequence layout, the noise schedule the refiner restarts from, guidance arithmetic, the block-grid mask and the block order it must be applied in, sequence bucketing, the expert-axis sharding predicate, and which submodules the regional-compile conditions select. The remaining 8 need CUDA and are skipped without it: the mHC mixing kernel against an FP32 reference, and the block-window mask against a dense `scaled_dot_product_attention` reference. They are flat files under `test/unit/`, so `_discover_unit_tests()` picks them up and they run in the existing suite with no CI change: ``` python3 sglang/multimodal_gen/test/run_suite.py --suite unit ``` The full 1080p path needs four cards and about ten minutes per clip, so it is not in the suite. ## Speed Tests and Profiling All figures below are one machine's numbers — 4x H200 at `--ulysses-degree 4` with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` — and are meant as relative comparisons, not as sizing targets. They are eager-mode figures; the compiled configuration and the comparison against the reference are in Benchmark below. **One 1080p clip, 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, text-to-video — 592s total:** text encoding 17.6s, preview denoise 452.8s, the preview-to-refiner handoff under 0.1s, refiner denoise 101.6s, decode 15.5s. Weight load is separate and paid once per process, about 5 minutes for both DiTs. Image-to-video costs more — the conditioning image adds 1680 patch tokens and the longer caption takes 24s to encode — and measures 741s. **Batch stability.** Eight clips of differing prompt length in one process gave refiner times of 101.6, 102.4, 101.0, 101.2, 100.8, 100.4, 101.8 and 103.6s. Flat, which is the property that matters for serving. Text encoding drops from 17.6s on the first clip to about 9s afterwards, as the memory-mapped encoder weights stay in the host page cache. **Tensor parallelism**, preview tier at 896x512, 20 steps, four ranks: pure Ulysses 124.5s; `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` 205.9s; `--tp-size 4` 608.1s, each using more memory per rank than the last. Neither DiT has a column- or row-parallel layer, so `--tp-size` shards no weights and only takes ranks away from Ulysses — those ranks stop sharding the sequence and duplicate full-length work. Rejected at startup rather than left for a user to discover. **Sequence length.** The refiner's packed sequence is `video + audio + text + reference`, so its length follows the prompt, and its `flex_attention` mask is compiled per length with each graph retained. Six clips at 4 preview steps, where the first three share a prompt length: - rounding the sequence to a bucket: 100.8, 98.0, 99.4, 103.0, 102.3, 102.2s - using each length verbatim: 102.6, 100.8, 102.0, 174.1, 215.5s, then out of memory Two changes keep the graph count bounded. `Magi2RefinerDiT` rounds the sequence up to a multiple of 1024 rows before sharding, collapsing the whole 0-7000-token prompt range to eight lengths at under 0.4% padding. And `build_mask_mod` carries the valid-row length as a tensor rather than an int, since dynamo guards a captured int by value and would recompile per prompt length even at a fixed shape. `dynamic=True` is not an alternative; it costs 26s per clip. ## Benchmark Same box, same weights, same seed 42, same 1920x1088 two-stage tier at 100 preview + 5 refiner steps, 4 ranks on each side. This PR runs `--enable-torch-compile --regional-compile`. Nine clips per side, discarding each process's first clip while its graphs are still building: | | reference | this PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | preview denoise (100 steps) | 277.7s | 286.6s | | refiner denoise (5 steps) | 46.1s | 41.9s | | decode (video and audio) | 8.9s | 7.8s | | **one clip, end to end** | **344.9s** | **349.3s** | **This PR is 1.3% slower** — 4.4s on a 345s clip, which is larger than the spread between runs. The refiner and the decode are faster; preview denoise is 8.9s slower and is where the difference sits. Stage times do not sum to the end-to-end row on either side, because the two implementations synchronize at different points, so the end-to-end row is the one to compare. Only this configuration was measured head-to-head. The reference's own published timings run 8 ranks, so they are not comparable to the 4-rank figures here. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. <!-- pr-states:start --> --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): <!-- slot:pr-test:start -->:x: [Run #32125795685](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125795685)<!-- slot:pr-test:end --> Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32125795184](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125795184)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end --> <!-- pr-states:end -->

signal.title: [Feat][GLM5.2] Shared KV Cache for Prefill CP
signal.text:
## Motivation DSA Prefill context parallelism requires every CP rank to consume the complete Main KV and Indexer history. Upstream main supports a layer-sharded path through [#29421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29421), using NCCL and remaining applicable across NVLink domains. This PR adds another option for same-host deployments within one peer-accessible NVLink domain: CP ranks share one CUDA VMM view and directly read peer-owned HBM pages. The two paths cover different topology and communication trade-offs. Like layer sharding, the shared layout stores one aggregate Main-K/Indexer cache instead of eight replicated copies, providing up to 8x logical cache capacity over Base CP8 for the same KV memory budget. The difference is the access model: instead of materializing each owner layer on every rank through a collective, attention kernels directly read peer-owned pages through the shared VMM view. On full GLM-5.2-FP8 / H20-3e, Shared KV stays within 1.86% of Base CP8 warmed mean Prefill latency through 256K. Base CP8 fits about 380K tokens in the tested configuration; Shared KV is intentionally capped at 1.2M tokens for the benchmark and successfully serves a 1M input. The tested 100K L2 host-cache restore reduces latency by 92.67%. ## Modifications - Add `--enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache` for same-host DSA L1/L2 sharing. - Store Main KV and Indexer once per CP group with owner-sharded CUDA VMM pages; kernels read the group-wide cache directly without per-layer KV broadcast. - Preserve the same ownership in page-first HiCache and Mooncake Prefill transfer, with mandatory CP synchronization before peer data is consumed. ## Design Logical page `p` is owned by CP rank `p % cp_size`, and each rank allocates only its owner pages. CUDA VMM exposes the physical allocations as one group-wide tensor view. Main KV uses the canonical view; Indexer adds a rank-local alias over the same physical allocation for the paged DeepGEMM path, without duplicating HBM. A mandatory CP write fence runs before any rank reads peer-owned pages. Page-first L2 keeps the same logical IDs and ownership. Each rank allocates pinned DRAM only for its owner pages and transfers only between local DRAM and local HBM. CPU failure agreement and a device fence complete each group-wide backup or restore. Mooncake Prefill transfer uses bounded registered staging buffers rather than a second HBM cache. The current scope is one host, one peer-accessible NVLink domain, GLM-5.2 DSA, FP8 KV, `tp=attn_cp`, interleaved Prefill CP, `pp=1`, page-first L1/L2, and Mooncake Prefill transfer. HiSparse, speculative decoding, and L3 storage are not enabled with this path. ## Trade-offs Both shared KV and layer sharding remove CP cache replication. They differ in how each rank accesses the complete cache: **Layer sharding** ```mermaid flowchart LR L1["Layers are sharded across CP ranks"] L2["Owner rank provides the current layer KV"] L3["Per-layer NCCL collective"] L4["Materialize full-layer receive scratch
on every CP rank"] L5["Attention reads local HBM"] LC["General NCCL-connected topology
Cost: transfer, collective sync, full-layer scratch"] L1 --> L2 --> L3 --> L4 --> L5 --> LC ``` **Shared KV (this PR)** ```mermaid flowchart LR S1["Logical page p → owner rank p mod CP size"] S2["Owner-sharded HBM mapped into
one group-wide CUDA VMM view"] S3["Owner-only page write"] S4["Mandatory CP publication fence"] S5["Attention directly reads
local or peer-owned pages"] SC["One peer-accessible NVLink domain
No per-layer KV collective or full-layer scratch"] S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> S5 --> SC ``` | | Layer sharding | Shared KV | | --- | --- | --- | | Data access | Materialize the owner layer, then read local HBM | Read peer-owned pages through one VMM address space | | Communication | Per-layer collective transfer | No per-layer KV collective; mandatory write fence | | Temporary HBM | Full-layer receive scratch | No full-layer scratch | | Topology | Works across general NCCL-connected topologies | Requires one peer-accessible NVLink domain | | Main cost | Data movement and collective synchronization | Peer-HBM latency and write synchronization | In the current upstream implementation, the layer-sharded path has not yet optimized its communication to fetch only active/sparse KV. Under the matched setup used here, Shared KV reduces warmed mean Prefill latency by 49.01% at 4K (798.09 vs. 406.91 ms), 16.26% at 128K (14,877.29 vs. 12,457.69 ms), and 7.87% at 1M (179,701.77 vs. 165,565.18 ms). These results describe the current implementations rather than an inherent limit of layer sharding; the comparison should be repeated after its sparse-fetch communication path is optimized. ## Performance ### L1 Prefill Hardware/model: one H20-3e node, full 78-layer GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/CP8, FP8 KV, `page_size=64`, `mem_fraction_static=0.88`, FlashMLA Sparse Prefill, FlashMLA KV Decode, and 8192-token chunks. Base CP8 disables cache sharding and supports about 380K tokens in this configuration. Shared KV uses `--max-total-tokens 1200000` as a test limit; this configured limit is not the architectural capacity ratio. Base CP8 uses `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 24` to fit its maximum capacity. All other workload and backend arguments match. **Metric:** mean end-to-end latency over three measured requests after one warmup request and a cache flush. This is a mean, not P90. With output length 1, E2E latency is used as Prefill latency. Actual concurrency is 0.995-1.000 and cache hit rate is 0% for every row. | Input | Base CP8 | Shared KV | Shared vs Base CP8 | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4K | 399.87 ms | 406.91 ms | +1.76% | | 32K | 2,891.98 ms | 2,913.81 ms | +0.75% | | 64K | 5,869.68 ms | 5,925.54 ms | +0.95% | | 128K | 12,331.04 ms | 12,457.69 ms | +1.03% | | 256K | 27,087.90 ms | 27,591.12 ms | +1.86% | | 512K | N/A (capacity) | 66,010.15 ms | N/A | | 1M | N/A (capacity) | 165,565.18 ms | N/A | The 4K-to-256K rows are matched performance comparisons. The 512K and 1M rows demonstrate the additional capacity and are not Base CP8 latency comparisons.
Server and benchmark commands ```bash SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 \ PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python:$PWD/sgl-kernel/python \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer-path /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30080 \ --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 \ --attention-backend dsa \ --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse \ --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv \ --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --page-size 64 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \ --max-total-tokens 1200000 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --skip-server-warmup \ --enable-dsa-shared-kv-cache python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30080 \ --dataset-name random-ids \ --model /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --tokenizer /home/models/GLM-5.2-FP8 \ --num-prompts 3 --max-concurrency 1 \ --random-input-len ${INPUT_LEN} --random-output-len 1 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf \ --tokenize-prompt --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache \ --cache-report --output-details --disable-tqdm \ --seed ${SEED} --output-file ${OUTPUT_FILE} ```
### L2 HiCache With a 150K-token L1, `hicache_ratio=10`, page-first layout, `write_through`, kernel IO, and no L3, each rank allocates 11.57 GB for its owner pages. CP8 provides one aggregate 92.56 GB / 23,528-page L2 cache instead of eight replicated logical copies. An A/B1/B2/A test uses three distinct 100K prompts so B1 and B2 evict A from L1. Restoring A reports `device=0, host=99968`, reproduces `Paris` / token `[12089]`, and reduces E2E latency from 10,509.29 ms to 770.31 ms (-92.67%). No L3 backend is configured or observed. ## Correctness - Fixed short, 100K, and 128K output-1 prompts match Base CP8; a short semantic decode also matches. - GSM8K500 24-shot completion scores `0.956` against the registered `0.94` threshold. MMLU64 sanity scores `0.796875`, equal to ordinary Base. - Targeted CPU tests pass `90` cases, CP8 multi-GPU tests pass `3` cases, and the L2 host-only restore reproduces the cold answer. All changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass. signal.title: [Ngram spec v2] Precompute drafts and fully overlap
signal.text: ## Motivation In ngram spec v2, the draft computation is on cpu and can be parallelized with the verify, computing the possible drafts and copy them to gpu in advance. For the next batch, the precomputed drafts can be directly used if hits. And missed reqs will fallback to all-zero drafts. Therefore, we can implement fully overlap on ngram. ## Modifications **Precompute draft** 1. Add `precomputeDrafts` and `selectPrecomputedDrafts` C++ functions to precompute drafts and select the prepared drafts. 2. In `precomputeDrafts`, we use 2-phase precompute. In phase-1, are used as context to predict bonus tokens. Specifically, the direct children of the matched anchors are selected as bonus candidates. In phase-2, bonus tokens are appended to the context to generate the draft tokens for next batch. All the precomputed drafts are saved into cache and copied to gpu asynchronously. 3. In `selectPrecomputedDrafts`, the verified token is used to determine if the req hit/miss. The hit reqs will directly use the precomputed drafts and the miss reqs will generate new draft tokens right way. **Fully overlap** The overall flow is `apply precompute drafts for batch N if hit` => `verify batch N` => `sync accepted tokens of batch N-1` => `do 2-phase precompute` => `scheduler process_result & prepare batch` => `apply precompute drafts for batch N+1 if hit` => `verify batch N+1` => ...... 1. After launching the verification of batch N, we precompute the potential drafts of batch N+1. Firstly sync the accept tokens of batch N-1. Then use 2-phase precompute to predict the bonus and drafts. 2. After drafts are precomputed, copy the drafts, tree masks, and bonus tokens to gpu asynchronously on separate stream. 3. When batch N+1 arrives at ngram_worker, wait the copy stream of batch N are finished. Then check if the precompute drafts are hit. If hit, directly use it without querying ngram trie. Otherwise, fill all-zero drafts for the miss reqs. **Thus we can skip the cpu-side ngram trie query and sync, and directly launch the verification**. 4. `decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens` returns False when ngram and precompute are enabled, so that we can skip the sync in scheduler. 5. Fully overlap currently only support flashattention backend which doesn't require `seq_lens_cpu`. More attention backend will be supported in the future work. **Future work** - Optimize the workflow of continuous batching. Currently all new coming requests will be filled with all-zero drafts for their first decode step, because there's no precompute cache for a brand-new request and we can't query the ngram trie to obtain the real drafts. - Delay the sync. Currently we sync batch N-1 after batch N's verification is launched, because we need the accept token of batch N-1 on cpu to predict the bonus token and then predict the drafts. Perhaps the sync can be delayed to scheduler? Just like overlap schedule without ngram, sync when processing the result of batch N-1. After this sync, we do precompute. - When checking a request to be hit or miss, it's implemented by pytorch, introducing many small kernels. Can be rewritten into a triton kernel to further speedup. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k accuracy test with Qwen3-8B. **Baseline** **With this pr** ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### result overview We tested random datasets. The input and output length are 3500 and 1024 respectively, and concurrency ranges from 4 to 256. The result is shown below. **Across all the concurrencies, this PR achieves around 7% ~ 14% improvements on E2E latency**, although precompute path causes accept lens decreasing around 0.3. | **Concurrency** | **Setup** | **TTFT / TPOT (ms)** | **E2E (ms)** | **output throughput (token/s)** | **accept length** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **4** | Baseline | 65.73 / 2.21 | 2331.56 | 1731.39 | **3.94** | | | Fully Overlap | **61.00 / 2.06** | **2165.65** | **1878.37** | 3.68 | | **16** | Baseline | 93.03 / 4.11 | 4300.55 | 3649.3 | **3.86** | | | Fully Overlap | **96.20 / 3.72** | **3900.48** | **3955.03** | 3.7 | | **32** | Baseline | 177.15 / 6.9 | 7235.77 | 4142.33 | 3.75 | | | Fully Overlap | **169.62 / 5.87** | **6176.5** | **4833.5** | 3.75 | | **128** | Baseline | 1586.31 / 24.61 | 26766.91 | 4172.10 | **4** | | | Fully Overlap | **1646.36 / 21.45** | **23590.16** | **4565.85** | 3.8 | | **256** | Baseline | 8880.42 / 36.39 | 46102.65 | 3861.69 | **4.12** | | | Fully Overlap | **8518.43 / 33.34** | **42629.05** | **4159.3** | 3.72 | Benchmark commands ``` # random python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --model /upfs/models/Qwen/Qwen3-8B/ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9090 --backend sglang --dataset-name random --dataset-path /upfs/xiaoyuan/datasets/ShareGPT_V3_unfiltered_cleaned_split.json --num-prompts 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-input-len 3500 --random-output-len 1024 --max-concurrency 256 >./bench_logs_qwen3 2>&1 & ``` Server launch command `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_ENABLE_NGRAM_PRECOMPUTE=1 SGLANG_NGRAM_PRECOMPUTE_WIDE_BONUS_RATIO=0.5 SGLANG_LOG_NGRAM_PRECOMPUTE_STATS_INTERVAL=0 SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 SGLANG_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_SIZE=536870912 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model /upfs/models/Qwen/Qwen3-8B/ --tp 1 --dp 1 --port 9090 --host 127.0.0.1 --ep 1 --attention-backend fa4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 256 --speculative-algorithm NGRAM --watchdog-timeout 300000 >./log 2>&1 &` On random dataset, it achieves around avg_precomputed_cache_hit_rate=0.3336 (17096/51252). Perhaps still has room for improvement to reduce the number of miss reqs and recover the accept lens. ### Profile We profile the case where batch size is around 240. For ngram spec v2 baseline, the gap between 2 decode batches is 22ms. With precompute & fully overlap, the bubble between 2 decode batches **decreases from 22ms to 6ms**. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #32125217736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125217736) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32125217448](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32125217448)
